items.title: The impact of patient weight status on healthcare students' attitudes: Two experimental studies in midwifery and dental students.
items.abstract: Background Weight stigma refers to prejudice and discrimination based on body weight. Healthcare professionals often hold negative attitudes towards patients with overweight, which can negatively affect patient care and health outcomes. However, weight stigma is yet to be explored in midwifery and dental students. Methods Two online experimental studies using hypothetical patient vignettes were conducted in midwifery (n = 281; Study 1) and dental and non-dental students (n = 528; Study 2). Participants were randomly assigned to view a healthy-weight, overweight or obese patient vignette and then reported their attitudes, predicted time, advice they would provide and beliefs about obesity. Data were analysed using ANOVA and logistic regression. Results In Study 1, midwifery students held significantly more stigmatizing attitudes towards patients who were overweight than healthy-weight patients; however, there was no significant difference in attitudes towards patients with obesity. Predicted time spent with patients did not significantly differ as a function of patient weight status. In Study 2, dental and non-dental students reported more stigmatizing attitudes towards overweight and obese patients compared to healthy-weight patients. Predicted time spent with patients did not differ significantly. Dental and non-dental students were more likely to offer lifestyle-related advice to overweight and obese patients. There was no significant relationship between beliefs about obesity and attitudes towards treating patients. Conclusions Weight stigma is evident among healthcare students and can affect healthcare advice. Increased awareness of potential biases in midwives and dental students is needed and should form formal training to improve equitable healthcare delivery.

items.title: Virtual Social Interaction and Psychological Capital in Chemotherapy Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Background Cancer-related psychological distress remains underaddressed globally. Virtual interventions offer promising alternatives but lack evidence for enhancing Psychological Capital (PsyCap) in chemotherapy patients. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a virtual social interaction intervention on PsyCap in patients undergoing chemotherapy. Methods This single-blind randomized controlled trial (RCT) enrolled 76 chemotherapy patients hospitalized in the oncology ward of Imam Sajjad Hospital, Ramsar, Mazandaran, Iran. Participants were selected via convenience sampling and then allocated to intervention or control groups using an odd-even (alternating) assignment method. The intervention group participated in 6 weeks of virtual social interactions, consisting of asynchronous materials (recorded audio, short videos, images, PDF, and PowerPoint files) uploaded weekly to Iranian messaging platforms (Eitaa), as well as live synchronous group sessions conducted on the Skyroom platform with a minimum of 10 participants per session. The control group received standard care. The PsyCap was measured using Luthans' Psychological Capital Questionnaire at both baseline and post-intervention. The Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) models (A/B) were adjusted for baseline scores and age. Results The intervention group showed improvements across all outcomes, with the total PsyCap score increasing by 23.6 points. Components significantly increased: self-efficacy by 5.8 points, resilience by 5.8, hope by 5.5, and optimism by 6.5 (p 1). Conclusions Virtual social interactions significantly enhance PsyCap in chemotherapy patients. However, to confidently generalize these findings and make recommendations, similar studies need to be conducted and replicated in larger, multicenter trials.

items.title: Family Engagement and Shared Decision-Making in Adult Intensive Care Nursing: A Bibliometric Review and Thematic Analysis.
items.abstract: Background Family members contribute information, emotional support, bedside care and surrogate decision-making in adult intensive care, yet the nursing literature on family engagement remains conceptually and geographically fragmented. Aims To map the development, intellectual structure, collaboration patterns and thematic evolution of research on family engagement and shared decision-making in adult intensive care nursing. Study design This study was a bibliometric review with complementary thematic content analysis. Following the framework of Donthu et al., Scopus was searched on 16 July 2026 from inception, with bibliometric coverage restricted to complete calendar years through 31 December 2025. Scopus was used because it provides the cited-reference data required for co-citation and bibliographic-coupling analyses. Eligible records were journal articles and reviews concerning adult intensive care that examined family engagement or shared decision-making and included an identifiable nursing component. Performance analysis, co-authorship analysis, reference co-citation, bibliographic coupling, and keyword co-occurrence analysis were conducted using Python and VOSviewer, while cluster content was interpreted using inductive qualitative content analysis. Reporting followed the BIBLIO guideline. Results The review included 278 publications (1993-2025) from 117 journals and 47 countries. Annual output increased from two publications in 1993 to 32 publications in 2025; 141 publications (50.7%) were published during 2020-2025. Nursing journals produced most publications, whereas two multidisciplinary critical care journals produced 23 publications (8.3%) but 3090 of 11 220 citations (27.5%). The United States led with 104 publications; 23.9% were internationally co-authored. Co-citation analysis identified four intellectual foundations and bibliographic coupling five research fronts, led by family participation and nurse-family engagement. Thirty-nine author keywords formed six themes spanning end-of-life communication and ethics, family-centred nursing engagement and surrogate participation, family support and visitation, family presence in high-acuity care, caregiver experience and bereavement. Keyword trends moved from family needs and withholding treatment towards active engagement, implementation barriers and family nursing. Conclusion The field has progressed towards partnership but continues to under-specify nurses' roles, use inconsistent terminology and draw disproportionately on high-income Western settings. Relevance to clinical practice Critical care services should formalise nurses' responsibilities in family assessment, communication, advocacy and decision support while developing culturally responsive and implementable engagement models.

items.title: Associations Between Parity and Parasympathetic Regulation in Response to Infant Crying.
items.abstract: Research suggests that women's parasympathetic response to infant crying reflects regulation of arousal and is associated with caregiving behaviors. In particular, respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) withdrawal in response to infant cry stimuli has been associated with maternal sensitivity. However, the ways in which multiple reproductive and caregiving experiences (in terms of giving birth and raising a child) can modulate women's RSA in response to infant crying are still unknown. Our aim was to test whether women's RSA in response to infant crying is associated with parity. Participants included 184 women (62 nulliparous women; 86 primiparous women; 36 multiparous women). RSA was measured while women were watching a neutral video, followed by videos of crying infants. Analyses revealed that perception of infant crying was associated with a significant RSA withdrawal, compared to the baseline condition, in both multiparous and nulliparous women. A statistically significant RSA withdrawal was absent among primiparous women, possibly reflecting a more sustained physiological arousal to infant crying. We discuss the potential challenges in physiological regulation, indexed by RSA withdrawal, among primiparous women in response to infant crying. More sustained arousal may support an increased focus on infant signals but also predispose new mothers to perceive greater stress.

items.title: Incidence of Intensive Care Unit Delirium After Heart Surgery: A Feasibility Study of a Forest Environment Intervention.
items.abstract: Background Postoperative delirium is a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), particularly following cardiac surgery. It is associated with circadian rhythm disruption, sleep disturbances and adverse outcomes. ICU environments often lack natural time cues, which may exacerbate circadian misalignment and increase delirium risk. Aim The primary aim of the study was the evaluation of the implementation of two chronotherapeutic ICU interventions regarding recruitment, implementability and safety. Its secondary aim was to descriptively assess postoperative delirium across intervention groups. Study design This randomized feasibility study was conducted in a tertiary cardiac surgery ICU in Austria. Adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery were allocated to one of three groups: (1) forest environment, (2) light exposure or (3) standard ICU care. Interventions were applied for 12 h daily. Delirium was assessed at three postoperative time points using the confusion assessment method for the ICU (CAM-ICU) and intensive care delirium screening checklist (ICDSC). Results This study was conducted between March 2020 and 2025. Seventy-seven patients were enrolled, and 64 remained in the final analytical cohort. Interventions were delivered within routine care. Patients and ICU staff did not report intervention-related concerns. Implementation challenges included ICU restructuring, patient transfers due to COVID-19 and deviations from randomized allocation because of operational constraints. No intervention-related adverse events occurred. Delirium assessments were limited at several time points because of sedation, early ICU discharge or transfer. Across all groups, postoperative delirium was detected in 5 of 130 CAM-ICU completed assessments (3.8%) and 8 of 115 ICDSC completed assessments (6.9%), precluding inferential group comparisons. Conclusions Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions were feasible and safe in ICU care. Feasibility results highlighted challenges related to ICU logistics, sedation-related assessment limitations and pandemic-related disruptions. The unexpectedly low delirium incidence limited conclusions regarding intervention efficacy. Future trials should include larger high-risk populations and prospectively defined feasibility outcomes. Relevance to clinical practice Optimized ICU environments, including noise reduction and light management, may support delirium prevention. Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions are feasible additions to routine ICU care.

items.title: Pre-Drinking and Its Relationship to Sexual Diversity and Sexual Harassment in Nightlife Settings.
items.abstract: Introduction Sexual harassment is experienced by 50% of nightlife patrons and disproportionately more by LGBTQIA+ (i.e., lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual) patrons. The present study investigated its association with pre-drinking in Australian nightlife. Method An online survey assessing pre-drinking behaviours and various forms of sexual harassment was completed by a sample of 958 individuals aged 18-65 years. Results Pre-drinking volume (r = 0.11, p 2 (16) = 12.30, p = 0.02], females reported greater sexual harassment than males [χ 2 (1) = 47.13, p 2 (4) = 34.51, p 2 = 0.16, F(5, 170) = 6.31, p Discussion and conclusions The relationship between sexual harassment, pre-drinking, gender and sexuality is complex. The present study did not find that sexually diverse individuals engaged in more pre-drinking behaviours than heterosexual individuals, nor that LGBTQIA+ individuals report greater rates of sexual harassment than individuals identifying as heterosexual. However, women reported a larger number of sexual harassment experiences. Using these findings to inform interventions to reduce sexual harassment is indicated.

items.title: A pilot study of electromagnetic therapy versus biofeedback-based pelvic floor muscle training for pelvic organ prolapse: A mixed-methods approach.
items.abstract: Objectives This pilot study aimed to: (1) evaluate the effects of high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) therapy on pelvic organ prolapse (POP) symptoms and pelvic floor function; (2) compare outcomes across HIFEM, pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) with biofeedback and/or electrostimulation, and usual care; and (3) explore participant acceptability of the interventions. Materials and methods A mixed-methods pilot study was conducted in women aged >20 years with stage I-III POP. Participants were randomized to HIFEM, PFMT, or usual care. The HIFEM group underwent twice-weekly 28-min sessions for eight weeks using a non-invasive electromagnetic chair. PFMT consisted of supervised sessions incorporating biofeedback and/or electrostimulation. Usual care included lifestyle advice. Outcomes were assessed using validated questionnaires for POP symptoms and pelvic floor distress, digital palpation, and transperineal ultrasound. Results Twenty-eight women completed the study (HIFEM, n = 10; PFMT, n = 9; usual care, n = 9). Compared with usual care, HIFEM significantly improved pelvic floor muscle endurance (p = 0.001), whereas PFMT significantly improved muscle strength (p = 0.034), endurance (p = 0.023), and rapid contractions (p = 0.019). Only HIFEM demonstrated significant improvements in POP symptom severity (p = 0.015) and pelvic floor distress (p = 0.041). No serious adverse events were reported. Participant satisfaction was highest in the HIFEM group (100%). Qualitative analysis supported intervention acceptability, with participants reporting increased pelvic floor awareness, improved symptom control, and enhanced psychological well-being. Conclusions Both HIFEM and PFMT with biofeedback appear to be safe, acceptable, and effective non-surgical treatment options for women with POP. Although no significant differences were observed between the two interventions, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of the small sample size. Larger studies are needed to confirm comparative efficacy and inform clinical implementation. Clinical trial registration number NCT06532292. URL OF THE REGISTRATION SITE: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06532292?cond=Pelvic%20Organ%20Prolapse&intr=high-intensity&rank=1.

items.title: Voluntary exercise mitigates the effects of peri-adolescent social isolation on emotion recognition and the oxytocinergic system in male mice.
items.abstract: Social isolation, particularly during adolescence, is known to affect cognitive, emotional, and social behaviors as well as brain modulatory systems such as the hypothalamic oxytocinergic system. Interestingly, recent evidence indicates that exercise can exert beneficial effects on behaviors through the activation of the oxytocinergic system. Weaned male mice were either singly- or group-housed and were exposed to either an igloo or a running wheel until the end of the experiment. After 12 weeks in these experimental conditions, they were subjected to various behavioral tests to assess different dimensions of social behaviors (sociability, social recognition and emotion discrimination), anxiety levels, and spatial memory. The impact of peri-adolescent social isolation and of voluntary running activity on the oxytocinergic system was also evaluated. We found that peri-adolescent social isolation enhanced social investigation (social rebound) and impaired emotion discrimination in male mice, without affecting social novelty recognition, spatial memory or anxiety-like behavior. Social isolation also decreased the number of oxytocinergic neurons in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus, but not in the supraoptic nucleus, and did not affect circulating OXT levels. Voluntary exercise protected against social isolation-induced deficits in affective state discrimination and enhanced OXT plasma levels without altering the number of oxytocinergic neurons. Our results indicate that peri-adolescent isolation particularly alters socio-affective discrimination and the oxytocinergic system, that are mitigated by voluntary exercise. This suggests that exercise could alleviate emotion discrimination deficits induced by isolation, possibly through the improvement of oxytocinergic signaling.

items.title: ANCHOR: Communication Partner Training for Maintaining Friendships After Aphasia.
items.abstract: Background Aphasia significantly disrupts social relationships, with friendship loss occurring early after stroke and continuing into chronic stages. Despite friendships being prioritised by people with aphasia and families, they rarely receive explicit focus in rehabilitation. Communication partner training is an intervention with potential to keep friendship bonds strong after aphasia. Aims This paper describes the development of ANCHOR (Aphasia: Nurturing Connection, Honoring Ongoing Relationships), a communication partner training intervention protoype designed specifically for people with aphasia and their pre-existing friends-and the foundational elements of ANCHOR and how they informed its design and components, and then situates ANCHOR within the broader communication partner training literature with attention to partner type, candidacy and real-world delivery in service settings. Main contribution ANCHOR represents the first communication partner training intervention explicitly targeting friendship maintenance after aphasia. Development was grounded in a systematic research progression including lived experience research, relational competence theory and the behaviour change wheel, and a planned cycle of refinement across a two-year development period. Key distinguishing features include a hybrid delivery model that combines self-paced digital modules with in-person coaching sessions, universal 'talking tools' accessible to friends with minimal aphasia knowledge, first-year post-stroke timing to prevent relationship deterioration, and explicit attention to implementation barriers. Conclusions By grounding communication partner training design in lived experience, relationship theory and implementation science, ANCHOR is designed as a comprehensive, implementable approach to sustaining friendships after aphasia, thereby addressing a critical gap in post-stroke rehabilitation with potential to reduce social isolation and support mental health. ANCHOR is an intervention prototype and its core functions, forms and implementation supports will be refined as feasibility and trial data accrue. What this paper adds What is already known on this subject Aphasia greatly impacts the ability for people to maintain a strong social network. People with aphasia often lose most of their pre-stroke friends early in the recovery journey. Friends of people with aphasia need access to interventions that can help them understand aphasia and its impact on communication. What this study adds to the existing knowledge We developed a communication partner training program called ANCHOR based upon lived experience research involving people with aphasia and their friends and theories and relationship maintenance and behaviour change. ANCHOR is different than other communication partner training programs which target family members or healthcare providers in that it is limited to three face-to-face sessions, includes a self-guided digital component, and focuses on a standard package of communication strategies. What are the potential clinical implications of the study? ANCHOR continues to be refined and evaluated. It is our hope that ANCHOR will be a clinically feasible and person-centered communication partner training program that is effective in improving communication and relationships for people with aphasia and their friends.

items.title: Not All Thwarting Is Equal: Distinct Temporal Patterns Linking Teachers' Psychological Needs to Turnover Intention.
items.abstract: Background Teacher turnover intention has become a critical global concern, compromising teachers' psychological well-being, school workforce stability, and student learning outcomes. While psychological need thwarting (PNT) is recognized as a key antecedent of turnover intention, existing research has predominantly treated PNT as a unidimensional construct and overlooked the possibility that turnover intention may reciprocally shape teachers' subsequent need experiences. Integrating self-determination theory and conservation of resources theory, this study employed a two-wave cross-lagged panel model to examine bidirectional associations between the three PNT dimensions and turnover intention among Chinese teachers. Methods Data were collected from 1,061 teachers at Time 1 and 812 at Time 2 under a design permitting voluntary, wave-specific participation, with 332 teachers participating in both waves (M age = 41.19 years, SD = 9.13; 69.6% female); cross-lagged models controlling for gender and age were estimated using full information maximum likelihood, drawing on all available observations from 1,541 unique participants, with school ownership and school type incorporated into the missing-data model. Results An asymmetric temporal pattern emerged: among the three dimensions, only autonomy thwarting predicted subsequent turnover intention (B = 0.09, 95% CI [0.01, 0.17], β = 0.12, p = 0.023), whereas turnover intention predicted later competence thwarting (B = 0.22, 95% CI [0.02, 0.41], β = 0.11, p = 0.031) and relatedness thwarting (B = 0.19, 95% CI [0.01, 0.37], β = 0.13, p = 0.048) but not autonomy thwarting (B = 0.08, 95% CI [-0.07, 0.24], β = 0.06, p = 0.276). Although these cross-lagged effects were small in magnitude, they demonstrated distinct directional patterns across the three needs. Conclusion These findings suggest that turnover intention may function not only as an outcome of adverse need experiences but also as an antecedent of subsequent need states. This asymmetric pattern points to potentially relevant intervention targets: autonomy support for teachers who have not yet developed turnover intention, and competence and relatedness support for those already considering leaving.

items.title: The Impact of Cladribine Tablets on Cognition Over One Year in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis: A Preliminary Study.
items.abstract: Introduction Cognitive impairment is common in multiple sclerosis (MS), affecting >40% of patients. Cladribine tablets are a high-efficacy MS disease-modifying therapy to prevent relapses and limit disease progression. Our previous study showed cortical gray matter lesion stability over one year after the start of cladribine, though its effect on cognition is not well known. This study aimed to investigate the one-year impact of cladribine tablets on cognition in multiple sclerosis. Methods Fourteen MS subjects [age (mean ± SD) 50.2 ± 10.8, 7.14% men, 57.1% relapsing-remitting MS (n = 8), 42.9% secondary progressive (n = 6), expanded disability status scale 4.1 ± 2.1] were administered the Brief Repeatable Battery of Neuropsychological Tests (BRB-N) and the Stroop Color and Word Test (Stroop) at an average of 1.5 months from cladribine start. The BRB-N measures information processing speed (Symbol Digit Modalities Test, Paced Auditory Serial Addition Test [PASAT]), verbal memory (Selective Reminding Test [SRT]), visual-spatial memory (10/36 Spatial Recall Test), and verbal fluency (Word List Generation). Stroop assesses processing speed and executive function. When available, alternate versions of the individual cognitive tests were used at follow-up to reduce practice effects. Paired t-tests compared within-subject baseline and follow-up data. Results After one year, no worsening was noted on any cognitive test. Furthermore, both PASAT 3-second total correct and SRT total delayed recall trended toward improved scores on-study, with an average 3.4 (p = 0.07) and 1.1 (p = 0.05) point increase, respectively. Conclusion In this preliminary study, no clear decline in cognitive performance was detectable over one year in patients newly started on cladribine tablets.

items.title: Inpatient Dementia Mental Health Care in the UK: A National Mapping Survey of Ward Provision and Family Carer Involvement.
items.abstract: Objectives Inpatient mental health wards provide specialist care for people with dementia experiencing acute behavioural disturbance. The scale and configuration of this provision, and how these services involve family carers, have not previously been described at a national level. This study aimed to map ward provision across the UK and characterise existing policies and practices related to carer involvement. Methods A national cross-sectional online mapping survey was conducted across mental health wards providing care for people with dementia in the UK. Wards were identified through a structured multi-source search strategy. The survey captured ward characteristics, patient profile, staffing and approaches to carer involvement. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively; Fisher's exact test was used to examine associations between categorical variables. Results 209 wards comprising over 3100 beds across 80 provider organisations were identified. 63 wards (30.1%) participated, reporting 801 patients. Most patients were detained under mental health or capacity legislation (87.8%) and few were expected to return home (14.8%). While all wards reported involving carers in clinical decision-making, 44.4% indicated carers did not routinely attend MDT meetings and 30.2% did not routinely share care plans. Staff training in carer engagement was a consistent marker of greater carer involvement across multiple measures. Conclusions This survey provides the first national picture of inpatient dementia mental health care in the UK, revealing a service under considerable pressure and a consistent gap between the basic infrastructure for carer involvement and its meaningful integration into clinical practice. Staff training in carer engagement was strongly associated with greater carer involvement, pointing to an actionable route to improvement.

items.title: From Daily Attitudes to Alcohol-Related Harm: A Within-Person Serial Mediation Test Informed by the Theory of Planned Behavior.
items.abstract: Background The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) posits that attitudes influence behavior through intentions, yet this pathway has not been thoroughly examined at the within-person level in the alcohol literature. This study tested whether daily fluctuations in attitudes toward heavy drinking predicted same-day alcohol-related consequences and alcohol-induced blackouts through a serial mediation involving daily drinking intentions and alcohol consumption. Methods Participants were 87 heavy-drinking young adults (53.4% female; Mage = 22.22 years) enrolled in the intervention arm of a randomized clinical trial who completed up to 30 consecutive days of morning diary assessments. Multilevel models separated within-and between-person variance by person-mean centering daily predictors. Serial mediation pathways were estimated using multilevel regression models, and specific indirect effects were tested using Monte Carlo confidence intervals. Results On days when participants reported more favorable attitudes toward heavy drinking than their own average, they also reported stronger intentions to drink, which predicted greater same-day alcohol consumption. Greater drinking, in turn, predicted increased odds of both alcohol-related consequences and blackout. Significant serial indirect effects supported the hypothesized pathway from attitudes to consequences and blackout through intentions and drinking. Drinking intentions also directly predicted alcohol-related consequences independent of drinking quantity but did not directly predict blackout after accounting for drinking, suggesting differences in the mechanisms underlying these outcomes. Conclusion Findings provide day-level support for a TPB-informed pathway linking within-person fluctuations in drinking attitudes to alcohol-related harm through drinking intentions and alcohol consumption. Results extend prior between-person TPB research by demonstrating that attitudes and intentions function as dynamic, day-to-day processes that help explain when individuals are at elevated risk for harmful drinking outcomes. Daily attitudes and intentions may represent promising targets for ecological momentary interventions designed to reduce alcohol-related harm.

items.title: Functional Health Illiteracy in Cancer Patients and Caregivers in the Era of Precision Medicine and Immunotherapy: A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: Functional health illiteracy is a significant barrier to equitable cancer care for patients and caregivers, a challenge that is exacerbated by precision medicine and immunotherapy. This review article aimed at synthesizing current evidence on functional health illiteracy among cancer patients and caregivers and examines its interaction with the demands of precision medicine and immunotherapy. The article also outlines practical strategies to mitigate the impact of health illiteracy on therapy adherence, decision-making, and clinical outcomes. Articles published between 2010 and 2025 were identified through searches of PubMed, CINAHL, and PsycINFO. Policy reports from the National Cancer Institute, the Institute of Medicine, and the American Society of Clinical Oncology were also included to provide contextual background. Consistency in article selection was assessed using the K coefficient. Approximately 36-50% of cancer patients were found to be unable to effectively use health information. Older adults, racial and ethnic minorities, and individuals with lower incomes are disproportionately affected. The complex terminology of precision oncology further complicates matters for patients and caregivers, who must manage intricate drug regimens and monitor for immune-related side effects at home. Low health literacy is associated with reduced clinical trial enrollment, decreased therapy adherence, increased emergency department visits, and poorer survival. Interventions, including plain-language use, culturally tailored instructions, digital health skill development, and organizational modifications, have demonstrated efficacy in enhancing health literacy among cancer patients and caregivers. These approaches improve access to medical information, reduce misunderstandings, and support self-management. As precision medicine evolves, aligning clinical complexity with targeted health literacy strategies is essential to optimize adherence, decision-making, and clinical outcomes.

items.title: Difficult Clinical Encounters in Chronic Wound Care: An Interview Study of Nurses' Experiences and Approaches.
items.abstract: Although difficult social interaction patterns are scientifically addressed in other medical fields, it is an under-researched topic in wound care. A knowledge gap exists pertaining to what kind of interpersonal problems occur between patients with chronic wounds, their relatives and nurses. In an exploratory interview study, we analyzed 37 interviews with nurses from different settings to explore how they perceive and approach difficult encounters with patients with chronic wounds. A content analysis conducted with MAXQDA revealed three broad themes of difficult nurse-patient interactions. First, conflicts included aggression, violence, insults, arguments, unrealistic demands, discrimination, lying, complaints, and general unfriendly behaviour. Often, nurses function as a kind of outlet for patients' annoyance. Second, non-adherence was associated with perceiving treatment as difficult. Third, difficult but non-conflictual situations were also common, that is, various and multilayered issues which complicate treatment. In addition, an overview of what respondents considered an ideal wound care practitioner is provided. Interventions could target self-care, nonviolent communication, and health literacy.

items.title: Illicitly Traded Tobacco Use Among Samples of People Who Regularly Use Illegal Drugs in Australia, 2024-2025.
items.abstract: Introduction Australia's illicit tobacco trade poses major challenges, with evidence of increasing use. We examined: (i) use of illicitly traded tobacco (ITT) and reasons for use among two populations of people who use drugs in Australia; and (ii) factors associated with ITT use, versus exclusive licit tobacco use, in 2024 and 2025. Methods Cross-sectional samples of people who regularly (i.e., ≥monthly) used illicit stimulants (Ecstasy and Related Drugs Reporting System (EDRS); n = 1430) or injected drugs (Illicit Drug Reporting System (IDRS); n = 1749) were recruited April-July in 2024 and 2025. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with past 6-month ITT use. Efforts to restrict availability should prioritise supply-side controls, alongside treatment and demand-reduction strategies.

items.title: Environmental scan of hearing health services and databases in Australia: barriers and enablers for a national child deafness Learning Health System.
items.abstract: Objective To conduct a national environmental scan of child hearing health-related services and databases as part of the Australian National Child Hearing Health Outcomes Registry program, and to identify system-level barriers and enablers to developing a coordinated Learning Health System for deaf and hard-of-hearing children. Methods A cross-sectional national survey of organisations providing hearing health-related services or managing data for Australian deaf and hard-of-hearing children. The survey examined the scope and practices related to data collection, standardisation, interoperability, stewardship, and governance. Results Ninety-nine respondents from 92 organisations delivering 290 services participated. The scan identified a disjointed data landscape. Standardised data were limited, with inconsistent capture of key variables across organisations and 49.4% rating their data quality as acceptable or good. Interoperability was constrained by heterogenous data practices, including use of multiple databases (34.3%), limited external reporting (24.2%) and lack of accessible data dictionaries (71.9%). Stewardship and data governance arrangements were variable, with fewer than half of organisations reporting formal consent (47.6%), privacy statements (51.2%) or ethics oversight (38.1%). Despite these challenges, 56.5 and 54.8% of organisations expressed interest in data linkage and research participation, indicating readiness for coordinated system development. Conclusion Despite Australia's substantial investment in newborn hearing screening and hearing health-related services, fragmented data systems limit Australia's ability to monitor outcomes, equity and system performance in child hearing health. However, strong stakeholder interest in data linkage provides important momentum. These findings inform policy and service planning, and support staged development of a national child deafness Learning Health System through the Australian National Child Hearing Health Outcomes Registry.

items.title: Neurophysiological and Behavioural Effects of Combined Cannabis Concentrates and Alcohol Among People Who Regularly Use Alcohol and Cannabis.
items.abstract: Increasingly potent concentrated cannabis products containing high levels of Δ 9 -tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) are being consumed with alcohol. This combination is known to acutely impair cognitive and psychomotor abilities, although few studies have evaluated alcohol and cannabis co-use using neural measures. This naturalistic feasibility study explored the acute effects of co-intoxication on behavioural performance and brain activity, measured via electroencephalography (EEG), during a performance monitoring task administered three times over a 4.5-h period. Participants (N = 17, 65% male) were heavy drinking community members (age M = 31.7 years; SD = 10.27) who regularly use cannabis. EEG was recorded while participants completed a speeded visual-flanker task at baseline (sober) before consuming a standardized dose of alcohol and a cannabis concentrate product, followed by EEG recordings 1-h (intoxicated) and 4-h post co-consumption (recovery). Recordings were processed to obtain six event-related potential components: the stimulus-locked N1, P2, N2 and P3 and response-locked error-related negativity (ERN) and error positivity (Pe). Repeated measures ANOVAs revealed that behavioural measures at the intoxicated timepoint showed an increase in errors (p 2 p = 0.35) and significant decrease in response time (RT) (p 2 p = 0.50) compared to sober and recovery periods. Measures of brain activity also demonstrated significant change across time with largest amplitudes when sober, smaller amplitudes when intoxicated, then an increase in amplitude to near sober levels at recovery for stimulus-locked (P2, N2 and P3) and response-locked components (ERN and Pe). Thus, compared to sober and recovery periods, the behaviour at the intoxicated timepoint revealed significantly greater impulsivity (RT) leading to significantly higher error rates, while measures of cognitive processing (i.e., decision-making, error detection, performance monitoring/adaptation) showed significantly diminished levels of brain activity. Performance and neurophysiology measures remained diminished at recovery compared to baseline. Understanding neurocognitive functioning during co-intoxication may provide insights into specific cognitive processes that may impact function in everyday activities such as driving. Trial Registration: NCT06259916.

items.title: Pavlovian cues and self-control choice: The role of unpaired training.
items.abstract: Interventions seeking to reduce impulsive choice in nonhuman animals (i.e., preference for smaller sooner over larger later rewards [SSR vs. LLR]) often require long training durations. However, prior studies illustrate how a brief course of Pavlovian training can reduce rodents' impulsive choice by attracting them to the LLR and by providing an appetitive Pavlovian conditioned stimulus (CS) contingent on LLR choices. In these studies, the comparison group completed unpaired (UN) training where the CS and US never co-occurred. The present study added a truly random control (TRC) group to evaluate whether UN training made the CS aversive, exaggerating the effect of Pavlovian training on self-control. Following Pavlovian (PAV), UN, or TRC training, a lever CS was inserted into the chamber during half the delay to the LLR. PAV rats were significantly more attracted to the lever during training and chose the LLR significantly more often than TRC or UN rats. Significant sex differences were detected, with self-control influencing the effects of Pavlovian training predominantly observed in male rats. Because sex differences in self-control outcomes were not observed in the only other study to examine the effects of presenting an appetitive CS after LLR choices, possible reasons for this interexperiment difference are discussed.

items.title: Human Development and the Architecture of Everyday Worry: Latent Worry Profiles in the World Risk Poll.
items.abstract: Whether public concern about risk rises or falls with national development has been debated for three decades, but the debate has compared countries hazard by hazard, asking how much people worry rather than how worry is organized. We provide a person-centered analysis of everyday worry at global scale, applying latent class analysis to the six-hazard worry battery of the Lloyd's Register Foundation World Risk Poll and linking profiles to the Human Development Index (HDI) in 140 countries ( n=139,111 ; 2023 wave), with the 2021 wave ( n=118,703 ; 119 countries) as an independent replication. Four worry profiles replicate almost exactly across waves, including a configurationally distinct secure-basics profile (15% of respondents) combining low worry about food and water with high worry about crime, severe weather, and traffic. Profile prevalence is consistent with the ordered sequence predicted by a need-priority account of worry allocation: pervasive worry falls from 33% to 13% between low- and very-high-HDI countries, low worry nearly doubles, and the secure-basics profile holds steady across low- and medium-HDI countries before declining at higher development. Traffic accidents are the most intense worry in every tier below very high HDI. These gradients persist after adjustment for self-reported recent harm and demographic composition and are only partly accounted for by the objective hazard environment, though the cross-sectional design cannot separate development from macroregional clustering. Development is associated with the composition of worry, not only its overall level; risk communication may be better matched to a country's worry architecture than to a single global template.

items.title: The Role of Stress and Resilience Profiles in Emotional Health.
items.abstract: Distal and proximal life stressors, including past trauma, subjective social status, and perceived stress can accumulate over time, placing strain on the body and contributing to increased allostatic load. Consequently, those with heightened stress experiences are at elevated risk of both mental and physical health concerns. However, research suggests that resilience may be a seminal protective factor, often safeguarding against negative health outcomes in the context of stress. Despite the extensive research base in stress and resilience, limited investigations have focused on how they co-occur and shape emotion processes. The current study strives to address these gaps by (1) exploring patterns of distal and proximal stress and resilience and (2) mapping these patterns onto two emotion processes found to have significant influence on health outcomes: emotion regulation and emotionality stigma. A sample of 329 adults (M age = 37.83, SD age = 11.86) were recruited using an online recruitment system and reported on their experiences of distal and proximal stress, resilience, emotion regulation, and emotionality stigma. Participants primarily identified as non-Hispanic (90.2%) and White (77.8%), with a household income of less than $55,000 (52.8%). Using latent profile analysis (LPA), three unique subgroups emerged based on the co-occurrence of distal and proximal stressors with resilience: (1) low stress, high resilience, (2) high proximal stress, low resilience, and (3) high distal stress, moderate resilience. These profiles were significantly associated with emotion processes such that those in the high proximal stress, low resilience profile reported significantly lower emotion regulation than those in the other two profiles. Participants in both higher-stress profiles reported significantly greater emotionality stigma than those in the low stress, high resilience profile. Finding implications for future research and practice are discussed.

items.title: 'I Am a Person Before My Label': Exploring People's Perceptions of Different Discourses Associated With Dyslexia.
items.abstract: Language plays a central role in shaping how dyslexia is understood and negotiated across education, employment and everyday life. While debates have historically focused on diagnosis, less attention has been given to how adults who identify as dyslexic interpret and evaluate the labels applied to them. This article examines dyslexic adults' perceptions of dyslexia-related and neurodiversity movement terminology, drawing on a UK mixed-methods survey of 166 participants who identified as dyslexic, with or without co-occurring neurodivergences. Quantitative findings reveal a clear hierarchy of label preference. Participants strongly favoured dyslexia-specific, identity-based terms such as 'dyslexic', while rejecting broader, deficit-centred labels including 'learning difficulty', 'specific learning disability' and 'specific learning disorder'. Qualitative analysis shows these preferences are shaped by experiences of stigma and misrecognition. The findings show that adoption of a neurodivergent label varies depending on whether participants have single or multiple neurodivergent identities. Those with dyslexia alone expressed greater ambivalence towards the label of neurodiversity. In contrast, dyslexic participants alongside autism or ADHD were more likely to adopt the label. The study highlights the importance of listening to dyslexic voices in debates about terminology. It cautions against deficit-based and overly generalised language which risks reproducing stigma rather than challenging oppression.

items.title: Callous-Unemotional Traits and Aggression: Maternal Parenting as a Developmental Moderator.
items.abstract: Conduct Disorder (CD) is associated with persistent and severe forms of aggression, particularly among youth with callous-unemotional (CU) traits. Although CU traits are linked to proactive aggression, less is known about how environmental factors, such as parenting, shape these associations over time. The present study examined whether maternal and paternal warmth and hostility moderated the longitudinal associations between CU traits and proactive and reactive aggression in adolescents with CD. Participants included 148 youth with CD aged 12-17 years (M age = 15.57, 69% male, 51% African American) assessed at baseline and 6 months. Hierarchical regression models tested moderation effects of maternal and paternal warmth and hostility between CU traits and aggression subtypes while controlling for baseline aggression. Maternal warmth and hostility significantly moderated the association between CU traits and proactive aggression, such that CU traits predicted increases in proactive aggression under conditions of low maternal warmth and high maternal hostility. No significant moderating effects were observed for reactive aggression or paternal parenting. Findings suggest that the influence of CU traits on aggression is context-dependent and varies across aggression subtypes, with maternal parenting playing a key role in shaping the development of proactive aggression. By highlighting the interaction between dispositional traits and caregiving environments, these results refine theoretical models of aggression and identify potential targets for intervention, suggesting that efforts to increase maternal warmth and reduce hostility may help mitigate risk for severe, goal-directed aggression in this high-risk population.

items.title: A systematic review of observational and report-based measures of caregiver sensitivity: A Latin American perspective.
items.abstract: Sensitivity is a cornerstone of early childhood mental health; however, its measurement relies heavily on tools developed in English-speaking, high-resource contexts. This systematic review identified observational and report-based instruments used to assess sensitivity in caregivers of children aged 0-6 years. It evaluated the methodological robustness and usability of these instruments within Latin American contexts. Following a systematic search in Web of Science, Scopus, PsycInfo, and Redalyc, 732 eligible studies were identified. Based on a frequency-of-use threshold, 16 instruments (14 observational and 2 report-based) represented across 616 papers were selected for in-depth evaluation. Measures were coded for theoretical alignment with Ainsworth's sensitivity definition, psychometric evidence, and usability-specifically training accessibility, administration complexity, and evidence of use with diverse Latin American populations (e.g., caregivers in rural settings or with lower educational levels). Results revealed that only a minority of measures adhered explicitly to Ainsworth's original definition. Most instruments prioritized warmth and positive affect, potentially leading to cross-cultural underdetection in contexts where responsiveness is expressed through proximity and routine-based care. While observational tools predominated, report-based measures showed limited validation and minimal regional use. These findings highlight the urgent need for culturally grounded validation and the development of accessible training programs for the region.

items.title: Limitations in the Assessment of Pain Reporting Reliability-Validation of the Focused Analgesia Selection Test.
items.abstract: Background Unreliable pain reporting predicts placebo responses in clinical trials and has been documented in chronic pain populations. The thermal Focused Analgesia Selection Test (FAST) quantifies Pain Reporting Reliability (PRR) by assessing consistency when rating repeated thermal stimuli of varying intensities presented in pseudo-randomized order. However, FAST's validity as a pure measure of reporting reliability remains unclear. Methods We investigated whether PRR derived from the thermal FAST is confounded by individual differences in pain sensitivity (pain and tolerance thresholds), stimuli extending beyond individual pain ranges, and temporal trends. Fifty-five healthy participants (32 women) completed the thermal FAST protocol comprising 49 stimuli across seven temperatures (43°C-50°C). Results Higher pain thresholds predicted lower PRR (b = -4.66, 95% HDI [-9.18, -0.07]). Exploratory analysis suggests that rating variability was reduced when stimulation fell outside individual pain ranges (below-range: b = -8.04, 95% HDI [-11.44, -4.72]; above-range: b = -4.45, 95% HDI [-7.98, -0.90]). Greater coverage of FAST temperatures by individual pain ranges correlated with higher PRR (ρ = 0.33). Thermode repositioning to prevent habituation at the stimulation site may have induced acute sensitization at the repositioned site as pain ratings increased by +33 and +19 VAS points at the first two stimuli following repositioning. Excluding these trials improved median PRR by 16% (from R 2 = 0.65 to 0.81). Conclusions PRR derived from the current thermal FAST implementation likely conflates reporting consistency with pain sensitivity, psychophysical range effects, and procedural artifacts and may therefore risk misclassifying pain phenotypes as reporting inconsistencies. We propose methodological refinements, particularly individualized stimulus calibration and optimized repositioning protocols, which should be evaluated in confirmatory studies and chronic pain populations.

items.title: Validation of the Romanian Version of the Young Positive Schema Questionnaire in the General Population.
items.abstract: Early adaptive schemas (EASs) are a recent extension of schema theory, conceptualized as positive cognitive-emotional patterns that arise when core psychological needs are consistently met during early development. Although early maladaptive schemas (EMSs) have been extensively linked to psychopathology, empirical research on EASs remains comparatively limited. Our study aimed to validate the Young Positive Schema Questionnaire (YPSQ) in a nonclinical Romanian sample (N = 1309). The original 14-factor structure showed excellent fit, the YPSQ subscales demonstrated adequate to good internal consistency, and construct validity was supported by theoretically consistent associations with EMSs, personality traits, psychological well-being, and psychological distress. As hypothesized, EASs were negatively associated with irrational beliefs and positively associated with rational beliefs, extending evidence on the construct validity of EASs to cognitive constructs derived from rational emotive behavior therapy. Exploratory hierarchical regression analyses further indicated that EASs explained additional, although modest, variance in depression, stress, and anxiety beyond EMSs, providing evidence of incremental validity. Overall, the findings support the Romanian YPSQ as a psychometrically sound measure of EASs and reinforce the value of assessing adaptive schemas alongside maladaptive schemas. Further longitudinal and moderation-based research is needed to clarify whether EASs contribute prospectively to resilience or buffer the effects of risk factors on psychological distress.

items.title: Male mice are more susceptible than females to obesity-induced muscle atrophy when fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet.
items.abstract: Obesity-related skeletal muscle atrophy poses a significant health burden, with marked sex differences in this condition. However, the mechanisms underlying these sex differences remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether and to what extent skeletal muscle quality was impaired in C57BL/6 mice fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol (HFHC) diet, focusing on sexual dimorphism. Male and female mice were assigned to control or HFHC groups for 40 weeks. The results showed that both sexes fed the HFHC diet developed obesity and dyslipidemia, with males exhibiting a more severe phenotype. Notably, males experienced more pronounced obesity-induced muscle atrophy than females. This study further revealed that HFHC feeding disrupted physiological homeostasis in both sexes, leading to sexual dimorphism in gut microbial composition and short-chain fatty acid levels, with males displaying a diminished capacity to maintain metabolic homeostasis. Furthermore, males exhibited more severe mitochondrial dysfunction and higher oxidative stress levels compared to females, manifesting as reduced muscle strength and upregulated atrophy-related gene expression. Collectively, these findings indicate that long-term HFHC feeding disrupts gut microbiota and glucolipid metabolic homeostasis, further impairing mitochondrial function and exacerbating muscle atrophy preferentially in males, whereas females are relatively protected through superior maintenance of physiological homeostasis, resulting in milder muscle atrophy.

items.title: Is SARS-CoV-2 Infection (COVID-19) Associated With Congenital Anomalies? A Population Study of Congenital Anomaly Surveillance Data and Maternal SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Wales.
items.abstract: Objectives Explore the relationship between maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection and congenital anomalies in Wales. Study design Mixed observational epidemiological cross-sectional and cohort. Methods Congenital anomaly prevalence data were provided by the Congenital Anomaly Register and Information Service. Two comparisons were made using these data: firstly, congenital anomaly subgroup prevalence prior to and during the pandemic at population level, and in a cohort of women with laboratory-confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with the population trend. Results Prevalence of congenital anomalies in Wales was lower during the pandemic (mean 365 per 10,000 in 2020-22 vs. 454 per 10,000 in 2009-19) showing stable trends. However, the mean for abdominal wall defects increased from 9.8 per 10,000 births between 2009 and 2019 to 13.9 per 10,000 births in 2020-2022, largely attributed to an increase in omphalocele. A cohort of 486 confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infections led to 181 births affected by congenital anomalies, and the trimester of infection did not impact the adjusted odds of this occurring. Circulatory anomalies were most frequently reported, consistent with pre-pandemic population-level data. Urinary and cardiac anomalies were more prevalent in this cohort group than at population level. Conclusions There was no clear evidence at population-level of an association between congenital anomalies and maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection in Wales. However, a potential association with specific congenital anomalies cannot be excluded. Increased omphalocele is consistent with a Europe-wide trend that pre-dated COVID-19. National surveillance registries should remain vigilant.

items.title: Muscle Strength and Outcome Measures for Upper Limb Function in Adults With Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Background Myotonic dystrophy Type 1 (DM1) is a multisystem neuromuscular disorder with progressive distal and proximal weakness, including in the upper limbs. Limited research has been conducted on hand function and outcome measures. Methods Eighty nine adult DM1 participants were included in this cross-sectional study. The study describes upper limb strength and function and examines associations between motor impairments and clinical outcome measures, including comparing strength measurement methods. Disease severity was classified with the muscular impairment rating scale (MIRS) and the Brooke upper extremity scale was used as a classification scale of upper limb function. Muscle strength was measured using handheld dynamometers, and fine motor function with the Nine-Hole Peg Test and Nut and Bolt task. Upper limb function was rated with the Revised Upper Limb Module and global motor function with the Motor Function Measure 32. Patient-reported outcome measures included ABILHAND-NMD, ACTIVLIM, and the Myotonia behavior scale. Results Participants showed a wide spectrum of motor impairment from minimal distal to severe proximal weakness. Strength measures correlated significantly with functional tests, while PROMs reflected perceived limitations but showed ceiling effects. Disease duration correlated with muscle strength and upper limb function, while age and subtype were less important. Myotonia severity showed only weak correlation with functional outcomes. Conclusion No single measure fully captures upper limb function in DM1. A combination of strength testing, dexterity tasks, and PROMs provides a multidimensional assessment framework. Muscle strength assessment remains essential, and these findings support integrating multiple standardized measures for clinical trial endpoints and therapeutic evaluation in DM1.

items.title: Barriers to Proactive Health Management Among Elderly Patients With Coronary Heart Disease in Rural Areas: A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Aim To explore the lived experiences, perceived barriers, and internal unmet needs related to proactive health management among rural elderly patients with coronary heart disease (CHD). Design Descriptive qualitative study. Methods Using purposive maximum variation sampling, we recruited participants from rural elderly inpatients. All subjects were diagnosed with CHD and hospitalized at Shenyang Fourth People's Hospital between May and July 2025. Seventeen eligible participants completed face-to-face interviews lasting 40-60 min each. All interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Inductive descriptive thematic analysis was applied for data coding and to summarize content derived from the interviews. Data collection stopped once data saturation was reached. Results Multiple challenge domains with three main themes encompassing eight subthemes were extracted. First, barriers related to individual cognition and behavioural management, including limited disease awareness and pathogenic misconceptions, poor adherence to health-promoting behaviours, and impaired psychological adaptation; Second, barriers and trust deficits in healthcare system interactions, characterized by conflicts between medical decision-making and livelihood needs, as well as insufficient trust in primary healthcare services; and Third, limited family-social care support, encompassing impaired family caregiving function, disconnection of social support networks, and limited resources for health literacy empowerment. Conclusion Rural elderly patients with CHD self-reported a range of challenges hindering their proactive health management, including cognitive limitations, low trust in primary care, insufficient intergenerational care, and weak community support networks. Age-appropriate health education and county-level remote medical services are proposed as potential strategies to address these self-reported challenges, which may facilitate patients' proactive health engagement, though improvements in patients' long-term quality of life remain to be further investigated. Implications for the profession and/or patient care Nurses caring for rural elderly patients with CHD should provide age-appropriate, simplified health education to counter disease misconceptions and unsafe self-help behaviours, alongside individualized dietary and physical activity guidance. Nurses should identify and relieve patients' fear of acute CHD-related symptom episodes and guilt over burdening their families and offer simplified home-medication-management guidance for patients and their family caregivers. Impact The findings highlight patients' cognitive limitations, real-world family-care circumstances, and negative perceptions of grassroots healthcare as key considerations when delivering proactive health-management support for this population. Patient and public contribution No patients or members of the public were involved in the study design, recruitment, study conduct, interpretation of findings, or manuscript preparation. Reporting method The study report was guided by the COREQ checklist.

items.title: Implementation of a Preoperative Nursing Consultation in Elective Paediatric Surgery: An Implementation Science Perspective.
items.abstract: Aim To analyse the role of standardized protocols and nurse-led preoperative consultations in elective paediatric surgery and the factors influencing their implementation. Design Perspective article guided by the integrated Promoting Action on Research Implementation in Health Services framework. Data sources Structured search of Dialnet, PubMed, SciELO and the Cochrane Library for studies published between 2018 and 2025, conducted between January and March 2025. Of 547 records identified, 40 sources were eligible and 17 inform this article. Conclusion Available studies suggest that non-pharmacological interventions, family involvement and nurse-led preoperative preparation may reduce anxiety and improve the surgical experience. However, implementation remains inconsistent because of workload, limited training and resources and insufficient institutional support. Nurses are well placed to facilitate the translation of evidence into practice, while organizational culture and leadership determine sustainability. Implications for nursing practice Nurses can operationalize preoperative consultations through structured, developmentally appropriate assessment of child and parental anxiety and of pain; child- and family-centered education; non-pharmacological preparation; escalation of high anxiety or pain through agreed referral pathways; and local adaptation of evidence-based protocols with the multidisciplinary team. Impact This article addresses the gap between evidence and practice in paediatric preoperative care. It identifies barriers and facilitators related to the innovation, its recipients, the context and facilitation, and proposes nurse-led implementation strategies that require evaluation. It is relevant to perioperative nurses, managers and policymakers in paediatric surgical services. Reporting method No EQUATOR reporting guideline applies to perspective articles; the literature search is reported in the Methods. Patient or public contribution This perspective article is based on a structured literature search and on theoretical implementation frameworks. No primary data were collected, and no patients, caregivers, service users, or members of the public were involved in the design, conduct, analysis, or preparation of this manuscript.

items.title: Identification of Issues Contributing to Longer Length of Stay and Higher Readmission Rates for Parkinson's Patients Admitted to Hospital.
items.abstract: Background People with Parkinson's disease (PD) are a vulnerable cohort of people, more likely to suffer serious health-related problems when admitted to hospital. Literature suggests that health service improvement utilising a robust health care redesign framework, can improve local service delivery and outcomes for hospitalised PD patients. Aim/objectives This healthcare redesign project aims to identify the issues that contribute to PD patients experiencing a longer length of stay (LOS) and (re)admitting to a tertiary hospital in Sydney, Australia. Quantitative analysis of hospital data previously identified comorbidities present on admission that impact LOS and acquired complications that significantly extend LOS. This paper demonstrates the benefits of utilising mixed methods to provide a comprehensive picture of the PD patient's inpatient experience. Methods Mixed-methods healthcare redesign diagnostic tools were used to gather evidence and understand the issues. Results Seventy-eight percent (n = 831) of PD patients admitted to the emergency department were triage category 1, 2 or 3. 58.5% of PD patients have their PD medications charted within 4 h of admission. Their average LOS was 13 days. Data triangulation identified several barriers to optimal care, with prioritisation activities identifying three high-impact, feasible targets for improvement: PD medication management during nil-by-mouth periods, timely medication charting and timely discharge planning. Root causes (lack of formalised care pathways, limited access to resources and poor coordination of PD services) were identified as contributing to PD patients experiencing a longer LOS and higher readmission rates. Poor communication between clinicians within the hospital, fragmented transitions between hospital and community services and limited access to specialist resources were identified as key system-level barriers requiring prioritisation in the subsequent redesign phase. Conclusions The use of mixed methods provided a rich understanding of the PD patient experience of a hospital admission and prolonged length of stay. This study identified system-level barriers to optimal Parkinson's disease care, providing clear targets for service redesign to improve patient outcomes and hospital efficiency. Addressing gaps in Parkinson's disease medication management, discharge planning and interdisciplinary communication may improve inpatient outcomes, reduce avoidable complications and decrease hospital length of stay and readmissions. Implications for nursing practice Nurses play a critical role in advocating for and leading improvements in the quality, safety and efficiency of care for PD patients. This subsequently improves the PD patient's hospital experience. Nursing practice should focus on prioritising accurate and timely medication management, strengthening communication between clinicians to expedite discharge planning and advocating for PD-specific knowledge and education to improve patient outcomes, reduce length of stay and service efficiencies. Patient and public contribution Patients and members of the public were not involved in the design, conduct, analysis, reporting or dissemination of this healthcare redesign project.

items.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Periodontal Disease: Rethinking Adjunctive Therapy in the Metagenomics Era, the Pressing Need for Precision Treatment and Periodontal Resistome Mapping.
items.abstract: Systemic antibiotics are effective when used as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of periodontitis; however, their use must be balanced against antimicrobial resistance, which is a major threat to global public health. This review provides an expert synthesis of the literature and a field-level overview of antimicrobial resistance in periodontal therapy, highlighting current knowledge and emerging directions, while examining how adjunctive antibiotic protocols may contribute to resistance within the periodontal microbiome through emerging metagenomic insights. To provide this synthesis, the PubMed database was searched for English-language publications using combinations of the terms periodontitis, systemic antibiotics, antimicrobials, resistance, resistome, therapeutic adjuncts, resistance genes, susceptibility, antibacterial and drug resistance, and the findings are presented as a narrative review. The evidence indicates that a substantial proportion of patients with periodontitis harbour subgingival microbiota that are non-susceptible to at least one antibiotic used in periodontal therapy. Across the included studies, antimicrobial resistance was most frequently reported in Prevotella and Porphyromonas species, while some studies also identified virulence-associated factors in Staphylococcus aureus, a non-classical periodontal organism detected within the subgingival microbiota. Overall, current evidence indicates a high prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes in the subgingival microbiota of patients with periodontitis and highlights the ecological consequences of adjunctive antibiotic use. These findings reinforce the need to optimize antibiotic prescribing protocols within an antibiotic stewardship framework and support further metagenomic investigations to refine understanding of resistance patterns, gene-transfer mechanisms and microbiome disruption, with the aim of advancing precision-based periodontal care.

items.title: Bazi Bushen Attenuates Skeletal Muscle Decline Associated With Oestrogen Deficiency and Modulates FGFR1/ERK Signalling.
items.abstract: Postmenopausal oestrogen deficiency is associated with skeletal muscle loss and functional decline, thereby increasing the risk of sarcopenia in women. Considering the safety risks linked to hormone replacement therapy (HRT), alternative strategies are needed to attenuate skeletal muscle decline after menopause. A total of 24 female C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 6 per group): Sham-operated (SHAM), ovariectomized (OVX), OVX treated with estradiol valerate (OVX + E2) and OVX treated with Bazi Bushen (OVX + BZBS). Skeletal muscle mass and function were evaluated in four groups. RNA sequencing was applied to explore the molecular mechanisms and key signalling pathways underlying BZBS-induced muscle protection. We further examined the role of the FGFR1/ERK signalling pathway in mediating the effects of BZBS on myogenic differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts. The results showed that OVX mice had reduced grip strength and skeletal muscle mass, increased fat accumulation, reduced lean mass and impaired metabolic activity. These phenotypic alterations were accompanied by myofiber atrophy, increased collagen staining, endocrine perturbations and elevated expression of p16, p21, Atrogin-1 and MuRF1. BZBS ameliorated these abnormalities. RNA-seq suggested that FGF/MAPK signalling may be involved. In D-gal-treated C2C12 myoblasts, BZBS reduced Atrogin-1 and MuRF1 expression while restoring MYHC and MYOG expression. Mechanistically, BZBS suppressed FGFR1/ERK signalling activation and bFGF partially reversed the protective effects of BZBS. Taken together, these findings suggest that FGFR1/ERK signalling may contribute to the protective effects of BZBS. Our findings provide evidence for the beneficial effects of BZBS on skeletal muscle deterioration associated with oestrogen deficiency.

items.title: Skin-Protective Effects of Marinophyll, a Carotenoid From Marine Erythrobacter sp. SDW2.
items.abstract: Background Previous studies have highlighted that marine organisms, such as microalgae and marine bacteria, exhibit significantly higher and more sustainable biosynthetic yields of unique carotenoids compared to terrestrial sources. These advantages in production efficiency have sparked significant interest in developing materials derived from marine origins. Marinophyll, natural carotenoids extracted from marine sources, have demonstrated potential in managing oxidative stress and inflammation linked to various skin conditions. Materials and methods HaCaT keratinocytes were treated with various concentrations of Marinophyll and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) to assess cell viability and intracellular ROS production. Antioxidant enzyme expression, including Nrf2, HO-1, and SOD2, was evaluated using RT-PCR and immunocytochemistry. The anti-inflammatory effects of Marinophyll were investigated in HaCaT cells treated with IL-4 and Poly I:C, and skin barrier repair was assessed in human skin explants using immunofluorescence staining. The skin explants were obtained from healthy adult donors (aged 43-57 years) undergoing elective breast reduction or abdominoplasty surgery, with informed consent and approval from the relevant ethics committee. All tissues were provided by Seoul National University Bundang Hospital. Results The results showed that Marinophyll reduced intracellular ROS production in H 2 O 2 -exposed HaCaT cells. Additionally, Marinophyll significantly upregulated the mRNA and protein expression of Nrf2, HO-1, and SOD2 in HaCaT cells. Pretreatment with Marinophyll reduced the levels of inflammatory cytokines IL-1α and IL-1β induced by IL-4 and Poly I:C. In human skin explants, Marinophyll enhanced filaggrin expression, contributing to improved skin barrier function. Conclusion Marinophyll demonstrates significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and skin barrier-enhancing properties, making it a promising candidate for therapeutic applications in managing oxidative stress and inflammation-associated skin disorders.

items.title: Plasma Interleukin-10 Levels and IL10 Genetic Variants Are Associated With Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Severe COVID-19 Treated With Corticosteroids.
items.abstract: We aimed to evaluate the association between IL10 variants and plasma IL-10 levels and clinical outcomes in patients with severe COVID-19 treated with corticosteroids. We studied 944 patients with severe COVID-19 who were treated with corticosteroids. The clinical outcomes evaluated were in-hospital mortality and the requirement of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). The variants IL10 rs1800872, rs1554286, rs3024505, and rs3122605 were determined using TaqMan SNP assays, and IL-10 levels were measured by ELISA at the start of corticosteroid treatment (T1) and after 8 days (T2). The rs1800872-TT (p = 0.035, OR = 1.55, 95% CI = 1.03-2.33) and the rs1554286-AA genotypes were associated with IMV (p adj = 0.036, OR = 2.42, 95% CI = 1.12-5.95). IL-10 levels were higher at T1 than at T2. At T2, IL-10 levels were higher in non-survivors (15.9 vs. 7.0 pg/mL, p < 0.001) and in patients requiring IMV (9.9 vs. 5.5 pg/mL, p < 0.001). Among non-survivors, IL-10 plasma levels did not decrease at T2. The alluvial plot revealed that 51.9% of patients in the highest IL-10 tertile at T1 remained in the highest tertile at T2, with a mortality rate of 50%. IL10 rs1800872 and rs1554286 contribute to the risk of requiring IMV. Elevated IL-10 levels after corticosteroid treatment were linked to in-hospital mortality and IMV.

items.title: Biosynthetic Pathways and Regulation of Antibacterial Compounds From Endophytic Fungi: From Chemistry to Genomics and Biotechnology.
items.abstract: Endophytic fungi are non-pathogenic symbionts that represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive secondary metabolites. However, genome-mining studies reveal that most of their biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remain transcriptionally silent under standard laboratory conditions, leaving much of their chemical diversity unexplored. This review examines antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi by integrating three complementary aspects: metabolite chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and strategies for activating cryptic BGCs. Endophytic fungi produce polyketides, non-ribosomal peptides, terpenoids, phenylpropanoid-derived compounds, and hybrid metabolites with antibacterial activities mediated through inhibition of ribosomes, cell wall and membrane biosynthesis, and bacterial resistance mechanisms. Their genomes encode diverse PKS, NRPS, TPS, and hybrid biosynthetic systems, many of which remain cryptic. Advances in chemical elicitation, co-cultivation, epigenetic modulation, CRISPR-based engineering, genome mining, and machine learning are accelerating the activation of silent clusters and the assignment of BGCs to their metabolites. Several fungal metabolites exhibit potent activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including MRSA, and some enhance the efficacy of existing antibiotics. This review highlights current progress, identifies remaining challenges in metabolite production and BGC annotation, and outlines future directions for translating endophytic fungi into a sustainable platform for next-generation antibacterial drug discovery.

items.title: Epigenetic silencing of PDLIM4 promotes colorectal cancer by impairing BTF3 autophagic degradation and activating PI3K/Akt signalling.
items.abstract: Background Epigenetic silencing of tumour suppressor genes is a pivotal early event in colorectal cancer (CRC) pathogenesis. PDZ and LIM Domain 4 (PDLIM4) is a member of the PDZ-LIM family with context-dependent roles in tumour progression across different malignancies. However, its specific role and epigenetic regulation in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain elusive. Methods We integrated multi-omics datasets and clinical cohorts to evaluate PDLIM4 expression and promoter methylation. Stool DNA was analyzed to assess the feasibility of non-invasive detection of PDLIM4 promoter methylation. PDLIM4 knockout and overexpression cell lines were constructed to perform functional assays including proliferation, apoptosis, and stemness. In vivo experiments were validated utilizing xenograft mice or an azoxymethane (AOM)/ dextran sulphate sodium salt (DSS) CRC mouse model with intestinal epithelial cell-specific overexpression of PDLIM4. Mechanistic investigations were conducted using coimmunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry, RNA sequencing, ChIP-qPCR and pharmacological rescue experiments. Results We identified a progressive loss of PDLIM4 protein along the normal-adenoma-carcinoma sequence, driven by DNMT3A-mediated promoter hypermethylation, and lower PDLIM4 expression was associated with adverse patient prognosis. PDLIM4 methylation was also significantly increased in stool DNA from CRC patients compared with healthy controls. Mechanistically, genetic ablation of PDLIM4 significantly blunted the therapeutic efficacy of the DNA demethylating agent 5-Azacytidine against CRC. Functionally, PDLIM4 restoration suppressed CRC cell proliferation and stemness while enhancing apoptosis in vitro, and reduced tumour growth in both AOM/DSS and xenograft models in vivo. At the molecular level, PDLIM4 interacted with BTF3 and promoted its autophagic-lysosomal degradation, thereby limiting PI3K/Akt signalling, with NTRK2 identified as a potential transcriptional target linking BTF3 to PI3K/Akt activation. Conclusion DNMT3A-mediated silencing of PDLIM4 is an early epigenetic event that facilitates CRC progression. PDLIM4 suppresses tumour growth by promoting BTF3 degradation, thereby restricting PI3K/Akt signalling. Thus, PDLIM4 methylation may have potential as a biomarker for early CRC detection. Key points DNMT3A-mediated PDLIM4 promoter hypermethylation is an early event in colorectal tumorigenesis. Restoring PDLIM4 suppresses CRC proliferation and stemness while promoting apoptosis in vitro and in vivo. PDLIM4 promotes the autophagic-lysosomal degradation of BTF3 and restrains PI3K/Akt signalling. Stool DNA analysis supports the potential of PDLIM4 methylation as a non-invasive CRC biomarker.
