items.title: A Six-Day High-Intensity Interval Training Microcycle Improves Selected Indicators of Endurance Performance in Well-Trained Female Cross-Country Skiers and Biathletes.
items.abstract: We compared the effects of a 6-day high-intensity interval training (HIT) microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period (HIT block ) with a time-matched period of continued regular training (REG) on endurance performance in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes. Seventeen athletes (maximal oxygen consumption ( V˙O2max ): 55.1 (5.2) mL·min -1 kg -1 ) were assigned to either HIT block or REG. No differences in training volume or intensity were observed between the groups during the 4 weeks preceding the intervention. During the intervention, HIT block completed five HIT sessions over 6 days (6 × 5-min work intervals; target rate of perceived exertion:17-18), with increased HIT replacing part of their habitual training and thereby reducing overall training load, whereas REG continued habitual training, including 3-4 moderate- or high-intensity interval sessions. Endurance performance was assessed during roller ski skating and included 15-min time-trial average velocity (velocity 15-min ), velocity at 4 mmol·L -1 blood lactate (velocity 4mmol ), and velocity during the final minute of incremental V˙O2max testing ( velocityV˙O2max ). HIT block demonstrated greater improvements than REG in velocityV˙O2max (3.6 (2.1)% versus 1.2 (1.6)%, p = 0.024) and velocity 4mmol (4.4 (2.9)% versus 0.0 (4.4)%, p = 0.023), whereas changes in velocity 15-min did not differ between groups (5.4 (5.0)% versus 1.3 (3.4)%, p = 0.083). An exploratory composite performance index combining these outcomes demonstrated superior improvements in HIT block compared with REG (4.5 (2.8)% versus 0.9 (2.6)%, p = 0.017). These findings indicate that a 6-day HIT microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period is associated with greater improvements in selected endurance performance indicators compared with continued regular training in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes.

items.title: γ-T3 Increases the Sensitization of Gastric Cancer Cells to OXA by a Regulation of ARHGAP29.
items.abstract: γ-Tocotrienol (γ-T3) exhibits potent anti-cancer effects in vitro and in vivo. Our previous study demonstrated that γ-T3 modulates autophagy activity in gastric cancer (GC) cells via the GSK-3β/β-Catenin pathway. In this study, we further explored whether γ-T3 also enhances the chemosensitivity of GC cells to oxaliplatin (OXA) by regulating ARHGAP29, and verified the direct binding between γ-T3 and ARHGAP29 as well as the physical interaction of ARHGAP29 with GSK-3β. We employed cell viability assays, flow cytometry, tumor cell spheroid formation assays, RT-qPCR, Western blot analysis, and stable overexpression transfection. Additionally, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), and chloroquine (CQ) rescue CCK-8 assays were performed for molecular interaction and autophagy function verification; we established a xenografted tumor model using MKN45 cells in BALB/c nude mice (nu/nu). γ-T3 and OXA inhibited GC cell proliferation in vitro and in vivo, with a synergistic effect when combined (CI = 0.55 in MKN45 cells). In a mouse model, intraperitoneal injection of γ-T3 (20 mg/kg b.w.) and OXA (2.0 mg/kg b.w.) suppressed MKN45 cell xenograft growth. This was related to cell cycle arrest and inhibition of cancer stem cells (CSCs). γ-T3 alone or combined with OXA altered autophagy-related protein levels after 48 h treatment, with elevated LC3-II/LC3-I ratio and Beclin1 expression, and reduced p62 abundance, functional rescue with autophagy inhibitor CQ confirmed that the changed autophagy contributes to drug-induced cell death, and this phenotypic change was accompanied by suppressed GSK-3β/β-Catenin pathway activity. ARHGAP29 was inversely correlated with GC prognosis; CETSA results validated the direct intracellular binding between γ-T3 and ARHGAP29, and Co-IP assays confirmed physical interaction between ARHGAP29 and GSK-3β. γ-T3 inhibited the expression of ARHGAP29 at protein and mRNA levels in a time- and dose-dependent manner, whether alone or with OXA. Overexpression of ARHGAP29 reversed the synergistic effects of γ-T3 and OXA in GC cells, further supporting the regulatory linkage between ARHGAP29 and the GSK-3β/β-Catenin axis. The combination of γ-T3 and OXA represents a promising therapeutic strategy to elevate oxaliplatin sensitivity and alter autophagy-related marker expression in GC, at least partially via the ARHGAP29-associated modulation of GSK-3β/β-Catenin signaling.

items.title: Azole-Resistant Aspergillosis: An Emerging Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenge in Paediatrics.
items.abstract: Introduction Invasive aspergillosis (IA) represents one of the most frequent invasive fungal infections in paediatric patients with risk factors. An increase in cases of azole-resistant IA has been reported in adult patients. The aim of this study is to present a series of 11 cases of paediatric patients with this pathology. Methods A retrospective descriptive study including paediatric patients with probable or proven azole-resistant IA treated between January 2019 and June 2024 in four tertiary hospitals in Spain. Results Eleven cases are reported, all patients with risk factors for IA, mainly with haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT) due to haematological malignancies and heart transplant in the early post-transplant period. These patients represent 22% of all proven or probable paediatric IA cases (n = 50) diagnosed in the study centres during the period. Five were previously receiving azole-based antifungal prophylaxis. The most frequently isolated species was Aspergillus fumigatus. Despite receiving at least partially active antifungals plus adjunctive treatment therapy from diagnosis, attributable mortality was high (8/11 patients). Conclusion Azole-resistant IA should be suspected in paediatric patients with risk factors, especially if they show poor clinical course or have received azole prophylaxis. The performance of invasive tests, as well as species identification and resistance testing, is essential to optimise treatment. In breakthrough IA it should be considered empirical treatment with an antifungal from a different class than the one used for prophylaxis, alone or in combination.

items.title: Increased Healthcare Utilization and Differential Outcomes for Pediatric Cancer Versus Non-Cancer Patients.
items.abstract: Background The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM) is a data standard that enables multicenter research. Primary objective was to describe the magnitude of healthcare utilization in pediatric cancer versus non-cancer patients. Secondary objective was to compare 6-month clinical outcomes related to abnormal lab tests and mortality. Methods In this multicenter retrospective study, we included pediatric patients 0-18 years at first medication administration. Cancer patients had a malignant neoplastic disease diagnosis and received chemotherapy. Index date was the first chemotherapy date. Non-cancer patients were assigned analogous index dates based on randomly sampled first medication to chemotherapy intervals. Outcomes were measured within 6 months of index date. Healthcare utilization included encounters, procedures, radiology, lab tests, and medications. Results Among 2810 cancer and 11,240 non-cancer patients, all evaluated healthcare utilization measures were significantly more common in cancer patients. The largest relative differences were observed for long inpatient stay (risk ratio [RR] 26.32, 95% confidence interval [CI] 15.00-46.17), computed tomography (RR 23.59, 95% CI 19.24-28.92), blood culture (RR 37.04, 95% CI 9.58-143.14), and intravenous medication (RR 17.69, 95% CI 8.75-35.75). Death within 6 months was higher for cancer versus non-cancer patients (RR 38.37, 95% CI 12.91-114.04). Conclusions Using the OMOP CDM, we found greater healthcare utilization and worse clinical outcomes among pediatric cancer patients than non-cancer patients, with the largest relative differences observed for inpatient stay, computed tomography, blood culture, and intravenous medication. These findings provide insight into resource utilization patterns and illustrate the OMOP CDM research potential for multicenter studies.

items.title: Genetic Risk, Lifestyle, and Colorectal Cancer Across Age at Onset: A Prospective UK Biobank Study.
items.abstract: Background Polygenic risk scores (PRS) and lifestyle factors are associated with colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether their associations and joint effects vary according to age at CRC onset remains unclear. We evaluated age-related heterogeneity in the associations of genetic risk and lifestyle with CRC and examined their additive interaction in early- and late-onset CRC. Methods We analyzed data from 405,453 cancer-free participants aged 38-73 years at baseline in the UK Biobank. PRS and a healthy lifestyle score (based on eight modifiable factors) were assessed. Age-scale Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for CRC risk by age at onset. Heterogeneity across age intervals was assessed using likelihood ratio tests. Additive interaction was assessed using the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI), and differences in standardized incidence rates were evaluated. Results During a median follow-up of 13.65 years, 6620 CRC cases were identified. Compared with low genetic risk, high genetic risk was associated with HRs of 3.72, 3.32, 2.80, and 2.01 for CRC occurring at ages Conclusions The associations of genetic susceptibility and baseline lifestyle with CRC varied according to age at onset. Positive additive interaction between genetic risk and an unfavorable lifestyle was observed for late-onset but not early-onset CRC. These findings provide further evidence that the relative and joint associations of genetic and lifestyle factors with CRC vary across the life course.

items.title: Pharmacogenomics in Cancer Treatment: Challenges and Opportunities in African Settings.
items.abstract: Background Cancer incidence in Africa is projected to reach 2.1 million new cases annually by 2040. Current treatment guidelines remain largely based on pharmacogenomic data predominantly from European and Asian genetic profiles, potentially compromising safety and efficacy in African patients. However, limited clinical validation data, extreme intra-population genetic diversity, and significant healthcare infrastructure barriers constrain the translational application of pharmacogenomics in Africa. Objective This review critically examines pharmacogenomic variants with established clinical actionability in cancer treatment, focusing on those with differential frequencies or African-specific alleles, and evaluates the evidence base for their implementation in African healthcare settings. Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, PharmGKB, dbSNP, and Google Scholar for peer-reviewed studies reporting pharmacogenomic variants in African or African-ancestry populations relevant to cancer therapeutics. We synthesised evidence from recent African and global studies on pharmacogenomic variants affecting commonly used chemotherapy agents. Results Several variants show marked frequency differences between African-ancestry reference populations and European populations, including DPYD rs115232898 (2.06% vs. 0.00%), CYP2D6*17 (18.76% vs. 0%), and CYP3A5*6 (12.82% vs. 0%). However, many of these estimates derive primarily from African-American datasets and should not be interpreted as representative of continental African populations. African-specific variants such as CYP2D6*17 and DPYD rs115232898 are underrepresented in guideline development datasets. Intra-African genetic diversity is the highest globally, with Khoi-San populations harbouring extensive private variation, suggesting that no single pharmacogenomic panel will be universally applicable across the continent. Conclusion While pharmacogenomics holds substantial promise for personalising cancer treatment in Africa, its current translational readiness is limited by a critical lack of African-specific clinical validation data. Priorities include multi-site validation studies, development of African-enriched genotyping panels, and integration of pharmacogenomic education into oncology practice. Implementation must be accompanied by ethical frameworks ensuring data sovereignty and equitable benefit-sharing.

items.title: Changes in Post-Transplant Vaccine Coverage After Implementing Structured Vaccine Reviews in Pediatric Solid Organ Transplant Recipients in British Columbia, Canada: A Canadian Immunization Research Network Study.
items.abstract: Background Children with solid organ transplants (SOT) are at increased risk of infections but may be under-vaccinated. In 2021, our center implemented structured post-SOT vaccine reviews. We conducted a single-center, pre-post observational study with a repeated cross-sectional design to assess changes in vaccine coverage from 2020 to 2024. Methods We performed a chart review of SOT recipients aged 2-18 years who were ≥ 1 year post-transplant and followed at our clinic on March 1, 2020, and/or March 1, 2024. Patients eligible at both time points (repeat participants) were included in both cohorts; those eligible once (single-time-point participants) were included in the respective cohort. We assessed individual and overall vaccine coverage, defined as receipt of all recommended non-live, non-seasonal vaccines. Comparisons used the chi-square and paired McNemar's test (two-sided p Results Overall vaccine coverage increased from 33% in 2020 to 51% in 2024. The most prominent changes were observed for 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide (PPV23) and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines, with significant improvements among both single-time-point (PPV23: 58%-88%, p Conclusions Structured post-transplant vaccine reviews were associated with an increase in coverage across most vaccines and all organ subgroups, supporting its integration into routine post-transplant care and prospective, multicenter evaluation.

items.title: Huaier Attenuates Renal Injury in Type 2 Diabetic Nephropathy by Ameliorating Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Inhibiting Tubular Epithelial Cell Apoptosis.
items.abstract: Background Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a major microvascular complication of Type 2 diabetes, with renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs) apoptosis playing a pivotal role in its progression. The aqueous extract of Trametes robiniophila Murr. (Huaier) has shown renoprotective effects, but its specific molecular mechanisms in DN remain to be fully elucidated. Objective This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of Huaier aqueous extract on DN and verify whether its anti-apoptotic mechanism is mediated through the Wnt/β-catenin pathway using the pathway activator SKL2001. Methods In vivo, KKAy Type 2 diabetic mice were treated with Huaier (5 g/kg/day) for 12 weeks to evaluate renal function and histopathology. In vitro, HK-2 cells were treated with high glucose and palmitate (HG + PA) to induce injury. The Wnt/β-catenin pathway activator SKL2001 was employed to determine if activating this pathway could abolish the protective effects of Huaier. Results Bioinformatics analysis indicates that the regulation of apoptosis is the primary mechanism by which Huaier improves DN. In vivo, Huaier reduced UACR and improved renal histopathology in KKAy mice. Consistently, TUNEL staining and molecular analysis confirmed that Huaier significantly suppressed RTECs apoptosis within the renal tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that Huaier significantly inhibited HG + PA-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and RTECs apoptosis. Notably, the administration of SKL2001 effectively reversed these protective effects, leading to increased β-catenin expression and elevated apoptosis levels despite Huaier treatment. Conclusion Huaier aqueous extract mitigates RTECs apoptosis and renal injury in Type 2 diabetic nephropathy by suppressing the Wnt5a/β-catenin signaling pathway.

items.title: Six Decades of Pelvic Exenterative Surgery for Gynaecological Malignancies: A Meta-analysis of Indications and Surgical Outcomes in 13,434 Cases Across 29 Countries.
items.abstract: Background/aim Robust international data on pelvic exenteration (PE) are limited. This study aimed to summarise indications, intent, surgical outcomes, morbidity, and mortality of PE for gynaecological malignancies. Materials and methods PubMed was searched from inception to November 2024 (PROSPERO CRD42024615187) following PRISMA guidelines. Data on histology, demographics, body mass index, PE type and intent, prior radiotherapy, resection margins, operative time, hospital stay, and Clavien-Dindo (CD) morbidity/mortality were extracted. Random-effects meta-analysis estimated pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI). Exploratory subgroup analyses compared pre- versus post-2005 studies and regions. Study quality was assessed using MINORS. Results We included 132 studies comprising 13,434 women. Pooled proportions of anterior, posterior, and total PE were 33%, 19%, and 49%, respectively. Indications were cervical (61%), uterine (13%), vulval (13%), and vaginal/other malignancies (17%). PE was performed for recurrent disease in 68%, and negative margins were achieved in 76%. Pooled CD grade I-IV complication rates were 21%, 38%, 28%, and 10%, respectively; 30-day mortality was 5%. From pre- to post-2005 studies, cervical indications declined from 76.1% to 61.0% ( p =0.008), uterine indications increased from 3.0% to 12.4% ( p p p Conclusion PE carries substantial morbidity, while perioperative mortality was approximately 5% overall and 3.7% in post-2005 studies. Given substantial heterogeneity, pooled estimates should be interpreted as broad descriptive summaries rather than universal benchmarks.

items.title: Safety of Multiple Sclerosis Treatments During Pregnancy: An Overview of the EU Regulatory Approach to Risk Management Planning.
items.abstract: Purpose Multiple Sclerosis (MS) may affect women of childbearing age. Information on safety of disease modifying treatment (DMT) in pregnancy is often limited at time of marketing authorisation. We summarised the EU regulatory experience with the implementation and performance of additional pharmacovigilance activities concerning safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding for medicines to treat MS. Methods We reviewed EU risk management plans (RMPs) for centrally authorised MS DMTs to identify additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding. Information was analysed descriptively for type of measure, data collection method and data source. For non-interventional cohort studies and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases, information on current status, planned and actual size and duration was retrieved. Results We identified 17 DMTs that included 21 additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding across 15 RMPs. These comprised nine non-interventional cohort studies and four structured follow-up activities of pregnancy cases that had been started. Of those, three were terminated due to low recruitment with an inclusion rate slower than planned, while inclusion was faster than planned in three finalised activities. Inclusion rate was slowest in primary data collection and faster in secondary analyses and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases. Conclusion Despite efforts to evaluate safety of MS medicines during pregnancy, recruitment and data collection remain challenging. Planning for use of multiple real-world data sources-including primary data collection, secondary use of electronic health records, and analyses of case reports-may help overcome these challenges and strengthen MS drug safety evaluations in pregnancy.

items.title: Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study.
items.abstract: Our objective was to evaluate metformin prescribed at the time of SARS-CoV-2 infection on the risk of developing Long COVID (LC) in electronic health record data. We conducted a new user analysis of metformin prescribed within 6 days of documented infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) versus experimental control: prescription for fluvoxamine, fluticasone, ivermectin, or montelukast. Inclusion criteria a clinic visit in the 0-6 months and the 6-12 months before infection. Exclusion criteria metformin or control within 12 months. Primary outcome LC or death (LC/D), to address death as a competing risk, among patients prescribed drug within Days 0-6 of infection. LC was defined by diagnosis code or computable phenotype. We used entropy balancing to estimate the average treatment effect with a weighted log-linear model. After weighting, there were 248 in the metformin and control groups; the average age was 53 (16); 16% were Black; and 16% were Hispanic. In the primary analysis, 10/248 (4.0%) in the metformin group developed LC/D versus 21/248 (8.5%) in the control group, adjusted risk ratio (aRR) 0.47 (95% CI 0.25-0.89, p = 0.02). For prescriptions on Days 0-1 relative to infection, aRR was 0.39 (95% CI 0.12-1.24); for prescriptions on Days 0-14, the aRR was 0.75 (95% CI 0.52-1.08). In this observational analysis, metformin prescribed within a week of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with a 53% lower risk of LC over 6 months than comparator medications. With the aRR of 0.47 (95% CI 0.25-0.89), any risk reduction between 75% and 11% is highly compatible with our data. This analysis of electronic health record diagnoses is important for the reproducibility of clinical trial results that ascertained the same outcome but via participant-report.

items.title: Prognostic Impact of Late Gadolinium Enhancement on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events and Time-Varying Attenuation of Risk in Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
items.abstract: Objectives To investigate the prognostic value of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patients and characterize the dynamic pattern of its risk effect over time. Methods We retrospectively enrolled patients who underwent Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) between 2020 and 2024, with MACE (cardiac death, heart failure re-hospitalization, or sustained ventricular arrhythmia) as the endpoint. Patients were stratified by MACE occurrence. Schoenfeld residual testing showed borderline deviation of the proportional hazards (PH) assumption for LGE extent (LV mass percentage). Thus, a time-dependent Cox model (Extended Cox PHs Model) with an LGE extent × follow-up time interaction term was built to assess dynamic hazard ratio changes, and independent MACE risk factors were identified. Results Among 173 DCM patients (age 47 ± 15 years, 105 males), 46 (26.6%) experienced MACE after a mean follow-up of 27 ± 16 months. The time-dependent Cox model identified LGE extent (baseline HR: 1.243, 95% CI: 1.162-1.329, p Conclusion LV LGE extent and LVEDVi independently predict MACE in DCM patients. The early prognostic value of LGE extent suggests a critical time window for early fibrosis intervention.

items.title: Prenatal Microarray Incidentally Diagnoses a Novel Inherited NF1 Intragenic Duplication.
items.abstract: Introduction Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) is a well-described autosomal dominant genetic condition with variable expressivity. Most commonly caused by intragenic heterozygous loss of function variants or whole gene deletions in the NF1 gene, there are few documented cases of NF1 due to partial gene duplication. Case summary Here we present the case of a proband with an undisclosed clinical diagnosis of NF1 who had been lost to follow-up as a teenager. She subsequently received a molecular diagnosis of NF1 following prenatal chromosome microarray. Amniocentesis was performed due to a high probability for trisomy 21 on first trimester combined screening and incidentally detected a novel 17q11.2 duplication. RNA analysis confirmed the pathogenicity of this partial gene duplication involving the NF1 gene, but not before the proband conceived a second pregnancy which also carried the 17q11.2 duplication. This resulted in a mother and baby with differing clinical features of NF1. The mother presented in childhood with the more common features of café-au-lait macules, bilateral axillary freckling, and later left forearm subcutaneous lipoma, while her son presented in the neonatal period with the less common isolated tibial pseudoarthrosis. Therefore, this demonstrates intrafamilial phenotypic variability. Contribution This case describes a pathogenic 17q11.2 duplication not previously reported in NF1 literature as well as demonstrating the ongoing importance of referral to a clinical genetics service in the event of any unexpected result on prenatal microarray, and the importance of thorough medical and family history elicitation, pre-test counseling, and informed consent.

items.title: Fungal ADP-ribosylation: an emerging signalling pathway in adaptation and virulence.
items.abstract: ADP-ribosylation is a posttranslational modification conserved across all domains of life and some viruses. While it is well established as a critical signalling mechanism in humans and is widely exploited as a therapeutic target in cancer, its roles in other kingdoms, particularly Fungi, remain poorly understood. Despite this, recent advances highlight the importance of fungal ADP-ribosylation in the regulation of key cellular maintenance processes such as DNA damage and oxidative stress responses, morphogenesis, growth, and proliferation. Here, we summarise our current understanding of fungal ADP-ribosylation and how it supports stress adaptation and virulence. While many aspects of fungal ADP-ribosylation remain unexplored, emerging discoveries underscore its importance in fungal biology and hint at a great potential for future antifungal therapies.

items.title: Association of runoff risk with private well contamination in a fractured dolostone aquifer.
items.abstract: In the United States, private well owners are responsible for monitoring and maintaining their drinking water but have little control over neighboring contamination sources and limited information about daily water quality. Potential for rapid contamination in karst settings exacerbates the challenge. The Runoff Risk Advisory Forecast (RRAF) is a real-time online tool available in five US states that helps nutrient applicators avoid times and locations of high runoff risk. We wanted to determine if RRAF could be repurposed in areas susceptible to groundwater contamination to inform well owners of conditions when contamination is likely. Private wells were repeatedly sampled on seven dates (32-36 wells per date) and analyzed for nitrate-nitrogen, total coliforms, and bovine manure markers. Three-day windows of RRAF risk prior to sampling were selected post hoc, ranging from 1 to 3 days prior for manure markers to 10-12 days prior for nitrate. Contaminants were associated with RRAF values of ≥75% within these windows based on observed weather. A hydrologic association between RRAF risk and groundwater depth was also apparent. Overall, results suggest the RRAF model anticipates conditions of elevated contamination risk for susceptible wells. For nitrate, between-well variation and delayed peak concentration suggested that well location and construction factors may be more informative than runoff events. Microbial contamination was rapid and distributed among wells, with one or more detections of coliforms in 31% of wells and bovine markers in 61% of wells. Thus, a warning system based on the RRAF model could help identify conditions of acute pathogen exposure.

items.title: Preoperative Psychosocial and Spiritual Health and Postoperative Complications After Colorectal Cancer Surgery: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Objective Postoperative complications following colorectal cancer resection remain common despite technical advances, yet associations of psychosocial and spiritual health with surgical risk are poorly characterized. Methods This prospective cohort study enrolled 985 patients undergoing colorectal cancer resection at a single tertiary center (2013-2021). Preoperative assessments included health behaviors (Smart Management Strategy for Health Assessment Tool), self-rated health status (5 Health Status Questionnaire), and health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30). The primary outcome was any complication within 30 days; secondary outcomes were complication subtype (surgical vs. non-surgical) and severity (minor vs. major). Multivariable stepwise logistic regression was performed per outcome. Results Overall, 305 patients (31.0%) experienced at least one complication: 235 surgical (23.9%), 106 non-surgical (10.8%), and 32 major (3.3%). Lower positive-thinking behavior was associated with overall (OR 1.52; 95% CI 1.11-2.07) and minor complications (OR 1.52; 95% CI 1.11-2.09); lower helping-others behavior with surgical complications (OR 2.06; 95% CI 1.27-3.35); and poor spiritual health with non-surgical complications (OR 2.11; 95% CI 1.37-3.26). Preoperative fatigue showed the strongest association with major complications (OR 4.04; 95% CI 1.60-10.21). Conclusions Distinct psychosocial and spiritual health domains were associated with distinct complication subtypes, with preoperative fatigue showing the strongest association with major complications. Whether these reflect modifiable contributors or markers of underlying vulnerability cannot be determined from an observational design; the findings identify patients who may benefit from additional supportive resources rather than a basis for risk stratification.

items.title: High Level of Component C1q Binding Protein (C1QBP) is Associated With Poor Prognosis and Dysfunction of Mast Cells in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Background Component C1q binding protein (C1QBP) is known as an important regulator of mitochondrial plasticity and is involved in antitumor immune response in cancers. Nevertheless, its role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) still remains largely unknown. Methods C1QBP expression in LUAD and adjacent normal samples was compared by Wilcoxon test, and the corresponding receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to estimate its diagnostic value. Associations between C1QBP expression levels and different clinical traits were analyzed by chi-square test; K-M curves were applied for analyzing survival differences, and univariate and multivariate Cox analysis were employed to construct the C1QBP-related nomogram model. Furthermore, GSEA and immune analysis were performed to explore the mechanism. Finally, rhC1QBP was applied to cultured mast cells in vivo to investigate its regulatory effect on mast cell dysfunction, and sh-C1QBP was injected into LUAD xenograft mice to explore the effect of C1QBP knockdown on tumor growth in vivo. Results The C1QBP expression level, with a preferable diagnosis effect, was significantly different between LUAD and normal samples, and was notably interrelated with gender, TNM stage, and Fustat in LUAD patients. LUAD patients with high C1QBP levels displayed lower survival rates. Our nomogram based on C1QBP expression and T stage displayed decent prediction capability. There was a significant difference in C1QBP expression in plasma cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), activated CD4 memory T cells, resting mast cells, and eosinophils between LUAD patients and the controls. Upregulation of C1QBP with rhC1QBP treatment promoted mast cell ferroptosis through interacting with the Cullin3 protein. While Fer-1, a ferroptosis inhibitor, counteracted rhC1QBP induced ferroptosis in mast cells. Knockdown of C1QBP inhibited tumor growth in xenograft mice. Conclusion C1QBP may be a promising potential prognostic biomarker in LUAD and a potential therapeutic target by affecting the immune microenvironment of LUAD patients.

items.title: SU5, a Stable Auraptene Analog, Ameliorates Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis Through Modulation of the FXR Signaling Pathway.
items.abstract: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH), a metabolic liver disease severely threatening public health, is characterized by hepatic steatosis, inflammatory infiltration, and fibrotic progression. Currently, there is still a lack of specific therapeutic approaches for MASH in clinical practice. Auraptene (AUR), a natural citrus-derived compound with demonstrated therapeutic potential against MASH, is limited in clinical translation by poor metabolic stability. To address this challenge, we evaluated the effects and mechanisms of SU5, a novel auraptene analog engineered for enhanced metabolic stability, in a MASH mouse model induced by a high-fat/high-sugar diet combined with carbon tetrachloride (CCl 4 ). SU5 treatment effectively reduced hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis in MASH mice. It activated the FXR pathway, regulating bile acid metabolism-related genes. SU5 also suppressed lipogenic genes, decreased inflammatory factors, and restored lipid homeostasis. Outperforming auraptene, SU5 is a promising MASH treatment option due to its enhanced stability.

items.title: Hollow Convective Carrier Design Enhances Biofilm Retention and Mass Transfer for Improved Nitrification Performance.
items.abstract: This study developed a novel carrier configuration (i.e., hollow convective carrier [HCC]) to enhance biofilm retention and mass transfer in biofilm-based wastewater treatment. The HCC was fabricated by stitching two layers of permeable nylon mesh to form internal hollow compartments, enabling biofilms to grow within protected spaces while maintaining diffusive and convective transport. Long-term reactor operation showed that HCC-based pure biofilm systems achieved faster start-up and better performance than single-layer convective carriers (CCs) and commercial polyethylene carriers (PEK5). The superior performance was mainly attributed to the improved biomass accumulation and mass transfer. HCC-based reactor exhibited higher biofilm densities (2.4-4.1 g/m 2 ) than CC (1.6 g/m 2 ) and PEK5 (0.6 g/m 2 ) carriers. Biofilms on the surface and inside the hollow compartments of HCC carriers had high nitrification activity and also accumulated more slowly-growing bacteria of Nitrospira than CC and PEK5 carriers. Nitrate tracer experiments confirmed that substrates could penetrate the thick convective biofilms on HCC carriers, with a mass transfer flux of 61.3 mg-N/(m 2 h) and overall mass transfer coefficient of 1.58 × 10 -6 m/s. Both mass transfer flux and overall coefficient in convective biofilms increased linearly with mixing intensity, supporting the role of convective transport in alleviating diffusion limitations. Overall, the hollow convective design integrates enhanced biofilm retention with improved substrate accessibility, providing a promising carrier strategy for stable and efficient treatment in biofilm reactors.

items.title: LncRNA A1BGAS1 Serves as a Tumor Suppressor in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Modulating the Expression of miR-3942-5P.
items.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the leading contributor to global cancer mortality, is associated with a notably unfavorable prognosis. This study aims to explore the regulatory interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p and its molecular mechanisms. The level of A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p in both tumor tissues and cell lines (BEAS-2B, A549, H226) were measured using qPCR. Functional effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression in NSCLC cells were evaluated through CCK-8, flow cytometry, and Transwell assays. The interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p was validated through dual-luciferase reporter assays and rescue studies. A1BG-AS1 expression was markedly reduced in both NSCLC tissues and cell lines. A1BG-AS1 expression was significantly associated with various clinical parameters. Overexpression of A1BG-AS1 suppressed NSCLC cell function. Mechanistically, A1BG-AS1 interacted with and negatively regulated miR-3942-5p, and the antitumor effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression were reversed by miR-3942-5p mimics.A1BG-AS1 inhibits NSCLC tumor progression by targeting miR-3942-5p.

items.title: Pan-Cancer Landscape of TMEM9 With Experimental Validation in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Background Transmembrane protein 9 (TMEM9) has been implicated in tumor progression, but its pan-cancer diagnostic, prognostic, and immunological relevance remains incompletely characterized. Methods TMEM9 expression, diagnostic and prognostic value, genetic alterations, functional states, and immune associations were systematically evaluated using TCGA, GTEx, and complementary public cancer databases. Experimental validation was primarily performed in HNSC models using Western blotting, colony-formation, wound-healing, Transwell, and xenograft assays, with additional exploratory validation in RCC models. Results TMEM9 showed good-to-high diagnostic performance in 15 evaluable cancer cohorts, with particularly high AUCs in CHOL (1.000), KICH (0.970), LIHC (0.949), and THYM (0.925), whereas BRCA also showed strong discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.890). Higher TMEM9 expression was associated with unfavorable survival in several cancers, although its prognostic relevance varied by tumor type. TMEM9 expression was also associated with cancer-related pathways, functional states, immune cell infiltration, and immunoregulatory gene expression in a context-dependent manner. Experimentally, TMEM9 knockdown suppressed colony formation, wound closure, migration, and invasion in HNSC cells and inhibited FaDu xenograft growth. Similar inhibitory effects were additionally observed in exploratory RCC models. Conclusion TMEM9 exhibits cancer-type-dependent diagnostic, prognostic, and immunological associations, whereas functional experiments support a tumor-promoting role for TMEM9 in HNSC. Exploratory RCC experiments suggest that this effect may also occur in selected renal cancer cellular contexts.

items.title: METTL7B-Mediated m6A Modification of PLEKHA4 Suppresses Ferroptosis via Reducing AURKA Ubiquitination to Promote Papillary Thyroid Cancer Progression.
items.abstract: The malignant progression of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is closely associated with the acquisition of ferroptosis resistance by tumor cells; however, the upstream regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aims to elucidate the function and molecular mechanisms of the methyltransferase-like 7B (METTL7B)/pleckstrin homology domain-containing family A member 4 (PLEKHA4)/aurora kinase A (AURKA) signaling axis in ferroptosis resistance in PTC. Our results showed that PLEKHA4 was highly expressed in PTC. By binding to kelch-like protein 12 (KLHL12), PLEKHA4 inhibited KLHL12-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of AURKA, thereby stabilizing the AURKA protein and enhancing ferroptosis resistance in PTC cells. Upstream, METTL7B stabilized PLEKHA4 mRNA and upregulated its expression through N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed that knockdown of METTL7B increased ferroptosis sensitivity and suppressed PTC progression. This study reveals a novel paradigm in which PLEKHA4, as an effector of m6A modification, regulates ferroptosis by interfering with ubiquitin-mediated degradation, providing a theoretical basis for targeting this pathway in the treatment of PTC.

items.title: Development of Highly Efficient Lysosome-Targeting Peptide Ligands for the Internalization of Extracellular Proteins.
items.abstract: Lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) induce the internalization of extracellular and membrane-associated proteins by routing them to lysosomes via endogenous receptors, such as the insulin-like growth factor-2 receptor (IGF2R), also known as cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor. While current IGF2R ligands are effective, expanding the LYTAC toolkit with structurally simple and synthetically accessible ligands remains a practical necessity. Here, we first validated that previously reported dimeric and monomeric peptides induce robust internalization, establishing them as effective IGF2R-targeting LYTAC ligands. To further optimize the peptide architecture, we performed systematic mutational scanning on its monomeric sequence to simplify the peptide architecture. We identified the L4 variant, which features a single leucine substitution at the fourth position. This optimized monomer induces greater internalization efficiency than the previously reported wild-type monomeric peptide ligand. To demonstrate its utility, we conjugated the L4 recruiter to a specific PCSK9 binder. The resulting bifunctional molecule successfully induced the dose- and time-dependent internalization of PCSK9. Collectively, these findings establish several peptide variants as practical and highly effective building blocks for the development of extracellular protein internalization platforms.

items.title: Sequential Associations of Sleep Architecture, Nocturnal Oxygenation, and Respiratory Disturbance With a Composite PSG-Derived Rhythm-Event Index.
items.abstract: Background Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), particularly obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), has been associated with cardiovascular complications including cardiac arrhythmias. However, the relative contributions of respiratory, oxygenation, and sleep architecture indices to composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index remain incompletely understood. Objective To investigate the sequential associations of sleep architecture, nocturnal oxygenation, and respiratory disturbance indices with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index in patients undergoing polysomnography (PSG). Methods Demographic, respiratory, oxygenation and sleep-architecture variables were extracted from PSG records. The primary outcome was a composite PSG-derived rhythm-event count, estimated as round(arrhythmia index × TST_hours) from the PSG-exported arrhythmia index, which was calculated during total sleep time only. Negative binomial regression used an offset of log(TST_hours). Because the outcome demonstrated overdispersion, negative binomial regression with an offset of log(TST hours) was used. Because the original 14-predictor model was over-parameterized for the sample size, a six-predictor model (age, sex, BMI, AHI, T90, and sleep efficiency) was chosen post hoc. This reduced model was not prespecified before the original analysis. Sleep efficiency was retained because it showed a strong signal in the exploratory 14-predictor model. The resulting p-values should therefore be interpreted as optimistic and exploratory. A sequential model-building approach (Model 1: age, sex, BMI, AHI; Model 2: plus T90; Model 3: plus sleep efficiency) was used to document the incremental contribution of each domain. A fully adjusted 14-predictor model was fitted only as a supplementary analysis. Wald 95% CIs and bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (2000 resamples) are reported. Results Forty-one participants were included (mean age 47.8 ± 13.5 years; median BMI 29.4 kg/m 2 ). Severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30 events/hour) was present in 56.1%. Median arrhythmia index was 3.2 events/hour, with marked overdispersion. In the six-predictor model, only higher sleep efficiency was associated with lower arrhythmia rate (IRR = 0.946 per 1 percentage-point increase, 95% CI 0.921-0.972, p Conclusion In this exploratory selected sleep-center cohort, AHI and other respiratory-event indices were not independently associated with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index. Only higher sleep efficiency showed a robust association with lower arrhythmia rate, but this finding is hypothesis-generating and may reflect unmeasured confounding. These results require confirmation in larger prospective studies and should not guide clinical risk stratification.

items.title: "Life and Lower Limb Threatening Condition" Clinical Features, Management and Outcomes of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Complicated by Gas Gangrene: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a common complication of diabetes in low- and middle-income countries and may be complicated by gas gangrene (GG), a rapidly progressive, life-threatening infection. This prospective study assessed whether GG can be diagnosed clinically in low-resource primary care and explored factors associated with wound-healing outcomes in DFU complicated by GG. From December 2021 to June 2025, consecutive patients with diabetic foot infection and clinically active GG were enrolled. Data included demographics, ulcer history and examination, SINBAD classification, GG signs, sepsis status, comorbidities, management, and outcomes. All participants had classical clinical features of GG and were admitted for urgent surgical treatment. Ninety-nine patients (58 male) with classical GG were admitted for urgent surgery. Initial amputation was required in 18% (major 12%, minor 6%). Ten patients were lost to follow-up; that included six who died from foot-ulcer-related causes. Of 89 followed, 30 (33.7%) healed in 225.5 ± 126.9 days, while 59 remained unhealed after 146.1 ± 175.4 days; major amputations during treatment were more frequent in the healed group. Having a previous history of ulcer showed to increase the time to heal by 136 days. A one-day increase in treatment duration was associated with a 1% decrease in both the chance of healing or risk of amputation. Early diagnosis, aggressive medical and surgical intervention are the keys to decreasing morbidity and mortality of diabetic patients with gas gangrene; and remain the mainstay treatment of this dangerous condition globally. Patient's with previous ulcer history were found to need longer time to heal. Increasing treatment duration seems to be a double-edged sword, as while it is associated with reduced risk of amputation, it also decreases the chance of ulcer healing.

items.title: Two-Stage Estimation for Causal Inference Involving Semi-Continuous Exposures.
items.abstract: Methods for causal inference are well developed for binary and continuous exposures, but in many settings, the exposure has a substantial mass at zero-such exposures are called semi-continuous. We propose a general causal framework for such semi-continuous exposures, together with a two-stage estimation strategy. A two-part propensity structure is introduced for the semi-continuous exposure, with one component for exposure status (exposed vs unexposed) and another for the exposure level among those exposed, and incorporates both into a marginal structural model that disentangles the effects of exposure status and dose. The two-stage procedure sequentially targets the causal dose-response among exposed individuals and the causal effect of exposure status at a reference dose, allowing flexibility in the choice of propensity score methods in the second stage. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the resulting estimators, and characterize their limiting values under misspecification of the propensity score models. Simulation studies evaluate finite sample performance and robustness, and an application to a study of prenatal alcohol exposure and child cognition demonstrates how the proposed methods can be used to address a range of scientific questions about both exposure status and exposure intensity.

items.title: Quercetin activates lysosomal function to ameliorate neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits in chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
items.abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH) is a major contributor to vascular cognitive impairment (VCI), often resulting in progressive learning and memory deficits. Quercetin (Qu), a natural flavonoid with potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, demonstrates neuroprotective potential against ischemic injury, yet its mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. In this study, a rat model of CCH was established by bilateral common carotid artery occlusion, followed by Qu administration at doses of 20, 40, and 80 mg·kg -1 . In parallel, HT22 cells subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) were treated with Qu at 5, 10, or 20 μmol·L -1 . Behavioral tests, histological staining, ELISA, and Western blot were used to assess cognitive performance, neuronal injury, lysosomal activity, NF-κB pathway activation, and inflammatory cytokine levels. Hippocampal RNA sequencing was also performed. Our results demonstrate that Qu greatly improved cognitive performance and attenuated neuronal damage in both the cerebral cortex and hippocampus. Mechanistically, Qu improved lysosomal function and suppressed NF-κB-mediated neuroinflammatory response, leading to less production of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Notably, co-administration of a lysosomal inhibitor attenuated the neuroprotective effects of Qu, underscoring the functional importance of lysosomal activation. In conclusion, Qu alleviates CCH-induced cognitive decline and neurodegeneration by restoring lysosomal function and inhibiting NF-κB-driven neuroinflammation. These findings support the therapeutic potential of Qu for VCI and provide a rationale for its further development as a neuroprotective agent.

items.title: Artemisinin derived from Artemisia annua L. promotes thrombopoiesis via targeting FLT3: a novel strategy for thrombocytopenia management.
items.abstract: Artemisia annua L. (A. annua) has long been documented in traditional Chinese medicine for managing hemorrhagic conditions, attributed to its cooling and hemostatic properties. These historical applications suggest a potential role of A. annua in platelet-related disorders, although its hematopoietic mechanisms remain unclear. To investigate the thrombopoietic activity of A. annua, identify its bioactive constituent, and elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects on thrombopoiesis. Chemical profiling identified major compounds in A. annua. MK differentiation was assessed in K562, Meg-01 cells, and primary murine haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). A murine radiation-induced thrombocytopenia (RIT) model was used to evaluate in vivo efficacy. Molecular docking, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and signaling assays were conducted to explore molecular mechanisms. A. annua promoted MK differentiation, upregulating CD41/CD42b and enhancing polyploidization. Artemisinin was identified as the principal active compound. It promoted MK maturation in vitro and restored platelet counts, MK numbers, and HSPC populations in RIT mice without inducing systemic toxicity. Artemisinin also reduced bone marrow (BM) apoptosis and DNA damage while restoring platelet function. Mechanistically, artemisinin directly bound to FLT3 and activated the FLT3/MAPK pathway, leading to increased phosphorylation of MEK/ERK and upregulation of NF-E2 and TAL1. FLT3 and ERK inhibition abrogated these effects. Artemisinin is a potent thrombopoietic agent that acts via direct activation of FLT3 and its downstream MAPK signaling cascade. The findings identify FLT3 as a novel therapeutic target for thrombocytopenia and support the potential clinical application of artemisinin in radiation-related hematological disorders.

items.title: Improving the physician-patient relationship through timely caring services in Taiwan's no-fault childbirth compensation system.
items.abstract: Objective Malpractice pressure in obstetrics contributes to clinician burnout, defensive practice, and declining participation in high-risk maternity care. Taiwan's Childbirth Accident Emergency Relief Act (CAERA) integrates a national no-fault compensation system with mandated caring services, including early communication, emotional support, and administrative assistance after childbirth-related adverse events. This study is to evaluate the timeliness, content, and perceived effectiveness of caring services under CAERA and their association with patient satisfaction and physician-patient relationships. Materials and methods This cross-sectional study analyzed nationwide survey data from compensated families and medical institutions following childbirth-related adverse events. Perceptions of caring service timing and content were compared between patients and providers. Associations between service timeliness and satisfaction outcomes were examined using standard statistical methods. Results A total of 1345 family and 1074 institutional responses were analyzed. Substantial perception gaps were identified. Only 38.6% of families reported receiving caring services within 2 days, compared with 82.4% of institutions. Families also reported lower rates of communication (44.0% vs 81.4%), procedural assistance (69.7% vs 93.6%), and emotional support (62.2% vs 95.0%) than providers reported delivering (all P Conclusion Substantial gaps exist between provider-reported and patient-perceived caring services. Early engagement is associated with higher satisfaction and stronger physician-patient relationships. These findings suggest that the success of no-fault systems depends not only on financial compensation but also on prompt caring services.

items.title: A Comparative Analysis of Deaths Due to Drug-Related Causes Between Rural and Urban Areas in the United Kingdom, 1997-2026.
items.abstract: Introduction Multiple jurisdictions report disproportionately elevated rates of drug-related harm in urban settings, alongside unique treatment needs in rural populations. We examined differences in case characteristics, circumstances of death and implicated drugs among individuals dying from drug-related causes, stratified by rural or urban setting, and determined changes in the proportion of deaths between settings over time. Methods Retrospective registry-based analysis of coronial records of individuals who died from drug-related causes, submitted to the National Programme on Substance Use Mortality in the UK, 1997-2026. UK Government Rural-Urban Classification methodology dichotomised cases using postcode at date of death. Results Overall, 39,975 decedents died, 36,350 (90.9%) in urban settings. The urban percentage decreased significantly over the study period from 96.6% in 1999 to 92.3% in 2025 (AAPC -0.34%, 95% CI -0.47% to -0.15%, p = 0.002). Accidental poisoning was the most common direct cause of death in both rural (45.5%) and urban (54.8%) settings, while intentional self-poisoning was more common rurally (17.3% vs. 9.5%). Opioids were the most frequently implicated drug group in both rural (61.1%) and urban (65.4%) settings. The median number of drugs implicated did not differ significantly between settings (both 2, IQR 1-3), but rural decedents had a significantly higher median number of prescribed implicated drugs (1, IQR 0-2 vs. 0, IQR 0-2). Discussion and conclusions Over three decades, approximately one in 11 UK drug-related deaths occurred rurally. Intentional self-poisoning was substantially more common in rural fatalities, and opioids were the leading implicated drug group across both settings.

items.title: The present and future of HIV and viral hepatitis co-infection.
items.abstract: HIV and hepatitis virus co-infection remains a major global health challenge, driven by shared transmission routes, populations with overlapping modes of acquisition, and potentially compounded disease progression. Co-infections of HIV and hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) remain prevalent, particularly among people who live in endemic areas, key populations, people who inject drugs, men who have sex with men, and migrants from endemic regions. Antiretroviral therapy is shifting towards regimens without HBV activity, increasing the risk for HBV infection or reactivation in some individuals. Although direct-acting antivirals have reduced active HCV infection considerably in many high-income settings, residual disease burden, reinfections, and inequitable access to treatment persist. Hepatitis delta virus continues to represent a severe but underdiagnosed co-infection among individuals with HIV-HBV co-infection, with insufficient global surveillance data. Acute hepatitis A and E increasingly affect people with HIV, presenting both as outbreak-related and sporadic cases, particularly in the context of suboptimal vaccination coverage. Contemporary management emphasises systematic screening, vaccination, integrated antiviral strategies, and public health interventions to reduce liver-related morbidity and mortality in people with HIV.

items.title: Interfacility Variation in Diagnosis and Tocolysis for Threatened Preterm Labor and Its Association With Gestational Age Threshold for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Perinatal Centers in the Chugoku-Shikoku Region of Western Japan.
items.abstract: Aim To describe interfacility variation in threatened preterm labor (TPL) management in a perinatal care network in western Japan and the association between the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission threshold and the long-term tocolysis policy. Methods A cross-sectional, facility-level questionnaire survey was conducted for all 43 perinatal maternal and child health centers in the Chugoku-Shikoku region of western Japan in 2024. Centers reported diagnostic criteria for TPL, use of objective scoring systems, first-line intravenous tocolytic drugs, NICU admission gestational age threshold, and institutional policies regarding planned duration of intravenous tocolysis (short-term, ≤ 48 h; long-term, > 48 h). Factors related to the adoption of long-term tocolysis were evaluated using logistic regression. Results Valid responses were obtained from 32 centers (74.4%). A long-term-only tocolysis policy was reported by 65.6% (21/32) of centers. Diagnostic criteria and thresholds for intervention varied widely, and only three centers (9.4%) used an objective severity score, such as the preterm labor index or tocolysis index. Ritodrine hydrochloride was used as the first-line intravenous tocolytic drug in 93.8% (30/32) of centers. The NICU admission threshold differed among centers. In multivariable analysis, centers with a higher NICU admission threshold were more likely to report a long-term-only policy (adjusted odds ratio, 1.38 per 1-week increase; 95% confidence interval, 1.04-1.83; p = 0.028). Conclusions Management of TPL showed marked interfacility variation in the regional perinatal care network. The NICU admission threshold was associated with the institutional tocolysis-duration policy, suggesting that regional perinatal system structure should be considered when discussing optimal tocolysis duration.

items.title: A Large Language Model-Guided Q-Learning Method for Food Safety Sampling Decision-Making.
items.abstract: Food safety sampling is a critical measure for safeguarding public health; however, current regulatory practices are challenged by fragmented risk signals, constrained inspection resources, and suboptimal inspection efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a food safety sampling decision-making method based on large language models (LLM)-guided Q-learning. First, we leverage LLMs to extract and analyze key elements from unstructured online food safety public opinion data. This is integrated with clustering analysis and the entropy weight method to achieve quantitative risk assessment and grading. Subsequently, a food category-region risk score matrix is constructed, and the allocation of sampling frequency is formalized as a sequential decision-making problem under resource constraints. Q-learning is then introduced to learn optimal sampling strategies, using LLM-generated structured heuristic values as prior guidance, thereby reducing ineffective exploration and enhancing training efficiency. Experimental results, based on data from 30 provincial administrative regions, 457 municipalities/counties, and 25 food categories, generated 4690 risk evaluation records as effective inputs for decision-making. The results demonstrate that the derived sampling strategies align with risk priors, allocating higher sampling intensity to high-risk food category-region combinations while maintaining coverage balance across food categories and regions. Compared to the baseline without heuristic guidance, LLM guidance significantly reduces convergence iterations while maintaining steady-state rewards. This indicates that the proposed method accelerates policy learning without compromising long-term returns. In conclusion, this study validates that the proposed method achieves a closed-loop integration of risk assessment and decision optimization, providing a data-driven methodology for intelligent food safety regulation.

items.title: Toward a digital urinary biopsy for early risk stratification in diabetic kidney disease: Anchoring shed cells, vesicles, and cell-free DNA to spatial kidney cell states.
items.abstract: Background Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of end-stage kidney disease worldwide. However, albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), which define and stage DKD, report established injury and do not resolve the cellular heterogeneity underlying variable progression. Urine, the only biofluid to traverse every nephron segment, carries shed cells, extracellular vesicles (EVs) and cell-free DNA (cfDNA), each retaining information about its cell of origin. Main body This review develops the concept of a digital urinary biopsy, in which the three compartments are read together against spatial single-cell kidney atlases to infer non-invasively which cell states are active and whether niche-associated programs are engaged, an approach we term atlas-anchored molecular profiling. For each compartment, we tabulate study population, sample size, processing, assay, performance and validation status. Because shed-cell RNA, selectively sorted vesicle cargo and cfDNA methylation differ in origin, measurement scale and bias, each requires its own reference matrix, sampling function and background terms. All three carry renal information in feasibility studies, yet none is a validated clinical assay in DKD. Moreover, a cfDNA methylation reference at the required resolution is lacking, and no named computational method has been tested on urine. Conclusion We therefore present the framework as a structured research hypothesis and define the required validation, from analytical and clinical validity to prospective demonstration of utility, with non-albuminuric DKD, which albuminuria-based screening misses, as the index use case. It offers a testable route to cell-resolved, non-invasive staging of DKD rather than a demonstrated capability.

items.title: The hazard of fluency: a framework for governing AI liability in organizational decision-making
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence transitions from numerical, discriminative algorithms to fluent Large Language Models (LLMs), human-machine interaction faces a profound paradigm shift.Historically, users exhibited algorithm aversion toward classical opaque systems.Nowadays, the conversational fluency of generative AI has triggered an opposing crisis: uncritical overreliance, frequently resulting in the CHOKE phenomenon (Certain Hallucinations Overriding Known Evidence).This paper argues that treating algorithmic trust as a linear metric linked to transparency to be maximized via Explainable AI (XAI) is fundamentally incomplete.Specifically, in highly conversational systems, unchecked trust becomes a severe organizational vulnerability.To address this, we propose a 3D Trust Calibration Framework, a multidisciplinary model that maps three dimensions of interaction: System Modality (Analytical vs Conversational), Decision Stakes (Low vs High), and Organisational AI Governance (Frictionless vs Structured).Drawing on Cognitive Psychology and Agency Theory, we deconstruct how in working environments conversational fluency of AI systems drives employees to engage in "unseen sub-delegation", treating the LLM as a shadow agent.This creates a severe governance hazard for the organization: while the employee minimizes their cognitive effort and acts as a superficial liability buffer, the organization unknowingly absorbs the reputational, legal, and operational consequences of algorithmic failures.Moving beyond purely technical paradigms of AI transparency, our theoretical framework establishes a new architectural ontology of trust and AI governance in modern organisations, providing a structural blueprint for designing accountable, friction-positive decision workflows.

items.title: Creator Type, Content Format, and Engagement Among Highly Liked Cancer-Related TikTok Search Results: A Cross-Sectional Content Analysis.
items.abstract: Background Engagement differences by creator type among highly liked cancer-related TikTok videos remain unclear. Methods We analyzed 250 videos from five cancer searches, selecting the first 50 results per search filtered to the preceding six months and sorted by likes. Health professionals or trainees were classified as medical. The primary analysis modeled log-transformed views by creator type, adjusting for followers, video age, content type, and cancer search. Results Adjusted views showed no significant difference (ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.44-1.85; p = 0.773). Medical creators had a higher adjusted share rate (ratio, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.24-3.24; Holm-adjusted p = 0.026). Median views per follower were lower for medical creators (2.55 vs. 16.40; ratio, 0.16; 95% CI, 0.06-0.45; Holm-adjusted p = 0.003). Conclusions Despite no clear difference in absolute views, lower views per follower raise the possibility that medical creators have more limited reach beyond established audiences than nonmedical creators, while greater sharing may broaden distribution.

items.title: Association Between Intolerance of Uncertainty and Coping Behaviours Among Pregnant Women With Fear of Childbirth: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Aims This study aimed to explore the associations among intolerance of uncertainty, childbirth self-efficacy, fear of childbirth, and coping styles among primiparous women. Design A cross-sectional study. Methods This study performed subgroup analysis based on a parent cohort of 532 primiparous women established from October 2022 to November 2023. A total of 294 pregnant women with fear of childbirth were selected from this cohort as participants. Participants completed the Childbirth Attitude Questionnaire (CAQ), Revised Prenatal Coping Inventory (NuPCI), Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-9 (IUS-9), Childbirth Self-Efficacy Inventory (CBSEI-C32), and a sociodemographic data sheet. Kruskal-Wallis tests and Mann-Whitney U tests were used to analyse differences in prenatal coping scores across demographic characteristics. Spearman correlation analysis was used to examine the relationships among fear of childbirth, intolerance of uncertainty, childbirth self-efficacy, and prenatal coping. Finally, Mplus 8.3 was used to test the mediating roles of fear of childbirth and childbirth self-efficacy in the relationship between intolerance of uncertainty and prenatal coping. Results Structural equation modelling showed that intolerance of uncertainty was positively associated with avoidance coping (B = 0.202, β = 0.228, 95% CI [0.068, 0.355]), with fear of childbirth mediating the relationship between intolerance of uncertainty and avoidance coping (B = 0.186, β = 0.210, 95% CI [0.132, 0.314]). Intolerance of uncertainty was not directly associated with planning-preparation coping but was indirectly negatively associated with planning-preparation coping through fear of childbirth and childbirth self-efficacy (B = -0.042, β = -0.040, 95% CI [-0.093, -0.014]). Intolerance of uncertainty was not directly associated with spiritual-positive coping but was indirectly positively associated with spiritual-positive coping through fear of childbirth (B = 0.033, β = 0.088, 95% CI [0.009, 0.181]). Conclusions No direct association was observed between intolerance of uncertainty and either planning-preparation coping or spiritual -positive coping among pregnant women with fear of childbirth. Pregnant women with higher levels of intolerance of uncertainty exhibited more severe fear of childbirth and greater use of avoidance coping and spiritual-positive coping. Implications for the profession and/or patient care Nurses should focus on the perception of uncertainty regarding childbirth and the coping behaviours adopted by pregnant women with fear of childbirth, assess their cognition about childbirth, and guide them to view childbirth positively, thereby reducing fear of childbirth and enhancing their coping ability for childbirth. Reporting method This study adheres to the STROBE (Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology) guidelines for cross-sectional studies. Patient or public contribution Pregnant women were surveyed to collect relevant data.

items.title: DBT Modulates Copper-Dependent Cuproptosis-Related Injury in Experimental Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy.
items.abstract: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a severe cardiovascular complication of chronic alcohol consumption, but its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Cuproptosis is a recently identified copper-dependent form of regulated cell death; however, its role in ACM remains unclear. In this study, male C57BL/6 mice were fed an ethanol-containing Lieber-DeCarli liquid diet to establish an ACM model, and RNA sequencing combined with bioinformatics analysis was performed to identify cuproptosis-related genes. Among the candidate genes, dihydrolipoamide branched-chain transacylase E2 (DBT) showed a consistent trend of downregulation across both independent RNA-seq cohorts, and was further validated by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. ACM mice exhibited increased serum and cardiomyocyte copper content, altered cuproptosis-related markers and impaired cardiac function. In AC16 cells, DBT knockdown induced copper overload, cuproptosis-related molecular alterations and mitochondrial dysfunction, which were markedly alleviated by the copper chelator tetrathiomolybdate. Conversely, DBT overexpression attenuated EtOH-induced copper overload, cuproptosis-related molecular alterations and mitochondrial dysfunction, with effects similar to those of tetrathiomolybdate. These findings suggest that DBT regulates ACM-related cardiomyocyte injury through cuproptosis-associated processes at the cellular level and may represent a potential therapeutic target for alcohol-induced myocardial injury.

items.title: AAPM Medical Physics Practice Guideline 18.a: Superficial radiation therapy using low-energy kilovoltage x-rays.
items.abstract: Superficial radiation therapy (SRT), utilizing low-energy kilovoltage (kV) x-rays typically in the 50-100 kVp range, is a well-established modality in dermatology and radiation oncology clinics for the management of non-melanoma skin cancer and various benign dermatological conditions. The comprehensive medical physics practice guidelines presented in this report are designed to facilitate adherence to minimum standards for SRT delivery. A technical overview of commercially available SRT systems in the United States is provided. Detailed guidelines for commissioning and routine quality assurance are presented, specifying daily, monthly, and annual tests, alongside established action limits. The SRT clinical workflow is delineated, encompassing patient simulation, treatment time or monitor unit calculations, data entry, independent treatment plan review, and radiation delivery. A summary of typical state regulatory requirements for x-ray machines is included. Adherence to relevant state regulations is emphasized and radiation safety considerations, comprising structural shielding, radiation surveys, personnel monitoring, signage, periodic spot checks, and machine operation, are discussed to ensure a safe and effective clinical environment. References to relevant societal practice guidance are provided to support standardized clinical implementation.

items.title: Person-Centred Climate Despite Unmet Fundamental Care Needs: Findings From inCHARGE Using a Convergent Parallel Mixed Methods Design.
items.abstract: Aim To explore person-centred care in surgical inpatient settings by examining the person-centred climate alongside patients' experiences of the fulfilment of fundamental care needs. Design A convergent parallel mixed methods design. Methods Surgical inpatients (n = 26) completed the Person-centred Climate Questionnaire-Patient version and participated in structured interviews, comprising binary questions with open-ended elaborations. Quantitative and qualitative data were analysed separately and thereafter brought together through an integrated interpretation of the findings. Results Questionnaire scores indicated a person-centred climate. Interview findings showed that patients described staff as kind, present, and compassionate, while also reporting several unmet fundamental care needs related to information, participation, hygiene, toileting, and symptom management. The integrated findings showed that patients reported a person-centred climate while simultaneously describing shortcomings in the delivery of fundamental care. Conclusion These findings highlight that global assessments of person-centred climate may overlook deficiencies in fundamental care and underscore the importance of considering multiple dimensions when evaluating person-centred care in clinical practice. Implications for the profession and/or patient care Assessing person-centred care requires attention to both the care climate and the extent to which patients' fundamental care needs are met. Combining structured measures with opportunities for patients to describe their care experiences may improve the identification of unmet needs and inform efforts to strengthen person-centred care in practice. Impact The study illustrates that being treated with kindness and goodwill does not necessarily ensure high-quality person-centred care. The findings are relevant for clinicians, nurse leaders, and researchers and support the use of multi-method approaches when evaluating person-centred care. Reporting method The quantitative and qualitative content in this study is reported in accordance with the relevant STROBE guidelines. Patient or public contribution The project is part of a research program developed in collaboration with the nurses and nursing leaders at the care units. WHAT DOES THIS PAPER CONTRIBUTE TO THE WIDER GLOBAL CLINICAL COMMUNITY?: The findings highlight the importance of combining different approaches when evaluating person-centred care. Asking about concrete care situations and experiences may help reveal unmet fundamental care needs that might otherwise remain hidden in survey responses.

items.title: Quality of Life, Self-Image, and Body Acceptance Among Mastectomized Women: A Questionnaire-Based Study in Maranhão, Brazil.
items.abstract: Aim To evaluate quality of life, body image, body acceptance, and sexuality among women after unilateral mastectomy, comparing those with and without breast reconstruction. Design Analytical observational cross-sectional study. Methods The study included 100 women aged 18 years or older who underwent unilateral mastectomy for primary breast cancer and were recruited consecutively between January 2019 and February 2022 at two tertiary oncology referral hospitals. All participants were interviewed 3-6 months after their respective surgical procedure. Quality of life was assessed using the validated Portuguese version of the World Health Organization Quality of Life Instrument-Short Form (WHOQOL-BREF). Body image, body acceptance, and sexuality were assessed using five study-specific, nonvalidated questions. Adjusted analyses were performed for the psychological WHOQOL-BREF domain and, post hoc, for reported change in sexual desire. Results Of the 100 participants, 38 underwent breast reconstruction and 62 did not. Women with breast reconstruction had higher scores in the psychological, social relationships, and environment domains of the WHOQOL-BREF, whereas no differences were observed in the physical health domain or the two general items. After adjustment for age and adjuvant treatment, breast reconstruction remained associated with a higher psychological domain score. Body image and appearance differed significantly between groups, whereas self-satisfaction, acceptance of physical appearance, acceptance of bodily changes, and current sexual activity did not. A higher proportion of women with reconstruction reported a change in sexual desire after surgery; however, the direction of change was not assessed. Correlations between body image-related variables and quality-of-life domains were generally negligible or weak and were considered exploratory. Conclusion Breast reconstruction was associated with differences in selected psychological, social, and environmental dimensions of quality of life and in the WHOQOL-BREF item on body image and appearance, but not with physical health, the two general WHOQOL-BREF items, self-satisfaction, acceptance of physical appearance, acceptance of bodily changes, or current sexual activity. These findings highlight the multifactorial nature of psychosocial adaptation after mastectomy and the importance of comprehensive survivorship care. Implications for the profession and/or patient care These findings support individualized nursing assessment of psychosocial adaptation after mastectomy, including body image, sexuality, and quality of life, and may inform patient education, supportive referrals, and shared decision-making when discussing reconstructive options. Impact This study highlights psychosocial dimensions of survivorship that may be relevant to women after mastectomy and to nurses involved in psychosocial assessment, patient education, supportive care, and coordination of multidisciplinary services. STROBE checklist for cross-sectional studies (STROBE_checklist_cross_sectional.pdf). Patient or public contribution Patients were not involved in the design, analysis, or interpretation of the study. They participated as study participants and provided data through the study-specific interviews and questionnaires.
