items.title: A Pivot Study of 2-Hydroxyisoflavanone Dehydratase in Quercus lobata.
items.abstract: This study proposes a methodological framework for investigating the regulatory architecture and evolutionary stability of the HIDH gene in Valley oak (Quercus lobata), reflecting the new ValleyOak3.0 assembly. The core of the methodology lies in distinguishing true biological divergence, such as frameshifts and alternative coding sequences, from computational artifacts by integrating an alignment modulator into the analytical workflow. The research systematically evaluates two primary architectures across Multiple Sequence Alignment effectors: sequence length expansion of the entire coding sequence (three categories), non-homologous segments associated with alignment modulation (six categories), enrichment patterns linked to sequence preference (four categories), and a density-based two MSA-independent metrics (four categories in total). By integrating an alignment modulator and incorporating reading frame analysis as a critical parameter, the methodology focuses on distinguishing true biological divergence, such as frameshifts and alternative coding sequences, from computational artifacts. While the application of the alignment modulator increased analytical precision from 42% to 71%, the findings reveal that reference motifs are inconsistently distributed across all effector categories, suggesting that their presence does not inherently guarantee transcriptional activity. Ultimately, this methodological transition from digital reconstruction to biological function provides a high-precision tool for discriminating between functional binding sites and background noise. This transition offers deeper insights into the advanced genomic characterization of Quercus lobata, serving as a valuable reference for ecotypic fitness changes in heterogeneously distributed oak species.

items.title: H5N5 virus transmission is driven by repeated cross-Atlantic introductions and transmission among high latitude seabirds
items.abstract: In November 2025, the first global H5N5 infection was reported in a person in Washington State. Previously, these viruses had only been detected in seabirds and shorebirds near the Atlantic Ocean, suggesting potentially distinct ecology from dominant H5N1 strains. Using 354 global H5N5 genomes, we show that H5N5 viruses have been carried by high latitude seabirds and shorebirds across the Atlantic at least 9 times, with introductions more frequent in the fall and spring. We reconstruct a plausible path of cross-continental movement via Arctic or sub-Arctic regions, followed by a year of cryptic circulation prior to human spillover. These data show that H5N5 viruses have undergone far more intercontinental movements than previously recognized, and exhibit host and geographic patterns that are fundamentally distinct from dominant H5N1 lineages. The distinct host ecology, geography, and movement, paired with the capacity to infect a person, suggest that enhanced surveillance may be warranted.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-driven Biomarker Discovery for Precision Psychiatry.
items.abstract: Poor phenotype quality and small cohorts remain major constraints in psychiatric biomarker research, and recent methodological advances increasingly address them. Language models turn clinical text into analysable variables at a scale manual chart review cannot reach. Self-supervised models learn from the unlabelled signals psychiatry already collects. Variant-effect prediction makes molecular interpretation computable, and research agents have generated and experimentally confirmed candidates outside psychiatry. These capabilities act early, on what is measured, what can be learned from it and which candidates are proposed. None of the artificial intelligence capabilities reviewed here yet reaches the stages at which a candidate becomes a clinical test. Producing candidates is becoming cheap while qualifying them is not. This review is organised around that asymmetry rather than by disorder or marker catalogue. It separates the measured characteristic, the prediction model and the intended clinical use, and treats method family as distinct from evidential stage. Across the selected evidence, discrimination is supported more strongly in development data than in independent evaluation, and prospective evidence that model-guided use improves care is scarce. Many reported metrics also address a simpler task than the intended decision: diagnosis instead of differential diagnosis, general prognosis instead of differential treatment benefit. The review proposes a six-stage framework linking intended use, measurement validity, model evaluation, comparative utility and monitored deployment, and places each capability on it, clarifying where methodological progress can accelerate discovery and where conventional clinical validation remains indispensable.

items.title: Narrative group intervention for wellbeing and violence reduction among incarcerated women: a Sicilian qualitative study.
items.abstract: Purpose This study describes an action research intervention conducted in the female ward of a Sicilian penitentiary, aimed at promoting emotional awareness, enhancing relational competencies, and fostering solidarity, with the consequent goals of reducing interpersonal violence and improving psychological wellbeing. Design/methodology/approach The intervention involved 20 women over one month, employing female Greek myths as narrative tools to facilitate the elaboration of traumatic experiences and the reconstruction of personal identity. Two groups of ten participants engaged in one two-hour session per week for each group over four consecutive weeks (totaling 4 sessions / 8 h per participant). Needs assessment was conducted through individual clinical interviews. Findings The intervention produced heightened awareness of experienced violence, improved emotional regulation, and strengthened metacognitive capacities. Participants spontaneously assumed the role of peer educators, disseminating content throughout the broader ward community. A marked improvement in the relational climate was observed, alongside emerging solidarity dynamics. Artistic artefacts served as instruments of public representation and institutional communication. Research limitations/implications The absence of a control group, ethically precluded in custodial settings, restricts causal inference. Outcome assessment relied primarily on qualitative observation rather than standardised psychometric instruments. Penitentiary contingencies prevented follow-up evaluation of the stability of observed changes. Findings pertain to a single Sicilian institution and may not be generalisable across diverse custodial contexts. Future research should incorporate pre- and post-intervention standardised measures, longitudinal follow-up, and comparative analysis of different narrative typologies to strengthen evidence and enhance replicability of the intervention model. Practical implications The intervention demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of myth-based narrative group work in women's custodial settings, providing practitioners with a structured, gender-sensitive and culturally accessible psychoeducational model. The protocol - characterised by brief duration, low resource requirements, and adaptability to varied educational levels - is transferable across different institutional contexts. The spontaneous emergence of peer education dynamics further suggests that structured group interventions can amplify their impact beyond formal participants. Penitentiary professionals, psychologists and educators may adopt and adapt this approach to promote emotional regulation and violence reduction. Social implications This study contributes to advancing gender-responsive and rehabilitative approaches within the penitentiary system, addressing the specific vulnerabilities of women in prison. By targeting interpersonal violence and promoting prosocial dynamics, the intervention supports safer detention environments and broader social reintegration. The emphasis on solidarity, emotional competence and identity reconstruction speaks to wider societal commitments to gender equality, restorative justice and the reduction of social inequalities. The cascading effects observed through peer education indicate potential for sustainable, community-level change within custodial institutions, with implications for public health and post-release social inclusion. Originality/value This study makes an original contribution by introducing female Greek myths as narrative mediators in a women's prison psychoeducational intervention, demonstrating their effectiveness across diverse educational levels without requiring direct trauma exposure. A further distinctive element is the spontaneous emergence of peer education dynamics, indicating the capacity of structured group work to generate systemic change beyond formal boundaries. The interdisciplinary integration of anthropological and psychological perspectives, combined with an ecologically situated action research design, provides a novel and transferable framework for evidence-informed practice in custodial settings. items.title: Deals for delivery: Exploring consumer perceptions of price promotions and nutrition information on meal delivery apps.
items.abstract: Objective Meal delivery apps (MDAs) increase access to unhealthy foods and employ promotional strategies to encourage purchase. MDAs are often not captured by nutrition-related policies applied in other settings (e.g. energy labelling required on menus in physical fast food stores). This study aimed to understand Australian consumers' (i) use of and perceptions of promotions on MDAs, (ii) perceptions of healthiness of foods available on MDAs, and (iii) preferences for the inclusion of nutrition information on MDAs. Methods Twelve online focus groups were conducted with 112 Australian adults. Data were analysed thematically. Results Three themes emerged: (1) expectations that MDAs were for convenience and treats, not healthiness; (2) promotional offers were considered integral to using MDAs and often influenced food choice; and (3) limited interest in nutrition information on MDAs - most participants perceived that it would not be useful given health was not a priority. Conclusions This study offers insights into how consumers perceive price promotions and the complex interplay of factors influencing food choice on MDAs. Implications for public health Policy interventions that restrict promotion of unhealthy foods and increase promotions for healthy foods (e.g. price promotions) may assist in improving the nutritional quality of purchases on MDAs.

items.title: Capacity: a priority issue for biodiversity conservation in Central Asia
items.abstract: Abstract Central Asia possesses some of the least known but most spectacular and intact wild landscapes of any region globally, hosting diverse communities of species adapted to temperate and arid grassland ecosystems. Growing recognition of these values and the threats to them posed by rapid economic development are likely to generate increased support and investment for conservation action. We undertook two studies during 2022–2025 to better understand regional conservation priorities and conservation capacity, during which we conducted 117 meetings and online calls with representatives of government, international development, donor and civil society organizations engaged with conservation in the region. Eighty-three per cent of the 55 participants questioned about conservation priorities considered low levels of technical, managerial and leadership capacity to be a significant constraint on the effectiveness of conservation action. We highlight various options for addressing these gaps in skills and knowledge and urge governments and international institutions supporting conservation in Central Asia to make capacity building a priority for their intervention and investment in the region.

items.title: STRAND: a comprehensive subcellular-resolved spatial transcriptome RNA architecture and navigation database.
items.abstract: Subcellular RNA localization serves as a critical regulatory layer governing cellular polarization, local translation, and functional compartmentalization. Recent advances in high-resolution spatial transcriptomics have provided unprecedented opportunities to resolve these intracellular architectures at single-molecule resolution. However, relevant datasets are dispersed across studies and repositories, vary substantially in processing procedures and standards, severely limiting their cross-study reuse. To bridge this gap, we present STRAND (Subcellular-Resolved Spatial Transcriptome RNA Architecture and Navigation Database), a curated data resource and analysis platform for the automated harvesting, quality control, and interpretation of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data. Through an agent-assisted curation pipeline, STRAND has assembled 35 subcellular-resolution datasets from six major platforms, covering 17 tissue types in human and mouse and totalling ∼4.9 billion transcript coordinates. Building upon this standardized data resource, STRAND provides an analytical workflow spanning cell segmentation evaluation, cell-type annotation, RNA localization/colocalization pattern annotation, and subcellular compartment inference. Two case studies demonstrate that STRAND successfully identifies established RNA localization patterns in cultured cell lines and detects drug-induced RNA relocalization in cardiomyocytes. STRAND is openly available at https://strand.phasep.pro.

items.title: Electrophysiological properties of mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive.
items.abstract: The neocortex has the largest volume, whereas the cerebellum houses the most neurons of the mammalian brain, underscoring paramount functions for interactions between them. Neocortical projections to the cerebellum involve both the mossy fibre and climbing fibre systems; mossy fibres find their origin predominantly in the pons, whereas the climbing fibres are relayed via subnuclei of the inferior olive (IO) that receive cortical input via the mesodiencephalic junction (MDJ). Given that climbing fibres regulate cerebellar plasticity in a timing-dependent manner, the MDJ-IO pathway probably contributes to both sensorimotor and cognitive learning. However, the physiological properties of IO-projecting MDJ neurons remain largely unknown. Here, we made targeted whole-cell recordings in brain slices of the mouse MDJ, separating IO- from non-IO-projecting neurons following retrograde tracing. We show that IO-projecting neurons are, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, highly spontaneously active and capable of high-frequency bursts of ≤350 Hz during current injections. Optogenetic stimulation shows that excitatory neocortical inputs to IO-projecting MDJ neurons can be integrated directly with excitatory inputs from the cerebellar nuclei. Moreover, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, IO-projecting MDJ neurons depolarize and repolarize quickly, and hyperpolarizing inputs consistently trigger rebound action potentials upon stimulus offset. This hyperpolarization is probably induced predominantly by inhibitory inputs from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey, which provide prominent bilateral inputs to MDJ neurons, as revealed by viral tracing in Gad2-Cre mice. Our results highlight how neocortical inputs to the MDJ can be transformed into diverse IO firing patterns and thereby contribute to the required specifics of cerebellar learning. KEY POINTS: The mesodiencephalic junction is an important brainstem region connecting the cerebral cortex with the cerebellum through its projection to the inferior olive, the sole source of the climbing fibres that drive cerebellar learning. We find that mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive represent a population of physiologically distinct neurons, capable of high firing frequencies and rebound activity following hyperpolarization. We reveal that mesodiencephalic junction neurons receive prominent excitatory inputs from neocortex and cerebellar nuclei, whereas their main inhibitory inputs are derived from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey. These findings shed light on how the activity of neurons in the mesodiencephalic junction can be regulated and how these neurons might influence activity in the inferior olive, and thereby cerebellar learning.

items.title: First-in-Human Phase 1b/2a Trial Shows Safety with MEK 1/2 Inhibitor EDV2209 as A Novel Treatment for Spontaneous Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
items.abstract: We report findings from a Phase 1/2a clinical trial (EUCT No. 2024-514590-22-00, STOP-DCI), an interventional, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple ascending-dose, first-in-human trial to determine safety and evaluate clinical outcome for the MEK 1/2 inhibitor EDV2209 in patients with severe spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). In Phase 1b (N = 11), three cohorts received a single intracerebral ventricular (ICV) bolus (8.55 µg, 17-28.5 µg). In Phase 2a (N = 16), two cohorts were given three ICV injections of 28.5 µg EDV2209 or placebo over 18 h, beginning within 8 h of SAH onset.The study found an equal distribution of adverse events between treatment and placebo with no treatment-associated safety concerns. Outcomes and mortality were as expected or better for patients with severe SAH in the patients treated with EDV2209. Pharmacokinetics were reproducibly stable in the CSF with no detectable levels of EDV2209 in plasma.Treatment with EDV2209 was considered safe and was interpreted to provide potential benefit for improving patient outcome following severe SAH. These results provide a rationale to continue with a Phase 2b / 3 study powered to determine efficacy as well as safety.

items.title: Italian guideline on palliative care in adult patients with grade 3/4 gliomas.
items.abstract: Background The palliative and supportive care needs of adults with glioma are complex. In 2017, the European Association for Neuro-Oncology (EANO) published the guideline on palliative care (PC) in this population. Objective To develop a clinical practice guideline for the PC of adults with CNS WHO grade 3/4 gliomas by updating and adapting the EANO guideline to the Italian context. Methods The guideline was produced by an interdisciplinary, consumer-inclusive panel appointed by the three main Italian scientific associations for neurology, neuro-oncology and PC, following the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Results The panel formulated two clinical questions, addressed by three recommendations (all based on very-low-certainty evidence) and one Good Practice Statement: (1) We suggest the use of structured communication interventions to convey diagnosis, prognosis, and/or therapeutic and care options (conditional recommendation). (2) We recommend using approaches/tools to facilitate information processing in adults with glioma with reduced decision-making capacity (strong recommendation). (3) We believe it is appropriate to monitor the emotional impact that communication can have, and to provide support to adults with glioma and their caregivers (Good Practice Statement). (4) We suggest offering adults with CNS WHO grade 3/4 glioma a healthcare model that integrates the best anti-tumor and palliative treatments through early, dynamic, interdisciplinary, and multi-professional management of emerging health needs. The integrated model should be aligned with patients' care preferences and caregivers' needs and provided throughout the whole disease trajectory and across all care settings (conditional recommendation). Conclusions This guideline provides recommendations for improving communication and integrated PC for adults with glioma and their caregivers. It also provides indications for future research priorities in this population.

items.title: Ethics of HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) Implementation Research in Inpatient Psychiatry: A Qualitative Study of Patient Perspectives.
items.abstract: People living with serious mental illness (PLSMI) experience disproportionately high HIV incidence, yet remain underrepresented in HIV prevention research. PLSMI are often excluded from pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) interventions in acute care settings. Inpatient psychiatry units (IPUs) are a promising but unexplored venue for PrEP intervention. However, such research requires designs sensitive to privacy, autonomy, therapeutic misconception, and inflicted insight unique to this population. We conducted semi-structured, qualitative interviews with PLSMI recruited from an academic medical center IPU. Eligible participants were ≥ 18 years old, HIV-negative, met ≥ 1 CDC PrEP-eligibility criterion, and were within 72 h of discharge. Interviews explored five domains: acceptability of IPU-based PrEP research, autonomy and undue influence, dignity and privacy, potential for inflicted insight, and fairness of randomized designs. Transcripts were analyzed thematically. Participants (n = 30; mean age 30.4 years; 80% Black; 72% male) expressed acceptability of PrEP-related research on the IPU, describing participation as informative, engaging, and aligned with their recovery goals. Privacy emerged as a central concern due to the communal IPU environment. Autonomy was consistently emphasized; participants felt more empowered to refuse research than clinical activities, and very few feared consequences for refusal. Views on randomization were mixed: some endorsed its fairness, while others preferred need-based allocation. These findings offer foundational guidance for ethically grounded PrEP research in inpatient psychiatry. PLSMI viewed IPU-based PrEP research as acceptable and potentially beneficial, and identified clear ethical priorities. Future studies should prioritize privacy, reinforce voluntariness, and transparently explain randomization.

items.title: Why dentists should return to the anatomy laboratory.
items.abstract: Anatomy has traditionally been taught as a foundational subject completed before clinical dental training, with limited opportunities for structured anatomical education after graduation. However, advances in implant dentistry, periodontal and regenerative surgery, injectable therapies, imaging, and orofacial pain management increasingly require detailed and clinically contextualized anatomical knowledge. This Perspective argues that anatomy should be regarded as a lifelong component of dental education rather than a preclinical prerequisite. Clinical experience generates anatomical questions that students may not yet recognize, allowing practicing dentists to reinterpret anatomy through the lens of patient care. At the same time, contemporary anatomical research continues to identify clinically relevant variations, tissue relationships, and structural continuities, demonstrating that anatomy remains an active clinical science. Continuing professional development should therefore incorporate clinically oriented anatomy education, particularly cadaveric dissection, which enables direct appreciation of anatomical variability, tissue planes, three-dimensional relationships, and operative perspectives. The goal is not simply to teach dentists more anatomy, but to help them ask better anatomical questions throughout their careers. Integrating anatomy into continuing education may improve clinical decision-making, prevent avoidable complications, enhance patient outcomes, and reduce associated medicolegal risk.

items.title: Phylogenetic correlation between the Type IV Secretion System and HIP1 suggest an adaptation for horizontal gene transfer conserved at the phylum level.
items.abstract: Most cyanobacterial genomes are rich in the GCGATCGC octamer, also known as Highly Iterated Palindrome 1 (HIP1). Despite its description over three decades ago, the biological function of this highly abundant sequence is only beginning to be elucidated. HIP1 is recognized by two DNA methylases, DmtA and DmtC, and is characterized by its evolutionary conservation and a quasi-periodic distribution within genomes. However, whether the phylogenetic distribution of HIP1 correlates with the presence of functional categories of protein families remains unknown. Here we investigated whether certain protein families share a phylogenetic distribution with this abundant palindromic sequence across cyanobacterial genomes. Our analysis revealed a strong phylogenetic correlation between several proteins of the Type IV secretion system (T4SS) and the abundance of HIP1. This finding aligns with recent discoveries demonstrating that HIP1 enhances DNA transformation in a methylation-dependent manner in two distinct cyanobacterial species. Consequently, we hypothesize that HIP1 function as a conserved adaptation for horizontal gene transfer (HGT) at the phylum level, potentially by serving as a DNA-uptake recognition sequence in cyanobacteria.

items.title: Educational professionals' experiences of supporting pupils with CHD: implications for collaboration between paediatric cardiology services and schools.
items.abstract: Background Children and young people living with CHD are at increased risk of neurodevelopmental, psychosocial, and educational challenges. Educational professionals play a key role in supporting these pupils but often receive limited condition-specific information, and little is known about how communication between healthcare services and schools can be improved. This study explored educational professionals' experiences of supporting pupils with CHD and opportunities to strengthen collaboration between paediatric cardiology services and schools. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with educational professionals ( n = 15) from mainstream primary, post-primary, and specialist schools in Northern Ireland. Interviews explored experiences of supporting pupils with CHD, communication, information needs, and training requirements. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings were complemented by a pre-post evaluation of an online CHD teacher training webinar. Results Four interrelated themes were identified: (1) Desire for structured communication; (2) need for individualised information relating to the educational environment; (3) managing uncertainty in the classroom; and (4) striving for inclusivity via flexibility. Participants relied on parents for clinical information and reported limited direct communication with healthcare professionals. Teachers requested practical, child-specific guidance to support classroom decision-making. Webinar findings demonstrated improved knowledge and confidence following training. Conclusions Educational professionals are committed to supporting pupils with CHD but often do so with limited clinical guidance and fragmented communication pathways. Strengthening communication between paediatric cardiology services and schools, alongside practical, child-specific resources, may reduce uncertainty, improve teacher confidence, and promote more consistent educational support for pupils with CHD.

items.title: Invisible Fathers of Multiples: A Qualitative Survey Study Exploring Early Parenting Experiences of Multiple Birth Fathers in the UK.
items.abstract: Multiple birth fathers remain largely invisible in perinatal research, policy and practice, despite facing distinctive practical, emotional and financial challenges. This study explores the early parenting experiences of multiple birth fathers in the United Kingdom using qualitative survey data from 107 participants, analysed using thematic analysis. Drawing on a social capital framework, it examines how access to structural, relational and cognitive resources shapes fathers' wellbeing. Four themes were identified: the complexities of early multiple birth fatherhood, fathers' mental health, the visibility of their needs, and experiences of support. Fathers described the intensity of raising multiples as 'doubly hard', characterized by exhaustion, financial strain, and 'survival mode' in the first year. Many reported significant mental health challenges, including stress, guilt, and feelings of being 'stretched to breaking point', yet often did not seek support or found available services generic and unhelpful. Experiences of support were inconsistent: while some benefited from flexible employers or strong social networks, others reported minimal professional engagement and perceived services as primarily mother-focused. Peer support from other multiple birth parents was valued but not always accessible. Access to structural resources such as paternity leave, financial support and tailored services was limited, while relational and cognitive resources, including shared understanding from professionals and peers, were uneven. Although UK-based, these findings reflect wider international gaps in father-inclusive perinatal care. Greater recognition of multiple birth fathers, alongside tailored mental health support and multiples-specific services, is needed to improve outcomes for families with multiples.

items.title: A multicenter whole-genome sequencing cohort of bleomycin-induced pneumonitis in predominantly clinically low-risk patients.
items.abstract: Bleomycin is a key component of curative-intent chemotherapy for germ cell tumours (GCT) and Hodgkin Lymphoma (HL), but its use is limited by bleomycin-induced pneumonitis (BIP). Although established clinical risk factors predict some cases, BIP also occurs without these. Preclinical models and small human studies implicate a contribution of drug metabolism, oxidative stress, immune and fibrotic pathways that may contribute to susceptibility. We aimed to identify germline genetic contributors to BIP in predominantly clinically low-risk patients to improve risk stratification in GCT and HL. We retrospectively identified 21 patients (13 GCT, 8 HL) who developed clinically significant BIP despite predominantly low clinical risk. Clinical data were collected and, where possible, blood samples were obtained for whole-genome sequencing (WGS). Analysis focused on a curated BIP-risk gene panel, derived from a literature review of genes/alleles implicated in BIP, alongside polygenic risk scores (PRS) for relevant lung and autoinflammatory/autoimmune pathology. Median age was 39 (GCT) and 49 (HL) years; 67% were life-time non-smokers. Most patients with BIP experienced CTCAE grade < 3 (76%), and 52% received corticosteroids. WGS was performed in 18 individuals. Missense variants with low general population allele frequency were observed in 9 genes within the curated panel, although the significance of these remains unknown. PRS analysis in 12 individuals of European ancestry showed no association of BIP with established PRS for lung disease or autoinflammatory/autoimmune disease. Biologically plausible candidate germline variants involved in lung surfactant biology and inflammatory signaling were identified. These exploratory findings provide candidate genes and pathways for future investigations into the genetic basis of BIP.

items.title: The Time Has Come to Develop a National Strategy to Prevent and End Child Sexual Abuse.
items.abstract: The title of this festschrift is adapted from an introduction written by Jon Conte for a (different) journal's special section about child sexual abuse prevention. A special section, and not a full special issue, due to too little work in this space, as he lamented. Yet even in the past couple of years, there has been remarkable growth in the area of child sexual abuse prevention research, documenting what works, and what needs work across a multitude of prevention strategies. Enough to fill a book and enough to underpin the development of a robust national strategy. Child sexual abuse is preventable, not inevitable, as Jon helped to demonstrate through his work as an editor, educator, and scholar.

items.title: Malaria and associated factors after RTS,S/AS01 vaccination in children in Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abrem Municipality, Ghana: A facility-based cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: ObjectiveMalaria remains a major public health challenge in Ghana despite the implementation of multiple control measures, including the RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) malaria vaccine. This study assessed malaria rapid diagnostic test positivity and associated factors among individuals presenting with suspected malaria in the Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abrem District, Ghana.MethodsThis facility-based cross-sectional study included 400 individuals of all age groups who presented with suspected malaria at the Salvation Army Hospital, Ajumako Ba. Malaria was diagnosed using rapid diagnostic tests. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, malaria control practices, environmental exposures, and vaccination status were collected using structured questionnaires. Associations were assessed using chi-square tests and binary logistic regression to identify independent predictors of malaria infection.ResultsThe overall malaria rapid diagnostic test positivity rate was 20.8% (83/400). Malaria test positivity differed significantly by age (p < 0.001), with the highest burden observed among children and adolescents. Sleeping under a mosquito net the preceding night was strongly protective (adjusted odds ratio = 0.17, 95% confidence interval: 0.07-0.40, p < 0.001). In contrast, sharing mosquito nets with one person (adjusted odds ratio = 4.51, 95% confidence interval: 1.31-15.50, p = 0.02), with more than one person (adjusted odds ratio = 4.76, 95% confidence interval: 0.92-24.47, p = 0.06), prolonged nocturnal outdoor activity (adjusted odds ratio = 4.49, 95% confidence interval: 1.44-14.03, p = 0.01), and proximity to gullies or stagnant water (adjusted odds ratio = 2.49, 95% confidence interval: 1.24-5.01, p = 0.01) significantly increased malaria risk. Among children younger than 7 years, malaria prevalence was lower in RTS,S/AS01-vaccinated children (29.6%) compared to unvaccinated children (60%), although differences were not statistically significant overall. Significant associations in this age group were observed with mosquito net use, nocturnal outdoor activity, and nearby vegetation.ConclusionMalaria rapid diagnostic test positivity remains high in the Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abrem Municipality, particularly among children. Mosquito net use, nocturnal outdoor activity, and proximity to potential mosquito breeding sites were associated with rapid diagnostic test positivity. The small vaccine-eligible subgroup limited conclusions on RTS,S/AS01 vaccination. Integrated, community-based malaria control strategies remain essential for sustained reductions in malaria transmission.

items.title: Self-reported genitopelvic pain disorders and symptoms among individuals with confirmed or suspected slipping rib syndrome: An exploratory cross-sectional survey.
items.abstract: ObjectiveSlipping rib syndrome is an underrecognized condition characterized by hypermobility of the false ribs (ribs 8-10), resulting in pain throughout the abdominal and pelvic regions. This study aimed to describe genitopelvic pain disorders and related experiences among individuals with slipping rib syndrome.MethodsAn exploratory, descriptive, cross-sectional survey was distributed using convenience sampling from July 2024 to November 2024. Sociodemographic characteristics, diagnostic timelines, and the Patient Global Impression of Change were used to assess the self-reported efficacy of pelvic floor physical therapy for genitopelvic pain disorders among individuals with slipping rib syndrome.ResultsSeventy-nine individuals with slipping rib syndrome participated; most were women (92.2%) and White (96.9%), and the mean age was 33.4 years. The average diagnostic delay was 5.4 years, and frequent misdiagnoses included costochondritis, anxiety, and gastrointestinal conditions. More than half (54.4%) had Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, predominantly the hypermobile subtype (81.1%). More than 50% reported moderate to severe impacts of slipping rib syndrome on sexual activity, and 26.9% attributed their vulvar or pelvic pain directly to the condition. Common comorbidities included hypertonic pelvic floor, chronic pelvic pain syndrome, endometriosis, vaginismus, interstitial cystitis, and pudendal neuralgia. Among participants who received pelvic floor physical therapy for genitopelvic pain disorders and symptoms, the mean Patient Global Impression of Change score was 4.5, indicating no change to minimal improvement, and 18.2% reported worsening symptoms. Diaphragmatic breathing similarly resulted in no improvement or worsening of symptoms in many participants.ConclusionsThis study is the first to explore the potential impact of slipping rib syndrome on sexual activity and its possible contribution to genitopelvic pain disorders. Symptom overlap with gynecologic conditions complicates diagnosis and management. These findings underscore the importance of evaluating for slipping rib syndrome during pelvic health assessments, particularly in patients with persistent or unexplained pelvic and abdominal pain. Further research is needed to clarify the musculoskeletal mechanisms underlying pelvic pain and to guide interdisciplinary care for individuals with slipping rib syndrome.

items.title: Proportion of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis among rifampicin-resistant cases evaluated using the GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay in Western China: A retrospective observational study.
items.abstract: ObjectiveDrug-resistant tuberculosis (TB), particularly multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB),tuberculosis, remains a significant public health problem in Western China. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of rifampicin and isoniazid resistance, including multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, and to assess the proportion of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis cases among those with rifampicin resistance as detected using GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay, with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis defined based on the MeltPro TB assay.MethodsThis retrospective observational study employed a cross-sectional diagnostic concordance design. In total, 345 patients were enrolled between December 2022 and September 2023; among these, 280 (81.16%) were newly diagnosed. Drug susceptibility profiles were determined using the MeltPro TB and GeneXpert MTB/RIF assays. Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis was defined based on the MeltPro TB assay, which served as the molecular reference rather than a definitive gold standard. Sensitivity and positive predictive value were calculated with 95% confidence intervals against MeltPro-defined multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.ResultsAmong the 345 patients, 22 (6.38%) were isoniazid-monoresistant, 12 (3.48%) were rifampicin-monoresistant, and 33 (9.57%) had multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Among the 209 samples positive on both MeltPro and GeneXpert MTB/RIF, 30 (14.35%) were rifampicin-resistant according to the GeneXpert MTB/RIF; 25 (83.33%) of these had MeltPro-defined multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. This proportion differed according to treatment history, with 11/16 (68.75%) among newly diagnosed patients versus 14/14 (100.00%) among previously treated patients. The sensitivity of GeneXpert MTB/RIF detected rifampicin resistance against MeltPro-defined multidrug-resistant tuberculosis among newly diagnosed patients was 100.00% (95% confidence interval, 71.51-100.00), and the positive predictive value was 68.75% (95% confidence interval, 44.03-87.07).ConclusionsOnly 68.75% of newly diagnosed patients with GeneXpert MTB/RIF detected rifampicin resistance had multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, indicating that rifampicin resistance is a suboptimal surrogate for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in this population. These estimates are concordance-based rather than accuracy against a definitive reference standard, and comprehensive testing for both isoniazid and rifampicin susceptibility should be performed in clinical practice to guide treatment and mitigate transmission.

items.title: A balancing act: Passive ankle exoskeletons alter neuromuscular function and postural stability during balance.
items.abstract: Spring-loaded passive ankle exoskeletons have the potential to modulate neuromuscular function during standing balance by altering the mechanical demands placed on the muscle-tendon units spanning the ankle joint. This study investigated the effect of exoskeleton assistance on postural stability and neuromuscular function across balance conditions of varying difficulty. We hypothesised that assistance would improve postural stability and reduce ankle plantar flexor muscle activity during balance tasks, although these benefits may vary with balance task complexity. Participants performed standing balance tasks of varying difficulty with and without rotational stiffness provided by spring-loaded ankle exoskeletons. Balance tasks included (i) quiet standing with eyes open (EO), (ii) eyes closed (EC), and (iii) reduced base of support (RBOS). We recorded centre of pressure (COP)-based postural sway measures, lower limb joint kinematics, muscle activation data from the medial (MG) and lateral gastrocnemii (LG), soleus (SOL), and tibialis anterior (TA), and MG fascicle behaviour. Exoskeleton assistance reduced LG and SOL activation but also altered joint kinematics and coordination. Ankle-based adjustments were most evident with assistance during simpler balance tasks (EO and EC), whereas assistance during the most challenging task (RBOS) was associated with increases in COP sway velocity, COP variability and TA activation. Our results suggest that despite the potential energetic benefits from offloading the plantar flexors, passive ankle exoskeletons may induce unintended effects that hinder the control of standing balance, particularly during more challenging conditions. Further work is needed to determine the mechanisms underlying these effects.

items.title: Assessment of pathogen reduction strategies in reducing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) transmission in acute-care hospitals: an agent-based model study.
items.abstract: Background Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) infections are an urgent public health threat in the United States. Despite infection prevention and control measures, hospital CRE rates have not declined in the past decade. Novel drug-based pathogen reduction approaches may decrease CRE incidence, and mathematical models can assess implementation strategies. Methods We used agent-based modeling to evaluate a hypothetical drug with pathogen reduction properties for reducing CRE transmission in an example acute-care hospital. We compared a strategy that treated only clinically detected CRE-colonized patients-using three drug effectiveness (DE) levels (25%, 50%, 75%)-with strategies that treated patients identified through surveillance screening in addition to clinical cultures. Surveillance screenings (intensive care unit (ICU) or all-admission screenings) were implemented at 50% and 100% patient participation (PP). Model parameters were informed by administrative healthcare data and published literature. Results The baseline mean CRE colonization incidence was 27.4 per 10,000 patient-days (interquartile range [IQR]: 11.7-39.9). Compared to baseline, at DE = 25% the reduction in mean colonization incidence was 1.2% (-0.8%-3.2%) for the treatment-only strategy. At DE = 50%, treatment + ICU screening reduced incidence by 9.0% (7.1%-11.0%) at PP = 50% and 13.2% (11.4%-15.1%) at PP = 100%. The reduction reached 38.5% (37.1%-40.0%) for treatment + all-admission screening at DE = 75% and PP = 100%. Conclusions This study underscores the potential of novel drugs as pathogen reduction measures to reduce CRE incidence in US hospitals if deployed strategically. Findings highlight the value of developing pathogen reduction strategies for colonized patients to prevent CRE transmission and infections.

items.title: Space changes after premature loss of mandibular second primary molars: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Deciduous dentition plays a crucial role in mastication, phonetics, and maintaining arch space for permanent successors. While several systematic reviews have quantified spatial changes following first primary molar loss, specific evidence synthesis for second primary molars is lacking. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantify space loss following premature extraction of second primary molars and evaluate the clinical necessity of space maintenance. Five electronic databases (PubMed, Web of Science, LILACS, EMBASE, and Cochrane libraries) were searched without date restrictions (last search 03/06/2025). Inclusion criteria included randomized, quasi-randomized, and non-randomized clinical trials involving children aged 4-9 years with second primary molar indicated for extraction. Two independent investigators assessed studies for inclusion, evaluated risk of bias using ROBINS-I tool, and extracted data. Random-effects models with 95% confidence intervals calculated mean differences as effect measures. Four studies were included in qualitative synthesis, with three studies involving 38 children included in meta-analysis. Meta-analysis demonstrated mean mandibular space loss of 0.80 mm (95% CI: -1.00 to -0.60; p < 0.0001) at 3 months, 1.10 mm (95% CI: -1.24 to -0.96; p < 0.0001) at 6 months, and 1.24 mm (95% CI: -1.48 to -1.02; p < 0.0001) at 9-10 months post-extraction. Arch hemi-perimeter decreased by 1.06 mm (95% CI: -1.26 to -0.31; p = 0.001) at 6 months. Current limited short‑term evidence suggests that premature mandibular second primary molar loss in children with erupted first permanent molars results in mean space loss of approximately 1.24 mm over 9‑10 months. Whether this short‑term space loss translates into long‑term malocclusion or orthodontic treatment need remains unknown. Therefore, clinical decisions regarding space maintenance should remain individualized and based on arch length discrepancy, occlusal development, crowding, molar relationship, and long‑term orthodontic risk. The current evidence is insufficient to support routine space maintainer use. Maxillary arch evidence is too limited to support any conclusion. PROSPERO CRD42025640491.

items.title: Still's disease and malignancies: insights into the balance between inflammatory enhancement and immune control. Data from the International AIDA Network Still's Disease Registry.
items.abstract: Still's disease is an autoinflammatory condition marked by excessive activation of the innate immune system, resulting in intense and persistent systemic inflammation if left untreated. Chronic inflammation is recognized as both an initiator and promoter of carcinogenesis, although growing evidence suggests it may act against cancer development. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the cancer risk in patients with Still's disease. Data were obtained from the international Autoinflammatory Diseases Alliance (AIDA) Network registry for Still's disease. Statistical analysis included a machine learning-based approach to evaluate associations between independent variables and malignancy. A total of 626 patients with Still's disease were included, of whom 14 (2.2%) developed 15 malignant neoplasms. Patients with malignancy history exhibited higher age at disease onset and diagnosis, as well as longer duration of fever during flares. Machine learning-based analysis, including Elastic Net and Firth's penalized likelihood logistic regression, identified an association between cancer development and fever duration (relative risk = 1.002, 95% confidence interval 1.000-1.004, p = 0.01). Despite being a severe systemic inflammatory condition, Still's disease appears to be associated with a relatively modest prevalence of cancer. However, uncontrolled systemic inflammation, as reflected by prolonged fever duration, may contribute to carcinogenesis in these patients.

items.title: Incidence of degenerative cervical myelopathy: findings from an English population-based study.
items.abstract: Purpose Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (DCM) is the most common form of atraumatic spinal cord compression. Few population estimates have been reported, with most estimates derived from hospital records. The aim was to estimate the incidence of DCM in UK primary care. Methods Population cohort study using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) Aurum database of English general practices, restricted to adults aged 20 years and over, 2013-2023. Incidence was calculated as new DCM diagnoses per calendar year divided by the registered adult population at each year's midpoint, reported per 100,000 person-years with 95% CIs, crude and age-standardised (AS), by gender and age band. Trends were modelled using negative binomial regression, examining pre- and post-pandemic periods separately. Results A total of 10,439 incident DCM cases were identified, from 16,585,135 currently registered patients (average age at diagnosis 61.8 years; 55% male). Overall incidence was 7.9 (95% CI 7.8 to 8.1) per 100 000 person-years, higher in men (AS 9.6, 95% CI 9.3 to 9.8) than women (AS 7.5, 95% CI 7.3 to 7.7) peaking at ages 75-79 years (18.9 95% CI 17.8 to 20.1) per 100,000. Over the study period incidence reduced, but pre-pandemic was absent, and incidence rose significantly after 2020, indicating COVID-19-related diagnostic disruption rather than a true decline. Conclusions DCM incidence in UK primary care is higher than previously reported estimates, peaks in older males, and rose significantly after 2020. Primary care clinicians should be aware DCM may be more common than previously assumed.

items.title: The Public Health Implications of Online Food Delivery Platforms: A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: Purpose of review This review summarises current knowledge on the role of online food delivery (OFD) platforms in shaping dietary behaviours, sedentary behaviours and other related health outcomes. Recent findings OFD platforms predominantly promote and facilitate access to energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods. Drivers such as convenience, time scarcity, and algorithmic personalisation reinforce unhealthy eating patterns by making less healthy options more visible and accessible. Evidence concerning sedentary behaviour remains sparse. A small number of studies suggest that OFD use may be displacing traditional food procurement behaviours resulting in reduced physical activity. OFD platforms further influence health through environmental, labour, and corporate activities. Despite their growing influence, OFD platforms remain largely unregulated within existing policy frameworks. There is an urgent need for interdisciplinary research, improved methodological rigour, regulatory change, and industry accountability to mitigate the health risks associated with OFD platforms and harness their potential for promoting healthier diets and related health behaviours.

items.title: Transcription factor EB as a novel target for dimethyl fumarate to restore endothelial function in diabetes.
items.abstract: Diabetes mellitus-associated endothelial dysfunction represents a pivotal early event in diabetic vasculopathy, linking metabolic derangements to vascular injury. Dimethyl fumarate (DMF), an FDA-approved drug for multiple sclerosis and psoriasis, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, yet whether it protects against diabetic endothelial dysfunction and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, diabetic db/db mice and the non-diabetic db/m + littermates were treated with DMF (100 mg·kg -1 ·d -1 ) or vehicle for 4 weeks, and vascular function in aortic and mesenteric artery rings was assessed by wire myography. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and endothelial cell (EC)-specific Tfeb knockout (Tfeb ECKO ) mice were employed to investigate the target of DMF in vitro and in vivo. DMF restored the impaired endothelium-dependent relaxations (EDRs) in db/db mouse aortas and insulin-induced relaxations in mesenteric arteries, improved glucose tolerance, reduced aortic endothelial mitochondrial ROS (mito-ROS) accumulation, and lowered the expression of inflammatory markers. IL-1β induced phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention of TFEB (indicative of TFEB inhibition), mito-ROS production, and inflammatory responses in HUVECs and mouse aortas, all of which were reversed by DMF pretreatment. These protective effects of DMF were largely reversed by TFEB knockdown in HUVECs or in aortas of Tfeb ECKO mice. RNA sequencing data analysis revealed a substantial overlap between DMF-regulated and TFEB-overexpression transcriptional profiles, implicating a role of TFEB in DMF-induced suppression of inflammatory and oxidative pathways. Together, DMF ameliorates endothelial dysfunction in diabetes by inhibiting TFEB phosphorylation and restoring TFEB nuclear activity. Endothelial TFEB represents a critical mediator responsible for the vaso-protective effects of DMF and a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of diabetic vascular complications.

items.title: Sensory profiles for young males and females with ADHD and autistic characteristics.
items.abstract: Young people with ADHD frequently experience sensory differences. However, little is known about sensory differences between young males and females with ADHD and the extent to which frequently co-occurring autistic characteristics affect this. The aim of this paper was to determine whether perceptions of sensory problems differ between parents/caregivers and teachers, whether young males and females with ADHD experience different sensory profiles to one another and whether autistic characteristics affect these sensory experiences. The study included 78 young people (age range 5 to 17; M age= 10.60, SD = 2.92), including 48 males (age range 5 to 17; M = 10.65, 2.96) and 30 females (age range 6 to 17; M = 10.53, SD = 2.90) who were diagnosed with ADHD at a private UK assessment clinic. Paired samples t -tests identified that parents/caregivers and teachers differed in their perceptions of sensory differences. Parents/caregivers reported more differences related to sensory systems compared with teachers. A MANCOVA did not identify a statistically significant difference in sensory profiles between males and females with ADHD after controlling for age. However, the sample size may not have been large enough to detect real sex differences, if they exist. Finally, regression analyses were conducted to determine whether autistic characteristics affected the sensory experiences of young people with ADHD. Autistic characteristics were consistently associated with increased sensory differences in parent report, but not teacher report, while age showed a consistent effect across both informants. This study provides new insights into the sensory experiences of young males and females with ADHD and different perspectives of parents and teachers.

items.title: Trends in prescriptions and costs of psychotropic drugs in the UK from 2013 to 2023.
items.abstract: Background Understanding prescription trends and costs of psychotropic drugs is essential to inform mental healthcare policy and practice. However, comprehensive national evidence across psychotropic drug classes is limited, and little is known on how prescription volumes changed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aims We examined prescription trends and costs of psychotropic drugs in the UK and assessed changes in prescription volumes following the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. Method We analysed national Prescription Cost Analysis data from 2013 to 2023, for six major psychotropic drug classes. Annual prescription volumes, total costs and average costs per drug were estimated. Linear regression was used to assess temporal trends and changes in prescription volume during the pandemic years. Costs were adjusted for inflation to 2023 prices. Results Between 2013 and 2023, psychotropic prescriptions grew 4% (95% CI 3.9-4.2) annually. Prescriptions for antidepressants, antipsychotics, stimulants and anti-dementia drugs increased, but not for hypnotics and anxiolytics and drugs used in substance dependence. In contrast, total costs declined by approximately £328 million, and the average cost per drug dropped from £11 to £5.9. Prescription volume remained unchanged during the pandemic years, except for anti-dementia medications, which showed an annual reduction of 17.2% (95% CI 7.8-26.6) relative to the underlying temporal trend during the study period. Conclusions Our observed rising prescription trend is consistent with global evidence on availability and use of psychotropic drugs. Furthermore, we found a decrease both in total drug costs and average costs per drug.

items.title: Plasma and CSF neurofilament light chain measured by Simoa and Lumipulse: an inter-platform comparison across neurological disorders.
items.abstract: Objectives Blood neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an accessible biomarker of neuroaxonal injury, but clinical implementation requires robust analytical comparability across platforms. We evaluated plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse across neurological disorders, including paired CSF analyses to anchor plasma findings to the central compartment. Methods We included 383 individuals, comprising healthy controls and patients with neurodegenerative diseases, multiple sclerosis, and ischemic stroke. Plasma NfL was measured in all participants using Simoa and Lumipulse; paired CSF measurements were available in 92 individuals. Lumipulse intermediate precision and between-day repeatability were assessed according to CLSI EP15. Cross-platform agreement was evaluated using Spearman correlation, Passing-Bablok regression, and Bland-Altman analysis. Plasma-CSF associations and age-adjusted diagnostic differences were assessed separately for each platform. Results Plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse showed strong concordance in the whole cohort (ρ=0.90), with similarly strong CSF concordance in paired samples (ρ=0.90). Method-comparison analyses demonstrated constant and proportional bias, with systematically higher absolute plasma NfL values measured by Lumipulse. Plasma and CSF NfL were significantly correlated within each platform (ρ=0.72 for Simoa; ρ=0.77 for Lumipulse). Lumipulse blood and CSF assays showed high precision. Across both platforms, plasma NfL increased with age and was higher in neurological disorders than in healthy controls. Conclusions Simoa and Lumipulse capture a consistent plasma NfL signal across neurological disorders, but absolute concentrations differ, supporting platform-specific, age-aware interpretation in clinical practice.

items.title: An individually calibrated task to induce cognitive fatigue and assess fatigability in children: the TloadDChild.
items.abstract: Cognitive fatigue is predominantly investigated in adults but remains understudied in school-age children, despite being a frequent condition in their daily lives. In this proof-of-concept study, we present a new task designed to induce cognitive fatigue in children: the Time-load Dual task for Children (TloadDChild). This dual-task combines a Continuous Performance Task (CPT-X), and a binary choice task based on shape discrimination (round vs. pointed shapes). The task can be calibrated to allow individual adjustment of high (HCL) and low (LCL) cognitive load levels. The task also enables the investigation of underlying decision-making processes using the Drift Diffusion Model. A total of 43 typically developing French-speaking children (7-12 years old) completed the TloadDChild under both HCL and LCL conditions. We showed that the TloadDChild successfully induces cognitive fatigue in children and that cognitive load, manipulated through the HCL and LCL conditions, modulates both attentional performance and underlying decision-making processes. These findings provide evidence supporting the use of the TloadDChild to investigate the effects of cognitive load manipulation (HCL vs. LCL) on performance, cognitive fatigue, and underlying decision-making processes in school-age children.

items.title: Brain representations of visual short-term memories during healthy human aging: occipital decline and frontoparietal compensation
items.abstract: Visual short-term memory declines steeply with age, but the link to neural representations of memory content remains unknown. We used fMRI decoding to relate remembered motion-direction representations in visual and frontoparietal cortex to age and performance, in 115 adults, aged 25-87, from the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) cohort. Decoding was strongest in visual cortex, but also significant in frontoparietal regions, with different profiles. Visual representations weakened with memory load and age, and statistically mediated age-related performance decline, especially during recall. This coupling, however, weakened with age: some older adults retained stronger visual representations than performance implied, suggesting impaired access to a partially preserved memory trace. Frontoparietal representations, instead, were largely insensitive to load and strengthened with age during maintenance, partially offsetting performance decline. Therefore, interventions to boost VSTM in older adults might target compensatory frontoparietal representations during memory maintenance, and readout of untapped visual representations at recall.

items.title: Accelerated Long-Term Forgetting as a Candidate Behavioral Marker of Hippocampal Network Vulnerability: A Critical Review of Implications for Epilepsy, Cognitive Aging, and Preclinical Neurodegeneration
items.abstract: Memory impairment is a common cognitive comorbidity of epilepsy and can substantially affect quality of life. Most memory testing tasks measure learning and memory over about 20 to 30 minutes, which may not capture the complexity of long-term memory formation. Because long-term memories continue to consolidate over hours or days, weeks, or longer, more comprehensive evaluation methods may be needed to assess whether memories persist over time.This raises an important question: Do conventional memory assessments adequately assess the longevity of memory? One issue is accelerated long-term forgetting (ALF), characterized by relatively intact learning and short-delay recall, followed by disproportionately rapid forgetting over longer intervals. ALF has been studied most extensively in epilepsy and has been associated with abnormalities involving the hippocampus and related memory networks. In temporal lobe epilepsy, accelerated memory decay has been demonstrated between conventional delayed and longer-term recall. Impaired systems consolidation is a leading explanation, with possible contributions from sleep disruption, interictal epileptiform activity, and broader network dysfunction. However, substantial methodological variability across studies, including differences in learning procedures, retention intervals, outcome measures, and definitions of abnormal forgetting, limits comparison and interpretation of findings.This review integrates current knowledge from diverse areas, including epilepsy, neuroscience, sleep studies, brain imaging, and aging. It discusses the role of ALF as a measure of memory deficits, explores its biological basis, and assesses the strengths and limitations of existing research. We also consider whether ALF could serve as a candidate behavioral marker of hippocampal network vulnerability. Before this role can be established, extended-delay memory paradigms require greater methodological standardization and prospective multimodal validation. Understanding memory persistence as a key component of cognitive function may help refine memory assessment tools, improve understanding of neurological conditions, and develop new approaches to assessing cognitive health in patients with epilepsy and other neurological conditions.

items.title: Advancing Spatial Pattern Integration in Species Distribution Modelling With Computer Vision: How Grain Size and Extent Concepts Shape Predictions of Emerging Aquatic Insects
items.abstract: 1. Capturing spatial patterns in ecology necessitates jointly accounting for the concepts of grain size (i.e., the spatial resolution of the input data) and extent (i.e., the area covered by the input data). Species distribution models (SDMs) that rely on traditional machine learning models (e.g., Random Forest, MaxEnt) only integrate the grain size through environmental variables derived from raster data. Recent advances in deep learning have led to the development of Deep SDMs. Unlike traditional SDMs, Deep SDMs directly process image windows representing landscape context. Therefore, they can manipulate both the grain size and extent, through the spatial resolution and size of the windows, respectively. 2. This study evaluates how grain size and window extent affect Deep SDMs, and how grain size alters the importance of variables (i.e., pixels of the image windows). We used multispectral and LiDAR data from drone and satellite acquisitions, with spatial resolutions ranging from 31 cm to 10 m, and varied the window extent between 40 m and 100 m. Grad-CAM was used to assess the importance of variables for each data type and measure their spatial agreement. As a case study, the terrestrial distribution of Plecoptera and Trichoptera, two orders of emerging aquatic insects with contrasting dispersal capacities, was predicted. 3. Results demonstrated the capacity of Deep SDMs to integrate both the grain size and extent. They highlighted substantial variations in performance depending on the grain size (up to 0.26 AUC) and on the extent (up to 0.16 AUC). In particular, the best predictions were obtained using 2.5 m multispectral data at a 40 m extent for Plecoptera (limited dispersers), and the same multispectral resolution combined with LiDAR at a 100 m extent for Trichoptera (greater dispersers). Results also showed a moderate but notable change in variable importance with different grain sizes. 4. Given the growing availability of remote sensing products, our findings advocate for systematic analysis of grain size and extent with Deep SDMs. This is essential to efficiently capture spatio-ecological patterns and to better understand the studied species. Datasets and code are publicly available.

items.title: Integrating 16S and 18S sequencing reveals coupled prokaryotic and eukaryotic relationships in drinking water biofilms
items.abstract: Drinking water biofilms host diverse communities spanning all realms of life. However, despite the known interactions between opportunistic pathogens and microbial eukaryotes such as amoebae, most studies focus only on the prokaryotic populations in these systems. As a result, the degree to which microbial eukaryotes shape biofilm communities and the persistence of opportunistic waterborne pathogens, such as Legionella spp. is still largely unknown. Here we leveraged a set of 128 non-disinfected drinking water shower hose biofilms collected across Switzerland to characterize both communities and quantify eukaryotes' role in shaping prokaryotic communities and Legionella persistence. We found both communities to present a conserved set of core taxa dominated by oligotrophic bacterial families and amoebae. The prevalence of taxa was mainly driven by the phylogenetic diversity among their sequence variants rather than their number alone. We detected prokaryotic and eukaryotic communities to show similar patterns in their richness and composition, influencing each other more than abiotic building-level factors. Legionellaceae bacteria were detected in 82% of samples presenting a diversity extending known reference species and no clear dominant taxa. Legionellaceae richness did not correlate with the richness of known amoebal hosts, but rather other amoebae, indicating that eukaryotic taxa relevant for Legionella persistence extend beyond the classically described hosts. These findings highlight the importance of integrating the eukaryotic communities to understand the microbial ecology in drinking water biofilms and recognize the conditions which allow opportunistic waterborne pathogens such as Legionella to persist.

items.title: One Paleopathology: A Deep-Time Framework for Predicting Malaria Resurgence in the Climate Crisis
items.abstract: Malaria, the deadliest vector-borne disease in human history, is resurging under climate change, land-use change, shifting public health priorities, and declining global funding. In this Personal View, we argue that One Paleopathology, an interdisciplinary framework that integrates bioarchaeology, paleogenomics, historical (written) sources, paleoclimatology, and disease ecology, offers critical insights into malaria's climate-driven expansions and contractions over the past 10,000 years. Deep-time evidence shows how anthropogenic environmental modification, from ancient irrigation and urban expansion to wetland management, has shaped transmission dynamics across millennia, and how past communities used biocultural strategies to reduce malaria's burden. We advance two arguments for the framework's value: first, that deep-time analysis reveals how human–environment interactions structure malaria transmission; and second, that past disease outcomes, such as skeletal indicators of malaria and infant and child mortality, can serve as historical baselines to validate and improve predictive models. Integrating reconstructed paleoenvironments, built environments, subsistence and socioeconomic factors, and morbidity and mortality data with climate-informed mechanistic models and an expanded eco-syndemic perspective can strengthen projections of future risk zones. We urge planetary health researchers and policymakers to treat the past as a laboratory, so that surveillance and mitigation in climate-vulnerable regions, from the Mediterranean to the American South, address systemic drivers rather than transient hotspots.

items.title: The DIAS: quantifying coupled curve intersections in pharmacology, ecology, demography, and climatology
items.abstract: Abstract The comparison of coupled curves arises in many applied sciences. In vascular physiology, researchers ask how mediator production and vascular relaxation intersect as the concentration of a signalling molecule changes. In ecology, they ask when predator consumption and prey survival are balanced. In demography, they ask when the urban population surpasses the rural population. In all these cases, the point of intersection between two curves is often assessed visually, without formal uncertainty quantification. The Dias’ Intercept Analysis System (DIAS) is a practical framework for estimating the intersection point of two coupled curves and for comparing that point. The DIAS treats the intersection as a bivariate random vector, propagates uncertainty via the Delta Method, and provides a calibrated comparison through a parametric bootstrap procedure. Monte Carlo simulations show that the DIAS estimator is approximately unbiased and that its confidence intervals achieve coverage close to the nominal level. The method is illustrated through applications in pharmacology, ecology, demography, and climatology. In each case, the DIAS provides an estimate of the intersection point with interpretable uncertainty, allowing comparisons that would be difficult to make reliably by visual inspection alone. A free, open-source Shiny application makes it accessible to researchers without programming expertise.

items.title: A Morphological Dual-Staining Framework for Standardized Detection of Cell Death in the Microalga Dunaliella salina
items.abstract: Abstract The absence of a simple, universal protocol to detect algal cell death is a major bottleneck in aquatic ecology and carbon cycle research. This study bridges this gap by establishing a practical diagnostic framework based on parallel 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) and iodine staining, concurrently probing the two pillars of photoautotrophic vitality—metabolic activity (via respiratory electron transport) and photosynthetic storage integrity. Using the halotolerant, wall-less model Dunaliella salina , we applied the method to environmentally relevant stressors. It clearly distinguished viable cells and consistently classified four distinct death phenotypes: apoptosis-like, necrotic, plasmolysis, and a novel secretion-type death from microbial fouling. Notably, light-induced necrosis exhibited morphological hallmarks of singlet oxygen-mediated killing, analogous to Type II Photodynamic Therapy. Crucially, identical death signatures were detected in natural populations from Maharloo Hypersaline Lake, confirming ecological validity. Beyond providing a robust, field-adaptable toolkit, our findings expose a critical disciplinary gap: the lack of standardized nomenclature and diagnostic criteria for cell death in carbon-fixing unicellular organisms. As these organisms mediate nearly half of global carbon fixation, quantifying their mortality is essential for improving carbon fixation and growth models, accurately predicting carbon fluxes, assessing the resilience of aquatic carbon sinks, and evaluating climate change impacts. We therefore propose an international consortium on Cell Death in Carbon-Fixing Unicellular Organisms to standardize definitions of cell death phenotypes, unify methodologies through this dual-staining protocol, explicitly incorporate mortality into carbon fixation and growth models, and translate laboratory-based viability metrics into predictive tools for ecosystem- and photobioreactor-scale carbon management. Our framework provides the essential methodological foundation for this global standardization effort.

items.title: Is it Difficult to be a People-Pleaser? An Item Response-Theoretical Examination of the People Pleasing Scale
items.abstract: The phenomenon of people-pleasing (i.e., the tendency to sacrifice one’s own needs and obligations to help others) has recently attracted considerable attention in popular psychology. Empirical research has been devoted only recently to the development and validation of suitable measurement tools such as the People Pleasing Scale (Blötner, 2026; https://doi.org/10.1007/s12144-026-09519-2). The measure provides desirable psychometric properties from the perspective of Classical Test Theory, but in this framework, several statistical assumptions about item and scale characteristics remain untested. To address this gap, we subjected the People Pleasing Scale to item response-theoretical examinations as per the polytomous Graded Response Model (N = 2,538). The three-factor solution (Responsibility, Neglect of Own Needs, and Others’ Expectations) elicited sufficient model and item fit and predominant support for the assumption of local independence. Its three subscales provided favorable item discrimination and threshold parameters indicating that endorsement of the highest response categories requires only moderately elevated levels of people-pleasing. Seven of the 10 items provided information across comparatively broad regions of the latent trait continuum, albeit with lower peak information. These findings illustrate candidate items for future scale shortening without substantial loss of measurement precision.

items.title: Appreciating Ambiguity in Art: The effects of semantic distance and insight confidence on aesthetic appreciation
items.abstract: Previous work in psychology of aesthetics suggests that people tend to appreciate artworks they subjectively perceive as ambiguous. Yet ambiguity of an artwork is typically measured through viewers’ own ratings or qualitative measures which are well suited to within-person questions, but they do not, on their own, describe how much viewers disagree about what a work means. Defining ambiguity as the degree to which an artwork affords multiple interpretations, we introduce a computational, description-based measure that quantifies this multiplicity as the semantic distance between viewers’ descriptions. We complemented this with a metacognitive measure, insight confidence, which captures how confident viewers are in their own interpretations. We examined how these measures relate to aesthetic appreciation, operationalised as interest, emotional intensity, and cognitive affect. In an online study (N = 123), participants viewed artworks for 6 seconds and for each individual artwork either described them, rated their insight confidence and provided cognitive affect ratings, or they provided interest and emotional intensity ratings. Across artworks, those eliciting more divergent descriptions (greater semantic distance) received lower mean insight confidence. Contrary to preregistered predictions, such artworks also received lower aesthetic appreciation. These results indicate aesthetic appreciation is more strongly related to how certain a viewer is about what they are viewing rather than the degree of ambiguity of an artwork. Methodologically, the approach offers a way to quantify the divergence of open-ended verbal interpretations across viewers, alongside a measure of viewers' confidence in their own interpretation.

items.title: More Visibility for Diversity? A Systematic Review of LGBTQ+ Representation in Educational Psychology Journals
items.abstract: Students identifying as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, or otherwise non-heterosexual or non-cisgender (LGBTQ+) are increasingly represented. However, they still face additional challenges in educational settings, so Educational Psychology needs to research these issues. In this preregistered systematic scientometric literature review, we investigate (a) the extent of LGBTQ+ centered research in Educational Psychology journals, (b) common themes and trends, and discuss systematic gaps for future research. After searching all 41,992 articles on ERIC, published in the most impactful (Q1 and Q2) Educational Psychology journals, we combined scientometric-quantitative and qualitative methods to review 68 eligible articles. We found a surge in publications from 2000 onward, driven by special issues. For almost half of these high-impact journals, we found no published articles on LGBTQ+ issues on ERIC; most publish only a few per thousand, even though this topic falls within their scope. Most often, these articles were empirical, correlational, and US-based, with inconsistent measures of LGBTQ+ identities. Through qualitative thematic analysis, we identified seven research themes and highlighted pertinent research gaps. To strengthen the evidence base in the field, future research should conduct rigorous longitudinal and intervention studies with culturally diverse samples and adhere to open science standards.
