items.title: The Written Self: Decoding Personality and Sex Differences Through Explainable AI
items.abstract: This study demonstrates how natural language processing and explainable AI techniques can advance our understanding of personality psychology, using sex differences in language as a case study. By analyzing stream-of-consciousness essays from 2,240 undergraduates using BERT with integrated gradients attribution, we identify distinct linguistic markers that characterize sex-specific trait expression. Our approach illustrates how explainability methods can help to detect systematic variations in language patterns across different trait levels and between males and females. Logistic regression analyses reveal Neuroticism as the strongest predictor of language typical of each sex (OR = 2.11, p ≤ .001), followed by Extraversion and Agreeableness. The model achieves 82.8\% accuracy in sex classification, and the explainability technique shows that sex differences in language often diminish at extreme trait levels. The study's methodological contribution lies in demonstrating how explainable AI can advance personality assessment by providing interpretable insights into the complex interaction between sex and personality in natural language use. The study also illustrates how explainable AI can advance personality assessment beyond descriptive statistics to provide interpretable insights into complex psychological phenomena, demonstrating a framework for deeper exploration of personality psychology findings.

items.title: Hospital-level Variation in Medical Debt After Acute Traumatic Injury.
items.abstract: Objective To determine whether the treating hospital contributes to patients' medical debt following injury. Summary background data Trauma patients often have little or no choice in where they receive care. However, variation in hospital billing and collection practices, and their association with patient medical debt, remains poorly characterized. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult trauma patients hospitalized from January 2019 to December 2020 at 29 Level I and II trauma centers within a statewide quality collaborative. Trauma registry data were linked to quarterly consumer credit reports from 12 months preinjury through 18 months postinjury. The primary outcome was change in medical debt in collections from baseline to months 9-18 postinjury. Hierarchical mixed-effects models with empirical Bayes shrinkage and reliability adjustment estimated risk-adjusted hospital-level changes, adjusting for demographics, injury severity, and treatment intensity. Hospitals were classified as outliers if 95% confidence intervals for observed-minus-expected differences excluded zero. Results Among 20,613 patients (mean age 63 y; 49% female; 82% non-Hispanic White), mean change in medical debt was $314 (SD $3464). Four hospitals (14%) were high outliers, generating $365-$566 more debt per patient than expected, while 4 (14%) were low outliers, generating $292-$676 less. Low-outlier hospitals cared for younger, lower-income, and higher-risk patients yet produced less debt than predicted. Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. Conclusions Substantial hospital-level variation in postinjury medical debt persists after adjustment for clinical and demographic factors. Billing, financial assistance, and collection practices may represent modifiable targets to reduce financial hardship after trauma.

items.title: Maternal Healthcare Autonomy and Neonatal Mortality in Nigeria: A Survival Analysis Using the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey.
items.abstract: Background Neonatal mortality remains a major public health concern and contributes substantially to under-five mortality. Maternal healthcare autonomy is a dimension of women's empowerment that may be associated with healthcare utilization and improve neonatal survival. However, evidence on the role of maternal healthcare autonomy and its interaction with antenatal care (ANC) in reducing neonatal mortality remains limited. Methods This study used nationally representative data from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey, including the most recent births to women aged 15-49. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and log-rank tests compared survival probabilities. Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with the primary model adjusted for baseline maternal, socioeconomic and healthcare-related factors. Post-birth variables were examined in secondary analyses. Interaction effects between autonomy and ANC were assessed, and sensitivity analyses were used with Weibull proportional hazards and accelerated failure time models. Results Women aged 25-34 years had the highest proportion of high healthcare autonomy (22.10%), while women with no formal education were more concentrated in the low autonomy group (6.73%). Higher autonomy was associated with lower neonatal mortality hazards, although associations were not statistically significant in the primary model (substantial autonomy: aHR = 0.86; high autonomy: aHR = 0.76). Sensitivity analyses using Weibull models showed consistent estimates. Interaction analysis showed that ANC modified this relationship, with the lowest risk observed among women with high autonomy and ≥ 4 ANC visits. Conclusion Higher maternal healthcare autonomy was associated with lower neonatal mortality hazards, although the association was attenuated and not statistically significant after adjustment for baseline factors. Strengthening women's healthcare decision-making alongside improving maternal healthcare access may contribute to better neonatal outcomes.

items.title: Glycolysis in pulmonary fibrosis: From drivers to therapeutic opportunities (Review).
items.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a chronic and progressive interstitial lung disease with a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Current antifibrotic therapies only slow disease progression, underscoring an urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. In recent years, metabolic reprogramming, notably the shift towards aerobic glycolysis (the Warburg effect), has emerged as a key driver of PF pathogenesis. This review comprehensively examines the central role of glycolysis in fueling the fibrotic cascade. It summarizes the major risk factors and fundamental pathogenic mechanisms of PF. The review then delves into the molecular mechanisms by which profibrotic signals, such as TGF‑β1, remodel cellular metabolism. The upregulation and pathogenic roles of critical glycolytic nodes are detailed‑including glucose transporters, hexokinase 2, phosphofructokinase‑2/fructose‑2,6‑bisphosphatase 3, pyruvate kinase M2 and lactate dehydrogenase A‑in activated fibroblasts, injured epithelial cells and pro‑fibrotic immune cells. Furthermore, the interplay between glycolysis and key signaling pathways (TGF‑β1, hypoxia‑inducible factor‑1α, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Hippo, AMP‑activated protein kinase and sirtuins) that form feed‑forward loops to sustain the fibrotic process is discussed. Furthermore, therapeutic strategies targeting glycolytic enzymes and upstream metabolic checkpoints are highlighted, summarizing preclinical evidence for small‑molecule inhibitors and non‑coding RNAs as emerging regulators of glycolytic reprogramming. By consolidating current knowledge on glycolysis‑centric metabolic underpinnings of PF, this review underscores the promise of metabolism‑based interventions and discusses challenges for translating these findings into effective therapies.

items.title: Climate change and extreme weather events to intensify West Nile virus activity
items.abstract: Vector-borne zoonotic diseases pose a substantive risk to public health worldwide, yet predicting outbreaks at scales useful for public health response remains a critical challenge. Transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, West Nile virus is the leading cause of arboviral disease in the United States, progressing to neuroinvasive disease in approximately 1% of infections. Arizona's record-breaking 2021 outbreak, with 1,715 reported human cases and 127 deaths exemplifies this growing burden. Using a decade of mosquito surveillance data coupled with time-lagged weather patterns in a random forest framework, we developed spatial models predicting Culex abundance and West Nile virus occurrence across Arizona at weekly temporal and fine spatial resolution. Our weighted models classified viral occurrence with 98.9% accuracy and explained 65.3% of weekly variation in county-level human cases, with human cases lagging modeled activity by one week. Neither mosquito abundance nor viral occurrence declined at the extreme temperatures characteristic of Arizona summers, suggesting that thermal refugia sustain transmission. Drought-monsoon cycling, rather than temperature alone, emerged as the primary driver of West Nile activity, and projections through 2100 indicate intensifying activity under all climate change scenarios.

items.title: Design and evaluation of probe-capture sequencing for clinical Neisseria gonorrhoeae specimens
items.abstract: Characterizing the molecular epidemiology of Neisseria gonorrhoeae is essential for understanding disease burden, elucidating transmission dynamics, and informing clinical decision-making and public health interventions. Given that routine, culture-independent diagnostics rapidly and sensitively detect this difficult-to-cultivate pathogen, aligning genomic surveillance with these workflows is necessary to understand its epidemiology and evolutionary dynamics. To address this challenge, we investigated the utility of probe-capture sequencing to selectively enrich for pathogen-specific DNA during next-generation sequencing. Custom biotinylated oligonucleotide baits were designed using genetic information from publicly available genomes hosted on Pathogenwatch. Of the 32,574 assemblies, 2,877 representative genomes were selected to inform probe generation using core genome amino acid distance clustering and representation of unique resistance-associated genotypes and predicted resistance phenotypes. The resulting probe set provided generous coverage of the reference genome, N. gonorrhoeae FA 1090, with 94.6% nucleotide coverage and 99.3% of annotated genes covered by at least one probe. Piloting this technology on 12 clinical urine specimens with variable relative pathogen abundances revealed that probe-capture sequencing substantially increased the relative abundance of N. gonorrhoeae sequence reads from a complex sample (fold-change range, 226 - 2046), enabling considerable genome coverage, the construction of high-quality genome assemblies, and the detection of resistance-associated genotypes. These findings demonstrate that probe-capture sequencing is a viable method for enriching N. gonorrhoeae genetic material from clinical samples, enabling culture-independent genomic investigations into the epidemiology of hard-to-culture pathogens and providing actionable insights to inform clinical and public health interventions.

items.title: Chikungunya virus live-cell reporter systems reveal cell-type-dependent antiviral responses to ribavirin
items.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) remains a significant global public health threat, yet antiviral discovery is limited by experimental systems that provide little mechanistic resolution and rely heavily on transformed cell lines of uncertain physiological relevance. Here, we developed complementary live-cell CHIKV reporter systems comprising a dual-fluorescent subgenomic replicon and fluorescent infectious viruses that enable real-time monitoring of distinct stages of the viral replication cycle. By coupling an nsP3-tagged reporter to genomic RNA translation and replication with a subgenomic reporter of structural gene expression, we achieved temporal resolution of early and late replication events in living cells. Functional validation using replication-defective and subgenomic RNA-deficient mutants confirmed that the system distinguishes between viral RNA replication and downstream structural gene expression. Application of these reporters revealed distinct antiviral responses across transformed and physiologically relevant human cell models. Ribavirin and the nsP2 inhibitor RA-0002034 potently inhibited CHIKV replication in transformed cell lines. Unexpectedly, ribavirin activity was markedly diminished in primary human skeletal muscle myoblasts and dermal fibroblasts, despite robust antiviral effects in commonly used screening cell lines. Mechanistic studies showed that ribavirin-mediated inhibition was rescued by guanosine but not inosine supplementation and was recapitulated by mycophenolic acid, consistent with guanine nucleotide depletion as the predominant antiviral mechanism under the conditions tested. Notably, inhibition through this pathway was substantially less effective in primary human cells. Together, these findings establish versatile live-cell CHIKV reporter systems for mechanistic studies of viral replication and reveal striking cell-type-dependent differences in response to guanine nucleotide depletion. Our results demonstrate that host-cell context can profoundly influence both CHIKV replication and antiviral susceptibility, highlighting the importance of physiologically relevant models for understanding virus-host interactions and antiviral mechanism.

items.title: Interpreting Self-Reported Outcomes After AI-Assisted Writing Workshops: An Aggregate Sensitivity Analysis of Educational Claims
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence writing workshops are increasingly used in health-professions education, but immediate self-reports can be interpreted as evidence of learning or ethical competence beyond what they measure. This study applied an aggregate-data interpretation framework to a published single-institution evaluation of a hands-on AI-assisted academic-writing workshop. Public counts and item summaries were classified by construct, summarized with binomial working-model intervals for observed respondents, and reanalyzed with complete registered-list identification intervals that assigned every questionnaire nonrespondent first to the non-positive and then to the positive category. Among 64 respondents, 54 reported improved understanding, or 84.4 percent, with a working-model interval of 73.6 percent to 91.3 percent. Confidence and perceived ethical improvement were each reported by 45 respondents, or 70.3 percent, with intervals of 58.2 percent to 80.1 percent. Across 80 registrants, unrestricted nonresponse yielded identification intervals of 67.5 percent to 87.5 percent for perceived improvement and 56.2 percent to 76.2 percent for both confidence and ethical improvement. Positive delivery ratings were common. However, these measures did not assess objective knowledge, writing quality, source verification, ethical decision-making, or sustained practice. The evidence supports bounded descriptions of respondent experience only; effectiveness claims require linked objective assessment and delayed follow-up.

items.title: Prior Beliefs not Cognitive Reflection Predict People’s Accuracy when Judging Health (Mis)Information
items.abstract: Health misinformation affects individual and public health decisions and erodes trust in medical institutions. Online, people are often confronted with a large variety of both evidence-based and misleading content, making credibility assessments challenging. Judgment errors are not simply the result of a lack of access to accurate information but depend on a variety of cognitive, social and affective factors. In this study, we asked a quota-representative sample of the Austrian population (N = 343) to assess the veracity and credibility of 50 health claims drawn from real-world online information. Using a signal-detection approach, we examined which individual differences predicted accuracy, perceived credibility and response bias. Results indicate that stronger belief in alternative medicine and in conspiracy theories were associated with lower accuracy, whereas cognitive reflection, motivation for cognition and intellectual humility were not. Stronger belief in alternative medicine, more trust in science, and older age were also associated with being more likely to believe any information regardless of veracity. Overall, our results point towards prior beliefs, not cognitive variables, playing a larger role in what information people choose to believe. Implications for interventions are discussed.

items.title: Prevalence and factors associated with hypothermia among neonates born at selected health facilities in Kabale Municipality, south-western Uganda: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Global estimates of neonatal hypothermia ranges between 32% to 85%, with disproportionately higher rates reported in Sub-Saharan Africa. Reported prevalence varies widely between 50–83%, however, we never came across any published data that exists on the magnitude and prevalence of hypothermia in Kable Municipality and the wider Kigezi sub-region. We aimed to determine the prevalence and factors associated with hypothermia among neonates admitted at four health facilities in Kabale Municipality, south-western Uganda. Methods A cross-sectional study enrolled a total of 384 neonate consecutively between 1st April and 30th June, 2026 from the four facilities in Kabale Municipality, southwestern Uganda. Pproportionate to size sampling was used across study sites based on average monthly deliveries. Core temperature was measured using a digital rectal thermometer, and a structured, pre-tested questionnaire was used which can captured socio-demographic, maternal, newborn, obstetric, and newborn care characteristics. Multivariable logistic regression used to identify predictors of hypothermia in neonates. Results The prevalence of neonatal hypothermia was 50.3% (n = 193/384, 95% CI: 45.1–53.4%). After adjustment, factors independently associated with neonatal hypothermia were categorized into maternal and neonatal factors. Maternal factors included maternal level of education (primary; AOR = 1.35, 95% CI: 1.08–2.06), spouse’s employment status (unemployed; AOR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.37–1.69) mother having breastfeeding issues (absence versus presence; AOR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.25–2.04), leaking liquor/premature rupture of membranes (AOR = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.27–2.32), and Mode of delivery (caesarean delivery: AOR = 1.84, 95% CI: 1.29–2.47). Neonatal factors included not wearing a cap after birth (AOR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.08–2.21), and low birth weight (AOR = 1.68, 95% CI: 0.79–3.55). Conclusions Neonatal hypothermia affects approximately one in every two neonates admitted at these four Kabale Municipality facilities, underscoring it as a major public health concern in this setting. The high burden reflects the combined influence of maternal socio-demographic and obstetric characteristics alongside neonatal care practices, suggesting that no single intervention point is sufficient on its own. Given the substantial proportion of affected neonates, targeted facility-level interventions and continuous health worker training on thermal care protocols are warranted to reduce the associated morbidity and mortality risks in this population.

items.title: Nominal and real cigarette Price trends from a global dataset, 2008-2024 and implications for the World Health Organization's 3 by 35 initiative to tax unhealthy products
items.abstract: Abstract In July 2025, WHO launched the “3 by 35” Initiative calling on countries to increase real prices of tobacco, alcohol, and sugary drinks by at least 50% by 2035 to secure an additional $ 1 trillion in public revenue. We analyzed trend changes in countries’ nominal and inflation-adjusted retail cigarette prices over windows ranging from 2 to 16 years over the period 2008-2024, derived from nine editions of the World Health Organization Report on the Global Tobacco Epidemic. We found over 20% of nominal cigarettes prices (and up to 40% in WHO’s African region) were sticky, that is, unchanged across successive periods. Between 2008 and 2024, inflation-adjusted international dollar cigarette prices rose at a least squares annual trend growth rate of 2·9% (95% UI 2·8–3·0%).We found real price increases of 50% or more are rare over the short term, but over a third of countries achieved this over 10-year, often without implementing a conscious strategy to raise taxes. This, combined with the finding of a strong link between excise taxes and prices, suggests that it is feasible to achieve, and even surpass WHO’s 3 by 35 call to action for tobacco if countries strategize and accelerate tobacco tax increases.

items.title: Enhancing Urban Air Quality Forecasting: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Models
items.abstract: Abstract Predicting air quality accurately is essential, especially in fast-growing cities where pollution directly impacts public health and environmental policies. This study compares different machine learning models to forecast air quality in major Indian cities using data from 2015 to 2020. We tested several algorithms, including Extra Trees, Random Forest, Linear Discriminant Analysis, K-Nearest Neighbors, Logistic Regression, and a combination of Random Forest and Extra Trees as an ensemble model. Our results show that the ensemble model consistently provides the most accurate predictions, outperforming individual models by leveraging their strengths. This approach improves the classification of air pollution levels, making it more reliable for real-time air quality monitoring. The findings can help policymakers and environmental experts develop better strategies for reducing pollution and protecting public health. This research highlights the power of machine learning in tackling environmental challenges and improving air quality forecasting.

items.title: COVID-19 lockdown duration and transitions in family intergenerational support patterns: Evidence from the China Family Panel Studies
items.abstract: Abstract The family is the primary informal insurance mechanism through which economies buffer individual and aggregate risks, yet whether a major crisis activates intergenerational mutual aid or, instead, weakens intergenerational ties through physical isolation and resource strain remains unclear. Existing studies mostly examine changes in a single support dimension in isolation, or the simple before-versus-after correlation, and often rely on small, short-run samples, leaving the overall effect of the shock on the configuration of intergenerational support poorly understood. Using four waves (2016–2022) of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), we first classify intergenerational support into four cross-wave comparable patterns—Reciprocal, Filial-support, Interactive, and Detached—through latent class analysis, and then apply a multi-group difference-in-differences design to identify the causal effect of lockdown intensity on transitions between support patterns, its dynamic path, and its heterogeneity by household resources. We find that prolonged lockdowns shift households away from one-way support or detachment toward two-way reciprocity: the effect increases in lockdown intensity, is concentrated in the most strictly locked-down regions, and raises the post-pandemic probability of being Reciprocal by about 4.8 and 5.1 percentage points on average. The effect is delayed, being close to zero in the shock year (2020) and significant only by 2022. The shift toward reciprocity is widespread across income groups, whereas transitions into Filial-support are highly concentrated among low-income households. Overall, a major public-health shock triggers an adaptive reconfiguration of intergenerational support patterns, but its direction, lag, and form depend on shock intensity and household resources; the family, as an informal safety net, is resource-asymmetric, all the more so for vulnerable households. items.title: Beyond Digital Access: Algorithmic Inclusion and Universal Access for Older Adults on Digital Platforms
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study examines how algorithm-driven platforms reshape universal access for older adults after they have entered digital environments. It asks how platform design, recommendation systems, commercial targeting, and digital-by-default services create barriers to informed and autonomous participation. Methods A qualitative and explanatory design combines a narrative review, policy-document analysis, and mechanism-oriented comparison. Evidence was organized across four recurring settings: information access, health communication, online consumption, and digital public services. The analysis links technological accessibility, user capability, and rights protection. Results Four recurrent barriers were identified: narrowed information exposure through algorithmic filtering; amplified risk and misplaced trust in health communication; targeted consumer inducement accompanied by difficult redress; and participation exclusion created by digital-by-default public services. These barriers are reinforced by attention-based business models, reductionist profiling, superficial age-friendly design, and uneven family and community support. Conclusion Universal access requires more than readable interfaces or basic operational support. Algorithmic inclusion depends on understandable recommendation processes, meaningful user control, reversible personalization, accessible human assistance, and effective remedies. Policy, design, community support, intergenerational assistance, and older adults’ participation in evaluation should be treated as complementary elements of inclusive platform governance.

items.title: Antimycobacterial activity and preliminary characterization of a 2-thio-malonylurea derivative against clinically relevant Mycobacterium species
items.abstract: Abstract Mycobacterial infections remain a significant public health concern, particularly those caused by environmental and non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM). This study aimed to design, synthesize 2–11 , and evaluate 2-thio-malonylurea compounds as potential antimycobacterial agents. The synthesized compounds were subjected to in silico evaluation using SwissADME and screened for antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria. The most active derivative was subsequently evaluated against clinically relevant Mycobacterium species, and its effects on mycobacterial morphology and mammalian cell viability were investigated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and cytotoxicity assays, respectively. LQFM238 ( 7 ) exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity among the compounds tested, showing activity against both Gram-positive bacterial species, with MIC values of 125 µg/mL against S. aureus and 250 µg/mL against E. faecalis . It showed antimycobacterial activity against M. tuberculosis H37Ra (MIC 62.5 µg/mL), M. avium (MIC 25 µg/mL), M. abscessus subsp. bolletii (MIC 50 µg/mL), and M. abscessus subsp. abscessus (MIC 50 µg/mL), whereas MIC value ≥ 100 µg/mL were observed for M. intracellulare . SEM revealed marked morphological alterations after exposure to 500 µg/mL for 24 h. Cytotoxic effects were observed only at 41.67 µg/mL, with selectivity indices of 4.15 for M. avium and 2.08 for both M. abscessus strains. LQFM238 ( 7 ) demonstrated promising antimycobacterial activity, particularly against M. avium and clinical M. abscessus strains.

items.title: ABO Blood Group Distribution and Sociodemographic Profile of Patients with Pulmonary Tuberculosis in Luanda, Angola
items.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa. Although host genetic factors may influence susceptibility to infectious diseases, the relationship between ABO/Rh blood groups and pulmonary TB remains incompletely understood, particularly in African populations. Herein, we characterise the distribution of ABO/Rh blood groups and the demographic profile of patients with pulmonary TB in Luanda, Angola. Methods: This was a cross-sectional study conducted among patients with pulmonary TB treated at Hospital Divina Providência, Luanda, during the second semester of 2020. A total of 110 patients were selected by simple random sampling. Sociodemographic data were collected and ABO/Rh blood groups determined using anti-A, anti-B, and anti-D reagents. Results: Among the 110 participants, O+ was the most prevalent phenotype (51; 46.4%), followed by A+ (29; 26.4%), B+ (25; 22.7%), and AB+ (5; 4.5%). The mean age was 31.5 years, and males accounted for 57.3% of participants. Most participants had non-higher education (89.1%) and resided in Kilamba Kiaxi municipality (75.5%). ABO phenotype was not associated with age (p=0.423) or sex (p=0.522). Also, ABO was not associated with educational level (p=0.125), residence (p=0.769), occupation (p=0.864), alcohol consumption (p=0.748), or associated infections (p=0.365). Conclusion: The O+ blood group was the predominant ABO/Rh phenotype among patients with pulmonary TB in Luanda, followed by A+, B+, and AB+. No associations were identified between ABO phenotype and demographic or clinical characteristics. Larger multicentre studies incorporating appropriate non-TB control groups are warranted to clarify the potential relationship between ABO phenotypes and TB susceptibility in Angola.

items.title: Parent perspectives on the potential use of smart inhalers for asthma management in children: a qualitative interview study.
items.abstract: Objective Achieving adequate adherence to preventer medication remains a challenge in the management of pediatric asthma. A minimum of 75% adherence is recommended to achieve adequate clinical control, however actual adherence rates are often lower and are influenced by the unpredictability of family life and competing demands. Smart inhalers aim to support adherence to preventer medications by monitoring use and providing medication reminders, as well as tracking reliever use. This study explored the perceptions of parents of children aged 5-9 years with recent uncontrolled asthma regarding the potential usefulness of smart inhalers to manage their children's asthma, and perceived barriers and facilitators to their use. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted via Zoom with parents residing in New South Wales, Australia. Interviews explored parents' perspectives about barriers to asthma management, awareness and perceived need for smart inhalers, desired features and functionalities, attitudes toward data sharing, perceived support requirements and cost considerations. Data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive analysis approach. Ten parents participated (children aged 5-8); none had previously used a smart inhaler to manage their child's asthma. Results Overall attitudes toward smart inhalers were positive. Four primary themes were identified: perceived benefits of smart inhalers, including access to reliable medication data to share with healthcare providers; barriers to adoption, including concerns about technology difficulties; cost considerations with affordability influencing the likelihood of uptake; and implementation needs including the need for support for initial set up. Conclusions Parents generally viewed smart inhalers as a promising tool for managing childhood asthma. Study findings suggest that successful implementation will require consideration of cost, ease of use, and adequate support for use.

items.title: Fossil fuel use, urban air pollution, and health in rapidly growing African cities: Implications for sustainable and low-emission urban development.
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization and persistent reliance on fossil fuels in African cities have intensified ambient air pollution, posing significant public health and environmental challenges. This critical systematic review with policy synthesis, conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 reporting principles, synthesizes evidence on fossil fuel sources, urban air quality trends, health impacts, structural drivers, and policy responses while identifying evidence gaps and opportunities for integrated interventions. Diesel-powered road transport, backup generators, and household energy use emerge as dominant sources of particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, black carbon, and volatile organic compounds, disproportionately affecting children, the elderly, and low-income populations. Observed pollution levels often exceed World Health Organization guidelines, yet monitoring networks are sparse and unevenly distributed, limiting exposure assessment. Structural and institutional factors including urban sprawl, energy insecurity, weak fuel standards, and fragmented governance amplify emissions and health burdens. Policy synthesis indicates opportunities for co-benefits through transport electrification, clean cooking transitions, renewable mini-grids, and integrated urban planning, with interventions capable of simultaneously improving air quality, population health, and climate mitigation outcomes. Evidence-policy gaps highlight the need for cross-sectoral coordination, enhanced monitoring infrastructure, and health-informed energy and transport strategies. This review is intended to provide an evidence-informed policy synthesis for national and city governments, urban planners, environmental regulators, public health agencies, and development partners. By integrating evidence across energy, transport, health, and urban planning, it identifies practical pathways for reducing fossil-fuel dependence while improving air quality, population health, climate resilience, and sustainable urban development in rapidly growing African cities. Implications : This review identifies fossil-fuel-powered transport, diesel generators, and household energy use as major contributors to urban air pollution and related health risks in rapidly growing African cities. Priority actions include cleaner fuels, stronger vehicle and fuel standards, expanded air-quality monitoring, public transport reform and electrification, clean cooking transitions, and renewable mini-grids. Integrating health evidence into urban energy and transport planning can reduce pollution exposure, protect vulnerable populations, and support low-emission, equitable, and climate-resilient urban development.

items.title: Guiding principles for modelling cellular transport homeostasis.
items.abstract: Cellular transport homeostasis evolved as a universal strategy linking the dynamic interactions between membrane transport, metabolism and biosynthesis in all cells. The entangled nature of these interactions, together with the effects from additional processes influencing homeostatic variables generate complexities that render intuition an unreliable interpreter and predictor of cell responses often prompting for modelling help. The main variables in transport homeostasis are membrane potentials, cell volume, ion and neutral solute fluxes through active and passive membrane transporters, cytoplasmic amounts and concentrations of soluble ions and neutral solutes, charge and concentrations of impermeant cytoplasmic solutes, charge and osmotic coefficient of cytoplasmic proteins, and cytoplasmic H+, Ca2+ and Mg2+ buffering. Models of cellular transport homeostasis developed to explain puzzling, unexpected or conflicting observations in epithelia, red blood cells, malaria-infected red blood cells, reticulocytes, sickle cells, and plant guard cells proved essential for explaining underlying mechanisms in many experimental, physiological and pathological contexts and for elucidating conflicts greatly expanding our knowledge of the cell systems investigated thus far. The transport homeostasis loop is an ancient circuit that preserves cellular integrity. In this cycle, metabolic ATP powers families of membrane pumps that sustain ionic gradients across plasma membranes. These gradients act as secondary sources of energy for the passive transport of ions through channels and through ion-coupled solute carriers. These, in turn, supply the substrates for metabolic ATP production and for the biosynthesis of proteins, lipids, RNA and DNA that replace decayed membrane transporters, closing the transport homeostasis loop. This review outlines the foundational principles applied when developing models of this dynamic circuit and of the achievements resulting from their application in different cell types.

items.title: Patient and public involvement in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis research in Japan: a survey through nationally advertised ALS Café events and a pilot advocacy training program.
items.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) remains an incurable, progressive neurodegenerative disease. Patient and public involvement (PPI) has been increasingly recognized as a means to enhance the relevance, quality, and efficiency of research; however, its implementation in intractable neurological disease research remains limited in Japan. This webinar-based study, conducted through nationally advertised ALS Café events, aimed to clarify current PPI awareness among the Japanese ALS community and to explore strategies for promoting patient advocacy. Data were collected during the "ALS Café" held in September 2024 and a subsequent patient advocacy training program organized in October 2025. Among 79 respondents (42 patients with ALS and 37 caregivers), approximately 80% reported being unfamiliar with the concept of PPI, yet 72.2% expressed willingness to participate once the concept was explained. Among the 57 respondents willing to participate, interest was highest for involvement in translating research findings into practice (56.1%) and in identifying research themes (47.4%), and most (93%) stated that they expected no remuneration beyond reimbursement of expenses. The subsequent training program was well received, with mean evaluation scores exceeding 8.0 on a 0-10 scale, indicating high comprehensibility among participants (changes in knowledge or willingness to participate were not assessed). Respondents were a self-selected group of ALS Café participants with limited demographic characterization who may not represent patients and caregivers who do not participate in such events, and the training program evaluation lacked a pre-training baseline; these limitations should be considered when interpreting our findings. These findings reveal substantial stated willingness among Japanese patients with ALS and their caregivers to contribute to research despite low baseline awareness of PPI. This gap between limited awareness and high stated willingness suggests that targeted educational efforts could meaningfully expand patient engagement in ALS research. Systematic awareness-building initiatives, structured and accessible engagement opportunities, and sustained collaborative relationships between researchers and the patient community are essential for strengthening patient advocacy and accelerating drug development for ALS in Japan.

items.title: Smartphone and Highly Visual Social Media Use Following Acute Treatment for Anorexia Nervosa: Associations With Eating Disorder Severity and Clinical Impairment.
items.abstract: Anorexia nervosa (AN) has high relapse risk following acute treatment. Though highly visual social media (HVSM; e.g., Instagram, TikTok) use is associated with higher eating disorder (ED) psychopathology, little research has examined HVSM use during this vulnerable period. This study characterized digital engagement of women recovering from AN and investigated associations between digital engagement and ED psychopathology. Participants were N = 90 cisgender women discharged from acute AN treatment within the past 2 months, recruited for a pilot trial evaluating a digital relapse-prevention tool. Baseline surveys assessed smartphone and HVSM use, content-specific engagement, and ED psychopathology (Eating Disorder Examination-Questionnaire; Clinical Impairment Assessment). Spearman correlations and multivariable regression models were used to evaluate relationships between these variables. Instagram was the most used platform (93.3%), followed by Facebook, YouTube, Snapchat, and TikTok. Controlling for covariates, HVSM use was significantly associated with ED severity (b = 0.441, 95% CI [0.108, 0.774]) and clinical impairment (b = 3.443, 95% CI [0.602, 6.285]). Viewing and posting ED content on HVSM were each associated with greater ED severity; viewing ED content was additionally associated with clinical impairment. Engagement with ED recovery content was not associated with ED psychopathology and did not attenuate associations between HVSM use and ED psychopathology. HVSM use and ED content engagement were associated with elevated ED psychopathology in women recently discharged from AN treatment. Descriptive patterns suggest algorithmic delivery of ED content through greater reported exposure than intentional following. Clinicians may consider assessing and planning HVSM behaviors during treatment and the post-acute recovery period.

items.title: A Precision-Delivered Singlet Oxygen Generator With an Inbuilt Safety Switch for Induction of Pancreatic Beta Cell Stress and Death.
items.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin dependence. Preclinical models have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of T1D. Chemical agents such as streptozotocin or alloxan are widely used to induce beta cell destruction without the need for genetic alteration. However, streptozotocin and alloxan exhibit variable efficacy, can be taken up non-specifically into other organs, and possess carcinogenic properties. As such, there is a need for more specific and less toxic models of beta cell stress. Here, we design and evaluate ROXendin668, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) agonist coupled to a singlet oxygen (1O2) sensitizer. ROXendin668 targets pancreatic beta cells through engagement of GLP1R and potentially GCGR, followed by red light-controlled generation of 1O2. Upon illumination, ROXendin668 selectively ablates MIN6 β-cells and primary islet β-cells and induces localized β-cell stress in vivo after systemic delivery. Thus, ROXendin668 represents a precise, controllable, and potentially safer alternative to existing chemical models of beta cell stress.

items.title: Transdiagnostic metacognitive therapy compared to disorder-specific cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety disorders: a study protocol for a randomized controlled superiority trial.
items.abstract: Anxiety disorders are highly prevalent worldwide and are associated with functional impairment, reduced quality of life and high societal costs. With only approximately 50% of patients achieving remission following cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), the evaluation of other effective treatments is warranted. Studies suggest that metacognitive therapy (MCT) may be more effective than CBT for anxiety disorders. Although transdiagnostic treatment may be beneficial for treatment implementation and dissemination in routine care, there is currently only one adequately powered study comparing transdiagnostic MCT (tMCT) to disorder-specific CBT for anxiety disorders. The main aim of this trial is to investigate the effectiveness of tMCT compared to disorder-specific CBT for anxiety disorders. The trial also aims to investigate potential mediators of treatment effects in tMCT and CBT, to conduct a health economic evaluation and to explore patients' perspectives on the treatments. This trial is a prospective, pragmatic, two-arm parallel-group randomized controlled superiority trial comparing tMCT with disorder-specific CBT, conducted in outpatient psychiatric services in Stockholm, Sweden. A sample of 86 adults with a principal diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder, social anxiety disorder or posttraumatic stress disorder will be recruited and randomly allocated to tMCT or CBT. Primary outcomes are self-rated symptoms of principal diagnosis, and secondary outcomes are clinical severity, remission rates, depressive symptoms, functional impairment and quality of life. Outcomes will be assessed at pre- and post-treatment as well as at 6- and 12-month follow-up. Metacognitions and cognitions as potential mediators will be measured weekly during treatment. Cost-effectiveness of tMCT compared to CBT will be investigated. Semi-structured interviews will be conducted with participants from both conditions. Considering the potential of MCT, further research is needed to evaluate its effectiveness compared to CBT, particularly MCT in a transdiagnostic format. Results from this trial will add to the evidence base for tMCT and inform treatment development, decision-making and implementation of effective treatment for anxiety disorders in routine care. items.title: Neural mechanisms underlying the effects of cognitive fatigue on physical effort-based choice.
items.abstract: Fatigue is a state of exhaustion that influences our willingness to engage in effortful tasks. While both physical and cognitive exertion can cause fatigue, there is a limited understanding of how fatigue in one exertion domain (e.g., cognitive) affects decisions to exert in another (e.g., physical). We first trained human participants to associate their physical exertions with a numerical scale of effort levels. Participants then completed a forced-choice task for prospective physical effort before and after completing bouts of a cognitively fatiguing working memory (3-back) task. Functional magnetic resonance imaging was used to measure brain activity during the choice and 3-back tasks. Using computational modeling of choice behavior, we found that participants reported increasing levels of cognitive and physical fatigue, but it was only the increasing feelings of cognitive fatigue that made them more risk-averse for high levels of physical effort. An analysis of the functional magnetic resonance imaging findings showed that right anterior insula encodes cognitive fatigue-induced increases in participants' subjective costs of physical effort compared with a baseline rested state, while increasing activity in right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex tracked time spent on the 3-back task. A psychophysiological interaction analysis revealed that fatigue-related activations right anterior insula and right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex are correlated and that these regions are linked in an exertion-domain general fatigue network. Our results support the idea of a general fatigue signal that integrates exertion-specific information to guide effort-based choice.

items.title: When Athletes Ask About Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy.
items.abstract: Athletes exposed to repetitive head impacts (RHI) may seek clinical evaluation because of concerns about chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a neuropathologically defined disease that cannot currently be diagnosed during life. As public awareness of CTE has expanded, clinicians face challenges communicating diagnostic uncertainty, interpreting non-specific symptoms, and addressing concerns about future neurological health. This Current Opinion examines the widening gap between public expectations and scientific capability and considers its implications for athlete-centered care. We discuss how clinicians can acknowledge uncertainty without dismissing patients' concerns, identify potentially treatable contributors to symptoms without prematurely attributing them to neurodegenerative disease, and use shared decision-making to guide individualized evaluation and management. We also consider how concerns about CTE may influence decisions about continued participation and return-to-sport among current athletes. Meeting these challenges requires coordinated interdisciplinary care, evidence-based communication, and clinical approaches that prioritize meaningful intervention even when diagnostic certainty remains unavailable.

items.title: Elevated mitochondrial metabolism in Down syndrome iPSCs reduces commitment to neuroectoderm.
items.abstract: A key feature of Down syndrome (DS) is reduced neurogenesis. Here, we provide evidence that increased mitochondrial metabolism in DS stem cells reduces their ability to commit to neuroectoderm (NE), one of the earliest steps in the development of the nervous system. We show that mitochondria in induced pluripotent stem cells derived from individuals with DS (3S-iPSCs) have a higher membrane potential and increased capacity for calcium uptake via the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) compared to isogenic, euploid controls. Consequently, 3S-iPSCs proliferate faster and spend less time in G1 of the cell cycle. This reduces the opportunity for growth of a primary cilium, an important developmental signaling hub. Inhibiting MCU or slowing proliferation of 3S-iPSCs is sufficient to increase ciliation and improve commitment to NE. In summary, we provide evidence that a mitochondria-to-cilia signaling axis important during the earliest steps of neurogenesis is dysregulated in DS iPSCs.

items.title: Genotype and phenotype analyses of 689 individuals with PCDH19-clustering epilepsy.
items.abstract: PCDH19-clustering epilepsy (PCDH19-CE) is an infantile-onset neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by clusters of seizures, typically triggered by fever. PCDH19-CE follows an unusual X-linked inheritance pattern whereby heterozygous females, and males with X-chromosome disomy or pathogenic postzygotic mosaic PCDH19 variants, are affected, while hemizygous males are spared. We aggregate published PCDH19 variants and their corresponding PCDH19-CE phenotypes to analyse phenotype-genotype correlations. Data extracted from 110 publications identified 689/735 (94%) individuals with PCDH19 variants and the typical PCDH19-CE phenotype. Three hundred seventy-three unique PCDH19 variants were identified; 195 were not recorded in ClinVar. Seizure onset prior to 12 months of age was associated with more severe intellectual disability (p < 0.001) and the presence of psychiatric morbidity (p = 0.001). There were no phenotypic differences between missense, nonsense, and frameshift variants or between individuals of different geographical backgrounds, which was assessed as a proxy for ancestry. Twenty-nine hemizygous males with constitutive PCDH19 variants did not exhibit the typical PCDH19-CE phenotype, suggesting that the identification of variants in these individuals likely results from chance or ascertainment bias. The correlation between earlier seizure onset and poorer neurodevelopmental outcomes emphasises a critical window for therapeutic intervention. The lack of phenotypic difference between variant types demonstrates that loss of PCDH19 function underpins PCDH19-CE. Moreover, the identification of PCDH19 cytoplasmic domain variants in 78 affected individuals challenges the traditional view that PCDH19-CE is caused primarily by defects in cell-cell adhesion, as variants in this domain are expected to disrupt the nuclear function(s) of PCDH19.

items.title: Identification of fluid endocannabinoid and sphingolipid biomarkers in schizophrenia. A machine learning approach toward clinical value.
items.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) diagnosis relies on subjective clinical evaluation, with symptoms often overlapping between psychiatric conditions, hindering early intervention, and creating an urgent need for objective, accessible biomarkers. Lipids, especially endocannabinoid system (ECS) and sphingolipid metabolism members, are promising candidates given their implication in SCZ pathogenesis and measurability in accessible biofluids, with minimally invasive procedures. Our study conducted the first comprehensive crossover of endocannabinoids (eCBs) and sphingolipids in matched cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum samples from antipsychotic-naïve SCZ patients (SCZnaïve, n = 49), antipsychotic-treated patients (SCZtreat, n = 56), and healthy volunteers (HVs, n = 51). The machine learning Integrated Disease Explanation and Risk Scoring (IDEARS) platform was applied to eCBs, N-acylethanolamines, ceramides, and sphingomyelins quantified using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, identifying key discriminatory features across biofluids and conditions (CSF AUC: SCZnaïve = 0.87, SCZtreat = 0.94; serum AUC: SCZnaïve = 0.87, SCZtreat = 0.90). Anandamide emerged as the top CSF feature in SCZnaïve patients, showing significantly elevated levels (q = 0.010) compared to HVs. Notably, though not statistically significant under conventional statistics, IDEARS identified anandamide as a top ten serum feature. Additionally, elevated sphingadiene backbone (d18:2) sphingolipids were conserved between the CSF and serum of SCZnaïve (q C24) species potentially reflecting antipsychotic metabolic effects. Our results support the involvement of the ECS and sphingolipid imbalances in SCZ, highlighting the potential of machine learning for novel biomarker discovery, including stratification across biofluids, and therapeutic monitoring toward more objective psychiatric care.

items.title: Implementation strategies for digital relapse prevention in schizophrenia identified during a randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Digital mental health technologies hold promise, yet their integration into routine care remains challenging. This study reports findings from an implementation workshop conducted midway through an ongoing multi-site randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating a smartphone-based relapse prevention app for patients with schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder. Sixteen stakeholders, including developers, researchers, and clinicians, discussed experiences and barriers using a semi-structured agenda, incorporating prior feedback from three focus groups with people with lived experience, and analyzed the discussions using an adopted R(E)-AIM framework (Reach, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance). Findings highlight the need for structural, technical, and personnel adjustments to support sustainable implementation. Key recommendations include integrating digital tools into discharge planning, enhancing interdisciplinary collaboration, delegating digital responsibilities, and streamlining technical workflows to facilitate seamless adoption. These insights inform feasibility considerations and strategic requirements for digital interventions in severe mental illness, offering guidance for future RCTs and practice-oriented integration of digital therapeutics in psychiatric care.

items.title: Management of Chronic Subdural Hematoma in Thrombocytopenia: Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization - Based Strategies Versus Medical Management or Surgery Alone.
items.abstract: Thrombocytopenia complicates management of chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH), but no study has compared middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) with surgery or medical management in this population. We evaluated MMAE-containing strategies versus medical management or surgery alone in cSDH with platelets below 100×103/µL. Using the TriNetX Research Network, we identified adults with cSDH and platelets below 100×103/µL (or below 50×103/µL for the severe-thrombocytopenia analysis). We performed three propensity-score-matched comparisons: standalone MMAE versus medical management and surgery plus MMAE versus surgery alone at platelets <100×103/µL; and standalone MMAE versus medical management at platelets <50×103/µL. The primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality; the secondary outcome was surgical evacuation (a composite of surgical evacuation or mortality at platelets <50×103/µL). After matching, cohorts ranged from 147 to 373 patients per group (standardized mean differences below 0.10 for nearly all covariates). At platelets <100×103/µL, standalone MMAE was associated with lower mortality than medical management (26.9% vs 37.3% hazard ratio 0.65 [95% CI 0.50-0.85]), and surgery plus MMAE was associated with lower mortality than surgery alone (20.5% vs 30.7%; hazard ratio 0.61 [95% CI 0.38-0.97]). At platelets <50×103/µL, the mortality comparison between standalone MMAE and medical management did not reach significance (34.2% vs 44.0%; hazard ratio 0.72 [95% CI 0.49-1.05]). Subsequent surgical evacuation did not differ significantly in any comparison. For patients with cSDH and thrombocytopenia, management strategies incorporating MMAE were associated with lower 90-day mortality than medical management or surgery alone. Prospective confirmation is needed, including in severe thrombocytopenia, where the mortality comparison did not reach significance.

items.title: Memory reactivation alters the fate of neutral episodic memories following a subsequent independent experience.
items.abstract: Memory reactivation may lead to strengthening, weakening, or updating depending on the experience that follows retrieval. Although post-reactivation modification has been shown for emotional, aversive, and naturalistic episodic memories, it remains unclear whether a consolidated neutral memory for an everyday-like event can be distorted when reactivation is followed by a subsequent independent episodic experience. Yet memories that later become relevant for testimony often initially concern neutral everyday events, such as conversations, routine encounters, or the presence of a person in a given context. Here, we examined whether a consolidated complex neutral episodic memory could be modified when reactivation was followed by a subsequent independent episodic experience. Participants encoded a neutral audiovisual story and returned one week later for an incomplete reminder designed to reactivate the original memory. After reactivation, one group encoded a second neutral audiovisual story, whereas another group received the reminder only. Two control groups either encoded the second story without prior reactivation or received no reminder. One week later, memory was assessed using free recall, cued recall, recognition, and temporal order tasks. Exposure to the second episodic experience was associated with reduced accurate recall and increased memory distortions. Critically, participants whose original memory was reactivated before encoding Story 2 later incorporated significantly more accessory details from Story 2 into their recall of Story 1 than participants who encoded Story 2 without prior reactivation. In contrast, reminder-only reactivation was associated with better preservation and fewer distortions. These effects were expressed primarily in free recall. Thus, prior reactivation was associated with greater incorporation of information from a subsequent independent episode into the original memory.

items.title: MDMA-Assisted Therapy for Veterans with Comorbid Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Alcohol Use Disorder: Clinical Outcomes from the First Open-Label Pilot Trial.
items.abstract: Co-occurring posttraumatic stress disorder and alcohol use disorder (PTSD-AUD) are highly prevalent among U.S. Veterans and associated with greater symptom severity, functional impairment, and poorer outcomes than either disorder alone. Existing treatments demonstrate modest effectiveness, with persistent challenges in engagement, retention, and sustained improvement. To evaluate the feasibility, safety, tolerability, and preliminary clinical outcomes of investigational 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA)-assisted therapy for Veterans with comorbid PTSD-AUD. We conducted the first open-label trial of MDMA-assisted therapy in Veterans (N = 10) with PTSD-AUD. The intervention included 11 therapy sessions (three preparatory, two MDMA assisted therapy sessions, and six integration), followed by a 4-week follow-up. Primary outcomes were PTSD symptom severity and alcohol consumption, measured by the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) and Timeline Follow-Back (TLFB). Secondary outcomes assessed safety and tolerability. Exploratory outcomes included alcohol craving and substance misuse. Recruitment and retention were strong with 90% of enrolled participants completing treatment. MDMA-assisted therapy was associated with significant reductions in PTSD symptoms (p = 0.006, d = 1.241). Descriptive reductions were observed in alcohol consumption, including a 31% reduction in drinks per drinking day and a 54% reduction in heavy drinking days, although these changes did not reach clinical significance. No serious adverse events were reported. Treatment-emergent adverse events were non-serious and consistent with expected acute MDMA effects under protocol monitoring. Substance-use measures did not indicate systematic increases in alcohol or other substance use; one participant reported an isolated recurrence of cocaine use. Findings support the safety, feasibility, and tolerability of MDMA-assisted therapy and provide preliminary descriptive evidence of improvement in PTSD symptoms and alcohol-related outcomes. Larger randomized controlled trials are needed to evaluate efficacy, durability, and benefit-risk profile in this population.

items.title: The metabolic-brain axis: GLP-1 signaling, insulin resistance, and obesity pharmacotherapy in neurodegeneration.
items.abstract: The intersection of metabolic disease and neurodegeneration represents one of the most consequential frontiers in translational neuroscience. Converging epidemiological, mechanistic, and pharmacological evidence supports a bidirectional metabolic-brain axis in which systemic insulin resistance, obesity, and chronic metabolic inflammation are associated with and may contribute to alterations in neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, and neuroimmune homeostasis. GLP-1 receptor agonists, originally developed for glycemic control and weight management, have therefore been investigated as potential disease-modifying therapies across Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and related neurodegenerative conditions through mechanisms including neuronal PKA activation, microglial NLRP3 suppression, mitochondrial biogenesis, and restoration of AQP4 perivascular localization that may contribute to glymphatic waste clearance. Direct human evidence for these CNS mechanisms remains limited or absent, with current support derived primarily from preclinical models and indirect human data, as detailed in Table 1, warranting dedicated investigation in the context of GLP-1 receptor agonism. Importantly, the two pivotal phase 3 programs designed to test this hypothesis in humans - EVOKE/EVOKE+ in early Alzheimer's disease and Exenatide-PD3 in Parkinson's disease - have both now reported, and neither demonstrated a statistically significant benefit on its primary clinical endpoint, despite favorable biomarker and epidemiological signals preceding these results. This review synthesizes current knowledge on brain insulin signaling, GLP-1 neurobiology, obesity-driven neuroinflammation, and the translational evidence for metabolic therapeutics in neurodegeneration, and uses the dissociation between mechanistic plausibility, epidemiological association, and null confirmatory trial results to identify critical knowledge gaps and translational barriers related to CNS target engagement, optimal dosing, and disease-modifying efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists. The review is organized into four major themes: brain insulin signaling, central GLP-1 biology, obesity-associated neuroinflammation, and the translational evidence supporting metabolic therapies for neurodegenerative disease.

items.title: CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS AND OUTCOMES IN ADULTS WITH BACTERIAL MENINGITIS AND NEGATIVE CEREBROSPINAL FLUID CULTURES.
items.abstract: Ten to thirty percent of patients with bacterial meningitis have negative CSF cultures, yet their clinical characteristics and outcome remain poorly defined. Between 2006 and 2023, adults with bacterial meningitis were prospectively included in a nationwide cohort study. Patients with negative CSF cultures were compared to those with positive CSF cultures. Outcome was assessed using the Glasgow Outcome Scale, with scores of 1-4 classified as unfavourable. CSF samples from microbiology-negative patients underwent additional testing with the IS-pro assay, a broad-spectrum PCR technique. CSF cultures were negative in 413 of 3,132 episodes (13%). A pathogen was identified in 328 (80%) through blood culture, CSF bacterial PCR, or antigen testing, leaving 85 episodes without microbiological confirmation. Patients with negative CSF cultures more often received pre-admission antibiotics (13% vs 10%, p=0.02) and had lower rates of unfavourable outcome (29% vs 39%, p<0.001). Blood cultures were positive in 53%, and CSF PCR detected a pathogen in 49%. The IS-pro assay detected Streptococcus pneumoniae (n=5), Streptococcus bovis group/Streptococcus intermedius (n=5), and Streptococcus constellatus (n=1). Bacterial meningitis patients with negative CSF cultures have more favourable outcomes. Combining CSF cultures with blood cultures and CSF PCR improves pathogen detection, while broad-spectrum PCR may help identify atypical pathogens.

items.title: Recent Advances in Immunomodulatory Biomaterial Strategies for Neural Tissue Healing.
items.abstract: Central and peripheral nervous system injuries represent major causes of neurological disability worldwide, yet current treatment methods are limited by issues including donor site morbidity, regenerative capacity, and tissue availability. Engineered biomaterials are being investigated as alternative strategies for neural tissue repair, but their regenerative efficacy remains variable, in part because of unresolved neuroinflammation and immune-mediated fibrous tissue formation. This review highlights immunomodulation as an important consideration beyond conventional biocompatibility and focuses on macrophage and microglial responses as key components of biomaterial-mediated neural repair. Here we start by outlining the distinct immunological landscapes of central and peripheral neural injury. We then examine how intrinsic material properties including stiffness, porosity, surface chemistry, electrical characteristics, and fiber alignment can influence immune cell behavior. Within this framework, we survey recent preclinical studies of major biomaterial platforms and distinguish, where experimental controls permit, intrinsic material-mediated effects from those produced by incorporated therapeutic cargos. Finally, we discuss the field's inconsistent phenotyping standards, reliance on rodent models, and common failure to assess long-term immunogenicity. Progress toward translation will require rigorous multi-marker characterization of immune-cell states, tissue- and injury-specific interpretation, standardized longitudinal assessment, and stronger integration of immunological outcomes with regenerative and functional endpoints. Collectively, these considerations position immunomodulation as a central design principle for the development of biomaterials for neural tissue repair. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Neural injuries often fail to heal because inflammation persists and implanted materials can promote scar formation. This review moves beyond describing biomaterials as simply biocompatible by evaluating how their physical and chemical properties actively shape macrophage and microglial behavior. By comparing recent strategies across peripheral and central nervous system repair, we identify immune-cell polarization as a central design target and examine how stiffness, porosity, alignment, surface chemistry, degradation, and therapeutic cargo influence healing. We also highlight major limitations in the literature, including inconsistent immune markers, limited long-term testing, and reliance on rodent models. This framework can guide the development of safer, more effective neural repair materials while improving the rigor and clinical relevance of future studies.

items.title: EEG Feature-level integration for robust command generation in SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces.
items.abstract: Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have been widely studied for efficient command generation via spatiotemporal information integration and advanced stimulation paradigms. However, users may intentionally or unintentionally suppress SSVEP responses, leading to the SSVEP Blocking Response (SSVEP-BR). This phenomenon, characterized by attenuation or disappearance of SSVEP, has been largely overlooked despite its potential for command generation without additional stimuli. This study aimed to exploit SSVEP-BR to enhance command generation under limited visual stimulation. A novel detection method was proposed based on alpha rhythm sensitivity during transitions between SSVEP and SSVEP-BR states. An EEG feature-level integration strategy was further developed to integrate correlation and alpha rhythm features, enabling effective characterization of their temporal evolution. An asynchronous BCI system was implemented for real-time robotic arm control. Experiments on 11 offline subjects demonstrated that the proposed method improved SSVEP-BR detection performance. Compared with the previous SSVEP-BR detection framework, average improvements of 17.11%, 8.50%, and 5.44% were achieved in precision, recall, and specificity, respectively. Furthermore, an online robotic grasping experiment was conducted with 5 subjects, where the proposed asynchronous BCI system achieved 8-command generation using two stimulation frequencies. Unlike prior studies focusing on algorithmic optimization or stimulation design, this work introduced SSVEP-BR as an additional controllable neural response and demonstrated its effectiveness in improving command generation without increasing stimulus complexity. Incorporating SSVEP-BR into SSVEP-based BCI frameworks improved flexibility and robustness, enhancing the practicality of asynchronous brain computer interaction systems.

items.title: Within-state transcriptional remodelling predominates in a 41-gene ageing programme of human prefrontal OPCs.
items.abstract: Ageing impairs oligodendrocyte precursor cell (OPC) function, but it is unclear whether age-related transcriptional changes in the human cortex mainly reflect shifts in OPC-state composition or remodelling within transcriptionally defined states. We defined a bidirectional 41-gene OPC ageing programme (22 age-down and 19 age-up genes) and tested it in two external cortical single-nucleus datasets that were not used for gene selection. The age-down and age-up components showed the expected associations in each dataset. In paired RNA-chromatin profiles from 349 donors, formal decomposition showed that within-state change accounted for 98.8-99.5% of the programme's adjusted cell-mean contrast, whereas composition accounted for 0.8-1.2% under the primary clustering configuration; composition point estimates remained approximately 2% or less across five clustering resolutions and three representations. The relative occupancy of a commitment-associated OPC state declined with age in both donor sources after adjustment for sampled OPC depth, but removing this state left the broad programme essentially unchanged. Promoter accessibility changed in parallel with the RNA programme and correlated with paired RNA scores. The decomposition applies to the adjusted contrast of this 41-gene programme, and the occupancy estimate describes sampled OPC nuclei rather than absolute tissue abundance. Together, the results distinguish transcriptional remodelling distributed across OPC states from a focused change in commitment-associated state representation.

items.title: Glia proliferation and heterogeneity in CMT1A: Involvement of RUNX2-Schwann cells and endoneurial fibroblasts.
items.abstract: Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 1 A (CMT1A) is the most common inherited peripheral neuropathy, caused by duplication of the peripheral myelin protein 22 (PMP22) gene and characterized by dysmyelination and defects in myelin maturation. Hypercellularity, defined as an abnormal increase in the number of cells within a tissue, is a prominent feature of the disease, although its origin, persistence, and underlying mechanisms remain controversial. Here, we performed a time-course analysis of sciatic nerves from wild-type (WT) and CMT1A rats between 2 and 12 months of age. We demonstrated that CMT1A nerves exhibit persistent cellular proliferation extending into adulthood. This phenotype is confirmed by bulk RNA-seq data showing sustained enrichment of proliferation-associated gene signatures. Cell-type signature analysis identifies overrepresentation of immature, neural crest-related, and epithelial-mesenchymal transitional (EMT) transcriptional programs in CMT1A nerves. Among the most upregulated genes, RUNX2 showed strong and prolonged expression at both transcript and protein levels. Consistently with the key role of RUNX2 in the activation of the injury response, CMT1A nerves also showed a marked enrichment both in SOX10+/JUN+ cells and in SOX10+/RUNX2+ cells, indicating a maladaptive activation of the injury-like Schwann cell (SC) program. Interestingly, we detected robust upregulation of SMOC2, an extracellular matrix protein selectively expressed by endoneurial fibroblasts, pointing to activation of non-canonical cell types and altered extracellular matrix remodeling. Together, these data demonstrate that CMT1A peripheral nerves are characterized by chronic hypercellularity associated with persistent proliferation, EMT, and dysregulated injury transcriptional programs, collectively pointing at progressive and multicellular nerve remodeling as a relevant pathomechanism in the disease.

items.title: Effects of a prolonged distance run on plantar vibration perception.
items.abstract: During a half marathon, the foot is exposed to prolonged repetitive mechanical loading, which may affect plantar mechanosensory function. This study investigated changes in whole-foot vibration perception threshold (WF-VPT) after a half marathon. Using a pre-post-design, 23 recreational runners participated. Overall, data from 20 participants were analysed after three participants were excluded as outliers. WF-VPT were assessed, after 10-min acclimatization period at room temperature, before and after the half-marathon using a vibration exciter platform at 30 and 200 Hz. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests showed a significant increase in WF-VPT at 30 Hz (p = 0.02) and a significant decrease in WF-VPT at 200 Hz (p = 0.001). At 30 Hz, the median (interquartile range) WF-VPT increased from 1.77 (1.50-2.36) µm before exercise to 2.08 (1.87-2.83) µm after the half marathon. In contrast, at 200 Hz WF-VPT decreased from 0.09 (0.08-0.12) µm to 0.06 (0.04-0.10) µm. Furthermore, linear mixed-effects models assessed the effects of age, plantar temperature, and gender on WF-VPT at 30 and 200 Hz. Only age showed a significant positive association with WF-VPT at both frequencies. The frequency-specific changes in WF-VPT may be associated with differential contributions of mechanosensory pathways involved in low- and high-frequency vibration perception. Differences in the structural and functional properties of these pathways may influence how they respond to mechanical stimulation and running-related loading.

items.title: Microglia TREM1 promotes lipid droplet accumulation and microglia M1 polarization via NF-κB pathway to induce neuroinflammation-mediated central sensitization in chronic migraine.
items.abstract: Chronic migraine (CM) is closely associated with neuroinflammation and central sensitization. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1 (TREM1) regulates glial inflammatory activation, yet its precise role in CM pathogenesis remains unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the specific function and underlying mechanism of TREM1 in driving CM progression. A nitroglycerin (NTG)-induced mouse CM model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated BV2 microglial model were established. Then, western blot, immunofluorescence, and ELISA were performed to evaluate TREM1 expression, central sensitization, microglial polarization, lipid metabolism, and neuroinflammation. Furthermore, BV2 cells were stimulated with TREM1 antagonists LP17 or IKKβ overexpression plasmids to explore the effect of TREM1 and NF-κB pathway involved in the microglial polarization and lipid metabolism in CM. NTG challenge significantly upregulated TREM1 expression in TNC microglia of CM mice, and triggered abnormal microglial M1/M2 polarization and increased the expression of central sensitization-associated markers (c-fos and CGRP), as well as the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-1β). In vitro, TREM1 inhibition by LP17 treatment significantly attenuated LPS-induced LDs accumulation, neuroinflammation and shifted microglial polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype in BV2 cells. However, overexpression of IKKβ effectively reversed the protective effects of LP17 in LPS-stimulated BV2 cells, restoring LDs accumulation, microglia polarization, and pro-inflammatory cytokine release. TREM1 promotes microglial LDs accumulation and M1 polarization via the NF-κB pathway to induce neuroinflammation-mediated central sensitization in CM.

items.title: The neurobiology of menopause: Implications for brain aging and Alzheimer's risk.
items.abstract: A growing body of evidence implicates the menopausal transition as a neurobiological inflection point in women's brain aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) vulnerability. Menopause is a midlife neuroendocrine transition characterized by a decline in sex steroid hormones and widespread systemic effects. The brain is not a passive recipient of ovarian hormones but an active endocrine-sensing organ. Menopause, however, does not act in isolation: the ovarian-brain axis is established embryonically, activated at puberty, remodeled during pregnancy and postpartum, and reconfigured during the menopausal transition, with implications for later-life brain aging. This review places menopause within a lifespan neuroendocrine framework, examining mechanisms by which the transition may influence the brain, including altered hormone signaling, bioenergetics, synaptic plasticity, neurovascular function, inflammation, and AD-related pathology. It then reviews evidence linking menopausal timing to neurobiological and AD vulnerability, discusses estrogen therapy, and considers menopause as a biologically plausible window for risk stratification and prevention.
