items.title: ERIS2: A deep-learning platform for predicting mutation-induced protein stability changes.
items.abstract: Accurately predicting changes in protein thermodynamic stability upon mutation is a fundamental challenge in protein engineering and therapeutics. Deep learning has improved prediction, but many models remain limited by small, imbalanced training data and poor generalization across mutation types. Here, we present ERIS2, an attention-convolutional deep learning framework that integrates contextual sequence embeddings with atomistic and residue-level structural features from experimental protein structures to predict mutation-induced stability changes. Trained on large-scale experimental measurements combined with curated ProTherm data, a 5-fold ERIS2 ensemble achieved Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.69 on S461, 0.51 on S669, and 0.60 on S96, three blind-test datasets sequence-disjoint from all training configurations, and showed negligible anti-symmetry bias on Ssym forward and reverse pairs. ERIS2 is freely available as a structure-based web server without registration, providing a robust framework for protein stability prediction and advancing computational tools for protein engineering and therapeutic design.

items.title: Psychological resilience is associated with increased heterogeneity in the clinical aging phenotypes of patients with cancer.
items.abstract: Cancer and its treatments are associated with accelerated aging. Emerging evidence suggests that patients' self-reports of symptoms, functional status, and resilience can identify clinical aging phenotypes. The purpose was to identify distinct clinical aging phenotypes using: six (evening fatigue, sleep disturbance, depression, state anxiety, cognitive function, physical function); seven (addition of pain); and eight (addition of resilience) clinical indicators and evaluate for differences in patient characteristics and quality of life (QOL) outcomes among the phenotypes. Outpatients (n = 1340) completed questionnaires prior to their second or third cycle of chemotherapy. Three separate latent variable models using six, seven, and eight clinical indicators were created. Differences among phenotypes in demographic and clinical characteristics and QOL outcomes were evaluated using parametric and non-parametric tests. Determination of clinically meaningful differences in QOL scores was done using Cohen's d. For the six and seven indicator models, two and three distinct phenotypes were identified, respectively. For the eight indicator model, five distinct phenotypes were identified: Very Low (32.6%), Low (32.2%), Moderate (16.4%), High (13.2%), and Very High (5.6%) clinical age. Being female, younger, having a higher comorbidity burden, and lower functional status were associated with the worst clinical aging profiles. QOL scores decreased in a stepwise fashion and differences were clinically meaningful. Inclusion of a measure of psychological resilience in the model allows for better discrimination of inter-individual variability in clinical aging phenotypes of oncology outpatients. This approach may assist with identification of patients at increased risk for accelerated aging.

items.title: Clinical correlates of complete versus partial remission in major depressive disorder: an exploratory analysis of three cohorts.
items.abstract: Remission in major depressive disorder (MDD) is conventionally defined as a 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) score ≤7, but patients within this range may retain residual symptoms. We explored whether complete remission (HAMD-17 <4) and partial remission (HAMD-17 4-7) differ in baseline clinical features, symptom trajectories and endpoint functioning. Three cohorts were analysed separately: GSRD (N=2583, cross-sectional, tertiary centres), PANDORA (N=215, week 12) and STAR*D level 1 (N=1565). We estimated effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals, false discovery rate (FDR) correction, adjusted and imputed models, alternative cut-offs, individual symptom trajectories and cross-validated discrimination. Baseline differences between complete and partial remitters were small (median absolute standardized difference 0.08-0.15). No baseline variable survived FDR correction; only a concurrent severe-episode rating in GSRD did (odds ratio 2.10, 95% CI 1.43-3.07). In STAR*D, partial remitters had slightly higher baseline HAMD-17 (g=0.15, 95% CI 0.00-0.31), and most item-level associations were explained by overall severity. Baseline features did not discriminate the groups in individual patients (cross-validated AUC 0.42-0.55). Symptom scores of the two groups separated within 4-6 weeks and did not converge during follow-up. In STAR*D, the estimated rate of improvement did not differ detectably, and the model-estimated asymptote was higher in partial remitters. At STAR*D exit, partial remitters had worse work and social adjustment (g=0.45) and quality of life (g=-0.63) despite similar baseline values. Complete and partial remission identify different endpoint states, but baseline clinical features predict this distinction poorly. These exploratory findings require prospective confirmation.

items.title: Constantin von Economo (1876-1931): cytoarchitectonic roots of modern network neuroscience.
items.abstract: Constantin von Economo (1876-1931) is widely remembered for his seminal description of encephalitis lethargica, yet his broader contribution to cortical organization remains underappreciated. Beyond clinical neurology, von Economo and Georg Koskinas, a neurologist-psychiatrist, contributed to the broader cytoarchitectonic tradition by developing one of the most detailed architectonic frameworks of the human cerebral cortex, emphasizing laminar heterogeneity, regional transition, and structural specialization. These concepts can be reconsidered in relation to contemporary models of large-scale brain organization. In particular, cortical territories associated with von Economo's work, including the anterior insula and anterior cingulate region, are now recognized as key hubs in salience processing and contain the distinctive spindle-shaped neurons later termed von Economo neurons. Recent advances in connectomics, cortical gradient mapping, and laminar neuroimaging have renewed interest in the relationship between cortical microstructure and distributed functional networks. From this perspective, von Economo's work may be viewed not simply as a landmark in classical neuroanatomy, but as a historically important structural framework that can be reinterpreted in relation to modern ideas of structure-function coupling and network-level brain organization. This historical vignette revisits his life, scientific contributions, and enduring relevance to contemporary neuroscience and neurosurgical thinking.

items.title: Involvement of users and caregivers in mental healthcare decision-making within low-and middle-income countries: A scoping review.
items.abstract: Inclusive healthcare decision-making is a cornerstone of recovery-oriented mental health services, contributing to improved outcomes, enhanced autonomy, and reduced stigma. While substantial research on mental healthcare decision-making has been conducted in high-income countries, there is limited evidence from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where sociocultural norms, family structures, and health system constraints may shape decision-making differently. This review sought to synthesise evidence on service user and caregiver involvement in mental healthcare decision-making in LMICs and identify contextual factors influencing these processes. A scoping review was conducted following Arksey and O'Malley's five-stage framework. English-language studies from 2008 to 2025 were identified through databases and grey literature searches. Eligible studies extracted examined the involvement of people with mental health conditions and/or caregivers in mental healthcare decision-making within LMICs. Two reviewers independently coded descriptions of involvement using an inductive content analysis approach. Three overarching themes emerged: (1) active user involvement, reflecting service users' participation in and co-creation of decisions about their care; (2) family dominance, where family members significantly influenced or controlled decision-making processes; and (3) drivers of decision-making, including cultural norms, stigma, economic hardship, social relationships, and health system constraints. Overall, decision-making was predominantly shaped by family authority and contextual factors, with relatively limited evidence of shared or supported decision-making approaches. The search yielded 21,830 records, with an additional 46 studies identified through grey literature searches. Following screening, 36 studies were included. Studies were conducted across Africa (n = 12), Asia (n = 22), and the Middle East (n = 2). Mental healthcare decision-making in LMICs is embedded within complex family, cultural, and structural contexts that both enable and constrain service user participation. This review contributes to promoting a contextualised understanding of mental healthcare decision-making in LMICs.

items.title: A randomised feasibility trial of VR-enhanced cue exposure therapy versus neutral VR exposure for cocaine use disorder, with wearable monitoring and JITA-EMA: Feasibility randomised controlled trial protocol.
items.abstract: Cocaine use disorder (CUD) is associated with high rates of relapse, with craving and cue reactivity playing important roles in ongoing use. Cue Exposure Therapy (CET) aims to reduce conditioned responses to drug-related cues through extinction learning, but traditional approaches may be limited by poor ecological validity. Virtual reality-enhanced Cue Exposure Therapy (VR-CET) offers a potentially more immersive and realistic method of delivering cue exposure. Concurrently, advances in wearable physiological monitoring and just-in-time adaptive ecological momentary assessment (JITA-EMA) enable the real-time assessment of craving in everyday life. To assess the feasibility of recruitment, consent, randomisation, blinding, intervention delivery and retention over 8 weeks post-randomisation. This is a two-arm, parallel-group, randomised feasibility trial conducted in UK community drug treatment services. Sixty adults receiving treatment will be randomised (1:1) to either VR-CET or an active VR-Relaxation control condition. Both arms will receive six VR sessions over four weeks, alongside continuous physiological monitoring using a wearable device and smartphone-based JITA-EMA for eight weeks. Feasibility outcomes will include recruitment, retention, intervention adherence, wearable wear time, EMA completion, acceptability, and safety. Clinical outcomes will include cocaine use measured by Timeline Follow-Back, cue reactivity assessed through subjective and physiological measures, and participant-confirmed craving episodes captured via wearable-triggered JITA-EMA. Qualitative interviews with participants and service providers will explore intervention acceptability and implementation facilitators, barriers and suggestions. Planned start date is July 2026, and enrolment is due to end in April 2027. Data analysis is estimated to be completed by the end of spring 2027. To our knowledge, this is the first feasibility RCT of VR-CET for CUD within UK drug treatment services. Results from this trial will help assess the feasibility of integrating VR-CET, continuous physiological monitoring, and real-time craving JITA within CUD treatment. This can be used to inform the design of a future definitive trial and contribute to the development of personalised, technology-enabled approaches to relapse prevention and substance treatment. Trial registration: ISRCTN21409750, https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN21409750.

items.title: LAMP2A gene therapy mitigates Parkinson's disease-related pathology in nonhuman primates.
items.abstract: Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), regulated by its lysosomal receptor LAMP2A, is a key pathway for αSynuclein (αSyn) clearance and a direct target of αSyn-related neurotoxicity. Rodent studies show that LAMP2A enhancement reverses neurodegeneration, whereas its deficiency accelerates pathology. To test translational relevance, we examined whether increasing LAMP2A expression in nonhuman primates could mitigate α-synucleinopathy induced by injections of Parkinson's disease patient-derived Lewy body (LB) extract. Increasing LAMP2A expression protected nigral dopaminergic neurons from LB-induced αSyn neurodegeneration, delayed the formation and release of pathology-related αSyn species, and evoked a beneficial effect on motor behavior and on cognitive functions of the primate model. Our findings provide preliminary preclinical evidence supporting CMA enhancement as a therapeutic strategy for αSynucleinopathies.

items.title: Psychological flexibility in the work-caregiving interplay of employed family caregivers of people with dementia (DAILY-FLEX): Protocol of an experience sampling study.
items.abstract: Employed family caregivers of people with dementia face competing work and caregiving demands that can negatively affect well-being across both domains. The Work-Home Resources model proposes that demands and resources influence cross-domain functioning through changes in personal resources. Psychological flexibility (PF), the ability to remain open to difficult experiences while acting in line with personal values, may represent a dynamic personal resource in this process. However, its real-time role in the daily work-caregiving interface remains largely unknown. This protocol describes the DAILY-FLEX study, which aims to investigate momentary and daily bidirectional spillover between work and caregiving demands/resources and domain-specific well-being, and to examine whether PF mediates these associations. This observational intensive longitudinal study uses Experience Sampling Methodology combined with baseline assessment. A minimum of 30 employed family caregivers of people with dementia will be recruited in the Netherlands through memory clinics, caregiver networks, and community outreach. Participants will complete a baseline questionnaire followed by a 14-day ESM protocol consisting of eight semi-random momentary assessments and one evening questionnaire per day using the m-Path smartphone application. Momentary assessments capture contextual demands and resources, PF, caregiving-related affect, and work engagement. Evening questionnaires assess daily work and caregiving demands/resources, PF, general well-being, and daily job satisfaction. Multilevel mixed-effects models and longitudinal mediation analyses will be used to examine lagged cross-domain spillover and PF as a within-person mediator. This study provides a fine-grained examination of how work and caregiving interact in daily life among employed family caregivers of people with dementia. By focusing on PF as a dynamic mediating mechanism, the study may identify actionable targets for tailored psychosocial interventions and workplace support strategies aimed at improving caregiver well-being and sustainable employment.

items.title: BitterBuster: A virtual world for understanding naturalistic patch foraging.
items.abstract: The past decade has seen a resurgence of interest in the naturalistic behavior of patch foraging in both the neural and cognitive sciences. Patch foraging is observed throughout the animal kingdom and requires the integration of multiple cognitive processes, including value and perceptual learning, spatial estimation, the evaluation of instantaneous return rates, and anticipating future effort. Here, we present a novel virtual environment, BitterBuster, for studying patch foraging in humans. In the BitterBuster game, players navigate a virtual world with four neighborhoods (patches) populated with houses (harvest points) containing inhabitants known as "Oomplets". The goal is to search for "bitter" Oomplets, characterized by the union of specific body colors and textures. Each neighborhood has a different overall probability of containing bitter Oomplets and, within each, specific house locations predict the relative rate of bitter Oomplets. BitterBuster can be used for solo or team based foraging, where the tasks of exploring and perceptual learning are implemented by two separate players working together. Our results show how both the solo and team version of BitterBuster can accurately measure multiple aspects of naturalistic patch foraging, with participants learning to identify optimal patches, classify harvestable resources, and make rational decisions about when to leave a patch before overharvesting. BitterBuster is well-suited for researchers interested in the contextual, neural, and cooperative dynamics of foraging.

items.title: Development of iADJUST: a theory-informed, patient co-designed digital psychological intervention for adjustment in chronic kidney disease.
items.abstract: Psychological distress is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and associated with reduced quality of life and worse clinical outcomes, partly reflecting difficulties adjusting to illness demands. Psychological support remains inconsistently integrated within kidney care pathways, and existing interventions rarely specify or target the mechanisms underpinning adjustment to CKD. This paper describes the systematic development of iADJUST, a theory-informed patient co-designed digital psychological intervention targeting key cognitive and behavioural mechanisms involved in adjustment to CKD. Intervention development was guided by the Medical Research Council framework and integrated empirical evidence, psychological theory, and patient and public involvement and engagement. The Common-Sense Model of Self-Regulation and cognitive behavioural theories informed identification of modifiable maintaining mechanisms of adjustment to CKD. Intervention components were mapped onto these mechanisms and refined through co-design with people living with CKD. iADJUST is a six-session, primarily self-guided digital psychological intervention for adults with CKD who are not on dialysis or transplanted, delivered over 12 weeks with brief therapist support. It targets illness-related uncertainty, fatigue-related activity dysregulation, catastrophic "what-if" thinking, self-critical evaluation, behavioural withdrawal, and self-regulation processes relevant to maintenance and relapse prevention. It integrates psychoeducation, cognitive and behavioural strategies, maintenance planning, and elements from acceptance and commitment therapy and compassion-focused approaches, delivered through video, audio, and guided tasks and activities. iADJUST provides a theory- and evidence-informed psychological intervention for CKD explicitly mapping intervention components to maintaining cognitive and behavioural mechanisms of adjustment. Its feasibility is being evaluated in a randomised waitlist-controlled feasibility trial (ISRCTN91507822).

items.title: Pain, but not hypermobility, is associated with borderline personality disorder symptoms among individuals diagnosed with EDS or G-HSD.
items.abstract: Research examining borderline personality disorder (BPD) in individuals with Ehlers-Danlos Syndromes (EDS) and Generalized Hypermobility Spectrum Disorder (G-HSD) is limited, despite overlap between core BPD features (e.g., emotion dysregulation) and common EDS/G-HSD conditions (e.g., chronic pain). This study examined associations between BPD symptoms and EDS/G-HSD features. Data were from a retrospective chart review of patients evaluated at the GoodHope EDS Clinic between 2019-2021. Patients diagnosed with EDS or G-HSD (N=205) completed self-report measures of BPD symptoms and EDS/G-HSD features (i.e., pain severity/interference, autonomic symptom burden). Clinicians assessed joint hypermobility. An ANOVA examined group differences between individuals scoring above the recommended BSL-23 threshold (i.e., ≥ 1.5) and below the cut-off. A linear regression examined associations between EDS/G-HSD features and BPD symptom severity. Forty-five participants (22%) scored above the recommended BSL-23 threshold, indicating elevated BPD symptoms. These individuals reported greater pain severity, pain interference, and autonomic symptom burden compared to those below the cut-off score. In a linear regression, pain interference was the only EDS/G-HSD feature associated with BPD symptom severity; pain severity, joint hypermobility, and autonomic symptom burden were not significant. Greater pain interference was associated with more severe BPD symptoms among individuals with EDS/G-HSD. Further research is needed to clarify these relationships, enhance diagnostic accuracy, and improve interventions for this population.

items.title: Reading Skills and Reading Anxiety Symptoms in Youth.
items.abstract: Many children who experience reading challenges develop co-occurring mental health difficulties, such as reading anxiety. The current study tested the relationships between specific reading skills (decoding, fluency, and comprehension) and reading anxiety symptoms. Participants were 230 twins between 8 and 13 years old. Multi-level linear regression models were used to account for family relationships and covaried for age and sex. Age was positively associated and sex was not associated with reading anxiety. Lower decoding (β = -0.19, p < .001), reading fluency (β = -0.22, p < .001), and reading comprehension skills (β = -0.22, p < .001) were significantly associated with higher reading anxiety symptoms. When testing whether each reading skill contributed to reading anxiety after controlling for others, reading comprehension (β = -0.15, p = .010) remained significantly associated with reading anxiety symptoms, whereas decoding (β = 0.01, p = .90) and reading fluency (β = -0.13, p = .08) were no longer significant. Model comparisons followed a similar pattern indicating that reading comprehension (and to a lesser extent fluency) accounted for significant variance in reading anxiety over and above other reading skills, while decoding did not. Secondary analyses covarying for clinical anxiety and ADHD symptoms showed that the association between reading skills and reading anxiety could not be accounted for by these co-occurring symptoms. This study is among the first to examine relationships between specific reading skills and reading anxiety symptoms and highlights the need for improved identification and treatment of reading anxiety symptoms in struggling readers.

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of MRI-derived imaging biomarkers and machine learning-based classification in distal and myofibrillar myopathies.
items.abstract: To characterise and validate disease-specific muscle imaging patterns in distal and myofibrillar myopathies, quantify their diagnostic performance, and develop an imaging-based classification framework incorporating machine learning. Muscle MRI and CT scans from a multicentre national cohort of patients with genetically defined distal and myofibrillar myopathies were retrospectively analysed. The pattern of muscle involvement for each disease entity was described, and its sensitivity and specificity calculated. Supervised machine learning algorithms were trained using muscle scores and imaging-derived features, and their diagnostic performance was compared using balanced accuracy. A total of 165 patients (mean age 48 ± 16 years; 87 men), including 138 molecularly confirmed cases spanning 19 disease genes, were analysed. Overall, 6350 muscles were systematically evaluated. Key findings included early biceps femoris short head involvement in GNE myopathy, "fat pockets" in myotilinopathy, and early flexor hallucis longus involvement in desminopathy. All imaging patterns showed high sensitivity and specificity (from 75 to 100%). Among the tested machine learning models, XGBoost achieved the highest performance, correctly distinguishing among 11 genetic disease entities with a balanced accuracy of 69%. Distal and myofibrillar myopathies demonstrate reproducible disease-specific imaging signatures with high diagnostic accuracy. Integration of these imaging biomarkers into a machine learning framework enables systematic prioritisation of likely genetic diagnoses and may facilitate diagnostic work-up in these heterogeneous inherited muscle disorders. Question How accurately do muscle MRI patterns distinguish distal and myofibrillar myopathies, and how do imaging features perform in an updated MRI-based diagnostic algorithm? Findings Disease-specific muscle MRI patterns showed high diagnostic accuracy, while XGBoost achieved the highest balanced accuracy among machine learning models for imaging-based disease classification. Clinical relevance Refined muscle MRI patterns provide diagnostically useful imaging biomarkers in distal and myofibrillar myopathies. Their integration into machine learning-based classification models may facilitate precision diagnostics and guide targeted genetic testing.

items.title: Early childhood serum and urine metabolite signatures of internalizing, externalizing, and ADHD traits and their trajectories to adolescence: the Rhea mother-child cohort.
items.abstract: Early-life emotional and behavioral difficulties increase vulnerability to later psychopathology, but it remains unclear whether a biological footprint is detectable in early childhood. We aimed to identify serum- and urine-based metabolite signatures of internalizing, externalizing, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) traits in 6-year-old children and examine their associations with traits through adolescence. We analyzed 196 participants of the Rhea cohort (Greece), with serum and urine metabolomics at age 6 and internalizing, externalizing, and ADHD traits assessed at ages 6, 11, and 15. Trait- and biofluid-specific metabolite signatures were identified using elastic net regression with cross-validation. Associations with subsequent traits at repeated time points were evaluated using confounder-adjusted linear mixed-effects models. Metabolite signatures comprising amino acids, acylcarnitines, phosphatidylcholines, and gut microbiota-related metabolites were identified for internalizing, externalizing, and ADHD traits. Serum metabolite scores were associated with increased internalizing (β = 0.40; 95% CI 0.14-0.68) and externalizing traits (β = 0.83; 95% CI 0.56-1.1). Urine metabolite scores were associated with internalizing (β = 0.42; 95% CI 0.16-0.68) and externalizing traits (β = 0.69; 95% CI 0.43-0.95), while the association with ADHD traits was nominal (β = 0.25; 95% CI: 0.006-0.502; nominal p = 0.045; BH-FDR p = 0.054). Associations were stable over time for internalizing and ADHD but weakened with age for externalizing traits. This proof-of-concept study shows that complementary serum and urine metabolomic profiles in early childhood are associated with subsequent internalizing and externalizing trait trajectories, while a nominal longitudinal association was observed between the urine metabolite profile and ADHD traits. These findings warrant evaluation in larger independent studies.

items.title: Delayed associative memory and recall error patterns in mild cognitive impairment: discriminant capacity of the Italian face-name association test.
items.abstract: Cross-modal associative memory impairment is one of the earliest cognitive markers of neurodegenerative disorders and may be particularly sensitive to the detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). The Italian Face-Name Association Test (ItFNAT) assesses face-name associative memory through immediate recall (IR), delayed free (DFR), and total recall (DTR), and qualitative indices. This study provides psychometric properties, discriminative capacity, and diagnostic accuracy in older adults. A total of 136 older adults underwent a neuropsychological assessment and were classified as cognitively healthy (CH = 72) or as having MCI (N = 64). Partial correlations assessed internal, convergent, and discriminant validity, whereas ANCOVAs, logistic regressions, and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated diagnostic performance compared with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). IR and DTR scores showed associations with established neuropsychological measures, whereas DFR displayed a largely independent profile. After controlling for age and education, CH participants outperformed the MCI group on IR and DFR and showed higher Free Recall and Interference indices. Logistic regressions identified DFR as the strongest independent predictor of diagnostic status. ROC analyses demonstrated significant discrimination between groups for both DFR (AUC = 0.711) and the MoCA (AUC = 0.705), with no significant difference between the two ROC curves. While the MoCA showed higher sensitivity, DFR provided greater specificity, with an optimal cut-off of ≤ 3.21. These findings support the ItFNAT as a clinically useful measure of associative memory in aging. Particularly, DFR appears sensitive to early cognitive decline and may provide complementary information to standard cognitive tests.

items.title: A comprehensive review of mixed-species biofilm infections and innovative therapeutic strategies.
items.abstract: Mixed-species biofilm infections are important causes of persistent and difficult-to-treat infections. Compared with monospecies biofilms, mixed-species communities contain microorganisms with different physiological and genetic characteristics that interact through metabolic cooperation, chemical signaling, competition, and modification of the local environment. These interactions, together with the EPS matrix, physiological heterogeneity, and HGT, can increase antimicrobial tolerance, contributing to treatment failure and infection recurrence. Polymicrobial biofilms are associated with chronic wounds, respiratory infections, catheter- and device-associated infections, and other persistent infections. However, treatment of polymicrobial biofilms remains challenging because their complex structure and interspecies interactions can reduce antimicrobial efficacy. This review summarizes the clinical significance, formation, and persistence of mixed-species biofilms and discusses recent therapeutic strategies for their control. We also discuss recent approaches for controlling polymicrobial biofilms, including natural compounds, QS inhibition, CRISPR-Cas-based approaches, biofilm matrix targeting, metabolic and nutrient disruption, nanotechnology, and phage therapy. Recent studies show that these approaches can inhibit biofilm formation, disrupt established biofilms, enhance antimicrobial activity, and selectively target specific microbial populations. However, their effectiveness varies with microbial composition, biofilm maturity, matrix characteristics, and treatment conditions. Overall, current evidence supports the development of targeted and combination-based strategies for mixed-species biofilms. Further studies using clinically relevant models are needed to exactly define treatment efficacy and support the translation of these approaches into clinical practice.

items.title: Extracellular vesicles from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells protect grafted islets against endoplasmic reticulum stress-induced mitochondrial dysfunction via modulating XBP1-based calcium homeostasis.
items.abstract: Although islet transplantation is an ideal option for individuals with diabetes, early graft failure due to beta cell apoptosis and stress-induced dysfunction severely limits long-term efficacy. Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hucMSCs) have multiple functions including maintaining cellular homeostasis. However, it remains unknown as to whether extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from hucMSCs (hucMSC-EVs) provide protective effects against transplant-related trauma-induced islet injury. This study aimed to investigate the effects of hucMSC-EVs on islet graft survival in a syngeneic mouse model of islet transplantation and to examine the mechanism of protection. EVs were isolated from cultured hucMSCs and characterised by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking and western blotting. The effects of hucMSC-EVs on islet graft function were evaluated in a mouse model of streptozocin-induced diabetes via co-transplantation under the kidney capsule. Beta cell survival and function were assessed by immunofluorescence, TUNEL staining, insulin secretion assays and in vivo imaging. Endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) and mitochondrial dysfunction were further analysed in primary islets and NIT-1 beta cells under thapsigargin- or tunicamycin-stimulated ERS models. Further calcium imaging, JC-1 staining, western blotting and Seahorse assays were performed. microRNA sequencing was conducted and the role of miR-182-5p and XBP1 in mediating hucMSC-EV function was verified using knockdown, overexpression and dual-luciferase assays. Co-transplantation of hucMSC-EVs with 250 islet equivalents significantly improved glycaemic control (p<0.01) and glucose tolerance (p<0.01) in diabetic mice. Apoptotic beta cells were significantly reduced in grafts receiving EVs, as shown by TUNEL assays (p<0.05) and cleaved caspase 3 staining (p<0.05). Ex vivo, hucMSC-EVs were internalised by beta cells and protected against tunicamycin-induced apoptosis (p<0.01), preserved insulin expression and restored glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. While ERS enhanced interactions between endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, hucMSC-EVs maintained calcium homeostasis, improved mitochondrial energy metabolism and alleviated ERS. Small RNA sequencing and functional analysis identified that XBP1-targeted miR-182-5p was enriched in hucMSC-EVs, which further fine-tuned endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria communication via reducing inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors at mitochondria-associated membranes and activated Nrf2 to restore mitochondrial calcium homeostasis under ERS. miR-182-5p inhibition reversed the protective effects of EVs on beta cell calcium homeostasis and viability. In vivo, depletion of miR-182-5p in hucMSC-EVs abolished the ability to prevent beta cell apoptosis and improve glycaemic control in diabetic mice. hucMSC-EVs significantly improved the survival and function of islet grafts by delivering miR-182-5p, which targeted XBP1 to modulate mitochondria-associated membranes, attenuate ERS and restore mitochondrial calcium homeostasis. These findings highlight a novel cell-free EV-based therapeutic strategy for improving the outcome of islet transplantation.

items.title: Fitness level, but not sex, affects exercise-induced pain modulation.
items.abstract: In a previous study by our group (Nold et al., 2025), we investigated exercise-induced pain modulation after high-intensity compared to low-intensity exercise in a heterogeneous sample of diverse fitness levels. Exploratory analyses suggested an interaction of sex, fitness level, and drug treatment, indicating that males showed increasing hypoalgesia after high- compared to low-intensity exercise with increasing fitness levels, which was diminished when naloxone was administered. In contrast, these effects were not evident in females. These exploratory findings warranted further investigation to determine if and to what extent exercise-induced pain modulation depends on fitness level and/or sex. In this current study, we investigated an all-female sample (N=21) of high fitness levels using a similar paradigm as in the previous study, comparing heat and pressure pain ratings after high-intensity and low-intensity exercise. Our data show an interaction of exercise intensity and stimulus intensity in heat pain, with greater pain relief following high-intensity exercise, especially at the highest stimulus intensity. Despite results for pressure pain not reaching significance, a similar trend was evident. These results suggest that females at a high fitness level also show exercise-induced pain modulation for high-intensity compared to low-intensity exercise. Furthermore, we pooled the data of the current and previous study, providing evidence for fitness level but not sex to moderate exercise-induced pain modulation in heat pain. These findings suggest that exercise-induced pain modulation depends on fitness level but not on sex.

items.title: The impact of cognitive processes associated with image recognition on visuo-vestibular interaction.
items.abstract: An increasing number of articles in the literature highlight the importance of saccadic remodulation in compensatory mechanisms, and the reappearance of SHIMP saccades following a vestibular insult correlates strongly with an improvement in symptoms reported by patients on the DHI. To assess the influence of attentional processes and working memory on visuo-vestibular interaction, we designed three independent yet interrelated experiments.In the first two experiments, perfectly healthy subjects (first experiment) and patients with a history of unilateral or bilateral vestibular deficits (second experiment) underwent vHIT in SHIMP mode and the Functional Head Impulse Test. The two tests were performed in the same session, initially separately ("separate protocol") and subsequently simultaneously ("combined protocol"). The mean latency of SHIMP saccades and their degree of clustering were analyzed, and finally, the recognition rate of the Landolt C. Subsequently, any variations in these parameters between the "disjoint protocol" and the "joint protocol" were assessed, and, in the second experiment, the differences between the "disjoint protocol" and the "joint protocol" were correlated with the severity of symptoms measured by the DHI. The aim was to verify whether, during the "joint protocol," the near-simultaneity of the two tasks, both mediated by shared parietal cortical substrates, altered any parameters. In the third experiment, we used vHIT in HIMP mode and fHIT, performed in disjointed and joint protocols. The objective was to verify whether the conjunction of saccadic function and cognitive load related to recognition could influence the latency and clustering of recovery saccades favorably.Conclusions: Results suggest visual recognition impacts visuo-vestibular interaction, supporting integrated dual-task protocols for ecological balance assessment and resolving clinical discrepancies, though larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm these preliminary findings.

items.title: Combined Nav1.7-Nav1.8 channel abrogation: Supralinear suppression of excitability in a subpopulation of peripheral sensory neurons.
items.abstract: There is a pressing need for nonaddictive pain therapeutics. Despite the genetic validation of peripheral voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels as targets for non-opioid pain therapy, isoform-selective inhibition of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 has yielded limited efficacy in clinical studies, with Nav1.8 blockade providing statistically significant but only partial pain relief. This raises the question: if block of Nav1.8 relieves pain only partially, what is needed for better pain relief? In this study, we utilized dynamic clamp, which permits precisely calibrated functional addition or subtraction of the current from any given channel, to systematically interrogate the combinatorial landscape of multiplex abrogation of currents from Nav1.7 and Nav1.8, both major contributors to electrogenesis within dorsal root ganglion neurons. We demonstrate that partial, simultaneous attenuation of both conductances drives a supralinear increase in current threshold in many sensory neurons. Responses to Nav1.8 functional subtraction span a broad spectrum, whereas responses to Nav1.7 subtraction are comparatively uniform. Neurons with greater sensitivity to functional loss of Nav1.8 show greater suppression of excitability during combined Nav1.7-Nav1.8 attenuation, while weak Nav1.8 responders remain comparatively resistant. These findings identify electrogenic dependence on Nav1.8 as a major source of functional heterogeneity in sensory neurons and demonstrate that Nav1.7 acts cooperatively with Nav1.8 to shape the consequences of channel attenuation. Our results indicate that combined Nav1.7-Nav1.8 targeting should outperform isoform-selective block in suppressing firing in a subpopulation of pain-signaling neurons, while not producing universal suppression.

items.title: Language Proficiency and Code Switching in English-Spanish Autistic Bilingual Speakers.
items.abstract: Purpose Evidence that bilingual exposure does not negatively affect language outcomes in autistic individuals has expanded over the past 15 years. However, research on bilingualism in autism has been limited to focusing on one language or each language separately, which does not capture natural bilingual dynamics such as code switching. This study examined how English-Spanish autistic speakers use their languages to communicate in semistructured settings. Method Thirty English-Spanish autistic bilingual individuals (age range: 5.33-42.33 years) participated in two semistructured interactions with either a caregiver or a bilingual examiner. In each context, participants were instructed to speak either English or Spanish. Video recordings were transcribed and coded for code switching. Language proficiency in each language was measured using mean length of utterance in morphemes and number of different words. From the transcripts, we extracted rates of target language utterances (matching the instructed language), intersentential code switching (using the noncontextual language), and intrasentential code switching (mixing languages within an utterance). Results Participants were, on average, more proficient in English than in Spanish. Code switching occurred primarily when participants were instructed to speak Spanish, with English-dominant individuals and those who were less proficient in Spanish switching back to English more frequently. Code switching was also more frequent during interactions with a familiar caregiver than an unfamiliar examiner. Conclusions The language of English-Spanish autistic individuals reflects expected patterns of bilingual use. They showed greater proficiency in their societal than in their heritage language and seemed to rely on code switching primarily to compensate for limited proficiency in their nondominant Spanish. These findings add to the growing body of evidence that bilingualism should not be viewed as detrimental in autism.

items.title: Differential Effect of Endovascular Treatment in Medium or Distal Vessel Occlusion: A Distal Secondary Analysis.
items.abstract: Background Patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion stroke are heterogeneous. Randomized trials show no net benefit of endovascular treatment (EVT) over best medical treatment (BMT) alone, which may mask heterogeneity of treatment effect. We used an externally developed machine learning model to predict excellent early neurological outcome (EENO) with BMT alone and examined whether the effect of EVT differed across predicted risk. Methods A Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) model was trained to predict EENO (24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score of 0-2) in patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion treated with BMT alone in a local Bernese Stroke Registry. This model was applied to patients from the DISTAL randomized trial (55 centers and 11 countries), who were randomized to EVT plus BMT or BMT alone. We tested for interaction between predicted EENO and treatment allocation on the primary outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale shift), repeating this using admission NIHSS alone. Results In the development cohort (n=257, 42% female, and mean age 70.4±14.8 years), 54% achieved EENO. In the DISTAL cohort (270 BMT alone, 269 EVT plus BMT, 44% female, and mean age 74.9±12.0 years), the model showed moderate external discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.73). A significant interaction was found between predicted EENO and treatment effect ( P interaction =0.012): in 152 patients predicted to achieve EENO, EVT was associated with worse 90-day modified Rankin Scale score (common odds ratio, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.27-0.84]), whereas no treatment effect was seen in 387 patients predicted not to achieve EENO (common odds ratio 1.13 [95% CI, 0.79-1.60]). A model using admission NIHSS alone showed comparable discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.71) and a common odds ratio for EVT of 0.47 (95% CI, 0.25-0.89) in patients with an NIHSS score of ≤4 and a common odds ratio of 1.05 (95% CI, 0.75-1.47) in patients with an NIHSS score of >4 ( P interaction =0.029). Conclusions EVT was harmful in patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion predicted to achieve EENO with BMT alone, and an NIHSS-alone model performed comparably to the multivariable model. Registration URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05029414.

items.title: What Is the Most Appropriate Method for Determining Minimally Clinical Important Difference in Grade 2 Spondylolisthesis? A QOD Spine CORe® Study.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Minimally clinically important difference (MCID) defines the smallest difference in patient-reported outcomes (PROs) required for a level of clinical improvement. The hypothesis of this study is that at least one of the MCID thresholds in this study will provide appropriate MCID thresholds for the PROs in grade 2 spondylolisthesis. Methods This study used the Grade 2 Spondylolisthesis module of the Quality Outcomes Database Spine CORe® Study Group, which included 328 patients from 14 institutions. PROs collected include Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) for back pain and leg pain, and European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions (EQ-5D). Seven MCID thresholds were calculated with North American Spine Society satisfaction scale as the anchor. Each method was evaluated using area under the curve, reflecting the ability to predict satisfaction. Results There were 328 patients with ≥80% 5-year follow-up. The optimal percentage cutoff method generally demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy for defining MCID in ODI, NRS back pain, and NRS leg pain, whereas the optimal numeric cutoff method generally demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy for EQ-5D. For ODI, 2-year optimal percentage cutoff was 30.4% and 5-year optimal percentage cutoff was 38.1%. For NRS back pain, 2-year optimal percentage cutoff was 75.0% and 5-year optimal percentage cutoff was 42.9%. For NRS leg pain, 2-year optimal percentage cutoff was 62.5% and 5-year optimal percentage cutoff was 66.6%. For EQ-5D, the optimal numeric cutoffs were 0.293 at 2 years and 0.128 at 5 years. Conclusion Using satisfaction as an anchor, this study identified the optimal percentage cutoff as the most appropriate method for determining MCID in ODI and NRS pain scores, while the optimal numeric cutoff was most appropriate for EQ-5D in grade 2 spondylolisthesis. These findings provide reference definitions for evaluating postoperative improvement in this patient population.

items.title: Compensation of hyperexcitability with simulation-based inference.
items.abstract: The activity of healthy neuronal networks is tightly regulated, and a shift toward hyperexcitability can cause various problems, such as epilepsies, memory deficits, and motor disorders. Numerous cellular, synaptic, and intrinsic mechanisms of hyperexcitability and compensatory mechanisms to restore healthy activity have been proposed. However, quantifying multiple compensatory mechanisms and their dependence on specific pathophysiological mechanisms has proven challenging, even in computational models. We use simulation-based inference to quantify the interactions of putative compensatory mechanisms in a spiking neuronal network model. Various parameters of the model can compensate for the changes in other parameters to maintain baseline activity, and we estimated their compensatory potential. Furthermore, specific causes of hyperexcitability - interneuron loss, excitatory recurrent synapses, and principal cell depolarization - have distinct compensatory mechanisms that can restore normal excitability. Our results show that spiking neuronal network simulators could generate hypotheses about the mechanisms of pathophysiological network mechanisms.

items.title: Longitudinal PET RANO 1.0 and RANO 2.0 response assessment in vorasidenib-treated IDH-mutant gliomas: the VORAFET study.
items.abstract: Background Conventional MRI may not fully reflect the biological activity of vorasidenib. PET may detect treatment-related metabolic changes before structural changes become evident on MRI. We evaluated longitudinal PET and MRI changes in patients with IDH-mutant gliomas receiving vorasidenib. Methods VORAFET is a longitudinal study of adults with IDH-mutant gliomas treated with vorasidenib. Eligible patients had predominantly non-enhancing WHO grade 2 or 3 gliomas, had not received prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was longitudinal metabolic and structural imaging response according to PET RANO 1.0 and RANO 2.0. Integrated [¹⁸F]FET PET/MRI was performed at baseline and every 3 months. Results Thirty-nine patients were included; at baseline, 23 and 29 had PET and MRI-measurable disease. As best response, PET RANO 1.0 identified 2 complete and 12 partial responses, yielding an ORR of 60.9%; median time to first response was 4.5 months (range 3-12 months). RANO 2.0 showed no complete or partial responses, whereas 5 patients achieved minor response at a median of 9 months (range 6-12 months). Progressive disease occurred in 6 of 39 patients (15.4%) according to PET RANO 1.0 and in 1 of 39 (2.6%) according to RANO 2.0. Patients with PET-PD more often had subtle contrast enhancement and showed higher baseline FLAIR volume, MTV, TBRmax, and TBRmean. Conclusions PET RANO 1.0 identified metabolic changes during vorasidenib treatment that were not always reflected by RANO 2.0 assessment. Longer follow-up is needed to clarify the relationship between PET metabolic changes and MRI findings and to determine their clinical significance.

items.title: Targeting Mitochondrial Redox Signaling Promotes Neuroregeneration and Functional Recovery in a Multiple Sclerosis Model.
items.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including multiple sclerosis (MS), are characterized by progressive neuronal loss and limited regenerative capacity. To stimulate in vivo neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis by harnessing the untapped regenerative potential of endogenous neural progenitor cells (NPCs) that are upregulated in the CNS under disease conditions, we developed a novel compound that targets Notch signaling, a pathway known to suppress neuronal differentiation of NPCs. Furapyrrodole, which was identified by screening a natural product-like synthetic chemical library, binds to and activates the mitochondrial reductase CYB5R3, which naturally downregulates Notch signaling downstream of γ-secretase. The in vivo efficacy of furapyrrodole was evaluated in mice with experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a mouse model of MS. Furapyrrodole treatment after the peak of EAE disease significantly improved motor function and promoted recovery of motor neurons and myelination by stimulating endogenous NPC-derived neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis. In addition, furapyrrodole supresses neuroinflammation in the CNS. Collectively, these findings indicate furapyrrodole is a promising therapeutic candidate for MS by harnessing endogenously upregulated NPCs and inducing anti-inflammation. Our study demonstrates for the first time that modulation of mitochondrial redox signaling promotes neuroregeneration and remyelination without causing severe adverse effects.

items.title: Distinct gradients of cortical architecture capture visual representations and behavior across the lifespan.
items.abstract: The microstructure of cells within the human cerebral cortex varies across the cortical ribbon, where changes in cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture are thought to endow each region of the cortex with its unique function. While fine-scale relative to a cell, these changes at the population level impact architectural properties of the cortex measurable in vivo by noninvasive MRI, such as the thickness and myelin content of the cortex. This raises the question of whether or not we can use these in vivo architectural measures to understand cortical organization, function, and development more broadly. Using the human visual cortex as a test bed, we demonstrated two architectural gradients, one in which cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture converge and another in which they diverge. These two gradients underlie the structural and functional topography of the visual cortex, even predicting the presence of new visual representations. Moreover, the two gradients show distinct visual behavior relevance and lifespan trajectory. These findings provide a more general framework for understanding the human cortex, showing that architectural gradients are a measurable fingerprint of functional organization and ontogenetic routines in the human brain.

items.title: Oxytocin neurons signal state-dependent transitions from rest to thermogenesis and behavioral arousal.
items.abstract: Core body temperature (Tb) is defended within narrow limits through thermoregulatory behaviors like huddling, nesting, and physical activity, as well as autonomic responses like brown fat thermogenesis. While Tb displays regulated fluctuations across different behavioral states and rest/arousal cycles, the neural control of these transitions remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the relationship between oxytocin neurons of the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVN OT ) and behavioral and autonomic thermoeffector pathways across physiological states in mice. First, we show that PVN OT neurons are activated during social thermoregulation. We then demonstrate that in vivo PVN OT calcium dynamics align with transitions from rest to thermogenesis and behavioral arousal. Counter to our initial hypothesis, these dynamics were observed in both social and non-social contexts. Using a computer vision model to track thermoeffector pathways, we demonstrate that precisely timed stimulation of PVN OT neurons during low-Tb resting states increases thermogenesis followed by behavioral arousal. We therefore suggest a model in which PVN OT neurons facilitate homeostatic state-dependent transitions in thermo-behavioral states.

items.title: Stress signaling and physiological modulation by glycine betaine for cadmium-resilient maize.
items.abstract: Glycine betaine (GB), a naturally occurring osmoprotectant, stabilizes proteins, membranes, and osmotic balance under abiotic stress. It effectively mitigates oxidative damage and maintains redox homeostasis, making it a promising candidate for cadmium (Cd) tolerance. Cd toxicity is a major constraint to sustainable agriculture due to its phytotoxicity and bioaccumulation. This study evaluates the effect of GB applied via seed priming and foliar spray on Cd stress in two maize cultivars with contrasting tolerance ( CZP and MMRI). Plants were exposed to 500 mM CdCl₂ under controlled conditions, and morpho-physiological and biochemical traits - including biomass, chlorophyll, protein, reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), proline, GB, soluble sugars, phenolics, and flavonoids - were measured. Cd exposure reduced biomass, chlorophyll, and protein, while increasing ROS, MDA, and H₂O₂. Treatments, particularly seed priming, enhanced osmoprotectants and antioxidants, restoring osmotic balance and redox homeostasis. CZP showed greater biochemical resistance and lower Cd translocation than MMRI. Overall, GB-mediated stress modulation involves physiological reprogramming, with seed priming proving more effective than foliar spray. This study provides novel insights into GB-driven amelioration of Cd stress in maize.

items.title: Canopy nutrient balance predicts autumn senescence across U.S. forests.
items.abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems are changing rapidly under global nutrient enrichment, yet how canopy nutrients balance shapes the seasonal end of photosynthesis, a critical control on ecosystem carbon cycling, remains unclear. Rising anthropogenic nitrogen inputs are shifting many ecosystems towards relative phosphorus limitation, with uncertain consequences for autumn phenology. Here, we combined airborne imaging spectroscopy with remotely sensed phenology to test whether canopy nutrient ratios predict spatial variations in autumn senescence across National Ecological Observatory Network sites in the United States. Higher canopy N:P is consistently associated with earlier senescence in 20 out of 25 sites, whereas higher N:K has opposite effects in 19 sites after controlling for climate, elevation, dominant species, and canopy structure. Growing-season productivity is generally related to later senescence, but only modestly mediates the direct nutrient-phenology associations. These findings add a phenological dimension to the functional impacts of nutrient imbalance on terrestrial ecosystems and demonstrate that nutrients provide predictive power beyond climate alone. Continued nitrogen deposition is expected to increase relative phosphorus limitation, a shift that could be associated with earlier senescence and shorter growing season. Incorporating canopy nutrients into phenological models may therefore improve forecasts of canopy duration and carbon fluxes under ongoing nutrient enrichment.

items.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates chronic pain and comorbid depression through Gut-Metabolite-Brain axis remodeling to restore mPFC Glu/GABA balance.
items.abstract: The comorbidity of chronic pain and depression is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder involving dysregulated microbiota-gut-brain communication. Although electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for both pain and depression, the mechanisms linking peripheral microbial-metabolic remodeling to central neurotransmitter regulation remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed an integrated multi-omics approach in a spared nerve injury (SNI) rat model to investigate the gut-metabolite-brain mechanisms underlying EA's efficacy. EA significantly alleviated mechanical hypersensitivity and depressive-like behaviors while restoring mPFC Glu/GABA balance, accompanied by normalization of the glutamate transporter EAAT2 and the GABA-synthesizing enzyme GAD67. Metagenomic analysis showed that EA remodeled the gut microbial ecosystem by increasing microbial diversity, suppressing opportunistic pathobionts, including Bacillus cereus, Alistipes onderdonkii, while enriching SCFA-associated genera, including Butyricimonas and Romboutsia. These alterations were accompanied by coordinated remodeling of amino acid and butanoate metabolism. Correlation network analysis identified Pipecolic acid as a central metabolic node linking gut microbial alterations with mPFC GABAergic neurotransmission and behavioral recovery. Although individual bacterial genera did not significantly mediate its restoration, causal mediation analysis demonstrated that the Pipecolic acid-GABA axis significantly mediated improvements in both mechanical allodynia and anhedonia, supporting Pipecolic acid as a functional metabolic hub linking peripheral metabolic remodeling to central GABAergic regulation. Collectively, these findings identify peripheral metabolic remodeling as a key mechanistic interface through which EA coordinates gut microbial ecology and central neurochemical homeostasis, providing a systems-level framework for understanding the therapeutic mechanisms of acupuncture in pain-depression comorbidity.

items.title: Profiling of pollen in honey using multispectral imaging flow cytometry.
items.abstract: Pollen identification from honey (melissopalynology) is of great economic and consumer relevance. Traditional microscopy is time-consuming and dependent on expert knowledge, thus limiting high-throughput analyses. We tested whether pollen images generated with Multispectral Imaging Flow Cytometry (MIFC) classified by machine learning (ML) (convolution neural networks (CNNs) and random forest (RF)) can serve as a fast and reproducible method for identifying pollen in honey. We examined how the classification of honey pollen is affected by images from different matrices (anther and honey samples), how results compare with traditional microscopic analysis and used a set of human-interpretable image features to better explain ML results. The study focused on the six common target pollen in honey Brassica, Castanea, Centaurea, Helianthus, Phacelia and Tilia type. A classifier trained with a combination of anther and honey brightfield and fluorescence images provided the best predictions for 13 monofloral and 10 polyfloral honeys. Yielding pollen identification results comparable to microscopy, three times more pollen can be evaluated, and a measurement time of a maximum of 10 min, the method demonstrates its high potential as a powerful screening tool in melissopalynology.

items.title: Water stable isotopes reveal the ecohydrological importance of stemflow infiltration for mature and juvenile European beech.
items.abstract: Stemflow of forest trees can contribute a significant fraction of water to forest's water fluxes; however, it is still unclear whether and to what extent trees and their neighbours use stemflow for water uptake and supply. We applied deuterium-enriched stemflow equivalent to a 23-mm throughfall event to adult Fagus sylvatica trees to trace stemflow through the soil and trees. We continuously measured in situ water stable isotopes in soil and xylem water and destructively sampled xylem water in the crowns of adult labelled, nonlabelled F. sylvatica and nonlabelled Picea abies, complemented by destructive xylem water sampling of neighbouring juvenile F. sylvatica. Stemflow water supported up to 5.7 ± 2.1% of daily sap flux of adult F. sylvatica trees labelled at the stem base and was detectable in xylem water for several weeks. In the soil, deuterium-enriched stemflow was present at a maximum distance of 0.40 m from the labelled tree. Moreover, nonlabelled juvenile trees within a distance of 2 m showed uptake of labelled water, indicating rooting into soil compartments affected by stemflow. We demonstrate the importance of stemflow as a water source for both adult and neighbouring juvenile F. sylvatica, even when soil water is not limiting.

items.title: Decomposition and mycorrhizal suppression of saprotrophs remain stable after wildfire and clearcut disturbance in boreal forests.
items.abstract: Boreal forests store a large portion of global terrestrial carbon, primarily in soils, yet their sensitivity to environmental changes remains uncertain. Disturbance is one major agent of change, with dominance shifting from wildfire to forest management over the past century. Mycorrhizal suppression of saprotrophic decomposition may be an important control on boreal soil carbon storage, but its occurrence and magnitude remain uncertain. Additionally, the distinct impacts of wildfire and clearcutting on decomposition and soil microbial communities remain largely unexplored. We quantified mycorrhizal suppression of saprotrophs and decomposition in needle and humus litter through a root-exclusion experiment in 31 sites across wildfire (4-375 yr since disturbance) and clearcut chronosequences (1-109 yr since disturbance) in northern Sweden. Mycorrhizas suppressed decomposition by 15.5 ± 5.9% overall, with no consistent change over time after disturbance. This pattern was linked to absolute fungal abundance but not to other microbial community shifts, soil temperature or soil moisture. Decomposition rates were stable across time since disturbance for all substrates and disturbance types. Our findings improve understanding of mycorrhizal-decomposition interactions and highlight the need to further explore key fungal traits and compositional changes, especially at the soil surface, that regulate carbon storage dynamics in boreal soils.

items.title: How do we know when invasive species control strategies work?
items.abstract: Controlling invasive species is costly and difficult but can have major ecological, economic, and health benefits. Researchers commonly compare the efficacy of specific control methods. However, invasive species control programs vary greatly in overarching goals and often occur over large areas, long timeframes, and varied environmental and social contexts. The success of these programs likely hinges on factors including organizational structures, concurrent restoration activities, geographic and temporal scope of control, and the invasive species' biology. To enable assessment of the relative influence of these common features, we propose clearer definitions of success in invasive species control and explicit comparisons among control programs. Post hoc assessment of existing programs' success will complement system-specific studies to guide strategies that work in real-world situations.

items.title: Invasion legacies of Carpobrotus edulis negatively affect the endangered Iberodes littoralis subsp. gallaecica.
items.abstract: The invasive South African plant Carpobrotus edulis threatens biodiversity and disrupts coastal ecosystems, yet the effects of soil legacies on the life cycle of native plants remain poorly understood. Here, we assessed whether a short-term invasion by C. edulis induces soil changes that remain after removal and affect the performance of the endangered dune plant Iberodes littoralis subsp. gallaecica across its life cycle. In 16 experimental plots (eight previously invaded and eight non-invaded), we characterised soil properties at two depths and sowed seeds from five I. littoralis populations to assess germination, survival to flowering, flowering phenology, flower number, leaf reflectance, biomass traits and reproductive output. Previously invaded plots showed reductions in NH4+-N, total N, Cu and Zn, and increases in δ13C, P and Al, while invasion effects on NO3--N and pH varied with soil depth, as did soil-plant relationships. Soil legacies promoted germination in I. littoralis but reduced survival to flowering, flowering duration, growth and reproductive investment, ultimately resulting in lower seed production. Despite phenotypic differences among provenances, intra-specific variation did not mitigate the adverse effects of soil legacies on plant performance. Our findings show that just 14 months of C. edulis invasion can leave soil legacies in nutrient availability and soil chemistry, with functional consequences for I. littoralis across its full life cycle. These results highlight the importance of considering legacy effects of invasion beyond early life stages of native plants and accounting for depth-related variation in soil properties and soil-plant relationships in restoration planning.

items.title: Genipin-crosslinked cellulose/chitosan/β-cyclodextrin molecularly imprinted hydrogel for green selective extraction of chlorogenic acid and bioactive wound dressing application.
items.abstract: Chlorogenic acid (CGA) is a naturally occurring polyphenol with multifaceted therapeutic potential, including antimicrobial, antioxidant, and regenerative activities; however, its conventional isolation process often relies on organic solvents, raising significant ecological and environmental concerns. In this study, a cellulose-based molecularly imprinted hydrogel (MDH@SMIP) was prepared using cellulose-based hydrogel (MDH) as the substrate by genipin cross-linking (β-cyclodextrin and chitosan functional monomers). MDH@SMIP is capable of extracting CGA from crude extracts of lingonberry (Vaccinium vitis-idaea L.) to produce an antibacterial and antioxidant hydrogel dressing (MDH@SMIP-CGA), which can then be used directly for wound healing. MDH@SMIP-CGA enables stimuli-responsive and controlled delivery of CGA in response to the wound microenvironment to achieve wound bacterial inhibition and reactive oxygen species clearance. MDH@SMIP-CGA exhibits excellent biocompatibility and promotes cell proliferation and migration. Distinct from conventional workflows that rely on organic solvents to extract phytochemicals and then re-load them onto dressings, this work integrates green molecular imprinting directly into a biocompatible cellulose hydrogel. The imprinted network simultaneously recognizes, enriches and delivers CGA from crude lingonberry extract, while responding to the mildly acidic wound microenvironment for on-demand release. This all-in-one recognition-and-dressing strategy thus offers a more environmentally friendly route from crude plant biomass to a precision wound therapy that combines infection control, anti-inflammation and tissue regeneration.

items.title: Transgenerational responses of invasive cocklebur species to microplastic stress: Stage specificity and interspecific divergence.
items.abstract: Microplastic pollution and plant invasions are converging threats to terrestrial ecosystems. Whether microplastics elicit adaptive transgenerational responses in invasive plants-rather than exerting uniform toxicity-remains untested. We hypothesize that parental microplastic exposure alters offspring performance, with the direction and magnitude of effects depending on polymer type, particle size, and abundance. Using a three-factor fully randomized design, we exposed three invasive cocklebur species (Cyclachaena xanthiifolia, Xanthium italicum, and Xanthium spinosum) to polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene (PE), and polypropylene (PP) at three sizes (5, 50, and 500 μm) and three abundances (519, 2074, and 4148 items kg-1), and quantified responses across parental life-history stages and F1 germination. Contemporary responses were stage-specific: germination in C. xanthiifolia and X. italicum was governed by three-way interactions, whereas later traits shifted toward polymer-type-dominated effects; X. spinosum showed size-dominated germination and type- or type × size-dependent later traits. Transgenerational effects diverged among species: C. xanthiifolia exhibited size-mediated F1 facilitation concurrent with type-driven parental inhibition; X. italicum showed direct, type-dependent facilitation; and X. spinosum showed no systematic transgenerational transmission. PLS-SEM supported these species-specific pathways. Because F1 performance was assayed only under control conditions, these patterns are consistent with-but do not demonstrate-a predictive adaptive response. Our results indicate that microplastics can act as species-specific modulators of invasive plant life histories across generations, highlighting the need to incorporate multi-factor, stage-specific, and transgenerational endpoints into microplastic risk assessment.

items.title: Seasonal divergence and long-term dynamics of dissolved organic carbon concentration and storage in the open-water regions of Lake Taihu from 2000 to 2024.
items.abstract: Concentration-based assessments may overlook changes in dissolved organic carbon (DOC) inventory when lake water volume varies seasonally. Here, we combined MODIS observations, an XGBoost retrieval model, and lake water storage (WSC) to reconstruct DOC concentration (DOCc) and DOC storage (DOCs) over 100 consecutive seasons from spring 2000 to winter 2024 across the analyzed open-water domain of Lake Taihu. The model was developed from 411 satellite-in situ matchups and achieved an R2 of 0.69 and an RMSE of 0.61 mg/L on the held-out validation dataset. DOCc exhibited a distinct bimodal seasonal cycle, with higher values in spring and autumn and lower values in summer and winter, whereas DOCs remained relatively high from spring through autumn and declined markedly in winter. Log-scale accounting partitioned DOCs variability into DOCc (44.7%) and WSC (56.0%) variance terms, together with a -2.1% covariance term and a 1.4% residual, showing that the DOCc and WSC terms were of comparable magnitude. Long-term changes were also season dependent: DOCc showed net declines from 2000 to 2024 in spring and summer but no robust monotonic trend in any season, whereas autumn DOCs showed the clearest positive long-term tendency in the baseline analysis, with a slope of 121.55 t C/yr. The runoff proxy also covaried consistently with WSC in spring and winter. Overall, DOCc and DOCs captured complementary but non-equivalent aspects of lake carbon dynamics, demonstrating that seasonal water-volume variability is integral to DOC inventory estimates and can yield patterns not evident from concentration alone.

items.title: Mineral triboelectricity as an electron source for microbial autotrophy: implications for carbon and nitrogen cycling in energy-limited environments.
items.abstract: Triboelectrification converts mechanical contact and separation into interfacial charge, yet whether mineral-derived triboelectric electrons can sustain microbial growth and metabolism remains unclear. Here, we report a mechanically powered autotrophic pathway in which mineral-mediated triboelectrification converts mechanical energy into an extracellular electron supply. Within the α-Fe2O3-Rhodopseudomonas palustris biohybrid, triboelectrically generated electrons were routed through cell-envelope redox conduits into respiratory metabolism, thereby converting interfacial charge into cellular energy and reducing power. This bioenergetic conversion coupled inorganic carbon fixation to nitrate respiration, sustaining autotrophic growth and lycopene biosynthesis in the dark without conventional chemical electron donors. Its compatibility with distinct mechanical inputs, electroactive microorganisms, and terminal electron acceptors demonstrates the broad adaptability of this energy-coupling pathway, whereas mineral-dependent performance identifies interfacial charge generation as an important control on microbial electron supply. These findings identify mineral-solid triboelectric contact as a distinct interfacial route linking mechanical energy to microbial carbon and nitrogen transformations, highlighting its potential relevance to biogeochemical processes in energy-limited environments.

items.title: Dual-Pathway Peroxymonosulfate Activation on FeNi-CNT@Al 2 O 3 for Efficient Tetracycline Hydrochloride Degradation.
items.abstract: Transition metal alloy catalysts are promising for advanced oxidation processes, but their application is often limited by insufficient interfacial electron transfer and poor stability. Herein, we engineered a robust FeNi-CNT@Al2O3 catalyst, derived from waste aluminum ash, for the activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and tetracycline hydrochloride (TCH) degradation. The catalyst features nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with encapsulated Fe-Ni alloy nanoparticles grown on an alumina-rich carbon matrix, creating an efficient interfacial catalytic platform through the synergy between CNT-mediated electron transfer and Fe-Ni-enhanced redox cycling. The optimized Fe1Ni2-CNT@Al2O3/PMS system achieved 100% TCH degradation with 73.5% chemical oxygen demand (COD) and 69.3% total organic carbon (TOC) removal within 30 min. Mechanistic investigations revealed that the degradation is dominated by a non-radical 1O2 pathway, with radical species ( and ) and direct electron transfer as secondary contributors. Density functional theory calculations further elucidated the critical role of Fe-Ni alloy loading in enhancing interfacial PMS adsorption and charge transfer. Notably, the catalyst maintained 91.8% TCH removal after 100 h of continuous operation. This work provides a sustainable strategy for upcycling solid waste into high-performance catalysts and elucidates the mechanism of 1O2-dominated PMS activation for persistent organic pollutant remediation.

items.title: Preferential Adsorption of Perfluoroalkyl Carboxylic Acids with Different Chain Lengths via Hydrophilic-Hydrophobic Interface Regulation.
items.abstract: Recently, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) pollution has gradually shifted from a pattern dominated by traditional long-chain PFAS to a more complex situation where both short-chain and long-chain PFAS coexist. This poses significant challenges to conventional adsorbents such as activated carbon (AC) and ion exchange resins, whose adsorption performance is strongly influenced by PFAS chain length, adsorbent surface chemistry, and multiple interactions. Herein, we designed and prepared aminated polyurethane (PU) sponge materials by introducing alkylamines with different carbon-chain lengths, denoted as PPU-C2, PPU-C6, and PPU-C14 according to the carbon-chain lengths of the grafted alkylamines, thereby constructing interfaces with progressively tuned hydrophilic-hydrophobic characteristics. The resulting material exhibited chain-length-dependent adsorption preferences toward perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acid (PFCA) of different chain lengths. Specifically, PPU-C2 achieved a removal efficiency of 72% for ultra-short-chain trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) with a maximum adsorption capacity of 596 mg g-1, whereas PPU-C6 exhibited the highest adsorption capacity toward perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) (829.2 mg g-1) with a removal efficiency of 89%. In contrast, PPU-C14 showed superior affinity toward long-chain perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), achieving a removal efficiency of 96% and a maximum adsorption capacity of 848.2 mg g-1. Experimental and theoretical results supported a chain-length-dependent matching relationship between PFCA molecular structure and local interfacial polarity. Appreciable PFCA adsorption performance was also retained in natural water samples. The material also exhibited good reusability. This study highlights the role of interfacial hydrophilic-hydrophobic regulation in governing chain-length-dependent PFCA adsorption and provides a basis for designing adsorbents with tunable affinity toward PFCA of different chain lengths.
