items.title: Translating Place Identity into Textile Motif Design
items.abstract: Place identity is expressed through symbols, practices, and visual representations. Translating regional identity into textile motifs requires a systematic approach that connects local visual sources with meaningful design decisions. This study aims to identify Pangandaran's visual identity sources, translate them into textile motif compositions, and evaluate the resulting prototype. A practice-based design research approach was employed using a modified design thinking process incorporating a visual-semantic translation matrix. Five visual sources were identified and classified, with the Marlin Fish Monument serving as the primary motif, supported by coastal landscapes, fishing activities, marine biota, and vegetation. These sources were transformed through stylization, visual hierarchy, and repeat pattern development into three design alternatives. The selected coastal panorama composition was evaluated as a digital prototype by 17 respondents comprising textile industry experts, textile design academics, and potential users. Descriptive analysis revealed favourable perceptions of recognizability, visual distinctiveness, aesthetic quality, and textile applicability, with pooled mean scores ranging from 4.3 to 4.9. The findings provide preliminary evidence of perceived regional associations rather than independently verified recognition. This study contributes a traceable visual-semantic translation approach that connects regional identity sources with textile design decisions, offering a methodological reference for developing place-based textile products.

items.title: Separating experience reporting from content recall in dream reports across sleep stages
items.abstract: Abstract Contentful dream reports are less frequent after non-rapid eye movement (NREM) than rapid eye movement (REM) awakening. This gap could reflect fewer reports of any experience or less recalled content within those reports. Distinguishing them requires retaining white dreams, experiences reported without recalled content. We audited the questions and codes behind all 20 datasets in the Dream EEG and Mentation database. Fourteen supported comparisons of any reported experience, ten supported content recall within experience reports, and one mapping merged white dreams with negative reports. A Bayesian hierarchical model decomposed the gap within six datasets supporting both comparisons at both stages. Averaged equally across datasets, contentful reports were 21.4 percentage points less frequent after NREM awakening. Most of this primary gap came from fewer reports of any experience: 16.6 points (95% credible interval 9.6 to 22.9), compared with 4.9 (− 4.1 to 12.3) for less recalled content. The experience-report contribution remained positive across weighting, sample and model checks. Content contributions depended on the datasets and weights averaged; both contributions were clearly positive in a four-dataset subset with at least ten records per stage. Uncertain-answer coding shifted the balance between negative reports and white dreams. Contrasting contentful with negative reports combined experience reporting with content recall. Theories must explain why any experience is reported less often after NREM awakening. Neural classifiers targeting any reported experience should retain white dreams in the positive class and assess content recall separately.

items.title: From Admired Figures to Ideal Partners: A Developmental Relational Prototype Model of Adult Mate Preferences
items.abstract: Early interpersonal experiences may contribute to adult partner preferences through autobiographical memory, emotional learning, and relational schemas. This study proposes the Developmental Relational Prototype Model (DRPM), which conceptualizes admired interpersonal qualities encountered during childhood and adolescence as one possible developmental source of later relational expectations. Data were collected from 799 participants in India, Oman, and the United Arab Emirates during 2006–2010, comprising 394 unmarried adults aged 18–25 years and 405 married adults aged 35–55 years. Unmarried participants reported desired qualities in an ideal future partner, whereas married participants retrospectively reported positively valued qualities associated with admired opposite-sex figures. Among unmarried participants, culture and clean habits (58.11%) and love (51.00%) were the most frequently reported partner characteristics. Recall of at least one positively valued quality was reported by 91.62% of unmarried and 75.31% of married participants, with a significant association between marital-status group and recall, χ²(1, N = 799) = 38.32, p < .001, OR = 0.28. Findings provide preliminary support for DRPM while indicating associations rather than causal developmental effects.

items.title: Explorando el engagement académico en América Latina: Una revisión panorámica y teórica
items.abstract: La literatura contemporánea reconoce al engagement académico como un constructo fundamental para comprender el rendimiento, la permanencia y el bienestar del estudiantado universitario. No obstante, en América Latina la evidencia empírica continúa siendo fragmentada y concentrada en universidades urbanas, lo que limita su aplicabilidad en contextos rurales, privados e interculturales. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar los enfoques teóricos, metodológicos y las principales tendencias de la investigación sobre engagement académico en la educación superior latinoamericana. Para ello, se realizó una Scoping Review de investigaciones publicadas entre 2014 y 2025 en las bases de datos Scopus y Web of Science. Tras un riguroso proceso de selección, se incluyeron 14 artículos científicos. Los hallazgos evidencian que el engagement actúa como mediador entre los recursos personales y académicos, además de constituir un factor protector frente al agotamiento emocional, la desmotivación y la intención de abandono. Asimismo, se identificó un predominio de estudios correlacionales y un creciente interés por la validación de instrumentos psicométricos y el análisis del compromiso académico en entornos virtuales. Se concluye que el engagement académico representa un factor estratégico para fortalecer el bienestar, la permanencia y el desempeño estudiantil, aunque persisten importantes vacíos de investigación en diversos contextos latinoamericanos.

items.title: Supervisor need-thwarting behaviour and followers' turnover intentions: a conditional moderated mediation model
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how supervisor need-thwarting behaviour relates to employee turnover intentions through needs frustration, and how interactional justice and job insecurity conditionally moderate this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected through a two-wave survey of Australian workers (n = 359). The proposed conditional moderated mediation model was tested using Hayes' PROCESS Macro Model 11 in IBM SPSS v28. Findings Supervisor need-thwarting behaviour was positively associated with turnover intentions, both directly and indirectly through needs frustration. The indirect relationship was conditionally moderated by interactional justice and job insecurity. Interactional justice buffered the positive association between need-thwarting behaviour and needs frustration when job insecurity was low. This buffer was nonsignificant at average insecurity, and reversed in slope when insecurity was high, producing a significant index of conditional moderated mediation. Originality/value This study frames supervisor need-thwarting behaviour as an aspect of harmful leadership, and positions needs frustration as the psychological mechanism that connects supervisor behaviour with turnover intentions. Our arguments advance distinct explanatory roles for self-determination theory and conservation of resources theory, and conceptualise interactional justice as a contingent relational resource that provides a buffering capacity which is undermined by job insecurity.

items.title: Tree island area in oil palm agroforests directly and indirectly drives evaporative fraction
items.abstract: Abstract. Evapotranspiration (ET) – the combined water flux from soil and vegetation to the atmosphere – is a key component of water cycling and climate regulation, and strongly affected by land-use changes. The evaporative fraction (EF), representing the proportion of available energy allocated to ET, is often preferred over ET as a target variable in studies involving repeated measurements under varying weather conditions. In Sumatra’s lowlands in Indonesia, (evapo)transpiration of dominant land-use types including oil palm monocultures is well studied; however, there is a lack of studies assessing ET (or EF) across diverse mosaic landscapes and types of land-use such as oil palm agroforests. Across 52 experimental plots – forest restoration patches known as “tree islands” – in an oil palm landscape (EFForTS-BEE), we tested whether the experimental treatments ‘planted tree diversity’ and ‘tree island area’ influence ET and EF as derived from UAV (uncrewed aerial vehicle)-based thermography and subsequent energy balance modeling. A random partition linear model showed that planted tree diversity (1, 2, 3, or 6 species) did not affect plot-level ET or EF, whereas tree island area (25, 100, 400, or 1600 m2) had a positive effect, with EF increasing by 17 % from the smallest to the largest tree islands. A structural equation model revealed that the effect of tree island area on EF was mediated by both direct and indirect pathways. Specifically, a strong direct effect of island area on EF (Std.Beta = 0.44, p < 0.001) was complemented by an indirect pathway through increased observed woody plant diversity and stand structural complexity. Stand structural complexity had a positive effect on EF (Std.Beta = 0.20, p < 0.05), while neither the vegetation index GNDVI nor tree height variability had significant effects. The observed tree-island-area effect can be explained by a decrease of EF along an edge gradient detected inside the larger tree islands. Our findings suggest that larger tree islands enhance ET and EF through structural and biodiversity-related mechanisms. This underscores the importance of tree islands in human-modified landscapes, not only as biodiversity refugia but also as functional elements that support climate regulation.

items.title: Horizontal gene transfer and reciprocal chimerism in Compactonostoc (Nostocales, Cyanobacteriophyta) with evidence for two new species in the genus
items.abstract: The genus Nostoc has long been known to be polyphyletic, and recent taxonomic work has segregated several Nostoc-like lineages into new genera, including Compactonostoc. Until now, C. shennongjiaensis was the only described species in the genus. In a survey of biological soil crusts from Santa Catalina Island (California, United States), we isolated two Nostoc-like strains that phylogenetically affiliate with Compactonostoc. A polyphasic approach based on morphology, 16S rRNA gene phylogeny, 16S-23S ITS rRNA secondary structures, and cloned ribosomal operons revealed that each strain harbored two highly divergent ribosomal operon types. One operon (Type 2) is closely related to C. shennongjiaensis and contains the two tRNA genes in the ITS rRNA region, whereas the second (Type 1) lacks tRNA genes and is strongly allied to the horizontally acquired Type 1 operon previously reported in Kalymmatonema (as Scytonema hyalinum), indicating an ancient horizontal gene transfer event from an unsampled Nostocaceaen lineage. In one of the isolated strains, we additionally detected two reciprocal chimeric operons (Type 2/1 and Type 1/2), with crossovers in a conserved region of the 16S rRNA gene, demonstrating ongoing recombination between operon types. The ITS rRNA region percent dissimilarity, ITS rRNA region domain structures, and 16S rRNA gene percent similarity, together with consistent morphological differences, support recognition of the two strains as new species of Compactonostoc, C. mediiheterocytium and C. chimera, both clearly distinct from C. shennongjiaensis. Our results document rare ribosomal-operon horizontal gene transfer and reciprocal chimerism in Compactonostoc and highlight the need to examine multiple clones and operons when describing cyanobacterial taxa based on rRNA genes.

items.abstract: Дослідження присвячено комплексному аналізу просторової структури та рівню концентрації природно-заповідного фонду (ПЗФ) Рівненської області в системі державного управління лісами після реорганізації колишніх держлісгоспів у надлісництва філії «Поліський лісовий офіс» ДП «Ліси України». Проведено ретроспективну гармонізацію відомчих статистичних матеріалів станом на 1 січня 2023 року від 16 колишніх лісгоспів до 8 сучасних надлісництв. Вперше застосовано коефіцієнт концентрації чотирьох фірм (CR4) та індекс Герфіндаля-Гіршмана (HHI) як просторово-структурні індикатори управлінського навантаження. Здійснено систематизацію документованих збитків, завданих об'єктам ПЗФ та лісовим екосистемам внаслідок збройної агресії РФ, та проаналізовано екологічні наслідки замінування 5-кілометрової прикордонної смуги з Республікою Білорусь. Встановлено високий рівень просторової нерівномірності: чотири провідні надлісництва (Висоцьке – 24.82%, Клесівське – 18.78%, Рафалівське – 16.06%, Соснівське – 13.76%) концентрують 73.42% площі ПЗФ області (CR4 = 73.42%, HHI = 0.1642). Задокументовано, що лісові пожежі внаслідок ворожих атак завдали шкоди довкіллю на суму понад 7 млн грн із викидами більше 2.2 тис. тонн CO2. Замінування прикордоння створило суцільний бар'єр для міграції великих ссавців та унеможливило натурний моніторинг Рівненського природного заповідника. Обґрунтовано необхідність переходу від уніфікованого до просторово-диференційованого управління лісами.

items.title: Rearchitecting Global Oil Security: The UAE Inland Canal as a Systemic Redundancy Solution (A Real-Options and Capacity Reservation Approach to the Sharjah-Fujairah Corridor)
items.abstract: This study addresses a core problem in infrastructure finance and public-goods provision: how to finance and govern a costly, non-excludable, crisis-contingent transit asset that markets systematically underprovide, using a proposed 116-kilometre Sharjah-Fujairah corridor as the empirical case. The paper combines a single-case analysis of the 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure, comparative analysis of canal, tunnel and pipeline analogues, and transparent financial modelling, capital-recovery, break-even-toll, capacity-reservation and real-options valuation, drawing on International Energy Agency, Energy Information Administration, maritime-intelligence, Brookings, OPEC, FATF and Central Bank of the UAE sources. The pipelines cannot structurally replace the chokepoint, leaving only 3.5-5.5 of roughly 20 million barrels per day redirectable. A canal-pipeline hybrid is the only buildable reference design, costing a reference $130-160 billion once documented megaproject-overrun rates are applied. A capacity-reservation fee of about 3 percent of importers' Hormuz-crude value covers the capital charge and, under real-options valuation, is recovered within roughly 16-27 crisis days. Governance must be anchored in enforceable AML/CFT and sanctions controls. The corridor is viable only as a global energy-insurance instrument aligning payment with benefit through reservation contracts, evidence-gated phasing, and engineered financial integrity. The framework generalises to other concentrated transport nodes.

items.title: Indigenous Sea Gardens have been Adapting to Sea Level Change for at least Four Millennia
items.abstract: Abstract Indigenous peoples along the northwest coast of North America have maintained sea gardens (clam gardens), an ancestral form of mariculture, for at least four thousand years. While their occurrence is being increasingly reported, the degree to which Holocene sea level change has obscured existing ancestral structures along parts of the coast was unknown. We used intertidal and subtidal archaeological excavations, ground-penetrating radar, and radiocarbon dating to assess sea garden wall structure, thickness, and site formation processes at two coastal sites in southern British Columbia, Canada. By comparing sea garden wall depth to the local relative sea level history, we found that sea gardens have been continuously modified and maintained for at least four millennia, and that the morphology of sea gardens is different in areas of transgressing versus regressing shorelines. Moreover, we found that different local sea level histories will influence the visibility of these monumental features today. These observations, woven with Indigenous knowledge, demonstrate that not only is sea gardening an enduring, adaptive cultural practice that has been resilient to changes in sea level position for millennia, but also offers a strategy for climate change adaptation today.

items.title: EVALUATING SOIL QUALITY ACROSS MULTIPLE SOIL TYPES FOR SUSTAINABLE OIL PALM PLANTATIONS IN CENTRAL KALIMANTAN, INDONESIA
items.abstract: Assessing soil quality is essential to ensuring the long-term sustainability of oil palm plantations by aligning agricultural productivity with environmental and social dimensions.This study examines the influence of soil type on soil quality in Kotawaringin Timur District, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia.Specifically, it evaluates four representative soil types (Histosols, Inceptisols, Ultisols and Entisols) using the soil quality index (SQI) framework, identifies key indicators through a minimum data set (MDS), and proposes soil-specific management strategies.The methodology includes field surveys, biological and physicochemical soil analyses, SQI computation and statistical evaluation, with six replications per soil type.Results demonstrate significant variation in SQI values: Low for Histosols (0.245) and very low for Ultisols (0.178), Inceptisols (0.180) and Entisols (0.182).Soil organic carbon (SOC), exchangeable magnesium (Ex-Mg) and available phosphorus (Av-P) were identified as critical indicators influencing soil function.To improve soil quality, the application of organic amendments such as compost, biochar and biofertilisers derived from oil palm residues is recommended.Integrating weed biomass may further enhance nutrient availability and soil resilience, supporting sustainable plantation management tailored to site-specific conditions.

items.title: límites planetarios como condiciones de frontera para la sostenibilidad corporativa
items.abstract: El presente artículo expone la problemática del abordaje instrumental, parcial y fragmentado de los límites planetarios en la gestión organizacional. La sostenibilidad corporativa enfrenta una tensión central en el antropoceno: mientras las organizaciones incrementan sus discursos, reportes, estrategias ambientales e innovaciones, la degradación de los sistemas biofísicos que sostienen la vida continúa profundizándose. El objetivo del documento entonces es analizar cómo los límites planetarios pueden ser comprendidos como referencias biofísicas para repensar la gestión organizacional y la sostenibilidad corporativa. En cuanto a la metodología, se desarrolló una revisión crítica e integrativa, la búsqueda se realizó en Scopus y Google Scholar, y esta se dividió en tres bloques; se utilizaron diferentes criterios de búsqueda y selección como: palabras clave, ecuaciones de búsqueda, tiempo (2007-2025) y nivel de relevancia; finalmente, fueron seleccionados 52 documentos temáticos y 3 metodológicos, los cuales fueron sometidos a una revisión y análisis profundo; y posteriormente, se construyó una síntesis integrando desarrollos teóricos de diversos campos disciplinares. Los resultados evidencian que la adopción de los límites planetarios en la gestión organizacional puede permitir el desplazamiento de la sostenibilidad corporativa, desde una lógica de eficiencia, riesgo, reputación e innovación incremental hacia una comprensión sistémica, multiescalar y biofísicamente condicionada.

items.title: Tubastraea coccinea (Cnidaria: Anthozoa) is the globally dispersed species of Sun Coral
items.abstract: Species of the genus Tubastraea (sun corals) have dispersed globally over recent decades, but morphological trait identification has led to taxonomic confusion, with multiple authors proposing conflicting species identifications due to high morphological plasticity and overlapping diagnostic traits. We combined global-scale molecular phylogenetics with chromosome-level genome assemblies to resolve this taxonomic issue. Using mitochondrial and nuclear markers from 287 specimens across five ocean regions, including type localities in Bora Bora (T. coccinea) and Galapagos (T. tagusensis), we reconstructed phylogenetic relationships and inferred demographic history through approximate Bayesian computation. We also generated high-quality, chromosome-level genome assemblies for three morphologically distinct morphotypes from the Brazilian coastline. Phylogenetic and species delimitation analyses revealed two well-supported clades: a small, geographically restricted T. tagusensis clade confined to the Galapagos Islands, and a large cosmopolitan clade containing all worldwide samples, including T. coccinea from its type locality. Comparative genomic analyses of the three morphotypes revealed k-mer spectra compatible with triploidy and assemblies comprising 14 chromosome-scale scaffolds with extensive synteny and gene-tree discordance consistent with incomplete lineage sorting. Dispersal-route analyses identified the Southeastern Pacific (Galapagos) as the ancestral source, with at least two independent, human-mediated colonization events establishing populations in the Southwestern Atlantic, Gulf of Mexico, and Western Pacific. Our results establish Tubastraea coccinea as the cosmopolitan species responsible for global dissemination, while T. tagusensis is endemic to the Galapagos and not involved in the worldwide dispersion.

items.title: LAND USE CHANGE PATHWAYS IN THE BARUMUN WATERSHED: ASSESSING THE ROLE OF OIL PALM EXPANSION
items.abstract: Indonesia is among the world's major palm oil producers, and oil palm expansion is often associated with deforestation.This study examines gradual land use and land cover (LULC) changes from 2000 to 2023 in the Barumun watershed, North Sumatra, using Landsat 5 Thematic Mapper (TM) and Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager (OLI) imagery processed through Google Earth Engine.A Random Forest (RF) machine learning algorithm was applied for supervised classification.The results indicate that forest cover decreased by 5.12% over 23 years.The primary conversion pathway was forest to other land with tree cover (accounting for up to 54.60% of initial forest loss), which was later converted to oil palm plantations.Oil palm area increased by 13.91%, but direct forest-to-oil palm conversion was limited.These findings suggest that oil palm was not the primary cause of initial deforestation in this watershed.The results provide evidence for policymakers to distinguish between direct and indirect land use change pathways when designing sustainable land management strategies.

items.title: Local Community Development in the Context of Biodiversity Conservation: Challenges and Conflicts in Romania
items.abstract: The intersection between rural economic development and biodiversity conservation constitutes one of the most polarizing challenges in contemporary environmental governance. In Romania, the expansion of protected areas - especially through the European Natura 2000 network - has frequently clashed with the socio-economic aspirations of local communities, which were often divided, manipulated in the short-term interests of some. This paper examines the systemic conflicts that arise between the need to develop local infrastructure, expand tourism and modernize agriculture, exploit different resources on the one hand, and strict legal requirements for ecosystem conservation on the other. Using a multidisciplinary approach rooted in socio-ecological resilience and environmental sociology, this study analyses different typologies of conflicts in diverse Romanian landscapes, from vulnerable wetland ecosystems in the Danube Delta, on the Danube in monte, in areas adjacent to other rivers, to fragmented forest habitats in the Carpathian Mountains. The research highlights that top-down conservation policies often trigger localized resistance, mainly due to economic marginalization, restricted access to resources (such as grazing and timber exploitation, ballast, sand mining, etc.) and inadequate compensation mechanisms for wildlife damage. In addition, the study assesses how unregulated infrastructure and real estate development in biodiversity hotspots threaten critical ecological corridors. The findings indicate that the current institutional framework in Romania fails to adequately bridge the gap between scientific conservation objectives and community-driven development needs. Ultimately, this paper argues that mitigating these environmental conflicts requires a shift from strictly punitive enforcement of conservation laws to participatory management models. By actively integrating local stakeholders into decision-making processes and implementing sustainable bioeconomy initiatives, policymakers can transform biodiversity from an economic barrier into a catalyst for community resilience, ensuring long-term ecological stability and social cohesion, with the ultimate goal of reaching a convergence of interests of all parties involved.

items.title: Governance pathways shape trophic recovery under climate change in the western Mediterranean Sea
items.abstract: Abstract Marine ecosystems are increasingly shaped by the interacting effects of climate change and human activities, yet the extent to which alternative socio-economic pathways can modify future ecological trajectories remains poorly understood. Here, we integrate climate projections with coherent socioecological scenarios to evaluate long-term ecosystem responses in the western Mediterranean Sea. Using a spatially explicit marine ecosystem model (Ecopath with Ecosim) representing 92 functional groups and five fishing fleets, we simulated ecosystem dynamics from 1995 to 2020 and projected changes to 2100 under contrasting pathways combining climate forcing, fisheries management, marine protection, and habitat restoration. Scenarios included a sustainability-oriented pathway (SSP1–RCP2.6; Global Sustainability), two high-emission pathways with contrasting governance (SSP3–RCP8.5; National Enterprise and SSP5–RCP8.5; World Markets), and associated status quo baselines. Socio-economic pathways substantially modified the ecological outcomes of climate change. Under Global Sustainability, reduced fishing pressure, expanded marine protection, discard mitigation, and habitat restoration promoted rapid rebuilding of commercial and predatory biomass, recovery of conservation-relevant species, and improved trophic structure within two decades, although fisheries catches declined. In contrast, high-emission pathways produced slower and more uneven responses. Despite sharing the same climate trajectory, National Enterprise and World Markets generated markedly different outcomes, highlighting the importance of governance priorities, technological development, and spatial management in shaping ecosystem futures within the same climate constraints. Responses were spatially heterogeneous across the basin, revealing uneven ecological benefits, vulnerabilities, and trade-offs among regions and functional groups. Our findings demonstrate that marine ecosystem trajectories are shaped by interactions between climate forcing and human activities and highlight the potential for management, conservation, and restoration to enhance ecosystem resilience under future climate change.

items.title: Variation in rhizosphere microbial communities and nitrogen- and phosphorus-cycling functional genes among rubber plantations in Yunnan, China
items.abstract: Introduction Rhizosphere microorganisms are important participants in soil nutrient transformation. However, variation in rhizosphere microbial community composition and nitrogen (N)- and phosphorus (P)-cycling functional gene profiles among rubber plantations in Yunnan Province remains unclear. Methods Metagenomic sequencing was used to compare rhizosphere microbial community composition and N- and P-cycling functional gene profiles among the rubber plantations located in five major natural rubber-producing areas in Yunnan Province, China: Gengma (MD), Ximeng (XM), Mengla (ML), Jinghong (JH), and Jiangcheng (JC). Results Bacterial and fungal community composition and N- and P-cycling functional gene profiles differed significantly among the five rubber plantations. JC exhibited higher fungal diversity and richness, but its bacterial diversity was significantly lower than that in MD. The bacterial communities were dominated by Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota, and Actinomycetota, and the relative abundance of Acidobacteria was significantly enriched in JC compared to JH. Furthermore, Mucoromycota, Ascomycota, and Basidiomycota were the dominant phyla in the fungal community. At the functional level, compared to JC, key genes associated with N cycling were significantly enriched in ML, including N assimilation ( glnA , gltB , gltD ), dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium ( narG , narH , nirB ), nitrification ( nxrA , nxrB ), and denitrification ( napA , napB ). Furthermore, the nosZ gene was also significantly enriched in MD compared to JC. Regarding the P cycle, compared to JC, genes associated with high-affinity phosphate transporters ( pstA , pstB , pstC ) and polyphosphate degradation ( ndk ) were significantly enriched in MD, whereas the organic phosphorus mineralization-related gene phnX exhibited the opposite trend. Meanwhile, compared to MD, the polyphosphate degradation-related gene ppk2 was significantly enriched in ML, whereas the inorganic phosphorus solubilization-related gene pqqC exhibited the opposite pattern. Hierarchical partitioning identified soil pH, total phosphorus (TP), and total potassium (TK) as the primary factors significantly associated with variations in bacterial community composition and P-cycling functional gene profiles. Conclusion In summary, the composition of rhizosphere bacterial and fungal communities, as well as the functional gene profiles related to N and P cycling, differed significantly among the investigated rubber plantations. These variations were closely associated with soil physicochemical factors. These findings may provide a microbiological basis for further developing site-specific nutrient management strategies in rubber plantations.

items.title: Correction: A strategy towards the “good”: a diagnosis of Lake Karla, Greece management practices during the last 20 years
items.abstract: 1.1 Why is there a need for lake restoration?Healthy freshwater ecosystems provide essential services to society -services that are costly and often impossible to replace once these systems are degraded. According to the SOER 2015 review on the health of freshwater systems in Western and Central Europe, the pressure reported to most affect surface waterbodies is pollution from diffuse sources, in particular from agriculture, causing nutrient enrichment (EEA, 2015). Globally, inland waters support a disproportionately large fraction of biodiversity relative to their surface area, yet they remain among the most threatened ecosystems on Earth (Dudgeon et al., 2006). Human intervention has disrupted hydrology and landuse connectivity across catchments for centuries, exposing freshwater bodies to compounding pressures from agricultural runoff, urban encroachment, hydromorphological alteration, and overextraction (Haase et al., 2023). Globally, these ecosystems face an acute biodiversity crisis, while increasing risks from climate change and pollution make effective management increasingly uncertain. Shallow lakes ecology is inherently complex due to the interplay of external nutrient loading, internal sediment release, and alternative stable states that can shift rapidly under climate or hydrological forcing (Scheffer et al., 1993;Jeppesen et al., 2007). Warm, shallow lakes in Southern Europe face additional thermal stress, longer stratification-free periods, changes in precipitation and storminess (Meerhoff et al., 2012;2022) and reduced dilution capacity compared to their northern counterparts, making recovery trajectories both slower and less predictable (Moss et al., 2011). They are particularly vulnerable to eutrophication: once shifted to a turbid, phytoplanktondominated state through the interplay of external nutrient loading, internal sediment phosphorus recycling, loss of macrophytes, and suppression of zooplankton grazers, internal feedback mechanisms make recovery both slow and non-linear (Scheffer et al., 1993;Jeppesen et al., 2007). Restoration approaches must therefore target multiple pressures and feedback loops simultaneously rather than a single stressor. Given the vulnerability of "warm" freshwaters of Southern Europe and the overarching nature of human pressures acting upon them (including unsustainable use of nitrogen and phosphorus, over-extraction, and climate change) the restoration target for improving their ecological status and their ecosystem services is essential. There is also a growing evidence that such systems play an important role in climate regulation through the emission of greenhouse gases (predominantly CH₄; Downing et al., 2021), adding a further dimension to the urgency of their management. Irrigated agriculture accounts for more than 80% of total allocated freshwater in some Mediterranean regions (Araus, 2004), creating a fundamental tension between food security imperatives and the ecological integrity of water bodies. Maintaining this balance requires approaches that explicitly link catchment-scale land management to in-lake ecological functioning.Ecosystem restoration is the process of assisting the recovery of an ecosystem (state) that has been degraded, damaged, or destroyed (Council of the EU, 2023) and has been established as a global priority under the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration (2021Restoration ( -2030) ) and, in Europe, through the Nature Restoration Law (EU 2024(EU /1991;;). Restoration is an increasingly important approach in lake water quality management: the most common restoration target for lakes is to improve their ecological state and the ecosystem services they provide to society (Tammeorg et al., 2023). In this context, restoration means assisting the recovery of ecosystems that have been degraded or destroyed, as well as conserving/sustaining those that are still intact (Gann et al., 2019;May et al., 2020), while the term 'sustainable lake restoration' implies that even a single well-designed intervention can deliver long-lasting effects without requiring repeated future interventions (Tammeorg et al., 2023).. The degree to which recovery can be achieved is a complex issue that depends primarily on the removal of the main pressures combined with the in-lake biogeochemical interactions (Goldyn et al., 2014). The desire to restore freshwaters degraded by land use change, agriculture, or other environmental stressors has emerged primarily over the last decades, driven by the recognition that passive recovery is insufficient for heavily modified systems. The need to manage lakes in a more sustainable manner is recognised under EU Water Policy and, more recently, under the Nature Restoration Law, which explicitly aims to support green economic development alongside ecological recovery.Under the Post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework (December 2022), restoration targets now mandate that at least 30% of terrestrial, freshwater, coastal, and marine ecosystems be brought under active restoration by 2030, placing renewed urgency on diagnosing why past interventions have succeeded or failed. According to the latest European Environment Agency assessment, more than half of European freshwater bodies still fail to meet the criteria for good ecological status set by the Water Framework Directive (WFD, 2000/60/EC. The new environmental challenges such as the SDGs, the Green Deal, and the Circular Economy require "sustainable" management and restoration solutions to deliver multiple environmental and socio-economic co-benefits extending beyond the scale of intervention (Tammeorg et al., 2023;2024). This is particularly critical in the Mediterranean basin, where the complexity produced from a combination of factors like semi-arid climate, intensive irrigated agriculture, and rapidly intensifying drought cycles; creates conditions of structural water stress (Balzan et al., 2019) that conventional grey infrastructure alone cannot resolve. These all shape the framework of challenges and opportunities for freshwater ecosystem conservation (Stefanidis et al., 2025).Despite sustained policy efforts under the WFD, the ecological status of European lakes remains poor across most Member States. The EEA (2018) reported that 44% of lake water bodies failed to achieve good ecological status or potential (with eutrophication remaining the dominant pressure in lowland lakes) and the same percentage remained in the 2025 EEA report, with eutrophication, hydromorphological alteration, and diffuse agricultural pollution identified as the principal drivers of degradation enhanced by climate change. These pressures are not uniform across the continent: Poikane et al. (2019) showed that nutrient criteria and ecological thresholds vary substantially across European lake types, and that the response of biological quality elements to nutrient loading is highly lake-type specific; implying that restoration targets cannot be applied uniformly. A broad typological framework for European rivers and lakes developed by Lyche Solheim et al. (2019) confirmed that lake typology is a prerequisite for meaningful cross-country comparisons of ecological status and restoration effectiveness. At regional scale, reflecting the structural sensitivity of warm systems (cyanobacterial dominance, macrophyte loss, and trophic state hysteresis) and the weaker top-down control (Beklioglu et al., 2007;Jeppesen et al., 2007), substantially greater nutrient load reductions are required to trigger the shift from turbid to clear-water state compared to temperate lakes (Romo et al., 2005) meaning that Mediterranean lakes and reservoirs may exhibit systematically lower ecological quality ratios than their northern counterparts for equivalent nutrient loads.Our case study is a typical Mediterranean freshwater ecosystem (Lake Karla, Greece) having the peculiarity that it used to be a natural shallow lake until the 1960s, when it was drained for agricultural and health reasons. In 2010, a new, smaller Lake Karla was re-established, situated in the lower, deeper part of the former natural lake (Figure 1). It was designed as a shallow lake (mean depth ~2 m) with a surface area of 38 km², intended primarily as a wetland restoration initiative while simultaneously serving irrigation, flood attenuation, and groundwater recharge functions. items.title: Substrate-mediated oxidative stress alleviation and rhizosphere microbiome modulation enable submerged macrophyte restoration in high-turbidity water
items.abstract: Introduction Ecological restoration of submerged macrophytes in highly turbid waters is severely hampered by light attenuation, which imposes significant oxidative stress on plants and disrupts their physiological homeostasis. While suspended planting technology offers a solution by optimizing light exposure, the critical role of planting substrates in modulating plant stress tolerance and rhizosphere resilience remains largely unexplored—a knowledge gap that this study addresses for the first time. This study is novel in systematically linking substrate physical properties to plant redox regulation and rhizosphere microbiome assembly under turbid-water stress, providing an integrated plant–microbe perspective previously unaddressed. Methods In this study, we cultivated Vallisneria spinulosa Yan using four suspended substrates (plastic mesh, palm mat, linen cloth, and bamboo woven strips) in outdoor flume experiments, aiming to evaluate their effects on plant physiology, water remediation, and associated microbial networks. Results Our results demonstrated that the linen cloth substrate most effectively alleviated oxidative damage, as evidenced by significantly enhanced root development, biomass accumulation, and leaf photosynthetic pigment content, alongside a marked reduction in physiological oxidative stress markers. Functionally, all treatments achieved over 90% turbidity removal; however, the linen cloth group exhibited superior purification efficiency, with the highest total nitrogen and total phosphorus removal loads (2.32 × 10 -4 and 2.70 × 10 -4 g·m -2 ·d -1 , respectively). Critically, microbial community analysis revealed that the linen cloth substrate fostered a more complex and interconnected rhizosphere network, with a notable enrichment of a denitrifying bacterial family ( Comamonadaceae ), indicating a synergistic enhancement of plant–microbe mutualism under stress. Discussion Collectively, our findings identify linen cloth as the optimal substrate for suspended planting, not merely as a physical support, but as a catalyst for reinforcing the plant’s antioxidant defense system and orchestrating a beneficial rhizosphere microbiome, thereby providing a robust theoretical framework for applying this redox-based ecological engineering strategy in turbid water restoration.

items.title: Comparison of Faecal Anaerobic Fungi of Cows and Goats Offered Similar Diet
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anaerobic fungi (AF) are key contributors to fibre degradation in ruminants, yet their host-associated patterns remain poorly understood. The aim of this study was to compare the diversity and composition of AF in faeces of goats and cows offered similar diet and to evaluate the influence of animal species on the gut mycobiome. METHODS: A total of 15 female goats (Blond Adamellan) and 16 female cows (Brown Swiss) kept on an organic farm were fed pasture and hay. The fungal structure in faeces was examined by high-throughput sequencing using the D2 LSU region. RESULTS: Alpha diversity measurements revealed significantly lower species richness and evenness in goats compared to cows. Beta diversity analysis showed statistical dissimilarities and distinct community structures between the two ruminant species confirming host-specific clustering. Taxonomic composition differed significantly, cow samples were dominated by Caecomycetaceae and Neocallimastigaceae, particularly the genera Orpinomyces, Caecomyces and Cyllamyces. Goat samples were dominated by Anaeromyces, Caecomyces and according to relative abundance they formed two distinct clusters with highly similar fungal profile. Differential abundance analysis further highlighted the enrichment of Anaeromyces, unclassified genus within Caecomycetaceae, Feramyces and Pecoramyces in goats, whereas Caecomyces and Piromyces were more abundant in cows. CONCLUSION: These findings underscore the strong influence of host phylogeny on the faecal anaerobic fungal community.

items.title: Resistance to Thrips tabaci in onion wild relatives, and the role of intraspecific thrips diversity in overcoming resistance
items.abstract: Onion ( Allium cepa L.) is one of the most important horticultural crops worldwide, and Thrips tabaci is the main pest on it. It is a polyphagous, often insecticide-resistant, cryptic species with two main phylogenetic groups characterized by host range and reproductive modes: arrhenotokous and thelytokous. Host plant resistance, mainly antibiosis-type, is a promising solution for preventing or reducing T. tabaci population build-up. Resistant sources are absent in onion germplasm, but present in wild relatives. We determined the resistance mechanisms present in resistant (R) and moderately resistant (MR) onion wild relatives, and whether arrhenotokous and thelytokous (heteroplasmic or non-heteroplasmic) T. tabaci differ in overcoming this resistance. Oviposition rate, survival rate of T. tabaci immature stages, and length of the immature period from L1 to pupae were determined on R, MR, and susceptible Allium genotypes infested with arrhenotokous and thelytokous populations. The R species, A. prostratum , A. komarowii , and A. flavescens, block the cycle of arrhenotokous and thelytokous T. tabaci in the L1 or L2 stage. Allium prostratum showed antibiosis, while A. flavescens and A. komarowii showed antibiosis and antixenosis. The MR species, A. angulosum , A. senescens , and A. eduardii, partially impede the life cycle through antixenosis and antibiosis. Heteroplasmic and non-heteroplasmic thelytokous T. tabaci did not statistically differ, and they overcome the MR mechanisms better than arrhenotokous T. tabaci . Arrhenotokous showed a higher oviposition rate and lower survival (as specialists) than the thelytokous (generalists). Some of the identified sources, especially Allium prostratum , may be suitable for introgressing resistance into cultivated onion .

items.title: “Every professional is a climate professional”: a framework for climate responsibility in practice
items.abstract: Professionals are an important class of actors often overlooked in efforts to address climate change. Across fields such as health, law, education, the built environment, and media, they combine specialised knowledge, institutional authority, and public credibility, giving them a distinctive capacity to translate sustainability science into practice, reshape organisational systems, and coordinate climate action within their domains. This paper conceptualises professionals as a distinct class of climate actors and develops a generalisable framework for how their expertise, ethical values, and institutional authority can generate systemic change. We treat the professional role as a socially constructed position, formed first in higher education and then through accreditation and institutional norms that can unintentionally reinforce unsustainable practices. Universities and the bodies that accredit their programmes are therefore central sites for forming climate-ready professionals. Building on this, we set out a framework for enabling climate-aligned practice, organised around three interrelated stages: crisis translation, which frames climate change as integral to a profession's mission; ethical activation, which grounds climate responsibility in professional values; and institutional pathways, which shape how climate action is enabled or constrained by professional bodies, training regimes, and organisational systems. These stages operate across multiple levels, from individual practitioners to professional associations and the wider policy context. The analysis turns on a central tension. Professionals hold both the capacity to catalyse meaningful climate action and the potential to reproduce unsustainable structures. Reorienting professional norms, institutions, and practices is therefore essential if their expertise is to contribute to climate mitigation and adaptation.

items.title: Implications of hardbottom sponge community decline for ecosystem function in the Florida Keys, Florida (USA)
items.abstract: Human damage to the marine ecosystem of the Florida Keys may have begun in pre-Columbian times but expanded with European colonization about 400 years ago, particularly through overfishing of large species such as seals, turtles, and groupers. Around the turn of the 20 th century, draining of the Everglades and construction of the overseas railway altered forever the flow of fresh and saltwater in the ecosystem. But by and large, the resilience of the ecosystem remained intact until the late 1970’s-early 1980’s when it began to collapse, exemplified by phytoplankton blooms, seagrass and sponge die-offs, mass urchin mortalities, and coral disease. Today, seagrass meadows are relatively healthy but coral reefs harbor few corals and inshore hardbottom habitats have been stripped of sponges and octocorals among other taxa. Changes to hardbottom sponge communities between 2002 and 2018 throughout the Florida Keys are documented here, as are the ramifications of sponge loss on local benthic scouring, underwater soundscapes, and the effect on waterborne microbial communities and water chemistry by sponge filtration. From 2002-2018, sponge abundance and diversity declined by 66% and 34% (respectively), even in regions that did not experience sponge-killing cyanobacteria blooms. Without the presence of large sponges, benthic scouring is reduced, which promotes sedimentation and may hasten the transition of hardbottom habitat to seagrass. Loud, acoustically complex hardbottom soundscapes become acoustic dead-zones without soniferous species associated with large sponges, dampening the sonic signatures that larvae and other animal life stages use to navigate to hardbottom. The decline in sponges and the effects of their lost filtration is estimated to have reduced ecosystem-level removal of DOC by 30 – 56% and NH 4 by 40% along with an approximate 30% reduction in the release by sponges into the water of PO 4 and NO 2 -NO 3. Like that on the region’s coral reefs, the ecological phase-shift in shallow, hardbottom communities of the Florida Keys has been catastrophic and the dearth of sponges has had effects that cascade through the ecosystem.

items.title: Field deployable viral genomic surveillance using panviral integrated indexed primers
items.abstract: Abstract Rapid viral identification near the point of emergence could support outbreak investigation where sequencing infrastructure is limited. The Panviral integrated indexed Primer (PiiP) assay combines broadly reactive viral primers with integrated Oxford Nanopore indices and offline analysis. The workflow was evaluated using human, animal, and environmental samples from Cambodia and deployed with a portable laboratory at a live bird market under tropical conditions. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated detection across diverse sample matrices, although sensitivity varied by viral target and influenza subtype assignment was limited. During field deployment, environmental samples, including air samples, were processed on site, with initial viral read characterization available within 6.5 hours of sample receipt. The workflow reduces library preparation steps and enables same day viral screening outside centralized laboratories. These findings support further evaluation of PiiP for decentralized genomic surveillance, with confirmatory analysis required for uncertain taxonomic assignments.

items.title: Contrasting invasion risks of Pomacea canaliculata and Pontederia crassipes under future climate change in the middle and lower reaches of Yangtze River
items.abstract: The invasion and spread of alien aquatic organisms pose an increasing threat to ecosystem stability and functioning, biodiversity conservation, and socioeconomic development under ongoing climate change. However, limited attention has been given to the compound ecological risks of multi-species invasions driven by the combined effects of climate factors, topography, water quality, vegetation, and other environmental variables under future climate scenarios. Focusing on Pomacea canaliculata (P. canaliculata) and Pontederia crassipes ( P. crassipes ), this study employed the MaxEnt model and spatial analysis to identify key environmental determinants and to project current and future habitat suitability in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River Basin under SSP245 and SSP585 scenarios. The results show that the MaxEnt model performed with high accuracy for P. crassipes (AUC = 0.954) and good accuracy for P. canaliculata (AUC = 0.880). Temperature-related variables predominantly constrained the distribution of P. crassipes , with a cumulative contribution of 44.2%, particularly isothermality and temperature seasonality, whereas P. canaliculata was jointly influenced by terrain factors and thermal conditions, with contribution rates of 40.5% and 23.3%, respectively. In terms of current habitat distribution, P. canaliculata (28.23 × 10 4 km 2 ) occupies a larger range than P. crassipes (5.77 × 10 4 km 2 ), with P. canaliculata exhibiting a widespread distribution mainly concentrated in the Hanjiang Plain and the Jiangsu-Anhui coastal plains, whereas P. crassipes follows a belt-like distribution pattern, primarily spreading in Poyang Lake and the Yangtze River Delta. From 2021 to 2100, the suitable habitat of P. canaliculata is projected to expand under both SSP245 and SSP585 scenarios, with a more extensive and rapid expansion under the high-emission scenario (SSP585) (reaching 35.06 × 10 4 km 2 during 20 4 1–2060, an increase of 6.83 × 10 4 km 2 from present) High-suitability areas display an overall increasing trend, whereas moderate- and low-suitability areas exhibit marked inter-period fluctuations. In contrast, the suitable habitat of P. crassipes follows a trend of initial expansion followed by contraction under both climate scenarios, reaching the maximum total area during 2041–2060 under SSP245 (8.11 × 10⁴ km²) and SSP585 (6.81 × 10⁴ km²). After 2060, the suitable habitat begins to decrease and will significantly shrink to its current level during 2081–2100. The contrasting responses of the two species highlight the necessity for species-specific and climate-adaptive management strategies. Integrating climate projections with habitat suitability modeling can enhance early warning systems and support risk-based management of aquatic biological invasions in large aquatic ecosystems.

items.title: Conservation areas in the eastern Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt: a dynamic conceptual framework under land-use change
items.abstract: Summary The Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt is a biogeographical province, and its eastern sub-province faces intense pressures from land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). This study integrates a systematic conservation planning approach, species distribution models and LULCC projections to identify areas that facilitate the conservation of endemic biodiversity under a dynamic conceptual framework. We selected 13 species of amphibians and mammals as surrogates, obtained their geographical distributions and analysed the distributional patterns of species richness and rarity, which showed significant concentrations in volcanic mountain systems. Historical and future LULCC models indicated a continued expansion of rainfed agriculture, potentially reaching 70% of the study area by 2050, alongside a severe reduction in temperate forest. Currently, 65% of the potential habitat of endemic species and 43% of the potential habitat of geographically rare species are affected. Under pessimistic future scenarios, losses could exceed 95%. Although the priority conservation areas identified are relatively continuous core areas at present, future projections showed considerable fragmentation. We propose a possible dynamic conservation network linking permanent nodes with dynamic nodes and temporary ecological corridors according to ecological, seasonal or anthropogenic pressures. Furthermore, this approach integrates ecological, socioeconomic and governance dimensions to reconcile conservation with sustainable practices in highly transformed landscapes.

items.title: Biophilia as a temperament trait, not a universal: children’s attraction and aversion to biodiversity in the United States and Democratic Republic of Congo
items.abstract: Introduction The Biophilia Hypothesis proposes that humans have a universal attraction to the natural world, yet little is known about how this attraction emerges or varies during childhood. We tested the Biophilia Reactivity Hypothesis, which reframes biophilia as an early-emerging, individually variable, temperament-like orientation toward biodiversity. Methods We studied 295 children aged 3-13 years in two distinct settings: 124 children at the North Carolina Zoo in the United States and 171 children at Lola ya Bonobo Sanctuary in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. Children completed a biophobia measure adapted from the Revised Fear Survey Schedule and a novel image-based biophilia task assessing Backyard Biophilia, Wildlife Tolerance, and Biophilic Travel. Results Children showed substantial individual variation across biophilia and biophobia measures, with responses spanning the available scale ranges. U.S. children showed higher Wildlife Tolerance and Biophilic Travel scores than Congolese children, whereas Backyard Biophilia did not differ between groups. Patterns of animal fear also differed between samples: U.S. children reported greater fear of some insects and arthropods, whereas Congolese children reported greater fear of several predators and reptiles. Biophobia was not significantly correlated with any of the three biophilia domains in either sample, indicating that low fear does not necessarily imply greater attraction to biodiversity. Discussion These findings support a model of biophilia as an individually variable, multidimensional disposition rather than a uniform human preference. They also suggest that attraction to biodiversity and fear of animals are partly distinct psychological systems and highlight the importance of studying children’s biodiversity preferences across development in varying ecological and sociocultural contexts.

items.title: SYMBIOSIS: Integrating Biodiversity into the Future of Linear Infrastructure in Europe
items.abstract: Abstract Sustainable linear infrastructure advances the European Green Deal and TEN-T network while protecting ecosystems from land use, fragmentation, and climate impacts. The SYMBIOSIS project (Systemic Mobilisation for Joint Biodiversity and Infrastructure), funded by Europe’s Rail Joint Undertaking (ERJU), addresses the pressing need to integrate biodiversity conservation into Europe’s transport and energy system transformation. SYMBIOSIS bridges the gap between the Sustainable and Smart Mobility Strategy and the EU Biodiversity Strategy, promoting a systemic, cross-sectoral approach to embed biodiversity throughout all phases of infrastructure planning, operation, and renewal. The project supports infrastructure managers and decision-makers through harmonised environmental assessment practices, advanced monitoring tools, nature-based solutions (NbS), and guidance aligned with regulations, including the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the EU Taxonomy Regulation. As the first Coordination and Support Action (CSA) focused on rail and biodiversity, the EU-RAIL financed SYMBIOSIS project brings together 22 partners from 13 countries, with expertise in rail, road, energy, ecology, and policy. Its three core objectives are to enable mainstreaming in decision-making, provide practical tools for sustainable land management enhancing biodiversity and infrastructure resilience, and build a pan-European community to standardise biodiversity data collection and integration. This paper explores the project’s integrated approach, addressing biodiversity from data to design, monitoring to governance, and presents mid-term insights rather than validated empirical results.

items.title: Effects of pepper–mung bean intercropping on pepper productivity, nutrient accumulation, and rhizosphere microbial communities under continuous cropping
items.abstract: Continuous monocropping can impair sustainable pepper ( Capsicum annuum L.) production by disrupting soil nutrient availability, microbial communities, and biological functioning. Legume-based intercropping offers a potential strategy to alleviate these constraints, but its effects in continuously cropped pepper systems remain poorly understood. Here, a field experiment was conducted in a long-term continuously cropped pepper field to evaluate the effects of mung bean intercropping on pepper growth and yield, nutrient accumulation, rhizosphere soil properties, and microbial communities. Compared with pepper monocropping (MP), pepper–mung bean intercropping (IP) significantly increased average fruit weight and pepper yield, but did not affect plant height, stem diameter, or fruit number per plant. IP altered the accumulation and distribution of N, P, and K among pepper organs, particularly in reproductive tissues. In the rhizosphere, IP increased available N, P, and K and urease, dehydrogenase, and catalase activities, while total N, P, and K remained unchanged. Amplicon sequencing revealed significant differences in bacterial and fungal community composition between MP and IP. At the fungal genus level, Bisifusarium and Neocosmospora were enriched under MP, whereas Conocybe was enriched under IP. IP also increased the relative abundances of several bacterial taxa, particularly Vicinamibacterales , Vicinamibacteraceae , KD4-96 , and Rokubacteriales . Several IP-enriched taxa were positively correlated with rhizosphere nutrient availability, soil enzyme activities, and pepper yield-related traits. Overall, mung bean intercropping was associated with improved rhizosphere nutrient availability and enzyme activities, together with substantial restructuring of bacterial and fungal communities, and may therefore contribute to improved pepper productivity under continuous cropping.

items.title: Dactylogyridae (Monopisthocotyla) parasitizing Caenotropus labyrinthicus (Characiformes: Chilodontidae) from the Tocantins and Gurupi river basins, northern Brazil, with the proposal of Tocantinsiella n. gen. (Dactylogyridae) and four new species
items.abstract: Four new species, assigned to the proposed new genus Tocantinsiella n. gen., were described from the gills of Caenotropus labyrinthicus collected in the Tocantins and Gurupi river basins, northern Brazil: Tocantinsiella maranhensis n. sp., Tocantinsiella brassicae n. sp., Tocantinsiella vesiculosa n. sp., and Tocantinsiella flabellata n. sp. The new species are characterized mainly by the presence of a sclerotized, robust, and sinistral vaginal vestibule, as well as a copulatory ligament connecting the male copulatory organ (MCO) from the accessory piece, which represent morphological and diagnostic characteristics for the proposed new genus. Tocantinsiella n. gen. is morphologically similar to Heterothecium due to the presence of a sclerotized, sinistral vaginal vestibule, differing due to the presence of a copulatory ligament and a non-articulated MCO. Philocorydoras also shares similarities related to the morphology of the copulatory complex. However, species of this genus are recorded only in Siluriformes fishes. This study provides a significant expansion of the diversity of helminth fauna in fishes of the family Chilodontidae by describing a new genus and four new species of Monopisthocotyla in the host studied.

items.title: **Foundations of Global Ecology: A Comprehensive Analysis of the Biosphere, Ecosystems, and Ecological Interactions**
items.abstract: ### **Alternative Titles*** **Title Option 1:** The Web of Life: Hierarchical Structures and Trophic Dynamics in Ecological Systems* **Title Option 2:** From Biosphere to Niche: A Systematic Study of Ecosystem Components and Symbiotic Relationships* **Title Option 3:** Understanding the "Shelter of Life": Classifying Ecosystems and the Mechanisms of Ecological Survival ### **Subtitle****An Analytical Framework of Abiotic-Biotic Interactions, Ecosystem Classification, and the Flow of Energy from Producers to Decomposers** --- ### **Detailed Description** **Introduction and Context:**This research paper provides a foundational yet comprehensive exploration of ecological science, structured around the core principles of environmental biology. Recognizing that the study of the environment is fundamentally the study of survival, the paper systematically breaks down the complex web of life into understandable hierarchical units. It moves from the grand scale of the global biosphere down to the microscopic interactions occurring within specific ecological niches, establishing a clear vocabulary and framework for understanding how life sustains itself on Earth. **Core Themes and Structural Analysis:**The paper is structured to define the critical boundaries and components of ecological systems: 1. **The Hierarchical Framework:** The paper begins by defining the broadest concept—the **Biosphere** (the global zone of life)—and narrows down to the **Ecosystem**, a term coined by A.G. Tansley in 1935, representing the functional unit where living and non-living elements interact. It distinguishes between an organism's **Habitat** (its physical "address") and its **Ecological Niche** (its functional "profession").2. **Dual Components:** It explores the indispensable interplay between **Biotic components** (plants, animals, microbes) and **Abiotic components** (light, temperature, water, soil), demonstrating how physical environments dictate biological possibilities.3. **Classification of Ecosystems:** The analysis categorizes ecosystems into **Natural** (terrestrial forests, grasslands, deserts; and aquatic freshwater and marine systems) and **Artificial/Man-made** (agricultural fields, urban parks), highlighting the difference between self-sustaining systems and those requiring continuous human intervention.4. **Energy Flow and Trophic Levels:** A central focus of the paper is the continuous flow of energy. It delineates the roles of **Producers** (autotrophs capturing solar energy), **Consumers** (heterotrophs reliant on other organisms), and **Decomposers** (saprophytes breaking down organic matter to recycle nutrients back into the system).5. **Ecological Interactions:** The paper analyzes the complex relationships that drive community dynamics, categorizing them into **Mutualism** (where both species benefit, like nitrogen-fixing bacteria and legumes), **Commensalism** (where one benefits without affecting the other, like epiphytes on trees), and **Parasitism** (where one benefits at the expense of a host, like the *Cuscuta* plant). **Conclusion and Implications:**The paper concludes by emphasizing that these definitions are not merely academic. Human activities—such as deforestation, pollution, and urbanization—disrupt these delicate balances, compromising the entire trophic structure of the biosphere. By understanding the intricate dependencies between species (as seen in symbiotic relationships) and the vital role of decomposers in nutrient cycling, society can better appreciate biodiversity not as a collection of isolated species, but as a fragile, interconnected network. The paper argues that comprehensive environmental education, rooted in these clear ecological definitions, is the essential first step toward global conservation and sustainable development.

items.title: Macroscopic quantum coherence and entanglement in mechanical systems
items.abstract: The notion of a macroscopic quantum state must be pinned down in order to assess how well experiments probe the large-scale limits of quantum mechanics. However, the issue of quantifying so-called quantum macroscopicity is fraught with multiple approaches having varying interpretations and levels of computability and measurability. Here, we introduce two measures that capture independent macroscopic properties: i) extensive size, measuring the degree of coherence in position or momentum observables relative to atomic-scale units, and ii) entangled size, quantifying the number of entangled subsystems. These measures unify many desirable features of past proposals while having rigorously justified interpretations from quantum information theory in terms of coherence and multipartite entanglement. We demonstrate how to estimate them and obtain lower-bounds using experimental data from micro-mechanical oscillators and diffracting molecules. Notably, we find evidence for genuine multipartite entanglement of 10 5 to 10 7 atoms in recent mechanical superposition states.

items.title: Extracting intrinsic alignments in the Dark Energy Survey’s year 1 data, using the self-calibration method and LSST-DESC tools
items.abstract: Abstract We present the implementation of a Self-Calibration of Intrinsic Alignments of galaxies as an extension to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) Dark Energy Science Collaboration (DESC)’s weak lensing 3x2pt pipeline (TXPipe). As a demonstration, we have run this pipeline on the Dark Energy Survey (DES) year one data set. We find indications of a non-zero intrinsic alignment signal in the higher redshift bins, while in the lower bins our results look more uncertain. We believe this is caused by known issues with the individual galaxies photo-z estimation. This effect is particularly harmful for the self-calibration method, since it has high requirements for reliable estimation of the photo-zs, and the need for individual galaxy point estimates and tomographic binning to match. We show how different methods of recreating the redshift probability distribution can affect the detection of intrinsic alignment.

items.title: Juice/SWI during the Lunar-Earth-Gravity-Assist (LEGA) – Part 4: Antenna pointing and beam characterisation
items.abstract: Abstract. The Submillimetre Wave Instrument (SWI) onboard the Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) spacecraft consists of a 29 cm off-axis paraboloid antenna and two double-sideband heterodyne receivers operating in the frequency ranges of 530–638 and 1066–1286 GHz. This instrument is designed to study Jupiter’s atmosphere and the exospheres of the Galilean moons. We used the Lunar-Earth-Gravity-Assist (LEGA) data from August 2024 to characterise this antenna using several SWI observations pointing towards the Earth. The data analysis of the LEGA observations dedicated to the antenna beam allows us to characterise the antenna beam Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM), sidelobes, absolute pointing and receiver coalignement. Moreover, an estimate of the calibration efficiency factor has been obtained.

items.title: No Blue without Red: Evolutionary Properties of Super-Early Galaxies
items.abstract: The discovery of numerous luminous, super-early galaxies at z > 10 by JWST has revealed a striking diversity in their ultraviolet (UV) properties, ranging from extremely blue, dust-poor systems to a smaller population of significantly reddened sources. We investigate the physical origin of this diversity within the framework of the Attenuation-Free Model (AFM), in which radiation-driven outflows redistribute dust to large galactic radii, reducing the effective attenuation. Starting from a sample of 32 spectroscopically confirmed super-early galaxies, we apply the detailed AFM analysis to a subset of 17 systems with suitable size constraints and derive their key physical properties, including halo mass, star formation efficiency, metallicity, and outflow extent. We find that these systems reside in massive halos ( log M / M ⊙ ∼ 10.7 ) and exhibit moderate ( 0.01 ≲ ϵ * ≲ 0.05 ) star formation efficiencies, while frequently reaching super-Eddington conditions that trigger powerful outflows. Within the AFM framework, we propose a possible evolutionary sequence in which galaxies transition from a dust-obscured “Red Monster’’ phase to a UV-bright”Blue Monster’’ phase as outflows clear their central regions. The recently confirmed red galaxy EGS-z11-R0 at z = 11.45 is naturally interpreted as a system observed during this obscured phase. Compact ( r e ≲ 150 pc) sources are instead difficult to reconcile within AFM; we speculate that their emission is dominated by an AGN. Our results provide a coherent interpretation of super-early galaxy properties and highlight the key role of radiation-driven outflows in shaping galaxy evolution at cosmic dawn. Future observations with JWST and ALMA will be essential to test these predictions and further constrain the nature of the earliest galaxies.

items.title: Hyperonic equation of state for neutron stars: A systematic Bayesian comparison of density-dependent and nonlinear relativistic mean-field models
items.abstract: A systematic Bayesian inference study of the equation of state (EOS) of dense matter with strangeness is presented, extending five relativistic mean-field (RMF) models with both constant and density-dependent couplings to include the full baryon octet. The hyperon-nucleon couplings in the scalar channel are varied within ranges informed by hypernuclear data, while vector isoscalar couplings are fixed by the SU(6) symmetry quark model. Observational constraints from NICER (PSR J0030, J0437, J0740) and GW170817, theoretical constraints from chiral effective field theory ($χ$EFT) and perturbative QCD (pQCD), and experimental constraints from nuclear saturation properties are imposed simultaneously. We find that the inclusion of hyperons systematically reduces the maximum neutron star mass by $0.05$-$0.10,M_\odot$ across all models while increasing the radius at $1.4,M_\odot$ by $0.5$-$0.8$ km. The speed of sound exhibits a characteristic softening at densities $2$-$3,ρ_{\rm sat}$ coinciding with hyperon onset. All hyperonic models remain consistent with the $2,M_\odot$ constraint. Models with a more flexible isovector channel span a larger proton fraction when only nucleons are included. However, the extra flexibility is visibly suppressed by hyperons, meaning that the average proton distribution is independent of model flexibility when hyperons are included. Less flexible models show comparable or slightly increased proton fractions due to EOS stiffening when hyperons are included. Only a residual number of hyperonic equations of state give rise to a mass-radius curve with a negative slope at low masses. A $1.8,M_\odot$ neutron star with a radius larger than or similar to the radius of a $1.2,M_\odot$ star would provide strong evidence that the star contains baryonic degrees of freedom beyond nucleons.

items.title: axionbloch: An Open-Source Python Package for Simulating Axion-Induced Spin Dynamics
items.abstract: The interaction of ultralight bosonic dark matter with spins can be interpreted as a pseudomagnetic field acting on normal matter. Such interactions can be modeled as usual magnetic interactions using spin-evolution (Bloch) equations. axionbloch, an open-source Python package for simulating spin dynamics induced by both usual and exotic interactions, is presented. The numerical simulations serve as a tool for deriving axion signal signatures, which are crucial for designing experimental searches and data analysis. Simulations are calibrated against theoretical expectations, ensuring the accuracy of the simulated signals. axionbloch is available on GitHub, allowing researchers to simulate pseudomagnetic signals under specific configurations of axion models and experimental setups. The package is documented on Read the Docs and includes example scripts for application.

items.title: VAPOLA -- A multiyear, multiband polarization survey of AGNs and Sgr A* at millimeter wavelengths with ALMA. II. Spectropolarimetric properties and their evolution from 2017 to 2023
items.abstract: We aim to present a systematic analysis of the spectropolarimetric properties of a sample of 39 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) and Sagittarius A* observed with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array during five VLBI campaigns between 2017 and 2023. We characterized the compact cores in total intensity and polarization, focusing on the behavior of the linear-polarization (LP) fraction, electric vector position angle (EVPA), and Faraday rotation measure (RM) over time and spectral domains. We investigated both individual objects---such as M87, Sgr A*, 3C273, and 3C279---and ensemble properties of different source classes, including flat-spectrum radio quasars, BLLac objects, and other active galaxies. While total intensity and spectral index are generally stable on weekly timescales, polarization properties often exhibit strong variability, with significant day-to-day changes in LP, EVPA, and RM. Several sources display large EVPA rotations accompanied by variations in LP and RM, in some cases coinciding with flaring activity. We observe that the magnitude of RM increases with observing frequency for all sources for which we have reliable multiband measurements, consistent with Faraday rotation arising in a magnetized sheath surrounding the relativistic jet, although an origin in the accretion flow---particularly in the case of Sgr A*---cannot be ruled out.

items.title: Impact of Upstream Clumpiness on Supernova Remnant Forward Shock Evolution in Molecular Cloud Environments
items.abstract: Abstract Supernova remnants (SNRs) are widely considered to be the primary accelerators of Galactic cosmic rays. In recent years, detailed observations have significantly progressed for young SNRs interacting with molecular clouds, a prime example being RX J1713.7−3946. When molecular clouds are clumpy, their impact can affect not only radiation properties but also shock-wave propagation. Therefore, a quantitative understanding linking observational quantities with the ambient medium structure is highly required. In this study, we perform three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations to model a molecular cloud with an inhomogeneous density structure driven by supersonic turbulence and subsequent SNR formation. To investigate various presupernova environments, we systematically vary the medium clumpiness by replacing gas below a threshold number density with a low-density hot gas, quantifying the relationship between the forward shock velocity and the volume filling factor of the high-density clumps. As a result, we find that at an elapsed time of 1000 yr—a typical age for a young SNR—the forward shock can evolve consistently with the fast shock velocity measured in RX J1713.7−3946, provided that the clump volume filling factor is approximately 10% or less. Considering that hadronic gamma-ray emission originates exclusively from the clumpy, high-density gas, our findings suggest that the total energy of cosmic-ray protons in RX J1713.7−3946 is higher than previously estimated, amounting to at least a few percent of the typical supernova explosion energy.
