items.title: Metabolic sensor Gpr35 links dietary lipids to itch mediating neural circuits.
items.abstract: Impact of nutrition on systemic health is well-recognized but the specific sensors that couple western dietary lipid metabolites into the pathological triggers of chronic itch and inflammation remain elusive. Here, we identify a metabolic- to-sensory axis in which 9-keto-12,13-epoxy octadecenoic acid (EKODE), an endogenous dietary linoleic acid derivative acts as a potent ligand for the G protein-coupled receptor 35 (Gpr35) to drive chronic itch, inflammation, and heat hypersensitivity. We demonstrate that Gpr35 is selectively expresses in a distinct population of sensory neurons and genetic ablation of Gpr35 in sensory neurons attenuates EKODE and psoriasis-associated itch and inflammation. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of Gpr35 significantly attenuates itch in mouse models of psoriasis and atopic dermatitis. We show that Gpr35 signaling engages the itch-specific brain natriuretic peptide, defining a labeled-line pathway that is functionally distinct from classical nociceptive circuits. Collectively, our findings establish Gpr35 as a critical neuro-metabolic sensor in healthy and disease conditions.

items.title: Developmental pathways to aggression in mental disorders : The child and adolescent perspective of TRR 379.
items.abstract: Aggression in mental disorders is a clinically and societally highly relevant transdiagnostic phenomenon with heterogeneous developmental trajectories in childhood and adolescence: Aggressive behaviors may occur transiently and decline, but they may also stabilize across adolescence and persist into adulthood. The Collaborative Research Center Transregio 379 "Neuropsychobiology of Aggression: A Transdiagnostic Approach in Mental Disorders" investigates the biological, psychological, and social mechanisms that explain these divergent trajectories. The guiding framework is a developmental model in which aggressive biosignatures emerge from an imbalance between the developing negative valence system and cognitive control. During adolescence, reactivity to social threat, rejection, frustration, and status loss increases, while cognitive control systems continue to mature. Peers, exclusion, victimization, bullying, and puberty-related hormonal changes may shape these maturational processes. This article describes the child and adolescent developmental projects of TRR 379 and the longitudinal cohort. Understanding transdiagnostic biosignatures opens new opportunities for preventive and mechanism-based therapeutic interventions during critical windows of developmental plasticity.

items.title: Sex- and frequency-dependent acute pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic effects of smoked cannabis: a randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Cannabis use is rising among women. Studies suggest females are more sensitive to the intoxicating and misuse-related effects of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). While preclinical studies point to sex-specific development of tolerance, this has not been translated to humans. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 44 participants (22 F) smoked three cannabis strengths (0% [~0 mg] THC, 4% [~20 mg] THC, 10% [~60 mg] THC), provided blood for plasma analysis, and completed subjective mood and drug effects assessments and a self-administration task. Outcomes were analyzed by cannabis strength, sex, and use frequency ( > 4 vs. ≤4 days/week; balanced across sex). Relative to placebo, active cannabis strengths increased subjective effects and plasma THC and metabolites (ps < 0.05). Exploratory follow-up of interactions (cannabis strength*frequency p < 0.10) showed the frequent-use group exhibiting significant increases from placebo in misuse-related ratings ("Like", "Take again") and self-administering more cannabis than the occasional-use group (ps < 0.05), and this was not modified by sex. Ratings of "High", Sedation/impairment, Dysphoric arousal, and "Bad effect" were higher at active strengths for occasional-use males relative to sex- and/or frequency-matched counterparts (ps < 0.05; via exploratory follow-up for "High" and Sedation/impairment). THC and metabolites tended to be highest in frequent-use males. These findings contrast with previous evidence of greater cannabis sensitivity among females and point toward future investigation into sex-dependent exposure thresholds for tolerance development/escalation. Sex and frequency of use are both implicated in cannabis use disorder risk, and consideration of their interaction is critical in characterizing the acute effects of, and tolerance to, cannabis.

items.title: Artificial intelligence applications in microbiota-gut-brain axis research: Implications for Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Alterations in the gut microbiota (GM) are increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis through the microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA), influencing neuroinflammation, amyloid-β deposition, and tau aggregation. The inherent complexity of microbiota data necessitates artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to identify novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In this narrative review, we examined AI applications in AD-related GM research, including metataxonomic and metagenomic approaches. AI methods facilitate microbial signature identification and enterotype characterization associated with AD progression, enable multi-omics integration clarifying molecular pathways linking GM dysbiosis to neurodegeneration, support predictive modeling for early AD detection, and inform personalized MGBA-targeted interventions. Employed techniques include classical ML (e.g., random forests) for taxonomic classification, deep learning (e.g., neural networks) for complex pattern recognition, and explainable AI for identifying key bacterial taxa and metabolic functions. Significant challenges persist regarding methodological standardization, larger longitudinal cohorts, and ethical considerations in clinical applications. Future priorities include developing interpretable models, integrating longitudinal multi-omics data to establish causality, and validating AI-derived insights for precision AD prevention and treatment. AI uniquely enables high-dimensional, non-linear analyses that advance understanding of microbiome-brain interactions, though clinical translation requires rigorous validation and interdisciplinary collaboration.

items.title: Machine Learning in the Differential Diagnosis of Bipolar and Borderline Personality Disorders: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: BackgroundBipolar disorder (BD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) are associated with substantial morbidity and can be difficult to distinguish when symptoms are assessed cross-sectionally. This scoping review examines machine learning (ML) and related predictive approaches designed to differentiate the two conditions.MethodsWe searched Ovid MEDLINE, APA PsycInfo, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and selected computer science conference proceedings through July 2, 2026. Full-text peer-reviewed journal articles and conference papers were eligible when they used a data-driven computational or statistical prediction approach to distinguish, classify, or characterize BD and BPD. Of 2,594 records identified, 2,523 unique records were screened, and 24 full texts were assessed. Screening followed the Population, Concept, Context framework, Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, and preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses extension for scoping reviews.ResultsNine reports met the inclusion criteria. Seven participant-based reports contributed an aggregate of 986 report-level participants, although two reports used overlapping cohorts; one conference paper used synthetic data, and one study analyzed 149,798 Reddit posts. Studies including clinical samples reported BD versus BPD discrimination AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) values of 0.67 to 0.91 and accuracies ranging from 61.7% to 90%. These estimates were not directly comparable and were derived from small, often imbalanced samples using heterogeneous internal validation. No model was externally validated in an independent clinical cohort.ConclusionThe evidence remains preliminary and does not support clinical deployment. Reported performance is constrained by small samples, class imbalance, uncertain ground-truth labels, spectrum bias, and reliance on pre-existing diagnoses. Prospective studies in consecutive at-risk cohorts, with transparent reporting and independent external validation, are required.

items.title: Improving the Diagnostic Accuracy of Plasma Alzheimer's Disease Biomarkers With Objective and Subjective Cognitive Screening.
items.abstract: Blood-based biomarkers are increasingly used to identify Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology and may play an important role in early disease screening and participant selection for clinical trials. However, their performance across stages of cognitive impairment remains unclear. This study examined whether plasma biomarkers differ in their ability to predict amyloid pathology by performance on cognitive screening measures. Participants were older adults from the community-based Vanderbilt Memory and Aging Project (N = 154; mean age = 72 ± 6 years; 37% MCI). Plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau)231 and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) were measured using Quanterix Simoa technology. Amyloid positivity was defined by cerebrospinal fluid β-amyloid 42/40 ratio < 0.072. Objective cognitive impairment was defined as ≤ 26 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment; cognitive complaints were assessed by a single-item self-report. Logistic regression and stratified ROC analyses evaluated associations between biomarkers and amyloid status, with area under the ROC curve (AUC) values compared using DeLong's test. Forty-seven percent of participants were amyloid positive. Higher plasma p-tau231 was associated with increased odds of amyloid positivity (OR = 1.18, p < 0.001; AUC = 0.73). Discriminative accuracy was significantly higher among individuals without subjective cognitive concerns (AUC = 0.85) than among those individuals with concerns (AUC = 0.67; p = 0.02). Plasma GFAP was also associated with amyloid positivity (OR = 1.01, p < 0.001; AUC = 0.75) and showed greater accuracy among participants with objective cognitive impairment (AUC = 0.82) compared to unimpaired individuals (AUC = 0.63; p = 0.03). Plasma p-tau231 and GFAP were associated with amyloid pathology, but their diagnostic accuracy varied by cognitive screening results, highlighting the value of integrating brief cognitive assessments when interpreting blood-based biomarkers.

items.title: Circadian clock adjusted classes improve sleep, circadian health, and academic performance in medical freshmen.
items.abstract: University students often experience circadian misalignment with academic schedules, which may impair performance. This study evaluated whether a later-start schedule improves academic outcomes and circadian rhythms in first-year medical students. Incoming students ( n = 220) completed the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire; those with high social jetlag (SJL >120 min, n = 71) were randomized into either a later-start schedule (LS; classes ≥10:00 a.m., n = 30) or a standard early-start schedule (ES; 8:00 a.m., n = 41). Actigraphy data were collected from 112 students prior to examinations. Based on the objective temperature circadian phase (TCP) with a median acrophase split at 3:59 a.m. ES participants were categorized asearly (ETCP-ES, n = 41) or late (LTCP-ES, n = 41). All LS participants exhibited a TCP later than 3:59 a.m. and remained LTCP-LS group ( n = 30). Associations between scheduling, circadian metrics, and exam scores were analyzed using regression and sex-adjusted ANCOVA. TCP predicted exam scores overall (β = -0.217, p = 0.021), most evidently within ES (β = -0.291, p = 0.008). LTCP-ES students scored lower than ETCP-ES students ( p = 0.025). LTCP-LS students performed similarly to ETCP-ES students and showed greater circadian robustness, including higher rest-activity stability (p = 0.031), greater blue-light stability ( p = 0.029), and longer sleep duration ( p = 0.013).

items.title: State-Dependent Modulation of Corticospinal and Cortical Responses by Closed-Loop Paired-pulse TMS.
items.abstract: Brain oscillations shape cortical excitability in a phase-dependent manner. Cortical excitability reflects the net output of intracortical circuits, including inhibitory and facilitatory pathways. However, whether the phase of ongoing brain rhythms differentially modulates inhibitory and facilitatory responses remains unknown. Paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (ppTMS) can selectively engage these circuits, providing a unique tool to dissociate their contributions. We combined real-time EEG-guided closed-loop TMS with single- and paired-pulse TMS in 24 healthy adults (13 female) to probe how sensorimotor mu (8-13 Hz) and beta (14-30 Hz) oscillatory phase shapes responses associated with intracortical inhibitory and facilitatory processes. Single-pulse TMS (spTMS), short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI), and intracortical facilitation (ICF) were delivered at four phases (peak, falling, trough, rising). Motor evoked potentials (MEPs) and TMS-evoked potentials (TEPs) were recorded to assess corticospinal and cortical responses, respectively. We found that MEP amplitude was phase-dependent across all three stimulation types, with spTMS-evoked and ICF-conditioned MEPs showing the largest amplitudes at the rising phase, whereas SICI-conditioned MEPs were largest at the peak phase of the mu oscillation. TEP P60-N100 amplitude was modulated by oscillatory phase across all stimulation types, with maximal responses at the trough phase. SICI showed opposing phase patterns between the two measures, revealing a dissociation between cortical and corticospinal responses. MEP and TEP preferred phases were correlated across participants only in the ICF condition. These findings extend phase-dependent spTMS effects to paired-pulse stimulation and show that ongoing mu phase differentially shapes responses to SICI and ICF across cortical and corticospinal levels. Significance Statement Ongoing brain oscillations are known to shape cortical excitability across their phase cycle. However, whether this effect differentially influences inhibitory and facilitatory responses has remained unresolved. Here, using closed-loop EEG-guided transcranial magnetic stimulation in healthy adults, we probed how SICI- and ICF-conditioned responses vary across different phases of the sensorimotor mu and beta rhythms. We show that corticospinal and cortical responses to inhibitory and facilitatory paired-pulse protocols exhibit distinct phase-dependent patterns in the sensorimotor mu rhythm. These findings extend phase-dependent stimulation effects beyond single-pulse TMS and reveal that the relationship between cortical state and stimulation response differs across paired-pulse protocols.

items.title: Bivalent habenula modulation of human monoaminergic midbrain and cortical pathways.
items.abstract: The habenula is implicated in signaling negative reward prediction errors (RPE), yet direct evidence demonstrating its influence on downstream human brain circuits is limited. Using ultra-high field (7T) fMRI and dynamic causal modelling across two negative RPE-inducing experimental tasks, we characterize habenula-directed connectivity with monoaminergic midbrain and cortical pathways in healthy adults (n = 47, 24 males and 23 females; n = 43, 23 males and 20 females). Negative feedback drove habenula inhibition of ventral tegmental area and dorsal raphe nucleus activity, while positive feedback had an excitatory effect. These core effects are replicated across reversal learning and perceptual decision uncertainty tasks, establishing a generalizable mechanism for behavioral adaptation. Task-specific modulatory effects emerged in pathways between the subcortical and cortical regions (ventral tegmental area→dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, dorsal raphe nucleus→medial prefrontal cortex, and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex→habenula), revealing context-dependent cortical elaboration of negative RPE-driven habenula signals. This provides the first evidence in humans, using model-based effective connectivity, for bivalent modulation of habenula function on monoaminergic midbrain and cortical pathways, demonstrating how the brain integrates negative and positive signals to guide adaptive behavior. Significance Statement The habenula - an epithalamic brain region - plays a key role in the encoding of reward and punishment. Animal studies have demonstrated the habenula to be bivalently modulated by aversive and appetitive stimuli, resulting in the bidirectional modulation of monoaminergic brain region activity. Despite this evidence, the directional impact of bivalently modulated habenula activity on its circuitry has yet to be investigated in humans. This study leverages ultra-high field (7T) fMRI and dynamic causal modelling to reveal the impact of bivalent habenula modulation on monoaminergic midbrain and cortical regions across two distinct tasks. Through these methodologies, we demonstrate the habenula to have a key role in guiding adaptive behavior.

items.title: PTPRO restricts higher-order branching of terminal arbors through TrkB dephosphorylation.
items.abstract: The structural complexity of axon collateral terminal arbors shapes synaptic connectivity. In corticospinal projections, individual axon collaterals exhibit distinct patterns of terminal arborization, ranging from sparse local branches to dense, highly complex arbors in target regions such as the pontine nuclei. How this complexity is controlled remains poorly understood. Here, using corticopontine projections in male and female mice, we show that protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type O (PTPRO) selectively restricts higher-order branching of terminal arbors in the pontine nuclei without affecting collateral number. This function requires the intracellular phosphatase domain of PTPRO but not its extracellular region. We demonstrate that PTPRO dephosphorylates tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), and that the excessive terminal arborization caused by acute PTPRO loss is rescued by TrkB depletion or phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) inhibition. Together, these findings reveal that PTPRO-mediated TrkB dephosphorylation acts as a molecular brake on corticopontine terminal arbor elaboration. Significance Statement How individual axons regulate terminal branching within target regions is a fundamental question in neural circuit development. This study identifies protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type O (PTPRO), a receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatase that negatively regulates signaling through tyrosine phosphorylation, as a selective regulator of higher-order branching in corticopontine terminal arbors. PTPRO dephosphorylates tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), a neurotrophin receptor tyrosine kinase that promotes neuronal growth and branching, thereby restricting terminal arbor complexity without affecting collateral number from the main axon. Given that terminal arbor architecture determines the synaptic territory of each cortical input, PTPRO-dependent constraint on arbor elaboration may represent a general principle by which projection-specific arbor complexity is established across long-range circuits in the central nervous system.

items.title: Hexagonal modulation of theta rhythmic attentional sampling of visual space.
items.abstract: Spatial attention improves visual perception by selecting behaviorally relevant sensory signals. Traditionally, attention has been conceptualized as a static spotlight, while recent evidence posited that attention operates as a moving spotlight that samples visual space sequentially in discrete snapshots that are clocked by theta rhythms (∼3-8 Hz). While theta rhythmic attentional sampling has mainly been observed in fronto-parietal and occipital areas, theta oscillations also hallmark entorhinal-hippocampal grid-cell networks, which encode physical space in hexagonal patterns that guide overt exploration and navigation. We hypothesized that visual attention might rely on the same underlying principles and sample visual space in a hexagonal, grid-like configuration. To test this hypothesis, twenty participants (10 females and 10 males) performed a cue-guided attention task that probed behavioral performance as a function of space and time. Reaction times were assessed as a function of spatial location and varying cue-target intervals, which displayed spatially-structured theta rhythms. Specifically, higher theta power occurred at spatial locations that were aligned to multiples of 60°, consistent with an underlying hexagonal organization. Participants that exhibited stronger hexagonal sampling relied less on the spatial cue to guide their attentional allocation. In sum, these findings suggest that covert visual attention is organized in a hexagonal pattern that might be consistent with the grid-like structure known from the entorhinal-hippocampal system and highlight that theta rhythms could reflect a common organizing principle for spatial cognition. Significance Statement Attention prioritizes sensory inputs to optimize behavior. But how does attention sample the environment in space and time? Here, we demonstrate that attentional sampling of visual space is not uniform, but might preferentially explore locations that are oriented along a hexagonal pattern, reminiscent of the spatial configuration of entorhinal-hippocampal grid cells. Moreover, covert attentional sampling exhibited oscillatory theta signatures (3-8 Hz). In sum, these findings suggest that spatial attention and navigation may share a common organizing principle, and indicate that theta rhythms may orchestrate sampling behaviors in space and time as a unifying principle underlying spatial cognition.

items.title: Area MT carries acceleration information in a quickly and directly decodable representation.
items.abstract: We sought to better understand the neural representation of visual motion acceleration. A straightforward estimation of acceleration would involve calculating the rate of change of velocity, which itself would be calculated from change in position over time. As it is well-established that neurons in area MT encode velocity, the brain could thus indirectly estimate acceleration by calculating the change in MT's velocity representations. An alternative mechanism, however, could operate more rapidly and directly. In this case, the brain could exploit interactions between MT's standard motion encoding and idiosyncratic temporal dynamics of neural responses. Such direct decoding would thus exploit nonlinearities usually ignored in studies of MT coding. We tested between these two theories by measuring from ensembles of MT neurons while two male awake fixating macaques viewed linearly accelerating motion stimuli. Direct decoding of acceleration from MT was possible on faster time scales, and could be done with higher fidelity, than indirect decoding. Distinct motion acceleration information could thus be efficiently read out from rich and heterogeneous MT ensemble responses, regardless of the mechanisms that give rise to various forms of motion tuning that it exhibits. A similar analysis of activity in the medial superior temporal area (MST) did not suggest that this later stage of motion processing has a more refined acceleration representation. Together, these results suggest that the brain may opportunistically exploit nonlinear idiosyncrasies of neural responses to efficiently extract behaviorally relevant information on fast time scales, instead of performing explicit calculation of certain variables. Significance Statement This study aims to understand if linear acceleration information of visual motion is extracted and represented in primate visual motion areas MT and MST. By combining large-scale multi-area neuronal recordings, population-level analyses, and a rich set of moving stimuli, we show that linear acceleration can be decoded from MT activity. Specifically, our results demonstrate that (1) motion acceleration is encoded in MT, and can be directly and quickly decoded from MT ensemble activity, and (2) area MST, despite being a later stage of motion processing, does not refine acceleration representations. These findings call for revisiting how brain areas might efficiently extract behaviorally relevant information from the environment and highlight the importance of temporal dynamics in visual motion processing.

items.title: Perception of tones versus tone streams under random multi-tone masking and its representation in auditory cortex.
items.abstract: When repeated tones are presented among random masker tones, their perceptual organization is often variable. In some trials, they cannot be segregated from the masker tones. In other trials, often with a delay, they form coherent streams, segregated from the masker tones. A strong awareness-related negativity is evoked by each segregated tone of the stream in auditory cortex. A similar negative-going response has been observed when subtle, isolated tones are detected versus missed, raising the question of whether target tones that do not form a stream under informational masking are still perceived or not. Here a paradigm is introduced to probe this question while activity in auditory cortex was recorded with magnetoencephalography. Human listeners (13 female, 8 male) were instructed to indicate when they detected an isochronous stream of tones under multi-tone masking while listening to the stimulus. Thereafter, they indicated if a cue tone, presented subsequently to each trial, was comprised in the target and masker combination. Results confirmed that target tones could still be perceived in the subset of trials where they did not form a coherent stream, but the detectability in the cued frequency report was higher for tones forming a stream. A prominent awareness-related negativity was only observed when the tones formed a stream, suggesting that this response reflects the perceptual organization of the tones into streams and beyond the pure perception of the tones themselves. We speculate that the perceptual organization into a stream further enhances the detectability of the tones comprised in the stream. Significance Statement Tone sequences may form streams that segregate from competing aspects of the auditory scene, a phenomenon considered comparable to visual object grouping. In multi-tone masking, hearing out streams of repeated tones seemingly enhances tone detectability by a degree that makes it difficult to judge whether these tones could at all be perceived if they had not formed a coherent stream. We present a paradigm that allows for probing both, the perception of target-tone frequency and the formation of coherent streams in the same trials. Applying this setup in magnetoencephalography showed that the perceptual organization into a stream is more strongly represented in auditory cortex than the ability to correctly detect a tone frequency within a random tone masker.

items.title: Macaque Area LIP Reflects Confidence-Dependent Changes in Decision Policy.
items.abstract: The process of forming a decision gives rise to an estimate of its quality or likelihood of success. This graded sense of confidence is important for guiding subsequent decisions, but a neural mechanism linking subjective confidence to formation of the next decision has not been identified. We trained two male rhesus macaques to report a perceptual choice and simultaneous confidence judgment in a reaction-time (RT) motion discrimination task. Monkeys were more likely to repeat a rewarded choice when they reported low confidence on the previous trial, and showed greater changes in RT after a surprising outcome (low-confidence correct or high-confidence error). Neural activity in the lateral intraparietal area (LIP) encoded the previous trial's choice and confidence more strongly after a low-confidence correct trial, and the strength of history encoding was correlated with a trial-by-trial estimate of choice bias. Ramping dynamics of the decoded decision variable also depended systematically on the conjunction of confidence and reward on the previous trial, in a manner that reflected individual differences between animals. The findings suggest that LIP not only reflects the formation of the current decision but could participate in confidence-guided learning via adjustments of the subsequent decision process. Significance statement Decision confidence is of primary interest in the study of metacognition, yet it also plays a key role in learning, serving as a graded prediction of accuracy that modulates the response to feedback. Reanalyzing data from nonhuman primates performing a reaction-time (RT) motion discrimination task with explicit confidence reports, we found that adjustments of choice bias and RT were gated by the animal's self-reported confidence on the previous trial. The interaction of confidence and outcome (reward or punishment) was reflected in the activity of parietal (LIP) neurons on the subsequent trial, in ways largely consistent with the behavioral effects. The results and accompanying computational model suggest plausible functional links between the neuronal substrates of perceptual decision making and reinforcement learning.

items.title: State and Local Policymakers' Engagement with Neuroscience to Improve Health Policy in the United States.
items.abstract: Neuroscience is useful for making progress on public health challenges such as mental health, aging, violence, and addiction. State and local policymakers have substantial authority over these issues but do not always have access to the research and counsel they want. To inform initiatives that could bridge the gap, high-quality information on policymakers' existing and desired engagement is needed. We conducted four nationally representative surveys of local elected policymakers, local public sector staff, state legislators, and state public sector staff to gather this information. Across the four samples, 13.8-28.6% reported recently interacting with a neuroscientist, while 50.3-73.6% reported unmet desire to do so. Prior exposure to disseminated neuroscience information varied, from 19.1 to 68.0% across the samples. Unmet desire for neuroscience-related policy briefs (50.5-76.8%) and news articles (52.7-68.9%) were among the most common for all policymakers. Unmet desire crossed party lines, though with some partisan differences. These findings suggest several avenues to increase evidence-informed health policymaking.

items.title: Dopamine release in the medullary reticular formation is related to locomotor velocity.
items.abstract: Dopamine is classically recognized for modulating locomotion through basal ganglia circuits. However, it also modulates motor circuits in the brainstem and spinal cord. The medullary reticular formation (MRF) integrates supraspinal motor commands and relays them to the spinal cord, yet the role of dopamine in this region is poorly understood. Using the genetically encoded dopamine sensor dLight1.4, we observed that dopamine release in the MRF decreased during the initiation of locomotion and showed an inverse correlation with locomotor velocity. Dopamine release was also modulated during directional head turns. RNA in situ hybridization revealed D 2 R mRNA expression is present in about one-third of glutamatergic reticulospinal neurons (RSNs), whereas D 4 R mRNA expression is nearly absent. Retrograde viral tracing identified the A11 region, encompassing dopaminergic TH + cells, as the primary source of dopaminergic input to the MRF, with minimal contributions from other dopaminergic nuclei. Anterograde tracing demonstrated that A11 neurons project ipsilaterally throughout the rostrocaudal MRF and form putative synaptic contacts with neuronal populations that project to the spinal cord. These findings reveal discrete dopaminergic projections from the A11 region to the MRF and lead to the hypothesis that the A11-MRF dopaminergic pathway acts as a gain-control mechanism setting the excitability of D 2 receptor-expressing reticulospinal neurons, thereby providing state-dependent control of locomotor speed. Significance Statement The medullary reticular formation (MRF) is a critical hub for controlling diverse motor behaviors; however, the source and organization of its dopaminergic inputs remain unclear. Here we identify A11 dopamine neurons as the principal dopaminergic projection to the MRF. Dopamine signaling in the MRF correlates inversely with locomotor velocity and is modulated during ipsilateral head turns. Furthermore, the expression of D 2 Rs on glutamatergic reticulospinal neurons identifies these cells as primary targets for dopaminergic modulation.

items.title: KinomeX: A Source-Linked, Evidence-Traceable Atlas of the Human Kinome.
items.abstract: Protein kinase data originate from sources with different identifiers, definitions, and evidence models. KinomeX (https://kinomex.dokhlab.org) is an online platform that aligns the human protein kinase list from KinHub with reviewed entries from UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot and links each record to source-specific evidence. The catalog includes 678 protein entries: 522 KinHub core entries with 536 kinase-domain rows, and 156 reviewed UniProt entries labeled with the Kinase keyword (KW-0418), mostly phosphorylating lipids, nucleotides, sugars, or small molecules. Kinase profiles integrate reviewed annotations, 10,043 experimental structures, AlphaFold models, 1,021,421 ligand bioactivity records, 36,396 tissue-expression data from GTEx, 63,649 ClinVar variants, and live STRING connections. Missing records are marked as unavailable. We developed the Pharmaceutical Development Interest Score (PDIS), which combines citation, clinical-trial, structural, and chemical data with adjustable component weights. These rankings are consistent across numerous weightings (median Spearman ρ = 0.955) and better reflect Pharos target development levels than citation counts alone. Examples highlight 93 under-cited but structurally and chemically accessible kinases and 47 CNS-specific kinases, with evidence on structure, chemistry, and variants. KinomeX enables evidence review and hypothesis formation, using PDIS to indicate documented development efforts rather than biological significance.

items.title: Pde4b deficiency in female mice leads to enhanced extinction learning and blunted stress reactivity.
items.abstract: Fear extinction is a critical adaptive process that is disrupted in stress-induced disorders. Phosphodiesterase-4B (PDE4B), a regulator of intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling, has been implicated in fear learning and stress responsivity in males; however, its role in females remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the behavioural and physiological consequences of Pde4b knockout in adult female mice using a novel genetic model targeting the catalytic domain shared by multiple PDE4B isoforms. Pde4b knockout did not alter baseline innate (i.e., unconditioned) avoidance-like behaviour to a novel environment in the open field or elevated plus maze, nor did it affect fear acquisition. In contrast, Pde4b knockout significantly facilitated fear extinction learning and extinction recall. In addition, Pde4b knockout blunted corticosterone responses to acute restraint stress and was associated with reduced thymus weight, indicating altered stress responsivity. Estrous cycle stage did not significantly influence extinction behaviour. Together, these findings identify Pde4b as a regulator of fear recovery or extinction as well as stress physiology in female mice. Our results broadly extend prior work in males while suggesting sex-specific considerations in Pde4b function, underscoring the importance of examining females in preclinical models of stress-related psychopathology. These data support further investigation of Pde4b targeted strategies for disorders characterized by impaired fear extinction such as PTSD.

items.title: Altered stability of dynamic functional architecture in the co-occurrence of autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
items.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) frequently co-occur, whereas the underlying neurobiological mechanisms remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to identify alterations in dynamic functional architecture across ASD, ADHD, and their comorbidity. This study selected 287 participants from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange and ADHD-200 datasets, divided into ASD without ADHD (ASD-only), ADHD without ASD (ADHD-only), ASD + ADHD, and typically developing (TD) groups. In this study, we employed dynamic functional stability at the voxel level by measuring the temporal concordance of dynamic functional connectivity (DFC). Furthermore, whole-brain DFC analyses were conducted using clusters with significant stability alterations as seed regions. Group comparisons and correlation analyses were subsequently performed. Our results showed significant group differences in functional stability in the left superior frontal gyrus, orbital part (ORBsup), right pallidum, and left amygdala. Seed-based analyses identified altered DFC variability between the left amygdala and three regions, including the right middle temporal gyrus (MTG), the left insula, and the left superior occipital gyrus (SOG). Notably, DFC variability between the left amygdala and right MTG was significantly negatively correlated with Social Communication Questionnaire (SCQ) scores in the comorbidity group (r = - 0.620, p < 0.01, FDR corrected). From a dynamic perspective, our findings revealed that ASD, ADHD, and their comorbidity exhibited commonanduniquechanges in brain function, thereby enhancing our understanding of the pathogenesis underlying ASD + ADHD.

items.title: Improved motor learning in adenosine A1 receptor knockout mice.
items.abstract: Adenosine is a widespread neuromodulator, acting at A1 and A2A receptors in the brain. Adenosine plays role in a multitude of functions including sleep, homeostasis, neuroprotection and synaptic plasticity. Deletion of A1Rs in knock-out mice (A1R KO) revealed non-uniform effects on learning: learning sequential visual discrimination tasks was impaired, while spatial learning (Morris maze) and working memory tasks were not. Motor learning was also preserved in A1R KO mice. However, a systematic comparison of motor learning in KO and wild type (WT) mice has not been performed. Here we fill this knowledge gap by comparing motor learning in WT and A1R KO mice using an accelerating rotarod task. Both genotypes acquired motor skill and retained it after 1 week without further training. Genotype and Age had significant effects on improvement of motor skills relative to initial performance. A1R KO mice showed higher rate of learning than WT across training days, and reached better performance by the end of training (Day 5). However, retention after 1 week was better in WT mice, which improved relative to last day of training, while KO animals performed at the same level. We saw no differences between females and males, but older animals showed greater gains during learning and better retention. Finally, individual variability of motor learning was not related to measures of baseline motor activity, or anxiety. These results add new pieces to a multifaceted and intriguing picture of shifts in the brain functions resulting from A1R loss and warrant further exploration.

items.title: Transcranial alternating current stimulation as psychiatric intervention: A meta-analytic primer.
items.abstract: Background Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is an emerging neuromodulation approach targeting neural oscillations. Although mechanistic studies support its neurophysiological effects, clinical evidence across psychiatric symptoms remains limited. This transdiagnostic meta-analysis provides a quantitative assessment of tACS effects across psychiatric symptom domains and identifies areas of clinical promise. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized sham-controlled trials assessing tACS in adults with psychiatric conditions was conducted. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched until August 2026. Standardized mean differences (Hedges' g) were calculated using random-effects models, with exploratory analyses investigating clinical and methodological moderators. Results Eighteen studies (19 datasets; 1045 participants) were included. Compared with sham stimulation, tACS showed a moderate overall effect (SMD = -0.41, 95% CI [-0.60, -0.2], I 2 = 72%). The strongest significant findings were observed for depressive symptoms (n = 10; SMD = -0.44, 95% CI -0.76 to -0.01) and anxiety symptoms (n = 4; SMD = -0.64, 95% CI -1.12 to -0.17, I 2 = 62%). Significant improvements were also observed for obsessive-compulsive symptoms, inattention, and post-traumatic stress symptoms, although based on limited evidence. Exploratory analyses identified preliminary patterns across stimulation frequencies and symptom domains, including significant effects of gamma-frequency stimulation on depressive symptoms. Conclusion This transdiagnostic meta-analysis identifies early therapeutic signals of tACS across psychiatric symptoms, with the most consistent evidence observed for depressive symptoms. Frequency-specific effects may influence clinical outcomes and warrant further investigation to optimize stimulation parameters.

items.title: Effort-based decision-making:A value-based dissection and arousal-focused synthesis.
items.abstract: Work often leads to better outcomes in terms of health, nutrition, and reproductive success, suggesting that work execution should be favored by natural selection. However, work also involves expending energy and time, costs that biological systems aim to limit. Indeed, work is often accompanied by the subjectively aversive experience of effort, which motivates work avoidance. Accordingly, decision-makers need to trade off the expected benefits of the goal their work aims to achieve with the anticipated effort costs before engaging in any action. While such trade-offs are relatively well-characterized, effort-based decision-making involve several other essential components, including the representation of anticipated effort and its comparison with experienced effort, which allows learning. These components and their relation to arousal received considerably less attention. To thoroughly dissect effort-based decision-making, we here synthesize the framework of value-based decision-making and expand it with work preparation, execution and recovery subprocesses. This systematizes existing research, highlights the specificities of effort-based decision-making, and identifies understudied components. Moreover, we use this framework to analyze (neuro)physiological commonalities and differences between motor and cognitive effort. Finally, we propose a novel, arousal-based model of effort suggesting that required increases in arousal give rise to effort and serve as a common currency that effort indexes and effort-based decisions aim to minimize.

items.title: Norepinephrine neurons in the nucleus of the solitary tract mediate allodynia related to systemic inflammation in mice.
items.abstract: In response to peripheral inflammation, such as the intraperitoneal administration of lipopolysaccharide (LPS), inflammatory cytokines recruit afferent neurons that communicate the inflammation to the brain and, in addition, cytokines are released to the bloodstream and reach circumventricular organs in the brain, such as the area postrema (AP). The nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS) perceives peripheral inflammatory stimuli both directly from afferent peripheral nerves and indirectly through its bidirectional connection to the AP. Norepinephrine (NE) neurons within the NTS are known to mediate behavioral and physiological responses to stress, especially stress related to inflammatory challenges in the periphery. However, the limitations of traditional pain assays limit the understanding of the influence of NTS NE neurons on pain. Here, we used the Blackbox, a machine-learning assisted behavioral analysis apparatus that was developed specifically for the study of pain in rodents. First, we determined the Blackbox variables that correlate to allodynia in mice submitted to intraperitoneal injection of LPS. IP injection of LPS caused several changes to behavior and posture. Most notably, the distance travelled, hind paw toe spread and hind paw distance significantly decreased in response to LPS and strongly correlated with decreased von Frey mechanosensitivity threshold. Selective chemogenetic activation of NTS NE neurons caused similar pain-related behaviors, while inhibition of NTS NE neurons partially reversed the impact of LPS on pain-related behaviors. Taken together, these data show that the NE neurons within the NTS mediate allodynia in response to peripheral inflammation, contributing to the nociception aspect of sickness behaviors.

items.title: Challenges in Infection Prevention and Control in Paramedicine: A Modified Nominal Group Technique Consensus Study.
items.abstract: Background Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are a major patient safety concern, yet infection prevention and control (IPC) in emergency ambulance services is challenging due to unpredictable environments, operational pressures, and equipment limitations. Evidence is limited regarding how ambulance fleet and equipment design influence IPC compliance. This study aimed to identify expert priorities for improving the availability and utility of IPC equipment and consumables in paramedicine. Methods A modified Nominal Group Technique was conducted with experts in infection prevention, paramedicine, clinical governance, education, and operations. Participants collectively generated ideas concerned with IPC in emergency ambulance services and subsequently ranked these through an anonymous survey to determine priority areas. Results Ten experts participated. Human factors were ranked as the most influential determinant of IPC compliance, followed by education and training, physical environment, equipment and consumables, and contaminated equipment management. Key barriers included organizational culture, compliance fatigue, inconsistent education, uncontrolled environments, and fleet design limitations. Conclusion IPC compliance in ambulance services is primarily shaped by behavioral, organizational, and environmental factors rather than equipment provision alone. Systems-based, co-designed interventions addressing human factors, education, organizational support, and equipment design are essential to improve IPC adherence and enhance patient and clinician safety.

items.title: Muscle-specific reticulospinal contributions to limb-trunk coordination during standing arm curls in strength-trained and untrained individuals.
items.abstract: Limb-trunk coordination plays an essential role in daily actions. The reticulospinal contribution in limb muscles has been suggested to be modulated by long-term motor experience, such as strength training. However, it remains unclear whether reticulospinal contributions in limb-trunk coordinated movements are modulated by strength training. This study aimed to determine whether reticulospinal contributions to limb-trunk coordination differ between strength-trained and untrained individuals. Fifteen long-term (≥3 yrs) strength-trained and 15 untrained healthy men participated in this study. Participants performed a rapid bilateral arm-curl task while standing, using a load corresponding to 35% of their one-repetition maximum, in response to visual, visual-auditory (80 dB), or visual-startling (115 dB) stimuli. Electromyography (EMG) was recorded from the right biceps brachii (BB) and erector spinae (ES) muscles during the task. In the visual-alone condition, ES activation occurred closer in time to BB onset in the trained group than in the untrained group, indicating tighter temporal coordination between the limb prime mover and trunk postural muscles in strength-trained individuals. In both groups, visual-startling stimuli shortened the EMG onset of both the BB and ES, suggesting reticulospinal contributions to both muscles. Notably, the relative reduction in EMG onset of the BB induced by the startling stimulus was smaller in the trained group than in the untrained group, whereas no difference between groups was observed for the ES. These findings suggest that strength training may modify limb-trunk muscle coordination during standing arm curls and may be associated with muscle-specific adaptations in reticulospinal contributions.

items.title: Acute peripheral nerve injury induces coordinated VNUT upregulation in primary sensory neurons and satellite glial cells in sensory ganglia.
items.abstract: The vesicular nucleotide transporter (VNUT) plays a key role in ATP-mediated intercellular signaling by regulating ATP release into the extracellular space. In the central nervous system, VNUT is involved in communication between neurons and glial cells; however, its distribution in sensory ganglia of the peripheral nervous system remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate VNUT immunoreactivity in sensory ganglia following acute peripheral nerve injury. After tooth extraction-induced acute nerve injury, ATF3-positive primary sensory neurons, a marker of neuronal damage, were observed in sensory ganglia. VNUT immunoreactivity in ATF3-positive primary sensory neurons and adjacent satellite glial cells was markedly increased in a coordinated manner at days 1, 5, and 7 after tooth extraction. In addition, P2X 3 , P2X 4 , and P2X 7 receptor immunoreactivity was detected in primary sensory neurons, satellite glial cells, and macrophages. These findings suggest that VNUT-associated ATP signaling may contribute to communication among primary sensory neurons, satellite glial cells, and macrophages in sensory ganglia following nerve injury.

items.title: Using stakeholder-weighted outcomes in depression trials.
items.abstract: Mental health randomised controlled trials (RCTs) base treatment benefit on a sole primary outcome, that is typically symptom-based in depression trials. However, research with stakeholders, including service-users and clinicians, often reports that although symptoms are important, but other domains such as quality-of-life, social, and occupational functioning are also prioritised. This evidence is not influencing current RCT practice, with sole primary outcomes remaining the norm. This short communication discusses how Multi-criteria Decision Modelling (MCDM) could offer a solution to this mismatch of expectations, by using stakeholder priorities for outcomes collected in RCTs and combining them with outcome data to produce stakeholder-weighted composites. These can be substituted for the primary outcome, to provide a complementary view of benefit from a broader, stakeholder-weighted multidomain lens. This could reveal nuances in treatment benefit and an understanding of treatment alignment with stakeholder expectations.

items.title: A sex-specific platelet switch controls anti-tumor immunity in glioblastoma.
items.abstract: Sex differences in glioblastoma (GBM) outcomes are shaped by biological, hormonal, and immune factors, but the mechanisms driving these disparities remain unclear. We identify platelet protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) signaling as a regulator of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity. GBM patients exhibit increased platelet reactivity driven by PAR4. In murine models, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PAR4 prolongs survival in females, but not males, and is estrogen dependent, persisting in hormonal females regardless of chromosomal sex. The survival advantage is mediated within the tumor microenvironment through enhanced CD8 + T cell infiltration and function. PAR4-activated platelets suppress CD8 + T cell activity, whereas CD8 + T cell depletion abolishes both tumor-induced platelet reactivity and the PAR4-dependent survival advantage. Mechanistically, PAR4 inhibition enhances CD8 + T cell signaling through interaction with estrogen receptor β (ERβ). These findings demonstrate that platelets are critical regulators of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity and identify PAR4 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer.

items.title: Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA and inflammation in Charcot-Marie-Tooth 1A and Charcot-Marie-Tooth 2A.
items.abstract: Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) is released from cells during such processes as mitophagy and apoptosis and can act as an endogenous damage-associated molecular pattern that activates innate immune responses. We investigated levels of circulating cell-free DNA (ccf-DNA), including ccf-mtDNA and circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (ccf-nDNA), and serum interleukin-1β (IL-1β) in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease, specifically with CMT1A and CMT2A. This study enrolled 51 patients with CMT disease (42 with CMT1A and 9 with CMT2A, 31 males and 20 females) and 13 healthy controls (6 males and 7 females). The numbers of copies of serum ccf-mtDNA and ccf-nDNA, were quantified using ND1 and ACTB, respectively, before being measured via quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Serum IL-1β levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The number of ccf-DNA copies, ND1/ACTB ratio, and IL-1β levels were compared between the three groups. And the correlation analysis was performed. Serum ND1 levels were higher in patients with CMT1A (p < 0.01) and CMT2A (p < 0.001) than in healthy controls, so was the ND1/ACTB ratio in the CMT1A (p < 0.001) and CMT2A (p < 0.05) groups. Serum IL-1β levels were higher in patients with CMT1A (p < 0.01) and CMT2A (p < 0.001) than in healthy controls. The ND1/ACTB ratio was positively related to the number of onion bulbs in CMT2A. No significant differences in serum ACTB, ND1, ND1/ACTB, or IL-1β levels were observed between the CMT1A and CMT2A groups. Patients with CMT1A and CMT2A had higher levels of serum ccf-mtDNA and IL-1β than in healthy controls. These findings suggest association between increased circulating mitochondrial DNA and inflammation in CMT disease. However, no subtype-specific differences were identified between CMT1A and CMT2A.

items.title: The emergence of language-specific biases in visual attention in pre-reading toddlers from two cultures.
items.abstract: Skilled adult readers show biases in their visual attention that reflect the direction of their native writing systems (e.g., English readers scan left-to-right while Hebrew readers scan right-to-left), but it not yet clear when these biases develop. We tested the hypothesis that language-specific patterns of behavior precede the ability to read by testing how toddlers (2.5-4 years) exposed to different writing systems allocated their attention in a picture naming task. Across two communities, children tended to name objects in the direction that matched their native language. Hebrew-learning toddlers labeled objects from right-to-left, while English- and Spanish-learning toddlers showed the reverse pattern, and language-specific tendencies strengthened with age. These results demonstrate that children have begun to discover directional regularities associated with their language even before they receive literacy instruction and illustrate how cultural conventions exert a direct influence on children's attention from a very young age.

items.title: Factor analysing predictive processing: No evidence for a general factor across tasks.
items.abstract: Background & hypothesis Dysfunctional predictive processing (PP), specifically the aberrant weighting of priors, is a frequently-proposed mechanism for psychosis and schizotypy. Evidence mostly originates from single-task studies, which assume that all tasks measure a single latent construct of PP performance, but the underlying factor structure of PP tasks is unknown. PP deficits in psychosis may be better described by a two-factor, hierarchical model: weakened lower-level (perceptual) priors compensated by higher-level (cognitive) priors. Study design We implemented a multi-paradigm approach in a preliminary sample of healthy participants (N = 73) to investigate latent constructs underlying PP and their relationship to schizotypy. Participants completed 6 tasks measuring reliance on priors across language, memory, visual, and auditory domains. A factor analysis investigated whether performance across tasks is captured by a single or two-factor model. Study results Although a two-factor model best described performance, factors reflected within-task correlations rather than a PP hierarchy. Cross-task PP measures were poorly correlated, potentially due to unreliable outcomes and the task-specific weighting of priors. A full model including all task outcomes (not factors) only significantly predicted the severity of schizotypal aberrant beliefs. Conclusions These results do not indicate a single or two-factor hierarchical model of PP. It may be inappropriate to use results from single tasks to propose a generalised PP deficit in schizotypy/psychosis. Further multi-paradigm research with larger samples and different tasks is required to confirm these findings and evaluate alternative models that may describe PP. Future directions for creating standardised paradigms with reliable outcomes are discussed.

items.title: Serum neurofilament light chain and the 2024 McDonald criteria for multiple sclerosis: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: The 2024 McDonald criteria broaden the definition of multiple sclerosis (MS), enabling diagnosis in individuals with asymptomatic MRI findings or clinical presentations not meeting the 2017 criteria. We assessed whether these criteria identify such cases using independent laboratory/imaging biomarkers and whether these biomarkers predict subsequent disease activity. Participants with asymptomatic MRI findings or clinical presentations not meeting the 2017 criteria were included and stratified according to the 2024 criteria. Serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) and 3T brain MRI measures-including normalised brain volumes, T2 lesion load (T2LL), cortical lesion (CL) and paramagnetic rim lesion (PRL)-were compared between McDonald2024-positive and McDonald2024-negative groups, and with age/sex matched McDonald2017-positive cases according to the 2017 criteria; predictors of disease activity were assessed using penalised-Cox regression. A total of 141 participants were included: 95 not meeting the 2017 criteria (n = 64 asymptomatic MRI findings; n = 31 clinical presentations), stratified as McDonald2024-positive (n = 46) or McDonald2024-negative (n = 49), and 46 McDonald2017-positive cases. McDonald2024-positive vs. McDonald2024-negative cases showed higher age-corrected sNfL Z-scores (median 0.28[IQR 0.76] vs. -0.12[0.82], p = 0.003/pFDR = 0.006), reduced normalised thalamic volume (mean 0.009±[SD]0.0007 vs. 0.010 ± 0.0007, p = 0.003/pFDR = 0.006), and higher CL (1[4] vs. 0[0], p < 0.001/pFDR < 0.001) and PRL (1[1] vs. 0[0], p < 0.001/pFDR = 0.003) counts (differences remaining significant after age/sex, disease duration and T2LL adjustments). Biomarker profiles were comparable between McDonald2024-positive and McDonald2017-positive cases. Penalised-Cox regression (n = 52) identified sNfL Z-score and PRL presence as the most consistently selected predictors of disease activity, with higher bootstrap stability for sNfL (0.84) than PRL (0.76), and good model discrimination (C-index = 0.71). The 2024 McDonald criteria identify individuals not meeting the 2017 criteria who already exhibit MS-like neuroinflammatory/neurodegenerative pathological changes. These are reflected by laboratory and imaging biomarkers, including sNfL, which may predict subsequent disease activity and complement current diagnostic frameworks to support early clinical decision-making. items.title: How much neuroscience does a neuroscientist need to know?
items.abstract: How much of the brain's learned algorithms depend on the fact it is a brain? We argue: a lot, but surprisingly few details matter. We point to simple biological details-e.g. nonnegative firing and energetic/space budgets in connectionist architectures-which, when mixed with the requirements of solving a task, produce models that predict brain responses down to single-neuron tuning. We understand this as details constraining the set of plausible algorithms and their implementations, such that only 'brain-like' algorithms are learned. In particular, each biological detail breaks a symmetry in connectionist models (scale, rotation and permutation) leading to interpretable single-neuron responses that are meaningfully characteristic of particular algorithms. This view helps us not only understand the brain's choice of algorithm but also infer algorithm from measured neural responses. Further, this perspective aligns computational neuroscience with mechanistic interpretability in artificial intelligence (AI), suggesting a more unified approach to studying the mechanisms of intelligence, both natural and artificial.

items.title: Bipolar intracortical microstimulation expands the repertoire of neuronal activation patterns.
items.abstract: Objective Intracortical microstimulation is a promising approach for sensory restoration, but its spatial selectivity and variability of human perception are constrained by current spread and electrode configuration. We investigated how varying the return-electrode position during intracortical bipolar stimulation influences the spatial distribution and composition of activated neuronal populations. Approach: We combined two-photon calcium imaging in acute mouse cortical slices with biophysically grounded computational modeling to characterize neuronal activation at the cellular and population level. We applied bipolar stimulation across a range of electrode configurations, systematically varying current direction, electrode spacing, and stimulation parameters. Main results: Bipolar stimulation activated distinct neuronal populations depending on electrode configuration, with activation patterns becoming less overlapping as the angular difference between stimulation directions increased. Population-level analyses revealed a small number of dominant activation patterns across stimulation configurations. Electrode spacing influenced both the number of activated neurons and the spatial extent of activation, whereas polarity and waveform asymmetry had comparatively modest effects. Computational modeling indicated that bipolar activation predominantly reflected the combined effect of the two corresponding monopolar stimulations, with an additional bipolar-specific component. Neurons activated exclusively by bipolar stimulation were relatively sparse and spatially dispersed. Significance: Our findings demonstrate that varying bipolar electrode configurations produces distinct patterns of neuronal activation, providing an additional mode for recruiting different neural populations. Computational modeling suggests that these patterns largely reflect the combined contributions of the individual electrodes, with additional differences which may reflect non-linear neuronal or network interactions. Together, these findings provide insight into how the electrode configuration shapes cortical activation patterns and how intracortical bipolar stimulation provides additional ways to activate neuronal populations without increasing electrode density. .

items.title: Cenobamate in Focal-Onset Refractory and Super-Refractory Status Epilepticus: A Multicenter Cohort Study With Matched Analysis.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Cenobamate (CNB) is an antiseizure medication (ASM) with demonstrated efficacy in drug-resistant focal epilepsy, but its role in status epilepticus (SE) remains unclear. Emerging evidence suggests that it may achieve early clinically meaningful seizure control at relatively low doses, with an acceptable safety profile, supporting its potential utility as an urgent adjunctive therapy in severe refractory epilepsy. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of CNB for the treatment of focal-onset refractory SE (RSE) and super-refractory SE (SRSE) in real-world clinical practice. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using a prospectively maintained registry including adult patients with focal RSE and SRSE treated between January 2022 and October 2025. Clinical, EEG, and treatment data were collected. The primary outcome was sustained SE termination (>24 hours) with electroclinical resolution attributable to CNB. A secondary propensity score-matched analysis (1:2) compared CNB-exposed patients with matched nonexposed controls from the same registry (2011-2025), using target trial emulation principles. Results Thirty-one patients received CNB (mean age 61 ± 21 years; 54.8% male); 45.2% met criteria for SRSE. CNB was initiated a median of 4 days (interquartile range [IQR] 2-12) after SE onset after failure of 5 ASMs (IQR 4-5), at a median starting dose of 50 mg/d (IQR 25-50). Sustained SE resolution occurred in 26 patients (83.9%), including all patients with RSE (17/17) and 64.3% with SRSE. Response occurred after a median of 2 days (IQR 1-6). In the matched cohort analysis (28 CNB exposed vs 56 controls), SE resolution was higher in CNB-treated patients (82.1% vs 57.1%; p = 0.02). In multivariable analysis, CNB exposure was independently associated with SE resolution (adjusted odds ratio 5.9, 95% CI 1.2-30, p = 0.03). No serious CNB-related adverse events occurred. Mild adverse events were observed in 51.6%, most commonly somnolence. In-hospital mortality was 22.6% with no deaths attributed to CNB. Discussion In this multicenter real-world cohort, CNB was associated with high rates of sustained SE termination in RSE and SRSE and improved outcomes compared with matched controls, without serious safety signals. These findings support CNB as a potential adjunctive therapeutic option in refractory focal SE. Classification of evidence This study provides Class IV evidence that CNB is effective as an adjunctive therapy for the control of focal-onset RSE and SRSE in adult patients.

items.title: Resting-State Functional MRI and Clinical Outcomes After Acute Disorders of Consciousness: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Accurate assessment and prognostication of patients with acute disorders of consciousness (DoC) after severe brain injury remain a substantial clinical challenge. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) measures spontaneous, temporally correlated brain activity in the absence of external stimulation and provides objective insight into the integrity of large-scale neural networks that support brain function. Emerging evidence suggests that assessing neural integrity using rs-fMRI may improve outcome prediction in patients with acute DoC. This review summarizes the current evidence of rs-fMRI as an assessment tool during the acute phase of severe brain injury. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature search using MEDLINE and Embase databases from January 2006 to March 2026. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed empirical investigations of adult patients with acute DoC (<28 days postinjury) that examined associations between rs-fMRI measures and clinical outcomes. The systematic review protocol was registered in the PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251085923). Of 396 studies screened, 30 met eligibility criteria. Across these studies, a total of 800 patients (mean age = 48, 69% male) were scanned at a weighted average of 9.31 days after intensive care unit admission. Ten studies included patients exclusively with traumatic brain injury, 8 with cardiac arrest, 2 with encephalopathy, and 10 included mixed etiologies. The most frequently assessed resting-state networks were the default mode (n = 20) and executive control networks (n = 11), followed by visual (n = 6), salience (n = 6), sensorimotor (n = 6), and auditory (n = 5) networks. Across studies, significant associations between rs-fMRI measures and outcome were consistently reported, despite heterogeneity in methodology. The most commonly reported patient outcomes were functional or neurologic status, assessed at hospital discharge or between 3 and 12 months postinjury. Current evidence consistently demonstrates that rs-fMRI acquired during the acute phase of brain injury is associated with neurologic and functional outcomes in patients with DoC. In addition, rs-fMRI may help identify patients more likely to recover consciousness and achieve favorable functional outcomes by characterizing the integrity of large-scale brain networks. However, substantial heterogeneity and small sample sizes limit comparability across studies. Standardized acquisition and analysis frameworks, along with larger prospective studies, are needed to validate the clinical utility of rs-fMRI and support translation into an assessment tool after brain injury.

items.title: Rehabilitation of Swallowing and Language Ability in Patients With Severe Acquired Brain Injury: An Online International Survey.
items.abstract: Purpose Patients with severe acquired brain injury and disorders of consciousness (DoC) are noncommunicative and present with severe dysphagia. To characterize current practices, identify gaps, and explore emerging approaches in postcomatose rehabilitation, the DoC Special Interest Group of the International Brain Injury Association conducted an international survey on speech-language therapy (SLT) practices. Method An online questionnaire, available in seven languages, was disseminated to clinicians involved in swallowing and/or language and communication rehabilitation of patients with DoC. The survey captured (a) sociodemographic and practice setting information, (b) general postcomatose SLT practices, (c) swallowing assessment and management, and (d) language and communication assessment and management. Results Responses were obtained from 166 clinicians, predominantly speech-language pathologists (74%), working in acute/subacute care (38%) or in longer-term rehabilitation (71%). Most assessed (74%) and managed (74%) swallowing disorders, and 25% created or adapted their own assessment tools. For language and communication, most respondents reported assessing (82%) and managing (76%) these abilities, with frequent use of augmentative and alternative communication (71%). Family input was considered central, for identifying motivating stimuli (96%) and involving relatives in therapy (87%). While 29% developed their own language assessment tools, 51% did so for intervention tools, reflecting limited validated resources. Conclusions Clinicians worldwide assess and manage swallowing and communication in patients with DoC but report a lack of validated tools. Practice often relies on individualized approaches and clinician-developed materials, with family involvement. These findings highlight the need for enhanced training and standardized, evidence-based instruments to strengthen SLT practices across the continuum of care. items.title: Toward Culturally Responsive Clinical Practice: Intercultural Speech-Language Pathology Services for Acquired Pragmatic Communication Disorders in Traumatic Brain Injury and Right-Hemisphere Damage.
items.abstract: Purpose Acquired pragmatic communication disorders following traumatic brain injury and right-hemisphere damage can disrupt patient-provider interactions that are essential for effective health care. This clinical focus article explores how these disorders intersect with sociocultural factors such as race, language access, and health literacy, contributing to disparities in health care engagement and outcomes to offer culturally specific considerations. Method This clinical focus article integrates evidence from neurogenic communication disorders, intercultural pragmatics, and health disparities to inform assessment and intervention considerations for acquired pragmatic communication disorders across diverse cultural communication contexts and structural barriers in health care systems. Results Impairments in pragmatic communication can affect discourse management, conversational participation, and comprehension, reducing opportunities for shared understanding during clinical encounters. When these impairments intersect with cultural communication differences or limited health literacy, patients may experience greater difficulty navigating health care systems and participating in medical decision making. Current speech-language pathology assessment practices and rehabilitation models often fail to capture these contextual influences on communication. Considerations for speech-language pathology service improvements related to assessment and treatment are offered. Conclusions Advancing equitable neurogenic rehabilitation requires integrating intercultural pragmatics and sociocultural perspectives into assessment and treatment. Approaches such as dynamic assessment, holistic assessment, and telehealth offer practical pathways to improve assessment practices for individuals with acquired social communication disorders.

items.title: Longitudinal associations between romantic relationship involvement and quality, depression, and suicidal ideation among bisexual women.
items.abstract: Bisexual women have an increased likelihood of experiencing suicidal ideation (SI) and depressive symptoms than both heterosexual and lesbian women. Evidence suggests romantic relationship involvement may lead to worse mental health outcomes for bisexual individuals, even though it is frequently cited as a protective factor among heterosexual and lesbian/gay individuals. It is currently unknown whether romantic relationship involvement is associated with SI among bisexual women and whether other aspects of the romantic relationship (e.g., quality, partner gender) influence mental health in this population. The present study used up to eight waves of data from bisexual young women ( N = 390 across waves) who participated in a longitudinal cohort study and identified as bisexual during at least two consecutive waves (range = 2-8 waves; M = 3.96, SD = 1.93). Multilevel modeling was used to assess concurrent and lagged associations between relationship involvement, quality, partner gender, and mental health. Relationship involvement was not significantly associated with depression or SI in concurrent or lagged analyses. In contrast, at the between-person level, participants who reported higher relationship support (on average) reported lower depressive symptoms, and participants who reported having a female partner more often (on average) reported lower depressive symptoms and SI in concurrent analyses. The present findings suggest that relationship quality and partner gender, but not relationship involvement, are associated with depressive symptoms and SI among bisexual women. As such, relationship quality may be a useful intervention target to improve the mental health of bisexual women. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Who to ask? Children's partner choice reveals sensitivity to reputational incentives.
items.abstract: In navigating social relationships, children need to understand not only that peers are motivated to manage their reputations but also how these reputational incentives shape behavior. Across three nonpreregistered experiments, we explored whether children (aged 3-7; M = 67 months; N = 168) strategically direct their requests for resources to individuals whose reputations would most benefit from sharing. In Experiment 1, 4- to 7-year-olds, but not 3-year-olds, preferentially requested stickers from a puppet who believed he was being filmed over one who believed the camera was off. In Experiment 2, only 6- and 7-year-olds reversed this preference when sharing would be evaluated negatively. Similarly, in Experiment 3, only 6- and 7-year-olds strategically directed requests toward individuals observed by friends rather than by strangers. Together, these findings suggest a developmental shift from general sensitivity to observation to a more flexible understanding of how specific audiences shape others' behavior across contexts. items.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth.
items.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development-its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

items.title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning.
items.abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.
