items.title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum .
items.abstract: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

items.title: Ddx3x deficiency in mice impairs corticofugal motor circuits and causes motor deficits that are attenuated by early-life exercise.
items.abstract: The X-linked RNA helicase DDX3X is a high-risk gene for autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability primarily in females. Individuals with pathogenic variants in DDX3X have pervasive and often severe motor manifestations. Using mouse models, we studied the circuits underlying the motor phenotypes associated with Ddx3x deficiency and examined the feasibility of an early intervention to ameliorate motor trajectories. We show that Ddx3x controls both the development and later plasticity of motor circuits connecting the motor cortex with the pontine nuclei. Ddx3x haploinsufficiency during development affects the dendritic arborization of corticopontine neurons. Juvenile-onset Ddx3x loss in corticopontine neurons is sufficient to induce adult motor impairments overlapping with those caused by chemogenetic disruption of corticopontine circuits. Further, Ddx3x mutant mice engage corticopontine circuits in skilled motor tasks in a sex-dependent manner. Last, Ddx3x haploinsufficient female mice undergoing a juvenile motor intervention show long-lasting specific benefits in their adult motor function. Together, these findings establish Ddx3x as an essential regulator of corticopontine neuron development and function and provide an early motor intervention to ameliorate motor outcomes in a mouse model of DDX3X haploinsufficiency.

items.title: The efficiency of information gain by natural selection.
items.abstract: Natural selection enriches populations for genotypes that are well adapted to their environments, accumulating information about the selective conditions in the process. Therefore, selection can be viewed as a learning process through which populations acquire information about the environment. Motoo Kimura derived a relationship between the amount of information gained by selection and a measure of the inefficiency of the selective process, known as substitution load [M. Kimura, Genet. Res. 2, 127-140 (1961)]. Due to the gradual nature of selection and the ongoing mismatch of types to the environment, a lineage that is still acquiring information has lower mean fitness than a lineage that already has it. While this has been an influential insight, we find that Kimura's model is inconsistent with selection experiments involving Escherichia coli. To address limitations in this model and develop a more robust measure for the efficiency of selection, we turn to computational learning theory. We show that the learning-theoretic concept of regret quantifies the inefficiency of selection as a learning process in terms of relative lineage fitness. We establish bounds on the efficiency of information gain in general settings, including frequency-dependent selection and arbitrary environmental change. We experimentally validate these bounds and demonstrate that our extended theory recovers Kimura's fundamental insight. Finally, we show that selection is an asymptotically optimal algorithm for the basic problem faced by evolving populations and that it acquires information more efficiently than comparable processes in complex environments.

items.title: Sex- and age-specific development of ssRNA virus receptor expression in the human brain.
items.abstract: Neurotropic single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) viruses can disrupt brain function, yet little is known about how host virus receptor expression develops across the human lifespan or whether these trajectories differ between females and males. We focused on postnatal development using postmortem transcriptomic data from 33 human donors (4 months-82 years; both sexes), comprising 52 cerebral hemispheres and 15 brain areas, to characterize developmental patterns of 67 host receptor genes that mediate entry of major ssRNA viral families. Using sex-specific LOESS trajectory modelling, hierarchical clustering, and sliding-window differential expression analyses, we identified multiple non-linear developmental programs governing virus receptor expression. About half of female-male gene-area trajectory pairs exhibited divergent developmental patterns. Sex differences were most pronounced in the cortex, where high-dimensional receptor expression profiles were sufficient to predict the sex of individual cases. Sex differential expression was most frequent during early childhood, coinciding with sensitive periods of cortical circuit refinement. A targeted prenatal analysis revealed that virus receptor expression was predominantly male-biased before birth, contrasting with the predominantly female-biased expression observed during the early postnatal period. Although receptors from most viral families were broadly distributed across developmental programs, a subset of sex-by-age expression clusters showed some enrichment for specific viral lineages and glial-associated cell-type signatures. Together, these findings reveal that virus receptor expression in the human brain is organized into structured, sex-biased trajectories that dynamically reorganize over development, providing the first developmental atlas of viral entry receptors in the human brain.

items.title: Locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons have diverse activity patterns across species and biological context.
items.abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) brainstem cell group is evolutionarily conserved across vertebrates and influences both mind (cognition) and body (cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and immune functions) via two-putatively distinct-spontaneous activity patterns. Yet, the degree to which spontaneous LC firing rates and patterns are homogeneous across species has never been assessed due to inherently limited sample sizes. To remedy this, we pooled cross-species data from 20 laboratories to show that firing rates differ across species and are modulated by sex, age, and type of in vitro or in vivo preparation. Contrary to the prevailing dual-mode firing pattern schema, we observed patterns spread across a low-dimensional manifold, with subregions enriched for specific biological factors and neurodegenerative disease models. Our findings show considerable diversity in an ancestral vertebrate neuromodulatory system.

items.title: Assessment of light sensitivity using the Ocular Photosensitivity Analyzer: Discomfort threshold, pain threshold, and tolerance in healthy volunteers.
items.abstract: Photophobia encompasses a continuum of light-induced experiences from mild discomfort to overt pain and intolerance, yet clinical tools rarely quantify these distinctions, leaving many patients undiagnosed and untreated. This study employed the Ocular Photosensitivity Analyzer (OPA), a compact instrument for quantitative sensory testing (QST) with light, to investigate three perceptual levels in healthy adults: visual photosensitivity discomfort threshold (VPDT), visual photosensitivity pain threshold (VPPT), and an exploratory outcome, visual photosensitivity tolerance level (VPTol). Twenty-nine participants ages 19-34 underwent standardized OPA testing, during which they identified when light first became uncomfortable, painful, and intolerable. After each trial, participants rated the peak pain intensity (PI) and peak unpleasantness (UP) using visual analog scales. Measured illuminance values differed significantly across the perceptual levels (RM-ANOVA, N = 28, F(1.69, 45.6)=37.06, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.58; Mauchly's W = 0.82, p = 0.072), indicating sensory levels are differentiable. Post hoc t-tests revealed VPTol exceeded VPPT (N = 28, t(27)=-2.29, p = 0.030, dz = 0.43)), and both exceeded VPDT (VPTol: N = 29, t(28)=-7.69, p < 0.001, dz = 1.43, VPPT: N = 29, t(27)=-7.69, p < 0.001, dz = 1.47). Friedman's test revealed UP (N = 28, χ2(2)=17.64, p < 0.001, Kendall's W = 0.32) and PI (N = 28, χ2(2)=22.36, p < 0.001, Kendall's W = 0.40) differences across perceptual levels and post hoc Wilcoxon tests showed UP and PI increased between VPDT and VPPT (UP: N = 29, Z = -4.34, p < 0.001, r = 0.57, PI: N = 29, Z = -4.58, p < 0.001, r = 0.60) and UP increased between VPDT and VPTol (N = 28, Z = -2.92, p = 0.007, r = 0.39), suggesting that both affective and sensory dimensions of pain vary across perceptual levels. Although preliminary, these findings are consistent with a multidimensional framework of photophobia. Additionally, the OPA's ability to differentially quantify VPDT, VPPT, and VPTol offers a novel approach to characterize light sensitivity that may aid future assessment of abnormal light sensitivity.

items.title: "The significance of context": Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD.
items.abstract: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with various traits that influence individuals' experiences at work. While some may be experienced as challenging (e.g., when differences in executive function impact time management), others can be more positive (e.g., when curiosity motivates exploration and discovery). Plausibly, academia is a work environment where these positive aspects should be valued. However, ADHD is still often viewed from a medicalised perspective in workplace settings, despite the neurodiversity paradigm offering an alternative, non-pathologising way to frame these individual differences. Research has begun to explore employment experiences and outcomes for adults with ADHD; however, there is currently little data relevant to academic workplaces specifically. This qualitative study offers a critical realist analysis of interviews with early-career academics, seeking to understand first-person ADHD perspectives on establishing an academic career. Consistent with the neurodiversity paradigm, the analysis foregrounds (mis-)matches between individual 'neurotypes' and workplace environments. It also highlights an ecological view by exploring how ADHD matters both for individual careers and for collective knowledge production. Findings suggest that academia can, in principle, be a rewarding environment for ADHDers, though social and institutional pressures often inhibit this potential. Furthermore, having an 'ADHD neurotype' influences both individual career trajectories and wellbeing at work; at the same time, knowledge production at the collective level may benefit from the inclusion of ADHD academics. The findings are discussed in reference to ecological models of neurodiversity and their implications for universities aiming to facilitate neurodivergent contributions and inclusion at work.

items.title: A community health worker pilot intervention to increase patient portal use among people with HIV.
items.abstract: Use of patient portals is associated with improved engagement in care and health outcomes in a variety of healthcare contexts including among people with HIV (PWH). However, there are disparities in portal access and barriers to portal use including lack of awareness, need for more education, and mistrust or unfamiliarity with the technology used. We investigated whether a community health worker (CHW)-led pilot initiative could increase patient portal use among PWH. Participants who enrolled in the study received help with the patient portal (MyChart) and a one-time personalized 30-minute training session with the CHW on MyChart functions. Participants reported sociodemographic information, current MyChart use, barriers, and functions of interest. MyChart utilization data were retrieved for the six months before and after the training. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the data, and McNemar's exact tests were used to determine significant differences between pre-training and post-training intervals (a pre-post, single-arm study design). A total of 55 participants were enrolled and trained. The majority of participants were Black or African American (94.5%), and most had Medicaid or Medicare insurance (65.5%). The most frequently used MyChart functions included viewing lab results (65.5%) and health history (60.0%), scheduling appointments (56.4%), and sending messages (54.5%). The most commonly reported barriers were lack of time (21.8%) and not understanding how to use the portal (20.0%). There was a significant increase in read/view functions (reviewing test results, reading messages, etc.) after the training (61.8% to 81.8%, p-value = 0.048). The increase in use of write/update functions (responding to messages, paying bills, updating account information, etc.) was not statistically significant (56.4% to 72.7%, p-value = 0.216). The increase in use of some MyChart functions after the training indicates the potential of CHW-led interventions to address barriers and increase portal use among PWH.

items.title: Arousal-related neural circuits in consciousness disorders: Updated model integrating ascending reticular activating system and mesocircuit.
items.abstract: Consciousness emerges from the dynamic coupling of arousal and conscious content. Although the ascending reticular activating system predominantly regulates arousal, mesocircuit activity supports the integration of conscious content. Disorders of consciousness arise primarily from structural damage or functional disruption of these two core neural systems. Recent advances in neuroscience have enabled high-resolution mechanistic investigations of disorders of consciousness at the cellular and circuit levels. This review synthesizes advances from the past 5 years to delineate how distinct neuronal subpopulations within the ascending reticular activating system precisely regulate conscious states. Key neuronal regulators include cholinergic and glutamatergic neurons in the pedunculopontine tegmental nucleus, noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus, orexinergic neurons in the lateral hypothalamus, and basal forebrain astrocytes. The nucleus accumbens has emerged as a previously underrecognized hub that coordinates arousal and conscious processing. The ascending reticular activating system and mesocircuit achieve dynamic coupling through specialized thalamic subnuclei, notably the paraventricular thalamic nucleus, central lateral, and medial dorsal nuclei, as well as through experience-dependent cortical reorganization, thereby orchestrating transitions between conscious states. These circuit-level insights have informed the development of a multi-level, multi-modal intervention framework for disorders of consciousness. Future priorities include transitioning from acute anesthesia models to clinically relevant chronic disorders of consciousness models, identifying robust cross-species circuit biomarkers, and translating basic circuit findings into patient-oriented clinical research. The development of closed-loop adaptive neurostimulation may further refine our mechanistic understanding of disorders of consciousness and lay the groundwork for clinical translation.

items.title: Naphthenic acids as emerging petroleum-derived contaminants: Environmental fate, ecotoxicological effects, and human health implications.
items.abstract: Oil pollution represents a significant global environmental threat, with naphthenic acids (NAs) - naturally occurring carboxylic acid derivatives in crude oil-emerging as critical pollutants due to their persistence, bioaccumulation potential, and multifaceted toxicity. This review critically synthesizes current knowledge on NAs, focusing on their scientific definitions, analytical characterization, environmental fate, toxicological mechanisms, and research challenges. These compounds have been detected in diverse environmental matrices across multiple regions such as Asia, Europe, and North America, with concentrations reaching mg/L levels in oil-impacted environments, particularly in oil sands regions. Increasing evidence indicates that NAs can migrate from environmental media into living organisms, and demonstrate a clear potential for bioaccumulation. By integrating evidence across multiple biological taxa, we proposed an adverse outcome pathway framework illustrating that membrane perturbation and reactive oxygen species accumulation represent critical initiating events leading to adverse outcomes at cellular, organism, and population levels.​ However, human health risks remain uncertain due to limited information on exposure pathways, internal exposure levels, and epidemiological evidence. Future research should prioritize field-deployable detection techniques, standardized toxicity assessment frameworks, and improved characterization of human exposure levels. This review underscores the need for globally coordinated monitoring strategies and rigorous regulatory standards to mitigate NAs-related ecological and public health risks.

items.title: Bacterial epidemiology and attributable mortality of Ventilator-associated pneumonia before and after COVID-19 pandemic (2018-2021).
items.abstract: BackgroundVentilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in mechanically ventilated patients. The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly modified VAP epidemiology and microbial ecology.MethodsWe conducted a prospective multicenter cohort study within the REA-REZO network (≈20% of French ICU beds), 1 January 2018-31 December 2021. All adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation were included. VAP was defined according to ECDC criteria. Primary endpoints were VAP incidence density (per 1000 ventilation-days) and 30-day attributable mortality. Secondary endpoints included resistance patterns and pre-pandemic versus pandemic trends.ResultsAmong 98,047 patients, 12,251 patients developed VAP, with an incidence of 18.9/1000 ventilation-days. Peak incidence occurred at day 10 (29/1000 ventilation-days). Thirty-day attributable mortality was 4.9% [95% CI 3.7;6.2], rising to 7.2% [6.0;8.5] at 60 days. Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 78.0% of isolates, predominantly Enterobacterales (46%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (20%). Third-generation cephalosporin resistance reached 27% in Enterobacterales and 25% in P. aeruginosa . The COVID-19 patients had a higher VAP rate (19.5% vs 9.7%, p<0.001) and mortality (36.9% vs 31.0%, p<0.001).ConclusionsVAP remains highly prevalent in French ICUs with substantial attributable mortality. The COVID-19 pandemic nearly doubled VAP incidence and worsened resistance profiles. Intensified prevention bundles during the first 10 days of ventilation and reinforced antimicrobial stewardship are critical.

items.title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.
items.abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic, and (meta)proteomic data analysis within a FAIR-aligned environment. It also supports research in the health and infectious disease sectors, as well as in environmental microbiology. The platform's utility is exemplified through various use cases, including antimicrobial resistance tracking, biomarker prediction, microbiome classification, and functional annotation of key microbes. Built on reproducibility and community engagement, it supports the creation, sharing, and updating of best-practice workflows. Over 35 tutorials and learning paths empower scientists, fostering an ecosystem that keeps resources at the forefront of microbiological data analysis. The MGL enables collective analysis, democratising research, thereby accelerating discovery across the global microbiology community ( microbiology.usegalaxy.org , .eu , .org.au , . fr ).

items.title: Tree and neighborhood damage have distinct effects on delayed mortality after a severe hurricane.
items.abstract: Tropical forest resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration depend on tree survival. Disturbance events, such as hurricanes, generate distinct forms of damage at the individual-tree and neighborhood scale, providing a unique setting to disentangle the causal contributions of mortality drivers. Leveraging post-hurricane census data for nearly 4000 trees in the Luquillo Forest Dynamics Plot, Puerto Rico, we used a causal inference framework combined with Bayesian multilevel models to estimate the effect of individual- and neighborhood-scale damage on delayed tree mortality following Hurricane Maria (2017). Individual damage effects depended on species identity and tree size. Stem break emerged as the most lethal form of damage across the community. Neighborhood damage was associated with elevated mortality following Hurricane Maria, independent of focal tree damage. This effect was strongest among large trees, consistent with disproportionately high physiological stress resulting from greater inherent metabolic demands, refoliation energy costs, and evapotranspiration following canopy recovery. Severe biomass loss (> 75% crown loss) buffered large trees from negative neighborhood effects, revealing a positive pruning effect on survival. Our study advances mechanistic understanding of delayed tree mortality, while also suggesting how mortality patterns may shift with expected increases in disturbance severity under a warming climate.

items.title: Trait-based plant ecology: some history and some future.
items.abstract: Since around the year 2000, trait-based ecology has become self-aware as a strand of research within ecology. How did this happen? What is trait-based ecology now? And where might it go in future? This paper offers selective answers to those questions. We first outline the history leading up to the emergence of trait-based plant ecology during the 1990s. Second, we assess briefly what has been achieved up to mid-2020s. Third, we discuss two challenges (among many) for trait-based plant ecology over the next 25 yr. One is about the boundaries of species ranges along temperature gradients. Some of these boundaries may be decided by thermal tolerance, others by biotic interactions such as competition or pathogens. How can we identify which applies to which species? Which traits, feasible to measure across many species, might help with this? A second major challenge is about the global zonation of vegetation physiognomy or biome types. How well can we explain this in terms of traits, and from first principles, meaning via eco-evolutionary models for why different trait values should be competent and competitive in different settings? First-principle rules for how ecosystems are constructed should be central to ecology as a discipline.

items.title: A new species of the genus Dysommina from the Lakshadweep Sea, India (Anguilliformes: Synaphobranchidae: Ilyophinae).
items.abstract: This study describes a new Dysommina species, based on two specimens collected at a depth of ca. 600 m in the Lakshadweep Sea off south-western India. The new species differs from its congeners in having fewer total vertebrae (120-127 vs. 134 in D. castanea, 133-134 in D. brevis, and 137-141 in D. orientalis), fewer predorsal vertebrae (14-15 vs. 16 in D. pygmaea), fewer preanal vertebrae (24-27 vs. 28-31 in D. rugosa), and in a combination of morphometric, meristic, dentition and colouration characters. DNA sequences were generated and analysed.

items.title: Ecological risks of using non-native freshwater fish for biological control.
items.abstract: The use of freshwater fish as biological control agents has been widely implemented to manage populations of perceived nuisance species, ranging from disease vectors to aquatic weeds. While these introductions are often intended as a management tool, they can have unintended and severe ecological, economic, and social consequences. This review assesses the risks associated with using non-native fish for biological control, emphasising the challenges presented by their persistence, adaptability, and interactions with native species and ecosystems. Key case studies illustrate how species such as mosquitofishes (Gambusia spp.), grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella), and tilapias (mainly Oreochromis spp.) have inadvertently contributed to biodiversity loss, habitat degradation, trophic disruptions, and disease transmission, while often failing to effectively control the target species. We further explore the limitations of biocontrol strategies, including the context-dependent nature of species interactions and deferred negative impacts. Given the complexity and unpredictability of biological control interventions, rigorous impact assessments and long-term monitoring programmes are needed before and after introducing non-native fish as control agents, embedded within an adaptive management framework that allows for responsive decision-making based on observed ecological outcomes. Precautionary policies should prioritise habitat restoration and native species-based solutions over the introduction of non-native species to support more sustainable and ecologically responsible management decisions.

items.title: Biotic modulators of global change effects on plant communities.
items.abstract: Understanding and predicting future plant biodiversity and productivity is critical for prioritizing global change mitigation, conservation, and restoration efforts. One major challenge is that we know remarkably little about how interspecific interactions may modulate the effects of global change factors on diversity and productivity. Here, we develop and test a synthetic conceptual framework about how different 'biotic modulators' (herbivory, plant-plant interactions, pathogens, mycorrhiza) can either amplify or mitigate the effects of global change drivers (nutrient and CO 2 enrichment, changes in rainfall and temperature) on plant community biomass and diversity. We report that herbivores mitigated both biomass increases and diversity decline caused by different global change drivers, while plant competition did not significantly alter global change impacts due to mixed effects (both amplification and mitigation). Pathogens tended to function similarly to herbivores, while mycorrhiza both amplified and mitigated community responses. Our conceptual framework further identifies mechanisms by which species interactions can modify global change effects, provides new testable hypotheses, and identifies research gaps and future research directions. We conclude that plant consumers can be important agents for stabilizing plant productivity and safeguarding plant biodiversity in the Anthropocene, but that more research is urgently needed to understand the role of other biotic modulators.

items.title: Hepatospora eriocheir infection affects the fitness of adult Chinese mitten crabs in their non-native range.
items.abstract: For many invasive crustaceans, including the Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis), the prevalence and impact of parasites in their introduced range remain largely unexplored. The microsporidium Hepatospora eriocheir was recently detected in mitten crabs across Europe, yet little is known about its physiological effects on its host. In this study, the influence of H. eriocheir infection on physiological biomarkers in adult mitten crabs collected from rivers in Germany and Belgium was experimentally investigated. We assessed metabolic rates (routine and maximum metabolic rate, aerobic scope), haemolymph glucose and lactate levels, and lipid content in the hepatopancreas. Infection prevalence reached 27% in adult mitten crabs from the Belgian population and 38% in individuals from the German population. Infected individuals showed a significantly reduced maximum metabolic rate and aerobic scope, while the routine metabolic rate remained unaffected. Glucose levels were lower in infected crabs both at rest and post-exercise, which indicates that energy reserves have dropped, whereas lactate levels showed no significant difference. The lipid content in the hepatopancreas was reduced, likely due to direct exploitation of host resources by the parasite and damage to hepatopancreatic tissue. Together, these patterns indicate an impaired energy metabolism, which may hamper energetically demanding activities such as migration and reproduction. The Chinese mitten crab is a catadromous species, and as the examined crabs were at the life stage when they commence a long-distance migration for their single reproductive event, infection by H. eriocheir may compromise their ability to complete this migration and successfully reproduce.

items.title: Conflicting phylogenomic signals unveil reticulate evolution in Uraria and allies (Leguminosae: Desmodieae).
items.abstract: The tribe Desmodieae represents one of the most taxonomically challenging lineages within Leguminosae, characterized by high morphological diversity and phylogenetic incongruence that have long hindered generic delimitation. Here, we addressed this taxonomic problem using Uraria and its allied genera as a case study. We integrated genome-scale nuclear and plastid datasets generated from transcriptome sequencing and whole-genome resequencing to reconstruct the evolutionary history of this lineage. Our phylogenomic reconstructions, based on 1,079 single- or low-copy nuclear genes and complete plastomes, recovered Urariopsis brevissima as a strongly supported, early-diverging lineage and showed that Uraria and Christia are non-monophyletic. We observed gene-tree discordance in the relationships of Uraria and Christia, both among individual gene trees and between nuclear and plastid phylogenies. Using complementary phylogenomic approaches, we evaluated the sources of the observed gene-tree discordance, and found that gene-tree estimation error had the largest relative explanatory contribution overall, and gene flow had a greater explanatory contribution than ILS among the biological factors evaluated. Analyses of incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) and gene flow, together with network inference, yielded patterns consistent with a putative reticulation scenario between Uraria and Christia. On the basis of these phylogenomic findings, we proposed taxonomic treatments that recognize Urariopsis as a distinct genus and transfer Christia campanulata to Uraria. Our results not only clarify the taxonomy of Uraria and its allied genera but also offer a phylogenomic framework for reassessing generic delimitation in Desmodieae.

items.title: Ancestral state inference at an uncertain trifurcation: What colors of light could the common ancestor of the fungi "see"?
items.abstract: Reconstruction of the traits of extinct ancestors is a central challenge in evolutionary biology. This reconstruction is especially difficult in lineages such as fungi, whose extraordinary ecological, biological, and morphological diversity is underserved by a sparse fossil record. In fungi, therefore, this limitation makes phylogenetic comparative approaches essential for inferring traits at key ancestral nodes. Because the deepest fungal ancestors appear to be aquatic-and because extant aquatic fungi appear to retain several ancestral sensory systems, photoreception provides a compelling system for investigation of early fungal ecology and evolution. Yet modern fungi harbor a much broader diversity of light-sensing pathways, leaving unresolved which components were already present in the most recent common ancestor of fungi. Accurate assessment of the apparati for light sensing in the ancestor of all fungi is the very first step to understanding the evolution and divergence of fungal "eyes": receptors that are sensitive to specific spans of the wavelengths of visible light. Here, using recent fungal genome sequencing, annotation and phylogenomics, with particular emphasis on flagellated lineages, we reconstructed the ancestral presence or absence of all known fungal light-sensory genes. To account for uncertainty in early fungal relationships, we evaluated two competing phylogenetic hypotheses that differ with regard to the controversial placement of Blastocladiomycota. Across these analyses, the CyclOp and the White Collar light-sensing systems were consistently inferred to have been present in the fungal ancestor, whereas phytochromes were likely absent, providing a phylogenetically explicit foundation for understanding the early evolution of fungal photoreception.

items.title: Comparing adult defensive behavior with mating status in three species of false widow spiders.
items.abstract: Among a myriad of important traits exhibited by organisms that affect fitness are those associated with defense against natural enemies such as predators. These defenses are often broadly categorized as 'primary' and 'secondary'. The former describes a wide range of physical and behavioral traits and ecological ploys that create 'enemy-free space' for an organism, whereas the latter describes traits and strategies that are employed when contact with an enemy is unavoidable. Spiders, as both prey and predators, their repertoire of behaviors may include both defensive and offensive tactics when confronted with threats. Here, we compared secondary defensive behavior in three closely related species of spiders, the false black widow, Steatoda grossa, the Mediterranean false widow, S. paykulliana and the noble false widow, S. nobilis when confronted with different artificial stimuli. The size hierarchy of adult females of the three species is S. grossa<S. paykulliana<S. nobilis. Using a brush or hard-tipped tweezers, we recorded behavioral responses of virgin and mated (with egg sacs) females to probing or pinching actions. We anticipated more aggressive defenses by females when guarding their egg sacs. Our results revealed both passive (fleeing, feigning death) and aggressive (biting, pulling globular silk threads) responses to perceived threats among the three species, with S. paykulliana females tending to exhibit more aggressive responses than other Steatoda species. However, the presence of an egg sac did not significantly trigger more active and aggressive behavioral responses in the three species. Our results showed that behaviors to perceived threats in these congeneric spiders vary and are not correlated with female body size (at the species level).

items.title: Interfacial Polarity Matching Governs Chain-Length-Dependent Adsorption of Perfluoroalkyl Carboxylic Acids on Activated Carbon.
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants of increasing environmental concern because of their mobility, durability, and potential health risks. Activated carbon (AC) is widely used for PFAS removal, but its nonpolar surface primarily favors long-chain PFAS, whereas short-chain PFAS remain difficult to capture. Here, AC was coated with polydopamine (AC-PDA) and subsequently functionalized with alkylamines of different chain lengths to regulate its interfacial hydrophilic-hydrophobic properties. Ethylamine-grafted AC-PDA (AC-PDA-C 2 ) showed the highest adsorption for trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), hexylamine-grafted AC-PDA (AC-PDA-C 6 ) for perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA), perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), and perfluoroheptanoic acid (PFHpA), and decylamine-grafted AC-PDA (AC-PDA-C 10 ) for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA). Further increasing the grafted alkyl chain length to C 14 did not improve adsorption, indicating optimal interfacial matching rather than maximum hydrophobicity. The maximum Langmuir adsorption capacities for TFA, PFHxA, and PFNA were 0.51, 0.72, and 1.0 g g -1 , respectively. Mechanistic analyses revealed a chain-length-dependent transition from predominantly hydrophilic interactions for ultra-short-chain PFAS to mixed hydrophilic-hydrophobic interactions for short-chain PFAS and predominantly hydrophobic interactions for long-chain PFAS. These findings demonstrate that matching adsorbent interfacial polarity with PFAS chain length provides a rational strategy for enhancing PFAS enrichment and designing adsorbents for structurally diverse PFAS.

items.title: Riverine Inputs of Organophosphate Diesters Rival Triesters in the External OPE Load to Taihu Lake.
items.abstract: Organophosphate esters (OPEs), including organophosphate triesters (OPTEs) and organophosphate diesters (OPDEs), are widely detected in aquatic environments; yet their watershed-scale input pathways to shallow lakes remain insufficiently constrained. Here, we investigated OPTEs and OPDEs in dry deposition, rainwater and 13 major inflowing tributaries around Taihu Lake, with monthly sampling over one year (March 2024-February 2025; 156 surface-water samples, 60 deposition samples and 20 whole-event rainwater composites). Mean ∑ 12 OPDEs exceeded mean ∑ 30 OPTEs in tributaries (1486 vs 1068 ng/L), although median ∑ 12 OPDEs (73.3 ng/L) remained below median ∑ 30 OPTEs (836 ng/L), while OPDEs accounted for up to 83.2% of the combined input at individual western tributaries. Aryl OPTEs accounted for 77.4% of OPTEs in dry deposition, among which tris(2,4-di-tert-butylphenyl) phosphate (TDTBPP) was the dominant compound. Wet deposition delivered ∑ 30 OPTE fluxes (163-419 g/km 2 ·year) comparable to those of dry deposition (110-401 g/km 2 ·year), while ∑ 12 OPDE wet fluxes (6.73-162 g/km 2 ·year) exceeded dry fluxes (1.73-16.4 g/km 2 ·year) by about an order of magnitude. In contrast, tributary discharge delivered substantial OPDE loads to Taihu Lake. In tributaries, mean ∑ 12 OPDEs exceeded mean ∑ 30 OPTEs (1486 vs 1068 ng/L), although median ∑ 12 OPDEs (73.3/ng L) remained below median ∑ 30 OPTEs (836 ng/L); on an annual load basis, OPDEs accounted for up to 83.2% of the combined riverine OPE input at individual western tributaries. This OPDE dominance was primarily driven by bis(1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate (BCIPP), which showed high concentrations and strong contributions in several western inflows. These results reveal that Taihu Lake receives chemically distinct OPE inputs through dry deposition, wet deposition, and tributary discharge. More importantly, the BCIPP-rich riverine input suggests that OPDEs are major contributors to external OPE loads for Taihu Lake, rather than merely degradation markers of parent OPTEs, irrespective of whether they are formed in situ or released directly.

items.title: Asynchronous functional recovery and structural reconfiguration of water-sediment networks in an actively restored lake.
items.abstract: Internal nutrient loading often constrains the recovery of shallow eutrophic urban lakes. While temporal lags between water and sediment recovery are recognized, how active restoration reshapes their structural relationships remains poorly understood. We conducted a one-year in situ restoration experiment in Nanhu Lake (Wuhan, China) using six hectare-scale ecological enclosures (two replicate enclosures per treatment) to evaluate a gradient of restoration treatments: a baseline ecological restoration (ER; submerged macrophytes (Vallisneria natans), microbial flocculants, and algaecides), phosphorus retention treatment (PR; ER + lanthanum-modified bentonite), and nitrogen-phosphorus reduction treatment (NPR; PR + high-efficiency nitrogen removal materials). Compared with the same season before restoration, water-column conditions changed rapidly across all treatments, with significantly higher dissolved oxygen and lower total phosphorus and chemical oxygen demand, although chlorophyll a and NH 4 + -N also increased. In contrast, sediment responses lagged behind those of the water column. While most sediment physicochemical parameters remained unchanged after one year, sediment phosphorus-binding capacity increased, whereas total nitrogen and the potential DNRA rate decreased. No significant overall differences among the three restoration treatments were detected across the full sampling period. Furthermore, ecological network analysis identified fewer cross-compartment associations after restoration, suggesting reduced coordination between water-column and sediment dynamics, while water-column total nitrogen retained the highest closeness centrality in both periods. These findings highlight asynchronous water-sediment responses during the first year of restoration and support a phased management perspective that accounts for rapid water-column responses alongside slower sediment adjustment.

items.title: CaO/MgO nanoparticle-modified diatomite for co-retention of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus and mitigation of nutrient leaching from soil.
items.abstract: Excessive accumulation of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), dissolved nitrogen (DN), and dissolved phosphorus (DP) in citrus orchard soils may increase the risk of agricultural non-point source pollution. The simultaneous and efficient retention of these dissolved nutrients in complex multi-solute systems, such as lemon waste fermentation broth (LWFB), remains a significant challenge, and the retention behavior of modified materials under such conditions is still poorly understood. Herein, a modified diatomite composite incorporating in situ loaded CaO/MgO nanoparticles (CMNPs@AD) was successfully synthesized via a facile acid-base activation strategy combined with an equal-volume impregnation method to investigate its nutrient retention performance and underlying mechanisms in LWFB. The results showed that CMNPs@AD featured a mesoporous structure decorated with uniformly dispersed metal nanoparticles. In the Langmuir isotherm model, the theoretical maximum retention capacities of CMNPs@AD for DOC, DN, and DP were 22.39, 45.02, and 25.49 mg/g, respectively. Advanced characterization techniques and density functional theory revealed that the nutrient retention mechanism of CMNPs@AD involves multiple physicochemical processes. Soil column leaching experiments showed that, compared with the fertilization group, the application of 1.0 wt% CMNPs@AD significantly reduced DOC, DN, and DP leaching while increasing soil sucrase, urease, and neutral phosphatase activities. The nutrient-laden CMNPs@AD (CMNPs@AD-CNP) significantly improved seed germination performance. Moreover, pot experiments demonstrated that plants grown in the post-leaching T2 soil showed enhanced growth and biomass accumulation and higher chlorophyll content than those in the other treatments. This study developed a novel and cost-effective soil additive that effectively reduced the co-leaching losses of dissolved soil nutrients, providing a promising material-based strategy for mitigating nutrient leaching from soil.

items.title: Aeration-free microalgal-bacterial granular sludge for simultaneous nitrification, denitrification and phosphorus removal: Rapid start-up and functional differentiation.
items.abstract: The simultaneous nitrification, denitrification, and phosphorus removal (SNDPR) process based on aeration-free microalgal-bacterial granular sludge (MBGS) offers a promising aeration-free pathway for sustainable wastewater treatment, but suffers from prolonged and unstable start-up. In this study, we co-inoculated aerobic granular sludge (AGS) capable of SNDPR with pre-cultivated MBGS to achieve rapid start-up of the aeration-free MBGS-SNDPR process in a photo-sequencing batch reactor. This strategy maintained a stable biomass concentration, improved physicochemical properties of the granules, and achieved efficient removal of COD (88% ± 4%), NH 4 + -N (99% ± 1%), total nitrogen (TN, 85% ± 6%), and PO 4 3- -P (91% ± 7%) throughout 100 days of reactor operation. Two morphologically and functionally distinct MBGS types that evolved from the AGS inoculum were identified: MBGS-S originated from small AGS ( 1 mm) colonized by phototrophs. MBGS-S was dominated by nitrification and phosphorus removal, whereas MBGS-L was dominated by denitrification. Typical cycle tests and mass balance calculations demonstrated that the reactor achieved efficient SNDPR performance, produced less net CO 2 production than active sludge, and retained phosphorus in harvested biomass as a potential recovery pool. Microbial community analysis further indicated that SNDPR-related functional microorganisms persisted and abundances of key functional genes increased throughout the operation, thereby ensuring stable and efficient pollutant removal. Overall, this study provides insights into strategies for the rapid start-up of the aeration-free MBGS-SNDPR process and for the successful integration of functional microorganisms into this sustainable process.

items.title: Differential reproductive effects of two insect growth regulators (20-hydroxyecdysone and methyl farnesoate) on non-target aquatic organism: A case study using Daphnia magna.
items.abstract: Two insect growth regulators (IGRs), 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E) and methyl farnesoate (MF), are widely used in hormone-based pest control and may pose risks to aquatic ecosystems by disrupting the endocrine systems of non-target organisms. This study investigated the chronic (21-day) and acute (96-h) toxic effects of hazard characterization dose (50 μg/L) 20E and MF on reproduction, endocrine disruption, and underlying molecular mechanisms in Daphnia magna, a key model in ecotoxicology. Chronic exposure revealed that 20E significantly enhanced somatic growth (+5.4% body length at day 7) while inhibiting reproduction (-14.95% total offspring), whereas MF had no significant effects in surviving individuals, but suppressed overall reproduction through a mortality-driven effect. Acute exposure demonstrated that 20E elevated vitellogenin (+45.33%) and ecdysone levels (+22.09%), while MF primarily increased juvenile hormone (JH) synthesis (+7.99%). Transcriptomic analysis revealed that both compounds downregulated sphingolipid and glycerophospholipid metabolism pathways, with shared downregulation of MFE (Methyl farnesoate epoxidase) and EPPL (Ethanolamine-phosphate phospho-lyase) genes critical for JH and lipid homeostasis. Molecular docking predicted that 20E and MF could bind to the ecdysone receptor (EcR) and methoprene-tolerant (Met) proteins, with MF showing higher binding affinity to EcR (-6.95 kcal/mol vs. -6.05 kcal/mol for 20E). These endocrine disruptions are consistent with the suppression of reproduction via altered cholesterol mobilization and steroidogenesis pathways. This study provides novel insights into the mechanisms of estrogenic disruption in D. magna, highlighting the ecological risks of IGRs in aquatic environments.

items.title: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction.
items.abstract: Animal pollinators underpin biodiversity and global agriculture, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinate floral rewards and signals to attract pollinators remain poorly understood. Through phenotyping melon genetic diversity, we identified nectarless1 (nls1), encoding the YABBY-family transcription factor YABBY5 (YAB5), as a central integrator of pollinator-attracting traits. YAB5 interacts with CRABS CLAW (CRC) during nectary initiation to specify nectary identity by repressing alternative floral organ fates. As flowers mature, YAB5 directly activates 4-α-glucanotransferase 2 (DPE2) to promote starch remobilization required for nectar secretion and promotes petal growth and flower opening. In petals, YAB5 directly engages an MYB111-dependent flavonoid pathway that generates UV nectar guides, while indirectly influencing floral volatile emission. Disrupting YAB5, DPE2, or MYB111 reduces pollinator visitation. Together, these findings reveal how a developmental regulator couples organ specification with organ-specific metabolic programs to synchronize floral rewards and signals at anthesis.

items.title: Long-term crucian carp (Carassius carassius) resilience to duckweed (Lemnaceae) dominance in a small eastern English pond.
items.abstract: Successful scientifically informed fish conservation requires a good knowledge of how fishes have and will be affected by multiple stresses over the decadal-centennial timescales relevant to real-life fish-environment responses. By combining palaeoecological and monitoring data (regular sampling over 16 years), we studied the long-term response of an English pond population of crucian carp (Carassius carassius) to environmental stress (likely anoxia) posed by episodic periods of duckweed (Lemnaceae) dominance. Despite at least three major phases of prolonged high duckweed cover, in addition to historically recorded low water events, crucian carp persisted in the study pond for at least two centuries until the present day. During the most recent duckweed phase (spanning 6 years - 1999-2005), the crucian carp population edged close to extinction, with a few large individuals surviving and an elimination of recruitment (or at least severely reduced recruitment) over 4 years. Crucian carp recruitment resumed 1 year post-duckweed, however, and occurred at regular intervals subsequently leading to a population structure dominated by individuals of age 2-4 years. After 2002, a broader and more even population size and age structure was evident, suggestive of full recovery. The remarkable resilience of crucian carp to dense duckweed cover and likely associated anoxia is deserving of future research. Clearly, duckweed dominance in small hydrologically isolated ponds, as may be more prevalent under climate change, is one of the major threats to the crucian carp. Pond management aimed at decreasing tree canopy cover may help mitigate this by increasing surface wind movement of duckweed. Given multiple pressures on crucian carp populations throughout its range, we call for more active local-scale conservation projects to help reverse its current decline.

items.title: Quantifying environment-dependent global antibiotic resistance gene risk patterns and mitigation scenarios using integrated machine learning and counterfactual scenario evaluation.
items.abstract: Environmental antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) pose major ecological and public health risks, yet environmentally conditioned risk patterns and mitigation potential remain poorly quantified. This study aimed to characterize global ARG risk patterns, identify associated environmental and agricultural factors, and evaluate potential mitigation scenarios using an integrated machine learning framework. Using 274,382 sample-ARG-environment records and 150 environmental and agricultural variables, quantile models characterized conditional risk index (RI) distributions and upper-tail risks, multi-model analysis assessed predictive variable importance, and DML estimated covariate-adjusted conditional associations. Heterogeneity was assessed across habitats, countries, and ARG categories, followed by directionally constrained counterfactual evaluation of multi-factor mitigation scenarios. Global ARG risk varied strongly with environmental conditions. In predictive importance analyses, winter temperature anomalies, manure nutrient loading, and pesticide application were important for upper-tail RI prediction. Separately, DML identified positive conditional associations of RI with insecticide application, cropland nutrient surplus, and manure loading, and negative associations with nutrient use efficiency. These associations varied across habitats, particularly soil, crop roots, freshwater, and biological waste environments. Under a predefined 50% predicted RI reduction target, nine-factor adjustment reduced mean standardized adjustment distance by 69.1% relative to single-factor adjustment, although outcomes varied among ARG categories. These model-based findings support global ARG risk characterization and management prioritization within the One Health framework, subject to empirical validation.

items.title: A qualitative exploratory study of pathways to moral repair and moral injury in U.S. veterans.
items.abstract: Objective Potentially morally injurious events (PMIEs) are situations in which individuals perpetrate, fail to prevent, witness, or are directly impacted by actions that violate deeply held moral beliefs. Approximately half of U.S. veterans endorse PMIE exposure, and about 13% of those exposed meet criteria for probable moral injury, a syndrome of functionally impairing moral emotions, beliefs, and social behavior indexed to one's worst and most distressing PMIE. Little is known about why some individuals recover following PMIE exposure whereas others experience enduring impairment. Method This qualitative study examined psychological, social, and institutional processes that differentiate veterans with probable moral injury from PMIE-exposed noncases. In-depth interviews were conducted with 39 veterans (20 cases, 19 noncases) sampled from a nationally representative study. Applied thematic analysis was used to identify cross-cutting themes and compare trajectories across groups. Results Cases and noncases described similar acute moral distress, but their reported experiences diverged over time. Six overarching themes emerged the following: (a) a widening experiential gap characterized by identity disruption, moral emotions, and functional impairment among cases; (b) early emotional and behavioral responses that shaped trajectories; (c) the central role of social ecology in maintaining or eroding belonging; (d) divergent moral emotion trajectories (i.e., shame, guilt, anger) among cases; (e) meaning-making and repair processes facilitated recovery; and (f) the influence of leadership and institutional betrayal in exacerbating impairment. Conclusions These findings offer empirical support for key components of the social-functional model of moral injury, while generating hypotheses that highlight potential targets for prevention, mitigation, and treatment. items.title: Food waste to biomass approach: A sustainable strategy for the production of alternative microbial culture media for filamentous fungi growth.
items.abstract: The valorization of organic waste is still one of the challenges in the path towards environmental sustainability and a circular bioeconomy. This research aimed at assessing the ability of three substrates of organic residues (olive pomace, potato peels and the green seaweed Ulva lactuca) to be used as alternative culture media for filamentous fungi. Mycelial growth on these media was compared with the conventional Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) and Sabouraud media using three fungal species namely Fusarium oxysporum (F1), Fusarium solani (F2) and Alternaria alternata (N2) as biological models. The alternative media were made from waste materials, supplemented or not with glucose, and sterilized prior to the use. The measurements of mycelial growth were taken every day for 8 days and the data analyzed by multi-factorial ANOVA. Mycelial growth in all the waste-based media was found to be comparable to commercial media. Highest overall growth was seen in commercial PDA and Sabouraud media (19.9% and 19.3%) respectively. The glucose enriched formulations showed 13.2% (olive pomace) and 11.0% (potato peel) rich media with the remaining media showing less. The percentages of olive pomace, potato peels and U. lactuca were 12.9%, 9.3% and 1.2%, respectively, without the addition of glucose. Growth was significantly higher with glucose supplementation, showing the beneficial effect of the exogenous C supply and intrinsic nutritional value of the substrates. ANOVA revealed that incubation time and medium type significantly influenced mycelial growth across all three strains (p < 2.2 × 10-16), with significant interactions between medium and time (F1: F = 3.91, p = 6.08 × 10-10, F2: F = 163.31, p < 2 × 10-16, N2: F = 44.30, p < 2 × 10-16). The overall analysis of the three strains also indicated highly significant main effect for strain (F = 645.22) and incubation time (F = 391.95) as well as highly significant main effect for culture medium (F = 44.18) (all p < 2.2 × 10-16). Variations in texture and color that can be seen in the different media, however, may influence the macroscopic appearance of the mycelium and identification. Hence, these alternative media are recommended for post identification, subculture and preservation of fungal strains especially.

items.title: Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error.
items.abstract: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun's arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters ( Puffinus puffinus ) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

items.title: Three new species in Lentistoma, Neolindgomyces, and Ophiocreas from freshwater habitats.
items.abstract: During a survey of saprobic fungi in Jiangxi and Zhejiang provinces, China, three fungal species were collected from decaying wood samples in freshwater habitats. We selected the internal transcribed spacers (ITS1-5.8S-ITS2), large subunit (28S ribosomal RNA), small subunit (18S ribosomal RNA), translation elongation factor 1-alpha ( tef1 ), RNA polymerase II largest subunit ( rpb1 ), and RNA polymerase II second-largest subunit ( rpb2 ) genes for phylogenetic analyses. Maximum likelihood and Bayesian analyses were performed to clarify the phylogenetic affinities of the species. These species are separated from the other species in respective genera based on dimensions in ascomata, asci, and ascospores and DNA sequence data. Based on morphology and multilocus phylogenetic analysis, these species were confirmed as three new species and were named Lentistoma multiseptata, Neolindgomyces aquaticus , and Ophioceras jiangshanense . Newly added species are compared with other similar species, and comprehensive descriptions and micrographs are provided.

items.title: Soil texture and depth differentially regulate total and available nutrient stoichiometry in Yilong Lake basin agroecosystem, China.
items.abstract: The stoichiometric ratios of soil available nutrients serve as a pivotal indicator for assessing the sustainability of farmland and nutrient cycling efficiency within fragile ecosystems. Soil texture and depth are significant factors influencing nutrient availability, however, their regulatory mechanisms within highland lakeshore agricultural systems remain poorly understood. This study, conducted in the Yilong Lake watershed of the low-latitude plateau in southwest China, collected 216 soil samples. It innovatively determined both total organic carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus (SOC, TN, TP) and available carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus (DOC, AN, AP) simultaneously. Path analysis was employed to examine the direct and indirect associations between soil texture (Clay, Loam, Clay Loam, Sand) and depth (0-20 cm, 20-40 cm, 40-60 cm) on nutrient ratio measurements. Findings indicate: (1) Distinct nutrient limitation and leaching risk patterns emerged across soil textures: Loam exhibited strongest carbon and nitrogen sequestration capacity; Although Clay Loam exhibits reduced phosphorus availability due to iron and aluminium oxide immobilisation, it demonstrates pronounced nitrogen limitation rather than phosphorus limitation; Sand though rich in available phosphorus, had the lowest C:N, suggesting heightened carbon and nitrogen leaching risks. (2) Soil depth significantly altered nutrient ratios: topsoil (0-20 cm) showed marked nutrient enrichment, while subsoil (40-60 cm) exhibited elevated TN:TP, suggesting that nitrification may have intensified with increasing depth. (3) Path analysis revealed that texture directly regulates nutrient measurement ratios (DOC:AN) and indirectly governs C:N:P balance by influencing SOC, AP, and AN content; depth directly or indirectly affects measurement relationships through pathways such as TP. This study elucidates the key regulatory roles of soil texture and depth in nutrient ratios, particularly available nutrient balance, providing direct scientific evidence for implementing differentiated, precision nutrient management based on soil physical properties in Yilong Lake basin agroecosystems and other ecologically fragile areas.

items.title: Global bee bioregions mirror those of other taxa despite a uniquely bimodal latitudinal diversity gradient.
items.abstract: Bioregionalization, the partitioning of the globe into areas of biotic similarity, is one of nature's most striking patterns, and highly congruent boundaries have been identified across plants, tetrapods, ants, and butterflies. However, these taxa also share a unimodal latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG), raising the question of whether bioregionalization and the LDG are mechanistically coupled or instead arise from largely independent processes acting on different timescales. Bees (Hymenoptera: Anthophila) provide a natural test, their diversity peaking at mid-latitudes rather than in the tropics. Using range estimates for 3,370 species and a phylogenetic beta-diversity framework, we recover 21 bee bioregions nested within at least six major realms (Australasia, Indomalaya-Oceania, Nearctic, Neotropics, Palearctic, and Sub-Sahara) that closely align with those of other taxa despite bees' atypical diversity gradient. We propose that bioregionalization and species richness are decoupled because they arise from distinct processes: the former reflects historical dispersal and evolutionary history, the latter local diversification, extinction, and environmental filtering. Our analysis provides a global biogeographic framework for future bee research and highlights the processes shaping the world's major biogeographic boundaries.

items.title: Hydration at the base of the mantle transition zone by ancient subductions in Asia.
items.abstract: Whether and how the subduction processes result in water enrichment at the base of the mantle transition zone (MTZ) remain elusive. The major orogenic belts of the Asian continent, including the Central Asian, Tethyan, and Alpine-Himalayan belts, which record extensive subduction processes, offer an ideal target to address the hydration of the MTZ and its relationship with subduction. Here, we map water content at the MTZ base by combining mineral physics constraints on hydrous pyrolite and global seismic observations of velocity structure and 660-km discontinuity topography. Our results indicate an average global water content of approximately 0.14 wt%, with pronounced hydration anomalies in parts of Asia. Linking these anomalies with reconstructions of past subduction events since 410 Ma reveals extensive water delivery to the MTZ, particularly beneath parts of the Mongol-Okhotsk suture zone, the Central Asian Orogenic Belt, and the Tethyan orogenic domain, where water content exceeds 0.5 wt%. These results connect ancient subduction history to present-day mantle hydration, offering insights into Earth's deep water cycle.

items.title: Fast and efficient sexing of fifty parrot species with high-resolution melting analysis using feather lysate.
items.abstract: Background Because parrots (Psittaciformes) are morphologically monomorphic and conventional genetic assays have limitations, molecular sex determination remains challenging. Methods and results In this study, we developed a rapid and cost-effective high-throughput approach using high-resolution melting (HRM) combined with the amplification of crude DNA for sex identification across 50 parrot species from different genera. The dilution reagent HotSHOT buffer + Proteinase K was chosen to release crude DNA from feather samples, eliminating the extensive steps of DNA extraction. Six different assays were evaluated: P8/P2, P8/P9, P8/P2 + LPAR1, P8/P9 + LPAR1, F2/P2 + LPAR1, and F2/P9 + LPAR1. The F2 (W-specific) and P9 (ZW-specific) primers were newly designed, while all primer combinations targeted CHD1 and LPAR1 loci for discriminatory performance. HRM analysis generated distinct and reproducible sex-specific normalized fluorescence curves, difference curves, and derivative melting curves across diverse psittacine taxa. Amongst the assays, F2/P2 + LPAR1 and F2/P9 + LPAR1 showed highly reliable discrimination in 49/50 species, with F2/P9 + LPAR1 displaying clearly distant peaks diagnostic of CHD1-Z and CHD1-W amplicons. In contrast, the classical CHD1 primer sets demonstrated limited resolution in different taxa. Although minor adjustments to the HRM threshold and normalization parameters were required for optimal visualization in some species, the results remained reproducible. Conclusions High-resolution melting combined with direct real-time PCR significantly reduced the processing time and complexity of laboratory procedures, rendering it an efficient and reliable approach for large-scale bird sexing.

items.title: Microbial profiling of Drosophila in French Guiana reveals candidate microbial taxa associated with native and invasive host.
items.abstract: Invasive alien species (IAS) threaten biodiversity, human health, and economies, yet host-associated microbiome differences between invasive and native species remain poorly understood in natural systems. We investigated bacterial and fungal microbiomes of IAS and native Drosophila species collected along an anthropisation gradient in French Guiana. IAS occurrence declined strongly from coastal anthropised habitats toward rainforest localities. Using bacterial 16S rRNA and fungal ITS metabarcoding of pooled flies, we assessed microbial diversity and community structure across host species, host category (invasive vs. native), and locality. IAS-associated bacterial communities showed reduced alpha diversity and differed in structure from those of native Drosophila. Bacteriome variation was also associated with host phylogeny and locality; because host category was partially confounded with these factors, differences cannot be attributed solely to invasion status. Fungal communities were primarily associated with locality and host species. We further identified core and exclusive taxa and compared bacteriome composition with global reference datasets and microbiome literature, identifying bacterial and fungal taxa preferentially or exclusively associated with invasive or native hosts. Overall, our study characterises microbiome variation between invasive and native Drosophila in French Guiana and identifies candidate taxa for future functional investigation.

items.title: Genetic profiling via a novel PCR-RFLP method enabled identification of four genera of anaerobic gut fungi isolated from nyala, giraffe, and zebra hosts.
items.abstract: Herbivore gut microbiomes may contain a diversity of anaerobic gut fungi (AGF, phylum Neocallimastigomycota), important for fibre degradation. To perform functional studies and elucidate niches of AGF species, fungal isolates must be obtained into axenic culture, which is a resource-intensive process. Here we leverage the integration of morphological and functional assessments of AGF isolates with a newly developed PCR-RFLP strategy, to prioritise isolates of interest from faecal samples from zoo-housed animals for characterisation and confirmatory ITS or LSU sequencing. In silico prediction of PCR-RFLP profiles of cultured genera, followed by experimental validation, confirmed that LSU-based PCR-RFLP with AluI and Hyp188I digestion effectively identified fungi of distinct genera. Together our workflow resulted in isolation of a so far uncultured Piromyces (NY08) species and Neocallimastix cameroonii from nyala samples, as well as Feramyces austinii from giraffe and Khoyollomyces ramosus from zebra. Amplicon sequencing confirmed these species dominated AGF communities in their hosts, likely benefiting isolation success, and we identified enrichment conditions which also affected cultivability. The workflow developed here aids efficient AGF isolations, which are instrumental in expanding opportunities for functional studies that provide insight into the physiology and ecology of these fungi and help realise applications in white and green biotechnology.

items.title: The RNA virome of intertidal kelp in New Zealand reveals novel viral lineages associated with unhealthy kelp.
items.abstract: Pathogens can have major impacts on ecosystem function, especially when they infect foundational taxa such as habitat-forming kelp. Understanding which potentially pathogenic microbes are in an ecosystem is increasingly important as environmental change intensifies ecosystem imbalances, yet few studies have examined which viruses are associated with key habitat-forming macroalgae. Here, we screened multiple populations of intertidal / shallow-subtidal macroalgae in New Zealand for viruses. Samples were collected from three southern bull kelp species: Durvillaea antarctica, Durvillaea poha and Durvillaea willana. Total RNA was extracted and sequenced from both obviously 'unhealthy' kelp tissue and apparently 'healthy' tissue. We identified putative novel viral lineages belonging to the families Mitoviridae, Narnaviridae, Partitiviridae, Totiviridae, and the recently proposed Ormycovirus group. Viral abundance and diversity were notably higher at Lawyers Head (the site closest to a city) compared to other sites, especially in unhealthy kelp samples. The elevated viral presence at Lawyers Head may indicate that human impacts, such as pollution, are influencing viral prevalence. This study reveals that coastal macroalgae in New Zealand host diverse viral lineages, some likely pathogenic, and hints at the potential influence of anthropogenic pollution on marine virome composition.

items.title: Stable isotopes indicate consistent trophic structures but marked spatial variation in isotopic values across contrasting high-altitude Andean salars.
items.abstract: High-altitude Andean salars are poly-extreme wetlands that support communities dominated by microorganisms and important populations of flamingos. Much of the work on these systems has focused on microbial community composition and function, but little is known regarding their trophic ecology. We evaluated the use of stable isotopes to compare food web organisation and consumption pathways in three contrasting Andean salars. We analysed δ 13 C, δ 15 N and δ 34 S of primary producers, aquatic invertebrates and flamingos (feathers and faeces) in Laguna Puilar (Salar de Atacama), Salar de Tara and Salar de Pujsa. We quantified the isotopic niche volume and overlap between trophic components and used Bayesian mixing models to estimate the relative contribution of putative prey resources to flamingo diet. The trophic organisation was quite similar among the salars, however, the relative size of community and consumer isotopic niches differed markedly. At Puilar and Tara, most invertebrate niches were narrow and largely nested within the isotopic space occupied by flamingos, suggesting restricted resource use and limited dispersion in three-isotope space. In contrast, Pujsa showed a broader and more heterogeneous occupation of isotopic space among consumer taxa. Mixing models indicated that one or two dominant groups of aquatic invertebrates, together with diatoms, contributed substantially to the flamingos' diet, consistent with previous studies. The isotopic values of the feathers showed high variability, consistent with integration between multiple wetlands and, potentially, multiple species of flamingos, rather than simple local trophic generalism. Despite limitations related to the inability to assign feathers to specific species and incomplete coverage of meiofauna, the triple isotope approaches provided robust information on dominant energy sources and revealed local 'trophic identities' among salars. Stable isotopes therefore offer a non-invasive and effective framework for monitoring trophic structure in remote and difficult to study Andean salars under increasing anthropogenic pressure.

items.title: Preferences for Mental Health Interventions Among Farming Family Members.
items.abstract: Background Farming populations experience mental health difficulties at a higher rate than the general population. Farming family members are likely to face similar challenges given the structural absence of separation between home, workplace and family business; yet the specific intervention preferences of farming family members as a distinct group remain largely understudied. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted online with 16 Irish farming family members (4 male, 12 female; mean age 47.9 ± 17.2 years), and five focus groups were held with 16 key stakeholders (14 male, 2 female; mean age 44.8 ± 13.8 years) from Irish farming and rural organisations. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Four themes were identified: Farm-Centric Facilitators; Preferred Execution and Delivery; Content Preferences; and Challenges to Execution. Participants consistently emphasised the importance of embedding interventions within trusted farming organisations and community structures. Sessions were preferred during quieter farming periods, using informal, conversation-based formats, and delivered by facilitators with dual competency in both mental health and farming. Content priorities centred on increasing mental health literacy, normalising everyday emotional distress, and improving awareness of available supports. Stigma and the hard-to-reach nature of the population were identified as the primary implementation challenges. Conclusions Effective interventions for farming families should be community-embedded, practically flexible, and culturally grounded in agricultural life. Increasing mental health literacy and reducing stigma are critical components. These findings are interpreted through the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) and Medical Research Council (MRC) guidelines for complex interventions to inform future intervention development.

items.title: Gel-Free Capture of Microvolt-Level Neural Signatures Via a 3D Monolithic Carbon Fiber Dry Electrode.
items.abstract: Gel-based wet electrodes remain the gold standard for electrophysiology, but gel dehydration limits recordings. Existing dry electrodes partially address this limitation but suffer from high interfacial impedance. Here, a carbon fiber-based porous electrode (CFPE) is reported, comprising a three-dimensional conductive network coated with poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS). The CFPE establishes contact at hairy-scalp sites with an impedance of approximately 10 kΩ·cm 2 . On the forearm, its impedance at 10 Hz without skin preparation is 11.09 ± 1.03 kΩ·cm 2 , compared with 13.57 ± 2.07 kΩ·cm 2 for wet electrodes. After 6 h of wear, CFPE impedance reaches 1.3 times its initial value without skin preparation or gel, whereas wet-electrode impedance reaches 56 times its initial value when applied with skin preparation and conductive gel. High-fidelity electrocardiography, electromyography, and electroencephalography signals are captured with correlation coefficients exceeding 90% and signal-to-noise ratios comparable to wet electrodes. The CFPE further resolves microvolt-level speech-evoked frequency-following responses (FFR) and long-latency responses (LLR), with fidelity comparable to wet electrodes and significantly higher LLR SNR. These results demonstrate gel-free acquisition of weak neural biomarkers, opening a pathway toward prolonged, preparation-free neurophysiology.

items.title: Traumatic brain injury history moderates age-related episodic memory change in older veterans: the DOD-ADNI longitudinal cohort study.
items.abstract: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) has been associated with increased risk of dementia and cognitive decline, but its relationship with age-related cognitive trajectories remains unclear. This study examined associations between TBI history and age-related changes in cognitive function in aging military veterans. Methods Data from the Department of Defense-Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (DOD-ADNI) repository were used to evaluate whether TBI history moderates the relationship between age and longitudinal change in domain-specific cognitive performance. To investigate these relationships, this study utilized data from neuropsychological assessments collected at baseline and 12-month timepoints from a sample consisting of 203 Vietnam War veterans, 99% of whom were male, aged 60-84 years, with varying TBI histories. Results Results revealed that TBI history moderated the association between age and change in episodic memory. Older age was associated with greater memory decline among individuals with TBI. No interaction effects were observed for executive functions or language. Conclusions These findings suggest that TBI history is associated with differences in age-related episodic memory change and highlight the importance of considering TBI history in studies of cognitive aging. Considering the modest proportion of variance explained by the interaction and homogeneous veteran sample, additional research is warranted.
