items.title: Adaptive driving, not unsafe: Older drivers' compensatory strategies and lower simulated crash risk.
items.abstract: Objectives The global aging population has led to an increasing number of older active drivers. While age-related physical and cognitive changes are associated with increased crash risk, specific on-road adaptations and safety outcomes of older drivers remain unclear. This study examined distinct driving characteristics, personality traits, and cognitive processes related to decision-making among middle-aged and older drivers in a simulated driving environment. Methods We assessed driving performance in a high-fidelity motorcycle simulator across drivers in three age groups: middle-aged (30-54; n = 40), aged 65-74 (n = 34), and aged 75 + (75-86; n = 29). Comparative analysis focused on speed regulation, braking behavior, control stability, and accident rates. Additionally, questionnaire measures and a computerized decision-making task were employed to assess risk perception and risky decision-making. Results Compared to the middle-aged group, both older groups demonstrated a significantly more conservative driving profile: lower mean speeds, fewer speeding violations, longer braking maneuvers, reduced variation in throttle control, and a lower incidence of simulated accidents. Drivers aged 75+ also reported higher perceived risk in driving scenarios and displayed diminished discrimination between risk and non-risk situations in a braking decision task. Mediation analyses showed that steering variance in the simulator and self-reported health/safety risk-taking significantly mediated the relationship between age group and number of accidents. Discussion The findings indicate that older drivers adopt proactive compensatory strategies that could result in fewer simulated accidents. These findings challenge a purely deficit-oriented perspective on older driver safety, underscoring the critical role of behavioral adaptation and strategic self-regulation in maintaining safe mobility.

items.title: Overall, emotional and social loneliness and their associated factors: a large-scale cross-sectional study of young and middle-aged adults in Germany.
items.abstract: Background Loneliness is increasingly recognized as a major public health concern, yet little is known about the distinct patterns and associated factors of emotional and social loneliness during young and middle adulthood. This study examined age-related differences in overall, emotional, and social loneliness and associated sociodemographic, social, health-related, and personality factors among adults in Germany. Methods We analysed nationally representative data from the German Family Demography Panel Study (FReDA), including 14,443 adults aged 18 to 51 years. Loneliness was assessed using the validated De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Short Scale, distinguishing overall, emotional, and social loneliness. Multivariable regression models examined associations with sociodemographic, social, health-related, and personality factors. Analyses were stratified by age and gender. Results High levels of loneliness were common, with 24.3% of participants reporting intense emotional loneliness, 29.6% intense overall loneliness, and 35.8% intense social loneliness. Overall loneliness remained relatively stable across age groups. In contrast, emotional loneliness was lower in older age groups, while social loneliness was higher. Social relationships showed some of the strongest associations with loneliness, particularly social loneliness: discussing personal matters within one's social network (β = -0.32, 95% CI -0.37 to -0.28) and having a partner (β = -0.21, 95% CI -0.26 to -0.16) were associated with lower social loneliness, while first-generation migration background was associated with higher social loneliness (β = 0.31, 95% CI 0.24 to 0.38). Mental health burdens were consistently associated with higher loneliness, especially emotional loneliness, with depressed mood showing the strongest association (β = 0.22, 95% CI 0.17 to 0.27). Among personality traits, agreeableness was associated with lower social loneliness (β = -0.19, 95% CI -0.22 to -0.17), whereas neuroticism was associated with higher emotional loneliness (β = 0.17, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.20). Gender differences were generally small, as were associations with physical health conditions. Conclusions Loneliness in young and middle adulthood is multidimensional, with emotional and social loneliness showing distinct age-related patterns and associated factors. Social relationships showed some of the strongest associations with lower loneliness, while mental health burdens and first-generation migration background were associated with higher loneliness. Public health strategies may benefit from considering different loneliness dimensions and psychosocial contexts.

items.title: Digital Beautification and Attractiveness Perception: Female Faces Gain Greater Advantages, but Familiarity Attenuates Gender Differences.
items.abstract: Appearance significantly impacts social and evolutionary contexts, with women's facial attractiveness often being more influential. However, it remains unclear whether methods of appearance enhancement, such as makeup or digital beautification, affect perceptions of facial attractiveness differently across genders. Digital facial beautification is now widespread among both genders, allowing for meaningful cross-gender comparisons. This study employed an attractiveness rating task to examine how beautification affects unfamiliar (Experiments 1 & 2) and familiar (Experiment 2) female and male faces. The results showed: (1) For unfamiliar faces, beautification significantly enhanced attractiveness, showing a stronger effect on female faces compared to male faces; (2) For familiar faces, beautification also increased attractiveness, but the gender difference in the enhancement effect disappeared. Beautification thus has a more pronounced impact on unfamiliar female than male faces, but familiarity diminishes these gender disparities. It highlights that individuals are more sensitive to changes in attractiveness for female faces, and women benefit more from modifications to their appearance. This study reveals gender-differentiated effects of digital beautification on facial attractiveness and how familiarity moderates them, while also clarifying how widely used beautification technologies shape social impressions in everyday digital contexts.

items.title: Transdiagnostic Factors Influencing Job Tenure in People Living with Mental Disorders: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Purpose Studying mental health in the context of employment often focuses on individual disorders, potentially overlooking underlying commonalities across different diagnoses. A transdiagnostic perspective recognizes that certain aspects of job tenure may have broad-reaching implications for employability services that cut across multiple mental disorders. This scoping review seeks to identify common factors influencing job tenure in people living with mental disorders using a transdiagnostic approach. Methods The study protocol followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines and was registered on the Open Science Framework platform ( https://osf.io/rp97e/ ). The search strategy was completed in November 2025 and involved searches in 7 databases. Results A total of 9715 abstracts were uploaded to Covidence for screening. This scoping review included 110 studies and identified 17 factors influencing job tenure categorized based on modifiability and stakeholder responsibility, as follows-Entrusted to workplace stakeholders (1) workplace characteristics and working conditions, (2) psychosocial work environment, (3) informal support and perceptions; Entrusted to the individual and their support teams (4) psychological, social and practical characteristics, (5) receiving employment support, (6) psychiatric diagnosis, clinical symptoms and functioning, (7) support from relatives and broader social networks, (8) receiving therapy and counseling services, (9) daily functioning; Shared responsibilities (10) collaboration between all stakeholders, (11) disclosure of mental illness in the workplace, (12) motivation, (13) person-job fit, (14) work-life balance, (15) financial assistance during sick leave; Immutable factors (16) sociodemographic characteristics, (17) work and education history. Conclusion Findings support role clarification for stakeholders and guide service organization to improve job tenure across diverse mental disorders.

items.title: Psychoanalysis and Critical Social Justice.
items.abstract: Culture wars in Western society have entered the academy and are affecting the integrity of mental health professions by introducing identity politics in education, training, and public policy in the name of social justice. What seems like a righteous, ethical endeavor is in fact a harmful and destabilizing movement that aims to displace established psychological and psychotherapeutic paradigms that have their origins in psychoanalysis. Such political divisiveness introduces a real threat to humanitarian egalitarian principles that have traditionally informed psychoanalytic praxis based on apolitical commitments of care to all peoples regardless of their personal and cultural identities or past collective suffering. A return to professional civility, prudence, and therapeutic integrity requires an apolitical philosophy that stays focused on our universal humanistic obligations.

items.title: A continuous appraisal account of gratitude dynamics in social interactions.
items.abstract: Gratitude is a fundamental social emotion for interpersonal interaction. Previous studies have identified appraisals of benefactor's behavior and intention, and recipient's benefit as crucial determinants of interpersonal gratitude. However, they largely ignored the continuous appraisal nature of gratitude and left unclear how integrative evaluation of different determinants unfold when a beneficial outcome is not guaranteed. Here we developed an interpersonal interactive paradigm and asked participants to report their feelings at different appraisal stages of the interaction. In Experiment 1 (N = 52 participants), we demonstrated that this paradigm could effectively capture interactions between appraisals of benefactors' behavior and intention, and appraisals of recipients' benefit. In Experiment 2 (Experiment 2a: N = 61; Experiment 2b: N = 150; Experiment 2c: N = 72), we examined the continuous appraisal processes by showing that benefactors' help could substantially elicit recipients' gratitude without the evaluation of benefit, and that the outcome of help decision further interacts with the initial decision to affect recipients' gratitude towards benefactors. In Experiment 3 (Experiment 3a: N = 62; Experiment 3b: N = 150), we generalized the continuous appraisal approach to a more sophisticated context and examined the impact of help efficacy (helpful vs. useless vs. harmful help) on gratitude. Our findings suggest that benefactors' decision to help can elicit gratitude without outcome evaluation, the outcome that is decisively determined by benefactors' help has a strong effect on gratitude, and the outcome that is not directly affected by the help could nevertheless promote or dampen gratitude. Together, the current study advances our understandings of integrative evaluation of different determinants underlying interpersonal gratitude via a continuous appraisal framework.

items.title: A thematic analysis of how young professionals, aged 26 to 35, switch off and unwind from work.
items.abstract: BackgroundRecent research indicates that work-related affective rumination peaks among women aged 26 to 35 and subsequently remains elevated relative to men, representing a significant long-term health concern.ObjectiveThis study explored how young professionals, aged 26 to 35, psychologically detach from work.MethodsSemi-structured interviews were conducted with 18 participants, focusing on job demands, leisure activities, unwinding practices, and experiences of work-related thoughts outside of work. Transcripts were analysed using thematic analysis.ResultsThree superordinate themes emerged: 'Perspectives on work-life balance', 'Ability to switch off', and 'Techniques for switching off'. Participants reported similarly high-demand roles, limited detachment, and shared unwinding strategies; however, gender differences emerged in emotional responses and boundary-setting. Women reported greater emotional strain, perfectionism, and a need to legitimise leaving work on time, whereas men viewed rumination as productive and expressed little need to switch off. Interpersonal relationships and a lack of external responsibilities also shaped detachment experiences.ConclusionThe study highlights the need for person-centred interventions to support psychological disengagement in young professionals so that sustainable healthy work habits are established.

items.title: Mate preferences and the compatibility puzzle.
items.abstract: Researchers and laypeople commonly assume that romantic attraction depends, at least in part, on whether potential partners possess the traits that a person says they want. Yet recent studies suggest that such preference-matching effects (Preference × Trait statistical interactions) are often surprisingly small or even absent. Possible psychological explanations include (i) mate choice is multivariate, and so the matching effect for any given trait is heavily constrained, and (ii) traits permit flexible interpretations, in that the same trait can be interpreted differently depending on the partner to whom the trait belongs. Compatibility may derive not mainly from the matching of preferences and traits but rather from the way that two people recurrently extend and build upon shared positive experiences over time.

items.title: Reconstructing narrative coherence through podcasting after prolonged combat.
items.abstract: Prolonged combat can disrupt individuals' ability to organize experience into a coherent life narrative. Senior combat officers face distinctive demands, regulating their own emotions while leading others and making morally consequential decisions under sustained threat, often leaving wartime memories fragmented. This study examines how senior combat officers describe and attribute meaning to their participation in podcast conversations following prolonged military service. Fourteen senior combat officers from an Israeli reserve brigade, each with more than 400 reserve days since the October 7, 2023 war at the time of recording, recorded podcast episodes individually or with fellow officers and completed a brief post-recording questionnaire. Ten subsequently took part in in-depth follow-up interviews, which were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants characterized podcasting as a dialogical space in which unprocessed experiences could be articulated, organized, and reinterpreted. They recounted re-engaging with painful memories, reorganizing fragmented recollections into more coherent narratives, and renegotiating their identities as military leaders. They also described deliberately postponing emotional processing during combat to sustain leadership, with the podcast experienced as a later opportunity for reflection and bearing witness. Participants did not experience podcasting as therapy but as a culturally legitimate reflective practice. The study conceptualizes podcasting as a dialogical narrative practice through which, in participants' accounts, fragmented combat experiences took shape as coherent narratives; read through a post-traumatic growth lens, these processes may be associated with growth following prolonged combat.

items.title: Early intervention group therapy for hoarding in college students: A pilot study.
items.abstract: Despite the growing body of work to develop and evaluate treatments for hoarding disorder, no research has sought to therapeutically address the full scope of hoarding symptoms in an early intervention. The present study piloted two iterations of a cognitive-behavioral group therapy early intervention for college students with elevated hoarding symptoms, collecting preliminary feasibility, acceptability, and outcome data. Across an eight-session intervention program, participants ( N = 4) reported substantial decreases in saving cognitions ( t [3] = 3.86, p = .031) and clutter ( t [3] = 3.77, p = .033), with 75% reporting clinically reliable change in overall hoarding symptoms. Although all treatment-completing participants rated the protocol as acceptable, 60% ( n = 6) of participants assessed at baseline either dropped out ( n = 3), were excluded ( n = 2), or discontinued the intervention ( n = 1); additionally, each group experienced three session delays, each of which delayed the next session by 5.33 days on average (SD = 1.51), suggesting that additional research is needed to understand barriers to implementation of early intervention for hoarding in a college setting.

items.title: PPAR-γ/SGK1/GSK3β/Nrf2 signaling pathway contributes to the neuroprotective effects of lycopene in depressed mice.
items.abstract: Introduction Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a neuropsychiatric disorder associated with abnormal neuronal activity in specific brain regions. Recent evidence suggests that oxidative stress- and neuroinflammation-driven impairments in synaptic structure and neuronal function may contribute to depression, yet the precise mechanisms remain unclear. Lycopene (LYC) is a lipophilic dietary carotenoid that exhibits strong neuroprotective and antioxidant properties. Objectives Here, we report that LYC alleviates chronic stress-induced neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired synaptic transmission by activating the PPAR-γ/SGK1/p-GSK3β/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway. Methods and results Integrated transcriptomic and network pharmacology analyses prioritized PPAR-γ as a potential target of LYC. Moreover, pharmacological activation of PPAR-γ induced LYC-like effects by alleviating chronic stress-induced behavioral deficiency, oxidative stress and neuroinflammation, whereas CA1-local inhibition of PPAR-γ weakened LYC-mediated neuroprotection effects. Electrophysiological data further suggest that chronic stress weakened synaptic transmission and excitability in CA1 pyramidal neurons, while LYC improved the neuronal dysfunction through a PPAR-γ/SGK1/p-GSK3β/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that LYC activates the PPAR-γ/SGK1/p-GSK3β/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway to alleviate chronic stress-induced oxidative stress and neuroinflammation, thereby improving neuroplasticity and protecting against stress-related depression.

items.title: Association of maternal adverse childhood experiences with inflammatory and growth factor pathway activity during pregnancy: a cross-sectional proteomics-based KEGG pathway analysis in the ECHO cohort.
items.abstract: While maternal histories of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) have been linked to altered immune signaling during pregnancy, the specific inflammatory pathways underlying these associations remain poorly characterized. We leveraged high-dimensional proteomics to examine associations between maternal ACEs and pregnancy-associated inflammatory signaling pathways defined by the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) and tested whether these associations were moderated by neighborhood-level social vulnerability during pregnancy. Participants included pregnant individuals enrolled in the Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Cohort (N = 770). Circulating inflammatory proteins were assayed from maternal plasma using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Protein markers were mapped to Human Genome Organisation (HUGO) Gene Nomenclature Committee gene symbols and aggregated into KEGG pathway scores using curated definitions. Linear regression models evaluated associations between continuous maternal ACE scores and each pathway score. Following correction for multiple comparisons, higher maternal ACE exposure was associated with higher activity across 12 KEGG-annotated protein pathways, including AGE-RAGE, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, chemokine, Th17 differentiation, HIF-1, cellular senescence, Rap1, NOD-like receptor signaling, transcriptional misregulation in cancer, and infection-related pathway signaling. Domain-specific analyses identified the most consistent associations for childhood household dysfunction. Neighborhood-level social vulnerability during pregnancy did not moderate ACE-inflammation associations but was independently associated with higher KSHV infection and NOD-like receptor signaling pathway scores. Together, these findings indicate that maternal ACEs and prenatal social vulnerability are independently associated with small, but directionally consistent, differences in overlapping inflammatory and growth-related protein signals during pregnancy.

items.title: Does Phubbing Always Elicit Social Pain? The Role of Belonging Context.
items.abstract: Phubbing, a prevalent interpersonal phenomenon in which individuals divert their attention to their phones while neglecting their interaction partners during face-to-face interactions, has been associated with adverse psychological and relational outcomes, including social pain. However, the same "eyes-on-phone" behavior may not always be experienced as phubbing or evoke feelings of neglect and social pain. The present research examined whether belonging context shapes behavioral and neural responses to "eyes-on-phone" behavior during face-to-face interaction. In Study 1, 163 participants completed a scenario-based task that required them to judge how they felt about several stories, in which belonging context (positive, negative, unrelated) was crossed with attentional state (eyes-on-phone, eyes-on-you). In Study 2, 50 participants completed the Cyberball paradigm to manipulate different belonging contexts (positive, negative, unrelated) with 6 models, followed by an ERP experiment in which they judged whether images of these models displaying different attentional states (eyes-on-phone, eyes-on-you) made them feel neglect-related social pain. Across both studies, within "positive" contexts, "eyes-on-phone" behavior elicited greater social pain, including perceived neglect, emotional unpleasantness, and unwillingness to communicate (Study 1), as well as a greater tendency to endorse neglect-related social pain and larger P3 amplitudes (Study 2) than "eyes-on-you" behavior, whereas this pattern was not consistently observed in the "negative" or "unrelated" contexts. These findings indicate that phubbing is not inherently experienced as social pain. Rather, its social meaning depends on prior belonging context: a mismatch between contextual cues and subsequent attentional behavior may give rise to expectancy violations, which could contribute to social pain when the behavior is interpreted as neglectful.

items.title: Development and cross-tissue validation of a machine learning-based methylation profile score for the cortisol response to stress.
items.abstract: Background Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis (HPA axis) dysregulation is a risk factor for poor mental and physical health. Animal studies indicate that DNA methylation may regulate the HPA axis, although studies in humans have produced mixed results. A data-driven, machine learning approach may provide new insight. Methods Using a novel machine learning pipeline, we developed a methylation profile score (MPS) to predict the salivary cortisol response (AUCi) to the Trier Social Stress Test (TSST) from whole blood Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation 450 K BeadChip data (N = 84, mean age = 34, 49% female). Results The MPS was associated with the cortisol response in an independent, cross-tissue cohort (N = 53, mean age = 20, 51% female), both before (β = 0.33, 95% CI [0.09, 0.54]) and after a social stressor (β = 0.3, 95% CI [0.09, 0.47]). The effect remained statistically significant after adjusting for age, sex, ethnicity, and smoking, but it became non-significant at the pre-stress (but not post-stress) time point after additional adjustment for cell proportion estimates (pre: β = 0.16, 95% CI [-0.1, 0.47]; post: β = 0.26, 95% CI [0.004, 0.49]). Conclusions We developed a DNA methylation-based score that was associated with the cortisol response to stress in a separate, cross-tissue cohort. The predictive signal may depend, at least in part, on differences in cell composition associated with the phenotype. The methods used in this paper can be adapted and expanded upon in future research developing and testing novel epigenetic scores for complex, stress-related phenotypes.

items.title: Mapping Social-Psychological Factors Associated with Adolescents' Nutritional Habits - A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Adolescence is a formative period for the development of dietary habits, characterized by increasing autonomy in food choices and heightened susceptibility to social influences. Although numerous studies have examined social-psychological determinants of adolescent eating, the evidence remains conceptually, theoretically, and methodologically fragmented. This scoping review mapped social-psychological factors associated with adolescents' nutritional habits and examined the methodological and theoretical characteristics of this research. Following the Participant-Concept-Context framework, Web of Science, PsycINFO, PubMed, and Scopus were systematically searched for peer-reviewed qualitative and quantitative empirical studies published since 2000 involving adolescents aged 10-19 years. A total of 101 studies were included. Social norms, social modeling, peer and family influence, social support, self-efficacy, attitudes, and motivation emerged as prominent determinants of adolescent nutritional habits. Importantly, social influences were not inherently health-promoting or health-decreasing; their effects depended substantially on their behavioral and normative valence. The evidence base was dominated by cross-sectional research, with comparatively few longitudinal, experimental, or intervention studies. Analysis of the theoretical approaches used in the studies revealed that forty-one studies lacked an explicit theoretical foundation, while the extent to which theoretical frameworks informed hypotheses, study design, and interpretation varied considerably across the remaining studies. The mechanisms linking social identity (n = 3) to dietary behavior and the role of developmental differences within adolescence (n = 2) were comparatively underexamined. Based on these findings, we propose an integrative social-psychological framework distinguishing four interrelated levels of influence: individual processes, social identities, interpersonal social processes, and the broader social context, which may support the design of theoretically more informed studies targeting adolescent nutritional behavior.

items.title: Improvement in acuity following motion adaptation: The role of information at different spatial frequencies.
items.abstract: Prolonged exposure (adaptation) to blur, flicker or motion can transiently enhance visual acuity (VA). Such improvement could be linked to decreased contrast sensitivity (CS) for low spatial frequency (SF) image structure. Here, we determine if and why low SFs are required for such acuity improvement following adaptation. We measured CS using SF band-pass filtered optotypes with and without adaptation. We also measured CS for these stimuli in the presence of a SF low-pass fixed-contrast "pedestal". Adaptation to receding motion improves VA for conventional but not vanishing optotypes (which contain little low SF structure), indicating a crucial role for low SFs. Adaptation reduces CS at all SFs (particularly for the lowest SF). In unadapted observers - interestingly, however, CS for higher SF information is always enhanced/facilitated by a low SF pedestal. Therefore, any adaptation-driven suppression of low SFs must improve the discriminability (rather than detection) of high SFs to improve recognition. Using a simple filter-combination model, we show that recognition must be operating on information that has been combined across SFs.

items.title: Cross-linguistic semantic stability as a driving force of diachronic semantic evolution across lexica.
items.abstract: Word meanings change over time, yet the extent of change varies systematically within each lexicon. Although frequency, age of acquisition, and concreteness have been identified as within-language predictors, a language-general account of why some concepts show greater resistance to diachronic semantic change across languages remains elusive. Here, we propose that cross-linguistic semantic stability - the degree to which a concept's semantic neighborhood is conserved across languages - as a concept-level predictor of diachronic semantic change. We operationalized stability as neighborhood overlap between a target concept's nearest neighbors in English and the back-translated neighbors of its translation equivalents across 10 to 41 languages, and quantified diachronic change as neighborhood turnover in historical embeddings spanning up to 100 years in English, French, German, and Chinese. Higher cross-linguistic stability predicted less diachronic semantic change in each language and in an aggregated analysis of concepts shared across the four languages. This effect dominated all other predictors for shared concepts; remained significant after established psycholinguistic predictors were controlled; was represented as a direct conditional edge in partial-correlation networks; remained robust as the cross-linguistically shared concept set was expanded; and was replicated using historically derived stability estimates. Together, these findings reveal the topological consistency of a concept's semantic neighborhood across languages is a temporally durable, concept-level predictor of resistance to semantic change, linking synchronic cross-linguistic conceptual structure with diachronic lexical evolution across lexica.

items.title: General versus specific: Investigating the structure of individual differences in post-error slowing across time.
items.abstract: Erroneous actions are typically followed by behavioral slowing, known as post-error slowing (PES), along with other post-error adjustments. These effects emerge on the first trial following an error and can persist across subsequent trials. While PES has been extensively studied experimentally, less attention has been given to inter-individual variability. Evidence suggests that the mechanisms underlying individual differences in PES are largely domain-general, spanning multiple tasks. However, as time elapses from the point of error, task-specific processes may increasingly influence these individual differences. In this study, we applied latent variable modeling to two large samples of participants who completed three canonical inhibitory control paradigms. Our findings indicate that individual differences in PES reflect both domain-general and task-specific abilities, with the influence of the domain-general factor seeming to decrease over time following error commission.

items.title: The Body Acceptance by Others Scale-2: An examination of its psychometric properties in adults from Greece.
items.abstract: The 13-item Body Acceptance by Others Scale-2 (BAOS-2) measures generalised perceptions of body acceptance by others. Here, we examined the psychometric properties of a novel Greek translation of the BAOS-2. We asked 1009 Greek adults (age range 18-72 years) to complete the BAOS-2, alongside additional validated measures used to assess construct validity. Exploratory factor analysis in a first split-half subsample (n = 505) showed that a unidimensional model with all 13 items had acceptable fit. This model also had acceptable fit when examined using confirmatory factor analysis in a second split-half subsample. Composite reliabilities were adequate in both subsamples (ω = .95) and the unidimensional model evidenced complete measure invariance across subsamples. However, we found evidence of differential item functioning (DIF), with age, body mass index (BMI), and gender identity affecting responding to about half of the items in total. In addition, younger age and higher BMIs were associated with lower body acceptance by others. Our results also supported the convergent (positive associations with body appreciation, negative associations with internalisation of appearance ideals and social appearance anxiety), concurrent (positive associations with self-esteem, compassionate self-responding, and perceived social support), and discriminant validity (weak association with social desirability) of the Greek BAOS-2. Finally, incremental validity was supported insofar as a body acceptance by others predicted body appreciation over-and-above internalisation of appearance ideals. These results suggest that the Greek BAOS-2 had adequate psychometric properties, although future users of this instrument should be cautious about DIF for group-based comparisons.

items.title: Rapid recovery following disruptions in an attention-demanding task.
items.abstract: Previous research demonstrates that people can track multiple moving objects through disruptions, including when all the objects disappear for a brief gap. It seems likely that it takes us time to resume the tracking task after such a gap, and our primary goal in this paper is to measure that time. We refer to it as the recovery time because participants are recovering from the gap. We report five experiments using the multiple object tracking task in which participants tracked a subset of moving identical stimuli through a brief gap. One stimulus was probed at variable delays following reappearance, and we measured reaction time (RT) to identify the probe as a target or distractor. We estimated recovery time using the RT-by-probe delay function, finding a value around 40 ms. To our knowledge, this is the first report measuring this duration. Additionally, we found that the recovery time is consistent across factors that are known to affect the difficulty of tracking and target identification. These findings constrain theories about how the visual system handles gaps in tracking. They also are consistent with the hypothesis that the visual system pauses the tracking task during a gap by storing task-relevant information offline, then reloading it after the gap.

items.title: At the crossroads of change: Executive functions in the age of emerging simulation technology - A scoping review and driving simulator study on adaptive performance.
items.abstract: Simulators are pivotal in advancing mobility technology, yet human adaptation in the context of these technologies remains underexplored. This study investigates the role of core executive functions (working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility) in adaptive performance within driving simulators based on a scoping review identifying a research gap and conducting a driving simulator study addressing it. Results from the empirical study revealed no significant influence of working memory or inhibitory control, while cognitive flexibility showed a partial positive effect, highlighting its possible enhancing role in adapting to coordinative changes within simulated environments. Findings expand the scarce literature and underscore the need for further exploration, e.g., of how change complexity moderates these relationships. By differentiating executive functions and linking them to adaptive performance, this work advances the theoretical understanding of adaptation in the context of emerging technology. Furthermore, it may inform future research on potential training approaches targeting cognitive flexibility.

items.title: Frontal-parietal event related potential correlates of motor planning deficits in children with developmental coordination disorder.
items.abstract: Introduction Imitation and praxis deficits are key characteristics of developmental coordination disorder (DCD). Although behavioral impairments in imitation have been widely studied, less is known about motor preparation and attentional processes underlying thwillese difficulties. This study examined imitation of meaningless gestures to better understand motor planning deficits in children with DCD while controlling for involuntary mirror movements. Method Forty-nine children aged 7-10 years participated (DCD: n = 24; typically developing [TD]: n = 25). Participants performed meaningless hand and finger gestures within a two-step cue-target paradigm designed to assess event-related potentials (ERPs) related to preparatory attention and motor planning. After a visual cue, an imperative stimulus appeared 1100 ms later, prompting response execution. Offline video analysis measured mirror movements-defined as involuntary replication of the target posture in the non-task hand-and imitation errors during unilateral performance. Results Children with DCD showed significantly prolonged ERP latencies during preparatory and motor planning stages compared to TD peers, with no amplitude differences and no group differences in late attention positivity. Behavioral analyses revealed significantly more mirror movements across hand and finger postures in the DCD group (all p ≤ .002). Additionally, left-finger imitation errors were higher in the congruent condition for children with DCD (p Conclusion Children with DCD demonstrate delayed neural processing during motor preparation and planning, indicating temporal inefficiency and impaired interhemispheric motor regulation. Increased mirror movements and imitation errors further reflect difficulties in coordinating voluntary and involuntary motor control.

items.title: The machine between us: How AI shapes the way we speak.
items.abstract: Research increasingly uses voice and audio features to understand human-technology relationships. But findings regarding AI and spoken communication often appear somewhat contradictory. People can be blunt or even aggressive toward chatbots, speak more politely to voice assistants, and self-censor themselves when AI listens in the background during a call. Why? To address this heterogeneity, we propose a Conversational Role Framework that distinguishes whether the AI is (1) a conversation Partner that is directly addressed (e.g., a chatbot), (2) a Filter that transforms speech signals before another person receives it (e.g., a real-time translator that re-voices a speaker), or (3) an Ambient Listener that silently records, transcribes, and summarizes a human exchange (e.g., an AI note-taker summarizing a doctor-patient conversation). This framework helps explain seemingly conflicting findings and sheds light on why the same vocal cue can capture different meanings depending on AI's role in a given interaction.

items.title: Comparing Text-Based and Virtual Reality-Based Approaches for AI-Enhanced Instruction in Functional Communication Training: Exploratory Randomized Trial.
items.abstract: Training practitioners to implement functional communication training (FCT) is resource intensive. Emerging technologies, such as virtual reality (VR) and chatbots, may deliver training at scale. Their comparative effectiveness and whether skills taught in one modality transfer to another remain uncertain. This exploratory study evaluated the effect of multicomponent training packages featuring either VR or a chatbot on (1) posttraining performance on FCT implementation probes administered in both formats and (2) changes in participants' self-perceived knowledge, confidence, and usefulness. A convenience sample of 23 university students (mean age=24 y; 15/23, 65% female) were recruited through classroom announcements and peer referrals. Eligible participants (at least 18 years of age, available to attend trainings, and who had no history of discomfort associated with VR) were randomly assigned to either VR (n=12) or chatbot (n=11) training. Groups did not differ significantly across demographic characteristics. In-person trainings consisted of video-recorded instruction and rehearsal of steps in VR or with the chatbot during a single session. Approximate times of sessions, including tutorials and assessments, were 45 minutes (VR) and 55 minutes (chatbot). All participants' performance on FCT procedures was measured using 2 formats: a VR-based observed mastery probe (OMP) and a text-based probe (TBP). Participants also completed a survey measuring their self-perceptions. The number of FCT steps participants performed correctly (of 18) was analyzed using a binomial generalized linear mixed model, with random intercepts for participant and fixed effects of training group (chatbot vs VR), time (pretest vs posttest), and probe modality (OMP vs TBP); α=.05. Results indicated a main effect of time (odds ratio [OR] 36.09, 95% CI 20.75-62.75; P<.001). A significant 3-way interaction (time × probe modality × training group) indicated that the pattern of skill transfer differed by training condition and probe type (OR 6.10, 95% CI 2.08-17.86; P<.001). At posttest, the chatbot group significantly outperformed the VR group on the TBP (OR 4.14, 95% CI 1.20-14.24; P=.049), completing, on average, 4 more steps in the procedure (average marginal effect 0.22, 95% CI 0.04-0.41). Differences between groups on the OMP were not significant (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.18-2.07; P=.43). Across all self-report measures, there was no differential improvement by training condition at posttest. This study provides the first comparison of chatbot- and VR-based training for FCT. This extends prior work that compared VR against didactic instruction or assessed performance using a single modality. Findings contribute to the field by supporting the viability of text-based chatbots in training and underscoring the importance of the alignment between training and assessment modalities. Chatbot-enhanced training systems may extend access to evidence-based techniques, such as FCT, in areas with limited training resources. More work is needed to confirm effects and demonstrate applicability to practice.

items.title: A Multistage Fine-Tuning and Empathy Alignment Approach for an Emotional Support Dialogue System: Development and Evaluation Study.
items.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used for text-based emotional support. However, general-purpose LLMs may not consistently recognize emotional cues, adapt supportive strategies to contexts, or generate responses aligned with psychologically informed communication. The limited availability of large-scale, structured Chinese counseling data further constrains the development of models for context-sensitive emotional support. Objective We developed and evaluated YuanChat, a family of specialized LLMs for context-sensitive emotional support; assessed whether E-URIAL improved response quality; and compared YuanChat with base LLMs. Methods We constructed 2 datasets from anonymized real-world counseling sessions: ECD-3 (104,897 counselor response turns) for fine-tuning and D gold (9413 manually annotated counselor responses). Annotations covered emotional support conversation stages (exploration, comfort, and action), counseling techniques (clarification, support, and challenge), and empathic effects. We developed 2 YuanChat variants using GLM-4-9B-Chat and Huozi 3.5 as backbone models using parameter-efficient fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We then developed E-URIAL, an inference-time framework combining predicted emotion and support strategy labels with retrieved labeled exemplars. Given the dialogue history through the help seeker's latest utterance, each model generated a counselor-style response. We compared YuanChat with GPT-4, ERNIE 4.0, CharacterGLM, GLM-4-9B-Chat, and Huozi 3.5. The evaluation comprised (1) automatic evaluation on in-domain and external datasets, assessing empathy identification and empathic expression; (2) evaluation of empathy-related situational reasoning using an expert-developed multiple-choice benchmark; (3) evaluation by clinical experts (n=8) of empathic attunement, support strategy appropriateness, perceived helpfulness, and safety and professional boundary adherence; and (4) a complementary evaluation by volunteer master's students in clinical and counseling psychology (n=50) of response fluency, empathy, and perceived helpfulness. Results Fine-tuning increased YuanChat-Huozi3.5's empathic expression score from 0.57 to 0.68; empathy identification score increased from 0.54 to 0.59. In expert evaluation, YuanChat-Huozi3.5 received a higher empathic attunement score than the base Huozi3.5 model (1.279 vs 0.327; mean difference 0.952, 95% CI 0.746-1.152). Using professional counselor responses as the reference, the mean differences for YuanChat-Huozi3.5 were 0.148, 0.079, 0.039, and 0.002 in empathic attunement, supportive appropriateness, perceived helpfulness, and safety and professional boundary adherence, respectively. No statistically significant differences were detected between YuanChat-Huozi3.5 and the counselor references (all Holm-adjusted P ≥.29). Higher scores were observed when E-URIAL was applied. When E-URIAL was applied with 3 retrieved exemplars, YuanChat-Huozi3.5 achieved an empathy identification score of 0.69 versus 0.59 without E-URIAL, an empathic expression score of 0.79 versus 0.68, and a perceived helpfulness score of 0.74 versus 0.61. Conclusions The findings indicate that fine-tuning on real-world counseling data and annotating models with structured emotional support labels improved context-sensitive empathic responding in LLMs. Without updating model parameters, E-URIAL further improved empathy identification and empathic expression across multiple models. Together, these methods provide a scalable, theory-informed approach to enhancing the emotional support capabilities of LLMs.

items.title: Indirect Effects of a Prenatal Intimate Partner Violence Intervention on Infant Socioemotional Functioning: Examining the Pregnant Moms' Empowerment Program.
items.abstract: Objective The current study evaluated whether previously established intervention-related improvements in maternal psychological functioning (i.e. IPV revictimization, depression) and caregiving (i.e. empathy, developmentally appropriate parenting expectations, observed parenting sensitivity) indirectly impact infant temperament (i.e. Surgency/Extraversion, Negative Affectivity, Orienting/Regulation) and observed affect. Method Data were drawn from a quasi-randomized trial with N = 137 pregnant women who had experienced IPV. Results Results indicated that there were some indirect benefits of the PMEP for infants. Specifically, intervention-related decreases in maternal IPV revictimization contributed to more positive observed infant affect, while intervention-related decreases in maternal depressive symptoms led to lower levels of infant Negative Affectivity. Conclusions Study findings highlight the emergence of promising evidence to support the intergenerational benefits of PMEP for infants born to IPV-exposed mothers, suggesting that early intervention for families is not only possible but also likely engenders benefits across the family system.

items.title: Aging and sustained attention: The role of inhibitory control and mind-wandering.
items.abstract: Sustained attention is the ability to maintain focus on a task over time. However, sustained attention tasks often engage other cognitive processes such as response inhibition. Despite these inhibitory demands and age differences in inhibitory control, older adults often outperform young adults on sustained attention tasks. The present study aimed to further our understanding of the relationship between sustained attention and inhibitory control and how this is affected by age. To this end, we used two versions of the Gradual-Onset Continuous Performance Task, which typically includes gradual transitions between frequent "go" stimuli and infrequent "no-go" stimuli. We manipulated inhibitory demands by including a 90% go condition, which encourages habitual responding, and a 10% go condition, which reduces inhibitory demands. We also interspersed mind-wandering probes and included separate measures of inhibitory control (stop-signal and go/no-go tasks) to relate to Gradual-Onset Continuous Performance Task performance. Both older and younger adults showed better sustained attention when inhibitory demands were minimized, but older adults outperformed younger adults in both conditions, showing higher A' scores and less reaction time variability. Younger adults also showed more vigilance decline over time and reported more mind-wandering. Gradual-Onset Continuous Performance Task performance correlated with both stop-signal and go/no-go tasks, indicating a role for individual differences in response inhibition. These findings suggest that sustained attention is not only preserved but can also be superior in older adults. Maintained vigilance may help offset age-related declines in response inhibition and processing speed, supporting everyday functions such as driving, at least over relatively short periods. items.title: Age-related differences in speech production: Evidence from graph analyses.
items.abstract: Storytelling is a vital aspect of language processing requiring successful integration of characters, events, and actions. Cohesive stories include the necessary information to transition between utterances and convey the overall gist. Although older adults often produce more off-topic speech, it is unclear how age affects narrative organization across discourse contexts. Additionally, broader cognitive declines in aging, like differences in executive function, may contribute to discourse. The present study examined discourse using computational speech graph analyses in 268 healthy adults aged 20-81 years old. Participants completed two speaking tasks differing in contextual support: a picture book description and an open-ended speech prompt. Speech graphs quantified connectedness by modeling words as nodes and their sequential relationships as edges, capturing local and longer range aspects of discourse. Results indicated that age was correlated with increased repetition and less connected speech. There was also a main effect of task where the picture book task elicited denser, more interconnected speech with greater reintegration across the narrative, while the open-ended prompt elicited speech that was more locally repetitive with fewer links between earlier and later portions of the narrative. Critically, age-related differences in connectedness were most evident in the open-ended prompt and were independent of executive function, suggesting a gradual shift toward more locally constrained speech in later adulthood, particularly when speech must be generated and organized without external support. Importantly, graph-based measures were sensitive to these subtle organizational shifts, highlighting their potential to complement established discourse metrics and deepen our understanding of speech across adulthood. items.title: Sweet or bitter? A meta-analytic review on pleasantness and unpleasantness of revenge.
items.abstract: This meta-analysis examined what revenge feels like. We located 54 research reports (k = 99), comprising 14,612 participants and spanning the years 1974 to 2025. Overall, revenge was significantly associated with pleasant feelings (r = .19, [.12, .25]), but not significantly associated with unpleasant feelings (r = .06, [-.06, .17]). Specifically, both enacted and envisioned revenge were associated with pleasant feelings. This association was observed across different measurement types and assessment times, although it was stronger when feelings were assessed during revenge than shortly after revenge, suggesting that the pleasure of revenge fades with time. Findings were consistent across published and unpublished works as well as preregistered and non-pre-registered studies. Conversely, envisioned revenge was associated with unpleasant feelings, whereas enacted revenge was not. The association between revenge and unpleasant feelings weakened over the last 50 years and was moderated by the preregistration presence, such that revenge was positively associated with unpleasant feelings in non-pre-registered studies but negatively associated with unpleasant feelings in preregistered studies. Taken together, these findings suggest that revenge is particularly pleasant during the act itself, supporting the reinforcement model of revenge and providing little evidence that revenge is followed by pronounced unpleasant emotional aftertaste. items.title: On the same wavelength: Social evaluation through perceived emotional congruence.
items.abstract: People instinctively evaluate others by whether their emotions align, or clash, with their own. This rapid, often unconscious process, which we term affective wavelengths, posits that individuals assess social partners based on perceived emotional congruence. We propose that when another's emotional cues confirm our implicit expectation that others will feel as we do, the resulting positive metacognitive signal increases closeness and the inclination to interact. Conversely, when cues violate that expectation, the resulting negative metacognitive signal fosters social distance and disinclination. Unlike prior work, which has focused on how specific, potent emotions like shared pain or collective awe can bind people, affective wavelengths offers a bidirectional, mechanistic framework that applies categorically to any emotion. Seven experiments with 1,330 participants support the theory, with data from U.S. samples collected between 2016 and 2018 and a Thai sample across 2024-2025. Our findings demonstrate that perceived emotional congruence shapes social evaluation across valence, even when emotional cues arise from different situations. These effects persist across communication channels, replicate cross-culturally, and are resilient to perceptual noise. While emotional congruence can bridge ideological divides, its influence can be outweighed by contradictory contextual information. This research offers a novel framework for understanding how perceived emotional congruence steers social evaluation, shaping interpersonal judgments, relationships, and affiliation. items.title: Coregulation patterns in emotional sharing dynamics among adolescent friend dyads.
items.abstract: Adolescence is a critical period characterized by heightened emotional intensity and volatility during which peer friendships gradually replace family as the primary source of emotional support. Understanding patterns of emotional interaction between adolescent friends is crucial for promoting their socioemotional development. Guided by the temporal interpersonal emotion systems theory, the present study focused on emotional coregulation-reciprocal emotional linkage in which mutual damping enables dyads to reach dynamic equilibrium. We employed dyadic discussion tasks (negative problem discussion vs. pleasant topic discussion), combined with second-by-second facial expression coding to capture adolescents' emotional expressions. Emotional dynamics were modeled using the coupled oscillator model, and distinct patterns were identified through latent profile analysis. Associations between these patterns and individual traits as well as relational characteristics were also examined. In the negative context, two profiles emerged: "coregulation," marked by mutual emotional convergence and gradually stabilized over time, and "nonregulation," marked by persistent fluctuation without returning to equilibrium. Friendship duration was positively associated with the likelihood of entering the coregulation pattern, whereas perceived problem severity and affective empathy were negatively associated with this pattern. In the positive context, coregulation did not emerge as a typical pattern. Instead, dyads were differentiated by "in-phase" versus "out-of-phase" oscillation, which were not significantly associated with individual or relational factors. The results provide empirical evidence for understanding the emotional dynamics in adolescent close friendships and may help inform peer-oriented approaches aimed at supporting adolescents' socioemotional well-being. items.title: Temporal leadership and task performance among the military in Ghana: Mediating role of felt obligation and role clarity.
items.abstract: This study investigates the effects of Temporal Leadership (TL) on task performance among military personnel in Ghana, emphasizing the roles of felt obligation and role clarity. A quantitative approach with an explanatory research design was used in this study. This study attempted a census survey across the entire Armed Forces in Ghana, employing a structured questionnaire designed to capture detailed insights into the effects of temporal leadership on task performance among the Military. A total of 494 usable responses were included in the analysis. Hypotheses were tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) version 4.1.0.9. The findings revealed a strong positive correlation between temporal leadership, felt obligation, role clarity, and task performance in the military. Temporal leadership was found to have a positive and significant effect on military task performance, felt obligation, and role clarity. Furthermore, both felt obligation and role clarity significantly mediated the link between temporal leadership and task performance, with role clarity exhibiting a stronger mediating effect than felt obligation. Previous research on military personnel has investigated the impact of TL on performance improvement, with work engagement serving as a key mediator. This study is unique because it is among the first to explore felt obligation and role clarity as mediating factors in the relationship between TL and task performance.

items.title: The role of stereotypes in housing discrimination toward exonerees: A test of the counter-stereotype framework.
items.abstract: Formerly incarcerated individuals experience stigma and discrimination postrelease. However, little is known about the mechanisms driving discrimination toward exonerees. The goal of the current research was to investigate the effect of stereotype endorsement and the mitigating effect of counter-stereotype information on housing discrimination toward exonerees. We expected distinct stereotype profiles for exonerees and releasees (Study 1); discriminatory rental decisions toward exonerees (Study 2); stronger stereotype endorsement to predict lower willingness to rent (Study 3); and counter-stereotype information to improve rental decisions and attitudes (Study 4). Three online studies and one audit study were conducted. Study 1 (N = 643) assessed stereotype traits for exonerees and releasees. Study 2 (N = 377) examined the effects of stereotype endorsement on rental decisions toward exonerees and releasees. Study 3 (N = 551) examined the mitigating effect of counter-stereotype information on rental decisions and attitudes. Study 4 sent 818 randomized rental inquiries to capture real landlords' replies and availability to a control applicant or an exoneree described with counter-stereotype, individuating, or no additional information. Study 1 identified distinct stereotype profiles, with exonerees associated with paternalistic prejudice and releasees with contemptuous prejudice. In Study 2, stronger endorsement of releasee stereotypes predicted lower willingness to rent. In Study 3, participants made more favorable rental decisions and expressed more positive attitudes toward exonerees and applicants described with counter-stereotype rather than stereotype-congruent information. In Study 4, control applicants were more likely than exonerees to receive a reply and to be told the apartment was available, though landlords were more likely to indicate availability when exoneree inquiries included counter-stereotype information. Exonerees and releasees are stereotyped differently, and these stereotypes differentially predict housing discrimination. Providing counter-stereotype or individuating information can reduce, but does not eliminate, housing discrimination, underscoring the need for stigma-reduction efforts and policy reform. items.title: Sibling justice involvement and youth recidivism following first arrest.
items.abstract: Youth recidivism following a first arrest remains difficult to predict, and research on family-level risk has focused disproportionately on parents rather than siblings. This study examined whether justice-system involvement within adolescents' sibling networks was associated with youth rearrest during the year following youths' first arrest. We hypothesized that adolescents with justice-involved siblings would be more likely to be rearrested than adolescents without justice-involved siblings, with stronger associations for older siblings than younger siblings and for sibling incarceration than sibling arrest. We also compared threshold, dosage, and saturation models to evaluate how sibling justice-system exposure is best conceptualized. Data came from 326 adolescents in the Crossroads Study. Sibling arrest and incarceration were examined using threshold (dichotomous), dosage (count), and saturation (proportion) operationalizations. Logistic regression models predicted any rearrest, and negative binomial regression models predicted rearrest counts. Sibling incarceration showed the most consistent association with rearrest when operationalized as a threshold exposure: Youth with any incarcerated sibling had approximately twice the odds and expected count of rearrest. Sibling arrest was associated with rearrest primarily when measured cumulatively, through count and proportion indicators, rather than as a dichotomous exposure. Birth-order analyses suggested that associations were more evident for older than younger sibling exposure; younger sibling arrest and incarceration were not associated with rearrest in any specification. Sibling justice-system exposure is a family-level developmental context whose implications depend on the type of contact, extent of exposure, and developmental position of the exposed sibling. Findings underscore the importance of considering sibling networks in family-centered responses following first arrest. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Examining college sexual violence mandatory reporting policies and report outcomes: Evidence does not support a universal approach over alternative approaches.
items.abstract: Mandatory reporting policies for sexual violence in U.S. institutions of higher education (IHEs) require certain designated employees to report any potential sexual violence they learn about to IHE officials, even when the victim/survivor does not want to report. The most common policy approach is a Universal approach, in which all or nearly all employees are designated as mandatory reporters. However, some have adopted Alternative approaches (e.g., designating only select employees as mandatory reporters, considering survivor consent to the report). It is often assumed that Universal policies best facilitate beneficial outcomes, such as addressing cases of sexual violence and supporting survivors. Yet, these assumptions have not been supported with empirical evidence. This exploratory study examined if having a Universal approach (vs. an Alternative approach) was associated with the number of reports made to the Title IX office and key report outcomes following a mandated report. There were no formal hypotheses. This study used survey data collected from a national sample of Title IX practitioners in IHEs (N = 260). Title IX practitioners working at IHEs with a Universal policy received significantly more reports from mandatory reporters than those with an Alternative policy. However, there were no clear significant differences between policy approaches for other outcomes, including total reports, percentage of reports possibly actionable under Title IX policy, how frequently survivors responded to contact from the Title IX office, or how frequently survivors wanted or received a formal investigation process, accommodations, or resource referrals. There were few differences between policy approaches for important mandatory report outcomes, refuting assumptions that Universal mandatory reporting policies are associated with better outcomes than Alternative approaches. items.title: An intervention based on acceptance and commitment therapy for people experiencing work- or career-related difficulties: A randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: This randomized controlled trial assessed the effectiveness of a group intervention based on acceptance and commitment therapy designed for people facing work- or career-related difficulties (e.g., job loss, burnout). Participants were recruited with the assistance of community organizations providing career counseling services, and they were randomly assigned to either an intervention group (n = 82) or a waitlist group (n = 82). They completed questionnaires aimed at measuring process (i.e., psychological flexibility and inflexibility) and outcome variables (i.e., psychological well-being, psychological distress, meaning in life, and career engagement) on three occasions (baseline, postintervention, and follow-up). Participants took part in seven 2.5-hr sessions offered online during a 7-week period. Results of mixed-effects models on intention-to-treat data showed that the intervention led to an increase in psychological flexibility (d = .64), well-being (d = .32), and meaning in life (d = .42) and a decrease in psychological inflexibility (d = -.51) and distress (d = -.36). These effects were maintained at follow-up (17 weeks later), moderated by participants' initial levels of distress and precarity (for some outcomes). Indirect effect analyses showed that changes in psychological flexibility/inflexibility statistically accounted for these effects. The intervention had no significant effect on career engagement. Overall, this trial suggests that the intervention helped promote well-being and flourishing among people struggling with work- or career-related difficulties. items.title: [Nutritional problems in older people].
items.abstract: Healthy ageing has become a major public health priority in response to the rapid demographic shift toward an ageing population. In Poland, older people are projected to account for approx. 40% of the total population by 2050. The present study aims to synthesise current evidence regarding the nutritional status of older adults and to discuss the multifaceted determinants and consequences of malnutrition in this population group. A literature search for the years 2015-2025 was conducted in the MEDLINE/PubMed database using the keywords "elderly," "older adults," "geriatric patients," "malnutrition," "nutritional problems," "nutritional status," "nutritional risk," "chronic disease," "multimorbidity," "frailty," "disability," "activities of daily living" and "dependence." The search was repeated in the Google Scholar database using the keywords "elderly" and "malnutrition." Fifty-three articles were included in the analysis. The analysis shows that older adults are a high-risk group for malnutrition. The degree of malnutrition varies across the studied populations, with the highest percentage of malnourished older adults found in hospital settings. Malnutrition in older age encompasses both insufficient energy intake and deficiencies in essential vitamins and minerals. Its determinants are complex and include social factors, such as isolation and economic vulnerability, as well as physiological changes associated with ageing. Importantly, nutritional risk is frequently multifactorial and may involve simultaneous deficiencies in several nutrients. Preventive strategies should therefore combine systematic screening across diverse social groups with comprehensive, targeted interventions. These may include correction of nutritional deficiencies, use of medical foods, direct food provision to vulnerable individuals, and structured nutrition education for older adults, caregivers, and healthcare professionals from the immediate community of older people and encouraging older people to spend their time actively. Promoting physical activity and social participation is equally important in mitigating frailty and loneliness. Effective prevention of malnutrition is fundamental to healthy ageing. Med Pr Work Health Saf. 2026;77(4).

items.title: Reception Centre Nurses' Perceived Competence and Determinants of Implementation Behaviour Regarding the Revised Initial Health Assessment for Asylum Seekers.
items.abstract: Aim The aim of this study was to develop a comprehensive understanding of reception centre nurses' competence requirements and determinants of implementation behaviour related to the revised initial health assessment model for asylum seekers. Design This cross-sectional mixed-method study was based on data collected through an online Reception Centre Nurses' Competence Survey conducted in Finland in 2024. A total of 217 nurses were invited to participate, of whom 97 responded, yielding a response rate of 45%. Seventy participants also provided responses to the open-ended questions. The survey instrument is included as an appendix. Methods The survey consisted of background information, the Determinants of Implementation Behaviour Questionnaire and additional open-ended questions. Quantitative group differences were analysed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Qualitative data were examined using concept-driven thematic analysis. Reporting followed the Good Reporting of a Mixed Methods Study guidelines. Results Previous healthcare and reception centre experience supported successful implementation of the initial health assessment model, including adaptation to individual client needs. Reception centre experience enhanced understanding of practical model delivery, while healthcare experience strengthened competencies needed to assess diverse client populations. Successful delivery required both clinical and interpersonal competencies, and a public health nursing background contributed to a health-promoting approach and positive client attitudes towards the initial health assessment model. Conclusion The findings indicate that specialized competence and diverse work experience can support the initial health assessment model's implementation. The results highlight the necessity for targeted skills training and improved implementation strategies to support the effective use of the revised model. Patient or public contribution Reception centre nurses were involved in the study and later engaged in a workshop to reflect on the findings. Impact The study addressed the global challenge of meeting the complex and often unique health needs of asylum seekers, which requires highly competent healthcare professionals and the implementation of new clinical practices. Specifically, it examined reception centre nurses' perceived competence to meet the aims of the revised initial health assessment model and determinants of implementation behaviour. Competence was understood as nurses' perceived ability to apply the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required for conducting the revised initial health assessment. Factors influencing the enactment of this competence in practice were examined through determinants of implementation behaviour. Previous healthcare and reception centre experience supported successful implementation of the initial health assessment model, including adaptation to individual client needs. Reception centre experience enhanced understanding of practical model delivery, while healthcare experience strengthened competencies needed to assess diverse client populations. Successful delivery required both clinical and interpersonal competencies, and a public health nursing background contributed to a health-promoting approach and positive client attitudes towards the initial health assessment model. The findings will guide the training of nurses working with asylum seekers by clarifying the specialized competencies and diverse work experience needed for effective practice in reception centres. The results will also support organisations responsible for training and assisting health professionals in this field, highlighting the importance of targeted skills development and strengthened implementation strategies. More broadly, the study will inform healthcare systems and policymakers seeking to enhance the quality and consistency of health assessments for asylum seekers across different service settings, ultimately helping asylum seekers receive safe, effective, and high-quality care.

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Canal Wall Up Tympanoplasty With and Without Obliteration in Cholesteatoma Surgery.
items.abstract: Objective To determine the cost-effectiveness of the bony obliteration tympanoplasty compared with canal wall up without obliteration in cholesteatoma surgery from a healthcare payer perspective. Study design State-transition Markov model. Setting Tertiary care center in the Netherlands. Methods A state-transition Markov model was developed to evaluate costs and health outcomes over a 5-year time horizon. Health benefits were quantified in quality-adjusted life years. All costs were expressed in euros. Transition probabilities and complication rates were derived from a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study (n = 110 ears). Matching variables included cholesteatoma origin, disease extent according to the STAM classification, and prior middle ear surgery. Deterministic one-way sensitivity analyses and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. Results The model estimated 5‑year costs and health outcomes for a 40‑year‑old patient undergoing either bony obliteration tympanoplasty or the canal wall up technique without mastoid obliteration. Bony obliteration tympanoplasty resulted in higher mean costs (€5954 vs €4844), mainly driven by longer operative time. However, it also yielded more quality-adjusted life years over 5 years (2.76 vs 2.47). This corresponded to an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €3855 per additional quality-adjusted life year gained, which is well below commonly accepted willingness-to-pay thresholds. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis confirmed the robustness of these findings, indicating that bony obliteration tympanoplasty is cost-effective in 97% of simulations at a willingness-to-pay of €50,000. Conclusion Bony obliteration tympanoplasty is a cost-effective alternative to the canal wall up technique without mastoid obliteration for cholesteatoma surgery and should be considered in surgical planning.

items.title: Implementation of School-Based Traffic Light Labeling and Calorie Information Intervention to Reduce Sugary Drink Purchases Among Indonesian Adolescents.
items.abstract: Sugar-sweetened beverages consumption remains high among adolescents and requires effective interventions. This study evaluated the impact of traffic light labeling (TLL) displayed in the school canteens on beverage purchases among high school students. A 2-stage study consisted of a qualitative approach exploring preferred TLL designs and a quantitative quasi-experiment involving intervention and control schools. The intervention school displayed energy, sugar, and fat TLL on beverage menus for 2 months, preceded by an educational session, while the control school displayed a balanced nutrition poster. Beverage purchases were recorded at baseline, 1 month, and 2 months using an online self-administered questionnaire. At baseline, nutritional status and pocket money did not differ significantly between groups. Mean BMI-for-age z -scores were 0.03 ± 0.01 in the intervention school and 0.13 ± 0.01 in the control school. Repeated-measures analyses showed significant reductions in energy, sugar, and fat beverage purchases in the intervention group (all P < .05). Traffic light labeling combined with education may promote healthier beverage purchasing.

items.title: Embedding international research in global public health pedagogy: bridging the teaching-research divide for equitable learning.
items.abstract: The increasing complexity of transnational public health challenges requires educational approaches that equip future professionals with the skills to critically engage with evidence and address diverse global health priorities. This commentary argues that embedding international research within global public health pedagogy can strengthen equitable, inquiry-driven and practice-oriented learning. International research engagement enables students and educators to participate in collaborative knowledge production through cross-border partnerships, comparative research, authentic research projects, internships and global learning experiences. Such approaches may enhance critical thinking, analytical competence, cross-cultural understanding and evidence-informed decision-making. However, meaningful integration remains constrained by institutional, financial, technological, ethical and political barriers, particularly within low- and middle-income countries. To address these challenges, an equity-oriented framework comprising progressive curriculum integration, equitable partnerships and reciprocal capacity strengthening is proposed. Embedding international research into global public health education is an important strategy for preparing reflective, globally competent and socially responsive public health professionals capable of addressing contemporary and future global health challenges.
