items.title: Salivary Citrate Deficiency Defines an Endogenous Dentin Remineralization Failure State Through Glandular MT1/2-Zn<sup>2+</sup>-ACO2 Dysregulation.
items.abstract: Rapid caries progression occurs even when salivary flow and calcium phosphate availability are preserved, suggesting a knowledge gap in how available minerals are used for repair. Early-stage Sjögren's syndrome was examined as a clinical model of this condition. Salivary citrate was markedly lower in the disease cohort and was inversely associated with caries burden, whereas salivary flow and the major mineral ions did not differ from healthy controls. In mineralization systems with matched calcium and phosphate concentrations, the disease-associated citrate concentration reduced intrafibrillar mineral deposition, disrupted hydroxyapatite organization, and limited structural and mechanical recovery of demineralized dentin. Human salivary gland tissue, an immunization-induced rat model, and primary salivary gland epithelial cells showed a similar metabolic pattern: increased metallothionein 1/2 (MT1/2), reduced labile Zn 2+ , increased aconitase 2 (ACO2) activity, and citrate depletion. ZnSO 4 repletion increased intracellular Zn 2+ , reduced ACO2 activity, restored citrate toward control levels, and improved the mineralization activity of epithelial-cell supernatants. The data indicate that citrate availability influences dentin mineral utilization and associate citrate depletion with glandular MT1/2-Zn 2+ -ACO2 dysregulation. These findings support an association between glandular zinc-citrate dysregulation and impaired remineralization, suggesting that this mechanism may account for impaired endogenous remineralization despite preserved availability of the major mineral ions.

items.title: Seasonal Variation in Mood and Associated Patterns of Sleep, Activity, Circadian Rhythms and Light.
items.abstract: The mechanisms underlying seasonal mood variation are incompletely characterised. We tested whether wearable-measured sleep, activity, circadian and light exposure patterns are associated with seasonal mood variation in young Australians with emerging mood disorders. We analysed 733 observation periods from 422 participants (mean age 24.3 ± 5.5 years; 63% female) attending early-intervention clinics. Each observation included a clinical assessment paired with ≥5 valid days of wrist actigraphy. Season was modelled using sine-cosine functions of day-of-year. Sleep, activity and circadian features were reduced using joint and individual variation explained (JIVE). Light exposure features were reduced using principal component analysis (PCA) applied to light regularity, timing and exposure interval across 7 illuminance thresholds. Linear mixed-effects models tested seasonal effects on clinical outcomes; indirect associations for 12 candidate JIVE/PCA variables were estimated by cluster bootstrap. Depressive symptoms (β = -0.67, P = .023) and negative symptoms (β = -0.17, P = .041) peaked in winter, whereas manic symptoms peaked in autumn (β = 0.24, P = .019). Winter increases in negative symptoms were associated with an 'extended sleep with phase-delayed activity' profile (indirect β = -0.015, P < .002) and a 'constrained pattern of moderate-to-bright indoor light exposure' profile (indirect β = -0.038, P = .002), reflecting high day-to-day consistency with a narrow daily exposure window. The light association persisted after adjustment for time spent above the light threshold, which itself was not associated with symptoms. Winter increases in depressive symptoms were associated with lower overall physical activity levels (indirect β = -0.009, P = .040). No indirect associations were identified for manic symptoms. In this transdiagnostic youth sample, seasonal variation in mood was modest but was accompanied by differences in how personal light exposure was arranged across the day, not only in how much light was received and in daily activity patterns. These cross-sectional associations identify light patterning and activity rhythms as candidate modifiable targets for prospective and interventional research.

items.title: Multi-level factors influencing the implementation of Cambodia's National Policy on School Health: a qualitative case study.
items.abstract: Background Since the 2000 World Education Forum, international organizations have encouraged low- and middle-income countries to strengthen school health systems through national school health policies based on the Health Promoting School (HPS) concept. While these policies offer proven benefits, implementation remains challenging in many low- and middle-income settings. In Cambodia, despite the establishment of the National Policy on School Health (NPSH), implementation remains uneven and insufficient across administrative levels. While implementation factors have been identified at the national, provincial, and elementary school levels, evidence remains limited at the secondary school level. Therefore, the current study investigated the factors influencing NPSH implementation at the public secondary school level in Battambang province. Methods This qualitative case study assessed complementary information from 27 key informant interviews (KIIs) with stakeholders involved in policy implementation and 13 documents related to previous implementation efforts. Participants represented national policy, provincial, district, commune, and school perspectives. Content analysis combined deductive coding guided by Vince Whitman's wheel of factors influencing the implementation of policy and practice, with inductive coding of context-specific themes. Results Nine thematic domains were identified to influence NPSH implementation. Policy reform, policy implementation-adapted strategy, and champions and leaders at all levels were described primarily as enabling implementation. Dissemination gaps and limited understanding within the international and national guidelines domain, attention to external forces, and gender gap and mandated roles were described primarily as inhibitors. Dedicated time and resources, administrative and management support, and stakeholder ownership and participation contained both enabling and constraining processes. These categories describe reported implementation experience rather than measured effect or the relative importance of factors. Conclusions Participants described an interaction between a binding legal mandate and perceived local autonomy in the implementation of NPSH. Their accounts suggest that a clearer legal framework, support for local adaptation, leadership, and cross-sector participation may help implementation in this setting. This study did not establish causal effects or examine students' health and learning outcomes. Research across additional provinces, incorporating frontline staff, parents, students, and independent implementation data, is needed to assess the interpretations and their transferability.

items.title: A glycoengineered yeast-derived HA1-ferritin nanoparticle vaccine confers protective immunity against H7 avian influenza in chickens.
items.abstract: H7 subtype avian influenza virus is an important zoonotic pathogen threatening the poultry industry and public health. Recombinant subunit vaccines provide a safer alternative to conventional inactivated vaccines, while yeast expression systems offer advantages of low cost, scalability, and engineering flexibility. However, their application in avian influenza vaccine development remains underexplored. In this study, we use the methylotrophic yeast Komagataella phaffii as a low-cost, industrial-scale platform to produce hemagglutinin-1 (HA1) subunits with programmable N-/O-linked glycosylation. The methanol-utilization-slow (MutS) phenotype strain secreted 1.21 g/L HA1, and compared with the standard methanol-utilization-plus (Mut+) phenotype strain, the N-linked and O-linked glycans were significantly reduced [liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)/MS glycopeptide profile]. Despite hypoglycosylation, the antigen retained native conformation, binding H7-specific mAb Q74 with a KD of 1.34 × 10-7 M. SpyTag/SpyCatcher-directed conjugation to ferritin drove quantitative self-assembly into 30 nm virus-like nanoparticles. Formulated with CpG-ODN 1826, the HA1-MutS-ferritin candidate elicited Hemagglutination inhibition (HI) titers of 6.7 log2 in specific pathogen-free (SPF) leghorns at 28 days post-immunization (dpi), significantly enhancing HA1-specific IgY responses (p < 0.0001) while sustaining high-level circulating CD4+ T cells. At 28 dpi, chickens were challenged with 106 embryo infectious dose (EID)50 of H7N9 avian influenza virus; the formulation conferred 100% clinical protection and accelerated viral clearance, matching the performance of conventional inactivated vaccines. Yeast-based processes significantly reduce downstream purification costs and eliminate reliance on chicken embryos, providing a scalable and biosafe platform for rapid avian influenza control.

items.title: Cultural Initiatives in Public Hospitals: Situated Forms of Health Promotion in Argentina.
items.abstract: Cultural initiatives in public hospitals represent an underexamined form of health promotion in Latin America. This study examines how these initiatives are organized, implemented, and sustained in public hospitals in the city of Buenos Aires (Argentina). We use the term cultural initiatives to describe hospital-based programs and practices that mobilize artistic, heritage, and community resources; cultural managers are the actors who coordinate and sustain them within hospital structures. The qualitative, exploratory study was conducted between 2020 and 2022 and combined an online questionnaire completed across 18 hospitals with 25 semi-structured interviews. Manual thematic content analysis identified three interconnected dimensions: actors, settings, and institutional challenges. Cultural managers drew on hybrid occupational trajectories and institutional knowledge to connect clinical, cultural, and community actors. The initiatives transformed hospital spaces and created opportunities for expression, participation, and social connection, yet their continuity was constrained by fragmented roles, limited resources, scarce dedicated space, and weak formal recognition. These findings show that the health-promoting potential of cultural initiatives depends on the institutional work and organizational conditions that sustain them. By documenting the conditions under which cultural initiatives emerge and are sustained, this study contributes to international evidence on arts-based health promotion and highlights the need for dedicated roles, intersectoral partnerships, and the formal recognition of cultural action as a core component of equitable, community-centered care.

items.title: A semi-supervised diffusion model for automated segmentation of vascular plaques.
items.abstract: Segmenting vascular plaques in the carotid arteries, aorta, and iliac arteries on CT is important because plaque burden relates to cardiovascular and stroke risk and can guide treatment. However, manual labeling is often infeasible and time-consuming across large vascular regions. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) can leverage unlabeled CT data to enable accurate plaque segmentation with only limited labels. We applied a diffusion-based semi-supervised learning (SSL) method for vascular plaque segmentation in non-contrast CT by formulating the task as multi-class segmentation of plaques and 26 adjacent anatomical structures. The method employs a teacher-student architecture with a shared diffusion encoder to learn domain-invariant feature representations and separate teacher and student decoders to decouple labeled and unlabeled data, reducing overfitting and improving robustness. To address the severe class imbalance caused by the small size of plaques, we developed a plaque-aware oversampling strategy and a labeled-data-guided training for the shared encoder and student decoder. We used 142 NIH non-contrast CT scans, divided into 119 training scans and 23 validation scans. We externally evaluated the method on 95 scans from the University of Wisconsin and 50 scans from Medipol University Mega Hospital and compared its performance with supervised nnU-Net and a strong SSL baseline. The improved SSL method significantly outperformed the original SSL method and supervised training with the same architecture when using 14 labeled training scans ( p<0.0001 ). With these 14 labeled training scans, it achieved DSC values of 58.8% and 82.3% on CTRATE and Renal Donor, respectively, within 2.7--2.8 percentage points of the same architecture trained with all 119 training scans labeled. The SSL method segments plaques in the carotid, aortic, and iliac arteries with performance approaching that of fully supervised training while using only 14 labeled training scans, supporting scalable plaque burden assessment.

items.title: Approximating Peak Prevalence in Multistage SIR Epidemics.
items.abstract: Estimating peak prevalence is a central problem in epidemic modeling because it determines the period of greatest infectious burden and is closely linked to health-care demand. In multistage SIR models, however, peak prevalence is generally less tractable than in the classical model with exponentially distributed infectious periods. Motivated by the use of weighted infectious-stage aggregates as surrogates for prevalence, we investigate the relationship between the prevalence peak and the maximum of a weighted stage functional in a deterministic SIR-like epidemic model with k identical infectious stages, which we call an SI(k)R model. We show that this relationship depends critically on how the stage-progression rate is scaled as the number of infectious stages increases. Under naive scaling, in which the progression rate remains fixed, the weighted peak is asymptotically equivalent to the prevalence peak and the commonly used factor-two approximation fails. Under Erlang scaling, which preserves the mean infectious period, the multistage model converges to a delay formulation in which prevalence and the weighted stage functional become unweighted and triangularly weighted moving averages of incidence. This limiting representation provides a theoretical basis for the factor-two approximation and identifies the regimes in which it is accurate. It also explains why this approximation deteriorates as epidemic waves become more sharply peaked. We derive analytical error bounds and develop curvature-based and parameter-based corrections that substantially improve accuracy. Numerical studies confirm these improvements across a broad range of epidemiological parameters. Overall, the results show when weighted-stage peaks can be used reliably as proxies for peak prevalence and how the resulting estimates can be refined when the standard approximation loses accuracy.

items.title: Genomic analysis of early case samples from the 2025 Marburg virus outbreak in Ethiopia.
items.abstract: In November 2025, Ethiopia reported its first outbreak of Marburg virus disease, with a case fatality rate of 64%. Here we report the analysis of seven near-complete Marburg virus genomes from seven early cases. The outbreak lineage belonged to the MARV.A.1 clade, which is closely related to genomes from historical human cases and bats. A high nucleotide identity across the seven genomes suggests human-to-human transmission after a zoonotic spillover event. These findings highlight the importance of genomic surveillance for outbreak detection, response and preparedness.

items.title: Generating patient-friendly radiology reports with a local large language model: expert evaluation of quality and readability.
items.abstract: To assess the feasibility of using a locally hosted large language model (LLM) to generate patient-friendly radiology reports while avoiding cloud transfer of report text. In this retrospective study, 360 chest, knee, lumbar spine, and shoulder X-rays, and shoulder and abdominal ultrasound reports from Dutch primary care were included. Main report sections (n = 359) and conclusion sections (n = 350) were translated into patient-friendly versions using Gemma-3 (12B parameters) and assessed for accuracy and completeness on 5-point Likert scales. Readability was evaluated using text length and Flesch-Douma reading ease (FDRE) scores. Hallucinations were systematically documented. Statistical analyses included Kruskal-Wallis, Wilcoxon signed-rank, and paired t-tests. Patient-friendly conclusions achieved higher median accuracy scores than main reports (5 [Q1-Q3 5-5] vs 4 [3-5]), while completeness scores were high for both sections (5 [5-5]). Compared with original reports, patient-friendly reports were longer (median increase 65 words [48-84], p 60). Clinically relevant hallucinations occurred in 45 reports (12.5%). A locally hosted LLM demonstrated feasibility for generating patient-friendly translations of Dutch X-ray and ultrasound reports while avoiding cloud transfer of data, with better performance for conclusion sections than main reports. However, clinically relevant hallucinations remain a safety concern and indicate the need for clinician oversight and further evaluation before clinical implementation. Question Can a locally hosted LLM generate patient-friendly radiology reports while preserving data privacy and maintaining acceptable accuracy, completeness, and readability? Findings A locally hosted LLM generated patient-friendly report conclusions with higher quality scores than main reports, while clinically relevant hallucinations remained an important safety concern. Clinical relevance A locally hosted LLM has potential to generate patient-friendly radiology report translations without external cloud data transfer. Report conclusions appear to be the most promising initial application, although clinician oversight and further patient-centered validation remain essential before clinical implementation.

items.title: Insights into early-onset colorectal cancer from a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of colorectal cancer across the age continuum.
items.abstract: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC; diagnosed before age 50 years) is increasing worldwide. Although current data indicate that EO-CRC may be biologically distinct from average-onset CRC (AO-CRC; diagnosed at age ≥50 years), molecular differences remain poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from 189 primary CRC tumors (54 EO-CRC, 135 AO-CRC) spanning eight decades of life, with at least 20 tumors in most age decades. Our analyses stratified tumors by microsatellite status and accounted for tumor sidedness, stage, patient sex and neoadjuvant treatment history, modeling age continuously or categorically (EO-CRC versus AO-CRC). Among microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumors, those from younger patients were characterized by increased stromal and decreased epithelial proportions, which we confirmed using multispectral immunofluorescence and machine learning in an external cohort of 712 MSS CRC tumors (18 EO-CRC, 694 AO-CRC). Tumor epithelial cells from young patients exhibited increased expression of long noncoding RNAs and FN1, with a trend toward increased heterogeneity in copy number alterations. MSS left-sided EO-CRC tumors had more cell-cell interactions, with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-related signaling pathways (FN1/GDF/ACTIVIN) showing increased, cell type-specific interactions. Our large high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas uncovers age-associated features of CRC and provides a resource for the community to understand EO-CRC biology.

items.title: Local politicians' perspectives on mental health literacy in their political and social work environment.
items.abstract: BackgroundMental health literacy is important for local politicians working in socially demanding roles. Given the high prevalence of mental health problems and rising sick leave, they must engage with these issues in an informed and reflective way, particularly in elder care, a field characterised by public scrutiny, emotional strain, and frequent criticism.ObjectiveTo examine how local politicians responsible for elder care conceptualise mental health literacy and how they relate it to their own social work environment.MethodsThis qualitative content analysis study draws on 41 interviews with local politicians responsible for elder care across Sweden, representing a range of political parties, geographical contexts, and political roles.ResultsThe analysis resulted in two categories: Navigating mental health in a politicised work role, and Psychosocial pressures within a hostile political work environment The findings show that politicians work under demanding conditions characterised by high workload, public scrutiny, and the risk of threats and harassment from both citizens and political colleagues. Despite these challenges, the results reveal limited mental health literacy regarding their own psychosocial risks and work environment.ConclusionThis study highlights how the socially demanding work environment of local politicians shapes their understanding of mental health and contributes to psychosocial strain. The findings underscore the need for greater awareness, organisational support, and preventive measures to promote sustainable and healthy political work environments.

items.title: Support for cancer survivors in vocational rehabilitation programs in Norway: Experiences of cancer survivors and job counselors.
items.abstract: BackgroundAs more individuals remain in the workforce following a cancer diagnosis, many will face cancer-related late effects, including pain, fatigue, and cognitive impairments, which can hinder their return-to-work (RTW) process.ObjectiveThis study explored the RTW experiences of cancer survivors enrolled in vocational rehabilitation programs in Norway, and the experiences of job counselors supporting cancer survivors in their RTW process.MethodsQualitative interviews were conducted with five cancer survivors and five job counselors. The job counselors were employed in vocational rehabilitation enterprises operating under assignments from the public Norwegian Labor and Welfare Administration (NAV). NAV is responsible for administering social welfare benefits, providing employment services, and actively supporting individuals returning to work after illness or injury. Data were qualitatively analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis (cancer survivors) and a template organizing style analysis (job counselors).ResultsThree main themes emerged: Cancer-free but not healthy, Need for inclusive employment practices, and Lack of interdisciplinary collaboration. Cancer survivors frequently required workplace accommodations to address unexpected late effects, but these accommodations were not consistently provided by employers, prompting job counselors to also intervene with employers. Both cancer survivors and job counselors reported a lack of competence and interest in work inclusion among healthcare professionals. Additionally, the participants expressed frustration with NAV and perceived the follow-up of workers on long-term sick leave as inadequate, despite legal mandates.ConclusionsThe findings underscore the need for improved interdisciplinary collaboration to support cancer survivors in the RTW process and advocate for the integration of work inclusion into standardized cancer care pathways.

items.title: The role of platelet-rich plasma and stem cells in the management of osteoarthritis: Current evidence, clinical positioning, and translational challenges.
items.abstract: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapies are among the most widely used regenerative interventions for knee osteoarthritis (OA). Despite being driven by a broadly similar regenerative concept, important differences in biological characteristics, evidence availability, and regulatory requirements mean that they should not be regarded as broadly comparable therapies. At the same time, conflicting findings from clinical trials and evidence syntheses continue to shape interpretation and clinical decision-making. Substantial heterogeneity across products, treatment protocols, patient populations, and study designs has further complicated the evidence base. Yet as public enthusiasm and commercialization continue to accelerate, these uncertainties are often overshadowed by simplified narratives and therapeutic expectations. Amid this uncertainty, clinical interpretation should prioritise reliable evidence over expectation-driven narratives. In this rapidly evolving landscape, regenerative therapies should be considered through a cautious, evidence-based, and guideline-informed lens. Current evidence does not support routine, indiscriminate, or first-line use of regenerative injections in knee OA. PRP may be discussed as a selective option for carefully selected patients after inadequate response to established conservative treatments, but uncertainty about the magnitude and durability of benefit, together with caveats related to reporting limitations, spin, and costs, should be clearly communicated to support shared decision-making. MSC-based and other cell-based therapies remain less established and require further rigorous evaluation before broader clinical adoption.

items.title: From standards to implementation: Applying lean thinking to redesign nutritional care in inflammatory bowel disease patients - the Italian PONTE project initiative.
items.abstract: Disease-related malnutrition is common in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), worsens clinical outcomes and remains inconsistently managed across Italy. The PONTE project aimed to develop a national, standardised pathway for nutritional care in IBD using Lean A3 methodology. A five-member multidisciplinary working group comprising clinical experts from the Italian Group for the Study of Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IG-IBD), the Italian Society of Artificial Nutrition and Metabolism (SINPE) and the Italian Society of Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (SINuC) and two healthcare-management engineers applied Lean A3 methodology through five structured meetings to map current care, identify root causes, develop countermeasures and define performance indicators. The analysis revealed fragmented screening, unclear professional responsibilities and regional disparities in access to nutritional care, with underlying criticalities grouped into three domains: training, organisation and governance. The working group developed a reproducible Lean-based pathway integrating systematic nutritional-risk screening, GLIM-based diagnostic assessment, a designated nutrition referent, graded management and referral to Clinical Nutrition, professional and patient education, digital documentation and performance indicators. PONTE translates quality standards into a practical, measurable framework for nutritional care in IBD, supporting earlier identification of malnutrition, more consistent referral and equitable access to nutritional services while providing a basis for prospective implementation and evaluation.

items.title: [Translated article] Farmastock: A collaborative tool for the reuse of high-cost hospital medications in a public healthcare system.
items.abstract: The loss of high-cost hospital medicines due to expiration represents a structural problem affecting the efficiency and sustainability of the public healthcare system. This loss is not solely the result of management inefficiencies; it is frequently driven by unpredictable changes in patient clinical evolution that lead to the suspension of previously planned treatments, particularly in oncological, haematological, and immunological conditions. To describe the economic and operational impact of the Farmastock web-based tool for the inter-hospital redistribution of high-economic impact medicines nearing expiration within the Public Health System of Andalusia (SSPA), and to analyse its evolution, its behaviour by hospital type and the perception of professional users. A retrospective observational descriptive study was conducted on transfers registered in Farmastock between July 2019 and June 2025. Descriptive indicators (volume of transfers, cost avoided, most redistributed medicines) and comparative indicators (hospital type, province, efficiency per transfer) were analysed. An anonymous structured survey of professional users was included (Annex 1). A total of 1,462 transfers were registered, avoiding €5,055,822.98 in spending and redistributing 93,741 units. The most frequently transferred ATC group was antineoplastic agents. The average value per transfer was €3,458.16. District hospitals led in volume, while specialised hospitals demonstrated greater efficiency per transfer. The tool was highly valued by users and its use expanded to 27 hospitals. The descriptive findings suggest that Farmastock is a useful and well-valued tool associated with a positive trend in health system sustainability. Beyond the estimated economic impact, it has enabled the utilisation of medicines in exceptional clinical situations, such as palivizumab administration in paediatric patients. Future integration with artificial intelligence and corporate platforms could further amplify its impact.

items.title: Registered Nurses' Vital Sign Assessment and Respiratory Rate Practices: A Think-Aloud Observational Study in Adult Medical and Surgical Wards.
items.abstract: To explore how registered nurses assess and prioritise vital signs during routine clinical care, with a particular focus on respiratory rate practice, using a think-aloud observational approach. Observational qualitative study. Registered nurses performing routine vital sign observations were directly observed across adult medical and surgical wards in two metropolitan Queensland hospitals. Observation encounters were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim to capture nurses' verbalised actions using the think-aloud technique. Brief post-observation debrief interviews explored the clinical reasoning underpinning measurement practices. Data were analysed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis, integrated with descriptive summaries of observational data and measurement sequencing. Fifteen nurses participated in 25 observation encounters. Blood pressure was measured first in 84% of encounters and functioned as an operational anchor for observation practice. Respiratory rate was visibly counted in only 16% of encounters, despite respiratory rate values being documented in all observation charts, raising concerns regarding discrepancies between observed and documented practice. Five themes were identified: (1) Clinical reasoning during patient assessment; (2) Blood pressure as the operational anchor of observation practice; (3) Workflow efficiency shaping observation practices; (4) Respiratory rate as a backgrounded vital sign; and (5) Knowledge-practice gap in respiratory rate assessment. Despite recognising respiratory rate as an early indicator of deterioration, nurses rarely prioritised its measurement. Vital sign assessment was embedded within broader clinical reasoning but appeared to be structured primarily by workflow efficiency and device-mediated monitoring, rather than physiological priority. Respiratory rate was routinely backgrounded, despite its recognised importance in detecting clinical deterioration. Improving the completeness and reliability of vital sign assessment may require system-level attention to workflow, monitoring and documentation practices, alongside education. Improving respiratory rate assessment may require addressing workflow structures and clinical routines that influence how vital signs are prioritised during bedside observations, rather than focusing on education alone. Patients or members of the public were not involved in the design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, or reporting of this study. The study focused on the observation of registered nurses' vital sign assessment practices in adult acute care settings.

items.title: A longitudinal multi-brood study reveals a developmental shift toward dominance of low-molecular-weight toxins in monocled cobra (Naja kaouthia) venom.
items.abstract: Snakebite envenomation is a critical public health issue, with Naja kaouthia representing a species of high medical importance. Despite its neurotoxic potential, the ontogenetic variability of its venom remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated three distinct captive broods across multiple developmental stages. Analysis of venom protein profiles (via SDS-PAGE and RP-HPLC) and enzymatic activities (, LAAO, proteases, and hyaluronidase) revealed that venom composition is strongly influenced by brood origin and age. A consistent ontogenetic pattern was observed: juvenile venoms were characterized by higher-molecular-weight components and elevated proteolytic, hyaluronidase, and LAAO activities, whereas adult venoms exhibited a progressive accumulation of low-molecular-weight proteins and increased activity. These findings highlight a progressive, time-dependent transition in venom composition and functionality, underscoring the value of longitudinal studies across developmental stages. Such ontogenetic characterization offers relevant translational insights, as age-related variations in toxin profiles may inform antivenom formulation strategies and provide useful guidance for bioprospecting efforts seeking specific bioactive compounds across distinct developmental stages.

items.title: Nasal Photodisinfection and Surgical Site Infection Following Coronary Bypass Surgery: An Interrupted Time Series Analysis.
items.abstract: Surgical site infections (SSI) complicating coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) carry substantial morbidity and mortality. We evaluated compliance with nasal decolonization and SSI rates after institutional implementation of preoperative nasal photodisinfection in isolated CABG. Single-centre interrupted time series (ITS) of 2,172 procedures (June 2023-January 2026, transition month June 2025), comprising 24 pre-intervention months (mupirocin era, n = 1,678) and 8 post-intervention months (photodisinfection era, n = 494). The primary effectiveness outcome was conduit harvest surgical site infection (CHSSI) at 30 days; compliance with nasal decolonization was the primary implementation outcome. Secondary outcomes included total surgical site infection (TSSI). Step changes in log-transformed monthly rates were analyzed using restricted maximum likelihood segmented regression accounting for first-order autocorrelation; compliance was modelled untransformed. Compliance with mupirocin was 35.4% (68.1% in elective patients; 17.5% in non-elective patients), compared with 93.3% compliance with nasal photodisinfection. Compliance rose 37.0 percentage points (95% CI 21.9-52.0). TSSI was 9.1% pre-intervention vs 5.9% post-intervention (change in intercept RR 0.32, 95% CI 0.09-1.15, p = 0.080). CHSSI was 3.6% pre-intervention vs 1.7% post-intervention (change in intercept RR 0.20, 95% CI 0.05-0.72, p = 0.014). CHSSI was decreased after exclusion of the transition month (June, 2025) but this was no longer statistically significant. ITS estimates for sternal outcomes were directionally consistent but did not reach significance. Photodisinfection achieved higher compliance than mupirocin and was associated with significant CHSSI reduction that reached significance in the primary analysis but was dependent on the partial-implementation month of June 2025.

items.title: Bacterial microbiota profiling of human-biting ticks in Yozgat Province, Türkiye.
items.abstract: In the present study, the bacterial microbiota of ticks infesting humans in Yozgat Province, Türkiye, was investigated. Ticks were collected from 54 patients who were presented to the Emergency Service of the Yozgat Bozok University Research and Training Hospital between March and November 2019. The following tick species were identified: Hyalomma marginatum, Rhipicephalus turanicus, Rhipicephalus bursa, Haemaphysalis parva, Dermacentor marginatus, and Hyalomma aegyptium. 16S rRNA libraries were prepared from tick DNA pools using a two-step PCR protocol targeting the V3-V4 region. In the second (indexing) PCR, dual Illumina indexes and adapters were added using the Nextera XT Index Kit. The resulting libraries were then sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq platform. A total of 3782 operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were identified; an average of 127,823 reads were obtained per sample, and an average of 31,561 reads were retained after taxonomic assignment. The OTUs were classified into 20 phyla, 41 classes, 94 orders, 168 families, 344 genera, and 452 putative species-level taxa. At the phylum level, Proteobacteria were predominant (averaging 63%), followed by Actinobacteriota and Bacteroidota (each approximately 10%) and Firmicutes (9%). At the class level, Alphaproteobacteria (average 37%) and Gammaproteobacteria (26%) exhibited the highest relative abundance, while at the order level, Rickettsiales (34%) and Francisellales (17%) were prominent. At the family and genus levels, the dominant taxa were identified as Rickettsiaceae (33%), Francisellaceae (17%), Rickettsia (33%), Francisella (17%), and Coxiella (7%), respectively. The most prevalent species included symbiotic bacteria such as Francisella sp. and Candidatus Midichloria mitochondrii. The Kruskal-Wallis test, conducted from phylum to genus level to evaluate taxonomic composition differences among tick species, revealed no statistically significant differences (p ≥ 0.05 for all comparisons). In alpha diversity analyses, no significant differences were found between tick species in terms of Shannon and Simpson indices (Shannon: H = 7.69; p = 0.26, Simpson: H = 8.07; p = 0.23). Similarly, no significant differences were observed between sex and developmental stages (Shannon: p = 0.86, Simpson: p = 0.73). The Chao1 and observed OTU values indicated higher richness trends, particularly in the Hyalomma marginatum and Hyalomma sp. pools. However, Spearman correlations between sample size and diversity indices were not significant (p > 0.05). These findings provide a baseline overview of the bacterial microbiota associated with human-biting ticks in Yozgat Province and may serve as a foundation for future studies employing higher-resolution methods to assess pathogen presence and public health risk.

items.title: Development and Preliminary Application of a Self-Management Intervention Program for Breast Cancer Patients with Totally Implantable Venous Access Ports (TIVAP) Based on Health Empowerment Theory: A 12-Week Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: To develop and evaluate the efficacy of a self-management intervention program based on Health Empowerment Theory for breast cancer patients with totally implantable venous access ports (TIVAP). This study adopted a prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial design. Breast cancer patients with TIVAP were recruited from tertiary hospitals and underwent longitudinal quantitative outcome assessments at four follow-up time points. This randomized controlled trial was retrospectively registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) on February 2, 2026 (registration number: ChiCTR2600118117). The intervention program was developed through literature review and expert consultation. A total of 54 participants were randomly assigned to the intervention group (n=27) and the control group (n=27). Three patients were lost to follow-up during the 12-week study, and 51 patients (intervention group, n=26; control group, n=25) were included in the final complete-case analysis. The primary outcome was patients' TIVAP self-management ability measured by the C-SUPPH. Secondary outcomes included health empowerment (CEQ), quality of life (EORTC QLQ-BR42), and TIVAP-related complications, which were assessed at baseline (T0), 4 weeks (T1), 8 weeks (T2), and 12 weeks (T3). Repeated-measures ANOVA was used to analyze longitudinal continuous outcomes, and the chi-square test was applied for categorical complication data. For key continuous outcomes, between-group mean differences with 95% confidence intervals were reported to quantify intervention effects and improve result interpretability, rather than relying solely on P-values. All statistical analyses were performed using SPSS 27.0, with P＜0.05 indicating statistical significance. The dropout rate was 5.56%. No significant between-group differences were observed at baseline (P>0.05). From T2 onward, CEQ and C-SUPPH scores were significantly higher in the intervention group than in the control group (P<0.05). Between-group differences in the QLQ-BR42 symptom domain emerged at T2, while differences in the functional domain emerged at T3. At T3, the complication rate was significantly lower in the intervention group (8%, 2/25) than in the control group (30.77%, 8/26; χ²=4.192, P<0.05). The intervention effectively reduced TIVAP-related complications and improved health empowerment, self-management efficacy, and quality of life among breast cancer patients, providing a targeted clinical nursing strategy.

items.title: Predictors of severe measles outcomes in hospitalized patients in Jerusalem, 2025.
items.abstract: Measles is a vaccine-preventable disease. Defining risk factors for poor outcomes in hospitalized patients can improve future measles outbreak preparedness. Data were collected on all confirmed measles cases that were evaluated at one of the emergency departments (ED) in the three main hospitals in Jerusalem from the first reported case of the current outbreak on April 10th to December 31st, 2025. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed using robust Poisson multivariable models to calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR) for hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and death. Among 786 individuals who visited the ED with confirmed measles, the rates of hospital admission (≥1 day), ICU, ECMO and death were 83.4%, 6.4%, 0.8%, and 1.4%, respectively. Complete data were available for 567 patients, of whom 303 (53.4%) were males. Median age was 2.1 years (IQR 1.2-3.8), and 474 (83.6%) were younger than 5 years. Most patients were unvaccinated (91.0%). Secondary infections were frequent, including lobar pneumonia (28.7%) and community-acquired bacteremia (3.5%). Respiratory support and severe dehydration were associated with hospital admission (IRR 1.4, 95% CI 1.3-1.5; p<0.001 and 9.5, 4.8-18.4; p<0.001, respectively) and ICU admission (IRR 1.3, 1.2-1.4; p<0.001 and 5.2, 2.1-12.4; p<0.001, respectively). Community-acquired bacteremia was associated with death or ECMO (IRR 44.5, 12.5-158.6; p<0.001). Despite high access to medical care in this urban setting, measles caused substantial morbidity and mortality. Respiratory compromise, severe dehydration, and bacteremia identified patients at increased risk of severe outcomes.

items.title: Cardiothoracic Surgery Training Attrition (2014-2023): Predictors, Trends, and Delay-Adjusted Rates Across Traditional and Integrated Pathways.
items.abstract: Resident attrition disrupts training pipelines and threatens cardiothoracic (CT) surgical workforce sustainability. This study quantifies national attrition rates and identifies predictors using trainee data from the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC), while accounting for reporting delays. We analyzed de-identified records of 1,476 CT surgery residents entering ACGME-accredited programs from 2014 to 2023. Attrition was defined as departure before expected completion. Rates were stratified by year, gender, citizenship, and training pathway: integrated (TS-I) versus traditional (TS). Multivariable logistic regression, LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost with nested cross-validation were used to identify predictors. A parametric nowcasting model corrected for administrative reporting lag. The overall attrition rate was 3.9% (57/1,476), significantly higher in the TS-I than the TS pathway (7.0% vs. 2.6%, p 36 group (aOR 6.05, 95% CI 1.87-19.62) compared with those ≤30 years. Gender and citizenship were not significant after adjustment. Model performance was consistent across methods (AUC 0.67-0.72). Delay-adjusted analyses corrected an apparent decline in recent cohorts, revealing a stable underlying rate with a 3-4-year reporting lag. Training pathways are the strongest predictor of CT resident attrition, with TS-I trainees at markedly higher risk. Correcting reporting delays is critical for accurate workforce planning. These findings support targeted retention interventions for at-risk trainees.

items.title: The Right Ventricle in Focus: State-of-the-Art CMR Imaging - Challenges, Standards, and Innovations.
items.abstract: The right ventricle (RV) is recognized as a critical contributor to cardiovascular outcomes. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) has emerged as the reference standard for comprehensive RV assessment, enabling precise evaluation of ventricular volumes, function, flow, and tissue characterization. In this review, we provide a state-of-the-art overview of RV imaging using CMR. We first outline the anatomical and physiological features that distinguish the RV from the left ventricle. Next, we highlight the key technical challenges in imaging the RV, notably its complex geometry, prominent trabeculation, and thin myocardial wall. We then summarize current clinical CMR approaches, including cine imaging for volumetric assessment, phase-contrast techniques for flow quantification, and methods for tissue characterization such as late gadolinium enhancement. Additionally, we discuss advanced and emerging CMR techniques aimed at overcoming current RV imaging limitations, including high-resolution three-dimensional cine imaging, four-dimensional flow imaging, parametric mapping, and novel reconstruction strategies. These innovations hold promise for improving accuracy, reproducibility, and mechanistic insight into RV structure and function. Finally, we review the clinical role of CMR in major RV pathologies, including congenital heart disease, pulmonary hypertension, arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, and tricuspid regurgitation. Across these conditions, CMR provides vital diagnostic and prognostic information, with growing evidence supporting its role in guiding clinical management. As technical advancements continue and standardization improves, CMR is poised to transform RV evaluation from a historically challenging endeavor into a precise and impactful component of cardiovascular care.

items.title: Supplementation with fortified balanced energy-protein during pregnancy and lactation and infant growth outcomes in southern Nepal: a community-based 2×2 factorial randomized trial.
items.abstract: Small-for-gestational age birth and infant linear growth faltering are prevalent in South Asia. The World Health Organization recommends balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplementation in pregnancy for undernourished populations, but evidence on the extension of supplementation through lactation to improve infant growth remains limited. To examine the effect of daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy and lactation on infant mean length-for-age z-score (LAZ) and secondary growth outcomes at 6 months of age. MINT (Maternal Infant Nutrition Trial) was a 2x2 factorial, household randomized, unblinded efficacy trial to assess a daily fortified BEP supplement during pregnancy and/or lactation compared to no supplement on birth and infant growth outcomes in Sarlahi, Nepal. A modified intention-to-treat analysis estimated the effects of supplementation on infant growth outcomes using linear and Poisson regression models. Models without and with adjustment for birth size were used to estimate the overall effect and the effect independent of birth size, respectively. Among 1,554 mothers and 1,568 infants randomized after delivery, there was no interaction between pregnancy and lactation supplementation on the primary infant growth outcome. Neither BEP supplementation during pregnancy nor lactation had an effect on mean infant LAZ at 6 months (unadjusted mean difference for pregnancy: 0.01 [95% CI: -0.10, 0.12]; for lactation -0.02 [95% CI: -0.13, 0.09]). Significant differences were not observed for any secondary outcomes: mean weight-for-length z-scores, weight-for-age z-scores, infant weight, length, head circumference, mid-upper arm circumference or prevalence of stunting, wasting, and underweight at 6-months or for a subset of infants at 12-months. Null effects persisted after adjustment for birth size. In rural Nepal, daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy or early lactation did not improve linear or ponderal growth of infants at 6- or 12-months. To reduce the burden of early infant growth faltering, alternative strategies should be considered. NCT03668977. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03668977?term=nct03668977&rank=1.

items.title: Food Allergy Impact on Military Excellence: Epidemiology and Operational Outcomes.
items.abstract: Food allergy (FA) commonly disqualifies applicants from United States military service, though military members diagnosed with FA during service often continue to serve. The impact of FA on military operations is unknown. We aim to investigate the impact of FA on military operations by examining epidemiologic trends, demographics, and severe outcomes. We completed a retrospective study including active-duty service members with diagnostic codes for food anaphylaxis, food allergy, and food adverse reactions between 2017 and 2024. We collected epidemiologic data, demographics, and outcomes including medical encounters and evacuations. FA prevalence increased over time, peaking at 33,557 or approximately 2.4% of service members in 2024. FA prevalence was higher in women (4.5%), Black individuals (3.7%), individuals with either longer time in service or >2 deployments (3.9-4%). Prevalence was lower in Marines (1.2%), pilots/aircrew (1.9%), and combat/artillery/infantry (1.5%). In total over our 8-year study there were 4,275 emergency department (ED) visits, 143 hospitalizations, and 7 medical evacuations, averaging approximately 534 ED visits, 18 hospitalizations, and less than one medical evacuation annually. This study examining FA in the military reveals that although prevalence has increased, FA-related hospitalizations and medical evacuations remain uncommon. Although military accession policy nominally disqualifies many individuals with FA from service, the prevalence of FA in service members has increased over time. Based on our results, FA-related severe outcomes such as hospitalizations and medical evacuations are rare and do not currently pose substantial risk to military operations, supporting possible revision to current accession policy.

items.title: Early Sudden Cardiac Death Risk in Heart Failure: Time to Rethink Primary Prevention?
items.abstract: Despite advances in drug and device-based therapies, patients with heart failure (HF) face a substantial risk for mortality. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) accounts for up to half of all deaths in patients with HF and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), with a 6- to 9-fold higher risk compared with the general population. Recent data demonstrate that the risk for arrhythmic events cluster disproportionately more frequently within the first ∼6 months following the diagnosis of HFrEF despite the initiation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). This period is characterized by electrical instability, neurohormonal activation, and incomplete reverse remodeling; this is exacerbated by suboptimal exposure to GDMT. While temporal analyses suggest an overall decline in SCD rates in patients with chronic HFrEF, a persistent residual SCD risk that is clinically meaningful remains. While pharmacologic therapies reduce the risk for SCD to varying degrees, structural recovery often lags, creating a vulnerable phase during GDMT up-titration. Current guidelines mandate a waiting period of at least 3-6 months prior to implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) implantation to allow for potential ventricular recovery while GDMT is optimized. Moreover, the indication for primary prevention ICD implantation itself is being actively re-evaluated in the contemporary GDMT era. Yet this interval also exposes patients to an early arrhythmic risk, contributing to clinical apprehension. Wearable cardioverter defibrillators (WCD) may provide a noninvasive strategy to mitigate transient early SCD risk during guideline-mandated waiting periods. WCD platforms have demonstrated reliable arrhythmia detection and defibrillation capability, with high first-shock conversion rates and wear-time adherence in large-scale studies performed in clinical practice. WCDs enable continuous rhythm surveillance, which may support individualized decision-making regarding the timing of a permanent ICD implantation. This review synthesizes the contemporary burden and mechanisms of SCD in HFrEF and how approaches to primary prevention have evolved including an appraisal of the impact of GDMT on arrhythmic risk, current guideline recommendations, and examining the potential role of WCD therapy for protection during early phase vulnerability in these patients.

items.title: Developmental exposure to PBDE-47 induces sex- and organ-specific glucose uptake alterations linked to thyroid hormone disruption in rats: phenotypic parallels to early cardiorenal-metabolic crosstalk.
items.abstract: 2, 2', 4, 4'-Tetrabromodiphenyl ether (PBDE-47) is a ubiquitous persistent organic pollutant with developmental toxicity and thyroid-disrupting activity. Increasing evidence links PBDE-47 exposure to metabolic disorders, yet it remains unclear whether developmental PBDE-47 exposure disturbs glucose metabolism in multiple organs of offspring and how thyroid hormone (TH) changes relate to such effects. Using a rat model of perinatal PBDE-47 exposure, organ-specific glucose metabolism were assessed via positron emission tomography with the 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) tracer. Adult male offspring exhibited increased FDG uptake in the heart but decreased uptake in the brain and kidneys, whereas female offspring showed elevated uptake in the brain and kidneys and reduced cardiac FDG uptake. These changes were accompanied by sex-specific TH alterations, with increased T3 in males and decreased T3 and T4 in females. Correlation analyses revealed significant associations between TH levels and organ-specific FDG uptake. Intriguingly, these coordinated metabolic and endocrine disruptions exhibited early phenotypic parallels to features of the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework. Network toxicology identified 89 core targets, with PIK3CB, PIK3R1, PIK3R2, PLCG1, and PLCG2 as hub molecules enriched in apoptosis, endocrine signaling, insulin resistance, and central carbon metabolism pathways. Molecular docking suggested high-affinity binding of PBDE-47 to these targets, and gene set analysis further implicated PI3K/AKT, insulin receptor signaling, and the AGE-RAGE pathway. Collectively, this study suggests that perinatal PBDE-47 exposure elicits sex-specific multi-organ alterations in FDG uptake that correlate with TH disruption, providing a hypothesis-generating basis for developmental metabolic toxicity and highlighting phenotypic parallels to early cardiorenal-metabolic crosstalk.

items.title: Early-Life NO 2 Exposure and developmental coordination disorder in Preschool Children: A Cross-sectional Study.
items.abstract: Although air pollution is a potential neurotoxicant, evidence linking early-life nitrogen dioxide (NO2) exposure to motor development remains inconsistent, and large-scale studies are limited. This cross-sectional study investigated associations of prenatal and postnatal NO2 exposure with motor coordination performance and suspected developmental coordination disorder (DCD) risk among 105,280 children aged 3-5 years from Chinese National Cohort of Motor Development. Motor coordination was assessed using the Little DCD Questionnaire (LDCDQ). NO2 exposure was estimated using a high-resolution satellite-based random forest model. Linear mixed-effects models and generalized linear mixed models with a binomial distribution were applied to evaluate associations with LDCDQ scores and suspected DCD risk, respectively. Per interquartile range (IQR) increase in NO2 during the first trimester and from birth to 36 months, LDCDQ scores decreased by 0.20 (95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.08, -0.31) and 0.10 (95% CI: -0.02, -0.19), respectively. Odds ratios for suspected DCD were 1.07 (95% CI: 1.03, 1.11) for first-trimester exposure and 1.04 (95% CI: 1.004, 1.07) for birth-to-18-month exposure. Among three LDCDQ subdomains, general coordination showed the strongest association. Associations appeared to be stronger among boys. These findings suggest that early-life NO2 exposure may adversely affect motor coordination development of preschoolers, though the modest effect sizes were observed.

items.title: Early pregnancy exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and phthalates: linear and nonlinear associations with fetal growth in a Chinese birth cohort.
items.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that combined prenatal exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and phthalates (PAEs) may interfere with fetal development, yet relevant evidence based on fetal growth measures covering the transition phase from mid to late gestation remains limited. In this study, we enrolled 811 pregnant women from the Zunyi Birth Cohort and detected urinary metabolites of OH-PAHs and mPAEs in early pregnancy. Fetal growth measures including head circumference (HC), biparietal diameter (BPD), abdominal circumference (AC), femur length (FL), and placental thickness (PT) were collected at 14 to 27 weeks of gestation. Linear regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were used to explore linear and nonlinear relationships between exposure levels and fetal growth outcomes, and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) was further adopted to assess the combined effect of pollutant mixtures and screen core pollutants. RCS models revealed distinct linear and nonlinear exposure-response relationships for various pollutants. Supplementary RCS analyses using LOD-constrained truncated multiple imputation (truncated MI) indicated that overall exposure-outcome trends were largely consistent with the LOD/√2 substitution approach. Truncated MI was used to address measurement uncertainty within the low-exposure range. BKMR analyses found that the PAHs mixture was negatively associated with PT at the 75th percentile, with 1-OHPYR identified as the primary contributing component. For the combined PAH and PAE mixtures, MBP was positively associated with abdominal circumference z-scores (AC-z) at low concentrations, while MEP showed a negative association with AC-z at high concentrations.

items.title: Combined effects of LINE-1 DNA methylation and exposure to metals on renal cell carcinoma.
items.abstract: Exposure to heavy metals and trace elements is associated with renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Methylation of long interspersed nuclear element-1 (LINE-1), a surrogate marker of global DNA methylation, has also been linked to metal exposure and cancer-related outcomes; however, no studies have examined the combined effects of metal exposure and LINE-1 methylation on RCC. We evaluated the association between LINE-1 methylation and RCC and its pairwise combined effects with metals. We conducted a clinic-based case-control study of 204 incident RCC cases and 715 non-cancer controls, frequency-matched by age and sex. Cadmium and lead concentrations in red blood cells (RBC) and selenium concentrations in plasma were quantified, and LINE-1 methylation levels in blood leukocyte DNA were measured by pyrosequencing. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for associations of LINE-1 methylation and metal concentrations with RCC. Combined effects of each metal with LINE-1 methylation were assessed on an additive scale. LINE-1 methylation and RBC cadmium were positively associated with RCC, whereas plasma selenium was inversely associated with RCC. The odds of elevated LINE-1 methylation (highest tertile) were 5.79 times greater among RCC cases than controls (95%CI=3.48-9.61). The odds of both high RBC cadmium and high LINE-1 methylation were 16.45 times greater among RCC cases than controls (95%CI=8.12-33.30), and the OR-based interaction measures suggested a potential positive departure from additivity. The point estimates of additive interaction between low plasma selenium and high LINE-1 methylation were consistent with a positive departure from additivity, although the estimates were imprecise. Our study suggests a potential positive additive interaction between LINE-1 methylation and cadmium for RCC, whereas the findings for selenium require cautious interpretation. These findings support the consideration of epigenetic factors when evaluating associations between metals and RCC.

items.title: A mysterious danger for kidney disease exacerbations: short-term impacts of ultrafine particles on hospital visits.
items.abstract: Ultrafine particles (UFPs) are more toxic than fine particulate matter (PM2.5) but are generally ignored. Limited health research existed on UFPs, especially for kidney diseases. We investigated if UFPs could increase kidney-disease related hospital emergency department (ED) visits. Time-stratified case-crossover design was used for evaluating the short-term impacts of UFP. Daily exposure to UFPs was assessed by a previously validated chemical transport model. ED visits with principal diagnosis of kidney diseases, geocoded at street level, from 2013-2018, were obtained from New York State hospital discharge database covering 95% of all hospitals. Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate the excess risks (%ER) for every inter-quartile range (IQR) change (ERIQR). Among 269,945 ED visits, increasing kidney-disease ED visits were associated with UFPs on individual lag 1 day and all cumulative lag days (lag 0-1 to lag 0-6). The ER of ED visits peaked on lag 0-3 days (ERIQR = 0.74, 95% confidence interval: 0.28, 1.20). Stronger associations were found among non-African American, older adults (> 65 yrs.), during days with high temperatures, low humidity, and fall/winter season. Our findings suggested the kidney toxicity of UFPs and suggest that routine measures should be taken to monitor UFP concentration and control its emission.

items.title: Intracity-scale study reveals spatiotemporal variation of urban airborne microbiota and dynamics of antibiotic resistance/virulence genes.
items.abstract: Airborne microbiota are critical to urban air quality and public health, yet their spatiotemporal differentiation, community assembly, and profiles of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence factor genes (VFGs) across urban functional zones remain poorly characterized. In this study, monthly 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing was combined with seasonal metagenomic profiling of 12 composite samples and environmental data to investigate airborne microbiota at three sites representing commercial, industrial, and recreational zones in Changsha, China. Airborne communities showed similar spatial patterns among the investigated functional zones but strong seasonal variation, with Shannon diversity below 2.0 in July and above 6.0 in January. Proteobacteria dominated most samples, while key seasonal taxa shifted among Delftia, Cupriavidus, and Achromobacter. Neutral community modeling supported stochastic dominance (R2 = 0.664, Nm = 1,200), with 92.6% of operational taxonomic units within the 95% confidence interval. However, βNTI and RCbray analyses indicated increased deterministic selection in autumn-winter, coinciding with high pressure and pollutant accumulation. Metagenomics identified 25 ARG, 14 VFG, and 6 mobile genetic element (MGE) categories, with season explaining 53.9% of VFG compositional differences. Exploratory structural equation modeling identified associations between MGE abundance and ARG/VFG abundances (β = 0.75 and 1.09, respectively; both P < 0.001). Binning and contig co-localization showed that ARG-VFG-MGE co-harboring fragments were potentially affiliated with opportunistic pathogens such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae, indicating potential biosafety concerns. These findings identify season as a key driver of urban airborne microbiota and genetic risk factors, providing a basis for atmospheric biosafety monitoring and assessment.

items.title: Exploring "equigenesis" in the association between the natural outdoor environment, mental health and death by suicide before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: a population-based cohort study of more than 2 million records in Northern Ireland.
items.abstract: Recent evidence suggests that the natural outdoor environment (NOE) may mitigate socioeconomic inequalities in mental health, but it remains unclear how such associations vary between the pandemic and the non-pandemic period. Therefore, this study focused on the association between NOE and inequalities in mental health before and during the pandemic. We used a population-based cohort of individuals in Northern Ireland (NI), including more than 2 million General Practice participants from 2017 to 2022. NOE was assessed using the proportion of blue space and green space within the administrative neighbourhoods, respectively. Mental health outcomes included death by suicide, mental health-related hospital admissions and prescriptions. We applied multilevel Cox proportional hazards and logistic regressions. Further, we stratified the analysis by area-level deprivation index. The analyses were performed for the pre-pandemic (2017-2019) and during the pandemic (2020-2022), respectively. People living in neighbourhoods with a higher proportion of NOE (e.g., 4th quintile of blue space) had lower odds of being in receipt of mental-health-related prescriptions (e.g., pre-pandemic: OR=0.835, 95% CI=0.796-0.874; intra-pandemic: OR=0.802, 95% CI=0.763-0.844) and a lower risk of dying by suicide (e.g., pre-pandemic: HR=0.634, 95% CI=0.451-0.890; intra-pandemic: HR=0.684, 95% CI=0.469-0.998). However, there is no evidence that NOE is related to a lower risk of having a mental health-related hospital admission (e.g., pre-pandemic: OR=1.053, 95% CI=0.794-1.396; intra-pandemic: OR=1.044, 95% CI=0.778-1.401). The association between NOE and mental health-related hospital admissions, as well as the association between NOE and prescriptions, was more pronounced in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighbourhoods, especially during the pandemic. However, such "equigenesis" was only observed for death by suicide before the pandemic. Therefore, NOE may mitigate socioeconomic inequalities in mental health, especially during the pandemic. Our findings demonstrate the importance of sufficient NOE to support better and more equal mental health and preparedness for future pandemics.

items.title: How Might PBL 4.0 Be Practiced? Initial Operational Tools And Templates For Core Competence Development
items.abstract: This file contains three different documents that are normally individually shared with tutors as well as students. They serve as practical illustrations of how PBL 4.0 might be practices and hopefully thus exemplify the accompanying WHAT and WHY PBL 4.0 documents. Readers of the WHAT document will recognize its central distinction (AI-supported cognition versus epistemic outsourcing) running throughout this manual in more practical form: the recurring rule that you think, design, and analyze first, and only then use GenAI to extend that work. Respectively the three documents are: 1) First steps and tips for designing PBL workshops with some help from GenAI 2) Participation and feedback philosophy (page 42 and onwards) 3) Examples of core academic competencies per sessions (page 45 and onwards)

items.title: What Is PBL 4.0? Generative Epistemic Inquiry As A Framework For AI-Augmented Learning
items.abstract: Problem-Based Learning remains one of higher education’s most significant pedagogical contributions. Its core premise (that students learn more effectively, particularly for the application, transfer, and retention of knowledge, when actively engaging with problems than passively receiving information) is as valid as ever. What has changed is the environment: organisations restructuring around AI, professional roles shifting from execution to oversight, and civic life requiring disciplined reasoning in information environments that actively resist it. Many implementations of PBL, particularly at large scale, have not kept pace. Neither, in many cases, have the institutions responsible for it (optimising for procedural consistency, satisfaction scores, and completion rates) imperatives that solved real problems of equity and scalability, but that under certain conditions can create incentives that gradually erode exactly the challenge that makes education worth having. This document proposes a response and makes the case that the response is timely, practically feasible, and already taking shape in practice. What PBL 4.0 is. Generative Epistemic Inquiry adds a dimension that earlier PBL stages often did not reach: the collective interrogation of the assumptions and mechanisms underlying knowledge claims, rather than their application or reproduction. Students do not explain what theories say; they examine what those theories assume, and under what conditions they hold. The primary targets are epistemic agency and ontological reasoning. A practical classroom heuristic, Marginal Analytical Value (MAV), makes these concrete: a contribution earns its primary analytic credit if it advances collective reasoning beyond what any attentive reader could produce alone; with capable AI systems serving as a vivid contemporary illustration of where that baseline now sits. Clarifying, summarising, and connecting contributions retain their proper role; MAV simply names the upper bar against which deeper engagement is calibrated. This is a higher bar than most PBL currently sets, yet vital for the age of GenAI. Why the same competencies solve three problems at once. AI systems generate false positives and false negatives; detecting and acting on those errors requires domain-grounded, first-principles reasoning; not tool fluency. Meanwhile, AI is restructuring organisations in ways that remove the entry-level rungs through which junior employees have always developed practical judgment, raising the floor of what competence must look like on day one (this organisational forecast is actively debated; PBL 4.0’s argument does not depend on it materialising in the strongest form). And contemporary civic life requires citizens who can reason carefully in environments saturated with contested and manipulated information. These are not three separate problems. They are one convergence and the competencies PBL 4.0 develops (epistemic agency, argumentation, evidence evaluation, ontological reasoning) are precisely the ones that professional oversight, organisational survival, and civic participation all now require. In various fields and educational traditions, it has been mentioned that first-principles competencies are also the most durable investment in a fast-changing world: argumentation theory and the scientific method have remained functionally stable across centuries of technological upheaval, which is the opposite of the tool, or even specific theories, landscape. PBL 4.0 is not just a response to AI. It is a response to what AI reveals about competences higher education has long claimed to develop and has not always succeeded in developing under scale. How it works, and what makes it different. Eight integrated design principles together are designed to produce something that none of its parts contains separately. Strategic ambiguity (i.e., deliberately withheld resolution) requires students to determine what is actually at stake before solutions can be considered, introduced gradually through scaffolding and fading as capacity develops. The student-as-facilitator model rotates the responsibility for designing and leading sessions across the group: the preparation this demands is qualitatively different from anything participation alone produces. A learning contract at the start of each cycle establishes not just behavioural norms but a shared competency orientation (where each member is starting from, what the group needs to develop, and how the session design responds to that) making genuinely tailor-made learning environments possible rather than merely promised. Rotating Epistemic Observers make the group’s reasoning patterns visible in real time. AI is positioned as a preparation-phase analytical partner, engaged only after independent human analysis: the machine stress-tests, it does not originate. The assessment architecture addresses directly what most institutions avoid naming (namely that the current configuration of grade fear and evaluation asymmetry can produce a mutual performance of the relationship rather than the thing itself) and proposes structural alternatives rather than individual heroism. A layered competency-tracking system makes development visible from individual session to programme level, without adding administrative burden. The result is a learning environment that is adaptive, presence-based, and genuinely responsive to the specific group in the room; the things online formats and traditional lectures structurally cannot offer. How to adopt it. PBL 4.0 is a menu, not a mandate. Each element has independent value; a course that adopts three of them is already a materially different course. A course at PBL 2.5 or 3.7 is not failing; yet hopefully it is in motion and this framework gives guidelines for how to do so. However, while not required, full integration is designed to produce something emergent: a learning environment whose character becomes visible only from a distance, and which represents PBL’s most complete realisation of what it has always promised. The purpose. Every design choice in this document is ultimately made for the student in the room, and for the organizations and societies they will enter. The framework is therefore modular and architectural as these stakeholders vary in their needs. Overall, PBL 4.0 aims not to just credential students, but to develop them: into professionals who can reason from first principles when the theories and model fail, into people with a genuine internal locus of control rather than a performance orientation calibrated to the nearest evaluator, into thinkers robust enough to hold uncertainty without collapsing it prematurely and resilient enough to learn from failure rather than avoid it. The old ideal of the homo universalis (invoked here only for its core insight that depth across multiple fields produces a qualitatively different capacity to navigate genuinely novel territory — not for its historically narrow class, gender, and cultural framing) is not an historical luxury. In an age of rapid AI-driven change, the underlying competence it names (capabilities that are grounded rather than merely trained) is a personal, professional, and civic necessity. As such, a mastery orientation, adaptive reasoning, epistemic independence, and the kind of character that sustained intellectual difficulty actually builds: these are what PBL 4.0 is designed to develop. What this integrated framework is thus building toward are resilient, robust, and self-directed persons.

items.title: Mistrust, uncertainty, fear, and vaccine acceptability: quasi-experimental data from the United Kingdom and Portugal during the COVID-19 pandemic
items.abstract: Using a quasi-experimental design, this study tests a cognitive-affective model of vaccine acceptability focusing on the effects of relationships between trust, certainty, attitudes, and fear in a sample of 1132 adults in the UK (N = 648 [51.7%]) and Portugal (N = 486 [48.3%]) during the COVID-19 pandemic. A path model of the relationships between the variables was assessed using structural equation modeling. Participants in the experimental condition were asked to list what they thought were the major societal uncertainties concerning the COVID-19 vaccines (N = 566 [49.9%]). When subsequently asked, those in the experimental condition reported lower vaccine certainty than those in the control condition (N = 568 [50.1%]). Across the entire sample, lower vaccine certainty was associated with lower vaccine acceptability. Higher vaccine uncertainty was associated with less negativity toward vaccine refusers (which in turn was associated with lower vaccine acceptability). In addition to the direct positive effect of trust in science and scientists upon vaccine acceptability, there were mediated effects: higher trust in science and scientists was associated with higher fear. Fear was positively associated with vaccine certainty. Fear was also positively associated with negativity toward vaccine refusers. The results suggest that, in health crises, people may be more susceptible to identify with other vaccine refusers (and potentially ‘anti-vaxxer’ groups) if levels of uncertainty and mistrust are higher, thereby undermining vaccine uptake. The study makes an original contribution to the literature on vaccine acceptability by showing that vaccine certainty (and changes in vaccine acceptability) can be modified by a single intervention that asks people to describe what they think are important vaccine uncertainties. Furthermore, by examining the relationship of attitudes to ‘anti-vaxxers’ with the cognitive-affective model of vaccine acceptability, the research indicates the potential significance of uncertainty and fear upon social attitudes.
