items.title: Effects of Grit and Major Satisfaction on Metacognition in Nursing Students
items.abstract: This study examined the relationships among grit, major satisfaction, and metacognition among nursing students and identified key factors influencing metacognition.A descriptive survey design was employed.Data were collected from nursing students enrolled at a university in a designated region and analyzed using SPSS/WIN 26.0.Descriptive statistics, including frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations, were utilized to analyze general characteristics and main study variables.Differences in key variables based on participants' general characteristics were examined using independent t-tests and one-way ANOVA, followed by Scheffé's test for post-hoc analysis.Pearson's correlation coefficients were used to evaluate relationships among grit, major satisfaction, and metacognition.Finally, multiple linear regression was conducted to identify the primary predictors of metacognition.The findings demonstrated significant positive correlations among grit, major satisfaction, and metacognition in nursing students.Specifically, higher levels of grit and major satisfaction were associated with enhanced metacognitive capacity.Personality traits, grit, and major satisfaction were also identified as significant factors influencing metacognition.The regression model accounted for 61.2% of the explanatory variance, indicating strong predictive power.The results suggest that to effectively enhance metacognitive abilities in nursing students, educational strategies must consider individual personality characteristics.Furthermore, tailored educational interventions and multifaceted extracurricular programs should be developed and implemented to reinforce grit-defined as passion and perseverance for long-term goals-and to elevate overall major satisfaction, ultimately fostering more self-directed and competent future healthcare professionals.

items.title: Critically about the descriptive category "Generation Z"
items.abstract: Cel pracy Wartość naukowa kategorii opisowych w badaniach determinuje jakość wyników. Zarządzanie, jako nauka stosowana, stoi przed wyzwaniem przekształcania popularnych słów, używanych w organizacjach, w rygorystyczne kategorie naukowe. Niniejsze badanie koncentruje się na kategorii „Pokolenie Z”, dążąc do zapewnienia trójstopniowej weryfikacji jej wartości w dziedzinie zarządzania zasobami ludzkimi. Materiał i metody Zastosowanie podejścia mieszanego, w badaniu integruje analizy jakościowe i ilościowe dostosowane do wymagań każdego podcelu badawczego. Kluczowym punktem odniesienia dla syntezy i interpretacji danych jest paradygmat relacyjny. Z niego wynikają również wskazówki dla wykorzystania wyników badania Wyniki Kategoria „Pokolenie Z” została oceniona pod kątem trafności, wiarygodności i użyteczności. Wyniki określają wartość naukową i pragmatyczną kategorii „Pokolenia Z”. Zidentyfikowano także jego, potwierdzone przez respondentów, cechy. Wnioski Ponadto badanie zakłada, że wartość tej kategorii zależy od procesu jej społecznej i naukowej konstrukcji. Zamiast postrzegać etykietę jako nietrafiony deskryptor demograficzny, można ją w zarządzaniu wykorzystać do wspierania spójności organizacyjnej. Ta zmiana perspektywy – przejście od popularnego deskryptora do narzędzia rozwoju zarządzania zasobami ludzkimi – stanowi oryginalny, oparty na dowodach wkład, który wypełnia lukę między dyskursem powszechnym a rygorem naukowym.

items.title: A Qualitative Study on Nursing Students Understanding of Learning Content and peer Experience Through Participating in Role Play
items.abstract: This study aimed to explore nursing students' experiences of understanding course topics and peer relationships through participation in Role-Playing activities.It also examined the significance of these Role-Playing experiences in shaping students' academic self-efficacy and professional nursing competencies.The researchers collected data through reflective journals and in-depth interviews with 12 nursing students who participated in an Adult Health Nursing course.The collected data were analyzed using a phenomenological research method.The study results revealed the following: First, participants experienced an "enhanced understanding" of the diseases covered in the course topics while preparing for and performing the role-play.Second, through the interaction and collaboration required for preparation, they developed a sense of "closeness and respect" toward peers they had not previously known well.Third, while constructing case studies and writing scenarios based on the diseases in the curriculum, they experienced "empathy and a shift in perception" regarding the professional attitudes required of future nurses.Fourth, through the role-playing activities, they gained a fresh perspective on learning, interpersonal relationships, and the nursing profession, resulting in a satisfying experience of "discovering meaning."Based on these findings, the following suggestions are made: First, major courses should use diverse participatory teaching and learning methods, such as Role-Playing, rather than relying solely on traditional lectures.In particular, given the current educational landscape that incorporates various learning materials and technologies (including generative AI), it is essential to create an environment that encourages active student participation and moves away from passive knowledge transmission.Second, to conduct role-playing activities effectively, integrate pre-and postlearning sessions that build understanding of the relevant medical conditions.This integrated learning helps alleviate the difficulties learners face when developing case studies and scenarios suited to the role-play themes, transforming challenges into positive insights gained through peer interaction and enhancing academic selfefficacy by allowing repeated review and deeper engagement with the material.Furthermore, systematic learning through role play can serve as an effective teaching-learning strategy to improve nursing students' clinical competence, thereby contributing to the cultivation of the essential skills required of future professional nurses.

items.title: Gene tree conflict between genomic and functional partitions impacts phylogenetic inference in Zygophylloideae
items.abstract: Abstract The Zygophyllaceae subfamily Zygophylloideae includes seven genera and around 180 species distributed worldwide particularly in arid areas where they show adaptations to drought including C 4 and CAM photosynthesis. Phylogenetic relationships of Zygophylloideae have been analysed in several studies using Sanger sequenced markers, but none have been able to resolve all deeper relationships between genera in the subfamily. Here, we use ion semi-conductor sequencing of chloroplast and nuclear ribosomal regions to analyse these relationships and assess why they have proved so challenging to resolve. We sequenced 39 chloroplast genes and nuclear ribosomal 18S, 5.8S, and 26S genes and internal transcribed spacers (ITS) for key species of Zygophyllum sensu stricto, Roepera, Tetraena, Fagonia , Zygophyllum stapffii and monotypic Augea capensis ; and Tribulus of the subfamily Tribuloideae as outgroup. We aligned these with data from published chloroplast genomes followed by phylogenetic analyses using Maximum Likelihood and Bayesian approaches, summarising phylogenetic results separately for non-coding introns and intergenic spacers, and for genes that are, or are not, involved in photosynthesis. We combined the chloroplast data with sequences of three highly variable noncoding chloroplast regions used in previous studies of greater numbers of taxa, and similarly the nuclear ribosomal data with more densely sampled ITS sequences and assessed whether adding such data resulted in improved support for consistent topologies. We used a chloroplast sequence matrix to infer a dated phylogeny. Adding data did not always improve phylogenetic resolution which was apparently impacted by non-informative variation in chloroplast photosynthesis related genes as well as by conflicting chloroplast and nuclear signals. Chloroplast genes not related to photosynthesis provide robust support for a topology that is consistent with independent data and may therefore represent a useful species tree hypothesis. The cause of the gene tree conflicts remains unclear: potential explanations include functional constraints in photosynthesis related genes and introgressive hybridization and/or incomplete lineage sorting during an ancient rapid divergence. Further testing will require a broader sampling of lineages with different photosynthetic modes and multiple informative, independent, and selectively neutral gene trees.

items.title: Contribution of fine roots on carbon allocation patterns in Norwegian forests
items.abstract: Abstract. Boreal forests play a key role in the global carbon (C) cycle, with fine root production and turnover contributing to belowground C fluxes and inputs to soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. However, fine root biomass and production are difficult to quantify and introduce uncertainty in estimates of net primary production (NPP), limiting the assessment of C allocation patterns in boreal forests. The objective of the present study was to assess how different fine root modelling approaches influence estimates of NPP, gross primary production (GPP), carbon use efficiency (CUE), and belowground C allocation to fine roots in Norwegian boreal and nemo-boreal forests. Using Norway’s national forest resource map together with MODIS remote sensing data, we estimated fine root biomass and production using three approaches that differed in how foliage biomass was derived: two based on leaf area index (from MODIS or the forest resource map) and one based on allometric biomass equations. These approaches were combined with alternative fine-root turnover rates and foliage-to-fine-root biomass ratios. Mean NPP derived from the forest resource map ranged from 318 to 243 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ across young to mature forests. In Norway spruce and Scots pine forests, NPP increased during early stand development, peaked between 50 and 80 years, and declined with increasing age. Comparison against European MODIS NPP revealed that tree growth alone accounted for 16 % of MODIS NPP, while including fine root and understory NPP contributions increased total NPP by roughly 3–5 times, depending on the fine root estimation method. CUE ranged from 0.30 to 0.63, showing age-related declines and species-level variation, with the lowest values in mature Norway spruce forests. Our analysis sheds light on the role of fine root biomass and production in forest C budgeting and their influence on NPP, CUE, and belowground C allocation. Excluding fine roots creates a major gap in forest C analyses and we conclude that the choice of method for fine root estimation has a strong impact on regional NPP and its component fluxes. Estimates of forest CUE may guide management by identifying areas with low efficiency, where interventions may enhance C sequestration.

items.title: Water Quality Assessment of Sisauli Wetland of Morang District, Nepal
items.abstract: Wetlands provide essential ecosystem services, including biodiversity conservation, water purification, nutrient cycling, and hydrological regulation. Assessing their water quality is therefore important for understanding environmental conditions and informing conservation priorities. This study evaluated the post-monsoon water quality of Sisauli Wetland in Morang District, Nepal, using selected physicochemical parameters to characterize aquatic conditions and identify monitoring needs. Water samples were collected from five representative sites following standard sampling procedures. Temperature, pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), and dissolved oxygen (DO) were measured in situ, whereas the remaining physicochemical parameters were analyzed in the laboratory using standard methods. Recorded values included a temperature of 30.2 °C, pH of 8.5, TDS of 92.2 ppm, and DO of 9.64 mg/L. Total alkalinity was 92 mg/L, while nitrate, nitrite, ammonium, and iron concentrations were 6.8, 0.48, 0.02, and 0.26 mg/L, respectively. The results characterized the sampled water as well oxygenated, with low dissolved solids, alkaline conditions, and alkalinity indicating buffering capacity. Nevertheless, the reported nitrite concentration and localized alkaline conditions warrant periodic monitoring to determine their persistence and ecological significance. The measurements provide a baseline for understanding post-monsoon physicochemical conditions, while conclusions about overall ecological health remain limited by the parameters assessed and the seasonal scope of sampling. Continued assessment across seasons, supported by biological indicators, would strengthen the evaluation of wetland condition and potential environmental pressures. The study recommends regular monitoring of nutrients, pH, and DO, together with effective conservation measures, to detect changes in water quality and support the long-term ecological integrity of Sisauli Wetland.

items.title: Locally Available Beans as an Alternative Low-Cost Nutrient Source for Yanagi (Agrocybe aegerita) Mushroom Culture in the Philippines
items.abstract: Mushroom farming provides economic opportunities, but in the Philippines, the high cost of commercial culture media hinders its development. This study aimed to determine whether locally available beans could serve as a cheaper nutrient source for cultivating Agrocybe aegerita in Tabuk City. In this study, researchers measured the mycelial diameter of A. aegerita on five media: Water Agar (T−), Potato Dextrose Agar (T+), and black bean (T1), mung bean (T2), and white bean (T3) agar. A One-Way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD test was applied at the 5% significance level. The species was identified on the basis of its appearance, and the media were prepared by boiling the beans to obtain a broth. The results indicated that PDA (T+) gave the greatest mycelial diameter (49.63 ± 13.28 mm), followed by black bean (31.87 ± 0.517 mm), mung bean (29.09 ± 0.522 mm), and white bean (27.19 ± 0.522 mm) agars. All the legume-based media outperformed the negative control. Higher humidity also slightly inhibited mycelial growth. Although PDA remained the most effective, agars made from black, mung, and white beans are viable alternatives. The study suggests that further research should be carried out to improve methods of media preparation and to promote affordable mushroom production in rural and low-resource areas.

items.title: River Health Assessment of the Ganga River via Geomorphic Metrics: The Anthropocene Context
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Rivers, particularly large river systems, constitute one of the most fundamental life‐support systems that have sustained civilisations and are projected to be a critical determinant for the future sustenance of human civilisations. A river can be termed a healthy ecosystem only when all the flora and fauna are in and along the river, the cultivation in floodplains is healthy, and the river's form is in equilibrium. The Ganga River system in India is a large river system with high geodiversity and biodiversity, where about one‐third of India's population depends on the river directly or indirectly. This study focuses on the development of a Geomorphic River Health Index (gRHI) based on eight geomorphic attributes derived from geospatial data, including sinuosity, braid‐channel ratio, width/depth ratio, occupancy, floodplain development, bar density, bar complexity and stream power. The selected river health parameters were analysed using a multi‐criteria decision‐making technique, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), in a GIS framework. We adopted a five‐fold river health classification framework (i.e., near‐pristine, good, fair, poor and degraded) for the entire Ganga River system from Gomukh to Farakka. Our results, based on geospatial data and supported by field observations, indicate that most reaches of the Ganga River in the higher mountainous stretch are in ‘near pristine’ condition, while some in the lower reaches fall into the ‘good’ and ‘fair’ classes. In contrast, several reaches in the alluvial part show ‘poor’ river health, primarily associated with flow reduction and sediment accumulation leading to morphological degradation, which is well manifested in geomorphic indicators used for river health assessment in this study. The geomorphic framework presented in this study can serve as a good template to evaluate river health and link this to scenarios of habitat suitability, environmental flows and flood risk associated with large river systems.

items.title: Proposal for monitoring the Eastern Grey Squirrel (Sciurus carolinensis) in Poland
items.abstract: The report presents a nationwide, continuous monitoring program for the invasive eastern grey squirrel (Sciurus carolinensis) in Poland, aimed at early detection and prevention of its spread. Monitoring focuses on high-risk areas such as urban parks, deciduous forests near cities, protected areas and border regions. The program includes repeated surveys across seasons using camera traps, field observations, winter nest searches and citizen reports. Grey squirrels pose a serious threat to native fauna, particularly the red squirrel, through competition and disease transmission. Immediate removal of detected individuals, strict enforcement of legal bans, cross-border cooperation and public awareness are emphasized. Effective monitoring combined with rapid response offers a real opportunity to prevent the establishment of this invasive species in Poland.

items.title: Catching small fish in a big pond: optimizing fish environmental DNA detections
items.abstract: Biomonitoring of teleost fish using environmental DNA metabarcoding is frequently performed using the 12S ribosomal RNA marker gene, especially with the MiFish primer set. These primers have associated laboratory and bioinformatic processing challenges that can generate spurious, incomplete, or inaccurate results. Here, we address each challenge to minimize off-target amplification and maximize the accuracy of observed species richness and community composition of the target taxa (teleost fish). We first tested the effects of amplification and sequencing library preparation protocols. We next tested infrequently used parameters in the common bioinformatic software program DADA2 using both environmental samples and mock communities with known composition. Our results support removing known off-target amplicons prior to sequencing and demonstrate that certain parameter settings can maximize the number of fish amplicon sequence variants generated bioinformatically. Furthermore, while changes in OMEGA_A and pooling parameters may yield additional amplicon sequence variants and previously undetected taxa, these amplicon sequence variants generally do not improve biodiversity estimates and are more likely to have associated uncertainty in taxonomic annotations. Based on our results, we recommend the following approaches using the MiFish 12S marker for marine biomonitoring: 1) Incorporate amplicon size selection prior to sequencing, 2) Consider increasing OMEGA_A and investing in manual curation of results.

items.title: Invasive rats and threatened lizards on islands: a DNA metabarcoding approach to assess dietary spectra and trophic interactions on the Aeolian archipelago
items.abstract: Abstract Island ecosystems often host endemics that are highly vulnerable to invasive species. In the Mediterranean biodiversity hotspot, the Endangered Aeolian wall lizard Podarcis raffonei is undergoing severe population decline. Its largest remaining population, on Vulcano Island, dropped by c. 60% from 2017 to 2022. A newly identified threat is the invasive black rat Rattus rattus , recently recorded at high densities in the area. Using DNA metabarcoding of faecal samples, we investigated potential trophic interactions between rats and lizards on Vulcano and provided a detailed characterization of the lizard’s diet across three populations. Podarcis raffonei primarily consumed arthropods (65.7%), particularly Hymenoptera, Hemiptera and Lepidoptera, but also a significant proportion of plant matter (34.3%) including Asterales, Fabales and Poales. Rats exhibited a similarly broad diet; they showed a limited dietary overlap with lizards for animal resources but a high dietary overlap for plant resources. No lizard DNA was found in rat faeces. These findings suggest that trophic competition, rather than direct predation, may be a key driver of the lizard’s decline. This study highlights the power of DNA metabarcoding to reveal cryptic ecological interactions and provides crucial insights for urgent conservation measures, including rat control and habitat management under the LIFE EOLIZARD project.

items.title: Responsible Management Education and Its Potential as an Epistemic Object of Change
items.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether and how RME can be performed as an epistemic object to broaden business schools’ education on climate change. The research builds on a qualitative case study involving 10 Finnish business schools. The analysis reveals that RME is performed as both an epistemic object and a boundary object, with different implications for its embeddedness within institutions. Our findings show how accreditations have introduced RME as a boundary object enforcing performativity around sustainability themes yet enabling disciplines to maintain their distinct or limited roles. At the same time, RME is met with both resistance and compliance, depending on how well the object fits with disciplinary boundaries and career trajectories. Lastly, as an epistemic object, RME encourages co‐reflexivity, which is essential for climate‐proofing business schools. We discuss the possibilities of a hybrid orientation of RME as both a boundary object and an epistemic object for enforcing climate‐orientation in management education.

items.title: Climate change impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem-based adaptation mechanisms in Azerbaijan
items.abstract: Climate change is altering ecosystems, species distributions and the services that support human well-being, while habitat loss and unsustainable resource use intensify ecological vulnerability. This narrative review examines the major pathways through which warming, hydrological change and extreme events affect biodiversity and identifies adaptation mechanisms relevant to Azerbaijan. The paper synthesizes authoritative global assessments, peer-reviewed literature and selected national policy documents, with emphasis on forests, mountain ecosystems, freshwater habitats, agricultural landscapes and nature-based solutions. The reviewed evidence links climate stress to habitat modification, range shifts, altered seasonal processes, water scarcity and increasing pressure on ecosystem services, although local impacts depend on land use, exposure and species-specific sensitivity. Ecosystem-based adaptation offers opportunities through habitat restoration, ecological connectivity, water and soil conservation, sustainable forestry and biodiversity-sensitive land management. These measures require careful ecological design because poorly located tree planting or other single-purpose interventions may create trade-offs for water resources and native species. For Azerbaijan, integrating biodiversity monitoring into climate planning, aligning adaptation investments with watershed-scale risk, and involving local communities are practical priorities. The review concludes that protecting ecological function is both a conservation objective and an economic resilience strategy. Its contribution is a context-specific policy synthesis rather than a new quantitative assessment of climate impacts.

items.title: Changing waters: from waterscape to landscape and back again
items.abstract: Across Sweden, around 2,400 lake-lowering and drainage projects since the early nineteenth century converted wetlands and lakes into fields, fixing a particular vision of progress into ditches, land deeds, and sediment. This article reviews 82 archival, scientific, and policy sources to ask what was done, why, and when, and to trace how these interventions continue to shape contemporary restoration politics. Lake drainage modifications started gaining interest in the 1830s and peaked around 1870–1930, enabled by ideals of patriotic ‘improvement’, expanding credit, and the 1879 Drainage Act. The resulting hydro-social legacies, long-lasting impacts on water systems and related social arrangements, such as subsiding peat, altered runoff pathways, and internal stores of various metals and compounds, complicate future plans to refill old lake basins and rewet peatlands for climate and biodiversity goals. Evidence from Swedish rewetting experiments indicates that restored peatlands can experience transient increases in total phosphorus and total mercury in outflow waters, while recently rewetted sites may remain net carbon sources during the first years after intervention. Restoration is conceptualised as a negotiated, case-specific intervention in which targeted projects, long-term monitoring, and shared governance confront historical debts rather than rely on expectations of a return to pristine nature.

items.title: Intestinal and Urinary Helminthiases: Prevalence, Polyparasitism and Associated Factors among Schoolchildren in the Sahelian and Sudanian Zones of Chad
items.abstract: ABSTRACTIntroduction. Polyparasitism involving intestinal helminths and schistosomes is common among schoolchildren in sub-Saharan Africa, but its structure and determinants remain poorly documented in Chad. This study aimed to describe helminth species richness, infection intensity, infracommunity structure, and factors associated with polyparasitism among schoolchildren in the Sahelian and Sudanian zones of Chad. Methods. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in 19 rural public schools between September 2021 and February 2022. Stool samples were examined using a single Kato–Katz smear read twice, and urine samples were examined after centrifugation. Factors associated with polyparasitism were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Results. Of the 1,443 pupils enrolled, 1,408 provided both stool and urine samples. Nine helminth taxa were identified. The prevalence of intestinal helminths was 35.87% (505/1,408), while the prevalence of Schistosoma haematobium was 45.46% (656/1,443). Heavy-intensity infections affected 41.6% (273/656) of S. haematobium carriers and 42.1% (83/197) of S. mansoni carriers. Polyparasitism affected 23.08% (325/1,408) of pupils and comprised 28 infracommunity types. Polyparasitism was less likely in the Sahelian zone than in the Sudanian zone (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42–0.74) and more likely among pupils aged 15–18 years than among those aged 10–14 years (aOR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.03–2.06). Conclusion. Chadian schoolchildren harbour a diverse helminth fauna, with frequent polyparasitism and heavy schistosome infections. An integrated control strategy combining praziquantel and albendazole, health education, and improved sanitation is needed.RÉSUMÉ Introduction. Le polyparasitisme à helminthes intestinaux et à schistosomes est fréquent chez les écoliers d’Afrique subsaharienne, mais reste mal documenté au Tchad. Cette étude décrit la richesse spécifique, l’intensité des infestations, les infracommunautés et les facteurs associés au polyparasitisme chez les écoliers des zones sahélienne et soudanienne. Méthodes. Une enquête transversale a été menée dans 19 écoles publiques rurales entre septembre 2021 et février 2022. Les selles (un frottis de Kato–Katz lu deux fois) et les urines (centrifugation) ont été examinées. Les facteurs associés au polyparasitisme ont été étudiés par régression logistique multivariée. Résultats. Sur 1 443 élèves inclus, 1 408 ont fourni des selles et des urines. Neuf taxons d’helminthes ont été identifiés. La prévalence était de 35,87 % (505/1 408) pour les helminthes intestinaux et de 45,46 % (656/1 443) pour Schistosoma haematobium. Les infestations intenses touchaient 41,6 % (273/656) des porteurs de S. haematobium et 42,1 % (83/197) de ceux de S. mansoni. Le polyparasitisme (23,08 % ; 325/1 408) comprenait 28 types d’infracommunautés. Il était moins fréquent en zone sahélienne qu’en zone soudanienne (OR ajusté [ORa] : 0,56 ; IC à 95 % : 0,42–0,74) et plus fréquent chez les élèves de 15–18 ans que chez ceux de 10–14 ans (ORa : 1,45 ; IC à 95 % : 1,03–2,06). Conclusion. Les écoliers tchadiens présentent une faune helminthique diversifiée, un polyparasitisme fréquent et des infections schistosomiennes souvent intenses. Une lutte intégrée associant praziquantel et albendazole, éducation sanitaire et assainissement est nécessaire.

items.title: Development of Wildlife Identification System Based on Local Alignment Algorithm
items.abstract: Wildlife crimes seriously threaten biodiversity and public health security. Identifying the species of wild animals and their products involved in such cases is the key to handling them. This study aimed to establish a wildlife DNA identification system based on a local alignment algorithm, thereby providing reliable technical support for public security organizations with high-precision and high-efficiency species identification techniques. The system adopted the Smith–Waterman local alignment algorithm, recognized the local similarity of DNA sequences with dynamic programming, and solved the problem of heavy reliance on complete sequences when using traditional global alignment. The parameters were optimized in combination with the Basic Local Alignment Search Tool, and matrix calculation was accelerated with C-Extensions for Python, thus significantly enhancing the processing efficiency for large-scale data. The database was based on self-dedicated identification data from the College of Criminal Science and Technology, Nanjing Police University. Experts reviewed the data, and the accuracy and safety of data were ensured to avoid the risk of species classification errors in open-source databases. The system innovatively integrated the Streamlit framework to develop the visualization platform and user-friendly interface. The grassroots police officers obtained species-matching results and the related species information by inputting DNA sequences, thereby facilitating case handling. The system provides an efficient technical tool for combating wildlife crimes and maintaining biodiversity, with significant practical value and immense promotion potential.

items.title: Social imaginaries on wildfires, burning practices, and fire management in two Colombian national newspapers: tensions between risk, illegality, and ecological function
items.abstract: Introduction This article analyzes the construction of social imaginaries about the application of fire in two Colombian national newspapers, El Tiempo and El Espectador , based on three key concepts understood as distinct discursive categories: fire use and management, burning practices, and wildfires. Methodology A mixed-methods approach is adopted, combining artificial intelligence tools with qualitative analysis. The quantitative phase employs a BETO model to classify the evaluative framing of fire, while the qualitative phase utilizes a discursive analysis. The corpus consists of 504 items published in El Tiempo and El Espectador between 2020 and 2025. Results The findings show that, in the coverage of both newspapers, the application of fire is primarily represented as a problematic practice, associated with risk, illegality, and destruction. This trend is quantified by the predominance of negative valuations within the corpus. Based on the automatic classification of text fragments, 71% present a negative valuation, compared to 29% neutral. Specifically, “burning practices” concentrate 87.5% negative valuations and 12.5% neutral, while “wildfires” record 68% negative and 32% neutral, with no positive valuations identified in the manually annotated sample. In contrast, “fire use and management” has marginal visibility in the corpus, with only 24 news items; their manual classification as complete news items, reported separately because of its different unit and procedure, shows that 15 (62%) were positive and 9 (38%) negative, despite the potential of this concept to recognize ecological and territorial functions. Discussion These findings suggest that terminological distribution may contribute to consolidating interpretive frameworks that reduce the complexity of the phenomenon. Consequently, the analyzed coverage tends to leave the ecological and cultural dimensions of fire in the background, which may limit the legitimacy of integrated management approaches in environmental governance.

items.title: Between Skin and Brain: A Systematic Review of 712 Cases 1976–2025 Reveals a Highly Diverse Disease Spectrum in Chaetothyriales
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Black yeast-like species of the order Chaetothyriales cause superficial to life-threatening systemic infections. Comprehensive global epidemiology data remain limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to analyze the global epidemiology, spectrum of pathogens, clinical manifestations and outcomes of Chaetothyriales infections. METHODS: We systematically reviewed 712 cases reported between 1976 and 2025. RESULTS: The analysis revealed a steady increase in diagnosed cases, with Cladophialophora bantiana (21%), Exophiala dermatitidis (19%), and E. jeanselmei (15%) being the predominant causative agents; notably, the proportion of E. jeanselmei declined from 18%-28% in 1976-2015 to 7% in 2016-2025. Published cases were more frequent in tropical/subtropical regions; however, cases were reported from Africa. Although 42% of infections occurred in immunocompetent individuals, transplant recipients, diabetics, and those with CARD9 deficiency showed higher risk. Deep infections exhibited substantially greater mortality than cutaneous forms (47% vs. 7%; p < 0.001); particularly, central nervous system infections (58%) and disseminated disease (53%) were involved. CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights a seemingly growing burden of Chaetothyriales infections, possibly partly due to better recognition, emphasizing the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, and targeted prevention in high-risk populations.

items.title: Addressing environmental problems and the role of environmental policy in achieving sustainable development in Azerbaijan
items.abstract: In the modern era, ensuring sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with environmental safety and social welfare. Intensive use of natural resources, climate change, pollution of water and land resources, increase in waste, air pollution, and reduction of biodiversity are among the main factors affecting the long-term sustainability of economic development. The purpose of the study is to evaluate current environmental problems in Azerbaijan from the perspective of sustainable development principles, determine their impact on economic and social development, and substantiate directions for improving environmental policy. The study used a systematic and comparative approach, analysis of statistical data, and methods of scientific-theoretical generalization. The analysis utilized environmental statistical data from the State Statistical Committee of the Republic of Azerbaijan, state programs, and international documents. Existing statistical data show that both positive changes and problems requiring resolution exist in the fields of waste management, use of natural resources, and ensuring environmental safety. Based on the results of the study, the main directions determined for solving environmental problems include efficient use of resources, expansion of waste recycling, development of digital monitoring systems, application of green technologies, and strengthening the institutional capacities of environmental management.

items.title: Using ecosystem science to achieve ecological nutrient management
items.abstract: The reliance on inorganic fertilizers, along with the simplification of cropping systems and agricultural landscapes, fueled tremendous increases in yield while generating severe consequences for the biosphere, human health, and biodiversity. There is a critical need to address these issues and transition to a more sustainable approach to soil management and food production. Ecosystem ecology provides a flexible systems approach for understanding the complex and dynamic interactions among organisms, their environment, and agricultural management, which ultimately govern biogeochemical cycling and soil-mediated ecosystem services. This chapter reviews concepts from ecosystem ecology and related disciplines that form the foundation of ecological nutrient management (ENM), including how communities of plants and soil organisms govern soil organic matter dynamics and nutrient cycling. It presents the foundational principles of ENM and discusses key management practices that extend these principles into desirable improvements in agroecosystems, emphasizing how ecosystem science can be leveraged to implement ENM effectively.

items.title: Recent Progress on Limonoids: The Potential, Challenges, and Insights of Chemistry and Biology
items.abstract: Limonoids are an important class of highly oxygenated triterpenoids containing a distinctive 4,4,8-trimethyl-17-furanylsteroid skeleton. To date, over 2700 members, including azadirachtin, toosendanin, limonin, obacunone, nomilin, harrisonin, nimbolide, gedunin, salannin, nimbin, khayanolide, xylocarpin, swietenine, rocaglamide, trichilin, vilasinin, etc., have been isolated from citrus fruits and the plants of the Rutaceae and Meliaceae families. They play a significant role in the discovery of novel drug and pesticide candidates owing to their wide range of biological activities, such as protective, anti-inflammatory, anti-cancer, antimicrobial, and insecticidal properties. Therefore, their potential, challenges, and insights into the chemistry and biology of triterpenoid-type limonoids have recently garnered much attention. The focus of this review is not only to summarize the isolation, total synthesis, and structural modifications of limonoid-type natural products as potential therapeutic and pesticidal agents, but also to highlight the underlying mechanisms of their pharmacological effects from 2017 to 2025. Noteworthily, perspectives were given on the limonoid-type compounds as leads for further development of novel drugs and agrochemicals, and their applications in the future. Hopefully, this review can serve as a comprehensive reference for future research on limonoids and their derivatives in the pharmaceutical and agricultural fields.

items.title: Major pests of fruit and berry crops in the western region of Azerbaijan and environmentally safe control methods
items.abstract: In recent years, clearly observable global climate change in Azerbaijan, as in various geographical regions of the world, together with the expansion of intensive fruit orchards, has become one of the major factors contributing to the spread of diverse pest organisms, reduced crop productivity, and deterioration in the quality of agricultural products. In this context, studying pests of fruit and berry crops, determining their distribution patterns, and implementing environmentally safe control methods represent important components of modern plant protection. The aim of this study was to identify the most widespread pests affecting major fruit and berry crops cultivated in the Western region of Azerbaijan, particularly in the Ganja-Dashkasan and Gazakh-Tovuz economic regions, to assess their biological characteristics, distribution patterns, and harmful effects on plants, and to substantiate environmentally safe pest management and control measures. The study focused on major pests associated with apple, pear, plum, sour cherry, sweet cherry, apricot, peach, grape, strawberry, raspberry, and blackberry crops. The biological characteristics, feeding behavior, distribution, and damage caused by important pest species such as Aphis pomi, Cydia pomonella, Grapholita funebrana, Panonychus ulmi, and Metcalfa pruinosa were assessed based on literature data and field observations. Particular attention was given to the application of biological products, entomophages, pheromone traps, agronomic practices, plant-based preparations, and integrated pest management systems, which can contribute to reducing the intensive use of chemical pesticides.

items.title: Global Change Is Reshaping Coral Communities and Threatening Reef Physical Functionality
items.abstract: Coral reefs are undergoing profound compositional changes driven by climate change, disease, and chronic human disturbance. Coral cover is the primary metric used to track reef condition, but it often fails to capture the contributions of different coral species to reef carbonate production, structural complexity, and associated biodiversity. Here, I review evidence showing that global change disproportionately removes competitively dominant and architecturally complex corals, driving non-random changes and coral community homogenisation. These changes erode reef functionality, even when overall cover is maintained. Species-specific contributions to calcification and structural complexity span orders of magnitude, such that targeted losses of framework-building taxa collapse carbonate budgets and habitat architecture in ways not predictable from cover trends. These structural changes cascade through associated communities, undermining functional diversity and the ecosystem processes on which reef resilience depends. Critically, rebounds in coral cover frequently reflect the colonisation by fast-growing opportunistic species, which yield slow or absent recovery of physical functionality, while reassembly and the re-establishment of large, structurally complex colonies (and the physical functionality they provide) might lag by decades. Furthermore, as mass disturbance events occur at ever-shorter intervals, recovery windows close before reef-building potential and complexity can be fully restored. Monitoring, management, and restoration should therefore focus on trait- and species-explicit assessments that prioritise protection and restoration of keystone reef-builders, target sites with high functional potential, and reduce stressors at appropriate scales. Integrating functional metrics into policy and restoration planning is essential to safeguard reef geomorphic and ecological services under continued global change.

items.title: Proposal for a federated landscape of curated reference libraries for enhancing aquatic (e)DNA biomonitoring in Europe
items.abstract: DNA and environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding are transforming aquatic biodiversity monitoring in Europe. Still, the reliability of taxonomic assignments depends critically on the quality, completeness, and interoperability of the underlying DNA reference libraries. Here, we combine a landscape assessment of the current state of DNA reference libraries for aquatic organisms in Europe with a set of recommendations for a federated system of taxonomically curated reference libraries, following community consultation. We surveyed 26 major reference libraries across 40 attributes spanning taxonomic scope, metadata provision, curation practice, and technical accessibility, and complemented this with a questionnaire completed by 33 institutions actively generating new reference sequence data. Our assessment revealed a markedly heterogeneous landscape: databases vary widely in taxonomic and geographic coverage, molecular markers, and update frequency; most lack programmatic (API) access; and curation practice ranges from minimal taxonomic annotation to full phylogenetically-informed validation along with review of bibliographic references, with no collectively agreed minimum standard applied across databases or declared by data contributors. Building on these findings and on extensive stakeholder consultation within the eDNAqua-Plan project, we propose a federated system resting on three pillars: a minimum set of essential, interoperable metadata; standardised curation workflows culminating in a transparent, traceability-based quality ranking; and technical interoperability grounded in existing (meta)data standards (e.g., GSC MIxS, Darwin Core). We outline two feasible data-architecture options for implementation, together with a phased roadmap addressing governance and long-term sustainability. These recommendations aim to strengthen the reliability, reproducibility, and interoperability of eDNA-based aquatic biomonitoring across Europe and beyond.

items.title: Os Recuperação de pastagens degradadas em biomas brasileiros: análise comparativa de estratégias sustentáveis
items.abstract: A degradação de pastagens no Brasil compromete a produtividade agropecuária e os serviços ecossistêmicos, afetando os principais biomas nacionais. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar comparativamente a eficácia das estratégias de recuperação de pastagens degradadas nos biomas Amazônia, Cerrado, Caatinga e Mata Atlântica. Foi realizada uma revisão de literatura com artigos publicados entre 2014 e 2024, obtidos em bases como Scopus, Web of Science e Google Scholar, considerando estudos com resultados mensuráveis de recuperação. As estratégias foram avaliadas quanto à eficiência produtiva, recuperação do solo, custo de implementação e tempo de resposta. Os resultados indicam que sistemas integrados, como integração lavoura-pecuária-floresta e sistemas agroflorestais, apresentam maior eficiência global, promovendo ganhos simultâneos de produtividade e qualidade do solo. No entanto, essas práticas demandam maior investimento inicial e suporte técnico. Estratégias naturais, como regeneração secundária, mostram elevada eficiência ecológica, porém com resposta lenta. Observou-se que a eficácia das estratégias varia conforme as condições edafoclimáticas e socioeconômicas de cada bioma. Conclui-se que a recuperação de pastagens no Brasil depende da combinação de estratégias adaptadas regionalmente, sendo necessária a ampliação de políticas públicas para viabilizar sua adoção em larga escala.

items.title: Andean Glaciers in Times of Planetary Crisis
items.abstract: Abstract This special dossier examines how understandings of Andean glaciers transform under the planetary crisis, defined by humanity’s impact on geophysical processes at a planetary scale. Once regarded as remnants of deep geological time, glaciers have become emblematic casualties of anthropogenic global warming, their accelerated melting compressing geological history into human timescales and raising urgent ethical and political questions about protection, mitigation, and loss. This interdisciplinary collection, including contributions focused on Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and the wider region, calls for approaches that move beyond universalizing Anthropocene narratives and toward historically and territorially situated accounts of glacial change, challenging colonial and extractivist frameworks that have long shaped the governance of ice and nature. The introduction argues that dominant scientific and state-centered framings—rooted in objectivity, distant observation, and a physicochemical definition of ice—tend to abstract glaciers into universal, placeless indicators of global change, obscuring the local extractivist and colonial dynamics driving their destruction, particularly through mining of critical minerals for a green energy transition. Against this detached view, the dossier foregrounds situated, relational, and often Indigenous conceptions of glaciers as vital entities embedded in organic, social, and spiritual life.

items.title: Some like it hot, but others might not: the implications of climate change for the conservation of South African freshwater crab species
items.abstract: Abstract Primary freshwater crabs are keystone aquatic species, yet the potential impact of climate change on their distribution and conservation status remains unknown, particularly in biodiversity-rich areas such as South Africa. We employed maximum entropy and climatic niche modelling to evaluate the effects of climate change on the distribution of 17 Potamonautes species in South Africa and estimate protected area coverage for suitable habitats under both current and future climate projections of increased temperature, and the impact on the conservation of these species. Our results indicate that six of the 17 species are likely to experience a net loss of suitable habitat, and seven are projected to experience net habitat gains. Habitat changes for four of the 17 species are dependent on the climate scenario applied. Under predicted temperature increases, P. barbarai and P. isimangaliso are expected to experience significant habitat reduction, with P. isimangaliso being sensitive as a result of substantial predicted losses in both suitable and protected habitat. Conversely, P. depressus , P. flavusjo and P. warreni appear to be the least sensitive to climate change, gaining suitable habitat under both climate models. Unsurprisingly, we found precipitation to be a critical predictor of suitable habitat as these crabs are dependent on freshwater ecosystems. Our results underscore the importance of conservation strategies tailored to the unique predicted response of each species to climate change.

items.title: Elevating resilience: a multi-site synthesis of sediment placement as a lifeline for saltmarsh sparrows (Ammospiza caudacuta)
items.abstract: Many New England salt marshes are rapidly degrading due to the combined effects of accelerating sea-level rise (SLR) and other anthropogenic stressors, resulting in loss of high-marsh vegetation and threatening marsh-dependent wildlife such as the Saltmarsh Sparrow ( Ammospiza caudacuta ). Sediment placement (SP) is widely used to increase marsh elevation and resilience, yet long-term ecological outcomes, particularly for wildlife, remain uncertain. To evaluate SP efficacy, we synthesized biological and physical responses from four large-scale salt marsh restoration projects in Rhode Island monitored for up to 8 years following SP using a Before–After–Control–Impact (BACI) design. Vegetation recovery trajectories varied widely among sites. Spartina alterniflora cover declined consistently after SP, but robust high-marsh plant communities reestablished at only two sites, indicating site-specific restoration outcomes. Plant community complexity increased overall, with gains in species richness and diversity as S. alterniflora monocultures transitioned toward heterogeneous high-marsh meadows. Vegetation recovery was strongly linked to hydrology, with greater cover near drainage features (<35 m) and in areas of lower porewater salinity (<25 ppt). Avian use shifted through time. Recently restored, sparsely vegetated marshes were used by Piping Plover ( Charadrius melodus ) and other beach-nesting species, while Saltmarsh Sparrows nested within 4–5 years post-restoration. Male sparrow abundance was modestly higher at SP sites than controls, and nests were concentrated in areas recovering with Spartina patens , though limited vegetation structure resulted in lower nest placement and shallower thatch than reference areas. Marsh surface elevations increased 7–33 cm relative to mean high water following SP, improving hydrology by reducing flooding and enhancing drainage, and extending estimated marsh lifespans by 24–111 years under current SLR rates. Our multi-site synthesis demonstrates that SP can effectively restore marsh elevation, but ecological outcomes are strongly mediated by site-specific physical conditions, particularly hydrology. These results highlight the importance of long-term, multi-metric monitoring and adaptive management to maximize the conservation benefits of SP salt marsh restoration.

items.title: The plume carries no flag: unilateral seabed mining and the pollution duties that bind nonparties to UNCLOS
items.abstract: The USA has begun to license commercial recovery of polymetallic nodules in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone under its own statute, outside the International Seabed Authority, while the Authority’s exploitation regulations remain unadopted. Scholarship has treated this largely as a question of allocation, asking whether a nonparty can acquire good title to nodules in the Area, and has rebuilt what remains as a duty to cooperate. This article asks a different question: which pollution duties bind a nonparty that mines the Area, and on what legal basis. It argues that the environmental obligations of Part XII of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea are severable from the allocative bargain of Part XI. The duties of prevention, due diligence, and prior environmental impact assessment bind the nonparty as customary international law, on evidence that includes its own practice and its obligations under the 1958 Convention on the High Seas. The treaty-specific requirement of Article 209(2) does not bind it, but serves as evidence of what customary due diligence demands in the Area. A State that leaves the referent institution while remaining bound by the rule of reference engages in what the article names referential arbitrage, and the benchmark on which the arbitrage relies proves thinner than claimed but not empty. Sediment and discharge plumes then defeat the geography on which unilateral licensing depends: a licence draws a boundary, and a plume does not observe it. The 1972 London Convention excluded seabed mining discharge on the assumption that a seabed regime would govern it, a carve-out extended on credit that unilateral licensing never redeems. Exit does not remove State responsibility; it concentrates it on the licensing State. The article closes with measures that require no accession, among them an advisory request the Authority’s Council may make on its own motion.

items.title: Using Video Games to Teach Kepler’s Laws and Orbital Dynamics
items.abstract: Physics instructors often rely on demonstrations when teaching, using real-time examples to appeal to student intuition or tinkering with a physical system to develop a deeper and more natural understanding of a topic. However, some subjects, like Kepler's laws of planetary motion, are impractical to demonstrate at a human scale, and when reality proves difficult, it is often easier to move to simulations and video games. In particular, using video games in the classroom benefits student learning and allows students to learn practical information that they can transfer to the real world. The video game Kerbal Space Program (KSP) is notable for its commitment to accurate simulation of rockets and orbits, allowing players to explore the in-game solar system with their Kerbal astronauts only if they have mastered the laws of orbital dynamics. In my personal experience, I gained a better intuition about orbits during my years playing KSP than I did in graduate school, a common sentiment within the KSP community. I use KSP in my college introductory astronomy courses to make Kepler's laws more tactile with demonstrations and projects, developing intuition on advanced aspects of rocket science through experiments that are otherwise impractical at interplanetary scales.

items.title: Emergent Inflation in Fractional Cosmology
items.abstract: We investigate the dynamics of the early universe within an emergent fractional cosmological framework generated by a measure-deformed Newtonian action, without introducing additional propagating degrees of freedom. Considering asymptotic and dynamical requirements, we construct a minimal fractional potential that, together with the time-dependent fractional kernel, generates a regular pre-inflationary stage, quasi-de Sitter inflation, a dynamically controlled exit, and a subsequent finite duration radiation-like phase. The exact solution of the reduced early-time equation is obtained in two equivalent representations, and regularity selects a unique physical branch with finite principal curvature invariants at the initial boundary. Remarkably, the same exact trajectory evolves asymptotically toward the quasi-de Sitter regime, while an exact nonlinear analysis of homogeneous Hubble deviations establishes its asymptotic attractor character within the admissible expanding sector. Inflation ends dynamically near the zero crossing of the effective fractional force, leading to controlled background-level consistency relations among the inflationary duration, the fractional parameter, the effective equation of state parameter, and the exit scale. For the physically relevant post-inflationary regime, the model admits the characteristic radiation-like expansion over a finite post-inflationary interval. These results show that a coherent sequence of regular pre-inflationary, inflationary, and post-inflationary background dynamics can emerge from a simple and unified fractional Newtonian framework without invoking an inflaton field.

items.title: Assessing the robustness of amortized simulation-based inference to transient noise in gravitational-wave ringdowns
items.abstract: Gravitational waves (GW) emitted by binary systems allow us to perform precision tests of general relativity in the strong field regime. Ringdown signals allow for probing black hole mass and spin with high precision in GW astronomy. With improvements in current and next-generation GW detectors, developing likelihood-free parameter inference methods is crucial. This is especially important when facing challenges such as non-standard noise, partial data, or incomplete signal models that prevent the use of analytical likelihood functions. In this work, we propose an amortized simulation-based inference strategy to estimate ringdown parameters directly. Specifically, our method is based on amortized neural posterior estimation, which trains a neural density estimator of the posterior for all data segments within the prior range. The results show that our trained amortized network achieves statistically consistent parameter estimates with valid confidence coverage compared to established Markov-chain methods, while offering inference speeds that are orders of magnitude faster. Furthermore, we evaluate the robustness of the method against transient noise contamination. Our analysis reveals that the timing of glitch injection has a decisive impact on estimation bias, particularly during the tail of a signal with sparse information. Glitch strength is positively correlated with estimation error, but has limited effect at low signal-to-noise ratios. Mass and spin parameters are most sensitive to noise. This study not only provides an efficient and accurate inference framework for ringdown analysis but also lays a foundation for developing robust data-processing pipelines for future GW astronomy in realistic noise environments.

items.title: First results from the Juice magnetometer during the Lunar-Earth Gravity Assist
items.abstract: Abstract. Before reaching the Jovian system in 2031, the ESA Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) spacecraft will perform three Earth flybys. As well as providing gravitational assistance, these flybys are prime opportunities to assess performance and undertake in-flight calibration of the science payload in a well-understood environment. The first such interval occurred in August 2024, dubbed the Lunar-Earth gravity assist (LEGA) as it included a pass by the Moon in advance of the approach to Earth. The unique spacecraft trajectory allowed for sampling of various regions of the magnetosphere before exiting into the solar wind. In this paper, we report on the performance of the Juice magnetometer instrument (J-MAG) during the LEGA. J-MAG comprises three sensors—two fluxgate vector sensors and one Coupled Dark State Magnetometer (CDSM) scalar sensor—all of which were operational during the LEGA period. This represents the first time in the mission that the scalar sensor has operated in its nominal state. Here, we analyse J-MAG observations during key periods of the flyby. As well as inter-sensor comparison, we assess J-MAG data against geomagnetic field models during the approach to Earth, and compare with measurements from other spacecraft at the Moon and in the solar wind, which allow us to make suggestions for future calibration activities. Overall, the three sensors showed excellent performance at this early stage in the mission and confirmed that the scalar sensor meets the requirements for in-flight calibration of the fluxgate sensors at Ganymede. The LEGA also demonstrates the potential value of using cruise phase measurements for scientific exploration and solar wind monitoring.

items.title: Mrk 382: A Narrow-line Seyfert 1 Galaxy with Recurrent X-Ray State Transitions
items.abstract: Abstract We report recurrent X-ray state transitions in the nearby narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxy Mrk 382 using multiepoch observations from Swift, Chandra, XMM-Newton, and eROSITA, together with archival ultraviolet (UV), optical, and infrared (IR) data. The 0.3–2 keV flux varies by nearly an order of magnitude over ∼15 yr, with multiple transitions between bright and faint states. The X-ray spectrum shows strong state-dependent evolution, changing from a steep high-state continuum (Γ = 2.32 ± 0.04) to a much harder low-state spectrum (Γ = 1.39 ± 0.06), which also exhibits a narrow Fe K α line with an equivalent width of ∼330 eV. Reflection modeling indicates that the low-flux state is strongly reflection dominated, with the reflection fraction increasing from R refl ∼ 4.4 to ∼30, consistent with substantial changes in the inner disk–corona configuration. Photoionized absorption contributes to the spectral complexity, but its relatively modest column density suggests that absorption alone is unlikely to explain the full amplitude of the X-ray transitions. The UV emission shows possible long-term correspondence with the X-ray variability at smaller amplitude, while the optical and mid-IR bands vary more mildly. The spectral and multiwavelength behavior suggests that changes in coronal geometry may be accompanied by changes in its intrinsic energetics. Despite the dramatic X-ray variability, no extreme X-ray-weak state or clear optical spectral-type change is observed. Mrk 382 therefore provides a valuable nearby laboratory for studying the evolution of the disk–corona system and its connection to multiwavelength active galactic nucleus variability.

items.title: Primordial black holes from vector-induced curvature perturbations sourced by primordial magnetic fields
items.abstract: Generating an appreciable abundance of primordial black holes (PBHs) requires a substantial enhancement of primordial curvature perturbations on small scales. In this work, we propose a new post-inflationary mechanism in which such an enhancement arises during a stiff, or kination, epoch. The mechanism is driven by metric vector perturbations sourced by the vector component of the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor associated with primordial magnetic fields (PMFs). Since these first-order vector modes remain approximately constant during kination, they act as persistent nonlinear sources for second-order scalar perturbations. We show that the resulting vector-induced curvature perturbations are amplified toward the infrared cutoff of the kination band and exhibit the characteristic scaling $\mathcal P_{\mathcal R}(k)\propto k^{-5}$. As a concrete realization, we consider PMFs generated in a Ratra-type magnetogenesis scenario and find that the induced curvature perturbations can produce PBHs with an abundance large enough to constitute a substantial fraction of the dark matter.

items.title: Extreme PeV Accelerator Associated with GRS 1915+105
items.abstract: Abstract Microquasars, binary systems featuring relativistic jets, have emerged as sources for particle acceleration beyond PeV energies. We present a study of the broadband γ -ray emission from one of the most prominent Galactic microquasars, GRS 1915+105, based on data accumulated by LHAASO and Fermi Large Area Telescope over 4 and 17 yr, respectively. A joint analysis of LHAASO-WCDA and LHAASO-KM2A data reveals extended γ -ray emission whose centroid appears significantly shifted, by ∼0 . ° 13, from the binary system and its jets. The spectral energy distribution is well described by a curved spectrum with progressive steepening that can be described by a log-parabola function with no evidence for a sharp cutoff, consistent with parent particles reaching multi-PeV energies and an extreme acceleration efficiency approaching the limit set by the available potential drop across the source. Several features, most notably the shift of the emission and single power-law spectrum down to GeV band, favor radiation by cosmic rays accelerated in the source interacting with the dense ambient medium. Our spectral modeling implies that at least a few percent of the jet mechanical power is transferred to protons, whose maximum energy reaches beyond 5 PeV. These results strengthen the case for microquasars as exceptionally efficient accelerators in our Galaxy.

items.title: Signal-to-noise ratio contours for LISA
items.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will search for a stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) background at millihertz frequencies, from both astrophysical and cosmological sources, and thereby open a new chapter in GW astronomy. In the literature, LISA's sensitivity to prospective GW background (GWB) signals is often quantified in terms of an expected signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) assuming perfect knowledge of the detector noise. The commonly employed expression for the SNR is, however, valid only in the limit of a weak GWB signal, which renders a large number of SNR values reported in the literature inaccurate. In this paper, we address this issue by deriving for the first time an expression for the expected optimal SNR of a LISA auto-correlation measurement that is valid at arbitrary signal strength. Based on our generalized expression, we conclude that LISA data worth an observing time of T_obs across the frequency band from f_min to f_max will never yield an SNR in excess of SNR_max = sqrt(T_obs(f_max-f_min)), which evaluates to SNR_max <~ 10^4 for typical mission parameters. We illustrate our findings in terms of generalized power-law-integrated (PLI) sensitivity curves at different SNR levels, i.e., LISA SNR contour lines in plots of the GW energy-density power spectrum. In contrast to earlier work on PLI sensitivity curves, we notably find that the LISA SNR contours are bounded from above, approximately by the LISA strain noise curve multiplied by a factor of Euler's number e. For GWB signals not much weaker than this range, the expected SNR for a LISA auto-correlation measurement needs to be evaluated based on our new expression. Our numerical results for the LISA SNR contours are available on Zenodo [https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21275527].

items.title: Gravitational wave modeling of white-dwarf-compact-object binaries and observational outlook
items.abstract: We investigate the end stages of circular white-dwarf--compact-object binaries by developing a novel integrator implementing mass transfer and 2.5-order Post-Newtonian kinematics. White-dwarf--compact-object binaries are subject to two phases: a slow inspiral during which binary evolution is dominated by weak-gravity radiation reaction and a quicker ``outspiral" dominated by mass transfer. These systems have unique gravitational waveforms with several characteristic features including an accumulation of signal near the maximum cutoff frequency set by the transition between in- and outspiral. We investigate trends in gravitational wave parameters based on component masses. In particular, maximum cutoff frequency depends strongly on white dwarf mass and compactness. It is unlikely that extragalactic binaries will be measured by LISA or current or future terrestrial detectors. However, white-dwarf--compact-object binary end stages will be an important source for future decihertz detectors such as DECIGO and LGWA: The final inspiral of tens of white-dwarf--neutron-star binaries will be detected annually by LGWA, and millions of inspirals along with thousands of outspirals will be detected by DECIGO. The ultimate fates of these binaries are diverse and dependent upon the intricacies of angular momentum loss. In particular, we show that white dwarfs with partners of sufficiently low/high mass can end their lives in common envelopes/mergers, while white dwarfs do not enter contact with partners of intermediate mass. The highest frequencies produced by white-dwarf--compact-object binaries in our tests are 10--20 Hz---incapable of mimicking sub-solar-mass compact object signals in terrestrial detectors or explaining S251112cm-like signals.

items.title: A giant magnetic eruption from the asymptotic-giant-branch star Mira A
items.abstract: Mass loss during the advanced evolutionary stages of low- and intermediate-mass stars is traditionally attributed to dust-driven winds, whereas the influence of magnetic fields remains poorly constrained. However, recent observations show massive directional mass ejections from the nearby asymptotic-giant-branch (AGB) star Mira A that do not appear to be driven by radiation pressure on the dust. We aim to observationally investigate whether magnetic fields are responsible for the mass-loss ejections from Mira A. We obtained full-polarisation ALMA observations of the SiO v=1, J=5̊ightarrow4 maser transition at 215 GHz with angular resolutions of 1.5--2.6 au. The observations reveal a highly magnetised loop-like mass ejection traced by strongly polarised SiO masers extending to approximately eight stellar radii. The morphology, polarisation pattern, energetics, and kinematics indicate a magnetically driven eruption analogous to a stellar coronal-mass ejection (CME). These observations demonstrate that magnetic eruptions can dominate mass loss from evolved stars and imply that magnetic fields must become an integral component of future models of AGB (and potentially other cool-giant) winds.

items.title: Solid-State Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Search for Axion-like Dark Matter with Broadband SQUID Magnetometry
items.abstract: We report the results of an experimental search for ultralight axion-like dark matter in the mass ranges 18.9–20.6 and 21.6–21.9 neV. The Cosmic Axion Spin Precession Experiment-electric probes the axion-nuclear electric dipole moment coupling. We perform solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance on 207Pb spin ensembles which reside in a polarized ferroelectric crystal. The background axion-like dark matter field induces an oscillating torque on the 207Pb spins via the electric dipole moment coupling gd. The experiment is calibrated with pulsed magnetic resonance measurements covering two frequency bands (4.57–4.97 and 5.23–5.29 MHz) that correspond to the axion Compton frequencies associated with the identified axion mass ranges. By sweeping the leading magnetic field applied to the sample, we are able to detect the 207Pb nuclear magnetic resonance in these frequency ranges using a superconducting quantum interference device, inductively coupled to the sample with a broadband circuit. We establish the upper bounds |gd|<4×10−4 GeV−2 with 95% confidence in these frequency bands. Our results demonstrate the detection and small-tip angle calibration of low-field 207Pb nuclear magnetic resonance, allowing for sensitivity to axion-like dark matter in the nanoelectron-volt axion mass range.

items.title: Little Red Dots are Direct-collapse Black Hole–forming Galaxies
items.abstract: Abstract “Little red dots” (LRDs) at 4 < z < 8 are one of the most challenging discoveries by JWST to date because their distinctive V-shaped spectra and compact morphologies defy conventional astrophysical interpretation. Previous attempts to explain LRDs as compact stellar systems, heavily cocooned black holes (BHs) with differential flows, supermassive stars, or more exotic objects like “black hole stars” cannot either show how they formed, explain the origin of the dense shells needed for the absorption features in their spectra, or account for their observed abundances or inferred lifetimes. Here we show that LRDs are simply direct-collapse BH galaxies in which the BH is still shrouded by the massive disk that created it. Our cosmological simulations yield spectra that are good matches to those of LRDs because high densities at the center of the disk trap X-rays from the BH and produce the observed Balmer absorption features while allowing UV, optical, and reprocessed IR flux to partly escape. The host galaxy forms a dense 10 8 M ⊙ cluster of stars with a radius of 150 pc next to the BH, consistent with observations of LRDs. Our models reproduce a wide variety of LRD spectra, from typical objects like RUBIES-EGS-42046 at z = 5.28 to those with the strongest Balmer breaks such as MoM-BH * −1 at z = 7.76 and those at the highest redshifts like CAPERS-LRD-z9 at z = 9.29.

items.title: Empirical Determination of the Galactic Neutron Star–Black Hole Merger Rate Using StarTrack Models
items.abstract: Abstract The discovery of a pulsar in a binary system with a black hole would provide a unique laboratory for testing general relativity in the strong-field regime and offer vital constraints on massive star evolution. We assess prospects for the detectability of such systems by utilizing the radio pulsar population and survey models within the modeling package PsrPopPy and, as a proof of principle, two evolutionary models with different treatments of common-envelope phases from the stellar population synthesis code StarTrack. For these two models, assuming the radio pulsar beaming model proposed by Tauris and Manchester and accounting for the effects of orbital motion on pulsar detectability, we calculate upper limits on the number of neutron star–black hole systems in the Galaxy and the corresponding merger rate given the lack of any radio-detected pulsar–black hole binary systems in current radio surveys. For the most constraining model, we find a Galactic merger rate of R < 4.3 Myr − 1 (at 95% confidence). These results are extrapolated to the expected horizon distance for the fifth LIGO observing run, leading to LIGO detection rate estimates that are consistent with the latest values reported by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration. Our results indicate that the increased sensitivity of FAST, MeerKAT, and DSA offers the best prospects yet for uncovering this elusive population.

items.title: Ensemble pulsational characteristics of eclipsing binaries containing β Cep stars observed by the TESS mission
items.abstract: Massive pulsators in eclipsing binaries provide precise, model-independent stellar parameters that, combined with asteroseismic constraints, provide powerful probes of internal rotation, convective-core mass, angular-momentum transport, and mixing in massive stars. This study investigates the pulsational characteristics and their impact on the structure and evolution of β Cep pulsators in eclipsing binaries. We analysed an ensemble of 65 β Cep stars in eclipsing binaries, identified rotationally split modes where possible, and statistically derived the dependence of pulsational properties on binary orbital parameters. The interior properties of the systems were also derived using pre-computed grids of stellar structure models with and associated pulsation frequencies using and an asteroseismic routine that tracks the age and rotation of the star in the entire β Cep instability region. MESA StORM Interior rotation rates are derived for 14 systems that exhibit rotational mode splitting. While differential rotation is tentatively inferred for HD 112485, quasi-rigid rotation is found for the primaries of other systems except CZ Vel. Detailed forward asteroseismic modelling was conducted for HD 112485 and EK Cru to deduce their seismic and core properties, as well as their evolutionary state. HD 112485 is one of the least evolved β Cep stars asteroseismically modelled to date, with a core hydrogen mass fraction of X_ c = 0.501_ -0.013 ^ +0.009 . The two reproduced zonal modes in HD 112485 are the first radial-order dipole pressure mode and the second radial-order quadrupole gravity mode, while the zonal modes in EK Cru are the second-order quadrupole mixed mode and the third-order dipole pressure mode. A multivariate regression shows a negative correlation of the pulsation amplitude with pulsation frequency, and no statistically significant relationship with the orbital period. In addition, no significant relationship is observed between the pulsation frequency and the orbital period in the current sample.

items.title: Large-scale Stellar Bars and Nuclear Activity in Narrow-line Seyfert 1 Galaxies
items.abstract: Abstract We present a statistical comparison between barred and unbarred narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies (NLS1s) to investigate the role of large-scale stellar bars in fueling active galactic nuclei (AGNs) with low-mass black holes. From a parent sample of 492 NLS1s selected from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey and Pan-STARRS1 (PS1), we construct a PS1-resolved matched sample of 101 barred and 101 unbarred NLS1s, matched in redshift, inclination, and image quality. Unbarred NLS1s are modestly but consistently brighter than barred NLS1s in several optical AGN luminosity indicators, including λL λ (5100 Å), broad H α , broad H β , narrow H α , narrow H β , and [O iii ] λ 5007, with typical offsets of ∼0.1–0.25 dex; the broad H α and narrow-line offsets are statistically significant, while the continuum and broad H β offsets are marginal. Monte Carlo resampling and a Bayesian model support the same direction of offset. In contrast, the main narrow-line diagnostics, including [O iii ]/H β , O3N2, and the [S ii ]-based electron density, are statistically consistent between the subsamples, although barred NLS1s show a higher N2 ratio. Within the barred subsample, the bar strength parameter e max shows a mild anticorrelation with the optical continuum and broad Balmer-line luminosities. These results indicate that large-scale stellar bars are not associated with enhanced instantaneous optical AGN luminosity. Instead, barred systems may experience more regulated or time-variable inner gas delivery, building circumnuclear gas reservoirs without necessarily increasing accretion power observed at the epoch traced by optical AGN emission.
