items.title: Multiplicity of Massive stars in the Milky Way (M3W). II. The brightest single O stars: Variability and systemic velocities
items.abstract: Multiplicity of Massive stars in the Milky Way ( is a project designed to augment our knowledge of the dynamical properties of massive stars within several kiloparsecs of the Sun. An often overlooked aspect of such properties is the determination of accurate systemic velocities, as they are affected by variability effects such as pulsations, line infilling by wind and disks, and incomplete knowledge about the central wavelengths. This lack of accuracy impairs studies on the origin of runaway and walkaway stars as well as on the velocity dispersions of stellar clusters. In this second paper of the series we wanted to increase the accuracy of the O stars systemic velocities in both isolated and multiple systems. To that end, we established how different wavelength regions are affected by variability, determined the thresholds for the detection of spectroscopic binarity, and obtained accurate central wavelengths including the effects of contamination, forbidden lines, and wind infilling. Our sample consists of the 41 brightest O stars (B łe 7.0 mag) thought to be single at the beginning of the project (summer 2025). We used multi-epoch high-resolution spectroscopy from the łili project cleaned with the UNWIND code and stellar models computed with FASTWIND. The epoch spectra were cross-correlated to study their variability in the form of radial velocity (RV) dispersions. The RVs were computed from (a) cross-correlation of H and He lines with FASTWIND models, (b) profile fitting of metallic lines, and (c) (for very fast rotators) cross-correlation of the full spectrum with a template star. A comparison between the RV dispersions for wavelength regions respectively dominated by He lines and by Hβ reveals different groups of stars in terms of variability: (a) non-supergiant slow rotators, (b) fast rotators, (c) supergiants, and (d) Oe stars. This is likely a manifestation of the different role of pulsations, winds, and disks in RV variability. We used that analysis to determine RV dispersion thresholds for the detection of new spectroscopic binaries (SBs). We also used a FASTWIND grid to establish the effects of (a) the presence of lines close to Balmer lines, (b) the existence of forbidden components in two lines, and (c) wind infilling in the determination of accurate RVs. With all of that, we determined RVs for our 41 stars, checked their accuracy comparing results from our three methods, and in some cases discovered significant differences with literature values. Our detailed analysis has further revealed four SB1 systems that were unknown in the summer of 2025 (68 Cyg, HD , HD A, and HD ), one new SB2 (HD ), two new Oe stars (HD and HD ), and three new Onfp stars (ξ Per, 68 Cyg, and HD ). items.title: Enzymatic Conversion from a Vicinal Diol to a Vicinal Diketone: Computational Study of the Conserved 6-Pyruvoyltetrahydropterin-Forming Stage in Mammalian and Bacterial PTPS
items.abstract: As a zinc- and magnesium-dependent triphosphatase, 6-pyruvoyl tetrahydropterin synthase (PTPS) catalyzes the conversion of dihydroneopterin triphosphate (H2NTP) to 6-pyruvoyltetrahydropterin (PPH4) and a triphosphate ion, representing a typical reaction for vicinal diketone biosynthesis from vicinal diol. The molecular mechanism of PTPS remains elusive owing to the lack of structural data containing native substrate H2NTP and magnesium ion. Here, we performed a quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) investigation based on a predicted PTPS structure, elucidating the complete atomistic reaction mechanism for triphosphate ion formation and stereoselective product generation. The overall catalytic reaction of PTPS proceeds via two half-reactions, each comprising four sequential proton-transfer steps. Both half-reactions involve the conversion of a hydroxyl group on the substrate into a carbonyl group, ultimately furnishing the pyruvoyl-containing product PPH4. The third proton transfer in the first half-reaction occurs preferentially on the Si-face of the critical carbanion intermediate, yielding the (R)-configured product, in agreement with the reported experimental detection results. These calculations not only unveil the structural origins of stereoselective vicinal diketone product formation, but also uncover a non-canonical triphosphate elimination pathway driven by a charge-center shift that facilitates C–O bond cleavage. These findings broaden the mechanistic paradigm of triphosphatase-mediated phosphate chemistry and offer foundational insights for synthesizing vicinal diketones from vicinal diols.

items.title: Investigating IceCube Neutrino Alerts with the HAWC Gamma-Ray Observatory
items.abstract: Abstract Neutrino emission from astrophysical sources has long been considered a signature of cosmic-ray acceleration. The IceCube Neutrino Observatory has observed a diffuse flux of TeV–PeV neutrinos, but very few confirmed sources have emerged. With the recent publication of the IceCube Event Catalog (IceCat-1), IceCube has released a list of probable astrophysical neutrinos from 2011 May to 2020 December, with follow-up alerts released via the Astrophysical Multi-messenger Observatory Network (AMON). Using the archival data from the High Altitude Water Cherenkov (HAWC) Gamma-Ray Observatory, we search for gamma-ray outbursts spatially coincident with these neutrino alerts using a Bayesian block algorithm. In this work, we consider 380 alerts, up to 2026 May 19, that are within HAWC’s field of view. We observe approximately a 5% coincident detection rate, which is consistent with expectations from background. Two of these detections contain the active galactic nuclei (AGNs) Mrk 421 and Mrk 501. We discuss the possibility of these AGNs producing the observed neutrino events when considering the HAWC results.

items.title: Stock-level volatility forecasting using machine learning: A comparative study of GARCH, Random Forest, LSTM, and GRU on US Equities.
items.abstract: Forecasting stock price volatility at the individual stock level is a major challenge in managing financial risks; it has widespread implications for portfolio strategies, pricing derivatives, and assessing regulatory capital adequacy. Although there have been a number of studies using market indices (e.g., VIX and associated methods) to study forecasting stock market volatility, relatively few studies have applied and evaluated a number of different types of machine learning methods to individual stock data in terms of actual (realised) volatility forecasting. This study fills that gap by presenting a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between stock price volatility and various machine learning techniques on a sample of ten well-known US stocks (across three sectors: technology, finance, and energy) based on data from January 2018 to December 2024 (1,759 trading days). We apply five modelling approaches: a classical GARCH(1,1) econometric model, a classical GJR-GARCH(1,1,1) econometric model, a Random Forest regressor, a two-layer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, and a two-layer Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) network. For each of the four modelling techniques, we use a rolling 5-day annualised actual (realised) volatility forecast as our final outcomes. Evaluation of the prediction results of each of these models was measured using RMSE, MAE, QLIKE loss, parametric Value-at-Risk (VaR) measures, Expected Shortfall (ES), and the Kupiec backtest. We also performed an analysis of the prevailing market regime through K-Means clustering, created an ablation study using variables as features in the models to assess the importance of those variables, and developed a computational efficiency benchmark for each model. In terms of predicted errors, Random Forest was proven to yield very low predicted error (mean RMSE = 0.0892) in comparison to deep learning methods, plus Random Forest was able to be trained approximately 7 times faster than deep learning methods. GRU was ranked second and outperformed LSTM on most of the metrics used in this evaluation. GARCH models remain a viable option for estimating risk measures and calibrating VaR, especially during period of stability in the financial markets.

items.title: Directed transport of fractional‑order asymmetrically coupled particle chains in ratchet potential.
items.abstract: This work constructs a fractional-order model to describe the dynamics of particle chains with asymmetric coupling subject to non-uniform viscoelastic media and an asymmetric periodic potential. The effects of multiple control parameters on the collective directed motion are systematically investigated. Numerical results reveal that the fractional-order coupled system can achieve directed transport in the absence of external forces and noise driving. Under suitable coupling strengths, the directed transport velocity of the particle chain generally rises as the fractional order increases. We also find that the average velocity of the particle chain exhibits generalized resonance responses with varying system parameters, featuring single-peak, double-peak and multi-peak resonant behaviors. Such resonant behaviors are sensitive to system parameters and originate from the competition between fractional power-law memory and interparticle coupling. Reverse directed transport can be triggered under appropriate parameter combinations, arising from the interplay of asymmetric coupling, medium memory and ratchet potential. Furthermore, under appropriate system parameters, noise can enhance the directed transport velocity, manifesting stochastic resonance in the system.

items.title: Dynamic analysis and spatiotemporal evolution of multi-stage knowledge dissemination under AI-enabled dual-channel "Interpersonal-Human-Machine" interaction.
items.abstract: With the deep integration of digitalization and artificial intelligence technologies into enterprise knowledge management, AI-assisted learning is reshaping the channels through which knowledge is acquired within organizations. Meanwhile, knowledge dissemination is evolving from traditional interpersonal interaction toward human-machine collaborative interaction. In light of this transformation, this study develops a multi-stage 2SEIR-CA dynamic model of knowledge dissemination under an AI-enabled mechanism that incorporates dual-channel "interpersonal-human-machine" interaction. Specifically, employees are classified into five states: employees who have not yet mastered the knowledge, employees with limited knowledge mastery, employees with strong knowledge mastery, knowledge-disseminating employees, and knowledge-exited employees. On this basis, the next-generation matrix method is employed to calculate the basic reproduction number of the system and to analyze the existence and stability of equilibrium points. An optimal control model is then established to derive strategies for promoting knowledge dissemination, and a cellular automaton model is introduced to characterize its spatiotemporal evolution. The results show that the system exhibits a pronounced threshold effect: when key dissemination parameters exceed their critical levels, knowledge can continue to diffuse within the organization; otherwise, it will gradually decay. Second, the AI-enabled mechanism enhances knowledge transformation efficiency and contact intensity, thereby significantly promoting the transition of employees with strong knowledge mastery to knowledge-disseminating employees. Third, the optimal control strategy proposed in this study can optimize transformation pathways across different stages under resource constraints, thereby improving overall dissemination efficiency and maintaining the structural stability of the dissemination system. Fourth, the spatiotemporal simulations demonstrate that, under optimal regulation, knowledge dissemination can form a stable diffusion pattern with high coverage. Under the assumptions and parameter settings of the proposed model, the findings provide theoretical insights into the dynamic mechanisms underlying AI-enabled knowledge dissemination and offer model-based implications for knowledge management practices in organizations.

items.title: The training-discovery paradox: Evidence from citizen science.
items.abstract: Training enhances classification accuracy in citizen science by directing visual attention toward predefined features, but may constrain attention to unexpected objects or features. We examined this tradeoff through an analysis of 206 citizen science discoveries and through controlled experiments using eye-tracking and verbal protocols. The analysis of existing discoveries showed that untrained contributors produced a broader range of discovery types, including the majority of opportunistic and serendipitous discoveries. In the primary experimental study, explicitly trained observers showed 34% fewer fixations on non-diagnostic features compared to untrained observers. Training also reduced attention to secondary entities and constrained how observers described novel stimuli, a phenomenon we term classification transference. Trained observers described unfamiliar entities by referencing missing trained-category features rather than reporting new attributes. Implicitly trained observers preserved broader attentional sampling while maintaining sensitivity to variation. The second experimental study provided a robustness check with 84 additional participants using written responses and confirmed the patterns observed in the first experiment. These findings demonstrate that training shapes both where observers look and what they report, establishing a perceptual boundary on discovery potential that conventional accuracy measures cannot detect.

items.title: A method for brain tumor detection and localization by means of deep learning and reliable prediction explainability.
items.abstract: Brain tumors, which are abnormal growths in the brain or central spinal canal, represent a serious global health threat. In 2023, they were responsible for 94,390 cases and 18,990 deaths in the US. Early detection with Magnetic Resonance Imaging is critical for effective treatment and higher survival rates. In this paper, we propose a method for the classification and localization of brain tumors in magnetic resonance imaging. Our method is based on the application of convolutional neural networks and for this task, we introduce and design a new network called the CBP_Net. The experimental analysis includes the Standard_CNN, a network designed by the authors, and other state-of-the-art networks, i.e., MobileNet, DenseNet, InceptionV3, ResNet50 and EfficientNetB0. This study emphasizes both quantitative and qualitative evaluations. The results demonstrate that the networks achieve optimal quantitative metrics: from 0.993 to 1.0 in accuracy. Qualitatively, we focus on visual explanations using Class Activation Mapping algorithms, specifically Grad-CAM and Score-CAM, to generate heatmaps highlighting relevant regions in the images. The Structural Similarity Index Measure is then employed to quantitatively measure the similarity between the heatmaps generated by the two CAM algorithms. This approach improves the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-driven brain tumor detection, helping clinicians diagnose.

items.title: BCFL-DAI-PUB: Blockchain-integrated federated learning with dynamic adaptive incentives for privacy-utility balanced credit risk modelling.
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of loan defaulters through collaborative analysis of financial data across multiple institutions is critical for maintaining financial stability and strengthening credit risk management. Although Federated Learning (FL) enables organizations to train models without exchanging raw data, its reliance on a centralized server introduces serious trust concerns, including vulnerability to gradient inversion and membership inference attacks. Blockchain-based Federated Learning (BCFL) addresses these challenges by cryptographically protecting and aggregating model updates through a smart contract, thereby providing a tamper-resistant learning process. In spite of these security enhancements, current BCFL frameworks do not ensure sustained client participation in real-world settings. Moreover, while traditional incentive mechanisms promote truthful participation and discourage free-riding and malicious behavior, they mainly reward model utility and neglect privacy contribution. To mitigate this limitation, we propose BCFL-DAI-PUB, a blockchain-federated learning framework integrating an innovative Dynamic Adaptive Incentive (DAI) mechanism to achieve a Privacy-Utility Balance (PUB). The proposed DAI dynamically applies three complementary incentive components, such as SCAFFOLD-based correction, adaptive differential privacy (DP-Boost), and monetary rewards, to jointly optimize learning utility and privacy protection. This work promotes honest participation, discourages dishonest behavior, and enables rapid recovery from malicious attacks, thereby improving global convergence and overall model effectiveness. The proposed BCFL-DAI-PUB achieves a final AUC of 0.91, improving upon the HE-based BCFL-PS-HER baseline (0.86) by 1.06×. By replacing homomorphic encryption with adaptive differential privacy and combining it with a dynamic incentive mechanism, the proposed framework improves both efficiency and resilience over the baseline, which relies on static reputation-based coordination. Compared with the baseline BCFL-PS-HER model, BCFL-DAI-PUB recovers from malicious disruption 1.82× faster and achieves approximately 1.22× higher MIA resistance, while the baseline incurs approximately 1.09× higher communication overhead and 1.14× higher storage overhead. These results show that BCFL-DAI-PUB improves predictive performance, strengthens privacy protection, reduces system cost, and provides more robust operation in blockchain-enabled federated credit-risk modelling.

items.title: Integrating YOLOv8-based disaster detection with deep reinforcement learning for closed-loop UAV emergency response scheduling: A simulation study.
items.abstract: Aerial perception and dispatch scheduling in unmanned aerial vehicle emergency response are commonly arranged as a one-directional pipeline, and the contribution of closing the loop between them has not been measured under controlled conditions. This study evaluates a framework in which a YOLOv8 scene classifier gates task discovery, a Disaster Situation State Matrix aggregates spatially indexed detection outputs under exponential temporal decay, and a proximal policy optimization scheduler acts on that matrix. Evaluation used a 32 × 32 grid testbed with four vehicles, ten training seeds per configuration, and one hundred frozen evaluation scenarios per seed, with a complete two-by-two ablation separating policy access to the state matrix from the rate at which the matrix is refreshed. Runtime perception updating raised task completion from 0.4971 to 0.5859 relative to an initial-snapshot policy, a gain of 8.87 percentage points (95% CI 7.26 to 10.32, Holm-adjusted p = 0.0078). Policy access to the state matrix carried a main effect of 36.42 percentage points (95% CI 34.83 to 37.79) and refresh rate a main effect of 1.81 percentage points (95% CI 0.90 to 2.82), with no evidence of interaction. Under a shared six-action interface and identical perception constraints, the proposed scheduler exceeded a greedy heuristic by 3.44 percentage points (95% CI 2.03 to 4.91, Holm-adjusted p = 0.0078). Replacing confusion-matrix sampling with replayed YOLOv8 predictions on held-out images reduced completion by 1.28 percentage points, and temporally persistent detection errors extended the longest uninterrupted error run to seventy-one steps. Structural exposure of the state matrix to the scheduling policy, rather than refresh frequency alone, accounts for the observed performance of the framework.

items.title: Climate and Other Human Causes of Spatial Variation in Mallard Mortality and Population Dynamics.
items.abstract: Wildlife population dynamics change across time and space, but few studies use formal spatiotemporal statistical models to understand these patterns. The population distribution of mallards ( Anas platyrhyncos ) in the Prairie Pothole Region of central North America (PPR) has shifted dramatically over the past several decades as agricultural intensity and climate have changed. We examined spatiotemporal variation in survival, natural mortality, and harvest mortality rates for mallards in the PPR from 1974 to 2023 using intrinsic conditional autoregressive models in a Bayesian framework. There was substantial variation over time and space for all demographic rates, and relationships between mortality and habitat variables varied by age and sex cohort. Specifically, environmental relationships indicate that habitats with less agricultural activity and more wetlands decrease survival via increased natural mortality driven by reproductive risks. We also found a worrying trend: females exhibited declining survival probabilities since the late 1980s and early 1990s. Our analyses demonstrate major variation in survival rates of a well-studied organism across an environmental gradient, reveal subtle but critical differences relative to inference obtained from pooled data, and provide a clear roadmap to future research that can inform spatially explicit conservation and management goals.

items.title: Stable Reference Genes for RT-qPCR in House Dust Mite Dermatophagoides farinae (Acari: Pyroglyphidae) at Different Developmental Stages.
items.abstract: To investigate the growth and development mechanisms in Dermatophagoides farinae , it is essential to understand its gene expression profiles across different life stages, which are typically assessed by transcriptional profiling based on RT-qPCR. Suitable reference genes are vital for ensuring reliable and accurate results; however, none have been established for this species across different developmental stages. Here, we analyzed expression profiles of ten frequently used reference genes ( RPL18 , RPS18 , RPS 9, EF1A , RPS28 , Actin , V-ATPaseB , GAPDH , RPL32 , and α-tubulin ) to determine their stability across different developmental stages of D. farinae . Four algorithms (GeNorm, NormFinder, BestKeeper, and ΔCt) were employed to examine gene stability, and their results were subsequently integrated by RefFinder to yield a comprehensive assessment. The results indicated that RPL18 and RPS28 were the two top-ranked stable reference genes, whereas α-tubulin and RPL32 showed the lowest stability. To confirm the robustness of the chosen reference genes, we assessed cytochrome P450 3A8 expression at developmental stages of D. farinae using three independent biological replicates and three technical replicates per stage. Normalization against RPL18 and RPS28 , individually or combined, produced expression patterns consistent with previously reported developmental trends of cytochrome P450 genes in mites and insects, namely higher expression in larvae and protonymphs, lower expression in later stages, and minimal expression observed in eggs. In contrast, unstable reference genes yielded inconsistent results, thereby confirming our findings. In conclusion, this study identifies two highly stable reference genes that will provide a robust foundation for precise gene expression normalization and functional studies in D. farinae .

items.title: Seabird Prey in Space and Time: Combining Multiple Datasets to Model the Distribution of Sandeel (Ammodytes marinus) and Sprat (Sprattus sprattus) in the North Sea.
items.abstract: Many seabird populations along the UK's East Coast have declined over the past three decades. A key concern is reduced availability of their primary breeding season prey, sandeel ( Ammodytes marinus ). While some seabirds have partially switched to sprat ( Sprattus sprattus ), this is not universal. Studying these predator-prey dynamics requires fine-scale estimates of prey distributions that are both spatially and temporally resolved-yet such data are limited, especially for sandeel due to sampling challenges. We evaluate the utility of large-scale ICES bottom trawl surveys to model sandeel distribution, combining them with winter dredge surveys designed specifically for this species. For sprat, we combine bottom trawl data with the Herring Acoustic Survey. Using hierarchical Bayesian spatiotemporal models (R-INLA), we estimate the biomass of small and medium sandeel (≤ 16 cm) and sprat across the entire North Sea from 2000 to 2020, accounting for spatial and temporal dependencies. We validate our sandeel models by comparison with other modelling approaches and ICES stock assessments. Results reveal marked regional variation: sandeel increased in Area 3 (Norwegian EEZ), declined in Areas 1 and 2 and fluctuated in Area 4. Sprat biomass increased over time, with a modest northward expansion. This study provides the first North Sea-wide, fine-scale, multi-decadal distribution models for these two key seabird prey species and identifies important regional drivers of their populations.

items.title: Cross-kingdom volatile networks shape plant resilience.
items.abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are interpreted as transient, unidirectional signals in plant-microbe interactions. We argue that this reductionist framing obscures their emergent role as regulators of ecological network dynamics, influencing stability-associated properties of plant-microbe systems. We propose a conceptual framework based on five principles (gradient logic, blend emergence, feedback reciprocity, threshold switching, and multiscale coupling) and use it to generate falsifiable predictions for how plant-derived and microbial VOCs operate as a cross-kingdom regulatory network shaping microbiome assembly, plant physiological plasticity, and multitrophic interactions. Key mechanistic gaps are critically evaluated alongside testable approaches for probing volatile-mediated ecological dynamics. Viewing volatile networks as adaptive ecological infrastructure reframes plant-microbiome resilience with implications for sustainable agriculture and ecological restoration under global change.

items.title: Effect of sampling on the descriptive distributions of correlated random walks.
items.abstract: Random walks are commonly used to model movement throughout the sciences, from the motion of particles and molecules to the observed behaviour of animals and crowds. The correlated random walk, which assumes a level of persistence between movement directions, has become ubiquitous in the analysis and modelling of movement in recent times. Whilst many properties of the correlated random walk are known, there are still many which are not fully understood and, therefore, under-utilised in movement data analysis. Here we consider the effect that sub-sampling has on the descriptive distributions of correlated random walks. Our work demonstrates the connection between the distributions of turning angles and step-lengths that characterise a correlated random walk, along with the resulting distributions found after sub-sampling. We provide examples for where this approach could aid in movement analysis as well as determining future ways the work could be extended.

items.title: The moderating role of anger rumination and self-control in the day-to-day associations between irritability and sleep in male adolescents: An exploratory experience sampling method study.
items.abstract: Background Irritability is highly prevalent in adolescents and may be exacerbated by sleep disturbances, with sleep patterns undergoing significant changes during this developmental period. Reciprocally, poor sleep may generate an increase in anger dysregulation. This exploratory study investigates the day-to-day associations between sleep and irritability, as well as the moderating effects of maladaptive (i.e., anger rumination) and adaptive (i.e., self-control) emotion regulation (ER) strategies. Methods Fifty-six male adolescents aged 12-18, with diverse sleep and emotional problems, participated in a 9-day experience sampling method study. Participants also completed self-report questionnaires assessing irritability, sleep quantity and quality, and maladaptive and adaptive ER strategies. Linear mixed effect models with lagged covariates were used to test associations and moderating effects. Results At the within-person level, sleep quality was associated with next-day irritability ( β std = -0.92, 95% CI [-1.31, -0.53). Higher daily anger rumination ( β std = 0.25, 95% CI [0.17, 0.34]), and daily self-control ( β std = -0.18, 95% CI [-0.27, -0.10]) were directly associated with higher next-day irritability. At the between-person level, lower self-control was also associated with higher next-day irritability ( β std = -0.52, 95% CI [-0.77, -0.27]). Interactions between daily sleep quality and between-person anger rumination ( βstdinteraction = 0.18, 95% [0.07, 0.30]), and self-control ( βstdinteraction = 0.75, 95% CI [0.38, 1.12]) were related with irritability. Reciprocally, lower irritability from the day was associated with better sleep quality the following night ( β std = -0.11, 95% CI [-0.20, -0.01]). Conclusion These preliminary findings suggest that sleep may be related to next-day irritability in adolescent boys and may vary as a function of anger rumination and self-control. Additionally, irritability also showed a potential association with subsequent sleep. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small, all-male adolescent sample. Future studies including larger and more diverse adolescent samples are needed to assess their generalizability and robustness.

items.title: Seeing Sound, Feeling Music: Crossmodal Correspondences, Audiovisual Emotion, and the Moderating Roles of Expertise, Age, Gender, and STEM Knowledge
items.abstract: Can the shape of a sound wave be visually observed, and can music be emotionally felt? This review synthesizes evidence from crossmodal correspondence research, audiovisual integration studies, and the psychology of music to argue that both questions are best answered through a single theoretical lens: the human perceptual system spontaneously maps auditory dimensions onto visual and spatial dimensions, and these same mappings participate in the generation of musical emotion. We first review the core correspondences — pitch–height, loudness–size, and the bouba/kiki sound–shape effect — documenting their universality, their roots in the physical statistics of the environment, and their neural substrates . We then trace how these correspondences support the deliberate visualization of sound in drawing and gesture paradigms , and review the literature on felt versus perceived musical emotion, including chills and their individual-difference correlates . The audiovisual integration literature shows that congruent visual information reliably amplifies both perceived and felt emotion in music . Finally, we evaluate four candidate moderators of the accuracy with which people see sound and the intensity with which they feel music: musical expertise, age, gender, and STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) knowledge. Musical expertise sharpens both crossmodal mapping accuracy and audiovisual temporal precision ; age follows an inverted-U trajectory for sound–shape association strength ; gender effects are documented but understudied ; and STEM training biases perception bidirectionally, sharpening domain-relevant attention while inducing expert blind spots . We close with an integrated framework and open questions for future research.

items.title: Attitude Toward Persons With Mental Illness in Bangladesh: Scale Validation and Status Assessment.
items.abstract: Background Stigma toward persons with mental illness remains a major barrier to mental health care. No validated Bangla instrument is available to assess attitudes toward persons with mental illness in Bangladesh. Objective This study aimed to adapt and validate the culturally adapted Bangla version of the Attitudes Toward Persons with Mental Illness (APMI) scale and to assess attitudes among undergraduate medical students and Islamic religious leaders in Bangladesh. Methods A psychometric validation study was conducted from July 2025 to June 2026 among 489 participants (249 medical students and 240 Imams). The original 16-item APMI scale was translated and culturally adapted following standard guidelines. The sample was independently divided into exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 245) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 244) subsamples. EFA used polychoric correlations, minimum residual extraction, oblimin rotation, and parallel analysis. CFA compared one- and two-factor models using the WLSMV estimator. Reliability, measurement invariance, group differences, and multivariable associations were also evaluated. Results EFA supported a two-factor structure comprising Fear/Social Avoidance and Interpersonal Acceptance. The correlated two-factor CFA model showed substantially better fit than the one-factor model (scaled CFI = 0.967, TLI = 0.956, RMSEA = 0.071, 90% CI 0.049-0.092, SRMR = 0.046). Ordinal alpha was 0.83 and 0.78. Measurement invariance was supported at the configural, partial metric, and partial threshold/scalar levels. Medical students had lower scores than Imams. After adjustment, the difference remained significant ( β = 5.02, 95% CI 2.89-7.15; p Conclusion The 10-item culturally adapted Bangla APMI scale demonstrates acceptable structural validity and internal consistency for assessing attitudes toward persons with mental illness for Bangla-speaking populations.

items.title: Time-Variant Patterns of Comorbid Depression and Anxiety Across Early to Late Adolescence: The Sex-Specific Role of Emotion Regulation.
items.abstract: Aims Depression-anxiety comorbidity is common in adolescence, yet prevention efforts often overlook the nonlinear course of psychosocial development. This study mapped the dynamic risk of depression-anxiety comorbidity across adolescence and examined whether emotion regulation moderated these associations by grade and sex. Methods We utilised time-varying effect modelling (TVEM) on data of youth from all primary and secondary schools in Chenzhou, China ( n = 58,622; grades 4-12), to map the dynamic change of comorbid risk and potential moderating role of emotion regulation, with consideration of sex difference. Participants reported depressive and anxiety symptoms through the patient health questionnaire and generalised anxiety disorder questionnaire, respectively. The emotion regulation questionnaire (ERQ) measured two dimensions of emotion regulation, cognitive reappraisal and expression suppression. Results Overall comorbid risk increased throughout adolescence. Anxiety (OR = 1.67, 95% CI [1.61, 1.74]) and depressive (OR = 1.68, 95% CI [1.50, 1.89]) symptoms had similar overall comorbid risk, while depression-related risk became stronger than anxiety-related risk in late adolescence. Sex-specific patterns revealed higher comorbid risks in females. A gradual risk progression across grades emerged in males, whereas females showed a steeper increase in depression-associated comorbidity and an anxiety-associated peak around grade 8 (OR = 1.74, 95% CI [1.69, 1.80]). The role of emotion regulation is more pronounced in females than males. Cognitive reappraisal had a protective role against anxiety-related comorbid risk (OR = 0.99, 95% CI [0.99, 0.99]) and a maladaptive role for depression-related comorbid risk (OR = 1.01, 95% CI [1.01, 1.01]). The maladaptive role of expressive suppression for anxiety-associated comorbidity peaked during middle school for females and only emerged during early adolescence for males. Interpretation Depression-anxiety comorbidity showed distinct grade- and sex-specific risk patterns across adolescence. These findings advocate for precise interventions prioritising anxiety management during primary-to-middle school transition and depression prevention during late adolescence. Emotion regulation interventions should be tailored by sex, adolescence stage and existing symptoms.

items.title: Deep Learning for Multi-Component Gearbox Fault Diagnosis on the PHM 2009 Benchmark: A Critical Review and Comparative Evaluation of Time–Frequency Representations and Network Architectures
items.abstract: Concurrent faults in gears, bearings and shafts remain among the hardest cases for vibration-based condition monitoring of industrial gearboxes, because their signatures overlap, modulate one another and shift with speed and load. The 2009 PHM Society gearbox has become the standard public benchmark for this multi-component problem, yet published results on it are scattered across input types, network designs and validation schemes, which makes headline accuracies hard to compare. This article presents a critical review of deep-learning diagnosis on this benchmark and the wider gearbox literature, organised around three design choices: signal representation, model family and evaluation protocol. To ground the discussion, we re-analyse a controlled experiment in which three convolutional architectures were trained on 10,240 images per representation (continuous wavelet transform scalograms, short-time Fourier transform spectrograms and wavelet synchrosqueezed images) covering eight spur-gearbox health states. A compact five-stage batch-normalised network reached 99.90%, 99.85% and 99.66% test accuracy with wavelet, Synchrosqueezed and spectrogram inputs, respectively, but the margins among the best models correspond to only a few of the 2,048 test images. On a separate held-out validation subset, accuracy fell to 94.53%, 92.03% and 77.34%, making the representation effect far more visible. Comparison with published capsule-attention, architecture-search and transformer studies shows that reported accuracies on the same benchmark range from below 80% to above 99.5%, mainly because of differences in splitting protocol. We conclude with a reporting checklist and research agenda for leakage-aware, physics-informed and deployable gearbox diagnosis.

items.title: US Carbapenemase Genomic Panel: An Open and Annually Refreshed State-by-Year Table of Carbapenemase Genes in Public U.S. Gram-Negative Genomes
items.abstract: Carbapenemase-producing Gram-negative bacteria are among the most urgent antimicrobial resistance threats in the United States, and public health lab-oratories increasingly characterize them by whole-genome sequencing. The NCBI Pathogen Detection project screens every public genome in its scope with AMRFinderPlus, but its outputs are organized by organism group and release rather than by place and time, and sample metadata are free text. This paper describes the US Carbapenemase Genomic Panel v1.0.0, an open, versioned ta-ble of five carbapenemase families (KPC, NDM, OXA-48-like, VIM and IMP) in public U.S. genomes of Klebsiella, Escherichia coli, Enterobacter, Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, tabulated by state, collection year, organism and harmonized isolation source (clinical, screening, environmental, unknown). Fam-ily membership follows the AMRFinderPlus Reference Gene Hierarchy, and every harmonization decision is published with the data. The v1.0.0 build, from NCBI data retrieved on 12 October 2026, covers 257,965 genomes, of which 38,511 (14.9%) carry at least one of the five families. NDM-carrying genomes (17,736) now outnumber KPC-carrying genomes (16,911), and NDM has exceeded KPC in every complete collection year since 2021. A state could be assigned to only 34.3% of carbapenemase-positive genomes; 90.2% of the remainder come from a single CDC BioProject (HAI-Seq Gram-negative bacteria) that records country only. The panel therefore supports national trend description and state-level description of the located public record, but not comparison of burden between states. The scripted pipeline is designed for annual refresh, with each version archived under a stable concept DOI.

items.title: Biodegradable polylactic acid microplastics pose greater field nitrous oxide emission risks than conventional polyethylene by reshaping microbial production-reduction pathways in a wheat-maize rotation system.
items.abstract: Microplastic contamination in agroecosystems is increasing, yet the field-scale effects of biodegradable microplastics on soil nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions remain unclear. We conducted a wheat-maize rotation field experiment to compare conventional polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs) and biodegradable polylactic acid microplastics (PLA-MPs) at three application levels. Measurements included N2O fluxes, soil physicochemical properties, N-transformation enzyme activities, potential nitrification and denitrification rates, functional gene abundances, N2O/(N2O+N2) product ratios, 15N-18O-based N2O production pathways. Two-way ANOVA showed that microplastic type was the most consistent determinant of key responses, whereas concentration and interaction effects varied among indicators and seasons. PE-MPs caused weak and variable changes in soil N cycling and cumulative N2O emissions. In contrast, PLA-MPs increased cumulative N2O emissions by 38.9-61.1%, increased dissolved organic carbon, lowered pH, suppressed ammonia monooxygenase activity and nitrification, and stimulated nitrite reductase activity, potential denitrification, and nirK/nirS abundances. Increased N2O/(N2O+N2) and (nirK+nirS)/nosZ ratios indicated a stronger imbalance between N2O production and nosZ-mediated reduction. Dual-isotope tracing further showed that microplastics reduced nitrifier nitrification and shifted N2O production toward nitrifier denitrification, coupled nitrification-denitrification, and heterotrophic denitrification, with the strongest shift under PLA-MPs. These results demonstrate PLA-MPs pose greater N2O emission risks than PE-MPs, biodegradability does not necessarily imply environmental safety.

items.title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis enhances salt tolerance in Eucalyptus grandis by coordinating antioxidant defense, hormone accumulation and ion homeostasis.
items.abstract: Eucalyptus is a globally important timber species, yet its productivity is markedly constrained by salt stress. Although arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi play crucial roles under environmental stress, the integrated physiological and molecular mechanisms by which they confer salinity tolerance in E. grandis remain incompletely understood. In this study, we explored the impact of inoculation with the AM fungus Rhizophagus irregularis on the physiological, biochemical, and transcriptional responses of E. grandis seedlings across a NaCl gradient (0-200 mM). The results indicated that AM symbiosis significantly alleviated salt-induced growth inhibition, membrane damage and water deficit. Relative to non-mycorrhizal plants, AM-colonized seedlings exhibited lower accumulations of osmolytes and oxidative stress markers, while maintaining higher activities of key antioxidant enzymes. Hormonal profiling revealed a coordinated downregulation of stress-related phytohormones in mycorrhizal plants under salinity. Additionally, AM plants accumulated less sodium (Na+) and more potassium (K+) than non-mycorrhizal controls, suggesting enhanced Na+ efflux and K+ uptake under salt stress. Genome-wide analysis identified 23 candidate SOS pathway genes in E. grandis, and qPCR expression profiling revealed that all of these responded to AM symbiosis under salt stress, suggesting that AM symbiosis may regulate SOS pathway gene expression as part of its salt tolerance mechanism. Redundancy analysis suggested strong correlations among enhanced antioxidant enzyme activity, hormonal adjustments, ion homeostasis and the expression of specific EgSOS genes. Collectively, these findings provide integrated physiological and molecular evidence that AM symbiosis improves salt tolerance in a woody species through modulation of antioxidant defenses, hormonal balance, ion homeostasis and SOS pathway gene expression.

items.title: Porcine jejunal Peyer's patches leukocytes are a potent source of mucosal IgA binding to Streptococcus suis and suilysin.
items.abstract: Human Streptococcus suis infections are frequently linked to undercooked pork consumption, particularly in Southeast Asia. Experimental evidence indicates that S. suis can cross the intestinal barrier and cause systemic infection in pigs, suggesting the gut as a plausible entry site. However, mucosal immunity against S. suis in the intestinal tract remains poorly characterized. Here, we provide initial insights into the intestinal source and production of mucosal IgA against S. suis in 8-week-old conventional pigs. We show that jejunal and ileal mucus contains IgA recognizing a commensal S. suis isolate as well as a virulent S. suis cps2 strain. Mucosal IgA antibodies also bind to the secreted virulence-associated protein suilysin (SLY). Flow cytometric analysis of porcine Peyer's patches (PP) leukocytes of the jejunum (JPP) and the ileum (IPP) revealed a significantly higher frequency of IgA + B cells in JPP. Moreover, JPP-derived leukocytes showed higher constitutive and stimulation-induced total IgA secretion than IPP-derived leukocytes. Stimulation, either with the T cell-associated factors CD40L and IL-21 or the TLR1/2 ligand Pam3Cys-SK4 induced anti-S. suis IgA secretion, particularly in JPP-derived leukocyte cultures, indicating a contribution of innate immune mechanisms and an important role for T cell help. Finally, IgA induced by in vitro stimulation of JPP- or IPP-derived leukocytes recognized commensal and virulent S. suis as well as SLY, involved in disrupting epithelial barriers. Our results suggest that S. suis elicits a mucosal immune response in the intestinal tract of conventional piglets, with B cells in JPP representing a key site of IgA production.

items.title: The MeerKAT 1.3 GHz survey of the Large Magellanic Cloud: Point Source Catalogue
items.abstract: Abstract We present a point source catalogue of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) using observations from the MeerKAT radio telescope across a broad frequency band centred at 1295 MHz (L-Band) with 12 sub-bands and a resolution of 8″×8″. We investigate source flux density distributions and spectral indices and compare these with previous similar radio catalogues such as those conducted with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) telescope at 888 MHz. This new MeerKAT survey reaches a lower average noise level of 11 μJy beam−1, compared with the previous ASKAP levels of 58 μJy beam−1. This higher sensitivity and resolution allow the detection of a significantly larger number of faint sources. The catalogue includes 339,128 point sources; a substantial increase over the 54,612 sources detected by ASKAP providing critical insights into the population distribution, spectral properties, positional accuracy, and overall improvement in source recovery and survey depth.

items.title: Expression of White and Gray Matter Autism Functional Network Connectivity Signatures in Infancy
items.abstract: Functional connectivity studies have provided valuable insights into altered brain organization in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, most functional connectivity studies focus exclusively on either gray matter (GM) regions or white matter (WM) tracts and examine specific age groups, rather than investigating their functional interactions across brain development. This limits our understanding of how GM-WM functional interactions evolve developmentally and may obscure important aspects of brain network organization in ASD. We combined integrated WM+GM functional network connectivity (FNC) with brain-wide risk scores (BRSs) to quantify ASD-associated pattern expression in ABIDE I/II and an independent infant cohort. We employed a NeuroMark framework with predefined WM and GM intrinsic connectivity networks templates, to estimate subject-level FNC. First, we identified two distinct patterns of altered WM+GM FNC in ASD: GM-related hypoconnectivity centered on the paralimbic network and WM-GM hyperconnectivity centered on the frontal network. These findings highlight the involvement of higher-order cognitive networks and the importance of WM-GM functional interactions in characterizing ASD-related connectivity alterations. Second, infants with a higher familial likelihood of autism exhibited greater mean expression of ASD-associated FNC patterns than those with a lower familial likelihood, as quantified by BRS. These group-level findings do not establish developmental persistence or predict diagnostic outcomes at the individual level.

items.title: Completeness and dynamical stability in exoplanet occurrence rates
items.abstract: Exoplanet population studies are often quantified through the "occurrence rate" of certain types of planet. This value can be calculated from a survey of a sample of stars by taking the "detection rate" and correcting with a completeness factor. This completeness is calculated via detection limits on each individual star, and can be calculated either individually for each detected planet or averaged in a certain area of parameter space. We test whether either the average completeness or individual completeness performs better than the other. We also test whether including dynamical stability constraints in the detection limits improves the occurrence rate results. We use synthetic sets of exoplanetary systems and calculate occurrence rates for each and compare to what the value would be with perfect information. We compare how close each method is to the ground truth to assess which is most suitable. Overall, in our synthetic sets, the average completeness is more reliable though it can be a problem if there is a sharp change in the underlying population within the area of parameter-space considered. We find that using dynamical stability conditions causes a bias in the occurrence rate and do not recommend using these.

items.title: Likely Metal Scarring in the Magnetic White Dwarf LHS 2534
items.abstract: There are only three white dwarfs known to possess metal-enriched polar caps due to magnetically guided accretion. These rare systems offer a unique opportunity to study planetesimal accretion and how magnetic fields influence the spreading of material across the atmosphere. To better study these processes however, more targets are needed. Here we report our findings from an observing campaign on the magnetic white dwarf LHS 2534. Time-resolved spectra at the MMT show clear variability in the strength of the Na I and Cr I features. We find that the strengths of these features vary over a period of 19.46 and 19.36 hours respectively, closely matching the 20.22 hour period determined from K2 photometry. Our findings demonstrate the ability to detect and study these variable objects with spectroscopy, and time-series observations of similar targets in the future will provide more insight into how these atmospheres form.

items.title: Dietary intake of vitamin B12 (cobalamin) and gastric cancer risk: a pooled analysis within the StoP Project.
items.abstract: The effect of vitamin B12 (cobalamin) intake on gastric cancer is unclear. We investigated this association within the Stomach Cancer Pooling Project. Data from eight case-control studies within an international consortium were harmonized. Study-specific quartiles of dietary B12 intake (μg/day) were created using food frequency questionnaires and country-specific dietary composition tables. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between B12 and gastric cancer were calculated using multivariable logistic regressions adjusted by major sociodemographic and lifestyle factors. A random-effect meta-analysis pooling study-specific associations was also conducted. Secondary analyses were further adjusted for Helicobacter pylori (Hp) and dietary factors. Analyses stratified by anatomical subsite, histological type, sex, age, smoking, alcohol, and socioeconomic status (SES) were performed. The main analysis included 2228 cases and 7096 controls. A borderline positive association was observed between vitamin B12 intake and gastric cancer (OR = 1.04, 95% CI = 0.99-1.10 per quartile of intake). Results only slightly attenuated after adjusting for Hp and dietary factors. No statistical heterogeneity was found by histology and anatomical subsite, despite a higher risk being observed for the intestinal subtype (OR = 1.10, 95% CI = 1.02-1.19 per quartile of intake). Women, the elderly, never smokers, no-to-low alcohol consumers, and individuals from high SES had an increased risk of gastric cancer with increasing B12 intake, with no significant heterogeneity. Overall, dietary vitamin B12 intake was not associated with gastric cancer risk, while a positive association was observed for intestinal-type gastric cancer and within specific population subgroups.

items.title: Innovation amidst Turmoil, Part 2: Narratives and Sensemaking among German Managers during the Pandemic
items.abstract: How actors make sense of complex and uncertain situations shapes their perceived agency to foster innovation and organizational change. We present a case study on the sensemaking processes of German managers during the COVID-19 pandemic to gain insights for researchers and decision-makers interested in navigating uncertainty. Based on data collected (n=209) via an online questionnaire and grounded in theories of sensemaking and narrative discourse analysis, we identify seven distinct narratives that reveal varying perceptions of agency, problem framing, and modes of acting under uncertainty: “Business as usual”, “early mover”, “stronger together”, “step-by-step”, “bold leadership”, “acting impossible”, and “against the tide”. Based on our case study, we identify promising avenues for future research and discuss the practical relevance of proactive and collective sensemaking, emotions, detecting weak signals, and future-oriented narratives in economics for decision-making under uncertainty as well as perceptions of agency in (organizational) innovation. items.title: The future workplace: developing the human-machine symbioscape
items.abstract: Purpose This paper develops the concept of the human-machine symbioscape to explain how work environments shape collaboration between humans and AI-enabled machines. Extending servicescape thinking from customer-employee encounters to hybrid human-machine work systems, the paper positions environmental design as a core antecedent of human–machine adaptive collaboration, with particular relevance for service and frontline settings where visibility, coordination, and role clarity are critical. Design/methodology/approach The paper is conceptual and theory building in nature. It synthesises insights from biological symbiosis, servicescape research, sociotechnical and sociomaterial theory, organisational sensemaking and team adaptation research to develop a deductive typology of the human-machine symbioscape as a three-tiered environmental construct, its cue categories, and its design-critical properties. The framework is further illustrated through a structured coding of relevant human-machine collaboration studies. Findings The paper conceptualises the symbioscape as a three-tier environmental architecture comprising physical–digital, socio-relational, and institutional–ecosystem conditions. Across these tiers, six cue categories shape what human and AI-enabled actors can notice, how they coordinate work, and how collaborative routines are reinforced over time. Drawing on Weick's sensemaking theory, the framework links these tiers to enactment, selection, and retention processes, and explains how they influence adaptation speed, adaptation effectiveness, and adaptation persistence in human–AI collaboration. Research limitations/implications The paper is purely conceptual and does not empirically test the proposed relationships. Its evidence base is limited to published studies and illustrative coding, with a strong emphasis on service and frontline contexts. It identifies an agenda for future research around operationalising symbioscape constructs, testing the proposed relationships empirically, and examining how individual tiers and cross-tier configurations jointly affect human–machine work. Practical implications The symbioscape framework provides managers with a structured lens for designing AI-enabled workplaces. It highlights how deliberate choices in physical–digital visibility and interface design, socio-relational workflow sequencing and interaction load, and institutional governance, training, and role architecture can improve the speed, quality and durability of human–machine adaptation. The framework can be used to diagnose service work environments, where frontline employees must coordinate with intelligent systems under conditions of customer presence, temporal pressure, and operational variability. Originality/value The paper introduces the symbioscape as a novel, three-tier environmental construct for human–machine collaboration, extending the servicescape from customer–employee encounters to hybrid human–AI work systems. It adds a missing environmental layer to human-machine collaboration research by systematically integrating dispersed insights on context into a coherent framework that links environmental cue structures to sensemaking and adaptation outcomes. For scholars, it offers an integrative conceptual architecture; for practitioners, it provides a foundation for designing and structuring future workplaces that foster adaptive human–machine collaboration.

items.title: An observational study of food-related emotional expectancies, diet quality and comfort eating in the UK adult population
items.abstract: Abstract According to expectancy theory, people eat food that they expect will bring positive emotions. The present research aimed to identify food and non-alcoholic beverages UK adults most expected to bring positive emotions; test influences of high fat, salt and/or sugar (HFSS) and branding on expectancies; and investigate associations of expectancies with diet quality and comfort eating (i.e. eating induced by negative emotions). A representative sample of UK adults (n 1203; M age = 47 years; 52 % women; 87 % white) viewed food and non-alcoholic beverage images and completed the Anticipated Effects of Food Scale-Brief, a food frequency questionnaire, and questions about comfort eating and sociodemographic background. We ranked means of positive expectancies, conducted multilevel modelling to test influences of HFSS and branding on expectancies and examined correlations among expectancies, diet quality and comfort eating. Participants more strongly expected eating branded HFSS (e.g. Cadbury Twirl chocolate) v. generic non-HFSS (e.g. prawn curry) would result in positive emotions [b = 0·10, se = 0·04, p = ·02, 95 % CI (0·02, 0·18)]. Greater positive expectancies for HFSS – branded and generic – were associated with worse diet quality, especially positive expectancies for ice cream sundaes, fizzy drinks and chocolate (rs = –0·14 to −0·19, ps < ·001). Greater positive expectancies for HFSS and negative expectancies for HFSS and non-HFSS were associated with more frequent comfort eating (rs = 0·08 to 0·30, ps < ·05). Targeting positive HFSS expectancies through food environment policy and behavioural programmes may be a promising strategy for improving diet quality and reducing comfort eating in the UK adult population. Adults who comfort eat may also benefit from challenging negative expectancies for all foods.

items.title: Le collectif de travailleurs indépendants comme forme d’organisation spécifique et en tension
items.abstract: Le travail indépendant peut conduire à s’associer en « collectifs » pour répondre à un ensemble d’enjeux et de difficultés, qu’elles soient psychologiques, identitaires, financières, de compétence, ou liées à l’accès aux ressources. Cet article conceptuel, illustré par quelques données empiriques, montre que ces collectifs d’indépendants, en tant qu’associations durables, mais sans formalisation juridique dédiée, traversent l’ensemble de la littérature, bien qu’ils soient associés à une liste de difficultés à dépasser, et qu’ils se distinguent clairement d’autres formes d’association ou de rapprochement de travailleurs indépendants (communautés, coopératives et coopératives d’activité). Cette analyse nous conduit à proposer une conceptualisation plus claire du collectif d’indépendants comme forme organisationnelle porteuse d’une tension inhérente, ainsi que des implications pour la théorie et la pratique, et un agenda de recherche sur le sujet.

items.title: A standardized dataset of full-body audio-visual stimuli of Central European women and men
items.abstract: Background Standardized visual stimuli are widely used in research on social perception and first impression formation, but available stimulus sets predominantly consist of static facial images. We present a dataset of standardized audio-visual recordings designed to provide static, dynamic, and acoustic information from full-body recordings of adult women and men. Methods The dataset contains recordings from 120 participants (59 women and 61 men; aged 18–40 years) recruited in the Czech Republic. Participants wore standardized sportswear and were recorded under controlled lighting, camera, background, and audio conditions while standing, walking, turning, and speaking a standardized sentence. We acquired video at 6 K resolution and then color-calibrated, cropped, and exported it as stimuli with faces obscured in 4 K, 24 fps, and Rec.709 color space. Audio was recorded separately into uncompressed WAV files. Separate files contain the standing, walking/turning, and speaking recordings and audio sequences. Conclusions The dataset provides standardized audio-visual stimuli for reuse in research on person perception and first impressions, including studies of bodily appearance, movement, voice, attractiveness, and physical-fitness perception. We provide detailed acquisition and processing information to facilitate reproducibility and reuse. The stimuli are publicly available on Zenodo and can be linked to separately reported anthropometric and physical fitness data.

items.title: Dynamic Movement Analysis of Horse and Rider in Showjumping
items.abstract: Dynamic Systems Theory (DST) provides a framework for investigating movement as an emergent and continuously adapting process, providing a new way to approach the study of showjumping, where rider and horse must continuously coordinate their movements under changing task demands. Previous biomechanical investigations of showjumping have largely relied on discrete analyses, limiting understanding of rider technique and horse–rider interaction as dynamic phenomena. This thesis therefore applied a DST framework to investigate rider and horse–rider coordination during show jumping using continuous three-dimensional kinematic analysis.Continuous kinematics of 17 riders and their horses were collected using a multi-inertial measurement unit system while jumping a 1.30 m fence. Rider hip–knee coordination and horse–rider coordination were quantified using vector coding analysis. Rider coordination was further characterised using temporal coordination, frequency distribution analysis and change point detection relative to forelimb take-off (FLTO). Horse–rider coordination dynamics were investigated using Shannon entropy, modelled with a Generalised Additive Model, and Transfer Entropy to quantify information exchange between rider inter-joint coordination and horse–rider coordination.Continuous hip–knee coordination analysis identified two distinct rider movement strategies during the approach to the fence. Additionally, Riders consistently exhibited a transition in coordination within -0.16 s to +0.02 s of FLTO, accompanied by a reduction in coordination variability. Horse–rider coordination was characterised predominantly by in-phase coordination, with the horse driving the movement, although multiple coordination patterns were observed throughout the approach. Fence type significantly influenced horse–rider coordination strategy frequency and coordination entropy. Transfer entropy demonstrated bidirectional information exchange between rider inter-joint coordination and horse–rider coordination, although effect sizes were small.This thesis introduces continuous coordination analysis as a novel approach for investigating rider technique and horse–rider interaction. By characterising rider inter-joint coordination and horse–rider system dynamics throughout the approach and jump, the findings provide new insights into the adaptable and highly variable nature of skilled performance. Collectively, the work advances both the methodological tools available for equestrian biomechanics and the understanding of horse and rider as a coupled dynamic system.

items.title: The past and potential antagonistic effects of fishing ban against nutrient loading control on eutrophication restoration in Lake Hongze
items.abstract: A bstract Integrated management strategies are often implemented to achieve comprehensive environmental restoration; however, the potential antagonistic effects among such measures are seldom examined. Fishing bans, aimed at enhancing fish biodiversity, may counteract the effectiveness of nutrient control measures in mitigating eutrophication. This study employs the PCLake model and structural equation modeling (SEM) to evaluate this hypothesis in Lake Hongze, the fourth largest shallow lake in China. The PCLake model was calibrated using observational data from Lake Hongze collected between 2016 and 2020. The calibrated model was subsequently applied in a hindcast analysis from 2020 to 2024 and a forecast simulation from 2025 to 2030 to assess the impacts of fishing bans. Combined with SEM path analysis, the results support the hypothesis that fishing bans can exhibit antagonistic effects on nutrient loading control by enhancing top-down regulation relative to bottom-up processes. Specifically, the fishing ban led to increased fish biomass, phytoplankton abundance, and nutrient levels over the past four years, while reducing the abundance of submerged macrophytes, zoobenthos, and zooplankton. Projections further indicate that such antagonistic effects would persist through 2030 if the fishing ban remains in place as planned. Additionally, model forecasts suggest that even with adjustments to the duration and intensity of fishing bans, antagonistic effects could be amplified under more stringent nutrient control scenarios. This study provides valuable insights into maximizing the net benefits of combined environmental management strategies through a systematic framework that evaluates both the effects and underlying processes of different interventions.

items.title: Cumulative thermal stress predicts functional change in coral reef fish communities
items.abstract: Marine heatwaves are altering coral reef fish communities through a combination of direct impacts of thermal stress and indirect impacts that degrade coral habitats. Impacts may vary for species in different functional groups (e.g. herbivore replacement of corallivores), altering the functional composition of fish communities that is critical to reef resilience. However, our understanding of trait-based responses of fish communities to marine heatwaves is inadequate, and mostly inferred from local scales and low numbers of species. Here, we use a Bayesian joint species distribution model based on data for 500 fish species from 286 sites surveyed across northern Australia to evaluate the impacts of marine heatwaves on species probability of occurrence and their interactions with four functional traits. The effects of degree heating weeks and coral loss on individual species probability of occurrence had the highest total and proportionally negative responses, respectively. Thermal affinity's positive response to cumulative heat stress (i.e. degree heating weeks) was the strongest trait effect. Community-level analyses predicted losses in habitat specialists, large-bodied fishes, corallivores and pelagic feeders along a gradient of marine heatwave stress. The loss and restructuring of functional diversity suggest that heatwaves will continue eroding fish-dependent ecological roles and associated ecosystem services.

items.title: Do herbivorous fish amplify the competitive dominance of floating-leaved plants over submerged plants?
items.abstract: Growing interest in the relationship between herbivorous fish and aquatic plants has revealed multiple pathways by which fish can influence aquatic plant biomass and coverage. However, the impact of herbivorous fish on species competition and community assembly in aquatic plants remains poorly understood. Here, based on a mesocosm experiment with four aquatic plant species (two floating-leaved and two submerged) and one herbivorous fish, we quantified competition coefficients among plant species and fish effects using a modified Ricker model. Floating-leaved plants exhibited stronger intraspecific than interspecific competition, indicating competitive superiority over submerged species. Crucially, selective grazing by herbivorous fish on submerged plants indirectly facilitated the dominance of floating-leaved species, exacerbating competitive asymmetry. These results demonstrate that herbivory indirectly affects aquatic plant community structure, not simply by removing biomass but also via higher-order interactions. Our research extends herbivore-plant interaction theory to freshwater ecosystems and offers guidance for aquatic plant restoration and biological management.

items.title: Exploring the Determinants of Green Purchase Intention and Behavior Among College Students in Fujian Province, China
items.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to identify the key determinants of green purchase intention and green purchase behavior among college students in Fujian, China. The study extends the Theory of Planned Behavior by incorporating environmental concern and environmental knowledge to provide a broader explanation of green purchasing decisions. Research design, data and methodology: A quantitative research approach was applied using structured questionnaires administered to 500 students from the Department of Business Administration at Meizhouwan Vocational Technology College in Fujian, China. All respondents had prior experience purchasing green products. A non-probability sampling approach combining purposive, quota, and convenience sampling was adopted. Data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling to evaluate the measurement model and test the proposed hypotheses. Results: Environmental concern, environmental knowledge, attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control all had significant positive effects on green purchase intention. Environmental concern showed the strongest effect, followed by perceived behavioral control and environmental knowledge. Attitude and subjective norms also had significant effects. Green purchase intention significantly influenced green purchase behavior. Conclusions: The findings support the applicability of the extended TPB framework in explaining green purchasing behavior among college students and suggest that universities can strengthen sustainable consumption by enhancing environmental awareness, improving access to green products, and fostering supportive social norms through environmental education and campus initiatives.

items.title: Adaptive Capacity and Climate Change Resilience of Coconut Farmers: A Philippines Case Study
items.abstract: Purpose: This qualitative study aims to examine the impacts of climate change on the livelihoods and production systems of coconut farmers, to analyze adaptation practices and strategies through the lens of sustainability and the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework, and to assess farmers’ levels of resilience and adaptive capacity to climate change within the context of the Philippines. Research design, data and methodology: The study employs a qualitative research design, with data collected through semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 43 purposively selected coconut farmers. The data were analyzed using content analysis and thematic synthesis in order to capture farmers’ lived experiences, perceptions, and grassroots-level adaptation practices. Results: The findings indicate that the majority of farmers clearly perceive changes in climatic conditions, particularly increased variability in rainfall, drought, and the frequency of extreme weather events. These changes have had direct impacts on coconut yields, income stability, and household economic security. In terms of adaptation, farmers have adopted a range of sustainable agricultural practices, including efficient water management, the use of organic fertilizers and soil amendments to restore soil quality, and crop diversification to spread production and income risks. These practices contribute to enhancing the resilience of farming systems and demonstrate alignment with the environmental and social dimensions of the ESG framework. Conclusions: However, the study also reveals that farmers’ adaptive capacity remains constrained by structural factors, notably limited access to financial resources, inadequate access to technology and reliable climate information, and insufficiently coordinated policy support. These constraints highlight significant gaps in the governance dimension of the ESG framework. In conclusion, the study underscores that strengthening climate resilience among coconut farmers requires the integration of grassroots-level adaptation practices with systematic policy support and governance mechanisms, thereby elevating adaptation efforts from the individual level toward long-term sustainability.

items.title: Toward Intelligent and Climate-Resilient Coastal Aquaculture: A Systematic Review Integrating Ecosystem Health, Marine Biotechnology, One Health, Data-Driven Technologies, and the Blue Economy
items.abstract: Background Coastal aquaculture is increasingly exposed to climate change, water-quality deterioration, disease risk, and demands for sustainable production. Evidence on ecosystem condition, biological resilience, marine biotechnology, One Health, digital technologies, and the blue economy remains fragmented across disciplines. This review integrated these domains within a common resilience framework. Methods Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, Scopus and PubMed were searched for English-language journal articles published from 2016 to 2 October 2026. Searches identified 5,439 records; 2,686 duplicates were removed, 2,753 unique records were screened, and 283 reports with verified full text were assessed. Twenty-two reports were excluded, leaving 261 studies for descriptive and thematic synthesis across six primary domains. Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of substantial heterogeneity in study designs and outcomes. Results The final synthesis comprised ecosystem, climate, and physical pressures (n = 25); biological, nutritional, molecular, and genetic resilience (n = 70); marine biotechnology and circular bioremediation (n = 32); One Health, biosecurity, and food safety (n = 53); data-driven and intelligent technologies (n = 50); and blue-economy, governance, and adoption (n = 31). Biological resilience, health protection, and intelligent monitoring were the largest evidence areas. Biotechnology supported nutrient removal and resource recovery, while governance, financing, markets, and capacity shaped implementation. Methodological appraisal classified 10.0% of studies as lower concern, 56.7% as some concern, and 33.3% as higher concern. Artificial light at night/light pollution emerged as a plausible but underexamined physical stressor rather than a separately searched exposure. Conclusions Climate-resilient coastal aquaculture is best treated as a coupled ecological, biological, health, technological, and socioeconomic system. Progress requires integrated environmental monitoring, resilient organisms, preventive health management, circular biotechnology, externally validated decision technologies, and enabling governance, with targeted research on nocturnal light environments.

items.title: Synthetic humanitarianism and algorithmic witnessing: generative AI and the politics of humanitarian representation
items.abstract: Humanitarian organisations have begun deploying generative AI imagery in their campaigns, a practice this article terms synthetic humanitarianism. The article asks what conceptual framework is required to analyse the ethical and communicative implications of this practice. Drawing on witnessing theory, decolonial critiques of humanitarian visibility, and technocolonialism, I argue that synthetic humanitarianism intensifies extractive and colonial logics that have structured humanitarian communication since its institutional emergence. I develop the concept of algorithmic witnessing to name the communicative condition in which generative AI systems produce the relations of testimony and moral address without any act of witnessing having taken place and, in the typical case, without the participation of those represented. The framework specifies four dimensions, testimonial fabrication, epistemic extraction, delanguaging, and stereoscopic automation, and I apply it to thirteen documented cases of generative AI image use in humanitarian communications between 2022 and 2025. The analysis demonstrates that these dimensions form a mutually reinforcing system in which the elimination of situated meaning-making enables fabricated testimony and the computational encoding of colonial visual archives produces automated stereotype. I argue that the most significant consequence of synthetic humanitarianism is political rather than epistemological. The displacement of situated meaning-making by algorithmic production tends to eliminate the last structural point at which affected communities could intervene in their own representation.
