items.title: Prevalence of Periodontitis in Pregnant Women Attending Antenatal Care at Health Facilities in Gondar Town, Northwest Ethiopia.
items.abstract: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of periodontitis in pregnant women in Gondar Town and factors associated with periodontitis. A cross-sectional study was conducted in Gondar Town among pregnant women attending antenatal care from February to June 2024. Data collection was conducted by trained professionals using a pre-tested, structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire through KoboToolbox, an online data collection platform. Periodontitis was assessed based on the presence of bleeding on probing, dental calculus and periodontal pockets, in accordance with the Community Periodontal Index (CPI). A binary logistic regression model was used to estimate the associations between sociodemographic, behavioural and clinical factors and periodontitis. Six hundred and twenty-eight pregnant women were included in the study (mean age = 27.8 years; SD = 5.1). The prevalence of periodontitis, bleeding on probing and calculus deposition was 32.8% (95% CI: 29.1-36.6), 64.3% (95% CI: 60.6-68.0) and 41.5% (95% CI: 37.6-45.5), respectively. Among pregnant women in Gondar Town, maternal age ≥ 35 years, antihypertensive medication use, and being in the third trimester of gestation were positively associated with periodontitis, whereas iron supplement use was negatively associated with periodontitis. The findings suggest that periodontitis is relatively common among pregnant women, highlighting the importance of preventive strategies and oral health screening during antenatal care follow-up.

items.title: Effectiveness of Community Water Fluoridation in Queensland: A Population-Based Causal Analysis Following the 2008 Policy Change.
items.abstract: Water fluoridation (WF) is an important preventive program against dental caries. Recent Cochrane reviews reported only limited new scientific evidence of WF. This research aimed to provide contemporary evidence on the causal relationship between WF and oral health. A causal framework was used to ensure methodological rigour in repeated cross-sectional, population-based studies of randomly selected 5 to 14 y old children in Queensland, thereby enabling controlled difference-in-differences (DiD) analyses. The primary exposure was access to WF, defined as newly fluoridated (New-WF; areas that became fluoridated since 2010), never fluoridated (No-WF), or long-term fluoridated areas (Long-WF). The outcomes were dental caries experience (decayed, missing, or filled tooth surfaces) and prevalence in the primary and permanent dentition, collected by dental examiners who were uniformly trained and calibrated during both phases. The DiD estimands were the differences in changes in outcomes between New-WF and the control (No-WF), estimated from multivariable regression models. Data of 5,407 children during 2010-2012 and 7,718 children during 2022-2024 were collected. Variations in key confounders (area and individual socioeconomic factors) were controlled for using inverse probability of treatment weights. Dental caries among children in New-WF had consistently declined relative to the control groups. In the primary dentition, the New-WF children had a 1.40-fold (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08 to 1.80) reduction in caries experience and a 1.28-fold (1.00 to 1.67) reduction in caries prevalence, equivalent to 1.1 fewer affected tooth surfaces and a 10.8% lower prevalence. In the permanent dentition, reductions were smaller: a 1.32-fold (0.95 to 1.84) reduction in caries experience and a 1.04-fold (0.81 to 1.33) reduction in prevalence. These findings show that WF is effective in preventing dental caries in children when disease levels are low and other preventive programs are available. This controlled DiD study provides robust contemporary scientific evidence of the effects of WF on dental caries, strengthening WF as a public health policy.

items.title: Efficacy of a Gamified Training Program for Improving Occupational Health and Safety Knowledge Among Italian Secondary School Students: A Randomized Controlled Field Trial.
items.abstract: This study evaluated the short-term effectiveness of an innovative gamified educational program based on the principles of the Italian Legislative Decree 81/2008 in improving occupational health and safety (OHS) knowledge among Italian secondary school students. A cluster-randomized controlled field trial was conducted in Italy from September 2024 to June 2025. Classes were randomized into experimental (EG) and control groups (CG). The intervention combined a seminar with three structured games (role-playing, board, and card games). Knowledge was assessed using a 15-item questionnaire (Q81) at baseline (T0) and post-intervention (T1). The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in Q81 score at post-intervention (T1). Of 930 eligible students, 927 participated (99.7%), 694 completed the study (74.6%), including 187 middle school and 507 high school students (NEG = 356; NCG = 338). Baseline Q81 scores were comparable between groups (EG: 5.6 ± 3.3 vs CG: 5.4 ± 2.9), whereas at T1, mean Q81 scores were significantly higher in the EG compared to the CG (9.0 ± 3.1 vs. 5.2 ± 2.9, P < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.26). Within-group analysis showed a significant improvement in the EG (P < 0.001), but not in the CG. Reliability analysis yielded alpha = 0.804, indicating good internal consistency. Gamification training improved OHS knowledge among secondary school students and may represent an effective educational strategy for early safety education. These findings support the integration of gamified OHS training into secondary school curricula to strengthen early safety education in line with the principles of Legislative Decree 81/2008. . Future studies should include larger samples, address item-level weaknesses and explore long-term behavioural outcomes.

items.title: Determinants of Perceived Transportation Barriers to Opioid Services Among Residents of Alabama's Black Belt.
items.abstract: Transportation can constrain access to opioid-related services in rural communities, yet little is known about how residents perceive this barrier in historically underserved Black Belt communities of Alabama. This study examined the level and correlates of perceived community-level transportation barriers to opioid services among 191 Black adults residing in three Alabama Black Belt communities. Cross-sectional data were collected through self-administered surveys, and multiple linear regression was used to examine sociodemographic, health, interpersonal, and opioid-related correlates. Our findings reported that, on average, participants perceived transportation as limiting community access to opioid-related services about half the time (M = 2.20on a 0-4 scale). Higher depressive symptoms, greater perceived community need for opioid-related services, and greater knowledge of state opioid policies and programs were significantly associated with greater perceived transportation barriers, while lower social isolation was associated with fewer perceived barriers. These findings highlight the importance of addressing structural barriers to improve access to opioid-related services. Interventions such as mobile health units, telehealth services, and transportation assistance programs may help improve service access and health outcomes in underserved rural communities.

items.title: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons.
items.abstract: Human neurons are postmitotic and long-lived, requiring precise genomic regulation. Normal neuronal function is highly dosage-sensitive, with copy number variants (CNVs) and heterozygous point mutations associated with a host of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric conditions1-4. Here we investigated somatic CNVs arising in single neurons to understand the dynamic processes that shape the normal neuronal genetic landscape. Altogether, we sequenced 2,357 single neurons from human postmortem brain from fetal to postnatal life. Two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches-Tn5-transposase-based amplification (1,526 neurons, 16 individuals) and primary template amplification5 (831 neurons, 12 individuals)-showed that an average of 25.9% [12.7-46%] of prenatal cortical neurons have highly aberrant genomes, that is, widespread CNVs involving multiple chromosomes. This proportion reduced by about 4.5-fold after birth across the two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches (Fisher meta-analysis P = 3.5 × 10-6). Neurons with widespread CNVs were mainly eliminated perinatally, timed roughly parallel to periods of programmed cell death6, whereas neurons with smaller CNV burdens declined slowly in frequency with postnatal age. CNVs in surviving neurons were depleted for dosage-sensitive genes and genes involved in neurodevelopmental disorders (hypergeometric test P < 0.05), suggesting selective elimination of neurons with these CNVs. Analysis of 44,861 nuclei with single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (snATAC) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) showed that neurons with high CNV burdens exhibited abnormal synaptic gene expression, suggesting that abnormal synaptic gene regulation contributes to neuronal elimination. Elimination of defective neuronal genomes might represent an important developmental genome quality-control process that may be vulnerable in neurodevelopmental disease, and suggests purifying selection during human neurodevelopment.

items.title: Population-scale single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of skeletal muscle reveals extensive context-specific genetic regulation.
items.abstract: Skeletal muscle tissue underlies several polygenic metabolic traits and diseases. Identifying their genetic mechanisms requires pinpointing cell types, regulatory elements, target genes and causal variants. Here we use genetic multiplexing to generate population-scale single-nucleus chromatin accessibility (single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (snATAC-seq)) and transcriptome (single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq)) maps across 287 frozen human skeletal muscle biopsies. We identify 13 cell types and integrate genetic variation to discover >7,000 expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) and >100,000 chromatin accessibility QTLs (caQTLs) across cell types, including context-specific eQTL/caQTL with significant G × C interaction. We identify nearly 2,000 eGenes colocalized with caQTL and construct causal directional maps for chromatin accessibility and gene expression. Almost 3,500 genome-wide association study (GWAS) signals across 38 relevant traits colocalize with sn-eQTL/caQTL, most in a cell-specific manner. These signals typically colocalize with caQTL and not eQTL, highlighting the importance of population-scale chromatin profiling for GWAS functional studies. The results of this study illuminate the genetic regulatory architecture of human skeletal muscle.

items.title: Effect of epigallocatechin-3-gallate on resin-dentin bond strength: A systematic review and meta-analysis of dentin pretreatment and adhesive incorporation strategies.
items.abstract: To systematically evaluate the effect of epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) on dentin bond strength and bonding durability according to its application strategy. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251003015). PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, EMBASE, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to July 2026. Clinical, in situ, and in vitro studies evaluating EGCG as a dentin pretreatment or incorporated into dental adhesives were eligible. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were performed independently by two reviewers using the RoBDEMAT and RoB 2 tools. Meta-analyses were performed using RevMan to evaluate the effects of EGCG on microtensile bond strenght, considering immediate and long-term outcomes, using random-effects models and reporting mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). 35 studies met the eligibility criteria. 17 evaluated EGCG as a dentin pretreatment, 15 investigated its incorporation into dental adhesives, and three assessed both strategies. Meta-analysis demonstrated that dentin pretreatment with EGCG significantly improved immediate and long-term microtensile bond strength. When incorporated into adhesives, EGCG improved bond strength after aging only in etch-and-rinse adhesive systems, whereas no significant effects were observed for self-etch adhesives. Risk-of-bias assessment indicated generally favorable methodological quality, although some concerns were identified in both clinical and in vitro studies. EGCG may improve resin-dentin bond strength, although its effectiveness depends on the application strategy and adhesive system. Dentin pretreatment showed more favorable results than incorporation into adhesive formulations.

items.title: Use of Opioids and Opioid Potentiators Among Nursing Home Residents in the United States: National Prevalence and Correlates.
items.abstract: Concurrent use of opioids and opioid potentiators (i.e., benzodiazepines, non-benzodiazepines, and gabapentinoids) can elevate the risks of potential harms (e.g., hospitalizations and deaths). However, no study has yet examined the co-use of opioids and opioid potentiators in US nursing homes. We used nationally-representative data in 2019 from Minimum Data Set 3.0 (MDS 3.0) linked with Part D claims and other data sources, and measured length of opioid use in the 120 days from the index assessment (short-term users: ≤ 30 days; medium-term users: 31-89 days, and long-term users: ≥ 90 days). In this cross-sectional study design, we estimated prevalence of opioid use and co-use of opioids and opioid potentiators by duration of opioid use. We also estimated resident- and facility-level factors associated with opioid use and co-use of opioids and opioid potentiators in long-stay nursing home residents. Of 135,347 long-stay nursing home residents, 32,550 (24.0%) had any opioid prescriptions. 7.1% were short-term opioid users, 5.5% were mid-term opioid users, and 11.4% were long-term opioid users. Among opioid users, 52.0% also had any opioid potentiators. The most frequently used potentiator class was gabapentinoids, followed by benzodiazepines and non-benzodiazepines. Pain and other comorbid conditions (e.g., anxiety) were significantly associated with such uses (p < 0.001). Cognitive impairment and dementia were associated with lower odds of opioid use and co-use of opioid-potentiators (p < 0.01). Long-term opioid use in older nursing home residents remains prevalent. The co-use of opioids and opioid potentiators is also prevalent in this population. Because co-use of opioid-potentiators can pose elevated risks for potentially avoidable harms, safer opioid-related medication use needs to be emphasized in long-term care settings. Alternatives to opioid use (e.g., non-opioid pain medications and physical therapy) should be considered, and regular medication reviews and deprescribing efforts will be critical in residents taking opioids in nursing home settings.

items.title: Effectiveness of the RISE Intervention for Elder Abuse and Self-Neglect: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Elder abuse and self-neglect (EASN) are prevalent and associated with significant adverse health and psychosocial outcomes, yet evidence on effective interventions remains limited. RISE is a community-based intervention designed to address EASN. This study evaluated the effectiveness and acceptability of RISE in a real-world community setting. We conducted a pragmatic, parallel-group, superiority randomized controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment. Older adults screened as at risk of or experiencing EASN were randomized following an initial consultation to receive either RISE plus consultation (intervention group) or consultation and referral provision only (control group). Blinded outcome assessment occurred at baseline, 3-month, and 6-month follow-up using telephone-based surveys. Primary outcomes included psychosocial measures of life satisfaction, perceived stress, self-efficacy, social support, and problem concern. Linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate group differences over time. Program satisfaction at 6 months was assessed using multiple linear regression. 114 participants entered the baseline analysis cohort; 93 completed three-month and 79 completed six-month assessments. RISE participants showed significantly greater improvement over time in life satisfaction (p < 0.001), perceived stress (p = 0.001), general self-efficacy (p = 0.023), social-interaction self-efficacy (p < 0.001), emotional support (p = 0.002), and informational support (p < 0.001). Problem concern did not show differential change (p = 0.404). Adjusted six-month program satisfaction was 4.61 points significantly higher with RISE (95% CI 3.25-5.97; p < 0.001). RISE was associated with improvements across multiple psychosocial domains and high participant satisfaction among EASN older adults. Findings provide evidence supporting a scalable, community-based response to EASN in jurisdictions lacking centralized protective service systems.

items.title: Do trends in alcohol harm mirror consumption? An analysis of adolescent ambulance attendances.
items.abstract: Adolescent alcohol consumption has declined across many high-income countries since the early 2000s, yet it remains unclear whether these reductions have led to less alcohol-related harm, particularly among higher-risk groups. Using the National Ambulance Surveillance System, we examined ambulance attendances for alcohol intoxication among adolescents (10-19 years) in Victoria, Australia, from January 2012 and December 2023. Multivariable regression, stratified by gender, assessed monthly changes in attendance rates per 10 000 by remoteness, adjusting for seasonality and COVID-19 lockdowns. A total of 25 928 attendances were recorded. A small but significant monthly decline in alcohol intoxication ambulance attendance was observed among males in major cities (B = -0.01 [0.01], P < .001). No significant trends were identified for males in regional areas or for females in metropolitan or regional areas. Despite declining adolescent alcohol consumption, intoxication-related ambulance attendances have remained largely stable over the past decade. The modest decline among males in metropolitan areas was considerably smaller than survey-reported declines in consumption, suggesting that population surveys capture different drinking patterns than those leading to acute harms. These findings highlight the need for ongoing monitoring and targeted prevention strategies, particularly for high-risk subgroups and regional populations.

items.title: Pulmonary Toxicity of Particulate-Phase Combustion Byproducts from Lithium-Ion Battery Fires.
items.abstract: The frequency of lithium-ion battery (LIB) fires is increasing globally, creating new challenges for firefighters and growing public safety concerns from smoke and intense heat. However, the health effects from exposure to LIB fires are not well understood. We collected soot and smoke particulate matter (PM) from LIB thermal runaway events (10 and 2 fire tests for soot and PM samples, respectively), filtered them to remove non-inhalable particles (>10 μm), analyzed for chemical composition and assessed for lung toxicity and pulmonary function in mice at 4 h and 24 h post exposure to 100 μg of the sample. Chemical and biological results were analyzed using a computational approach to identify hazardous chemical components that were potentially responsible for toxicity outcomes. Computational findings were further compared to those produced by other sources of air pollution. The soot sample contained more carbon species than the smoke PM sample (37% vs. 18%), whereas anions were higher in the PM sample (12% vs. 6%), and concentrations of inorganic elements were similar (23% vs. 28%). Fluoride particulate was found to account for up to 5% of the mass of each sample. Only soot significantly increased ventilatory timing and peak expiratory flow in mice and decreased relaxation time, while both samples caused significant increases in inflammatory responses. Soot and PM exhibited similar lung inflammatory outcomes relative to those caused by previously reported combustion-related air pollution sources. Computational analysis indicated that fluoride, Al, Fe, Ni, and Li from both samples were significantly associated with the lung toxicity responses (p < 0.05). The findings indicate that LIB fire soot and PM that contain hazardous metals and fluoride elicit pulmonary toxicity responses comparable to other sources of air pollution, increasing the need for awareness of potential strategies to mitigate public health impacts.

items.title: Landscape fire-sourced PM 2.5 and kidney function in children: evidence from a national cross-sectional study in China.
items.abstract: Landscape fire-sourced fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter ≤2.5 μm (PM2.5) may be more oxidatively active and biologically toxic than PM2.5 from other sources, but evidence of its kidney effects in children is limited. To examine the association between landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 exposure and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in children and identify potentially susceptible subgroups. This cross-sectional study included 12,102 children aged 5-18 years who participated in the China National Nutrition and Health Surveillance of Children and Lactating Women between October 2016 and December 2018. eGFR was estimated from serum creatinine (Scr), and three-year average pre-survey exposure to landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 was assigned using school addresses. Associations were estimated using linear mixed-effects models, with subgroup analyses by sex, obesity, NDVI, and nutrient intake. The mean age was 10.90 ± 3.12 years, and 6,064 participants (50.11%) were boys. Each IQR (0.505 μg/m3) increase in landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 was associated with a 0.83 mL/min/1.73 m2 reduction in eGFR (95% CI: -1.03, -0.62). The association was stronger among middle school students (β = -1.46 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI: -1.83, -1.09) than among primary school students (β = -0.59 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI: -0.84, -0.34; Pfor difference < 0.001). Stratified analyses showed significant between-group differences by NDVI, vitamin intake, and carbohydrate intake, with stronger inverse associations in the lower-NDVI and lower-intake groups (Pfor difference < 0.05 for all reported comparisons). Landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 exposure was associated with lower eGFR in the overall population, with stronger associations among middle school students and children with lower NDVI or lower vitamin or carbohydrate intake.

items.title: FTO deficiency mediates ferroptosis to exacerbate cobalt-induced neurotoxicity.
items.abstract: Cobalt, a toxic environmental contaminant, has been implicated in human neurological damage. However, the detailed molecular basis of cobalt-triggered neurotoxicity remains poorly uncovered. In the present study, we elucidated the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) demethylase fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) downregulation mediates the activation of ferroptosis to drive cobalt-triggered neurodegeneration. We established an in vitro model using H4 cells and an in vivo model using C57BL/6 mice. Animal experiments provided initial evidence underscoring the critical involvement of ferroptosis in cobalt-associated neurotoxicity. Furthermore, in vitro assays revealed that ferroptosis is triggered subsequent to oxidative stress induced by cobalt exposure. Notably, MeRIP-seq profiling of H4 cells and mouse cortex revealed that ferroptosis-associated genes exhibited differential m6A modification, suggesting m6A modification might be involved in modulating ferroptosis. Concurrently, Gene Ontology and KEGG enrichment analyses revealed that genes bearing differential m6A modifications were significantly clustered within pathways linked to ferroptosis as well as neurodegenerative diseases. Moreover, we found that FTO depletion effectively enhanced ferroptosis following cobalt-induced oxidative stress. Mechanistically, FTO depletion enhanced m6A modification of GPX4 and transferrin receptor protein 1 (TFRC) mRNAs, leading to reduced GPX4 and elevated TFRC expression, which aggravated cobalt-induced ferroptosis. More importantly, we observed that central nervous system specific knockout of Fto exacerbated cobalt-induced neurobehavioral deficits and neuropathological damage through ferroptosis activation. Collectively, these results provide important insights into cobalt-induced neurotoxicity by targeting FTO deficiency-mediated ferroptosis and offer an innovative strategy for investigating neurodegenerative processes driven by environmental toxicants.

items.title: Spontaneous Spirals in Spatial Systems
items.abstract: Several chemical and biological systems produce spontaneous spirals in their dynamical behavior, such as the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction in chemistry and the slime mold Dictyostelium in biology. In a previous study, such spiral wave formation was accurately replicated with a computational spatial system known as the Ideal Storage Cellular Automaton Model (ISCAM). Here, a more detailed investigation is presented of the ability of this model to generate spontaneous spirals depending on its parameter values. A dynamical systems analysis is performed, and bifurcation diagrams, phase space diagrams, and snapshots of the model's spatial dynamics are presented for a range of parameter values. This analysis reveals that spiral waves can only be sustained in the system when the parameter values of the model fall well within the regime of a so-called Neimark-Sacker bifurcation.

items.title: Recognition of auditory objects from continuous and ultra-sparse spike streams in neuromorphic devices
items.abstract: Energy consumption is a major concern for modern artificial intelligence (AI) applications. The brain is thought to achieve energy-efficient computation through sparse coding schemes. By emulating the spiking dynamics of the brain, neuromorphic chips hold the potential to realize energy-efficient AI. In this work, we use birdsong to demonstrate that auditory object recognition can be achieved using ultra-sparse coding. Feature-detecting neurons tuned to short temporal features ($\sim$37 ms), sampled from exemplar syllables, transform continuous auditory signals into streams of ultra-sparse spikes that mark the onsets and offsets of features within the signal. Spike patterns elicited by the exemplars are stored as templates. During recognition, template matching is performed using axonal delays between feature-detecting and template-detecting neurons. Recognition is further enhanced by an additional group of specialized binary neurons trained to discriminate between syllable categories with subtle differences. When tested on Bengalese finch songs, our approach achieved error rates below 5% using 10 to 40 exemplars per syllable type. We then implemented this recognition algorithm using spiking neural networks on Intel's neuromorphic chip, Loihi, and found that response latencies remain constant (approximately 17 ms per syllable), regardless of the number of templates used. Our results demonstrate the potential of neuromorphic chips for low-latency, low-energy recognition of complex sounds, including speech.

items.title: REVBRAIN: Real-time Probabilistic EEG Forecasting Using Residual Vector Quantization
items.abstract: Real-time forecasting of resting-state EEG signals is required by applications like brain-state-dependent stimulation, where computer generated actions are coupled with ongoing neural oscillations. Recently, the deep learning model WaveNet was proposed for the forecasting task. It shows superior accuracy compared to the prevailing method, the linear autoregressive (AR) model, and provides a built-in uncertainty measure due to its probabilistic modeling framework. However, inference using WaveNet is too slow for real-time use due to its sample-by-sample autoregressive operation: a single forecast requires evaluating the model tens or hundreds of times depending on the length of the prediction window. In this paper, we present REVBRAIN, a probabilistic deep learning method that produces forecasts in real time by generating the forecast over the whole prediction horizon at once. This is achieved by tokenizing the output space using residual vector quantization (RVQ) and generating forecasts over the items in the tokenized space. We tested REVBRAIN for forecasting 200 ms of EEG time series in the alpha-frequency band (8-13 Hz) and compared our results against WaveNet model. We found that REVBRAIN achieved real-time inference on a laptop GPU and an over $50\times$ speedup compared to WaveNet, while reaching superior prediction accuracy. By achieving real-time inference speed, REVBRAIN enables incorporating accurate and probabilistic EEG forecasting into BCI applications, opening up new ways for investigating the functioning of the human brain.

items.title: Generative discovery of chemical reaction networks
items.abstract: Chemical kinetics determines molecular stability, reaction selectivity and the evolution of reacting mixtures, but discovering the underlying reaction networks remains challenging. Here we introduce ReactNexus, a generative framework for kinetic-guided network exploration starting solely from reactant graphs. Generative models propose transition states and predict the full reaction trajectories connecting reactants and products, while calculations using a machine-learned interatomic potential verify connectivity and evaluate electronic barriers. On an in-distribution benchmark of 10,000 generated candidates, 80.8% connect to the input reactant after density functional theory (DFT) optimization and intrinsic reaction coordinate verification. The resulting networks uncover lower-barrier cooperative pathways and competition between catalyst release and catalyst-bound branches. In the examined carbocation cascades, coverage of known product precursors saturates after limited expansion and distinct entries converge onto shared intermediates, indicating a compact accessible reaction space. Network-derived candidate structures further assist mass-spectral interpretation of a complex nucleophilic aromatic substitution reaction. Together, these results establish a generative approach to reaction-network discovery and mechanistic analysis without predefined products or reaction templates.

items.title: Data Amount Heterogeneity Improves Performance in Federated Learning for Neuroimaging
items.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) allows for secure analysis of distributed data without data sharing. We and others have successfully applied FL to neuroimaging tasks, such as Alzheimer's disease classification from structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). FL trains a deep learning model locally at each site, encrypts the local model parameters and sends them to a federation controller that aggregates the local models under homomorphic encryption, the resulting community model is sent back to the sites for further training, and the process repeats for a number of rounds. FL often achieves learning performance (e.g., accuracy) close to centralized training, but no data leaves the sites and model parameters are protected through encryption and other measures. In this paper, we show that federations composed of sites with heterogeneous amounts of data (1 large site plus small sites) perform better than homogeneous (same data per site) federations, particularly in low data regimes, while reaching performance close to centralized training. Having a big site often results in faster convergence and higher final accuracy. Heterogeneous federations better exploit sites with small amounts of data, a common situation in large consortia such as ENIGMA.

items.title: Reconciling Giant Impacts with the Radius Valley: The Role of Silicate-Hydrogen Miscibility for Sub-Neptunes
items.abstract: Giant impacts are believed to play a major role in the assembly, long-term orbital stability, and resonant structure of exoplanetary systems. We revisit giant impact driven atmospheric escape while chemically coupling the interior and atmosphere by allowing for silicate-hydrogen miscibility. Incorporating hydrogen-silicate miscibility fundamentally alters atmospheric escape compared to chemically-inert models. While previous work on chemically-inert planets has found sub-Neptunes to undergo total atmospheric loss following collisions with impactors only a tenth of their mass, we find that including silicate-hydrogen miscibility can significantly reduce mass loss. This results from an increased envelope mean molecular weight, interior hydrogen sequestration, and modified compositional gradients in miscible planets. Miscible planets sequester hydrogen in their interiors post-impact, reducing the hydrogen available in the envelope for mass loss. As planets cool, hydrogen exsolves into their envelopes. Because more massive planets cool slower, they sequester hydrogen for longer, undergoing less mass loss. Thus, atmospheric retention depends more strongly on planet mass than impact energy, provided the impact does not gravitationally unbind the planet. Planets with masses $\gtrsim$4.50 $M_{\oplus}$ and hydrogen mass fractions > 5 % typically retain atmospheres of several percent after a giant impact, while planets with masses $\lesssim$3.30 $M_{\oplus}$ are almost entirely stripped of their envelopes. This allows sub-Neptunes with hydrogen-dominated envelopes to survive giant impacts. Contrastingly, lower-mass planets, which ultimately populate the super-Earth regime, are frequently stripped of their envelopes. Our findings suggest that super-Earths and sub-Neptunes could originate from a single population with rocky interiors even if post-disk-dispersal giant impacts were common.

items.title: lenscape: Fast, High-resolution $Δχ^2$ Maps of Microlensing Events
items.abstract: Planetary microlensing analyses rely on $Δχ^2$ maps across the binary-lens separation $s$ and mass ratio $q$ to locate degenerate solutions and bound parameter uncertainties. Because every grid point requires a full light-curve optimization with finite-source magnifications, constructing these maps is often the primary computational bottleneck in event modeling. Here I present lenscape, an open-source Python package that accelerates $Δχ^2$ mapping and suppresses local-minimum artifacts through multi-stage neighbor propagation and adaptive contour refinement. Applied to the planetary event MOA-2022-BLG-091, lenscape reproduces the published $50\times50$ map in 14 minutes and generates a $400\times400$ map in under two hours on a desktop computer.

items.title: 2026 ED138: A Large Trans-Neptunian Object in Early Rubin Observatory Data, and How Many More May Remain
items.abstract: We characterize a large trans-Neptunian object (TNO), 2026 ED138, discovered in data taken by the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory with the linking code pointdexter, and validate it independently. 2026 ED138 has absolute magnitude $H_V=3.19$, implying a diameter of 612-1530 km for geometric albedos between 0.25 and 0.04 and making it one of the ten intrinsically brightest known TNOs and a dwarf-planet candidate. At $i\approx19.4$ it is bright enough in the sky for ground-based spectroscopy and light curves and for detailed study with HST and JWST. Archival DECam detections extend its arc to more than ten years (3789 days). Its orbit, with barycentric $a=43.09$ au, $e=0.139$ and $i=24.4^\circ$, lies at the edge of the 12:7 mean-motion resonance with Neptune, like that of the dwarf planet Haumea, but with $g-r=0.63$ it is too red to be a member of Haumea's collisional family. 2026 ED138 was missed by earlier surveys because it lies far south and near the crowded regions of the Galactic plane. Our recoveries of the known TNOs with $H_V<4$ suggest that about 3 more objects like them, and probably more, remain undiscovered away from the Galactic plane. More such objects probably lie within $10^\circ$ of the plane, which no search has yet covered to this depth.

items.title: Coupled evolution of Earth's H2-rich proto-atmosphere and oxidized magma ocean: Efficient H2O production through dissolved H2 transport and atmospheric buffering of the magma ocean redox state
items.abstract: Giant impacts during Earth's final accretion likely generated global magma oceans, where the disproportionation of Fe^2+ at lower-mantle pressures and segregation of the resulting metallic iron into the core could have oxidized the magma ocean. Earth may nevertheless have had an H2-rich proto-atmosphere in chemical disequilibrium with the magma ocean, but the chemical coupling between this atmosphere and an oxidized magma ocean remains poorly constrained. Here we develop a coupled atmosphere-interior evolution model that includes diffusive transport in the boundary layer between the magma ocean and atmosphere, redox reactions in the melt, partitioning of oxide components and H2O among coexisting phases, and planetary cooling through a proto-atmosphere, with metallic iron produced by Fe^2+ disproportionation removed into the core as it forms. Atmospheric H2 transport into the magma ocean and subsequent H2O production become more efficient with increasingly frequent boundary layer renewal driven by buoyant overturn of dense melt cooled at the surface, allowing the atmosphere and magma ocean to chemically equilibrate within ~10^4 yr when the magma ocean is sufficiently deep and hot to extend into the lower mantle. Redox exchange with the atmosphere buffers the solidification-driven redox evolution of the magma ocean, preventing extreme oxidation or reduction of the coupled system. These results suggest that the coupled evolution could have contributed to early Earth's water inventory while maintaining a reducing H2-rich atmosphere.

items.title: Nongravitational Motion of 3I/ATLAS Far from the Sun: Robust Detection, Weak Constraints on the Activity Law
items.abstract: 3I/ATLAS provides an unprecedented astrometric data set for studying nongravitational (NG) effects in an interstellar object, but existing orbital solutions depend strongly on assumptions regarding the heliocentric activity law and the treatment of the astrometric data. We investigate the extent to which astrometric observations constrain the heliocentric dependence of the NG activity function, focusing on the identifiability of different functional forms of $g(r)$ within standard NG orbit-determination frameworks. Astrometric observations obtained at heliocentric distances larger than 3.49 au before perihelion and 2.67 au after perihelion were analysed. Purely gravitational and nongravitational orbital solutions were determined using several activity laws, including the standard water-ice sublimation law and flatter more volatile ice prescriptions. The resulting residual distributions were evaluated using normality tests and analyses of temporal trends in the observed-minus-calculated residuals. The distant pre-perihelion observations are well described by a purely gravitational (GR) orbit, whereas the distant post-perihelion data exhibit a statistically significant non-Gaussian residual distribution under the GR model. When the distant pre- and post-perihelion observations are combined, nongravitational acceleration becomes clearly detectable through a significant reduction in the residual rms and the disappearance of systematic residual trends. However, the astrometric data do not uniquely distinguish between the tested activity laws: standard water-ice, more volatile and extreme volatile prescriptions produce statistically comparable orbital fits despite their markedly different heliocentric dependences. The existence of nongravitational acceleration is therefore considerably better constrained by astrometry than its physical origin or heliocentric dependence.

items.title: PyMsOfa 2.0: A Pure-Python Implementation of the IAU Standards of Fundamental Astronomy Service
items.abstract: Astrometric calculations require authoritative algorithms so that every result is correct and reproducible. The Standards of Fundamental Astronomy (SOFA) service of the International Astronomical Union (IAU) provides such algorithms, officially released only in Fortran 77 and ANSI C. In an earlier paper we presented the first version of PyMsOfa, a Python package wrapping the SOFA C library. Here we present PyMsOfa 2.0, which re-implements the complete SOFA library in pure Python with NumPy. All 247 official SOFA routines are ported directly to Python, requiring no compilation of any external C library and running identically on Linux, Windows, and macOS. The routines operate on NumPy arrays, so arguments can be processed in batch, which is convenient for survey pipelines and Monte Carlo simulations. The package also provides an extension module with validated models not yet part of the official SOFA release, such as the improved precession--nutation model IAU 2006$_{J_2}$/2000A$_{R26}$. The reimplementation reproduces the official SOFA algorithms: all constants, series, and coefficients are taken unchanged from the SOFA source files, and routine names differ only by the pym prefix. We verify every routine against the official SOFA C release: most reproduce the C results to machine precision, the remainder within the accuracy tolerance stated in the SOFA documentation. The package has been applied to Gaia astrometric reduction and used in astrometric studies of the Closeby Habitable Exoplanet Survey (CHES) mission, and is available through PyPI, GitHub, and Zenodo.

items.title: NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's First View of the Neptune Trojan L5 (Trailing) Cloud: Two New Long-Term Stable Trojans
items.abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's combination of survey speed, sky coverage, and depth provides a unique opportunity to study the distant Trans-Neptunian region, including the Neptune Trojans. The Neptune Trojans are small bodies on orbits with Neptune's semimajor axis that are locked in the 1:1 mean motion resonance librating about the ice giant's stable Lagrange points, L4 (leading) and L5 (trailing), located 60$^{\circ}$ ahead of or behind the planet. For more than 15 years, the on-sky location of the L5 Neptune Trojan cloud has been coincident with the Galactic plane and Galactic center; the high stellar density has significantly hindered the discovery of L5 Neptune Trojans. In 2025, the L5 cloud has now moved sufficiently out of the galactic plane to overlap with the sky covered by Rubin Observatory's Science Validation (SV) survey that was executed during the Observatory's commissioning phase. We report on two new confirmed long-term stable (primordial) members of the Neptune L5 Trojan cloud (2025 MH348 and 2025 NN80), doubling the known sample, and one candidate (2025 MD138) that have been found in a preliminary search of the SV survey observations. We present our study to characterize the physical and dynamical properties of these objects and compare the L5 sample to the well-studied L4 cloud. This work also presents the first characterization of objects discovered by Rubin Observatory's moving object discovery pipelines using observations taken in an LSST-like cadence and as such, provides a blueprint for LSST-era analyses.

items.title: Young Planets around Young Accreting Stars: II. Circumplanetary Disk Formation and Accretion
items.abstract: We present global 3-D ideal-MHD simulations of young giant planets in a protoplanetary disk (PPD) undergoing magnetospheric accretion onto its host star. Extending our previous work, we insert three planets with planet-to-star mass ratio \(q = 0.01\) (\(\sim 10\) Jupiter masses) at 0.45, 0.9, and 1.8 times the magnetospheric truncation radius, \(R_T\) , thereby probing the low-density cavity, disk-cavity boundary, and turbulent inner disk. The outermost two planets develop circumplanetary disks (CPDs), whereas the innermost planet forms no persistent bound structure because its high velocity relative to the magnetosphere reduces the effective Bondi radius below the planet's size. The outermost planet forms a stable, coplanar CPD whose inner region is rotationally supported and rotates at nearly the local Keplerian speed within \(\sim 0.25\) Hill radii. High-latitude inflow and midplane decretion produce meridional circulation and continuous recycling between the CPD and surrounding disk. Inflow through the Hill sphere is comparable to previous Hill-based hydrodynamic estimates. The middle planet, located near \(R_T\), develops a persistent polar CPD whose angular-momentum vector is parallel to the disk midplane, demonstrating that coherent circumplanetary structures can form within highly dynamic magnetospheric flows. Based on both the effective Bondi radius and thermal-mass criterion, we identify conditions under which massive giant planets form CPDs in the inner disk. Estimated planetary inflow accretion rates imply mass-doubling timescales \(\gtrsim 10\) Myr due to the low disk surface density, suggesting that, in the magnetically active zone, these planets undergo only limited late-stage growth before disk dispersal.

items.title: Axon Initial Segment Plasticity in Affective Disorders
items.abstract: The axon initial segment (AIS) is a highly specialized compartment of the neuron thought to be an essential regulator of how neurons encode their responses. This region is topographically and biophysically tuned to the precise generation of action potentials and the regulation of spiking output. In addition to serving as a threshold region like other axonal regions, the AIS is uniquely optimized as a signaling domain so that cytoskeletal polarization, ion channel clustering, and intracellular signaling pathways converge upon this subcellular domain to produce a precise regulation of neuronal firing rate and timing. The nanoscale cytoskeletons and anchoring scaffolds at the AIS serve both to confine and to dynamically mobilize key signaling proteins and channels for a rapid yet adaptable regulation of spike initiation. Evidence suggests that AIS structure is exquisitely plastic to cellular, environmental, immune, and genetic factors known to be involved in the neuropathology of mood disorders. Precursors to pathology such as stress, chronic glucocorticoid excess, neural inflammatory signals, and genetic variation perturbing excitability by governing ion channel and receptor expression, can all produce alterations in the positional or dimensional parameters of the AIS with functional consequence to neuronal gain. Such alterations occur specifically in circuit nodes of emotion regulation such as the prefrontal limbic circuit, across neuronal populations and cell types, and alter trajectories of circuit function seemingly aligned with affective disorder symptom states. This work integrates current knowledge in the structure and electrophysiology of AIS function, activity dependent plasticity, and psychiatric neuroscience, to develop the hypothesis that remodeling of the AIS represents a convergent readout of the interactions between the immune system, stress response, and genetic alleles on neuronal function, a cellular mechanism through which the large components of neural circuit-based disease shape affective illness, potentially as an “axonopathy”. Furthermore, this review highlights the AIS as a potential new therapeutic target aimed at rehabilitating excitability threshold and gain for effective circuit function in the treatment of affective disorders within the emerging paradigm of precision psychiatry.

items.title: Loose coupling between Ca<sup>2+</sup> channels and release sensors as a synaptic correlate of higher-order brain function.
items.abstract: In the mature neocortex, functionally distinct areas are built by the same archetypes of neurons, but depending on the area, these neurons and their synapses are engaged in very different functions, ranging from lower-order processing of sensory information to higher-order associations and cognitive functions. We found significant differences in the functional presynaptic nanoarchitectures of the same types of pyramidal neuron synapses, depending on whether they are located in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) or in the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) of mice. Mature synapses in PFC operated with loose microdomain coupling, as opposed to tight nanodomain coupling in S1. These differences were associated with significant differences in synaptic timing, efficacy, and plasticity between areas. Our data suggest that the mature neocortex uses tuning of synaptic topographies to specialize seemingly identical types of neurons for their required function. They suggest that microdomain coupling in pyramidal neuron synapses could be a presynaptic structure-function correlate of higher-order neocortical functions.

items.title: Experimental Host Range and Pathogenicity on Maize of Maize Striate Mosaic Virus Transmitted by the Corn Leafhopper.
items.abstract: Maize striate mosaic virus (MSMV; species Mastrevirus striatis ) is an emergent mastrevirus ( Geminiviridae ) in South America, transmitted by the corn leafhopper Dalbulus maidis . MSMV symptoms in maize ( Zea mays ) include mottling with mild chlorotic streaks, but the extent of its damage and host range remain unstudied. In greenhouse experiments, we assessed 17 plant species (including maize as a control) as hosts to MSMV by symptomatology and PCR detection in 9 to 30 test plants per species, which were inoculated by caging 20 viruliferous leafhoppers/plant during 48 h; three to five plants/species were exposed to aviruliferous leafhoppers (negative controls). MSMV was detected in four inoculated grass species ( Urochloa brizantha , Andropogon gayanus , Saccharum spp., and Pennisetum glaucum ), but only Saccharum spp. (cv. CTC-9005) showed symptoms (chlorotic stripes). In maize, the virus was detected in 51.8% of the inoculated plants, of which only 45.9% showed typical MSMV symptoms (mottling and/or chlorotic streaks). We also evaluated the MSMV pathogenicity in two maize hybrids after inoculation with viruliferous leafhoppers caged at a density of 20 individuals/plant for 72 h; the inoculated hybrid plants and respective controls (exposed or not to aviruliferous leafhoppers) were grown in pots in a greenhouse to assess symptoms and yield. A multivariate analysis showed that the MSMV impact on maize varied with infection type (symptomatic versus asymptomatic). Both hybrids were highly affected when symptoms developed, whereas asymptomatic infection did not significantly alter plant development but still reduced grain yield in one hybrid. These findings are essential for understanding virus impact, transmission ecology, and management strategies.

items.title: More positive comment valence does not always correspond to more gifts: Different behavioral patterns of free and paid gifts in sports live streaming.
items.abstract: Gift behavior in sports live streaming does not increase synchronously as comment language becomes more positive. Based on 12,427 live-interaction records from five badminton finals of China's 15th National Games in 2025, this study examines at the minute level the relationships among comment valence, event phases, and free and paid gifts, with 4105 free-gift items and 282 paid-gift items counted in total. The results show that, in the primary model, more positive concurrent comment valence is associated with more free-gift items, but this relationship becomes weaker after further controlling for commenting activity; in contrast, neither the overall count nor the occurrence of paid gifts shows a significant relationship with comment valence. Paid gifts show an overall difference across event phases, with the periods around the completion of straight-game matches showing the clearest pattern, whereas the estimates around the completion of deciding-game matches are relatively unstable. Further analysis finds that, among minutes in which paid gifts have occurred, more positive comment valence is associated with more paid-gift items. Overall, although free and paid gifts occur during the same live-streaming process, they show result patterns that are not fully consistent in relation to comment valence and match progression. These relationships reflect minute-level behavioral changes in the livestream rather than a direct conversion from commenting to gifting by individual viewers.

items.title: Taif Roses: Historical Richness, Modern Industrial Vitality, and Global Reach—An Integrative Evidence Review, 2000–2026
items.abstract: Taif rose (Rosa damascena Mill. var. trigintipetala) is the defining crop of the Taif highlands of Saudi Arabia, a heritage practice inscribed by UNESCO in 2024 and a working industry whose farms, distilleries, and residue streams have only recently become objects of systematic study. This integrative review assembles the peer-reviewed evidence published between 2000 and 2026 and reads it against three claims embedded in the crop’s public identity: that it has a rich history, that it sustains a thriving modern industry, and that it holds a global presence. Crossref and OpenAlex were searched on October 15, 2026; 727 records were screened against verified bibliographic metadata, and 39 studies met the inclusion criteria. Findings were analyzed through reflexive thematic analysis and interpreted using the Evidence-Based Field-to-Formulation (EFF) framework developed here, which combines value-chain, circular-bioeconomy, translational-evidence, and place-based quality lenses over a digital enabling layer. Five themes emerged: chemical identity and terroir; bioactivity and safety; circular valorization of residues; propagation, stress physiology, and plant health; and digital and process innovation. The evidence confirms a measurable place-based chemical identity, a substantial and partly characterized residue stream, and a maturing propagation toolkit. It does not yet support the industry’s highest-value claims: no study has tested Taif rose material in humans, origin authentication remains unvalidated, and one included-adjacent study was retracted during the review. Taif rose is historically rich and industrially active, but its global presence is cultural and commercial rather than evidential. Closing that gap requires authentication science, safe residue routing, and early-phase clinical research.

items.title: Optimal Sensor Placement for Predicting Extreme Urban Pollution Events: A Unified Empirical and Optimization Approach
items.abstract: Urban air quality monitoring networks are traditionally designed to capture mean concentration fields. However, public health and environmental regulations are increasingly focused on extreme pollution events (e.g., the 99th percentile, p99), which exhibit high spatial variability driven by turbulence. Placing sensors at locations of maximum mean concentration (Cmean) often fails to capture these rare, extreme peaks. This study proposes a unified empirical and optimization framework for the active design of sensor networks specifically tailored for extreme value prediction. Using the COST ES1006 Michelstadt wind tunnel dataset, we combine the empirical relation p99 = Cmean + Kcσ with spatial interpolation and two optimization algorithms: Greedy forward selection and a Genetic Algorithm (GA). The objective is to identify the minimal set of sensor locations that minimizes the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of p99 predictions across all non-sensor locations. The results demonstrate that classical placement strategies (sensors at maximum Cmean) yield an MAE of 96.98 ppmV, highlighting their inability to capture spatial extremes. In contrast, the proposed optimization framework drastically reduces the prediction error. With only 10 sensors, the Greedy algorithm achieves an MAE of 18.16 ppmV, while the GA achieves 19.21 ppmV. Furthermore, a sensitivity analysis reveals a clear "elbow" in the performance curve: a network of 8 to 10 optimally placed sensors is sufficient to reconstruct the p99 field with an MAE of approximately 20 ppmV, beyond which diminishing returns are observed. The optimal sensor distribution reveals a balanced strategy, combining source-proximal, high-altitude, and peripheral locations. This methodology provides a robust, cost-effective tool for engineers and policymakers to design efficient urban air quality monitoring networks capable of accurately predicting worst-case pollution scenarios.

items.title: Multi-omics, multi-tissue analysis reveal role of extracellular matrix remodeling and sphingolipid homeostasis in edematous malnutrition (kwashiorkor).
items.abstract: Edematous malnutrition, aka kwashiorkor, is a phenotype of severe malnutrition whose pathophysiology remains poorly understood. In this case-control study, we employed plasma lipidomics, metabolomics, and proteomics, urine metabolomics and gut microbiome profiling to delineate molecular features specific to kwashiorkor in 60 children aged 6-59 months from Niger compared to marasmus (n = 60) and non-malnourished children (NAM) (n = 60) matched by age, sex, and clinical triage score. Features were defined as kwashiorkor-specific if they also correlated with edema severity and normalized following nutritional rehabilitation. We identified a plasma proteomic factor featuring lumican, gelsolin, and tetranectin and a lipidomic factor enriched in sphingolipids. Both differed in kwashiorkor compared to marasmus and NAM, were associated with edema grade, and trended towards normalcy after nutritional treatment, which are consistent with ECM remodeling and sphingolipid dysregulation. In contrast, neither (plasma and urine) metabolomic profiles nor gut microbiome composition showed kwashiorkor-specific signatures, although our urine and gut microbiome analyses may be underpowered. These findings advance understanding of kwashiorkor pathophysiology beyond nutrient deficiency and highlight ECM and sphingolipid features associated with its distinct clinical and molecular characteristics compared to marasmus.

items.title: Cascading effects of nano-biochar mitigate antibiotic resistance via phage-host interactions in the soil-crop ecosystem.
items.abstract: Controlling the spread of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in agroecosystems is central to One Health, yet whether nano-biochar-amended organic fertilizers can mitigate phage-mediated ARG dissemination along the fertilizer-soil-crop continuum remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed 120 viral metagenomes to examine how biochar-amended organic fertilizers modulate ARG dynamics, phage-associated functions, and phage-host interactions across the fertilizer-soil-lettuce continuum. The lettuce phyllosphere served as a key endpoint for ARG accumulation, exhibiting 4.1-4.9 times the total ARG abundance and 56.8-66.3% higher phage-encoded ARG abundance compared with rhizosphere and non-rhizosphere soils. Source-tracking analysis indicated that manure and soil inputs accounted for 50.8-57.0% of phyllosphere ARGs, while 111 manure-associated viral populations were shared with the phyllosphere at the viral cluster level. Notably, nano-biochar-amended vermicompost exerted a cascading mitigation effect, reducing manure- and soil-derived ARG inputs to the phyllosphere by 20.4-21.6% and manure-associated viral sharing by 51.6%. Meanwhile, nano-biochar-amended vermicompost reduced lysogenic phage-host interactions, phage-encoded ARGs, and auxiliary metabolic genes associated with antibiotic-resistant bacteria, which may contribute to reduced phage-associated ARG dissemination potential. Consequently, total ARG abundance in the phyllosphere decreased by 68.9-76.3%, while lettuce biomass increased by 54.1-61.5%. This work suggests that nano-biochar-amended vermicompost may mitigate antibiotic resistance risks and enhance crop productivity partly by attenuating phage-associated ARG dissemination across the fertilizer-soil-crop continuum, highlighting its potential for One Health-oriented resistance-risk control in agricultural production.

items.title: Influence of Foraging Effort and Diet on Maternal Energy Stores and Offspring Weaning Mass in Gray Seals ( Halichoerus grypus ).
items.abstract: Understanding how foraging behavior and diet influence individual reproductive success is a key interest in evolutionary ecology. This is particularly true for capital breeding species where the accumulation and storage of energy to support offspring is critical, often following the "bigger-is-better" hypothesis. Using data collected from female gray seals (Halichoerus grypus) at Sable Island, Canada, between 1995 and 2018, we tested the hypothesis that differences in foraging effort and diet prior to the breeding season, estimated through satellite telemetry, stable isotope (SI) signatures, and quantitative fatty acid signature analysis (QFASA), respectively, affect reproductive success. There was no relationship between dominant prey type, the energy density of estimated diets, and maternal postpartum mass (MPPM). Females consuming a diet of lower diversity and with more positive δ13C estimates, possibly indicating more benthic foraging, had higher MPPM. MPPM was the best predictor of offspring mass at weaning. However, metrics of maternal foraging effort and diet alone did not influence pup weaning mass when MPPM was included in the model. These results suggest that different foraging strategies and diets can lead to sufficient body energy storage that enables reproductive success in a capital breeder. Considering this colony was increasing rapidly during the study period, the influence of foraging effort and diet might differ in a stable or declining population where intraspecific competition may be more evident.

items.title: In Silico Characterization of Desert Locust-Derived Antimicrobial Peptides Against Drug-Resistant Bacteria.
items.abstract: The critical need to find solutions to antibiotic resistance in pathogenic bacteria is becoming increasingly pronounced globally. In response to the urgent problems posed by the current public health challenges, our study adds to the growing body of knowledge by extracting insect peptides using acidified solvents, identifying the peptides from immune-challenged and nonimmune-challenged Schistocerca gregaria nymphs, and evaluating their antimicrobial activities against 9 clinical pathogens. A total of 96 unique peptides were identified, 91% from immune-challenged nymphs. Three specific antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) were common in immune-challenged and nonimmune-challenged individuals. Eleven and 27 peptides were categorized as high- and moderate-confidence AMPs, respectively, with sequence homologies ranging between 33% and 67%. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of peptide extract from immune-challenged nymphs ranged between 5 and 25 μg/mL, compared to 7.9-100 μg/mL from nonimmune-challenged nymphs. The lowest MIC values (< 8 μg/mL) were observed against Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus faecalis, Listeria monocytogenes, Escherichia coli, and Streptococcus agalactiae. It was observed that 87.5% of the AMP extracts had lower MIC values against Strep. agalactiae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa compared to tetracycline. The hemolytic activities due to peptide extracts from nonimmune-challenged (SPE-A) and immune-challenged (SPE-B) locust nymphs were < 5%. Our work underscores insects' promise as sustainable AMP contributors, offering recommendations for further research to unlock their full potential in the design of new antimicrobial agents to overcome bacterial drug resistance.

items.title: Roe Deer Capreolus capreolus Home Range Size and Daily Distance in the Agricultural Landscape of East-Central Poland in Relation to Natural and Anthropogenic Factors.
items.abstract: Home range and daily distance traveled are the basic parameters of animal habitat utilization and emerge from complex interactions between animals and their environment. In this study, the home ranges, core areas, and daily distances traveled of 10 collared roe deer in east-central Poland were analyzed. The mean home range size for all animals was 136.1 ha (minimum convex polygon of 95% of points), and 69 ha (95% kernel density estimation); the mean core area was 10.9 ha (50% kernel density estimation). Core areas were larger in males than in females and larger in the winter period than in the growing period. Home range size decreased with increasing forest cover and increased with the number of wind turbines. Core area size was influenced only by the sex of the animal and forest cover. Neither the size of the home range nor the size of the core area depended on road density or settlement cover. The relationship between home range size and sex, natural factors, including forest cover, and season, is consistent with previous studies. Mean daily distance traveled for all animals was 3.14 km, and was lower in the growing period than in winter, and in females than in males. The daily distance traveled also decreased with increasing forest cover. Our study indicated a new anthropogenic factor shaping roe deer's spatial behavior in agricultural landscapes (wind farms). We concluded that roe deer have probably adapted behaviorally to wind farms as a new landscape feature. They probably treat wind farms like human settlements, generally avoid them, and use habitats at an appropriate distance from the turbines. We cannot, however, exclude the occasional fleeing behavior of roe deer near turbines. Further research should include a more detailed assessment of the behavior of roe deer and other terrestrial mammal species under the influence of wind farms.

items.title: Molecular Adaptations and Sex-Biased Regulatory Pathways in Multi-Year Diapause of the Cabbage Beetle Colaphellus bowringi : A Duration-Resolved Transcriptomic Analysis.
items.abstract: The cabbage beetle Colaphellus bowringi, a key pest of cruciferous crops, exhibits a multiyear dormancy strategy characterized by pronounced interindividual variation in diapause duration: individuals entering summer or winter diapause-though initiated synchronously within each seasonal cohort-may remain in diapause for periods ranging from several months to as long as 5 years. To elucidate the molecular underpinnings of this extended dormancy and its sex-specific regulatory patterns, we performed a duration-resolved, sex-stratified transcriptomic analysis. Adult males and females were sampled after 0.5, 1, and 2 years of diapause durations and subjected to high-throughput RNA sequencing. De novo assembly yielded 66,379 unigenes, of which 16,132 (24.3%) were removed as non-arthropod contamination, leaving 50,247 unigenes that were used for all downstream annotation and expression analyses. Comparative transcriptomic profiling revealed a conserved adaptive strategy during prolonged diapause: patterns consistent with coordinated suppression of energy-intensive metabolic processes coupled with increased transcript abundance of genes in cellular protection pathways-including antioxidant defense, xenobiotic detoxification, and protein homeostasis mechanisms. Sex-biased transcriptional responses were observed: females showed comparable or higher numbers of differentially expressed genes in matched duration comparisons, with sustained transcript abundance of genes associated with reproductive processes and somatic maintenance, whereas males displayed greater duration-dependent transcriptional remodeling, particularly in signaling cascades and physiological homeostasis networks. KEGG pathway enrichment analysis identified sustained activation of glutathione metabolism, autophagy, and lysosomal degradation pathways throughout diapause; notably, extended diapause (2 years) was specifically associated with significant enrichment of immune response and lipid metabolism pathways. Duration-dependent dynamics in gene expression underscore that diapause is not a static quiescent state but a highly regulated, multi-stage process involving duration-specific transcriptional reconfiguration. This study establishes the first duration-resolved, sex-resolved transcriptomic resource for C. bowringi and advances mechanistic understanding of long-term insect diapause-thereby informing the development of targeted, environmentally sustainable pest management strategies.

items.title: Behavioral and Physiological Response of Eucosma giganteana to Semiochemicals From Conspecifics and Silphium integrifolium .
items.abstract: Eucosma giganteana is a specialist herbivore on Silphium spp. and a major limiting factor to the commercialization of Silphium integrifolium, a perennial oilseed crop. Although it is known that (E)-8-dodecenyl acetate works as an attractant to E. giganteana, it is unknown whether it responds in a concentration-dependent manner, and whether this cue works throughout the season. Also unknown is whether these moths behaviorally or physiologically respond to other important semiochemicals, such as those emitted by conspecifics or its host. This information is important for developing volatiles for use in behaviorally-based management of E. giganteana. To address our questions, we performed field trapping with traps baited with (E)-8-dodecenyl acetate, characterized headspace emissions from E. giganteana, and used EAG and flight mill analysis to assess response to (E)-8-dodecenyl acetate and volatiles derived from S. integrifolium and conspecifics. Higher loadings of (E)-8-dodecenyl acetate in the field trapping studies conducted in 2024 resulted in increased captures of E. giganteana moths on sticky traps, which successfully monitored E. giganteana through their full flight period. EAG showed antennal depolarizations, which confirmed E. giganteana perceive (E)-8-dodecenyl acetate. In addition, female E. giganteana perceive volatiles emitted by S. integrifolium whereas males did not. Despite eliciting clear antennal responses and showing success in field monitoring, (E)-8-dodecenyl acetate did not influence flight behavior during the flight mill experiments under the tested conditions. Altogether this study shows (E)-8-dodecenyl acetate successfully monitored E. giganteana through the field season; more work is required to deploy it in behaviorally-based management IPM tactics.

items.title: Evaluating the Potential of Four Native Ziziphus Species for Restoring Savanna-Like Habitats in Jinsha River Under Climate Change.
items.abstract: The Jinsha River, as the upper section of the Yangtze River, plays a key role as an ecological barrier, yet its dry-hot valleys face severe degradation due to harsh climate and human activities. Four native Ziziphus species (Z. mauritiana, Z. montana, Z. mairei, and Z. xiangchengensis) were selected to assess their potential for restoring "valley-type savanna" vegetation through field investigations, species distribution modeling, germination experiments, and interviews. Field investigations showed that Z. mairei and Z. xiangchengensis exhibit limited distributions and small populations, requiring artificial propagation and protection. MaxEnt models performed well (AUC > 0.9). Ziziphus montana occurs in northwestern Yunnan and is primarily limited by temperature seasonality (bio4), elevation, and coldest quarter temperature (bio11). Under future climate scenarios, its suitable habitat is projected to contract by 11.3%-20.4%, with the remaining highly suitable area retreating toward the Jinsha River basin. Bio11 is the primary factor influencing the distribution of Z. mauritiana, and its suitable range is projected to expand by 44.1%-119.1%. Seed heteromorphism was documented for the first time in Z. xiangchengensis, Z. montana, and Z. mairei, classified into Type A (2 carpels) and B (3 carpels) based on carpel number, with Type A seeds dominating (66.0%-94.8%). These two seed types showed significant differences in temperature response and dormancy characteristics. Four Ziziphus species displayed strong physical dormancy, removing the endocarp and cracking the seed coat results in a 100% germination rate, providing a practical solution for large-scale seedling propagation. Based on assessment, Z. montana is more suitable for ecological restoration in the Jinsha River Basin. The population age structure is of the expanding type and serves medicinal, edible, agricultural, ecological restoration, and handicraft purposes. We advocate for community-based "interactive" ecological restoration, using economic incentives to drive ecological recovery. This study contributes to ecological restoration, germplasm conservation, and local economic development.

items.title: Cave-Dwelling Planariidae in Dinaric Karst Exhibit Differing Levels of Cave Trait Evolution.
items.abstract: The Dinaric karst encompasses a network of over 10,000 caves and represents one of the world's most important subterranean biodiversity hotspots. It is inhabited by remarkably diverse and often endemic species, including planarian flatworms. Although cave planarians have long been known from the region, they have not yet been investigated using an integrative approach, and their evolutionary relationships with surface-dwelling relatives remain unresolved. To address these gaps, we combined field sampling, phylogenetic analyses based on the COI and 18S genes, and phenotypic characterisation. Our results show that cave planariids in the Dinaric karst belong to at least three genera and are more widespread and diverse than previously assumed. We increased the number of cave records in the Dinaric karst from 26 to 37 and documented cf. Atrioplanaria and Phagocata in Croatian caves for the first time. Phylogenetic reconstructions are consistent with independent cave colonisation events, including multiple instances within the genera Crenobia and cf. Atrioplanaria. Variation in pigmentation and eye reduction, both within and between populations, further reveals heterogeneous evolutionary trajectories of cave-associated phenotypes. Our molecular phylogeny and documentation of trait variability constitute a first step towards establishing Planariidae as a model for investigating the mechanisms underlying the convergent evolution of pigment loss and eye reduction in cave environments.

items.title: Occurrence, Distribution, and Infestation Levels of Coccus hesperidum (Hemiptera: Coccidae) on Chili Pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) in South Sulawesi, Indonesia.
items.abstract: This study aimed to identify the coccid insect causing severe damage to field-grown chili pepper plants (Capsicum annuum L.) in South Sulawesi, Indonesia, and to assess its distribution and incidence. Infested chili pepper branches were collected, frozen for 48 h, and sent to the Indonesian Agricultural Quarantine Laboratory, Makassar, for identification. Specimens were mounted on microslides using Hein's mountant, oven-dried, and examined microscopically. A field survey was conducted in nine chili pepper-producing regencies to determine the pest's occurrence and associated plant damage. The insect was identified as the brown soft scale, Coccus hesperidum L. (Hemiptera: Coccidae). This study provides the first documented occurrence of C. hesperidum in South Sulawesi and the first evidence of chili pepper as its host. The pest was detected in four of the nine surveyed regencies, Makassar, Soppeng, Wajo, and Sidrap, with incidence varying among locations. The highest levels of infestation were recorded in Belawa, Wajo Regency (43%) and Marioriawa, Soppeng Regency (37%). The presence of C. hesperidum poses a potential threat to the sustainability of chili pepper production in South Sulawesi. Integrated management strategies are urgently needed, and further studies on the insect's biology and ecology, resistant varieties, natural enemies, cultivation practices, and judicious insecticide use are recommended.

items.title: Preliminary Evidence Suggests the Transcriptomic Response of Tricolored Bats to White-Nose Syndrome Is Similar but Not Identical to That of Little Brown Bats.
items.abstract: Understanding the pathophysiology of emerging wildlife diseases can inform treatment, improve the projections of long-term population trajectories, and reveal variation in population-level impacts among species. Research on white-nose syndrome (WNS) in hibernating North American bats has largely focused on a single highly susceptible species, the little brown bat (Myotis lucifugus). Another susceptible species, the tricolored bat (Perimyotis subflavus), has experienced population declines comparable to or greater than those of little brown bats but remains understudied. In particular, the immune response of tricolored bats to WNS has not previously been evaluated. Here, we conduct a preliminary analysis comparing part of the transcriptomic response of tricolored bats to WNS with the little brown bat response. We analyzed 14 tricolored and 13 little brown bat samples collected from Colossal Cave, Kentucky, USA in 2017, where WNS has been present since 2013. We also included 26 little brown bat samples collected from a nearby hibernation site in 1999, prior to WNS emergence. Lacking a proper pre-WNS control for tricolored bats, we conducted pairwise differential expression analyses between the three sample groups and evaluated the overlap between results to infer part of the tricolored bat response to WNS. These initial results suggested that tricolored bats exhibited differential expression patterns characteristic of susceptible species, including large changes in gene expression still apparent at the end of the hibernation season. Differentially expressed genes were associated with immune, metabolic, and circadian functions, broadly resembling the response observed in little brown bats. However, there was variation in the specific genes involved between the two species. Overall, tricolored bats appear to mount a pronounced immune response to WNS that is similar, but not identical, to that of little brown bats.
