items.title: Leaching Potential and Environmental Implications of Gold Ore Tailings From Ileki Ijesha, Osun State, Nigeria
items.abstract: Abstract Gold mining in Nigeria, particularly artisanal and small-scale operations, generates large volumes of tailings that pose serious environmental and public health risks due to heavy metal leaching and potential acid mine drainage (AMD). This study assessed the leaching behavior and geochemical characteristics of gold ore tailings from Ileki Ijesha, Osun State, using batch and dynamic column leaching experiments. Five representative samples were analyzed for pH and concentrations of key metals (Fe, Mn, Pb, Cd, Zn, Cr, Ca) by Atomic Absorption Spectrometry. Leachates were further evaluated through PHREEQC geochemical modeling for speciation, saturation indices, and sensitivity analysis. Results revealed elevated iron (up to 22.2 mg/L) and manganese (up to 11.2 mg/L) concentrations, with moderate lead levels (6.6–7.81 mg/L) under near-neutral pH conditions (6.06–7.73). Modeling indicated supersaturation with iron (oxy) hydroxides and a critical pH threshold (~ 5.5) for accelerated metal release. These findings highlight significant long-term AMD risks and underscore the urgent need for improved tailings management and regulatory frameworks in Nigerian gold mining regions.

items.title: The Use of Indigenous Knowledge Medicine by Traditional Health Practitioners to Treat Infertility in Mavhunda Village, Vhembe District: An Ethnomedicinal Inquiry
items.abstract: Abstract Infertility represents a complex reproductive health challenge worldwide, generating severe psychological distress, familial instability, and acute social stigmatization. In resource-constrained rural localities such as Mavhunda Village in the Vhembe District of Limpopo Province, structural barriers compel community members to seek healthcare from traditional health practitioners. This study examines the role of indigenous knowledge medicine in diagnosing and treating infertility. Framed through Ethnomedicine Theory, this qualitative single-case study employed purposive sampling to investigate experienced traditional health practitioners (n'anga and mungome) with over a decade of clinical practice. Empirical data gathered through semi-structured interviews and observational fieldwork reveal that practitioners utilize a sophisticated botanical pharmacopeia—including Muthavhatsindi ( Brackenridgea zanguebarica ), Musuma ( Diospyros mespiliformis ), Museto, and Mapfura steam therapies—alongside customary restorative rituals like U swela . The article calls for progressive public health policy reforms and formal collaborative referral networks.

items.title: Community Responses to Urban Heat Risk in Prayagraj Municipal Corporation, India
items.abstract: Abstract The increasing frequency and intensity of heatwaves under climate change are emerging as major public health concerns across rapidly urbanising regions of South Asia. This study examines heatwave awareness and perception, behavioural adaptation practices, and heat-related health outcomes among urban households in Prayagraj, a climatically vulnerable city in India's Indo-Gangetic Plain. The analysis is based on primary household-level data collected from 422 households through multistage cluster random sampling conducted between February and March 2026. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to examine socio-demographic variation in heat-related awareness, adaptive behaviour, and self-reported health outcomes. At the same time, Cronbach’s alpha was used to assess the internal consistency of behavioural adaptation and health outcome variables. Qualitative field narratives were additionally incorporated to contextualise lived experiences of heat exposure and adaptation constraints. The findings reveal widespread perception of increasing heatwave intensity, with 91.5% of respondents reporting rising heat exposure over their lifetime. Although adaptive practices such as increased hydration, dietary modification, and protective clothing use were widely adopted, a substantial proportion of households continued to report heat-related symptoms, including muscle weakness or cramps (49%), severe fatigue or exhaustion (42%), dizziness or fainting (31.3%), and heat stroke or high fever (27.1%). Significant socio-demographic disparities were observed across educational, occupational, and social groups, with informal workers and economically vulnerable households reporting comparatively greater heat-related health burden. The study underscores the need for inclusive and structurally grounded urban heat adaptation strategies that address occupational exposure, housing vulnerability, and broader social determinants of heat-health risk in rapidly growing Indian cities.

items.title: Living alongside asbestos mine tailings: Perceived stress and asbestos-related concerns in Canadian former mining regions
items.abstract: Abstract Background Growing evidence suggests that concerns about the health and environmental effects of contamination may contribute to psychological stress among communities. However, little is known about psychological stress and asbestos-related concerns among populations living in former asbestos-mining regions, particularly in Canada, once a world-leading chrysotile producer. This study aimed to characterize psychological stress among residents of two former asbestos-mining regions in Quebec and examine its associations with asbestos-related concerns and knowledge. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 191 adults. Respondents completed an online questionnaire assessing perceived stress, psychological distress, life events, asbestos-related concerns, knowledge about asbestos, and sociodemographic and contextual factors. Group comparisons examined perceived stress and asbestos-related concerns across contextual factors, and multiple linear regression examined factors associated with perceived stress. Results Respondents reported generally low levels of perceived stress (mean = 11.24 out of 40) and asbestos-related concerns (mean = 3.55 out of 18). items.title: Cancer-Related Stigma among University Students in Oman: Implications for Cancer Care
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Cancer-related stigma (CRS) refers to negative perceptions and attitudes associated with a cancer diagnosis, often resulting in discrimination, social exclusion, delayed healthcare-seeking behaviors, psychological distress, and poor health outcomes. As cancer incidence continues to increase in Oman and globally, assessing CRS is essential for informing interventions to improve cancer awareness and health outcomes. Aim To explore the prevalence of CRS and the associated factors among university students in Oman. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted. Data were collected from students across multiple universities in Oman (N = 380) using self-administered questionnaires comprising the Cancer Stigma Scale and the Health Consciousness Scale. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted to identify factors associated with CRS. Results More than 30% of participants believed that insurance companies could reconsider policies for individuals diagnosed with cancer (31%), felt that cancer ruins a person’s career (32%), considered individuals with cancer partly responsible for their condition (33%), and reported embarrassment discussing cancer with someone diagnosed with the disease (40%). items.title: Perspectives on traumatic brain injury screening among intersecting underserved populations: an exploratory study.
items.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to explore barriers and facilitators in traumatic brain injury (TBI) screening for underserved individuals and knowledge translation efforts to address challenges. Materials and methods Guided by qualitative description, we conducted four virtual focus groups: 10 people (7 female, 3 male) with lived experience of precarious housing, criminal legal involvement, and/or violence and 11 service providers (9 female, 2 male) supporting these populations with TBI. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings Barriers to TBI screening included (1) inconsistent implementation and competing priorities within organizations; (2) stigmatization and systemic challenges in service provision; and (3) a lack of a universal screening system and follow-up pathways. While potential facilitators to screening involved language, knowledge and resources, as identified in the following themes: (1) language matters: shaping conversations in TBI screening; (2) screening for all: knowledge and access; and (3) easy and engaging tools for screening. Conclusions Barriers to TBI screening persist. Systemic changes and targeted educational initiatives are needed to improve knowledge and awareness of TBI with sensitivity to potential circumstances of specific populations. Affirming conversational language in screening, along with providing tailored resources and access to follow-up support services that address social determinants of health, are essential.

items.title: Development and Pilot Evaluation of a Standardized and Accessible Rubric (OMNI) for Assessing Generative AI in Health Care Contexts: Four-Stage Mixed Methods Study.
items.abstract: Background The rapid adoption of generative AI in the community and health care necessitates reliable, human-led evaluation. Objective This study aimed to develop a standardized rubric to support health care professionals, administrators, and researchers in evaluating generative AI outputs in health contexts. Methods A rubric was developed through a 4-stage mixed methods study: literature synthesis, expert refinement, pilot application, and post-pilot feedback. The rubric was informed by 69 publications and refined through iterative feedback from a multidisciplinary expert panel (n=23). The pilot rubric was applied to 4 health care scenarios: responses to health-related Reddit questions, generation of health-related images and videos, responses to health professional continuing education questions, and automated physician-to-physician clinical documentation generation. Via these scenarios, 15 clinicians (medical practitioners, pharmacists, and medical oncologists) evaluated 250 input-output pairs using domain-level ratings and qualitative comments. The evaluated outputs included 200 AI-generated responses across the 4 health care scenarios and 50 physician-tagged replies in the health-related Reddit questions scenario. Results The final rubric, OMNI, comprised 10 evaluation domains (Accuracy, Safety, Recognizes Uncertainty, Completeness, Communicates Clearly, Empathetic, Context Aware, Referencing, Follows Instructions, and Avoids Coerciveness) assessed on 4-point Likert scales, supported by detailed instructional and example materials. Via the 4 pilot scenarios, assessors generated 9600 domain-level ratings and 4010 qualitative comments. The mean pairwise agreement for the 4-point Likert groups ranged from 30.8% to 53.4%, increasing to 59.3% to 79.6% when collapsed into broad agreement categories; Gwet's AC2 ranged from 0.49 to 0.80. OMNI differentiated strengths and weaknesses between models within scenarios, while recurrent limitations in Referencing, Recognizes Uncertainty, Completeness, Empathetic, and Accuracy were identified across scenarios. Multimodal image and video outputs had the highest occurrence of negative rating domains. Assessors reported OMNI was usable and indicated they would reuse it. Conclusions OMNI is a standardized, accessible rubric for expert-led evaluation of generative AI outputs in health contexts. Pilot application demonstrated that OMNI could differentiate AI performance across models and domains while generating structured feedback. Further work is needed to assess its applicability to purpose-built health AI tools, agentic systems, and organizational evaluation settings.

items.title: Safety of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors in Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Objective Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have demonstrated cardiorenal benefits in individuals with type 2 diabetes, but safety data in older adults remain limited. We evaluated the real-world safety of SGLT2is compared with dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) among individuals aged ≥75 years with type 2 diabetes. Research design and methods We conducted a population-based, active-comparator, new-user cohort study using administrative health databases from British Columbia, Canada. We included individuals aged ≥75 years with type 2 diabetes initiating SGLT2is or DPP-4is between 1 January 2021 and 31 December 2023. Primary outcomes were infection, diabetic ketoacidosis, acute kidney injury, fall, fracture, and all-cause hospitalization. Cox regression with propensity score-based standardized mortality ratio weighting was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs). Results The study included 4,997 SGLT2i initiators (median age, 79 years; 37% women) and 1,289 DPP-4i initiators (median age, 82 years; 50% women). Compared with DPP-4i initiation, SGLT2i initiation was associated with lower risks of acute kidney injury (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.60-0.95) and all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.77-0.98), with no difference in risk of infection. No differences were observed in risk of diabetic ketoacidosis, falls, or fractures, although CIs were compatible with both benefit and harm. Conclusions In individuals aged ≥75 years with type 2 diabetes, SGLT2i initiation was not associated with increased risk of harm compared with DPP-4i initiation, although estimates were imprecise for some outcomes. These findings may support consideration of SGLT2is as a treatment option in this population.

items.title: The impact of sequential analysis on drug decision-making in Canada.
items.abstract: Aim: In Canada (excluding Québec), public drug coverage generally relies on health technology assessment and reimbursement recommendations produced by Canada's Drug Agency - L'Agence des medicaments du Canada (CDA-AMC). At CDA-AMC, when multiple comparators are included in the pharmacoeconomic analysis, the corresponding results are reported using a sequential analysis. The aim of this review was to understand how the sequential analysis approach impacts the price reductions recommended in CDA-AMC drug reimbursement reviews. Materials & methods: A search was conducted of CDA-AMC reimbursement review reports published from January 2022 to December 2023 that included a cost-utility analysis with sequential analysis performed by the Sponsor and the economic re-analysis by CDA-AMC. An analysis of included reimbursement reviews was conducted to determine if the comparators chosen through the sequential analysis and selected for the price reduction in the final reimbursement recommendation were also the comparators most commonly used in current clinical practice. Additional analyses further examining reported market shares and list prices were conducted among reimbursement recommendations where the selected comparator was not the most commonly used comparator. An assessment examining the impact of comparator selection based on the sequential analysis on cost-effectiveness conclusions in CDA-AMC reimbursement reviews was also conducted. Results are presented by type of drug review (i.e., oncology vs nononcology products). Results: A total of 150 CDA-AMC reimbursement reviews published from January 2022 to December 2023 were identified and screened for eligibility. Of these, 37 reimbursement reviews - comprising a total of 60 recommendations (13 oncology and 47 nononcology products) based on sequential analyses - were included in the analysis. Among the included reimbursement recommendations, CDA-AMC chose a comparator that was not the most commonly used in clinical practice in 25 (42%) recommendations when determining the price reduction of the new medication (in accordance with CDA-AMC guidelines that permit selection of any comparator regardless of clinical utilization). Among these 25 reimbursement recommendations, the selected comparator represented Conclusion: Comparator selection is a vital aspect of health technology assessment. At CDA-AMC, comparator selection is driven by the sequential analysis approach, playing an important role in their economic assessment and reimbursement recommendation. Despite the relatively small number of sequential analyses examined, this review found that CDA-AMC recommendations based on a sequential analysis frequently refer to a comparator that is not widely used in real-world clinical practice, which can impede subsequent health technology assessment decisions that need to consider clinically prevalent comparators. This is notable as pairwise analyses conducted for this review demonstrated that selecting the treatments most often used in clinical practice as the comparator, rather than the CDA-AMC comparator, likely yields lower price reductions for new treatments that are more costly and more effective. These findings reinforce the importance of transparent and clinically informed comparator selection and points to the need for CDA-AMC to commit to providing economic assessments of all clinically relevant comparators to ensure payers have a complete and balanced picture of the evidence.

items.title: The Aspergillus fumigatus septation components Bud4 and Rho4 are essential for virulence.
items.abstract: Aspergillus fumigatus is the primary etiologic agent of pulmonary mold infections, the most severe of which is invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA). As the currently approved antifungal drugs are threatened by growing resistance rates and host toxicity, novel therapeutic options are urgently needed. Our recent work suggests that septation inhibition may be one such strategy, as aseptate strains of A. fumigatus are hypersusceptible to the echinocandin antifungal drugs and display significantly reduced virulence in animal models of IPA. In the current study, we expand upon our understanding of the anillin-like protein, Bud4, and Rho GTPase, Rho4, which regulate septation in Aspergillus nidulans and A. fumigatus , respectively. Whereas AnBud4 is not essential for septation in A. nidulans , deletion of the A. fumigatus ortholog (∆ bud4 ) resulted in complete loss of septation. A similar phenotype was also observed in ∆ rho4 , consistent with previous studies. Supporting a critical role for hyphal septation in the establishment of invasive aspergillosis, we find that ∆ bud4 and ∆ rho4 display avirulence in a mouse model of IPA characterized by a loss of tissue-invasive growth. Furthermore, both deletion mutations were able to convert anti-A spergillus echinocandin activity from static to cidal. Through titratable bud4 expression using a doxycycline-repressible promoter system, we also find that even partial repression of septation significantly increases echinocandin susceptibility. Taken together, these studies support a therapeutic strategy which could incorporate a septation inhibitor in combination with echinocandins to reduce tissue-invasive growth and improve antifungal susceptibility.

items.title: Antenatal Screening for Sexually Transmitted Infections to Reduce Preterm Birth or Low Birthweight (Philani Ndiphile Study): A Randomized 3-Group Trial.
items.abstract: Background Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Trichomonas vaginalis are predominantly asymptomatic curable sexually transmitted infections (STIs) associated with adverse birth outcomes. Whether antenatal STI screening improves birth outcomes remains uncertain. Methods In this randomized trial (NCT04446611), pregnant women ≥18 years were assigned before 27 weeks' gestation to (1) screening and treatment for C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae, and T. vaginalis at enrollment, with tests-of-cure (1-Time Screening); (2) screening and treatment at enrollment, repeated at 30-34 weeks (2-Time Screening); or (3) Standard-of-Care (syndromic management). The primary outcome was a composite of preterm birth ( Results Of 2247 enrolled, 1910 had live births. The composite outcome occurred in 22.9% of the 1-Time Screening (RR 0.99; 95% CI .81-1.21) and 20.6% of the 2-Time Screening groups (RR 0.89; 95% CI .72-1.09), compared with 23.2% of the Standard-of-Care group. Preterm birth occurred in 18.9% of the 1-Time Screening group (RR 1.00; 95% CI .80-1.26), 14.5% of the 2-Time Screening group (RR 0.77; 95% CI .60-0.99), and 18.8% of the Standard-of-Care group. Low birthweight occurred in 14.1% of the 1-Time Screening group (RR 1.10; 95% CI .83-1.46), 12.9% of the 2-Time Screening group (RR 1.01; 95% CI .76-1.35), and 12.8% of the Standard-of-Care group. Conclusions Neither STI screening strategy reduced the primary composite outcome or low birthweight alone. The 2-Time Screening strategy reduced preterm birth by 23%.

items.title: User Experience of a Canadian Web Application for On-Demand Preventive Health Care: Cross-Sectional Online Survey Study.
items.abstract: Background Amid the current primary care crisis, Canadians are increasingly turning to online resources, where misinformation is common. Launched in 2023, the web application Icanbewell provides free, reliable, evidence-based information on preventive health care. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the user experience of the Icanbewell web application. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional online survey in Canada. Participants were members of the public aged at least 18 years and health care providers residing in Canada who had internet access. A 9-item online survey was made available within the Icanbewell web application from July 8, 2024, to August 7, 2025. It invited users to rate their satisfaction with the app, suggest improvements, and describe what they learned from it. The single Likert-scale question was analyzed using summary descriptive statistics, and the short-answer questions were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. Results Of the 69 users who responded to the Icanbewell survey, 80% (n=55) were satisfied with the app, 9% (n=6) were dissatisfied, and 10% (n=7) were neither satisfied nor dissatisfied. Satisfaction ranged from 78.9% to 90.9% across participant gender, status as a health care provider or member of the public, language, and whether the respondent was attached to a primary care provider. A total of 46 (67%) respondents provided suggestions to improve the Icanbewell web application by optimizing the interface and adding medical content beyond prevention. Finally, 42% (29/69) of respondents indicated that they learned new information from using the Icanbewell app, including details about Canadian prevention guidelines, how to access various health resources, and general medical information on health and symptoms. Conclusions This study demonstrated user satisfaction and engagement with the app. Subsequent work should prioritize representative sampling to gather feedback from individuals not attached to a primary care provider, younger people, health care providers, and people in geographically diverse locations. Our results highlight an ongoing need for accessible, trustworthy, evidence-based prevention resources, along with support for clinicians in disseminating them to the public. Future involvement of patient partners in the design and evaluation of the web application will be important to ensure its inclusivity and relevance.

items.title: Mental Health Outcomes Among Migrant Caregivers: A Systematic Review of Prevalence, Associated Factors, and Supportive Interventions.
items.abstract: Background Migrant caregivers play an essential role in addressing global shortages in long-term and domestic care. However, demanding working conditions, social isolation, and migration-related stressors may adversely affect their mental health, while evidence on prevalence, determinants, and effective interventions remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize global evidence on the prevalence of mental health outcomes among migrant caregivers, identify associated risk factors, and summarize supportive interventions targeting their mental health. Methods Eight databases were searched for studies published between January 2015 and October 2025. Eligible studies quantitatively assessed mental health outcomes among migrant caregivers or evaluated supportive mental health interventions using validated measurement tools. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study design, populations, and outcome measures, results were synthesized qualitatively. Results A total of 48 studies were included (42 cross-sectional, 6 interventions). Prevalence of depression, anxiety, psychological distress, sleep problems, and caregiver burden varied widely across settings and measurement tools. Mental health outcomes were consistently associated with sociodemographic, occupational, environmental, physical health, psychosocial, migration-related, and COVID-19-related factors. Evidence on interventions was limited to six small trials, showing modest and inconsistent effects, with more consistent improvements in coping and mental health literacy than in depressive symptoms, varying by design and caregiver characteristics. Conclusions Migrant caregivers experience a substantial mental health burden associated with employment conditions, workplace social environments, and migration-related factors. Addressing their mental health requires both improved research designs and policy responses that extend beyond individual-level interventions to structural and social conditions.

items.title: Community-Level Inequalities and Risk Factors for Incident Oral Frailty.
items.abstract: Introduction Oral frailty, characterized by tooth loss, chewing difficulty, and swallowing problems, has been associated with adverse health outcomes in older adults. However, longitudinal evidence on community-level inequalities and determinants of incident oral frailty remains limited. Objectives This cohort study aimed to examine community-level inequalities in the incidence of oral frailty and identify individual- and municipality-level factors associated with its onset among older adults in Japan. Methods We analyzed data from 42,987 participants aged ≥65 y who completed the Japan Gerontological Evaluation Study surveys in 2019 and 2022. Oral frailty was determined using a validated prediction model including age, number of teeth, chewing difficulty, and choking. Individual-level variables included sociodemographic, health status, and social capital indicators. Municipality-level variables included population density, aggregated social capital, and the presence of prefectural or municipal dental health ordinances. Modified multilevel Poisson regression was used to estimate incidence rate ratios. Results The incidence of oral frailty varied across municipalities, ranging from 17.1% to 33.3%. In the fully adjusted multilevel model, individual-level factors significantly associated with a higher risk of incident oral frailty were male sex; being widowed, divorced, or never married; lower educational attainment; lower equivalent income; smoking history; current illness; and lack of social cohesion ( P Conclusion Community-level inequalities in the incidence of oral frailty are driven by both individual vulnerabilities and municipality-level factors. Notably, higher municipality-level civic participation tended to be associated with a lower incidence of oral frailty. Effective prevention requires comprehensive strategies that address socioeconomic factors and promote community-level civic participation.Knowledge Transfer Statement:This nationwide cohort study demonstrates that community-level inequalities in the incidence of oral frailty are substantial. They are largely explained not only by modifiable individual socioeconomic factors but also by municipality-level civic participation. These findings highlight the importance of integrating individual risk-based prevention with community strategies that may contribute to reducing oral frailty and related oral health disparities in aging populations.

items.title: From orchestra to classroom: learner-centered music training as a tool to support motivation to learn
items.abstract: Fostering more self-determined forms of motivation in students remains a key challenge in education. According to self-determination theory (SDT), educational environments supporting autonomy, competence, and relatedness enhance more autonomous forms of motivation. Music education in collaborative, learner-centered formats may provide such conditions. This study investigates whether participation in learner-centered orchestral training is associated with changes in children's general academic motivation.The study involved 113 children aged 8–10 years. Half joined a three-month orchestral program emphasizing active participation, peer collaboration, and public performance. The other half formed a control group with no music training. Motivation was assessed pre- and post-training using the Academic Self-Regulation Questionnaire.Children in the music group showed a greater reduction in external regulation compared to the control group. For intrinsic motivation, a descriptive trend toward improvement was observed in the music group relative to the control group, although the Group x Time interaction did not reach statistical significance.These findings suggest that learner-centered orchestral training may support a shift towards more self-determined forms of motivation, primarily through reduced external regulation.

items.title: Enabling automatic transcription of child-centered audio recordings from real-world environments
items.abstract: Abstract Longform audio recordings obtained with microphones worn by children—also known as child-centered daylong recordings—have become a standard method for studying children’s language experiences and their impact on subsequent language development. Transcripts of longform speech audio would enable rich analyses at various linguistic levels, yet the massive scale of typical longform corpora prohibits comprehensive manual annotation. Meanwhile, automatic speech recognition (ASR)-based transcription faces significant challenges due to the noisy, unconstrained nature of real-world audio. Previous attempts have assumed that ASR must process each longform recording in its entirety. In this work, we present an approach for automatic detection of those utterances in longform audio that can be reliably transcribed with modern ASR systems, allowing automatic and relatively accurate transcription of a notable proportion of all speech in typical longform data. We validate the approach on four English longform corpora, showing that it achieves a median word error rate (WER) of 0% and a mean WER of 16% when transcribing 30% of the total speech in the dataset. In contrast, transcribing all speech without any filtering yields a median WER of 52% and a mean WER of 51%. We also compare word log-frequencies derived from the automatic transcripts with those from manual annotations and show that the frequencies correlate at r = 0.94 (Pearson) for all transcribed words and r = 0.99 for words that appear at least five times in the automatic transcripts. Overall, the work provides a concrete step toward increasingly detailed automated linguistic analyses of child-centered longform audio.

items.title: Gamificación para Fortalecer la Comprensión Lectora en Estudiantes de Educación Básica en Ecuador: Revisión Sistemática
items.abstract: Justification: Reading comprehension difficulties among basic education students have driven the search for pedagogical strategies such as gamification; however, their effectiveness depends on the specific characteristics of the context in which they are implemented. Objective: Therefore, the aim of this study was to conduct a systematic review of the literature published between 2020 and 2025 on gamification strategies used to strengthen reading comprehension among basic education students in Ecuador and to analyze the reported results regarding their effectiveness. Methodology: The study was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The search was carried out in the Scopus, SciELO, Redalyc, DOAJ, and Latindex databases. A total of 34 records were retrieved, of which 12 studies were selected for analysis. Results: Findings indicate that gamification strategies were mainly developed through digital resources and structured instructional sequences integrating challenges, feedback, rewards, points, levels, badges, narratives, progression systems, and collaborative activities. Regarding effectiveness, the studies reported improvements in literal, inferential, and critical reading comprehension, with greater progress in inferential and critical processes. In addition, increases were found in motivation, participation, engagement, and interest in reading. Conclusion: The findings support the favorable effects of gamification in strengthening reading comprehension among basic education students in Ecuador.

items.title: A systematic approach to comparing how observation frameworks decompose teaching: The NICE model
items.abstract: The growing interest in observationally assessing instruction has led to the proliferation of observation frameworks, creating the need to compare across frameworks. We introduce the NICE (Noticing, Interpreting, and Combining Evidence) model, which systematically compares items from different frameworks on three steps: (1) what lesson events are noticed or attended to; (2) how lesson events are interpreted; and (3) how interpreted lesson events are aggregated to generate summary codes or scores. The paper uses the NICE model to compare items from the Protocol for Language Arts Teaching Observation (PLATO), the Joint Action framework in Didactics (JAD-MTQ), and International Comparative Analysis of Learning and Teaching (ICALT), using both math and language arts lessons from Nordic lower secondary classrooms. Results highlight both similarities and differences in how the three frameworks decompose and make sense of instructional practice. We find that NICE provides a systematic and nuanced way of comparing items across frameworks.

items.title: THE MEDIATING EFFECTS OF TRANSFORMATIONAL LEADERSHIP OF SCHOOL HEADS AND WORK ENGAGEMENT ON THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PROFESSIONAL SELF-ESTEEM AND TEACHER EFFICACY AMONG PUBLIC ELEMENTARY TEACHERS
items.abstract: The main objective of the study is to find out the significance of the mediating effects of transformational leadership and work engagement on the relationship between professional self-esteem and teacher efficacy. Utilizing a correlational technique along with a quantitative, non-experimental and mediation research design, data were obtained from 335 public elementary teachers working in four large schools. The researcher used a cluster sampling technique and the statistical tools mean, Pearson r, and path analysis. From the results of the study, it was found that there are very high levels of professional self-esteem, teacher efficacy, transformational leadership of school heads, and work engagement. Moreover, there are no significant relationships between professional self-esteem and transformational leadership, and between transformational leadership and teacher efficacy. There are also no significant relationships between work engagement and teacher efficacy, and professional self-esteem and work engagement. However, there is a significant relationship between professional self-esteem and teacher efficacy. Furthermore, transformational leadership and work engagement have no significant combined mediation on the relationship between professional self-esteem and teacher efficacy. The findings of this study provide implications for policymakers in drafting plans, school heads in creating programs, and teachers in improving their transformational leadership, work engagement, professional self-esteem, and teacher efficacy. Keywords: education, professional self-esteem, teacher efficacy, transformational leadership, work engagement, correlation, teachers, Philippines

items.title: The Relationship between Future Time Perspective and Climate Anxiety among Generation Z: The Moderating Role of Gender
items.abstract: Climate anxiety is an increasingly widespread psychological response among Generation Z, particularly as young people face increasing awareness of the long-term consequences of climate change. Nevertheless, its relationship with future time perspective and the moderating role of gender remain understudied in an integrated manner, particularly in the context of developing countries such as Indonesia. This gap highlights the need to examine how future-oriented cognition and individual characteristics jointly relate to climate anxiety. This study was conducted to determine the relationship between future time perspective (FTP) and climate anxiety (CAS), while simultaneously testing whether gender acts as a moderating variable in this relationship. A correlational quantitative design with a moderation approach was employed, involving 373 Generation Z participants (182 males and 191 females) selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data collection was carried out through the Future Time Perspective Scale (FTPS) and the Climate Anxiety Scale (CAS), which were then processed using Pearson and Spearman correlation tests as well as JASP-assisted moderation regression analysis. The analysis results revealed a significant positive relationship between FTP and climate anxiety (r = 0.384, p < 0.001), indicating that the higher an individual’s future orientation, the greater the climate anxiety they experience. Furthermore, the moderation regression model was statistically significant (F = 66.730, p < 0.001, R2 = 0.352), with both the main effects of FTP (B = 0.801, p < 0.001) and gender (B = 30.204, p = 0.008) being significant. The interaction between FTP and gender also showed significance (B = -0.445, p < 0.001), confirming the role of gender as a moderator in the relationship between FTP and climate anxiety. The positive association between FTP and climate anxiety was stronger among males than females. These findings indicate that future-oriented cognition is positively associated with climate anxiety and that this association differs across gender groups. The findings provide theoretical evidence that integrating cognitive and individual-difference factors may offer a more nuanced understanding of climate anxiety among Generation Z. Practically, the findings may inform the development of gender-sensitive psychological and educational approaches to climate anxiety; however, the cross-sectional correlational design does not establish the effectiveness of gender-specific interventions.

items.title: Telomere-to-telomere gapless genome assemblies of Coreius heterodon and Coreius guichenoti
items.abstract: Coreius heterodon and Coreius guichenoti are endemic cyprinid fishes of the upper Yangtze River Basin. C. guichenoti is classified as Endangered (EN) by the IUCN and listed as a national second-class protected wild animal in China, whereas C. heterodon is classified as Not Evaluated (NE) by the IUCN. However, genomic resources for these species have remained limited, constraining evolutionary and conservation genetic studies. Here, we present near telomere-to-telomere genome assemblies for both species. The assemblies span 1.09 Gb for Coreius heterodon and 1.08 Gb for Coreius guichenoti , with contig N50 values of 43.10 Mb and 42.62 Mb, respectively, and are anchored to 25 chromosomes. Repetitive elements account for approximately 58% of each genome, and 25,876 and 25,778 protein-coding genes were annotated, respectively. Both assemblies exhibit exceptional completeness, with BUSCO scores exceeding 98.9%, confirming their high quality and reliability. These genome assemblies provide high-resolution resources for future studies on genome evolution, adaptive diversification, and conservation genomics of endemic fishes in the Yangtze River Basin.

items.title: Arthropods communities in organic orchards and adjacent hedgerows on Terceira Island (Azores, Portugal): a dataset supporting biological control research
items.abstract: Organic orchards and their associated hedgerows can function as important ecological infrastructures in agricultural landscapes by providing shelter, alternative prey, floral resources and overwintering sites for arthropods involved in natural pest regulation. This role is particularly relevant on oceanic islands, where agricultural mosaics include endemic, native non-endemic and introduced taxa, and where biodiversity-friendly production systems may contribute to both ecosystem-service provisioning and early detection of potentially invasive species. Under the scope of the BIODIVERSA+ COMCHA project, we sampled arthropod assemblages in six orchards certified under the Organic Production System on Terceira Island, Azores, Portugal, comparing the orchard interior with adjacent hedgerows. Sampling was carried out in September 2025 and May 2026 using standardised active methods: SLAM traps (Sea, Land and Air Malaise), nocturnal Active Aerial Search, nocturnal foliage beating and diurnal foliage beating. The resulting dataset is structured as a Darwin Core Archive, with an Event table and an Occurrence table, and provides baseline information for evaluating the contribution of organic orchards and hedgerows to beneficial arthropod diversity and biological control research. We provide an inventory of arthropods collected in EU-certified organic orchards and surrounding hedgerows on Terceira Island, based on 46 sampling events in September 2025 and 36 sampling events in May 2026 (82 sampling events in total), distributed across six localities and two habitat types: Mixed Orchard and Mixed Hedges. During September 2025 and May 2026, a total of 15739 specimens were recorded in 1,863 occurrences records, representing four arthropod classes, 18 orders and 86 families. Of these specimens, 13854 were identified to species or subspecies level, corresponding to 196 distinct scientific names. Overall, the dataset includes 299 DTP morphospecies or taxonomic units. Among these specimens, 10596 specimens were recorded in 1300 occurrence records in September 2025, while 5,143 specimens were recorded in 563 occurrence records in May 2026. The identified species/subspecies include 11 endemic taxa, 57 native non-endemic taxa, 104 introduced taxa and 24 taxa of uncertain establishment status. In terms of abundance, native non-endemic taxa were dominant, followed by introduced, endemic and uncertain taxa. This dataset include four species that are new records for Terceira island: Dipoena melanogaster (C.L. Koch, 1837) (Araneae, Theridiidae), Textrix pinicola Simon, 1875 (Araneae, Agelenidae), Stenocaecilius caboverdensis (Meinander, 1966) (Psocodea, Caeciliusidae) and Euconnus campestris campestris (L.W. Schaufuss, 1866) (Coleoptera, Staphylinidae). The dataset provides a first standardized baseline for comparing arthropod assemblages between orchard interiors and hedgerows in organic fruit-production systems on Terceira Island, supporting future assessments of biological control potential, habitat management, biosecurity surveillance and Nature-based Solutions in insular agroecosystems.

items.title: Exploring red fox (Vulpes vulpes) occupancy, detectability and statistical power to inform monitoring decisions at Booderee National Park
items.abstract: Context The difficulties of invasive predator management can be exacerbated by suboptimal monitoring data. Developing a cost-effective, operationally achievable and statistically robust monitoring program is therefore a key component of biodiversity conservation and management. Aims To explore options to better balance the survey effort, cost and statistical power of the red fox (Vulpes vulpes) monitoring program at Booderee National Park (BNP), south-eastern Australia. Methods We analysed existing camera-trap data over an 8-year period to estimate fox occupancy and detectability. We then conducted a power analysis to assess our ability to detect reductions in fox occupancy of varying magnitudes under six hypothetical monitoring scenarios with varying survey effort. We compared how statistical power varied among scenarios between seasons of high and low fox detectability (i.e. summer and spring respectively), and across three levels of initial occupancy (Ψ = 0.75, 0.50, 0.25). Annual costs were estimated for each hypothetical scenario as well as the current fox monitoring approach at BNP. Key results Fox occupancy at BNP increased between 2017 and 2022, while recent monitoring demonstrated seasonal variation in fox detectability. Additional monitoring sites could help maintain statistical power to detect a change in the fox population at BNP when fox occupancy is low. For a given number of sites, statistical power was similarly maintained by doubling the deployment length or conducting monitoring when detectability is highest without increasing deployment length, with the latter option avoiding increased data-processing costs. Conclusions To balance monitoring and operational needs at BNP we suggest a continuous camera-trap monitoring program, with permanently established posts. This approach could standardise camera orientation, reduce potential biases in the data and provide up-to-date operational information required by park managers. Implications Existing data can bolster our understanding of factors influencing detectability, and provide insight regarding monitoring options to better balance survey effort, cost and statistical power.

items.title: Combination of cover crops and microbial biostimulants: Impacts on soil functioning, grape production, and juice quality in rainfed vineyards
items.abstract: Vineyards are intensively managed agroecosystems, which can reduce their soil functioning and biodiversity, with consequences for grape and wine quality. New regulations (e.g., Europe’s green policies) and market demand for environmentally respectful products are encouraging the adoption of a range of nature-based practices such as cover crops and microbial biostimulants, yet their combined effects remain poorly evaluated. We conducted a fully factorial field experiment in rainfed vineyards in southern Spain to assess the simultaneous effects of two sustainable management strategies: the use of winter cover crops, as opposed to year-round tillage, and the foliar application of a nitrogen-fixing microbial biostimulant at two doses (1x and 3x based on the recommendations of the manufacturer). Cover crops increased the activity of soil extracellular enzymes associated with the C, N and P cycles, indicating enhanced decomposition potential, whereas the biostimulant did not consistently alter soil enzyme activity. Across two seasons, cover crops slightly reduced yield, but this effect was non-significant, while the biostimulant increased production in the first vintage. Importantly, the combination of cover crops with a high biostimulant dose achieved yields comparable to, or even higher than, tilled controls. The combined treatments suggested potential synergistic responses in ºBrix (indicative of total soluble solids) and pH of musts. Using structural equation modelling, we provided additional mechanistic evidence that cover crops and microbial biostimulants are two compatible strategies that may enhance, through complementary mechanisms (i.e., promoting either soil or plant health), the sustainability of vineyards. Our findings support the combination of these practices as a viable pathway toward more resilient and environmentally respectful viticulture.

items.title: Collective Ecological Protection: A Systems-Level Theory of Microbial Community Stability
items.abstract: Microbial communities persist under recurrent abiotic and biotic disturbance, yet the organizational basis of this persistence remains incompletely explained. Existing frameworks describe resistance, resilience, functional redundancy, social evolution, and ecological networks, but do not explicitly define how demonstrated protective effects are distributed among community members or whether this distribution predicts stability beyond diversity, composition, and functional potential. Here, we propose the Collective Ecological Protection Theory (CEPT), a systems-level framework in which stability is influenced by a protective architecture: the directed, weighted, disturbance- and response-specific network through which the activity of a provider increases the persistence or functional performance of a recipient relative to a matched counterfactual. CEPT separates protective mechanisms from their organization and identifies six candidate descriptors: protective coverage, protective redundancy, mechanistic complementarity, spatial reach, modularity, and dependency concentration. Protection is context dependent and may be weakened by spatial separation, correlated failure, costly cooperation, exploitation, or dependence on a small number of providers. We derive four discriminating predictions based on matched-community rewiring, targeted provider loss, independent protection, and architectural reconstruction during recovery. CEPT receives support to the extent that independently measured protective architecture improves causal or out-of-sample prediction of a specified stability response beyond established compositional, functional, and environmental factors. It therefore offers a testable organizational explanation for how distinct protective processes combine to influence microbial resistance, persistence, recovery, and maintenance of function. By identifying distributed protection and single points of failure, CEPT may also provide a mechanistic basis for assessing ecological vulnerability and risk in disturbed microbial systems.

items.title: Influence of habitat structure and spatial configuration on bird abundance in wet grassland patches
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding how habitat structure and spatial configuration jointly influence species abundance is critical for conserving grassland birds in fragmented landscapes. We evaluated the effects of within-patch habitat structure and patch- and landscape-scale attributes on bird abundance in wet grassland patches ranging from 3,350 to 160,207 m², embedded within natural rangelands managed under extensive livestock grazing in southern Brazil. Using complete-coverage surveys of 60 patches, we modelled abundance for 46 species across five ecological guilds, relating species-specific counts to fine-scale habitat cover, patch area, shape, isolation, and surrounding habitat amount. Within-patch habitat structure emerged as the strongest and most consistent correlate of abundance, with bog vegetation and tall graminoid cover being the most frequently retained positive predictors. Among patch- and landscape-scale predictors, patch area showed uniformly positive effects across guilds, whereas isolation, patch shape, and habitat amount in the surrounding landscape had weaker and more heterogeneous influences. Responses were guild-dependent: bog- and shrub-associated species showed the strongest relationships with internal habitat structure and patch area, while open-country generalists responded weakly or inconsistently. Landscape-scale habitat amount provided limited explanatory power beyond patch attributes. Our results highlight the importance of patch size and internal structural integrity in shaping wet-grassland bird assemblages, whereas broader landscape configuration played a comparatively minor role. Conservation strategies should therefore prioritize the maintenance of large wet-grassland patches with bog vegetation and tall graminoid structure within predominantly natural grassland mosaics under extensive livestock use.

items.title: Consuming Ourselves to Death How Consumerism Stabilises an Unsustainable Society
items.abstract: How is a peaceful coexistence amid diversity on a finite planet possible? This article addresses this question through a cultural and social analysis of consumerism. Consumerism is interpreted not only as an objective of modernisation but also as a mechanism for stabilising societies characterised by social inequality, status competition, and weak forms of democracy. Since the globalisation of the Western model of development has led to a permanent war among human beings and against nature, a way out cannot lie in defending this model, but rather in its sustainable transformation. Alongside cultural change, social relations and democracy must be placed on new foundations, building bridges instead of walls.

items.title: From Agricultural Residue to Aviation Fuel: Classifying Oil Palm Trunk (OPT) and Reassessing Its Carbon, Sustainability and Policy Consequences
items.abstract: This qualitative literature review critically examines the proposed classification of oil palm trunk (OPT) as an agricultural residue and its implications for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) development. Anchored in Indonesia’s October 2026 CAEP/14 policy agenda, it differentiates regulatory feedstock designation from lifecycle carbon intensity, physical sustainability and certification eligibility. A critical thematic synthesis of 55 peer-reviewed articles published during 2020–2026, complemented by ICAO policy documents, identifies five interacting issues: the economic definition of residue; the boundary between assigned indirect land-use change treatment and actual core lifecycle assessment; the effects of trunk extraction on soil organic carbon, nutrients and counterfactual biomass management; uncertainties in feedstock logistics and conversion technologies; and traceability, social inclusion and avoidance of double counting. The review argues that an assigned zero ILUC value is neither a measured zero-emission result nor a substitute for actual LCA. It proposes a five-gate assessment architecture—regulatory recognition, ecological extraction, engineering validation, carbon accounting and independent assurance—and a phased Indonesian evidence roadmap. Findings support carefully conditioned residue utilisation, accompanied by representative plantation trials, technology-specific assessments, auditable supply chains and safeguards for smallholders. Neither OPT classification approval nor a default OPT lifecycle emissions value is presumed as of 15 October 2026.

items.title: Extended cubs’ care helping as a factor of reproductive success in a resident Golden jackal (Canis aureus Linnaeus, 1758) family group
items.abstract: A resident Golden jackal family behaviour was studied over eight years (2017-2024) and especially over two successive post-birth seasons (May-September) in 2023 and 2024, utilising stationary bait-site camera-trap recordings on the Bulgarian bank of the Danube River. Earlier research on the cooperative breeding in golden jackals suggests that the cubs are typically cared for by the breeding pair and possibly by young helpers (1+/ 2+ years old). However, here we show that the presence of an adult, non-breeding helper (‘uncle’) can be systematic, helping the breeding female for several years, thus replacing the father, who, in our case, did not seem to contribute in the care for the young. Our observations also suggest repeated instances of food sharing by the non-breeding senior male adult, directed towards junior adults (last year’s jackals). Furthermore, food sharing behaviour amongst junior adults and towards the cubs was also recorded. Our data help revealing a more extended presence of ’helpers’ than is traditionally described in literature, with more than one or two junior adults remaining with the group to assist the breeding female during the denning period. This extended helping behaviour may contribute to the resilience of jackal family groups, particularly in contexts of pronounced hunting pressure, as is the case within our study area. We conclude that this specific behaviour, amongst other factors, may help to explain the demographic success in the European Golden jackal and with this, its significant recent expansion beyond its traditional habitats.

items.title: Engytatus passionarius (Hemiptera: Miridae), a Potential Biological Control Agent of the Invasive Vine Passiflora foetida (Passifloraceae) in Australia
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Passiflora foetida senso lato L. (Passifloraceae), native to the Americas, is an invasive vine impacting areas of environmental, economic, cultural and social importance across northern Australia. The leaf‐sucking mirid, Engytatus passionarius Minghetti, Maestro and Dellapé (Hemiptera: Miridae), was recently described and identified as a potential biological control agent of P. foetida following native range surveys in northwestern Argentina. Its biology and host range were investigated in Argentina and under quarantine in Australia to assess its suitability for release. Host specificity was initially evaluated in the native range through field host range observations, laboratory studies assessing zoophagy and no‐choice tests on available Passiflora species. These studies indicated a high level of specificity to P. foetida , supporting further evaluation in Australian quarantine. Comprehensive no‐choice host specificity testing included 31 plant species selected based on their phylogenetic relationships to the target weed spanning the Passifloraceae, Salicaceae, Achariaceae, Violaceae, Euphorbiaceae and Phyllanthaceae. Feeding, oviposition and successful development to adulthood occurred consistently on P. foetida . Survival rates were significantly higher on the target weed than on nontarget plant species, where individuals experienced markedly increased mortality. Feeding on nontarget plants was generally low and exploratory, whereas consistent vegetative damage occurred on P. foetida . Developmental success for the mirid was also substantially reduced on nontargets (mean 0.2–4.6 F1 adults) compared with P. foetida (mean 52.5 F1 adults). Six nontarget Passiflora species were further evaluated in choice tests. E. passionarius consistently preferred P. foetida , initiating feeding more rapidly and producing higher nymph densities than on nontarget species. Completion of the life cycle occurred only on P. foetida . Overall, results from native‐range studies, quarantine experiments and field observations demonstrate that E. passionarius is highly host‐specific to P. foetida and represents a promising candidate for biological control in Australia.

items.title: Controlling Nitrogen Removalfrom Urban WastewaterinConstructedWetlands withNativeVegetationin Beijing
items.abstract: Excess nitrogen in urban wastewater effluent exacerbates eutrophication in water bodies, whereas nutrient-rich effluents can be reused for beneficial purposes, such as irrigation and agriculture. Therefore, controlling nitrogen removal is essential to meet water discharge quality standards and support sustainable water management, aligning with Sustainable Development Goal 6, which states to improve water quality, wastewater treatment, and safe reuse. This study investigates the control of nitrogen removal in urban wastewater using vertical flow constructed wetlands (VFCWs) with three native plants in Beijing: Phragmites communis, Typha orientalis, and Acorus calamus, pumice as substrates, and a COD/N ratio of 15/1. The objective is to identify the most suitable plant for producing effluent that meets key standards for water reuse. Synthetic influent was derived from a modified Hoagland solution. Water quality parameters, including dissolved oxygen, ammonium nitrogen concentration, nitrate nitrogen concentration, and total nitrogen, were continuously monitored over 17 days. Results showed that all three plant species significantly reduced the ammonium nitrogen concentration, with Typha orientalis performing the best. Due to the limited oxygen and short stabilization time, there is less nitrification and denitrification; therefore, the paper concludes that nitrogen removal is achieved through phytoremediation and pumice absorption. While the effluent quality met the criteria for reuse in urban landscaping, it did not meet the standard for discharge into the environment. The findings suggest that with improved system design, such as longer stabilization and added aeration, VFCWs could serve as a sustainable wastewater management solution.

items.title: Tropical peatland microbiomes as a One Health nexus: linking soil, plant, and climate health across land-use transitions
items.abstract: The One Health framework recognizes the intrinsic connections among environmental, plant, animal and human health. While soils and soil microbes have received substantial attention in the recent years, tropical peatlands still remain largely overlooked despite representing globally important reservoirs of carbon, biodiversity, freshwater. Microorganisms are central regulators of peat accumulation, nutrient cycling, greenhouse gas exchange and ecosystem resilience, yet their role as mediators of One Health outcomes has received limited attention. Emerging evidence from tropical peatlands demonstrates that land-use change, drainage, fire and agricultural conversion substantially alter microbial community composition and function, with cascading effects on ecosystem processes. In this Perspective, peatland microbiomes are proposed as critical but neglected One Health nexus linking soil health, vegetation dynamics, wildlife habitat quality, climate regulation and human wellbeing. Considering, oil palm plantations that produce the most consumed vegetable oil in the world, cover substantial portion of tropical peatlands, tropical peat also plays a crucial role in food security and safety. The perspective argues that microbial communities should move from being considered ecological indicators to becoming policy-relevant components of peatland governance. Furthermore, incorporation of microbiome informed indicators into restoration, carbon accounting and ecosystem health frameworks is proposed as a necessity. By integrating microbial ecology with One Health principles, tropical peatlands can serve as an impactful model system for understanding how belowground biodiversity underpins ecosystem services and planetary health.

items.title: Soil-Dwelling Insect Diversity Along a Post-Mining Recovery Gradient: Associations with Soil Chemical Properties and Mercury Contamination
items.abstract: Gold mining removes vegetation and topsoil, often leaving mercury (Hg) in the soil. However, the recovery of soil insects on mined land is poorly documented because soil macrofauna are usually analyzed as a single group. This study examined soil-dwelling insects along a time-since-mining gradient in an artisanal gold mining landscape in Dharmasraya Regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, and related them to soil chemical properties. Four land-use conditions on Ultisols were compared from January to March 2026: active mining, 5-year and 10-year ex-mining land, and secondary forest. Insects were hand-sorted from three 30 cm × 30 cm × 20 cm monoliths per condition and identified to family level, and soil pH, organic carbon, total nitrogen, C/N ratio, and Hg were analyzed. In total, 51 insects from 11 families and five orders were found, none of them on active mining land. The number of families rose from 4 to 8 and 11, and the Shannon-Wiener index from 1.27 to 1.81 and 2.24, at 5 years, 10 years, and in the forest. Ants dominated recovering sites, but their share fell from 44.4% to 25.9%. Diversity correlated positively with organic carbon (r = 0.98) and negatively with Hg (r = −0.97), although these exploratory results rest on four land uses. Family-level insect indicators may support monitoring of rehabilitation on gold-mined land.

items.title: Environmental occurrence of the algal morphogen thallusin and identification of Algoriphagus species as producers in the Baltic Sea (Kiel Fjord, Germany)
items.abstract: Marine macroalgae rely on interactions with associated bacteria for growth and development. In Ulva species, bacterial morphogens such as thallusin are essential for normal morphogenesis, yet their occurrence in natural coastal environments remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated spatial and seasonal variation in thallusin-associated morphogenetic activity in the Kiel Fjord (southwestern Baltic Sea, Germany) by combining bioassays with environmental analyses, microbiome profiling, UHPLC–HRMS, and bacterial culture experiments. Sterile-filtered seawater collected at 32 stations during spring, summer, and autumn was tested for its ability to induce normal morphogenesis in axenic Ulva compressa germlings. A morphogenetic index (MI), representing thallusin-associated activity, showed pronounced spatial and seasonal variation, with significantly higher activity in summer than in autumn. MI was positively associated with temperature and negatively associated with salinity and nitrite concentration. Targeted UHPLC–HRMS analysis confirmed thallusin in coastal seawater, with a concentration of 0.66 ± 0.21 nmol L - ¹ determined in a sample from a site exhibiting consistently high morphogenetic activity. Exploratory microbiome screening identified several bacterial genera as candidate producers. Subsequent culture-based bioassays and chemical analyses demonstrated thallusin production by four Algoriphagus species, all of which induced the characteristic morphogenetic phenotype, cell wall and rhizoid formation, in U. compressa . Together, these results provide the first direct evidence of thallusin in coastal seawater and expand the known diversity of thallusin-producing bacteria to members of the genus Algoriphagus . By linking environmental bioassays with chemical detection and experimental validation of bacterial producers, this study paves the way for investigating the environmental dynamics and ecological functions of bacterial morphogens in macroalgal–microbial interactions.

items.title: Diversified crop rotation reshapes soil nutrients, microbial communities, and functions in sorghum fields
items.abstract: Introduction Long-term continuous sorghum cropping degrades soil environments and causes continuous cropping obstacles. This study investigated whether diversified crop rotation can maintain soil health and improve the soil microenvironment for sorghum growth. Methods Using continuous sorghum cropping as the control (SSS), three rotation systems were established: sorghum-potato-sorghum (SPS), sorghum-common vetch-sorghum (SVS), and sorghum-green pea shoots-sorghum (SGS). Soil physicochemical properties, microbial community structure and diversity were analyzed using Illumina NovaSeq high-throughput sequencing, and functional traits were predicted using FAPROTAX and FUNGuild. Mantel tests and co-occurrence network analysis were also performed. Results All three rotation treatments improved soil physicochemical properties to varying degrees, with SPS showing the greatest nutrient enhancement. SVS markedly increased bacterial richness and diversity, while SPS significantly enhanced fungal richness and diversity. β-diversity analysis revealed that rotation treatments differed significantly from SSS, with SVS and SGS showing similar bacterial structures and SPS and SVS showing similar fungal structures. Functionally important microbial groups increased in rotation soils, whereas the pathogenic genus Fusarium remained relatively high in SPS. Mantel tests indicated that soil pH, TN, TP, TK, and AK were key factors influencing microbial community structure, with AK showing the strongest correlation. Nitrogen fixation and cellulose degradation were the dominant bacterial functions, while saprotrophic and ectomycorrhizal fungi were enriched in rotation soils. Co-occurrence network analysis showed that the rotation network had higher average degree, network density, modularity, and a larger connected component than the continuous cropping network. Discussion These findings indicate that diversified crop rotation effectively elevates soil nutrient levels, reshapes microbial community structure and ecological functions, and supports high-quality and stable sorghum production.

items.title: A curated global checklist of polychaetes (Annelida) from deep‑sea chemosynthetic and reducing habitats
items.abstract: Deep‑sea chemosynthetic and reducing habitats, including hydrothermal vents, cold seeps, methane seeps, whale falls, wood falls, organic falls and other reducing sedimentary environments, represent key systems for deep‑sea biodiversity research. Polychaetes are a species‑rich and taxonomically well‑studied benthic group in these environments. However, relevant records are scattered across taxonomic papers, regional surveys, ecological studies, monographs, reviews and databases. No dedicated global dataset is currently available with unified taxonomic validation, habitat coding and literature provenance. This paper introduces a publicly released curated global checklist dataset of polychaetes from deep‑sea chemosynthetic and reducing habitats (version 1.0.1). Compiled from published literature, the dataset harmonises scientific names, accepted names under the World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS), AphiaIDs, LSIDs and taxonomic status. The dataset is archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22011206) and contains 368 checklist‑level taxonomic records, amongst which 363 records are included in core statistics according to the 'includeInCoreStatistics' field. It provides taxonomic hierarchies, WoRMS identifiers, standardised and raw habitat descriptions, locality information, source references, plus taxonomic and ecological notes. Supplementary materials include a reference table, habitat controlled vocabulary, field dictionary, README, CITATION file, licence and version history. The dataset supports taxonomic syntheses, global‑ or regional‑scale biodiversity overviews, broad‑scale habitat‑association analyses and subsequent compilation of occurrence‑level data. It is not suitable for fine‑scale species distribution modelling, station‑level community analyses or sampling‑effort‑corrected richness estimation.

items.title: Niche Occupation and Rapid Adaptation Mechanisms of Invasive Guppies in Polluted Water Bodies
items.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are facing a global biodiversity crisis and biological invasion crisis at the same time. The guppy (Poecilia reticulata) is one of the most invasive fish species worldwide. It can successfully live in polluted water, providing a good model for studying eco-evolutionary processes of rapid adaptation and ecological niche occupation. This paper reviews the progress of ecological niche occupation and rapid adaptation mechanisms of invasive guppies in polluted waters. Existing research shows that the guppy can have its native range from South America to almost 70 countries in the world, and it often affects native species, such as resource competition, reproductive interference and changes in ecological functions. A polluted environment is conducive to rapid adaptation of guppy with multi-level, including life-history characteristics (transformation to an r-selection strategy), sexually selected characteristics (change and microevolution of sexually selected characteristics such as ornamental colors), the molecular-level variation or response (for example, CYP1A gene selection, transcriptome changes).On the other hand, the rapid adaptation of guppies, in turn, favours their niche occupation, giving rise to a positive feedback loop of "pollution→adaptation→invasion persistence". Currently, this field still has deficiencies in the balance of geographic coverage and the degree of contributions from phenotypic plasticity and genetic adaptation. This paper suggests that future studies should strengthen the cross-regional comparison and utilize genomic methods to integrate with field ecological observations to provide a scientific basis for the governance of invasion of polluted waters.

items.title: Checklist of threatened plants of Sabah, Malaysian Borneo
items.abstract: Covering approximately 10% of Borneo’s land area, Sabah is one of the global hotspots for plant biodiversity, yet it faces increasing threats to its flora due to habitat loss and exploitation. This paper aims to compile a comprehensive checklist of threatened plant species in Sabah based on assessments published in the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. A total of 660 vascular plant species from 73 families and 199 genera are classified as threatened and compiled in this checklist. Of these, 71 species are listed as Critically Endangered, 169 are Endangered, and 420 are Vulnerable. The high-value timber family Dipterocarpaceae, with 101 species from eight genera, has the highest number of threatened species. Notably, the genus Shorea contributes 44 species, the highest among all other genera. Around 76% of these threatened species are endemic to Borneo, including 239 species that are endemic to Sabah. Despite recent assessment efforts, only 39% of Sabah’s plant species have been evaluated under the IUCN Red List, and non-seed plants are severely underrepresented. This checklist provides essential data to inform conservation planning and policy in Sabah, underscoring the urgent need for continued assessment and protection of its unique plant diversity.

items.title: 2026 AOS Early Professional Awards to Devon DeRaad, Fengyi Guo, and Olivia M. Smith
items.abstract: The American Ornithological Society (AOS) annually bestows research awards honoring early-career researchers for their ornithological research. The AOS’s James G. Cooper Early Professional Award and the Ned K. Johnson Early Investigator Award are presented annually to recognize outstanding and promising work by researchers early in their careers. Our 2026 James G. Cooper Award winners are Devon DeRaad and Fengyi Guo. For 2026, the AOS awarded the Ned K. Johnson Award to Olivia M. Smith. Dr. Devon DeRaad is a La Kretz Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of California, Los Angeles. He earned his Ph.D. in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology from the University of Kansas in 2024 and his B.A. in Biology from Occidental College in 2017. Dr. DeRaad is an evolutionary genomicist whose research seeks to understand how speciation and extinction generate and maintain global biodiversity. His work integrates genomic, phenotypic, behavioral, and ecological data from bird populations worldwide, with a particular focus on island systems that provide natural laboratories for studying the full “life cycle” of species—from early divergence to hybridization and extinction risk. His research has helped resolve longstanding questions about rapid diversification, hybrid zone dynamics, and phylogenomic discordance in birds, including influential studies of kingfishers, scrub-jays, grosbeaks, and white-eyes. Dr. DeRaad has co-authored 30 peer-reviewed publications (12 as lead author), including papers in Science, Evolution, and Systematic Biology, and has secured more than $600,000 in competitive funding, including an NSF Postdoctoral Research Fellowship in Biology.

items.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission
items.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevant biological context. A domain-specific ontology organizes 14 evidence types into five categories: Zoonotic Surveillance, Transmission Evidence, Experimental Infection, Functional Mechanism, and Genomic Evolution. The platform integrates ontology-guided curation, large language model-assisted literature screening and candidate extraction, automated consistency checks, and curator review of flagged or ambiguous records, enabling daily updates. As of 4 August 2026, OmniVira contained 8072 publicly retrievable OVE records derived from 2623 source articles, spanning 60 ICTV virus families, 55 host orders, and 121 countries. Its responsive interface supports evidence-centred retrieval, source-text verification, and exploration of linked virus-host-literature relationships across desktop and mobile browsers. OmniVira provides a transparent, context-preserving resource for systematic comparison and synthesis of evidence related to zoonotic viral emergence and cross-species transmission.

items.title: A species distribution model integrating at-sea behaviour, phenology, and population size to inform marine risk exposure for a threatened seabird during breeding
items.abstract: Seabirds face myriad threats on land and at sea resulting in widespread population declines. Predictive species distribution models (SDMs) provide a powerful tool to estimate numbers of birds exposed to risks, and to attribute them to source populations. The Atlantic population of Leach’s Storm-petrel ( Hydrobates leucorhous ) has declined rapidly in recent decades; however, information on their exposure to threats at sea is lacking. We address this knowledge gap for the breeding period using a multi-year GPS tracking dataset ( n = 451 birds, 2016-2023) collected from six colonies which together comprise > 90% of the Atlantic population. As threat exposure can differ according to behaviour, we used a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to classify behavioural states and define associated risk categories (primarily in-air or on-water). We also summarized results by time of day because attraction to, and disorientation from, artificial light at night (ALAN) poses risks to Leach’s Storm-petrels. We developed a dynamic SDM predicting monthly relative densities at sea (June-September), for the western North Atlantic regional population, accounting for all 16 colonies with > 10,000 individuals. Reflecting geographic patterns in colony size, regional densities were highest east of Newfoundland in deepwater areas off the northern Grand Bank (Orphan Basin and Flemish Pass), and south of the Flemish Cap (Newfoundland Basin). At-sea densities increased through summer, being lowest in June when one parent is incubating, and highest in September when both parents forage at sea. Case studies indicated that relative to risks within Grand Bank oil and gas production areas, commencement of deepwater drilling in the Orphan Basin and Flemish Pass has substantially increased risks for Leach's Storm-petrels, because bird densities in these offshore areas are 2–4 times higher. Within our region, risks from ALAN were consistently estimated to be higher than risks from hypothetical oil spills. Though offshore facilities have been removed from the Scotian Shelf, ongoing bids for exploration licences suggest future risks for specific populations in Nova Scotia. We focused on oil and gas; however, our framework can be applied to other individual or cumulative risks to inform conservation planning for this threatened species.
