items.title: Microplastics in gastropod molluscs: a review of contamination trends in global studies
items.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have become a global concern due to their persistence in the environment and their harmful effects on ecosystems, infrastructure, society, and the economy, warranting immediate attention and action. Ecotoxicological impacts of MPs are significant, as they tend to infiltrate food chains, facilitating the trophic transfer of MPs and associated contaminants, and potentially endangering human health. The isolation and characterisation of MPs can be improved, enabling science to elucidate their fate in organisms. Molluscs are among the major groups affected by MP contamination, which can serve as vectors for the biomagnification of pollutants within aquatic food webs. This review demonstrates the global distribution, types, and chemical nature of MP contamination in molluscs. It summarises the different types of MPs reported from various molluscan species and compiles a detailed review table based on existing studies. Current research indicates that gastropods inhabiting diverse aquatic ecosystems, including freshwater, mangrove, marine, coastal, estuarine, brackish water, and semi-enclosed marine environments, are under threat of MP contamination. Studies also show that mangrove ecosystems appear to be the most heavily affected, with gastropods showing a high number of MP particles per individual. Fibres and fragments are the most commonly detected forms of MPs in gastropods, and smaller particles are more frequently ingested due to their size. A trend was observed in both MP contamination level and MP abundance, with larger gastropod species exhibiting higher MP loads than smaller species. The widespread presence of MPs in gastropod molluscs raises serious ecological concerns and highlights potential risks of human exposure through trophic transfer in the food chain. Hence, this review helps clarify contamination levels and highlights the importance of further research and management to control MP pollution.

items.title: How energy-transition technologies acquire media meaning: a systematic review of framing configurations and the media construction of socio-technical legitimacy
items.abstract: Research on media framing of energy-transition technologies has expanded across technologies and national contexts, but cumulative comparison remains difficult since studies conceptualize and operationalize “frames” in markedly different ways. This systematic review synthesizes 93 peer-reviewed studies of journalistic and news-media coverage to examine recurring framing structures, cross-technology and cross-national variation, temporal dynamics, and the explanatory capacity of existing designs. An iterative, theoretically informed harmonization identifies eight substantive frame domains: technofunctional performance, material-economic viability, ecological-climate consequences, governance-institutional capacity, energy-system security and geopolitics, health and safety, social-distributive justice, and socio-cultural or place-based compatibility. These domains are analytically distinct from evaluative orientation, transition-pathway positioning, and communicative form. Comparative evidence shows recognizable interpretive repertoires across technologies, but their salience, orientation, and linkage vary across energy systems, policy trajectories, implementation stages, journalistic settings, and event periods. The literature accumulates descriptive patterns more securely than independent technology, country, policy, or event effects. This study therefore proposes a review-derived framework for analyzing the media construction of socio-technical legitimacy as legitimacy-relevant representation rather than an audience or institutional outcome. Cumulative progress requires strategically comparable designs that distinguish substantive domain, orientation, pathway position, sponsorship, and journalistic organization.

items.title: Untapped potential: phosphorus recovery and reuse options from livestock manure and rendering by-products in the EU-27
items.abstract: Mismanagement of the animal by-products (ABPs) pig slurry, poultry manure and rendered by-products poses serious environmental problems. The need to reduce environmental impacts such as eutrophication caused by livestock farming has prompted European Union (EU) policymakers to introduce policies and strategies for more sustainable management of nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) and to improve the recirculation of P in agricultural systems. The above-mentioned ABPs represent an important source of phosphorus for reuse purposes. As a result, there is increasing interest in developing and promoting treatment processes and technologies that sustainably transform ABPs into valuable resources for use as agricultural inputs. This study explores the potential of recirculating P from pig slurry, poultry manure, and rendered by-products through existing treatment processes and technologies that convert ABPs into nutrient-balanced bio-based products (BBPs) such as compost, biochar, ash, struvite, bone ash, and animal bone char. Based on data obtained from relevant literature and databases, we computed the amount of manure and rendered by-products generated annually within the EU 27 from pig slurry, poultry deep litter, and slaughterhouse wastes, and the P derived from these ABPs including the amount of plant-available P in the BBPs. We also analyzed the application rate of the different BBPs in relation to the commonly applied mineral P-fertilizer diammonium phosphate (DAP). The results show that pig slurry and poultry deep litter are important sources of P in the EU-27, yielding annual P output averages of 170,000 tonnes from pig slurry, and 1,067,000 tonnes from poultry deep litter. Furthermore, our modeling shows that the field application rate of animal bone char (ABC) (74–131 kg/ha/yr) is highly comparable with that of traditional DAP (77–107 kg/ha/yr). This is an indication that ABC is an attractive and promising P-fertilizer option to consider from an environmental standpoint in the development of a more sustainable and circular agricultural system that does not depend exclusively on imported inorganic P-fertilizers. However, innovative incentives, techniques, and policies are needed to overcome economic and technical challenges affecting the introduction of ABC to the market.

items.title: Robust and cost-effective quantum network using Kramers-Kronig receiver
items.abstract: The quantum internet holds the potential to facilitate applications that are fundamentally inaccessible to the classical internet. Among its most prominent applications is quantum key distribution (QKD) networks, which connect two distant nodes to establish a secure key based on the principles of quantum mechanics. However, the subsequent extensive reliance on interferences in existing QKD protocols leads to the weak robustness of the system and the corresponding network. In this work, we propose a robust and cost-effective quantum network using the Kramers-Kronig receiver. We first propose a continuous-variable QKD protocol based on direct detection without interference, which achieves the recovery of quadrature components through the Kramers-Kronig relation. Subsequently, we have extended this protocol to continuous-variable quantum access networks, further highlighting the robustness and cost advantages of interference-free detection. The experimental results show that each user can achieve a secret key rate at 50 kbit/s within the access network range by using only one photodetector without interference structures. This scheme opens up new possibilities in establishing a robust and cost-effective quantum network, serving as a foundational element in the progress toward establishing a large-scale quantum internet.

items.title: Simultaneous determination of the Hubble constant and cosmic baryon density: Forecasts for the synergy between FRBs and emerging probes
items.abstract: Two of the most pressing challenges in cosmology are the persistent discrepancy in measurements of the Hubble constant, referred to as the Hubble tension, and the deficit of baryons in the local Universe, known as the missing baryon problem. Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide a unique probe of both the Hubble constant $H_0$ and the cosmic baryon density $Ω_{\rm b}$. However, constraints from FRBs alone suffer from a severe $H_0$-$Ω_{\rm b}$ degeneracy that prevents them from resolving either problem. We show that this degeneracy can be broken by combining FRBs with other emerging probes whose degeneracy directions differ in the $H_0$-$Ω_{\rm b}$ plane. Specifically, we quantify three multi-messenger approaches: FRBs paired with gravitational wave (GW) standard sirens, strong gravitational lensing (SGL) time delays, and 21 cm intensity mapping (IM) surveys. The combinations FRB+GW, FRB+SGL, and FRB+21 cm IM each deliver simultaneous constraints on $H_0$ and $Ω_{\rm b}$ better than (1%, 1.5%) in the $Λ$CDM model, and when dynamical dark energy is introduced, the constraining precision degrades gracefully as model complexity increases. Furthermore, within a model-independent framework, both FRB+GW and FRB+SGL constrain $H_0$ and $Ω_{\rm b}$ to precisions better than (1.5%, 3%). These precision levels are based on nominal observational expectations and would improve significantly under optimistic observational scenarios.

items.title: On the relation between magnetic field strength and gas density in the interstellar medium. II. Density uncertainties and diffuse gas constraints
items.abstract: The relationship between magnetic field strength and gas density is essential to understand the interstellar medium and star formation. Zeeman measurements in dense atomic and molecular gas phases have traditionally been used to directly probe magnetic field strengths in the Milky Way. This allowed derivation of a relationship between magnetic field strength B and gas number density n . We recently generalized this relation as a two-part power-law with non-zero slopes and a transition density given as B / B 0 ∝ ( n / n 0 ) α 1 for n ≤ n 0 and ( n / n 0 ) α 2 for n > n 0 . Here, we extend our previous hierarchical Bayesian framework by incorporating a large body of pulsar observations that probe the diffuse interstellar medium and explicitly modelling density uncertainties through a log-density intrinsic scatter R n applied to all densities. We also account for magnetic field geometry and measurement uncertainties through a magnetic hyperparameter to estimate B . This results in a stronger constraint on the diffuse gas part of the B – n relation. Our results confirm a non-zero exponent in the diffuse gas and a broad transition density with our best model and data set yielding maximum a posteriori results of α 1 = 0.20 − 0.03 + 0.01 , α 2 = 0.65 − 0.07 + 0.06 , n 0 = 3330 − 3220 + 270 cm − 3 , and B 0 = 10.11 − 5.97 + 0.71 μ G .

items.title: Using global gravitational potential weighted correlation function to constrain modified gravity models
items.abstract: We propose a new marked two-point correlation function weighted by the global gravitational potential as a probe for testing gravity models. Using the LCDM model based on general relativity (GR) as a reference, we investigate two representative modified gravity (MG) scenarios: f(R) gravity and nDGP. The mark used in this work, the global gravitational potential that is reconstructed from the galaxy distribution via the Poisson equation, is in contrast to the local property based mark (e.g., local galaxy number density or gravitational potential of host halo) used in previous studies. By applying two weighting schemes to quantify environment-dependent clustering, we find that this statistic is able to distinguish MG models from GR, with the signal being enhanced in regions corresponding to particular ranges of gravitational potential. These results indicate that the proposed statistic can serve as a useful complement to conventional clustering probes in future surveys, once observational effects and modeling uncertainties are properly taken into account.

items.title: Eclipse Properties and Superhump Evolution in the SU UMa-type Dwarf Nova Z Cha
items.abstract: Abstract The advent of large-scale time-domain surveys provides both opportunities and challenges for understanding accretion disk evolution in cataclysmic variables (CVs). Using high-cadence photometry from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), we investigate the eclipsing SU UMa-type dwarf nova Z Cha. Leveraging eclipses as a natural probe, we examine the evolution of the accretion disk through variations in eclipse depth, O – C of eclipse minima, and positive superhump (PSH) amplitude. During superoutbursts, all three quantities exhibit quasiperiodic modulations with a common period of ∼2 days, consistent with the precession period of an eccentric disk. We interpret these correlated variations as evidence of an eccentric, precessing disk: O – C traces the periodic shift of the system’s brightness center, while eclipse depth and PSH amplitude vary with the orientation of the disk bulge relative to the line of sight. In quiescence (Sectors 13 and 93), PSHs with periods of ∼0.0762 days show linearly decreasing amplitudes and periods, indicating gradual shrinkage of the eccentric disk and a slowing precession. Remarkably, a coherent signal with a period of ∼0.0729 days ( ϵ − ≈ −0.02) appears in the same quiescent intervals. This signal may represent negative superhumps (NSHs) coexisting with PSHs, although an orbital sideband of the PSH cannot presently be excluded with the available data. If confirmed as NSHs, their coexistence with PSHs would challenge the classical tilted-disk model, and could be explained by retrograde apsidal precession of an eccentric disk, where the inner disk precesses retrogradely (NSHs) and the outer disk progradely (PSHs); this interpretation remains to be tested by further observations.

items.title: Dark matter interpretation of the Super-Kamiokande antineutrino excess and predictions for JUNO
items.abstract: Super-Kamiokande has reported a small excess of electron antineutrino events in the 20 MeV energy range, in the search for the diffuse supernova neutrino background. We interpret this signal as a possible indication of dark matter that annihilates dominantly into neutrinos, pointing to a thermal dark matter candidate with s s -wave annihilation and with mass in the tens of MeV range. This mass scale naturally fits into rich dark sector extensions of the Standard Model. Neutrino experiments, including JUNO, will be able to test this hypothesis in the coming years.

items.title: GraphShed: A Data-derived Graph-based Watershed Group-finder
items.abstract: Abstract This study introduces GraphShed, a data-derived group-finder that applies top-down watershed segmentation to Voronoi-induced graphs, identifying galaxy systems directly from the density field via a GraphShed-derived linking length, with no density thresholds or tunable parameters. A GraphShed galaxy group catalog compared to a friends-of-friends (FoF) catalog is built from the IllustrisTNG100-1 simulation with a box size of ∼75 Mpc h −1 yielding 1067 and 987 systems, respectively. The GraphShed-derived linking length adapts to the global clustering power of the sample, varying by ∼18% relative to FoF across different sample selections; thus, catalog differences originate in the watershed segmentation. A cross-catalog comparison shows that ∼58% of FoF systems are identically reproduced by GraphShed, ∼5% are completely removed, and the remainder are partially shaved and/or split into multiple systems. While the M 200 distributions of the two catalogs are statistically consistent, other structural properties including, R 200 , sphericity, compactness, spin, and centroid shift, differ significantly in at least some richness ranges. The unweighted two-point correlation function of GraphShed systems exhibits a higher amplitude on small scales, r ≲ 1 Mpc h −1 and agrees with FoF for r ≳ 5 Mpc h −1 . A velocity-based classification reveals that GraphShed resolves more interacting pairs than FoF, demonstrating its ability to distinguish nearby overdense structures that position-only methods merge into single systems. These results demonstrate that GraphShed preserves cosmological statistics while providing a more resolved detection of galaxy systems and their dynamical interactions.

items.title: Unravelling the Role of Stacking Disorder on the Optoelectronic Properties of Zn3P2
items.abstract: Abstract Zinc phosphide (Zn3P2) is a promising photovoltaic absorber for thin-film and flexible solar cells due to its earth-abundant composition and favourable optoelectronic properties. Recent advances in epitaxy have enabled the growth of high-quality Zn3P2 thin films despite the challenges posed by its incompatible lattice parameter and thermal expansion coefficient. However, Zn3P2 remains prone to intrinsic extended defects, such as rotated domains, that can limit device performance. Here, using (scanning) transmission electron microscopy, we identify a class of extended defects that appear as planar faults described by displacement vectors lying in the (001) plane. Within a pseudo-cubic description of Zn3P2, we establish a direct correspondence between planar faults and rotated domains, showing that both arise from the flexible ordering of vacant sites in the Zn sublattice. First-principles calculations reveal an extremely low planar-defect formation energy of 2.5 mJ m−2, demonstrating that these defects form at essentially negligible energetic cost, in excellent agreement with their high experimentally observed occurrence. Additional density functional theory calculations show that the studied intrinsic planar defects neither introduce mid-gap electronic states nor significantly perturb the local electrostatic potential, indicating that they are electronically benign. Our results suggest that any connection between the observed planar defects and a reduction in device performance must therefore involve indirect mechanisms, such as strain effects or interactions with other defects.

items.title: Non-thermal emission in jets and winds: Expected emission and spectral index distributions
items.abstract: Abstract The origin of synchrotron emission in compact radio sources associated with active galactic nuclei (AGN) remains poorly understood. In a series of papers, we have examined diagnostic tools to disentangle the dominant underlying processes. In this study, we investigate the in situ evolution of cosmic-ray electrons (CREs) in compact AGN jets and winds, and examine how their evolution shapes the resulting observable radio properties. In jets, CREs experience multiple shock interactions as they propagate along the spine toward the hotspot and flow into the cocoon via backflows. In winds, CREs are predominantly accelerated at the Mach disc, with occasional re-acceleration within turbulent cocoon backflows. The continuous mixing of different CRE populations within the cocoon produces observational signatures that cannot be inferred from instantaneous conditions alone. In all jet simulations, spectral indices are flattest near the hotspot and steepen progressively away from the hotspots. In winds, spectra steepen with increasing distance from the Mach disc, with this trend becoming more pronounced at high radio frequencies due to radiative losses. We find the Mach disc to be a significantly more efficient CRE acceleration site than the forward shock in winds, which weakens as the wind expands to large scales. Since morphology, especially at low resolution, can be ambiguous for compact sources, spatially resolved spectral indices, particularly when combined with emission and polarization signatures, can provide a powerful diagnostic.

items.title: Searching for population III stars with line intensity mapping cross-correlations
items.abstract: Decades of searches for Population III stars in individual galaxies have yielded a few potential candidates, but a statistically robust characterization of the demographics of the first stars in the lowest-mass systems remains elusive. Line intensity mapping (LIM), an observational technique that measures fluctuations in the aggregate emission from the entire galaxy population --- including the faintest sources --- offers an alternative strategy that is especially well-suited for the Pop III era. With the recent launch of SPHEREx and the rapid development of a number of complementary LIM studies, we are poised to place some of the first LIM constraints on sites of star formation at high-redshift. In this work, we expand an analytical model for LIM power spectra, Zeus21/oLIMpus, to include Pop III stars and the emission lines identified as diagnostic signatures of star formation with a low-metallicity, top-heavy IMF, such as H$α$ and HeII. We introduce a flexible framework to estimate the measurement uncertainties associated with instrument and survey configurations, and apply these to study LIM signatures of the first stars in mock surveys carried out with SPHEREx and potential next-generation instruments. We quantify the sensitivity of the LIM signal to variations in Pop II and III parameters and forecast joint limits that can be placed on the Pop III star formation efficiency (SFE) and IMF shape with SPHEREx. We find that next-generation instruments will be necessary to comprehensively survey the Pop III theoretical landscape --- both with respect to `classical' and `exotic' Pop III models --- and identify design improvements that will enable such studies. Finally, we carry out a Fisher analysis to characterize synergies between SPHEREx and JWST, suggesting that joint constraints on the Pop III SFE and extensions to conventional Pop III models may be within reach.

items.title: Oscillations of dissipative neutron stars: The impact of hyperonic reaction rates
items.abstract: Tidal excitations of stellar oscillation modes during binary neutron-star inspirals offer a powerful probe of the composition of dense matter at supranuclear densities. Chemical equilibration plays a crucial, but often neglected, role in stellar perturbation calculations. If the chemical equilibration timescale is comparable to the oscillation timescale, then viscous effects can damp the modes. If the reactions are fast, some modes can completely disappear since their restoring force vanishes. Typically, these calculations, however, assume either instantaneous chemical equilibrium or no equilibration (frozen composition). Motivated by this, we investigate the effects of finite reaction rates on the oscillation spectrum of neutron stars containing hyperonic matter. We calculate the dominant non-leptonic weak interaction rates and incorporate them into the relativistic perturbation equations through a complex, frequency-dependent dynamical sound speed. We show that finite-rate effects naturally manifest as bulk-viscous dissipation, modifying the properties of both the fundamental ($f$) and gravity ($g$) modes. We further examine the impact on the tidal response by matching stellar perturbations to near-zone boundary conditions, demonstrating how viscous dissipation gives rise to a tidal lag. These results provide a consistent framework connecting microscopic reaction rates and the resulting bulk viscosity to the tidal dynamics of compact binaries, and represent a step towards incorporating viscous dissipation into gravitational-wave models of binary neutron-star inspirals.

items.title: Electron Acceleration by Turbulent Reconnection in Solar Flares
items.abstract: Abstract Solar flares can release magnetic energy explosively in the corona and produce high-energy particles on short timescales. However, how and where these particles are accelerated remains an open question. Here, we investigate the acceleration and transport of electrons during self-developed three-dimensional turbulent reconnection of solar flares by solving Parker’s transport equation in the framework of high-resolution MHD simulations. We find that thermal electrons at both the flare current sheet and loop top are rapidly accelerated up to ∼90 keV, with energy spectra exhibiting a power-law feature. Although the population of accelerated electrons at the flare loop top is larger than that at the current sheet, their spectral indices are similar, close to the values usually observed. More importantly, the acceleration is achieved by turbulence-driven compression structures of various scales rather than the supposed termination shock, particularly at the flare loop top. A portion of compression structures even forms shocks. These results highlight the critical role of turbulent reconnection in accelerating electrons, thereby shedding new light on the acceleration and transport of particles in other high-energy phenomena.

items.title: Sgr A* as a galactic PeVatron: Multimessenger signatures of the magnetic Penrose process
items.abstract: The magnetic Penrose process (MPP) is one of the most efficient mechanisms for extracting rotational energy from a magnetized Kerr black hole (BH), enabling charged particles to reach very-high energies. We investigate this process in Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*), the supermassive BH at the Galactic center (GC), focusing on its ultra-high-efficiency regime, in which neutrons undergo beta decay inside the BH ergosphere. As a key novelty, we compute the neutron production spectrum in the accretion flow directly from the nuclear reaction kinematics and follow neutron trajectories in the Kerr spacetime to determine the population that reaches the ergosphere and undergoes the MPP. From this population, we derive the spectrum of accelerated protons and show that Sgr A* can accelerate them up to PeV energies, strengthening its interpretation as a candidate Galactic PeVatron. We further compute the gamma-ray and neutrino emission produced through hadronic interactions of the escaping protons in the Central Molecular Zone. The predicted gamma-ray fluxes exhibit distinctive spectral features that could provide an observational signature of the MPP and may constitute a non-negligible contribution to the very-high-energy emission detected by H.E.S.S. and HAWC. The associated neutrino fluxes remain below the diffuse Galactic component inferred by IceCube, but may still contribute to the high-energy emission from the GC. Remarkably, the predicted signals lie within the projected sensitivity of SWGO for all scenarios considered here and, for some models, only a factor of a few below the nominal CTAO sensitivity, while KM3NeT/ARCA and IceCube-Gen2 will provide complementary tests. Our results establish the MPP as an observable mechanism for extracting BH rotational energy, providing a direct connection between horizon-scale physics and multimessenger observations that can be extended to other magnetized BHs.

items.title: Evolution of the High-energy Excess in Swift J1727.8-1613 during Its 2023 Flare State
items.abstract: Abstract We investigate the evolution of the high-energy excess in Swift J1727.8-1613 during its 2023 flare state using joint Insight-HXMT and INTEGRAL/ISGRI observations covering 2–500 keV. Fits to the broadband spectra with a model including thermal Comptonization and disk reflection leave systematic positive residuals above ∼150 keV. Adding a power-law component improves the fits and yields photon indices of Γ PL = 2.08–2.61, demonstrating that the high-energy excess beyond the thermal Comptonization continuum is present throughout the flare state. We also show that all spectra can be well described by the hybrid Comptonization model eqpair without requiring any additional high-energy component. The fitting results indicate that the energy supply to the electrons transitions from predominantly thermal heating to nonthermal acceleration, and that the electron injection spectrum steepens abruptly near the onset of the flare state. During this evolution, the radio spectral index changes from approximately zero to negative values, accompanied by the ejection of three transient jet knots. Based on this temporal association, we discuss a possible connection between the increase in nonthermal power indicated by our spectral analysis and the ejection of the transient jet.

items.title: What Drives Galaxy–Galaxy Differences in the Selective Attenuation Curve? New Perspectives from DESI DR1
items.abstract: Abstract Leveraging a sample of 3457 galaxies drawn from DESI DR1 and crossmatched with archival Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX) UV photometry, we construct new dust attenuation curves and measure how the shapes of these curves vary as a function of galaxy properties. Our curves are built by comparing the median flux densities of galaxies that have been divided into bins of nebular opacity, measured via the Balmer optical depth (i.e. the H α /H β ratio). When no further cuts on galaxy properties are applied, we find an attenuation curve very similar to previous work at low redshifts. We then test how the attenuation curves vary as a function of galaxy properties; stellar mass, specific star formation rate, metallicity, and ionization parameter. We find that the curve steepens significantly at higher specific star formation rate. In our data, there is not a clear link between the ionization parameter, mass, or metallicity and the attenuation curve slope.

items.title: Hard X-Ray Quasiperiodic Pulsations in X-class Solar Flares Observed by Aditya-L1/HEL1OS
items.abstract: Abstract We present the catalogue of quasiperiodic pulsations (QPPs) detected in hard X-ray (HXR) observations of X-class solar flares obtained with the High Energy L1 Orbiting X-ray Spectrometer (HEL1OS) instrument on board Aditya-L1 during 2024 July–2026 March. The catalogue comprises 34 flares spanning GOES classes X1.1–X7.1. QPPs are detected and studied using a uniform procedure based on ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) and wavelet analyses. Statistically significant QPPs are identified in 25 events (∼74%), demonstrating that QPPs are a common property of X-class flares. The detected periods range from approximately 1 to 3 minutes, with a pronounced concentration between 1.3 and 1.7 minutes, suggesting the existence of a preferential timescale that may be associated with kink or slow magnetohydrodynamic oscillations in the flaring region. The dominant periods remain nearly independent of photon energy across the 8–20 keV range, while the modulation depth increases systematically with photon energy following a power-law relation with an exponent of about 1.5. QPPs detected in different HXR energy channels exhibit strong phase coherence and positive cross-correlation coefficients, indicating modulation by a common physical mechanism. Several intense flares display HXR modulation depths of up to ∼25%, providing evidence for nonlinear effects. The observed statistical properties support models in which QPPs are generated by repetitive magnetic reconnection, either spontaneous or periodically modulated by magnetohydrodynamic oscillations. This study establishes HEL1OS as a powerful instrument for quantitative studies of flare QPPs during solar cycle 25.

items.title: The Role of Nonlocal Thermal Transport in Flare-driven Chromospheric Evaporation
items.abstract: Abstract Thermal conduction plays an important role in energy transport during solar flares. Flares heat the solar atmosphere to tens of megakelvins, which, combined with mean free paths in excess of 1 Mm, can cause the heat flux to become nonlocal. We use the magnetohydrodynamic Lare2d code to simulate a reconnective heating event with three different thermal conduction models: classical Spitzer–Härm (SH) along the magnetic field, local transport with a heat flux limiter (FL), and the nonlocal Schurtz–Nicolaï–Busquet (SNB) model that is routinely used in laser-plasma codes and has been benchmarked against a full Vlasov–Fokker–Planck treatment. The evolution of the atmosphere post heating is compared between simulations using each of these models. Due to a suppressed heat flux, SNB gives rise to significantly higher peak temperatures than SH. Further, with SNB transport chromospheric evaporation occurs later and has stronger extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) emission intensity. FL simulations have similar temperature evolution and chromospheric evaporation to SNB, however different values of the flux limiter work best for peak temperature, downflow velocity, and EUV emission intensity, and so there is no one optimal value for all cases. We conclude that the SNB model provides a practicable solution to incorporate nonlocal thermal transport at MHD scales, which will be crucial to improve the realism and accuracy of the next generation of solar flare simulations.

items.title: Interaction of Stellar Dipole and Disk Magnetic Fields in Accretion–Ejection Systems
items.abstract: Abstract We study jet formation from a magnetically diffusive, sub-Keplerian accretion disk threaded by different magnetic field configurations. We present two-dimensional, axisymmetric MHD simulations in spherical coordinates employing the PLUTO code. Our results show that the reference simulation, in which the disk is threaded by an initial large-scale poloidal magnetic field, reaches a quasi-steady state and produces a well-collimated jet. Both kinetic and magnetic torques are significant and evolve smoothly over time. The accretion process is established smoothly, with about 26% of the accreting material being delivered into the outflow. Alternatively, applying a purely stellar dipolar magnetic field produces weak and unstable outflows, characterized by inefficient angular momentum transport and strongly suppressed accretion. Additionally, in simulations where the stellar dipolar magnetic field is present alongside the disk’s initial poloidal magnetic field, the disk magnetic field predominantly stabilizes the system. It also facilitates angular momentum transport from the disk and sustains a significant outflow mass flux. Furthermore, we performed additional simulations that explicitly include an inner gap associated with the disk truncation region. These simulations were designed as a robustness test of the treatment of the innermost disk region and confirm that our main conclusions are not sensitive to the presence of this gap. Overall, our findings demonstrate that although the magnitude of stellar dipole plays an important role in the evolution of the accretion–ejection structure, the large-scale poloidal magnetic field threading the disk is essential for launching and sustaining a stable and well-collimated magnetized jet.

items.title: Barred Galaxies in MaNGA: Stellar Mass Dependence and Black Hole Growth
items.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the role of internal structures, such as stellar bars and active galactic nuclei (AGN), in shaping galaxy evolution using 7408 galaxies (2641 barred) from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory survey. Our analysis spans a wide stellar mass range, from dwarf to massive galaxies, examining how internal and environmental processes regulate galaxy evolution. Galaxies are categorized by morphology (ellipticals, E; lenticulars, S0s; early-type spirals, ETS; and late-type spirals, LTS), environment, and the presence of a bar. We find that barred galaxies have a higher median specific star formation rate (sSFR) than unbarred galaxies across most stellar mass intervals. This difference varies with host morphology, with LTS and S0 galaxies showing different trends across stellar mass intervals. The environmental trends of barred and unbarred galaxies are broadly similar within the same mass intervals. In AGN hosts, barred Seyferts tend to lie near the star-forming–green valley boundary, while barred LINERs preferentially occupy the green valley. We further examine the relation between stellar bars and black hole mass and find that barred galaxies host systematically lower black hole masses than unbarred galaxies, with environmental effects appearing to play a secondary role in shaping these differences. A multivariate regression analysis also shows that the positive bar–sSFR association remains statistically significant for star-forming galaxies after accounting for stellar mass, local density, AGN, and morphology. Our results highlight the interconnected roles of stellar bars, stellar mass, morphology, and environment in shaping galaxy star formation, providing new insights into the role of stellar bars in galaxy evolution.

items.title: Properties of Circumfacular Regions Derived from H α and Ca ii K Synoptic Observations of the Sun
items.abstract: Abstract Circumfacular regions are dark chromospheric structures surrounding magnetic regions whose properties and contribution to solar activity diagnostics remain poorly understood. We investigate their photometric and geometric properties using full-disk H α and Ca ii K observations acquired by the Chromospheric Telescope (ChroTel) from 2012 to 2020, spanning the maximum and declining phases of solar cycle 24 and the beginning of cycle 25. We develop an automated segmentation algorithm to identify circumfacular regions and define a photometric index analogous to existing excess and deficit indices. We compare their temporal evolution with those of plages, dark features, and filaments on solar-cycle and Carrington-rotation timescales. Circumfacular regions develop after the H α plage brightening become visible and persist into the decay phase of active regions. At activity maximum, they are the most extended chromospheric structures, covering more than half of the visible solar disk. Their mean intensity varies only weakly throughout the solar cycle; consequently, their index variability, as well as that of the other photometric indices, is driven primarily by changes in area coverage. H α and Ca ii K indices are strongly correlated, although their correlations weaken toward solar minimum. This activity-dependent relationship is primarily driven by the decline of the area of H α excess regions during periods of low activity and the increasing relative contributions of deficit and circumfacular regions. Our results therefore suggest that circumfacular regions should be considered when interpreting disk-integrated chromospheric observations of the Sun and solar-type stars.

items.title: Impact of geomagnetic storm intensity on thermospheric density and orbital decay of LEO satellites: a G1–G5 per-event analysis
items.abstract: Geomagnetic storms enhance thermospheric density and increase atmospheric drag on low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, accelerating their orbital decay, as illustrated by the loss of 38 Starlink satellites in February 2022. Prior multi-event analyses have characterized this response primarily through superposed epoch analyses (SEA). Here we apply a per-event approach: for each of 22 storms spanning G1 to G5 (2003–2024), including the May 2024 Gannon storm, we compare the storm-peak orbit of Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) or GRACE-Follow On (-FO) with a matched quiet-time reference orbit. The mean orbital decay rate enhancement generally increases with storm intensity (77.2%, 98.5%, 138.1%, 149.6%, and 166.5% from G1 to G5), although the scatter within each category is large. Operation altitude is also important: low-altitude events produce strong drag responses even under weak geomagnetic forcing. An empirical multiple linear regression model using quiet-time decay rate, maximum Kp, and operation altitude reproduces the storm-time decay rate (R² = 0.91; root mean square error, RMSE = 12.3 m/day; leave-one-out RMSE = 15.1 m/day). Replacing Kp with the open-ended Hp30 index gives similar results. These per-event benchmarks complement SEA-based analyses, provide a reference for empirical thermospheric models, and support storm-time orbit prediction for LEO satellites.

items.title: Scientific collaboration between Türkiye and the Turkic States: A comparative bibliometric analysis (1992–2025)
items.abstract: Objective. The objective of this study was to map and compare scientific coauthorship between Türkiye and the following countries: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan. The timeframe for this study is from 1992 to 2025. Design/Methodology/Approach. A longitudinal comparative bibliometric analysis examined 10,885 Scopus-indexed documents, representing 11,476 publication–country-pair relations. The author–affiliation records were validated, and the institutional names were normalized. The analyses encompassed annual output, bilateral and multilateral participation, institutional strength, and normalized weighted betweenness, as well as fractional disciplinary profiles based on Scopus source classifications. Results/Discussion. The most significant expansion in collaboration was observed after 2020. Of the country-pair relations examined, Türkiye–Azerbaijan accounted for 58.1% of the sample. Multilateral publications constituted 81.3% of the Uzbekistan relationship, whereas 59.8% of the Kyrgyzstan relationship was bilateral. Kyrgyz-Turkish Manas University exhibited a dominant presence within the Kyrgyzstan network, while central positions in Kazakhstan were distributed among multiple institutions. Physics institutes constituted the primary hubs within the Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan networks. The disciplines of Physics and Astronomy led the corresponding disciplinary profiles, whereas the discipline of Medicine led those of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. Conclusions. Türkiye's collaboration with the four states is characterized by a heterogeneity in institutional and disciplinary patterns, defying the adoption of a singular regional configuration. The publication volume, the country composition, and the institutional network position provide complementary evidence for identifying cooperation opportunities specific to each partnership. Originality/Value. The study integrates author-level collaboration validation, institutional network analysis, and fractional disciplinary profiling within a common comparative framework. The study extends earlier regional comparisons through 2025 and incorporates Uzbekistan.

items.title: Constructing a new hybrid model–Phy-XGBoost to predict the arrival time of coronal mass ejections
items.abstract: Predicting the arrival time of Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) is essential for space weather. In this study, we propose Phy-XGBoost, a physics-guided framework for CME arrival time prediction. We first extend the standard Drag-Based Model (DBM) to a Generalized Drag-Based Model (GDBM) to explore potential differences in the propagation of fast and slow CMEs, further refining it into a weighted GDBM (w-GDBM). To alleviate potential limitations of the physical model, we introduce XGBoost to predict the transit time residuals between observations and w-GDBM predictions using CME and solar-wind features. Across 800 random train test splits, Phy-XGBoost reduced the average MAE from 13.44 to 11.40 h and the average MedAE from 11.14 to 8.79 h compared with w-GDBM. Phy-XGBoost also achieved a comparable average MAE but a lower average MedAE than the purely data-driven XGBoost. These results suggest that the proposed physics-guided machine learning framework provides a promising approach to predicting CME arrival times.

items.title: Analysis plan (pre-registration): chance-alignment and measurement-error verification of the Phygas stage-1 screening
items.abstract: Analysis plan, written before any result of the verification runs was inspected, for the Phygas stage-1 screening of Gaia DR3 stars against young open clusters (volunteer computing, BitBOINC). It fixes in advance how 20 chance-alignment control runs and 20 measurement-error repeats of the whole catalogue are used to decide whether the number of slow, non-member star-cluster passages in the real data exceeds the chance level, and for which clusters: the data and runs, the primary outcome, the tests (an aggregate empirical test and per-cluster t tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction), a robustness criterion against measurement errors, checks that must pass before any result is interpreted, the rules for what will be claimed, and the known limitations. It also discloses what had been seen before the plan was written: one real run and one single-draw pilot control, in which the excess at the lowest relative speeds was found to be largely known cluster members, which is why members are counted separately. Planned venue of the results: Physics and Astronomy Reports (Istanbul University). Every task of the verification runs is computed by two different volunteers and accepted only when both results agree; all contributors are credited by BOINC user name. Changes to this plan after the date of this record will be listed as deviations.

items.title: Experience Improves Spatial Foraging Performance in a Complex Environment in Heliconius Butterflies.
items.abstract: Heliconius butterflies rely on spatial memory to maintain trapline foraging routes, repeatedly visiting pollen resources along memorized paths. Increased foraging performance resulting from learning the spatial distribution of resources is thought to have driven the evolution of this specialized behavior. Here, we experimentally test whether prior experience in a spatially complex environment influences relative foraging performance in the pollen-feeding butterfly Heliconius erato, a species with well-documented behavioral, ecological and neuroanatomical specializations for spatial learning. We reared freshly eclosed adults in either an open cage or a cage that was matched for resource distribution but structurally divided to increase the spatial complexity experienced by the butterflies. We then tested them individually in a controlled foraging assay under familiar and unfamiliar environments. Butterflies reared in the spatially complex environment efficiently reached the feeder regardless of familiarity with the environment, whereas butterflies reared in the open environment showed strong context dependence, performing well only in the open cage. These results indicate that prior experience of a spatially complex environment supports greater foraging efficiency in Heliconius butterflies, highlighting environmental structure as a likely determinant of the ecological value of spatial learning in this group, with potential consequences for foraging behavior in natural environments.

items.title: A Scalable Workflow for Extracting Species Interactions From Ecological Literature Using Large Language Models.
items.abstract: The contemporary ecological crisis calls for integration and synthesis of vast amounts of mostly scattered and often hard-to-extract ecological information that is dispersed across hundreds of thousands of scientific papers. Recent advancements in natural language processing (NLP) and the emergence of large language models (LLMs) offer a novel and promising approach to this persistent challenge. Here, we present a replicable and adaptable workflow that automates the extraction of a broad range of biological interactions among species from scientific literature using LLMs. We provide a demonstration of this workflow by performing a large-scale data extraction directly from a corpus of 83,910 scientific articles using OpenAI GPT-4o. Our approach successfully extracted a network of 144,402 interactions between 36,471 taxa. Performance analysis shows that the model exhibits a precision of 89.5% with a recall of 70.0%, demonstrating that a general-purpose LLM can perform complex ecological information extraction at scale for analysis and synthesis. Results depend on quality filtering choices and inherit biases present in the underlying literature, emphasizing the need for validation and quality control. Standardized outputs can be browsed, queried, or joined with existing interaction repositories and taxonomic backbones, facilitating downstream reuse and interoperability. Our case study shows that LLMs are capable of carrying out complex extraction tasks on key ecological data on a very large scale, paving the way for a multitude of potential applications in ecology and beyond.

items.title: Lost and Found: Western Honey Bee ( Apis mellifera ) Matrix Metalloproteinase 1 .
items.abstract: The quality of reference genomes is of utmost importance as they and the therein annotated genes and proteins serve as basis for many downstream applications. Although the current Western honey bee (Apis mellifera) genome assembly (Amel_HAv3.1) represents a significant improvement over previous versions (Amel_4.0, Amel_4.5), it nevertheless lacks certain protein-coding genes present in those earlier assemblies. One of these "lost and found" genes is locus 409868 of Amel_4.0 and Amel_4.5 which is missing due to an approximately 160 kb assembly gap on chromosome 10 in Amel_HAv3.1. Here we show that the A. mellifera genome indeed harbours locus 409868 encoding matrix metalloproteinase 1 (mmp1) and that it is expressed in at least four different mRNA isoforms in honey bee workers. Orthologues from other insect species have essential tissue and organ remodelling functions during development and gene knockdowns at specific developmental time points are lethal. As adult honey bee workers show in addition an elaborate age-based division of labour with drastic major morphological and physiological changes requiring extensive tissue and organ remodelling, leaving out mmp1 because of a missing gene in the reference genome, may mean leaving out a potential key player in development.

items.title: Old meets new: How emerging contaminants reshape the environmental behavior of legacy contaminants in soils-interaction mechanisms, remediation reassessment, and the regulatory role of soil organic matter.
items.abstract: Microplastics, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and antibiotics coexist in soils with legacy metal(loid)s, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and pesticides. These mixtures can alter contaminant fate, microbial selection, and remediation performance, but direct soil evidence remains uneven. This review synthesizes studies mainly from 2015 to 2025, earlier work, and selected early-online papers through June 2026. Soil evidence supports microplastic interactions with metals and PAHs; PFAS-metal evidence remains limited, mainly to retention. Antibiotic-metal evidence primarily concerns resistance co-selection rather than altered metal fate. We organize candidate processes into overlapping diagnostic tiers (physical co-location, interfacial chemical coupling, and biologically mediated feedback) and appraise evidence by study design, environmental relevance, mechanistic support, and risk of bias. A comparative map specifies required observations, alternative explanations, endpoint direction, and direct-evidence confidence. Concentration addition, independent action, and the combination index apply only to commensurable toxicological dose-response endpoints; transport, speciation, accumulation, and resistance require factorial or response-surface analyses. HIX, SUVA254, and PARAFAC components remain conditional dissolved organic matter proxies requiring method controls and independent validation. We classify remediation conclusions as direct mixture evidence, transferred single-contaminant principles, or author recommendations. The synthesis separates established findings from provisional interpretations.

items.title: Surplus Killing of Magellanic Penguins Spheniscus magellanicus by Puma Puma concolor) in Islote Lobos National Park, Northern Patagonia.
items.abstract: Surplus killing (SK) by large carnivores may generate high-intensity mortality events in colonial seabirds. Here, we document repeated predation events involving Magellanic penguins ( Spheniscus magellanicus ) and pumas ( Puma concolor ) in Islote Lobos National Park (ILNP, Río Negro, Argentina). During the 2024-2025 breeding season, only four adult penguins with cervical injuries and no signs of consumption were recorded, precluding their interpretation as SK. In contrast, during the 2025-2026 breeding season, multiple high-intensity mortality events were recorded at La Pastosa and Isla de los Pájaros, two islets harboring reproductive penguin colonies in the ILNP. Across all documented 2025-2026 events, at least 961 penguins were found dead, including 887 adults and 74 chicks. Carcasses exhibited cervical bite injuries and little or no evidence of consumption, while fresh puma tracks, feces, and direct observations of an adult individual within the colonies strongly supported puma predation. During the four consecutive breeding seasons prior to these events, population monitoring did not record mortality episodes of comparable magnitude and suggested stable population dynamics within the ILNP colonies. The mortality recorded during the 2025-2026 breeding season represented a minimum direct mortality of 3.52% of the local breeding adult population. These records represent the northernmost confirmed case of SK involving Magellanic penguins and pumas, extending the documented geographic range of this interaction by more than 1000 km northwards. They also suggest that repeated SK events may represent an important source of additive mortality for local penguin colonies. Our findings highlight the ecological importance of episodic terrestrial-marine trophic interactions and the need for continued demographic monitoring in coastal breeding systems.

items.title: Social attraction mediates collective foraging decisions in invasive yellow-legged hornets.
items.abstract: Group-living animals commonly use social information to locate and exploit resources. In many insects, fish, birds and mammals, this leads to collective foraging decisions by which animals aggregate on a single food source despite several alternatives of different or equal qualities. Here, we report collective foraging decisions in a widespread invasive hornet ( Vespa velutina nigrithorax ) that predates on bees and consume plant nectar. When given a choice between 2 identical sugar solutions (in feeders or in traps), wild hornets distributed asymmetrically between the 2 options, and this was more frequent as the number of hornets increased. Priming one of the food sources with dead hornets predictably biased the aggregation toward this particular food source, irrespective of whether the baits were conspecifics or hornets from a different species. Inter-attraction in yellow-legged hornets is thus passive and non-specific, possibly mediated by visual and/or chemical cues displayed by dead hornets. Social foraging may provide important benefits to hornets invading new territories and bring new perspectives for population control.

items.title: Nitrogen response differences at the flowering stage of maize (Zea mays L.) affect nitrogen use efficiency: a physiological and pathway analysis of nitrogen uptake, photosynthetic characteristics, and carbohydrate synthesis.
items.abstract: Background Reducing nitrogen (N) inputs while maintaining crop yield aligns with sustainable development goals. It is therefore important to elucidate the physiological mechanisms underlying maize N use efficiency (NUE). The physiological traits and transcriptional profiles of two maize cultivars, 'Qiangsheng 101' (QS) (a low N-sensitive cultivar) and 'Zhengdan 958' (ZD) (a low N-tolerant cultivar), were analyzed at two N application rates: 150 kg ha -1 (low N, LN) and 300 kg ha -1 (normal N level, NN). Results Compared with LN-ZD, LN-QS showed reductions of 11.22% to 14.29% in grain yield (GY), 11.73% to 23.53% in NUE, and 13.11% to 15.97% in radiation use efficiency (RUE). Relative to LN-ZD, LN-QS showed a 17.14% to 17.60% reduction in the relative chlorophyll content (SPAD) value and a 14.29% to 19.23% reduction in the net photosynthetic rate (Pn). Soluble sugar content decreased and starch content increased in LN-QS relative to LN-ZD (P Conclusion Under low N conditions, the reduction in N uptake and metabolic capacity in QS led to diminished photosynthetic performance, which subsequently constrained carbon assimilation, ultimately reducing NUE and GY, while ZD remained stable. These results provide valuable insights for the optimization of N management strategies and the improvement of maize productivity. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

items.title: A mid-Cretaceous island as a cradle of Southeast Asian plant biodiversity.
items.abstract: The renowned tropical flora of Southeast Asia is often regarded as being of relatively recent (Cenozoic) origin. Here, based on specimens embedded in mid-Cretaceous amber obtained from Kachin, Myanmar, we report on a large assemblage of exceptionally well-preserved plant fossils encompassing a rich diversity of angiosperms, together with many other seed plants and cryptogams. The morphospecies richness and clade diversity of this flora are among the highest recorded for any single Early to mid-Cretaceous plant megafossil assemblage. This ancient flora reached Southeast Asia rafted on the West Burma Block, an arc-shaped microplate that separated from the northwestern corner of the Australian Plate during the Jurassic and drifted north, finally colliding with Sundaland by the Eocene. The Burma Terrane remained low lying and at low latitudes in the intervening 100-50-million-year period, providing a sanctuary for clade preservation, a cradle for modern clade diversification and a conduit for transferring flourishing Gondwanan angiosperm lineages to Asia. These findings provide insight into the cradle of what ultimately became Southeast Asian angiosperm-dominated tropical forests, whose origins date back over 100 million years.

items.title: Solitary movement style predicts collective foraging while whom to follow emerges only in company
items.abstract: How far can behaviour inside a group, and the group's performance, be predicted from members measured while alone? We tested this on three public datasets of human collective foraging (621, 128 and 1,133 participants). A low-dimensional individual representation estimated from private-phase movement was mapped onto behaviour inside the group through a mapping learned on other participants. Private information processing was stable between the two halves of a session (split-half reliability, the correlation between the halves, 0.60--0.83) and predicted behaviour inside the group with correlations of 0.30--0.66. Selective social learning, following those who have succeeded or stopped, showed stable individual differences inside the group (reliability 0.45--0.59) yet was not predicted at all from the same person's private behaviour. Group performance was predicted with a correlation of 0.55 in all three datasets by simulations never fitted to group outcomes or by the mean of individually measured performance, a prediction carried by mobility and individual performance rather than by social weights. We found no credible evidence for an effect of how members were combined (equivalence bound 0.06). Whom to follow thus emerges only in company, which delimits what solitary measurements can predict and compose.

items.title: Perspective on AI and quantum open-source software
items.abstract: Quantum open-source software provides essential infrastructure for quantum science, and artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping its capabilities and transforming its development. However, verifying quantum software at scale remains difficult, and AI-generated contributions can increase the workload of maintainers. In this Perspective, we examine verification as a central requirement for reliable AI-assisted quantum software development and research. We analyze public repositories, records covering 110 repositories from five annual quantum open-source hackathons that we organize, and responses from more than 1600 participants in a community survey. Our analysis connects limitations in automated verification with the review burden on quantum software maintainers. We propose verification practices and contribution standards that require contributors to support their changes with reproducible evidence for maintainer review. We also examine how quantum open-source software can provide infrastructure for AI-driven research whose results the community can independently verify and build upon. We maintain an open-source companion repository to support reproducibility and help projects adopt and refine these proposals. Together, these contributions help the quantum open-source software community translate advances in AI into reliable quantum research through reproducible verification.

items.title: Probabilistic Stellar Mass and Radius Estimation with Bayesian Hierarchical Stacking
items.abstract: Accurate stellar parameters are essential for the characterisation of exoplanets, yet most host stars lack direct measurements of mass and radius. We aim to predict stellar masses and radii from commonly available observables and to quantify uncertainties and systematic effects in a way that is consistent with stellar observations. By not relying on a single model, we aim to obtain more robust predictive distributions and reduce sensitivity to model misspecification and outliers. We develop a Bayesian machine-learning framework that combines three probabilistic models through Bayesian hierarchical stacking (BHS): a Bayesian additive regression tree model, a two-process heteroscedastic sparse Gaussian process, and a hierarchical Bayesian neural network. The method propagates measurement uncertainties, accounts for correlations among inputs, and aggregates model variance into final predictive distributions. On a held-out test set the method attains a mean absolute relative difference (MARD) of 3.5% for mass and 2.1% for radius, improving on empirical-relation-based methods and standard machine-learning baselines. For 44 Kepler LEGACY stars, the BHS masses differ from estimates obtained with the BAyesian STellar Algorithm (BASTA) by a MARD of 4.8%, compared with 8.5% between the empirical relations and BASTA. Applied to about 2400 exoplanet host stars, the predictions differ from literature values by a MARD of 2.7% in both mass and radius. Residual analysis reveals mild underestimation for cool dwarfs, consistent with sparse training coverage, and positive offsets near the main-sequence turn-off that may reflect priors in isochrone-based catalogues. Internal consistency with g = GM/R^2 is greater for the BHS predictions, with a scatter in Delta log g lower by a factor of three than that of the literature values.

items.title: Counterfactual assessment of social media interventions by separating exposure from engagement
items.abstract: Social media interventions are usually evaluated in individual-level experiments, which are costly to scale and often miss collective effects. We propose the Exposure--Engagement model, whose parameters separately control what social media users are exposed to (recommendation) and how they engage (behaviour). After fitting it to the Italian Twitter debate (2018--2022), we validate it at individual and collective levels. We simulate behavioural interventions (prebunking and accuracy prompts), calibrated on effect sizes, and a recommender-system intervention (chronological feed), comparing effects on engagement, attention diversity, and segregation. All three reduce engagement. Behavioural interventions slightly reduce diversity, leaving segregation unchanged, whereas the chronological feed increases diversity and reduces segregation. For these interventions, changing recommendation does more for the debate's structure than changing behaviour. We design a recommender-system intervention that increases engagement and diversity while reducing segregation, although with about a tenth of the chronological feed's gains, showing the framework's potential for pro-social intervention design.

items.title: Searching for Circumplanetary Dust in the Cavity of the AB Aurigae Disk with ALMA
items.abstract: The young intermediate-mass star AB Aurigae is surrounded by a transition disk whose cavity contains several proposed protoplanets, including the debated source "AB Aur b" at a projected separation of $\approx 0.6$ arcsec ($\approx 93$ au). To search for circumplanetary material associated with these candidates, we have obtained the most sensitive ($\sim 20$ $μ$Jy/beam rms) and highest angular resolution ($\sim 30$ mas) ALMA Band 7 (0.88 mm) observations of AB Aur to date. We recover the asymmetric dust ring in the continuum emission peaking at $\sim 0.9$ arcsec ($\sim 140$ au) and compact emission at the stellar position, but detect no point source at the location of AB Aur b or any of the other proposed protoplanet candidates down to a $3σ$ limit of $60$ $μ$Jy. For optically thin emission, this corresponds to a dust mass of $\lesssim 0.0059 M_\oplus$ (for a dust temperature of 40 K), comparable to the circumplanetary disk around PDS 70 c. The $^{12}$CO emission fills the continuum cavity, revealing inner spiral structure and a clear rotation pattern. The gas at the position of AB Aur b is smoothly connected to the ambient disk with no localized excess or obvious kinematic deviation. If any proposed candidates are accreting, their circumplanetary material must have a low dust mass, a small physical size, dust that is optically thick, or a dearth of large mm-emitting grains.

items.title: Revisiting Sub-Neptune Population Synthesis: The Role of Core Luminosity in Boil-off, Photoevaporation, and the Radius Distribution
items.abstract: The observed bimodal radius distribution of close-in small planets provides important constraints on their formation and evolution. Two atmospheric escape mechanisms, photoevaporation and core-powered mass loss, have been widely invoked to explain this distribution. In this work, we revisit the physical assumptions underlying these models and investigate the role of core luminosity in driving outflows and shaping the radius distribution. We develop a population synthesis framework based on the SEAMIST evolution model, which self-consistently couples the two mass-loss mechanisms while accounting for envelope metallicity. We find that envelope metallicity strongly affects the resulting radius distribution, with 50-100$\times$ solar metallicity providing a good match to the observed population. Boil-off generally dominates atmospheric mass loss, while photoevaporation typically removes at most 3 wt\% of the envelope mass. We find that core luminosity contributes only $\sim$10-20\% of the thermal energy available for envelope re-equilibration during boil-off, producing an absolute mass-loss enhancement of only $\sim$0.4wt\%. Its effect is larger during photoevaporation, where the longer mass-loss timescale allows core heating to accumulate. Nevertheless, core luminosity has little impact on the long-term planetary radius distribution. These results suggest that core-powered mass loss is better understood as a modification to atmospheric escape through its lower-boundary conditions rather than as a distinct mass-loss mechanism. In our best-fit model, the radiative atmosphere contributes a significant $\sim$20\% of the total optical radius. Consequently, we highlight the need for improved radiative-atmosphere modeling in sub-Neptune evolution models to better understand the observed population distribution.

items.title: A Bayesian functional model with multilevel partition priors for group studies in neuroscience.
items.abstract: The statistical analysis of group studies in neuroscience is particularly challenging due to the complex spatio-temporal nature of the data, its multiple levels and the inter-individual variability in brain responses. Traditional ANOVA-based studies and linear mixed effects models typically provide only a limited exploration of the dynamics of group brain activity and of the variability in individual responses, potentially leading to overly simplistic conclusions and/or missing more intricate patterns. In this study we propose a novel Bayesian model-based clustering approach for functional data that simultaneously assesses group effects and individual deviations across the main temporal features in the data. To this end, we develop a multilevel partition prior to model the functional scores arising from a functional Principal Components decomposition of neuroscientific recordings. The proposed approach enables a thorough exploration of group differences and individual deviations without compromising on the spatio-temporal nature of the data. Through a simulation study we demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves correct classification in different clustering scenarios under low and high noise levels in the data. Finally, we consider an Electroencephalogram case study involving an object recognition task, where the proposed approach provides new insights into the underlying brain mechanisms generating the data and their variability.

items.title: Metal-Organic Framework@Polysulfone Composite Beads for Air Filtration of Postharvest Pathogenic Fungal Spores.
items.abstract: Phytopathogenic fungal infections pose a persistent threat to postharvest fruit quality and food security worldwide, with resistant strains increasingly limiting the efficacy of conventional fungicides. This study explored metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as an emerging class of antifungal materials and examined their potential for air-based decontamination in storage environments. Among the zinc- and copper-based frameworks tested, HKUST-1 and ZIF-8 demonstrated exceptionally broad-spectrum antifungal activity, completely inhibiting mycelial growth of Penicillium expansum, Penicillium citrinum, and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, while maintaining strong inhibition of Botrytis cinerea and Mucor piriformis. To enable practical deployment, the most active MOFs were incorporated into polysulfone composite beads via phase inversion, preserving their antifungal properties while offering a processable and scalable format. In vitro assays revealed that these MOF@PSF beads substantially suppressed both mycelial growth and spore germination, with HKUST-1@PSF and ZIF-8@PSF composites reducing conidial viability to near-complete levels. Mechanistic studies revealed that HKUST-1 primarily acts through substantial copper ion release (≈19 ppm), leading to pronounced metabolic inhibition, whereas ZIF-8 operates via reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Evaluation in a dual-chamber air-filtration prototype demonstrated remarkable performance: both composites reduced airborne spore transfer by 95.2-96.7% for P. expansum and by 99.4-99.6% for B. cinerea, effectively preventing contamination of the clean chamber and protecting the stored produce. These findings establish MOF@PSF composite beads as bioactive filtration materials that combine physical spore capture with intrinsic antifungal action, offering a residue-free route to limiting fungal dissemination during postharvest storage.

items.title: Ecology and conservation of subterranean biodiversity of Greater Lisbon, Portugal
items.abstract: Abstract Subterranean ecosystems harbour fauna moulded by extreme and stable conditions such as absence of light, narrow temperature ranges, high humidity and low availability of organic matter. The adaptations of cave fauna, coupled with the isolation of populations, often lead to a higher incidence of endemics and greater vulnerability to environmental changes. These ecosystems face severe threats caused by pollution and overexploitation, habitat loss and climate change, particularly evident in areas of increased human pressure as capitals of countries. In Portugal, more than 100 endemic cave‐adapted species have been identified, and close to its capital, highly urbanized and industrialized, the Greater Lisbon area hosts several unique endemic subterranean species that lack protection measures. We assessed the invertebrate faunal biodiversity and the conservation status of caves in the Greater Lisbon area. Our results show that arthropods dominate, in abundance and richness, the caves of the Greater Lisbon area, followed by molluscs. Ten endemic subterranean species were found, and of the 20 troglobionts recorded, 11 were found in only one cave, 5 in two caves and 4 in three or more. The overall most diverse was Poço Velho Cave, and the most troglobiont‐diverse was Alvide Cave, both in Cascais. Based on our results, we propose a preliminary conservation priority hierarchy for the studied caves. Our findings reveal that Greater Lisbon harbours irreplaceable subterranean habitats, that support diverse and exclusive invertebrate fauna, which face tremendous threats to their survival, underscoring the need for targeted conservation planning and biodiversity monitoring.

items.title: Do psychiatrists have a spider-sense? Clinical impressions as violations of interpersonal Bayesian expectation.
items.abstract: Psychiatric diagnosis depends on the clinician's ability to infer mental states from complex and dynamically evolving interpersonal signals. During the psychiatric interview, clinicians do not only collect explicit symptoms; they continuously sample a rich array of non-verbal and paralinguistic cues including gaze, prosody, affective reciprocity, and interactional timing. These signals are central to psychiatric assessment, yet their contribution to diagnostic reasoning remains poorly formalized. In this Review, we propose a computational account of clinical impressions in psychiatry. We integrate evidence from phenomenological psychopathology, social cognition, and computational neuroscience. We argue that such impressions may arise when the clinician's generative model of social interaction is persistently disconfirmed by subtle deviations in interpersonal behaviour, generating high-level social prediction errors experienced as a sense of incongruity or failed attunement. We formalize this process as VIBE: Violation of Interpersonal Bayesian Expectation. VIBE denotes a pre-reflective epistemic signal generated when observed interpersonal cues deviate from the clinician's expected model of social reciprocity. It is not a diagnostic criterion but orients hypothesis generation by drawing attention to disturbances in interpersonal predictability. We hypothesize that VIBE may constitute a transdiagnostic mechanism: different disorders, from schizophrenia to autism spectrum disorder and mood disorders, may disrupt distinct dimensions of interpersonal prediction. The Praecox Feeling, first described by Rümke in 1942, can be read as the earliest clinical formalization of this process and as its schizophrenia-spectrum instance, in which the profile of interpersonal violations is consistent enough to be clinically recognizable. This framework recasts the diagnostic impression as an embodied inferential process rather than an opaque subjective faculty. Teaching clinicians to articulate, examine, and recalibrate these impressions could strengthen diagnostic reasoning, reduce bias, and improve therapeutic attunement. VIBE provides a bridge between phenomenological psychopathology and computational neuroscience, and offers a tractable, empirically testable model for studying the neurocomputational basis of psychiatric clinical judgement.

items.title: Distinct Cross-Lagged Relations of Cognitive Reappraisal and Expressive Suppression With Perceived Social Support Among Chinese Adolescents.
items.abstract: Introduction Converging evidence suggests a close relationship between emotion regulation (ER) and perceived social support (PSS) among adolescents. Yet, little is currently known about their longitudinal cross-lagged associations within the Chinese cultural context, as well as the differential effects of different ER strategies. To address these gaps, the present study aimed to examine the cross-lagged associations between PSS and two specific ER strategies-cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression-in Chinese adolescents. Methods A total of 316 adolescents from Zhoukou, China (45.9% female; M age = 16.42, SD = 0.61, aged 14-18 years) participated in a three-wave longitudinal study, with data collected at 6-month intervals during senior high school. To examine hypothesized cross-lagged associations, we employed cross-lagged panel models, a well-established method for analyzing temporal associations (Kenny 1975). Results Cross-lagged panel model revealed that PSS at Time 1 was positively associated with cognitive reappraisal at Time 2, which in turn was positively related to PSS at Time 3. PSS at Time 2 also showed a positive correlation with cognitive reappraisal at Time 3. In contrast, no significant cross-lagged effects were observed between PSS and expressive suppression over time. Conclusions These findings contribute to a more nuanced understanding of the longitudinal cross-lagged associations between PSS and ER in adolescence, highlighting the association between supportive social environments and adolescents' ER strategies.
